items.how: File DD Form 293 with your service's Discharge Review Board. Free. Get help — do not do this alone.
items.hack: Liberal-consideration policy is the whole ballgame. Boards must give liberal consideration to discharges where PTSD, TBI, military sexual trauma, or sexual orientation contributed to the misconduct — which covers an enormous share of OTH discharges from the post-9/11 wars. Even better: a VA 'character of discharge' determination can get you VA healthcare and benefits WITHOUT a formal upgrade, and is a faster parallel track. Use free counsel — NVLSP's Lawyers Serving Warriors, the Veterans Consortium Pro Bono Program, and law school veterans clinics all take these cases at no cost.
items.deadline: DRB: 15 years from discharge. BCMR: nominally 3 years from discovery, routinely waived.

items.title: UCX — unemployment compensation for ex-servicemembers
items.org: U.S. Department of Labor, administered by state workforce agencies
items.who: Veterans who completed their first full term of active service (or were discharged early for a qualifying reason such as medical disqualification, pregnancy, parenthood, or service-connected injury), with an honorable or general discharge. Reservists need a continuous period of 90+ days. OTH, bad conduct and dishonorable discharges are excluded.
items.value: Your military service and pay are treated as covered civilian employment. Weekly amounts and duration are set by state law — typically $200-$800/week for up to 26 weeks depending on the state. Your benefit is computed from a DoL 'Schedule of Remuneration' keyed to your pay grade at separation, which DoL updates annually after each military pay raise.
items.how: File with the state workforce agency where you are looking for work (not necessarily where you were stationed). You need your DD-214 Member Copy 4. File immediately after separation — most states will not backdate.
items.hack: Two things kill UCX claims: (1) people wait until their leave sell-back and final settlement run out, but most states do not backdate, so you lose those weeks permanently — file the week you separate; (2) severance/separation pay and terminal leave can offset or delay benefits in many states, so ask the state agency specifically how they treat military separation pay before you assume you are ineligible. Also note: you cannot draw UCX at the same time as VA Chapter 31 VR&E subsistence or DEA benefits.
items.deadline: File immediately upon separation; most states do not backdate claims.

items.title: Veterans' preference in federal hiring — 5-point vs 10-point
items.who: 5-point (TP): veterans with 180+ days active service during a war, campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge was authorized, or service in specified date windows, discharged under honorable conditions. 10-point: veterans with a service-connected disability or a Purple Heart (CP/CPS/XP), plus certain spouses, widows/widowers and mothers of disabled or deceased veterans (derived preference).
items.value: Points are added to your passing score on competitive examinations. More importantly, 10-point preference eligibles with a 30%+ compensable disability (CPS) are placed at the TOP of the certificate for most positions — ahead of every non-preference candidate regardless of score.
items.how: Claim it on your USAJOBS application and attach documentation: DD-214 Member Copy 4 for 5-point; DD-214 plus SF-15 plus your VA rating letter for 10-point. Preference does not apply to Senior Executive Service or most merit promotion (internal) announcements.
items.hack: The derived preference for spouses, widows/widowers and mothers of disabled veterans is almost never claimed because almost nobody knows it exists. Also: veterans' preference applies to Reduction In Force (RIF) retention, not just hiring — a preference-eligible federal employee is materially harder to lay off, which is real money in a shrinking agency.
items.deadline: Claim at time of application; documentation must be attached before the announcement closes.

items.title: VRA — Veterans Recruitment Appointment (hired with no competition, up to GS-11)
items.who: Disabled veterans; veterans who served on active duty during a war or in a campaign/expedition for which a campaign badge was authorized; veterans who received an Armed Forces Service Medal; and veterans separated from active duty within the last 3 years. Honorable or general discharge required.
items.value: An agency can hire you NON-COMPETITIVELY — no vacancy announcement, no competing against the public — into any position up to GS-11 or equivalent. After 2 years of satisfactory service you MUST be converted non-competitively to a career or career-conditional appointment.
items.how: You do not apply to a VRA 'announcement' — there usually isn't one. You approach the hiring manager or agency veterans employment program office directly, tell them you are VRA-eligible, and ask them to appoint you. Bring your DD-214 and, if applicable, your VA rating letter.
items.hack: This is the single most under-used federal hiring path. Ninety percent of veterans grind USAJOBS announcements against hundreds of applicants when VRA lets an agency skip that process entirely. The move: find the specific job you want, find the actual hiring manager (not HR), and email them saying 'I am VRA-eligible, which means you can appoint me directly without an announcement.' Many managers do not know this is available and are delighted to skip a 90-day hiring action. Note the 3-year clock if your only eligibility basis is recent separation.
items.deadline: If qualifying only as 'separated within 3 years,' that window closes 3 years after separation. Disabled veterans and campaign-badge veterans have no time limit.

items.title: 30% or More Disabled Veteran appointing authority — non-competitive hiring at ANY grade
items.who: Veterans rated 30% or more service-connected disabled by the VA, or retired from active military service with a disability rating of 30% or more.
items.value: Unlike VRA, there is NO grade ceiling. An agency can non-competitively appoint you to any position at any grade you qualify for — GS-13, GS-14, GS-15. Initial appointment must exceed 60 days and is time-limited, but the agency can convert you to permanent at any point during the appointment without competition.
items.how: No vacancy announcement is required. Provide your VA rating letter showing 30%+ (or your retirement orders showing a 30%+ disability retirement) to the hiring manager or agency HR. Veterans' preference rules do not apply because there is no competition to be preferred in.
items.hack: This is the most powerful and least-used federal hiring authority in existence. If you are at 30% or above, you can be hired at a senior grade with no announcement, no rating and ranking, and no competitors. Combine it with the VRA message: email the hiring manager, name the authority ('5 CFR 316.302, the 30 percent or more disabled veteran authority'), and attach your rating letter. Managers who would never wade through a competitive action will absolutely use a no-announcement authority to hire someone they already want.
items.deadline: No time limit — eligibility persists as long as you hold the 30%+ rating.

items.title: VEOA — compete for internal-only federal jobs as an outside candidate
items.who: Preference-eligible veterans, and veterans with 3+ years of continuous honorable active service (even if not preference-eligible).
items.value: Lets you apply to merit promotion announcements that are otherwise restricted to current federal employees ('status candidates'). You get access, not an advantage — veterans' preference points do NOT apply under VEOA. Selectees receive career or career-conditional appointments.
items.how: On USAJOBS, look for announcements open to 'Merit Promotion' or 'Status Candidates' — these normally exclude the public. If the 'Who May Apply' section lists VEOA eligibles, apply and attach your DD-214.
items.hack: The competitive advantage is not points, it is the size of the field. A public announcement draws 400 applicants; a merit promotion announcement for a niche GS-13 might draw 12 internal candidates. VEOA puts you in the 12. Filter USAJOBS for 'Veterans' under Hiring Path and you will surface announcements most of the public never sees. Note: 3 years of continuous active service qualifies you even with zero disability and no campaign medal — many veterans wrongly assume they need preference.
items.deadline: No time limit.

items.title: Schedule A hiring authority for people with disabilities
items.who: People with a severe physical disability, psychiatric disability, or intellectual disability — including veterans, whether or not the disability is service-connected. Not veteran-specific, which is exactly why veterans miss it.
items.value: Non-competitive appointment at ANY grade, temporary or permanent. After 2 years of satisfactory service you can be converted to the competitive service without competition.
items.how: You need a 'Schedule A letter' — a signed statement from a licensed medical professional, a licensed vocational rehabilitation specialist, or any federal/state agency that issues disability benefits, certifying that you have a qualifying disability and are able to perform the job. The letter does NOT have to disclose your diagnosis. Submit it with your application and tell the hiring manager you are Schedule A eligible.
items.hack: Veterans with PTSD, TBI or major depression routinely qualify for Schedule A and never use it — they only think about VRA and the 30% authority. Schedule A is a second, independent non-competitive door, and a VA rating decision letter can often serve as the certifying documentation. If you are under 30% disabled (so the 30% authority is closed) but have a qualifying psychiatric condition, Schedule A is your no-grade-ceiling path.
items.deadline: No time limit.

items.title: Using USAJOBS correctly — the mechanics that get you referred
items.who: Any veteran applying for federal employment.
items.value: Most veterans are screened out for mechanical reasons, not qualifications. Fixing the mechanics is the difference between 'not referred' and an interview.
items.how: (1) Write a federal resume of 4-6 pages, not a 1-page civilian resume — include hours per week, month/year dates, supervisor names and salary for every position. (2) Mirror the exact language of the announcement's 'Specialized Experience' paragraph; HR specialists are literally checking for those phrases. (3) Answer the occupational questionnaire at the highest level you can honestly support and make sure your resume proves every claim. (4) Upload DD-214 Member Copy 4, SF-15 and VA rating letter where applicable. (5) Set up saved searches with the 'Veterans' hiring path filter.
items.hack: The single highest-leverage habit: read the 'Specialized Experience' requirement, then copy its verbs and nouns into your resume bullets verbatim where truthful. HR is doing a keyword-and-phrase match against that paragraph, not evaluating your potential. Second: apply on day one of the announcement — many agencies use cut-off numbers and close early once they hit a quota of applications.
items.deadline: Announcements often close early once an application cap is reached — apply the day it opens.

items.title: Military Spouse Preference (Program S) — DoD appropriated-fund hiring preference
items.who: Spouses of active-duty service members who relocate on PCS orders, applying for DoD appropriated-fund positions at the new duty location. Generally must be relocating with the sponsor and qualify for the position.
items.value: Preference in DoD competitive civilian hiring at the new location — if you are among the best qualified, you must be selected over non-preference candidates for positions up to a certain grade level.
items.how: Register through the DoD civilian personnel system at the gaining installation's civilian personnel advisory center as soon as you have PCS orders. You must register — it is not automatic.
items.hack: Register the day orders drop, not after you arrive. The preference is tied to a relocation window, and spouses routinely lose it by waiting until they have physically moved and settled. It applies only to DoD appropriated-fund jobs, so pair it with the separate Executive Order non-competitive appointment authority (below) to cover non-DoD agencies.
items.deadline: Tied to the PCS relocation window — register immediately upon receiving orders.

items.title: Military spouse non-competitive appointment (Executive Order 13473)
items.who: Three categories: (1) spouses of active-duty members relocating on PCS orders; (2) spouses of service members who are 100% disabled due to a service-connected injury; (3) un-remarried widows/widowers of service members killed on active duty.
items.value: Any federal agency, government-wide, may appoint you non-competitively — no announcement, no competition. Categories (2) and (3) have NO time limit; category (1) is tied to the relocation.
items.how: Tell the hiring manager or agency HR you are eligible under EO 13473 for non-competitive appointment. Provide PCS orders, the service member's 100% disability documentation, or the DD-1300/death certificate as applicable.
items.hack: Almost no one uses categories (2) and (3), which never expire. A spouse of a 100%-rated veteran, or a Gold Star widow/widower, can be directly appointed into any federal agency at any point for the rest of their life. This is dramatically more powerful than Program S, which only covers DoD and only during a relocation. Approach hiring managers directly and name the Executive Order.
items.deadline: Categories (2) and (3): no time limit. Category (1): tied to the PCS relocation.

items.title: Military Spouse Employment Partnership (MSEP) — direct partner-employer job portal
items.org: DoD Spouse Education and Career Opportunities (SECO) / Military OneSource
items.who: Military spouses of active duty, Guard and Reserve members. Free.
items.value: A job portal where several hundred partner employers have committed to recruiting, hiring and retaining military spouses — including many with portable, remote-friendly roles specifically designed to survive a PCS. Pairs with SECO career coaching (free, by phone) and MyCAA tuition assistance for eligible spouses.
items.how: Register at myseco.militaryonesource.mil and search the MSEP job bank. Book a free SECO career coaching session by calling Military OneSource at 800-342-9647.
items.hack: MSEP partners get spouse applications flagged, which matters more than the job listings themselves — the same job posted publicly and through MSEP goes to different queues. Also check MyCAA separately: spouses of active-duty service members in pay grades E-1 to E-6, W-1 to W-2, and O-1 to O-2 can get tuition assistance for licenses, certifications and associate degrees. Verify the current MyCAA benefit cap, which has been adjusted in recent years.
items.deadline: Ongoing. MyCAA has pay-grade eligibility windows that close on promotion.

items.title: Your security clearance is a cash asset — protect its currency
items.who: Any service member or veteran who held a Secret, Top Secret or TS/SCI clearance.
items.value: Cleared roles carry a well-documented salary premium over uncleared equivalents — commonly 10-20% for Secret and substantially more for TS/SCI with a current polygraph. A clearance also narrows your competition dramatically, because only cleared candidates can apply. For a mid-career technical role this is frequently a $15,000-$40,000/year difference.
items.how: A clearance is not 'yours' — it is granted by an agency and becomes inactive when you separate. It can typically be reinstated without a full new investigation if you are re-sponsored within 24 months of your last access (and you remain in Continuous Vetting). Record your clearance level, investigation type, date of last investigation, date of last access, and polygraph date before you separate; you will need them on every application.
items.hack: The 24-month reinstatement window is the whole thing. Take a cleared job within two years and the employer avoids a 9-18 month investigation — that is why they pay the premium. Wait 25 months and you are worth the same as an uncleared candidate. If you are separating without a cleared job lined up, prioritize ANY cleared role (even a lateral or slightly lower-paying one) to keep the clearance active, then move up from inside the cleared market. Also: SkillBridge into a cleared defense contractor is the cleanest way to hand off the clearance without a gap.
items.deadline: Roughly 24 months from last access for straightforward reinstatement — verify with the sponsoring facility security officer.

items.title: Operation Homefront Critical Financial Assistance
items.who: Post-9/11 service members and veterans. Broadest eligibility is for wounded/injured/ill service members (all ranks). Deployed and general active-duty assistance is limited to pay grades E-1 through E-6. Separated veterans need an Honorable or General (Under Honorable Conditions) discharge within 10 years of separation.
items.value: Direct grants (not loans) paying rent/mortgage, utilities, auto payments and auto insurance, food, home repairs, medical and vision expenses, baby items, home items and travel. Paid to the creditor/vendor, not to you.
items.how: Apply through the MyOH portal at my.operationhomefront.org. Eligibility questions: 1-877-264-3968. Expect to upload orders or DD-214, proof of the bill, and proof of the hardship.
items.hack: The rank cap is the thing people miss: if you are E-7 or above, or an officer, you are generally only eligible through the wounded/injured/ill track — so if you qualify there, say so explicitly on the application, because that track has both the widest expense list and the widest rank eligibility. Also note the 10-year post-separation window: this is not a lifetime veterans charity, it is a recent-transition safety net, so use it in your first decade out.
items.deadline: Within 10 years of separation for veterans; apply before the bill goes to collections.

items.title: Army Emergency Relief (AER) — same-day, zero-interest, and often a straight grant
items.who: Active-duty Soldiers and their dependents; retired Soldiers (longevity, medical, or age-60 retirement) and dependents; Army Reserve and National Guard on Title 10 orders for 30+ days and their dependents; unmarried surviving spouses and children of deceased Soldiers.
items.value: Zero-interest loans and outright grants for emergency travel, rent/mortgage/deposits, temporary lodging, food, non-TRICARE medical co-pays, vehicle repair, utilities, funeral expenses, furniture and appliances, home repair, PCS travel, child care, dental and clothing, passport/immigration fees, and special-needs medical equipment. Wounded Warrior Comfort Grants pay $1,000 at the time of hospitalization. Child care assistance up to $1,500 ($500/month for three months). AER awards over $13 million in education scholarships annually to spouses and children.
items.how: Apply through your installation's Army Community Service AER office, online at armyemergencyrelief.org, or through the American Red Cross when no AER office is nearby. Assistance is often provided same day and is always provided within 48 hours.
items.hack: AER is a benefit you earned, not charity, and it does NOT require your chain of command's permission for most categories — the old requirement for a commander's signature has been substantially relaxed. Retired Soldiers stay eligible for life, which almost no retiree knows. And the 48-hour guarantee makes AER the right call for a true emergency where a VSO grant would take three weeks.
items.deadline: Rolling. Scholarship applications have annual spring deadlines.

items.title: Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society — Quick Assist Loans and interest-free help
items.who: Active duty and retired Navy and Marine Corps members and their eligible family members; Reservists on Title 10; surviving spouses.
items.value: Interest-free loans and grants for basic living expenses, emergency travel, vehicle repair, funeral costs, medical and dental bills, child care and disaster relief. Quick Assist Loans provide small interest-free loans (commonly up to a few hundred dollars) with minimal paperwork to keep members out of payday lending. Also runs Visiting Nurse services, the Budget for Baby program, and education loans and grants.
items.how: Contact your local NMCRS office (on most Navy and Marine installations), call the society, or apply online at nmcrs.org. Reservists and those far from an installation can be served remotely or through the American Red Cross.
items.hack: The Quick Assist Loan is explicitly designed as a payday-loan killer — it is approved fast with almost no documentation, and it is interest-free. If a junior sailor or Marine is about to take a 400% APR payday loan, this is the intervention. Separately, Budget for Baby gives expectant families a free layette and a financial planning session, and almost every pregnant Navy/Marine spouse is eligible and does not know it.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Air Force Aid Society — Falcon Loans and community grants
items.who: Active duty Air Force and Space Force members, retirees, Guard and Reserve on Title 10 orders for 15+ consecutive days, and their dependents and surviving spouses.
items.value: Interest-free loans and grants for emergency travel, vehicle repair, basic living expenses, funeral expenses, medical and dental bills, and child care. The Falcon Loan provides a no-documentation, interest-free loan (commonly up to $1,500) approved quickly online. Also funds the General Henry H. Arnold Education Grant for dependent children and spouses, plus respite child care and Bundles for Babies.
items.how: Apply online at afas.org or through your installation's Airman and Family Readiness Center. The Falcon Loan is applied for directly online without a counseling appointment.
items.hack: The Falcon Loan requires no supporting documentation and no command involvement — it exists precisely so an Airman with a broken transmission does not miss work or take a predatory loan. Retirees remain eligible for life. Guard and Reserve eligibility keys off 15 consecutive days on Title 10, a lower bar than AER's 30 days, so Air Guard members often qualify when they assume they do not.
items.deadline: Rolling. Arnold Education Grant has an annual application window (typically winter/spring).

items.title: Coast Guard Mutual Assistance (CGMA)
items.who: Active duty and retired Coast Guard members, Reservists, Coast Guard civilian employees, Auxiliarists, and dependents and surviving spouses.
items.value: Interest-free loans and grants for basic living expenses, emergency travel, vehicle repair, medical and dental costs, disaster assistance, and funeral expenses. Also funds education grants and supplemental education assistance, and a layette program for new parents.
items.how: Apply through a CGMA representative at your unit, or online at cgmahq.org. Many awards can be processed the same day.
items.hack: CGMA covers Coast Guard CIVILIAN employees and Auxiliarists, which is unique among the service relief societies and is essentially unknown. It also has a strong record of standing up emergency assistance during government shutdowns and pay lapses, which have hit the Coast Guard specifically because it sits under DHS rather than DoD.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: VFW Unmet Needs — up to $2,500, paid straight to your creditor
items.who: Active-duty service members (including activated Guard and Reserve) and military families facing hardship connected to deployment, military activity, injury or financial stress. You do NOT have to be a VFW member.
items.value: Grants up to $2,500. Not a loan — no repayment. Covers rent or mortgage, utilities, vehicle expenses, child care, food and other daily necessities. The VFW pays creditors directly.
items.how: Apply at vfw.org/assistance/financial-grants. Provide proof of military status and documentation of the hardship (the bill, the eviction notice, the repair estimate). Each request is individually reviewed.
items.hack: Because the VFW pays the vendor directly, you should apply with the actual invoice or payoff quote in hand — applications with a specific creditor, account number and amount move much faster than 'I need help with rent.' Also, non-membership eligibility is the part people get wrong: veterans skip this program assuming they must join the VFW first. They do not.
items.deadline: Rolling. Apply before the account goes to collections or eviction is filed.

items.title: American Legion Temporary Financial Assistance (TFA) — for minor children
items.who: Veterans and active-duty service members who have at least one MINOR CHILD in the home. The child is the eligibility trigger. You generally do not have to be a Legion member.
items.value: Cash grants (historically up to roughly $1,500, non-repayable) for shelter, food, utilities and health expenses to keep a household with minor children stable.
items.how: Apply through your local American Legion post or department (state) service officer, who submits the TFA application on your behalf. Find your department at legion.org.
items.hack: The minor-child requirement is the filter almost everyone gets wrong in both directions — veterans without children apply and are denied, and veterans with children never apply because they assume it is a membership benefit. Go through a Legion service officer rather than applying cold; they know the documentation the national office wants and can get it moving in days. The same service officer is also a VA-accredited representative who can file your disability claim for free.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: USA Cares — emergency assistance with no rank or era cap
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans, active duty, Guard and Reserve, and their families. Verified as actively operating in 2026, headquartered in Louisville, KY, and running a support call center.
items.value: Need-based grants (not loans) paid directly to creditors for housing (rent, mortgage, eviction/foreclosure prevention), utilities, food, transportation and other basic needs. Also runs programs targeted at housing stability, employment transition, and combat-injured support.
items.how: Apply at usacares.org. Documentation required: DD-214 or orders, the specific bill or notice, and proof of income/hardship.
items.hack: USA Cares does not impose the E-1 to E-6 rank ceiling that Operation Homefront uses for general assistance, which makes it the better first call for senior NCOs and officers in a genuine crisis. Apply to USA Cares AND your service relief society AND the VFW simultaneously — these organizations do not treat each other as disqualifying, and a $1,200 rent shortfall is often solved by two partial grants rather than one full one.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Semper Fi & America's Fund — all branches, catastrophic injury and critical illness
items.who: Combat-wounded, critically ill and catastrophically injured service members and veterans from ALL branches — Air Force, Army, Coast Guard, Marine Corps, Navy and Space Force — and their families. Service dates from 1960 to present.
items.value: Eight program lines: Bedside Financial Support (immediate cash to families at the hospital), Housing Assistance, Transportation Assistance, a Visiting Nurse Program, Annette Conway Caregiver Retreats, Specialized and Adaptive Equipment, Skip's Kids (support for children of the wounded), and Disaster Relief. Case-managed with a long-term relationship, not a one-time grant.
items.how: Call 760-725-6780 or complete the intake questionnaire at thefund.org. A case manager contacts you directly.
items.hack: The name is the problem — the overwhelming majority of eligible Army, Navy, Air Force and Coast Guard members assume this is Marines-only and never apply. It is not. Also, 'critically ill' explicitly includes non-combat catastrophic illness (cancer, ALS, MS), so a veteran with a devastating diagnosis unrelated to combat can still qualify. The Bedside Financial Support is the fastest-moving money in the veteran nonprofit world — it reaches families within days of a catastrophic injury.
items.deadline: Rolling. Contact as early in a hospitalization as possible.

items.title: Modest Needs Self-Sufficiency Grants — for people just above the aid cutoff
items.who: Working individuals and families (veterans and civilians alike) who are employed, live just above the poverty line, and are ineligible for most conventional social assistance. A one-time emergency expense must be threatening their stability.
items.value: One-time grants typically in the several-hundred to ~$1,000+ range, paid directly to the creditor, to cover a single emergency expense — a car repair, a medical bill, a security deposit, a utility shutoff.
items.how: Apply at modestneeds.org. Applications are publicly visible to donors (personal identifying details redacted) and funded by donor votes, so the process takes weeks, not days.
items.hack: This is explicitly designed for the gap that catches working veterans: you earn too much for SSVF or TANF but one $900 transmission repair puts you on the street. It is not a fast program — do not use it for an eviction filed next week — but it is one of the very few sources that funds the 'too rich for welfare, too poor for a crisis' band. Pair it with a faster same-week source like AER or the VFW for the urgent part.
items.deadline: Rolling; funding cycle typically takes several weeks.

items.title: PenFed Foundation — emergency grants and veteran entrepreneur investment
items.who: Active duty, veterans, and military families. Specific programs have their own eligibility; you do NOT need to be a PenFed Credit Union member for most assistance programs.
items.value: Military Heroes Fund emergency financial assistance grants for service members and veterans in crisis; the Veteran Entrepreneur Investment Program (VEIP) which provides capital and mentorship to veteran-owned businesses; and Dream Makers, which provides matching down-payment grants (historically up to $5,000) for first-time homebuyers who are service members, veterans or military family.
items.how: Apply at penfedfoundation.org. Dream Makers requires you to be working with an approved lender and to meet income limits.
items.hack: Dream Makers is the sleeper: it is a grant, not a loan, it stacks on top of a VA home loan (so you can use a zero-down VA loan and still take the $5,000 for closing costs), and it is available through many lenders, not only PenFed. Most veterans using a VA loan never learn that a separate down-payment/closing-cost grant exists on top of it.
items.deadline: Rolling; Dream Makers funding is annual and can be exhausted.

items.title: Disabled American Veterans (DAV) — free claims representation and free rides to VA
items.who: All veterans. You do not need to be a DAV member, and you do not need to be disabled, to use a DAV National Service Officer.
items.value: Free VA-accredited claims representation by National Service Officers (themselves disabled veterans) in every state — filing, evidence development, appeals, and representation before the Board of Veterans' Appeals. Free DAV Transportation Network rides to VA medical appointments. Also disaster relief grants and an employment program.
items.how: Find a National Service Officer at dav.org or through your regional VA office. Appointments are free and there is never a fee or a percentage taken from your award. The Transportation Network is coordinated through VA medical center Voluntary Service offices.
items.hack: The free ride program is the most concretely valuable and least-publicized DAV service — for a rural veteran, a 120-mile round trip to a VA medical center is the actual barrier to care, and DAV runs a fleet of vans that does it for free. On claims: a DAV NSO does the exact same work a 'claim consultant' charges you five figures for, and does it for $0, because charging a fee for an initial VA claim is prohibited by law (38 U.S.C. 5901).
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Wounded Warrior Project Independence Program
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans and service members with moderate-to-severe brain injury, spinal cord injury, or neurological conditions that limit independence in daily living. Notably, the qualifying diagnosis does NOT have to be service-connected.
items.value: All at no cost: comprehensive needs assessment and goal setting, ongoing case management, supplemental home health care, alternative therapies (art, music, equine), stress management training, long-term care planning and financial/estate planning, and virtual wellness workshops. Caregiver support includes Operation Family Caregiver, respite care, Red Cross peer networks, and therapy connections.
items.how: Apply at woundedwarriorproject.org. Registration with WWP is free; the Independence Program requires a needs assessment to determine eligibility.
items.hack: The non-service-connected clause is the surprise: a post-9/11 veteran with a severe TBI from a civilian car accident can qualify. Most veterans self-screen out assuming VA-style service-connection rules apply. Also, the long-term care and estate planning component is genuinely valuable professional service that families with a catastrophically injured member otherwise pay an attorney several thousand dollars for.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: WWP Warriors to Work and Financial Readiness
items.who: Registered WWP Alumni — post-9/11 veterans and service members who incurred a physical or mental injury, illness or wound during or as a result of military service, and their family support members. Registration is free.
items.value: Warriors to Work provides free career counseling, resume support, interview preparation and employer connections. Financial Readiness provides free budgeting and debt counseling. Career and VA Benefits Counseling includes free VA-accredited benefits assistance. Also Project Odyssey (multi-day mental wellness retreats, free including travel), Soldier Ride (adaptive cycling events), and adaptive sports.
items.how: Register as a WWP Alumni at woundedwarriorproject.org, which unlocks all program access, then request the specific program.
items.hack: Register even if you do not need anything right now — registration is the gate on every WWP program including the free retreats, and it takes ten minutes. The distinction worth understanding: WWP is primarily a services organization, not a cash-grant organization. If you are looking for a check to pay rent, go to Operation Homefront, USA Cares, the VFW or your service relief society instead. If you want free career coaching, therapy-adjacent retreats and adaptive sports, WWP is genuinely well funded for those.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Gary Sinise Foundation — R.I.S.E. smart homes and emergency support
items.who: Severely wounded veterans and first responders. The R.I.S.E. (Restoring Independence Supporting Empowerment) program targets catastrophically injured service members — multiple amputations, severe burns, paralysis.
items.value: R.I.S.E. builds custom specially-adapted smart homes at no cost to the recipient, and also provides adapted vehicles, mobility devices and home modifications for those who do not need a full new home. The foundation also runs Relief and Resiliency emergency grants, Soaring Valor (WWII veteran travel), and Serving Heroes meal programs.
items.how: Apply through garysinisefoundation.org. Home programs require documentation of the qualifying injury and a lengthy vetting process.
items.hack: The under-used part is not the headline home builds (which serve a small number of people per year) but the smaller R.I.S.E. tier: adapted vehicles, track chairs, and specific home modifications for veterans who already own a home. That queue is shorter and the criteria are wider than the full-home program, and many veterans only ever hear about the homes.
items.deadline: Rolling; home builds have multi-year waitlists.

items.title: Tunnel to Towers Smart Home Program
items.org: Stephen Siller Tunnel to Towers Foundation
items.who: Catastrophically injured service members injured in the line of duty — typically quadruple/triple/double amputees, those with severe spinal cord injury and paralysis, or comparable catastrophic injuries.
items.value: A mortgage-free, custom-built or heavily adapted smart home with automation for lighting, climate, doors, security and appliances controlled from a tablet or voice — plus, for many recipients, an associated scholarship component for their children. Home values commonly run $500,000 to $800,000+.
items.how: Apply at t2t.org under the Smart Home Program. Requires documentation of the catastrophic line-of-duty injury and a formal application and vetting process.
items.hack: T2T is one of the largest and best-capitalized veteran charities in the country and is building at high volume — it is worth applying even if you assume the list is full. Check the separate programs too: the Fallen First Responder Home Program and Gold Star Family Home Program pay off the MORTGAGE on a home a family already owns (rather than building a new one), which is a different and much larger pipeline. T2T also runs a Homeless Veteran Program with case management, veterans villages and HUD-VASH partnership.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Tunnel to Towers Gold Star and Fallen First Responder mortgage payoff
items.org: Stephen Siller Tunnel to Towers Foundation
items.who: Gold Star families — surviving spouses with young children of service members killed in the line of duty — and families of first responders who died in the line of duty. The Let Us Do Good Village also houses eligible Gold Star and catastrophically injured families.
items.value: T2T pays off the family's existing mortgage in full, or provides a mortgage-free home. For a typical family this is $250,000-$500,000+ of debt erased in a single action.
items.how: Apply at t2t.org under the relevant program's eligibility requirements page.
items.hack: This is materially different from the Smart Home program and has a much wider pipeline: you do not need a new adapted house, you need your existing mortgage eliminated. Surviving spouses frequently only hear about the catastrophic-injury smart homes and never learn the payoff program exists. It also stacks with VA benefits — paying off the mortgage does not affect DIC, the Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance program, or home loan entitlement.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Homes For Our Troops — specially adapted custom homes, mortgage-free
items.who: Veterans injured in the Iraq/Afghanistan theater post-9/11/2001, who are retired or retiring from military service, with multiple limb amputations, partial or full paralysis, and/or severe traumatic brain injury. You must first hold a VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant letter of eligibility (or an SHA grant for loss of use of both hands) before HFOT will release an application.
items.value: A newly constructed, specially adapted custom home donated mortgage-free. HFOT also provides financial planning assistance and a peer support network after move-in. Homes are routinely valued well above $500,000 including the adaptations.
items.how: Submit an online inquiry at hfotusa.org/inquiry/. HFOT contacts you within 7 business days. You must accept the responsibilities of ownership — maintenance, property taxes, insurance and utilities are yours.
items.hack: The gating item is the VA SAH grant letter of eligibility, so file for SAH FIRST — that VA application is what unlocks the HFOT application. Many eligible veterans stall for a year because they inquire with HFOT before starting the VA paperwork. Also note you can use the VA SAH grant money itself (worth roughly $100k+ in FY2026, indexed annually) on a different property if HFOT is not a fit — the two are separate benefits and the SAH grant is yours regardless.
items.deadline: Rolling; build queues run multiple years.

items.title: Military Warriors Support Foundation Homes4WoundedHeroes
items.who: Combat-wounded veterans (Purple Heart recipients prioritized), or unmarried Gold Star spouses of a veteran killed in action. Must be honorably discharged or within 90 days of separation, and must NOT currently hold a mortgage. Must intend to occupy the home as a primary residence.
items.value: A mortgage-free home plus three years of family and financial mentoring. Homes are donated by corporate partners (banks, homebuilders) across many states.
items.how: Apply at militarywarriors.org/main-programs/h4wh. Available properties are listed by city on the site — you apply for a specific home, not for a generic place in a queue.
items.hack: Because you apply to specific listed properties, your odds depend enormously on geographic flexibility. A Purple Heart recipient willing to move to whichever city has an available home has a dramatically better chance than one waiting for a house in their current metro. The 'no current mortgage' rule is strict — do not buy a house while waiting. The three years of mandatory financial mentoring is a real obligation, not a formality.
items.deadline: Rolling, keyed to specific available properties.

items.title: Building Homes for Heroes
items.who: Severely injured post-9/11 veterans and their families — catastrophic physical injuries, severe TBI, and in some cases severe PTSD.
items.value: Mortgage-free homes, either newly built/renovated and adapted or purchased and gifted, plus home modifications for veterans who already own. Also provides financial planning and family support services after the gift.
items.how: Apply at buildinghomesforheroes.org. Requires documentation of the service-connected injury and a formal vetting process.
items.hack: Building Homes for Heroes has historically accepted severe PTSD as a qualifying condition in some cases, which is broader than HFOT (which requires amputation, paralysis or severe TBI plus a VA SAH letter). If you were screened out of HFOT for not qualifying for an SAH grant, this is the next application to file rather than the end of the road. Apply to all of the home organizations in parallel — they do not coordinate waitlists and there is no penalty for multiple applications.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Purple Heart Homes — modifications and housing for service-connected disabled veterans of ALL eras
items.who: Service-connected disabled veterans of all eras — explicitly including Vietnam and Korea era veterans, not just post-9/11. Programs include Veterans Aging in Place (VAIP) and Operation Veterans Home Renovation.
items.value: Home modifications for accessibility and safety (ramps, roll-in showers, widened doorways, grab bars, roof and system repairs) at no cost, and in some cases assistance acquiring a home.
items.how: Apply at purplehearthomes.org. Delivery is chapter-based, so availability depends on whether there is an active chapter in your region.
items.hack: This is the organization to go to when you are an older, non-catastrophically-injured disabled veteran — the demographic every headline-grabbing home charity excludes. A 74-year-old Vietnam veteran with a 40% rating who needs a wheelchair ramp and a walk-in shower is exactly the target, and is precisely the person who assumes 'those programs are for the Iraq guys.' Combine with the VA's Home Improvements and Structural Alterations (HISA) grant, which is a separate VA benefit that also pays for accessibility modifications.
items.deadline: Rolling; availability varies by chapter region.

items.title: Operation FINALLY HOME
items.who: Wounded, ill and injured veterans and the surviving spouses of the fallen. Covers a range of service-connected injuries including amputation, paralysis, severe TBI and PTSD.
items.value: Mortgage-free, custom-built homes and home modifications, built in partnership with homebuilders, developers and corporate sponsors across many states.
items.how: Apply at operationfinallyhome.org. Applications are typically tied to specific announced builds in specific communities.
items.hack: Like Military Warriors, availability is geographically driven by where a builder has donated a lot. Watch the organization's announced upcoming builds and apply when one is announced near a place you would be willing to live, rather than submitting a general application and waiting. Surviving spouse eligibility is often overlooked here.
items.deadline: Rolling, tied to announced builds.

items.title: Fisher House — free lodging next to military and VA hospitals
items.who: Families of hospitalized service members and veterans receiving treatment at a military medical center or VA medical center with a Fisher House on or near the campus. Veterans themselves may stay in some VA Fisher Houses while receiving outpatient treatment.
items.value: A private suite with a shared kitchen, laundry and common areas, at NO COST, for the duration of the patient's treatment. Fisher Houses have saved military and veteran families hundreds of millions of dollars in lodging costs. For a family whose veteran is in a 90-day rehab program, this is easily $10,000-$15,000 of hotel cost avoided.
items.how: You do not apply to Fisher House directly. Ask the hospital's social worker, case manager or patient advocate to refer you to the Fisher House manager at that facility. Referrals are made by the treating hospital.
items.hack: The referral comes from the hospital, which means your leverage is the social worker — ask for a Fisher House referral on day one of an admission, before the family has already booked a hotel, because rooms allocate on a rolling basis. If the Fisher House is full, that is exactly when you ask about Hotels for Heroes, which puts families in donated hotel rooms specifically when a Fisher House cannot accommodate them. And for the travel itself, ask about Hero Miles.
items.deadline: Request at admission; rooms allocate on a rolling first-come basis.

items.title: Hero Miles — free round-trip airfare for wounded warriors and their families
items.who: Wounded, injured and ill active-duty service members (including activated Guard and Reserve) undergoing treatment at authorized medical centers, and their family members traveling to visit them. Also families attending a dignified transfer of remains for service members killed in post-9/11 operations.
items.value: Round-trip airfare including taxes and fees, funded by donated frequent-flyer miles. Families cover only baggage fees.
items.how: Requests are submitted by the service member's caseworker, social work staff or casualty assistance officer at the medical center — not by the family directly.
items.hack: Because the request must come from a staff member, the failure mode is that nobody on the care team mentions it. Name it explicitly: ask the case manager to submit a Hero Miles request. Pair it with Hotels for Heroes (lodging when the Fisher House is full) and you can get a family flown in and housed for a multi-week hospitalization at zero cost.
items.deadline: Request as early in the treatment episode as possible.

items.title: Cohen Veterans Network — free mental health care with NO VA rating and ANY discharge status
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans REGARDLESS OF DISCHARGE STATUS, active duty with a TRICARE referral, National Guard and Reserve, and military family members (spouses, children, parents, siblings, caregivers). Pre-9/11 veterans are assessed individually based on clinician availability.
items.value: Evidence-based outpatient mental health treatment — PTSD, depression, anxiety, anger, grief, adjustment, couples and family therapy, child therapy. As of 2026 the network runs 23 clinics across 22 states plus Washington D.C., with five additional clinics opening on U.S. military bases in Asia. Telehealth available. Cost is never a barrier: uninsured clients may receive care at no cost.
items.how: Call 844-336-4226 or find a clinic at cohenveteransnetwork.org/clinics-intro. No VA enrollment, no VA rating, and no referral required for veterans.
items.hack: This is the single most important resource for veterans with a bad-paper discharge. If you have an Other Than Honorable discharge and the VA has denied you healthcare, CVN will still treat you, for free, immediately — no discharge upgrade required first. It is also the fastest route for FAMILY members, who are largely locked out of VA mental health care entirely. And there is no wait for a VA rating decision: you can be in therapy next week rather than in eighteen months.
items.deadline: None; ongoing intake.

items.title: The Headstrong Project — free, confidential, no-cost-to-you trauma therapy
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve, and in many locations their family members. Generally accepts all discharge statuses.
items.value: Free individual trauma-focused therapy with vetted civilian clinicians. Headstrong pays the provider directly, so there is no bill, no copay, and no insurance claim. Critically, treatment is CONFIDENTIAL and is not reported to the VA or DoD.
items.how: Apply at getheadstrong.org. Intake connects you to a clinician in their network, in person or via telehealth.
items.hack: The confidentiality is the point and is why this exists alongside the VA. A service member still on active duty, or a veteran holding a security clearance, who will not walk into behavioral health because of career consequences, can get real trauma treatment here with no record entering their military or VA file. That is a genuinely different product from VA care, and it is free. There is also no requirement to have a service-connected rating or to prove the trauma was combat-related.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Home Base — free intensive clinical program for PTSD and TBI
items.org: Home Base (Massachusetts General Hospital and the Boston Red Sox Foundation)
items.who: Veterans and service members of all eras and all discharge statuses, and their families. The Intensive Clinical Program accepts veterans nationwide, not just New England residents.
items.value: The Intensive Clinical Program delivers roughly two weeks of condensed, evidence-based treatment for PTSD, TBI, anxiety, depression and substance use — the equivalent of about a year of weekly outpatient therapy. Treatment, travel and lodging are provided at no cost to the veteran and a family member. Delivered through Mass General, a top-ranked academic medical center.
items.how: Call or apply at homebase.org. Intake includes a clinical screening to confirm the intensive format is appropriate.
items.hack: 'Free travel and lodging, nationwide' is the part veterans do not believe. You do not have to live in Boston — Home Base flies people in and houses them for the two-week program. Two weeks of Mass General-level intensive PTSD treatment would cost tens of thousands of dollars privately. It also accepts all eras and all discharge statuses, so Vietnam veterans and bad-paper veterans are both eligible.
items.deadline: Rolling; cohorts scheduled throughout the year.

items.title: Mission 22 — free treatment programs and veteran suicide prevention
items.who: Veterans, service members and military families of all eras. No VA rating required.
items.value: Free access to its Recovery and Resilience Program — a structured, self-paced digital program covering PTSD, TBI, moral injury, sleep, relationships and substance use — plus referrals to in-person treatment, peer support and family programming.
items.how: Enroll at mission22.com. The digital program is free and requires no clinical referral.
items.hack: The self-paced digital program is the low-friction on-ramp for a veteran who will absolutely not sit in a therapist's office yet. It is free, private, and requires no diagnosis, no rating and no intake interview — which makes it the right thing to send someone who has been refusing help. Use it as a bridge to Cohen Clinics or Headstrong, not a substitute for clinical care in a crisis.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Team Red, White & Blue — free physical and social connection chapters
items.who: Veterans, service members and civilian supporters. Free membership, open to everyone.
items.value: Free membership in a nationwide network of chapters running regular group workouts, runs, hikes, social events and service projects. Also runs Eagle Expeditions — multi-day outdoor experiences — and leadership development programming.
items.how: Join free at teamrwb.org and find your local chapter; most activity is coordinated through chapter apps and social channels.
items.hack: Team RWB's real product is not fitness, it is the replacement for the unit you lost. Isolation is the mechanism behind most post-service decline, and this is the cheapest and fastest intervention available — it costs nothing, requires no diagnosis, and you can show up to a Saturday workout this week. It is also a de facto professional network: chapters are full of veterans who are now hiring managers.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Team Rubicon — disaster response deployments that reuse your military skills
items.who: Veterans, service members, first responders and civilians. Free to join and free to deploy.
items.value: Free training (chainsaw operations, heavy equipment, incident command/ICS, sawyer, WFR) and free deployment to domestic and international disaster response operations. Team Rubicon covers travel and lodging on operations. Credentials earned (ICS certifications, heavy equipment operation, chainsaw) are real, transferable and resume-relevant.
items.how: Sign up at teamrubiconusa.org, complete onboarding, then volunteer for operations as they are announced.
items.hack: The free certifications are the underrated asset — ICS-100/200/700/800, sawyer and heavy equipment training are the kind of credentials that cost money elsewhere and open doors in emergency management, utilities and municipal work. Team Rubicon also restores the two things veterans actually miss (mission and team) in a way that no therapy program replicates, which is why it functions as informal mental health infrastructure.
items.deadline: Rolling; operations announced as disasters occur.

items.title: The Mission Continues — service fellowships and platoons
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans. Platoons are open broadly; fellowships have a competitive application.
items.value: Service Platoons are free local squads doing sustained community service projects in underserved neighborhoods. Fellowships place veterans in a 6-month structured service commitment with a nonprofit, historically with a modest living stipend, building civilian professional experience and references.
items.how: Apply at missioncontinues.org. Platoons require no application; fellowships are competitive with defined cycles.
items.hack: The fellowship is effectively a resume-repair mechanism for a veteran with a gap in employment — six months of documented civilian nonprofit work with a supervisor who will serve as a reference, which is exactly what a hiring manager wants to see instead of a blank year. Verify the current stipend amount and fellowship cycle dates directly, as these have changed over time.
items.deadline: Fellowships run in defined application cycles; platoons are rolling.

items.title: K9s For Warriors — free service dog, all eras, 18-24 month wait
items.who: Veterans of ALL eras with a clinically diagnosed PTSD, traumatic brain injury, or military sexual trauma, and a service-connected disability (the condition does not have to be combat-related). Serves all 50 states, Puerto Rico and Guam. You cannot bring your own dog — they do not train owned pets.
items.value: A fully trained service dog plus a three-week residential training program at no cost — on-site housing, meals, daily training, on-campus veterinary care and all equipment included. A comparably trained PTSD service dog costs $20,000-$50,000 on the open market. Training sites are Ponte Vedra, Florida and the Warrior Ranch in Helotes, Texas.
items.how: Apply at k9sforwarriors.org. Requires the application, a primary care physician's report documenting the clinical diagnosis, DD-214 Member Copy 4 with signature, an 'Agreement to Support' form with two support contacts, two reference letters, a full-length ID photo, a background check and a phone interview. Travel to training is your only potential cost, and outside resources may help.
items.hack: Current wait is 18-24 months, so apply the day you decide you want one rather than when you are in crisis — the application itself costs nothing and the clock only runs once you are in the queue. Note 'all eras': Vietnam veterans are eligible and routinely assume these programs are post-9/11 only. Also note MST is explicitly a qualifying condition, which is rare among service dog organizations.
items.deadline: Rolling; 18-24 month wait after acceptance.

items.title: America's VetDogs — free guide, service and PTSD dogs including for hearing loss
items.org: America's VetDogs (affiliate of the Guide Dog Foundation)
items.who: Veterans and active-duty service members of all eras with physical disabilities, vision loss, hearing loss, seizure disorders, or PTSD. Also serves active-duty personnel and first responders.
items.value: A fully trained guide dog, service dog, hearing dog, seizure response dog or PTSD service dog, plus training, at no cost — including transportation to campus and room and board during the two-week training class on Long Island, NY. Lifetime follow-up support included. Market value $50,000+ per dog.
items.how: Apply at vetdogs.org. Requires medical documentation of the qualifying disability and a functional home visit or interview.
items.hack: VetDogs covers disability types most PTSD-focused organizations do not — hearing loss and seizure disorders in particular. A veteran with severe service-connected hearing loss almost never thinks 'service dog,' but a hearing dog is a legitimate, free, life-changing accommodation. They also pay for your travel to training, which K9s For Warriors does not.
items.deadline: Rolling; multi-month to multi-year wait depending on dog type.

items.title: Warrior Canine Connection — mission-based trauma recovery through dog training
items.who: Service members and veterans with PTSD, TBI and related conditions, primarily at partner military and VA medical facilities.
items.value: A therapeutic model where the veteran TRAINS a future service dog rather than receiving one — the training itself is the clinical intervention, building emotional regulation, patience and social re-engagement. Free to participants. Separately, trained service dogs are placed with veterans at no cost.
items.how: Participate through a partner site (Walter Reed, various VA medical centers and community locations) or apply for a placement at warriorcanineconnection.org.
items.hack: The distinction matters: if you want a dog, the wait is years everywhere. If you want the therapeutic benefit now, the training program gets you working with dogs immediately with no waitlist, and the clinical evidence behind mission-based trauma recovery is real. Ask your VA facility whether it hosts a WCC program — many do and never advertise it.
items.deadline: Rolling; placement waitlists are long, training participation often is not.

items.title: Paws for Purple Hearts
items.who: Veterans and service members with PTSD, TBI and mobility impairments, served at campuses co-located with VA and military facilities in several states.
items.value: Free Canine Assisted Warrior Therapy (training service dogs as a therapeutic intervention) and free placement of trained mobility and psychiatric service dogs.
items.how: Apply at pawsforpurplehearts.org; availability is tied to their campus locations.
items.hack: Like Warrior Canine Connection, the therapy-through-training track has far shorter access than the dog-placement track. If you live near one of their campuses, you can start participating in weeks. Apply to K9s For Warriors, America's VetDogs, Warrior Canine Connection and Paws for Purple Hearts simultaneously — these organizations do not share waitlists and multiple applications are normal and expected.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: VA-accredited representatives are FREE — and charging for an initial claim is illegal
items.org: VA Office of General Counsel / VSOs (DAV, VFW, American Legion, PVA, AMVETS, MOPH, county VSOs)
items.who: Every veteran filing any VA claim. No membership, no fee, no income test.
items.value: A VA-accredited Veterans Service Officer files your claim, develops your evidence, tracks it, and represents you through appeals — for $0. County and state VSOs do the same. Under 38 U.S.C. 5901, NO ONE may lawfully charge a fee for preparing or presenting an INITIAL VA claim, including accredited attorneys and agents. Fees only become lawful after a decision has been issued and an appeal or supplemental claim is filed, and accredited attorneys are generally capped in the 20-33% range on past-due benefits, subject to VA review.
items.how: Find an accredited representative in the VA's official OGC accreditation search at va.gov (search by name or organization) or go to your county Veterans Service Office. Appoint them with VA Form 21-22 (organization) or 21-22a (individual).
items.hack: Verify accreditation in the VA's own database before you sign anything. If a company is not in that database, it is not accredited, and if it is asking for a percentage of your retro on a first-time claim, it is doing something Congress has made unlawful. County VSOs are the most underrated resource in the entire system — they are government employees whose entire job is your claim, they carry small caseloads compared to national organizations, and they are free.
items.deadline: Appoint a representative before you file, not after a denial.

items.title: Claim sharks — what they charge, and why the GUARD Act fight matters
items.org: Congress / VA / MOAA and VSO coalition
items.who: Any veteran approached by an unaccredited 'claim consultant,' 'VA claims coach' or 'medical evidence' company.
items.value: Knowing the math saves you five figures. Unaccredited consultants typically charge a contingency of roughly 3 to 5 times your monthly increase, or flat fees for 'nexus letters' and consultations. MOAA's 2026 advocacy documented that a veteran taken from 0% to 100% can face charges approaching $20,000 for work an accredited VSO does for free.
items.how: Refuse any fee arrangement on an initial claim. Use the VA OGC accreditation search to verify anyone who asks for money. Report unaccredited fee-charging to the VA OGC and your state attorney general — there have already been state enforcement actions, including a Texas prosecution of Vet Claims Insiders.
items.hack: The current legal gap is the whole business model: 38 U.S.C. 5901 makes it unlawful to charge for an initial claim, but the criminal penalty was stripped out decades ago, so enforcement is thin. The GUARD VA Benefits Act (H.R. 1732 in the 119th Congress) would restore criminal penalties; as of early 2026 it was still pending, not law. Until it passes, your protection is not the statute — it is simply never signing. There is no service a consultant provides that an accredited VSO, a law school veterans clinic, or NVLSP does not provide for free.
items.deadline: Ongoing; GUARD Act pending as of 2026.

items.title: Stateside Legal — free legal self-help and referral for military and veterans
items.who: Service members, veterans and their families. Free, nationwide, no income test to use the materials.
items.value: Free plain-language legal guides and interactive form-building tools covering VA benefits, discharge upgrades, UCX unemployment, SCRA protections, USERRA reemployment rights, consumer debt, family law, foreclosure and eviction — plus a searchable directory that routes you to free legal aid in your state.
items.how: Use the guides and the Find Legal Help directory at statesidelegal.org.
items.hack: This is the right first stop for anything legal because it tells you which of the free options actually handles your problem before you spend weeks on the wrong one. Its SCRA and USERRA material is particularly strong — USERRA reemployment rights (your civilian employer must take you back after mobilization, with the seniority and pension accrual you would have earned) are routinely violated and almost never enforced because nobody knows the right to enforce them exists.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: NVLSP Lawyers Serving Warriors — free national pro bono representation
items.who: Veterans nationwide with VA benefits claims, appeals, discharge upgrades, and military records corrections. Prioritizes complex cases and those with significant retroactive benefits at stake.
items.value: Free representation by volunteer attorneys from major law firms, coordinated by NVLSP. No fee, no percentage of your award. NVLSP also litigates class actions that have recovered billions in benefits for groups of veterans, and publishes the Veterans Benefits Manual that practitioners rely on.
items.how: Apply at nvlsp.org under Lawyers Serving Warriors. Cases are screened for fit and capacity.
items.hack: Go here for the cases that are too complex for a VSO and too unprofitable for a private attorney — discharge upgrades based on PTSD/TBI/MST, correction of military records, and long-running appeals. NVLSP also drove the major class actions on things like disability severance pay tax refunds and improper discharges, so if your situation resembles a known systemic error, they are the organization most likely to already have a case running that you can join.
items.deadline: Rolling; case acceptance depends on volunteer capacity.

items.title: The Veterans Consortium Pro Bono Program — free counsel at the CAVC
items.org: The Veterans Consortium Pro Bono Program
items.who: Veterans and family members who have appealed a Board of Veterans' Appeals decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC) and are unrepresented. Also runs discharge upgrade and guardianship/fiduciary assistance programs.
items.value: Free legal representation at the CAVC — the federal court that reviews BVA decisions — where roughly three-quarters of appealed cases result in some relief. Also free discharge upgrade help and a legal helpline.
items.how: When you receive a Notice of Appeal acknowledgment from the CAVC, the Consortium is notified and will contact unrepresented appellants. You can also apply directly at vetsprobono.org.
items.hack: Filing the Notice of Appeal to the CAVC yourself is easy and free and starts a 120-day clock from the BVA decision — and once you file, free counsel becomes available to you that was not available at the Board level. Veterans routinely give up after a BVA denial without realizing that the next step is a real Article I court with a high remand rate and free lawyers waiting. Do not miss the 120-day deadline; it is jurisdictional and generally cannot be waived.
items.deadline: Notice of Appeal to CAVC must be filed within 120 days of the BVA decision.

items.title: Law school veterans clinics — free representation by supervised students
items.org: Various law schools (Yale, Harvard, Stetson, John Marshall, Widener, Chicago-Kent and 40+ others)
items.who: Veterans, typically within the clinic's geographic region, with VA benefits claims, appeals, discharge upgrades and records corrections. Most have no income test.
items.value: Free, intensive representation by law students supervised by faculty attorneys. Because clinics carry tiny caseloads (often a handful of clients per student per semester), a veteran gets vastly more attorney hours per case than any other free option. Several clinics — notably Yale's Veterans Legal Services Clinic — have litigated landmark cases on discharge upgrades and PTSD.
items.how: Search for a clinic near you through statesidelegal.org's directory, the ABA's veterans legal services resources, or by contacting law schools in your state directly.
items.hack: This is the best-quality free legal help available to veterans, and it is invisible because law schools do not market. Clinics specifically want difficult, precedent-setting cases — a complicated discharge upgrade based on undiagnosed PTSD is exactly what a clinic director is looking for, whereas an overloaded VSO may not have the hours. Apply near the start of a semester when clinics take new cases.
items.deadline: Clinics typically take new cases at the start of each academic semester.

items.title: ABA Veterans Legal Services and state bar veterans clinics
items.org: American Bar Association / state and local bar associations
items.who: Veterans and military families. Most state bar veterans programs have no income test for a free consultation; ongoing representation may.
items.value: Free legal consultations and referrals through ABA-coordinated programs and state bar veterans committees. Many state bars run recurring free legal clinics at VA medical centers, stand-downs and armories, covering VA benefits, family law, consumer debt, landlord-tenant, expungement and estate planning.
items.how: Start with the ABA's Veterans Legal Services directory or call your STATE bar association and ask for its veterans legal assistance program. Also check whether your VA medical center hosts a Medical-Legal Partnership — many do, placing free attorneys inside the hospital.
items.hack: The VA Medical-Legal Partnership is the hidden one: dozens of VA medical centers host free legal clinics on site, because unresolved legal problems (eviction, child support, benefits denial) are a leading driver of veteran homelessness and suicide. Ask your VA social worker whether your facility has an MLP. You can get a lawyer at the same building as your appointment, for free, with no separate application.
items.deadline: Clinic schedules vary; many are monthly.

items.title: National Veterans Wheelchair Games — free, VA-run, largest adaptive sports event in the world
items.org: Department of Veterans Affairs and Paralyzed Veterans of America
items.who: Veterans with spinal cord injuries, neurological conditions, amputations or other mobility impairments who use a wheelchair for sports competition, and who are eligible for VA health care.
items.value: A week of competition across roughly 20 adaptive sports. Registration is free and VA typically covers or heavily subsidizes travel, lodging and meals through the veteran's sponsoring VA medical center. For a first-time participant this is a fully funded week that reliably changes people's trajectory.
items.how: Register at wheelchairgames.org. For 2026 the event ran July 9-14 with registration opening February 2, 2026. Contact NVWGInfo@va.gov. Your VA medical center's Recreation Therapy service sponsors your attendance — that is who you talk to first.
items.hack: The entry point is your VA medical center's recreation therapist, not the national website. They control the sponsorship funding that pays for your travel, and they have slots that go unused every single year because nobody asks. Ask in the fall for the following summer. VA runs a whole circuit of these: Winter Sports Clinic, Golf Clinic, Golden Age Games, Creative Arts Festival and TEE Tournament — the same recreation therapist can sponsor you for any of them.
items.deadline: Registration typically opens in February for a July event; confirm current year dates at wheelchairgames.org.

items.title: National Disabled Veterans Winter Sports Clinic — free adaptive skiing in Snowmass
items.org: Department of Veterans Affairs and Disabled American Veterans
items.who: Veterans with traumatic brain injury, spinal cord injury, orthopedic amputation, visual impairment, or certain neurological conditions, who are eligible for VA health care.
items.value: A week of adaptive alpine and Nordic skiing, snowmobiling, scuba, rock climbing and other winter sports in Snowmass, Colorado. Instruction, adaptive equipment, lodging and meals are provided. Commonly described as 'Miracles on a Mountainside.'
items.how: The 2027 clinic runs March 27 – April 3 in Snowmass, CO, with the application window opening August 1, 2026. Contact wintersportsclinic@va.gov or (970) 263-5040. Apply through your VA medical center.
items.hack: The application window opens roughly seven months before the event and fills — August 1, 2026 for the spring 2027 clinic. Put it on a calendar now. This is the clinic with the strongest reputation among newly disabled veterans specifically because it is early-rehabilitation-friendly: they will get a recently paralyzed veteran onto a mountain within a year of injury, which does more for outlook than months of outpatient therapy.
items.deadline: Application window opens August 1, 2026 for the March 27 – April 3, 2027 clinic.

items.title: National Veterans Golden Age Games — free senior sports competition
items.who: Veterans age 55 and older who are enrolled in VA health care. Competition is stratified by age group, so a 90-year-old competes against peers.
items.value: A week of competition in swimming, cycling, bowling, track and field, pickleball, shuffleboard, air rifle and more. It is the only national multi-sport competition specifically for older veterans, and it doubles as a health-promotion program. The 2027 games run June 23-29.
items.how: Qualify and register through your VA medical center's Recreation Therapy service. Contact GoldenAgeGames@va.gov.
items.hack: This is the most demographically mismatched program in the VA system — it is designed for the Vietnam and Korea generation, who are also the veterans least likely to be plugged into VA recreation services. If you have a father or grandfather enrolled in VA health care who has gotten sedentary and isolated, this is the single highest-leverage thing to sign him up for, and the VA medical center will fund the trip.
items.deadline: 2027 games June 23-29; registration dates announced through VA medical centers.

items.title: National Veterans Creative Arts Festival — free, and you compete from home
items.org: Department of Veterans Affairs and the American Legion Auxiliary
items.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care who participate in creative arts therapy at a VA facility. Competition categories cover art, creative writing, dance, drama and music.
items.value: A national juried competition; first-place winners are flown to the national festival with travel, lodging and meals covered, to perform or exhibit. For the 2027 cycle, the competition submission window is February 1 – March 15, with winners announced in June 2027.
items.how: Enter through your VA medical center's creative arts therapy or recreation therapy program. Contact amy.kimbler@va.gov.
items.hack: Unlike the sports events, you compete by SUBMISSION, not by traveling — so a veteran with severe mobility limitations, agoraphobia or no travel budget can enter from home and only travels if they win (in which case VA pays). It is also the most accessible entry point into VA recreation services for veterans who will not do sports, and creative arts therapy itself is a covered VA service most enrollees never ask about.
items.deadline: 2027 submission window: February 1 – March 15, 2027.

items.title: National Disabled Veterans Golf Clinic and TEE Tournament
items.who: Veterans with visual impairments, amputations, spinal cord injuries, TBI and other disabilities who are eligible for VA health care.
items.value: A week of adaptive golf instruction and competition plus other adaptive sports, with instruction, adaptive equipment, lodging and meals provided. The 2026 Golf Clinic ran September 13-18 in Iowa City, IA; the application window was January 26 – March 20, 2026.
items.how: Apply through your VA medical center. Contact nicholas.beelner@va.gov or (319) 358-5963.
items.hack: The application window closes roughly six months before the event — March for a September clinic. The TEE (Training, Exposure, Experience) Tournament is a separate event with its own window. These smaller clinics are far less competitive to get into than the Wheelchair Games, so a first-timer's odds are much better here.
items.deadline: 2026 window was January 26 – March 20; confirm 2027 dates with your VA medical center.

items.title: National Veterans Summer Sports Clinic — relaunching 2027
items.who: Veterans with disabilities eligible for VA health care. Historically targeted at recently injured veterans, with surfing, kayaking, sailing, cycling and track.
items.value: A week of introductory adaptive water and summer sports with instruction, equipment, lodging and meals covered. VA lists this as a new program launching in 2027 with details to be determined.
items.how: Watch department.va.gov/veteran-sports for 2027 details. Contact David.Tostenrude@va.gov. Apply through your VA medical center's Recreation Therapy service.
items.hack: Because it is relaunching, the 2027 inaugural cohort will have far less competition for slots than established clinics. Get your recreation therapist to flag you now, before the application process is publicized.
items.deadline: 2027 launch; details to be announced.

items.title: Project Healing Waters Fly Fishing — free gear, instruction and trips, weekly and local
items.who: Disabled active military service personnel and disabled veterans. Broad eligibility — physical or psychological disability, any era, and you do not need a specific rating percentage.
items.value: Free fly fishing and fly tying instruction, free equipment (rods, reels, vises, materials — commonly $500-$1,000 of gear per participant), and free fully outfitted fishing trips. Delivered through 200+ local programs, most meeting at VA medical centers, Warrior Transition Units and community sites, year-round.
items.how: Find a local program at projecthealingwaters.org and just show up. There is typically no formal application and no cost.
items.hack: The genius of this one is the cadence: it is a WEEKLY local meeting, not a once-a-year retreat. Recovery and connection come from showing up regularly, and almost every other recreation program is a single event you attend and then go home from. Most programs meet inside VA medical centers, so it is also the easiest possible on-ramp for a veteran already coming in for appointments. Ask your VA recreation therapist or check the site for your nearest program.
items.deadline: Rolling; local programs meet year-round.

items.title: Warriors and Quiet Waters — free Montana fly fishing expeditions
items.who: Post-9/11 combat veterans and service members with combat-related physical or psychological injuries, and in some programs their partners/spouses.
items.value: A multi-day, fully funded fly fishing expedition in Bozeman, Montana — travel, lodging, meals, guides, gear and clothing all provided at no cost. Also runs couples/partner programs recognizing that the spouse is also carrying the injury.
items.how: Apply at warriorsandquietwaters.org. Selection is competitive and cohort-based.
items.hack: The partner programming is the differentiator. Most retreat organizations treat the veteran as the patient; WQW explicitly funds the spouse to attend, which addresses the relationship damage that actually drives post-service collapse. If you are a combat veteran whose marriage is the thing under strain, apply to the couples cohort specifically.
items.deadline: Cohort-based with application cycles through the year.

items.title: Higher Ground — free therapeutic adaptive recreation camps
