items.who: Veterans and service members with TBI, PTSD and physical disabilities, and their family members. Serves all eras.
items.value: Free multi-day therapeutic recreation camps combining adaptive sports (skiing, cycling, rafting, climbing) with structured clinical curriculum on sleep, anger, relationships and reintegration. Travel, lodging, meals and instruction are covered. Family camps include spouses and children.
items.how: Apply at highergroundusa.org. Programs run out of Sun Valley, Idaho and partner locations.
items.hack: Higher Ground is more clinically structured than most 'veteran retreat' organizations — the recreation is the delivery vehicle for an actual curriculum with follow-up, not just a free trip. That makes it a better fit if you want measurable change rather than a good week. The family camp option is rare and valuable: it treats the household rather than the individual.
items.deadline: Rolling application, cohort-scheduled.

items.title: Outward Bound for Veterans — free wilderness expeditions
items.who: Veterans and service members of all eras, including Guard and Reserve. No disability rating required and no requirement to have deployed.
items.value: Free multi-day wilderness expeditions — backpacking, mountaineering, canoeing, sailing, dogsledding — with course tuition fully funded by donors. Participants typically cover only their own travel to the course start point, and scholarships for travel are often available.
items.how: Apply at outwardbound.org/veterans. Courses run nationwide throughout the year.
items.hack: No rating and no deployment requirement is the key detail — this is open to essentially any veteran, which makes it one of the few high-quality free experiences available to someone with a clean record and no service-connected disability who is nonetheless struggling with the transition. Courses are also expressly designed around team interdependence, which is the specific thing veterans report missing.
items.deadline: Rolling; courses scheduled year-round with earlier application for summer slots.

items.title: Sierra Club Military Outdoors
items.who: Service members, veterans and military families. Open eligibility, no rating required.
items.value: Free outings — backpacking, rafting, climbing, camping — organized nationally and through local Sierra Club chapters, with gear and transportation often provided. Also advocates for veteran access to public lands.
items.how: Find trips and contacts at sierraclub.org/military-outdoors, or contact your local Sierra Club chapter's military outdoors coordinator.
items.hack: Because it runs through the existing Sierra Club chapter network, availability is much denser than a single-campus organization — there is probably a chapter within driving distance of you. It also has no application, no vetting and no disability requirement, so it is the lowest-friction outdoor option on this list. Pair it with your free lifetime Military/Veteran America the Beautiful pass and the cost of getting outdoors goes to essentially zero.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: WWP Soldier Ride — free multi-day adaptive cycling events
items.who: Registered WWP Alumni — post-9/11 wounded, ill or injured veterans and service members. Registration with WWP is free.
items.value: Free multi-day adaptive cycling events. WWP provides the adaptive bicycle (handcycles, recumbents, tandems for visually impaired riders), travel, lodging and meals at no cost. The point is not the ride, it is a structured peer cohort experience.
items.how: Register as a WWP Alumni at woundedwarriorproject.org, then apply for a specific Soldier Ride event on the events calendar.
items.hack: WWP will fit and provide an adaptive bike you could not otherwise access — a handcycle runs $3,000-$8,000 retail. Even if you never ride again, going through the fitting tells you exactly which adaptive equipment works for your body, which is information you can then take to VA Prosthetics, who may issue you one. Use the free event as an equipment trial.
items.deadline: Rolling; specific events have registration windows.

items.title: SSVF — rapid rehousing and homelessness prevention money, paid to your landlord
items.org: VA-funded community grantees (Supportive Services for Veteran Families)
items.who: Very low-income veteran families who are homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness. Discharge requirements are broader than for most VA benefits — many SSVF grantees serve veterans with other-than-honorable discharges. Income limits are keyed to area median income.
items.value: Temporary financial assistance paid directly to third parties: security deposits, first month's rent, rental arrears to stop an eviction, utility deposits and arrears, moving costs, emergency housing, transportation, and child care. Plus case management, help obtaining VA benefits, and legal referrals.
items.how: Call the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at 877-424-3838 (free, confidential, 24/7) and ask for your nearest SSVF grantee. You can also find the SSVF Provider Intake List at department.va.gov/homeless.
items.hack: Call BEFORE you are homeless — 'imminent risk' qualifies you, and prevention money (paying your arrears so you never lose the apartment) is far easier to get and far more effective than rehousing money after an eviction. Most veterans wait until they are already out. Also, SSVF is administered by local nonprofits with real discretion, so if one grantee says no, another in the same metro may say yes. And the broad discharge eligibility means bad-paper veterans who were denied VA healthcare can still get SSVF.
items.deadline: Rolling; call at imminent risk, not after eviction.

items.title: VA Grant and Per Diem (GPD) — transitional housing beds
items.org: VA-funded community providers (Grant and Per Diem program)
items.who: Homeless veterans. Like SSVF, GPD providers often serve veterans with discharge statuses that would bar them from other VA benefits.
items.value: Funded transitional housing beds with supportive services — case management, employment services, substance use and mental health treatment linkage — at community provider sites nationwide, at no cost to the veteran. Includes Bridge Housing, Low Demand, Hospital to Housing, Clinical Treatment and Service-Intensive Transitional Housing models.
items.how: Call 877-424-3838 or contact the Homeless Veterans Program / HPACT coordinator at your nearest VA medical center.
items.hack: The 'Low Demand' model is the one to know about: it accepts veterans who are actively using substances and would be turned away from abstinence-required shelters. For a veteran in active addiction, that is the difference between a bed and the street. Ask specifically for a Low Demand or Bridge Housing GPD bed rather than a generic shelter referral.
items.deadline: Rolling; bed availability varies locally.

items.title: U.S.VETS — the largest veteran-specific homeless services nonprofit
items.who: Homeless and at-risk veterans and their families. Serves veterans regardless of discharge status at most sites.
items.value: Transitional and permanent supportive housing, career and employment services, mental health and substance use counseling, and outreach — operating residential sites across roughly a dozen states and territories, serving tens of thousands of veterans annually.
items.how: Find a site at usvets.org and contact it directly, or get referred through the VA at 877-424-3838.
items.hack: U.S.VETS pairs housing with an actual employment services arm on the same campus, which is unusual — most housing programs hand you a bed and a referral list. If you are trying to get back to self-sufficiency rather than just off the street, a provider that does both under one roof materially shortens the path. Availability is site-specific, so relocating to a city with a U.S.VETS campus is sometimes the fastest route to stability.
items.deadline: Rolling; site-specific availability.

items.title: Volunteers of America — veteran housing and reentry services
items.who: Homeless and at-risk veterans, including justice-involved veterans reentering from incarceration. Serves veterans with a wide range of discharge statuses.
items.value: Transitional and permanent supportive housing, SSVF-funded rapid rehousing in many markets, employment services, substance use treatment, and reentry services for justice-involved veterans.
items.how: Find your local affiliate at voa.org. Many VOA affiliates are also SSVF grantees, so contacting VOA and calling 877-424-3838 may lead to the same place.
items.hack: VOA is one of the few large providers with genuine depth in JUSTICE-INVOLVED veterans — a population that is disproportionately veteran, disproportionately bad-paper, and excluded from most veteran charities. If you or someone you know is coming out of incarceration, VOA plus the VA's Veterans Justice Outreach (VJO) specialist at your nearest VA medical center is the correct pairing. Also ask about Veterans Treatment Courts, which exist in most states and can divert charges entirely.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Veterans Inc. — New England's largest veteran services provider
items.who: Veterans and their families, primarily across the six New England states, with some programs nationally. Serves veterans regardless of discharge status.
items.value: Emergency and transitional housing, SSVF rapid rehousing and prevention, food pantry, employment and training services (including HVRP-funded job training), and substance use and mental health support.
items.how: Call Veterans Inc. at their 24/7 assistance line or apply at veteransinc.org.
items.hack: Veterans Inc. runs a Department of Labor HVRP (Homeless Veterans' Reintegration Program) grant, which is a specific funded job-training pipeline for homeless veterans that most people have never heard of. HVRP grantees exist in most states — ask any homeless services provider whether they hold an HVRP grant, because it comes with training dollars attached that a generic case manager cannot access.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Swords to Plowshares — Bay Area services plus national legal and policy work
items.who: Veterans, with direct services concentrated in the San Francisco Bay Area. Its legal and policy work reaches veterans nationally.
items.value: Supportive housing, employment and training, and a nationally respected legal department specializing in discharge upgrades, bad-paper advocacy and VA benefits appeals. Publishes widely used practitioner guidance on 'bad paper' discharges.
items.how: Bay Area services at swords-to-plowshares.org. Their legal self-help and advocacy materials on discharge upgrades are free and useful regardless of where you live.
items.hack: Even outside California, their published guidance on other-than-honorable discharges and character-of-discharge determinations is among the best free material in existence — they largely wrote the playbook that other clinics use. If you are pursuing a discharge upgrade anywhere in the country, read their materials before your first meeting with a representative so you know what evidence to bring.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: SBA VetCert — SDVOSB/VOSB certification moved from VA to SBA in January 2023
items.who: Small businesses at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more veterans (VOSB) or service-disabled veterans (SDVOSB). For SDVOSB you need a VA disability rating — and ANY compensable rating qualifies, including 0% and 10%; there is no minimum percentage.
items.value: Certification unlocks sole-source and set-aside federal contracts. The government-wide SDVOSB prime contracting goal is 3% of federal contract dollars — tens of billions annually. Certification is free to obtain.
items.how: Apply at certifications.sba.gov. You will need SAM.gov registration, your DD-214, your VA rating letter (for SDVOSB), and ownership/control documentation (operating agreement, bylaws, stock ledger). Certification is valid for three years.
items.hack: Two things people get wrong. First: since January 1, 2023 certification runs through SBA, not the VA's old VetBiz/CVE process — self-certification for federal SDVOSB set-asides is no longer valid, and businesses that never migrated lost eligibility. Second: 0% and 10% ratings count. Enormous numbers of veterans with a 10% tinnitus rating do not realize they are service-disabled for SDVOSB purposes and are leaving a federal set-aside channel on the table. Get certified BEFORE you chase contracts — certification takes weeks to months and you cannot bid a set-aside while pending.
items.deadline: Certification valid 3 years; renew before expiration.

items.title: VA's 'Rule of Two' and Vets First contracting preference
items.who: SBA-certified SDVOSBs and VOSBs bidding on VA contracts.
items.value: Under the Veterans First Contracting Program (38 U.S.C. 8127-8128), the VA MUST set aside a contract for SDVOSBs or VOSBs whenever the contracting officer reasonably expects at least two certified veteran-owned firms will bid at a fair and reasonable price — this is the 'Rule of Two,' upheld by the Supreme Court in Kingdomware Technologies v. United States (2016). VA's veteran-owned contracting spend runs into the billions annually and its percentage far exceeds any other agency.
items.how: Get SBA-certified, register in SAM.gov, then target VA opportunities specifically at sam.gov and through VA's Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization.
items.hack: The Rule of Two makes the VA structurally the best federal customer for a veteran-owned firm — the preference is mandatory, not discretionary, and SDVOSBs sit at the TOP of VA's priority order, ahead of VOSBs and every other socioeconomic category. Start with the VA, win past performance there, then expand to agencies where the 3% goal is merely aspirational. Also check your state: dozens of states run their own SDVOSB/VOSB set-aside programs with separate certifications, and state procurement is far less crowded than federal.
items.deadline: Ongoing.

items.title: Boots to Business — free SBA entrepreneurship training (and it is a TAP track)
items.who: Transitioning service members (as the TAP Entrepreneurship track), veterans of all eras, National Guard and Reserve, and military spouses. Free.
items.value: A two-day Introduction to Entrepreneurship course on the installation, plus the follow-on Revenue Readiness online course, delivered free by SBA and its resource partners. Covers opportunity assessment, business model canvas, market research, financials and funding. Directly connects you to VBOC counselors and SBA lenders.
items.how: Register through your installation TAP office (choose the Entrepreneurship track) or at sbavets.force.com / sba.gov/bootstobusiness. Veterans and spouses who are already separated take Boots to Business Reboot, delivered in communities rather than on base.
items.hack: Take the Entrepreneurship TAP track even if you have no intention of starting a business. It costs you two days you are already required to spend in TAP, and it is the only track that gives you a continuing relationship after separation — with a VBOC counselor who will keep advising you for free for years. Spouses can attend too, which is the cheapest business education a military family will ever get. Boots to Business Reboot means missing it while in uniform is recoverable.
items.deadline: Available through TAP before separation; Reboot available indefinitely after.

items.title: Veterans Business Outreach Centers (VBOC) — free lifetime business counseling
items.who: Veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve, and military spouses. Free, no income test, no time limit.
items.value: Free one-on-one business counseling, business plan development, financial projections, market research, mentoring, and help assembling an SBA loan package — for the life of your business. SBA funds a national network of VBOCs covering every state and territory.
items.how: Find your regional VBOC at sba.gov (Veterans Business Outreach Center locator) and request counseling. Also use SCORE mentors and Small Business Development Centers (SBDCs), which are free to everyone.
items.hack: A VBOC counselor will assemble your SBA loan application package with you at no charge — this is exactly the work a loan packager charges $2,500-$7,500 for. Lenders also take a referred, properly-packaged VBOC application more seriously than a cold one. Use the VBOC for the package, SCORE for industry-specific mentorship, and the SBDC for market data, and you have assembled a free advisory board.
items.deadline: None; unlimited free counseling.

items.title: SBA loan fee relief for veterans (SBA Express and 7(a))
items.who: Small businesses at least 51% owned and controlled by veterans, service-disabled veterans, active-duty members participating in TAP, reservists, National Guard members, or current spouses of any of these, or a widowed spouse of a service member who died in service or of a service-connected disability.
items.value: The SBA guaranty fee on SBA Express loans is waived (reduced to zero) for eligible veteran-owned small businesses, historically on loans up to $500,000. On a $350,000 loan that is thousands of dollars saved at closing. SBA Express also offers faster turnaround (36-hour SBA response) and revolving lines of credit.
items.how: Apply through an SBA Express lender and identify the business as veteran-owned; the lender applies the fee relief. Prepare the package with a VBOC counselor first.
items.hack: Fee structures and program authorities change with SBA appropriations and rule updates, so confirm the CURRENT fee relief amount and loan ceiling with your lender or SBA district office before you budget for it — this program has been modified multiple times. Also look at the Military Reservist Economic Injury Disaster Loan (MREIDL), a low-interest loan for a small business that suffers economic injury because an essential employee is called to active duty — almost no employer of a reservist knows it exists.
items.deadline: Verify current fee relief terms with SBA; program terms have changed repeatedly.

items.title: VetFran — franchise fee discounts from 600+ franchise brands
items.who: Honorably discharged veterans; many participating brands extend offers to active duty, Guard, Reserve and military spouses.
items.value: Discounts on initial franchise fees from hundreds of franchise brands — commonly 10-50% off, with some brands waiving the fee entirely for veterans. On a $45,000 franchise fee, that is $4,500-$45,000. Some brands also offer financing assistance and royalty reductions in year one.
items.how: Browse participating brands and offers at vetfran.org, then contact the brand's franchise development team and identify yourself as a VetFran candidate before you begin the process.
items.hack: Identify yourself as a veteran at FIRST CONTACT, before you are deep in the franchise sales process — several brands treat the discount as an incentive to sign, and it is much harder to retroactively apply once you are in the pipeline. Also note the discount is on the initial FRANCHISE FEE only, which is typically a small fraction of the total investment (buildout, equipment, working capital) — do not let a $15,000 discount talk you into a $500,000 commitment. Run it past a VBOC counselor and a franchise attorney first.
items.deadline: Ongoing; individual brand offers change.

items.title: Warrior Rising — free entrepreneurship program with grants up to $20,000
items.who: Veterans and immediate family members of veterans who want to start or grow a business ('vetrepreneurs'). Free.
items.value: Free business education through Warrior University, one-on-one mentorship, and access to business grants reported up to $20,000. Also provides ongoing community and pitch opportunities.
items.how: Apply at warriorrising.org, complete the Warrior University coursework, then become eligible to pitch for grant funding.
items.hack: The grant is gated behind completing the free coursework, which is actually the point — Warrior Rising is screening for follow-through, and the completion rate is low enough that finishing the curriculum meaningfully improves your odds. Treat the coursework as the application. Immediate family member eligibility is also unusual and means a veteran's spouse or adult child can access this even if the veteran does not.
items.deadline: Rolling; grant eligibility follows coursework completion.

items.title: Hivers & Strivers — angel investment for veteran-founded startups
items.who: Early-stage startups founded by graduates of U.S. military academies and, more broadly, veteran founders. Equity investment, not a grant.
items.value: Angel investment rounds historically in the roughly $250,000-$1,000,000 range into veteran-led startups, plus the operational and network value of a veteran-heavy investor base.
items.how: Pitch through hiversandstrivers.com. This is a real venture investor with real diligence — you need traction, a scalable model and a cap table that can absorb equity.
items.hack: Do not confuse this with the grant programs. Angel capital is expensive money that costs you ownership and control forever, and it only makes sense for a business with a genuine path to a large exit. A services business, a franchise or a local shop should take the SBA loan and the Warrior Rising grant instead and keep 100% of the equity. Know which kind of business you have before you pitch.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Task Force Movement — trucking, cybersecurity and healthcare career pipelines
items.who: Veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses seeking placement in trucking/supply chain, cybersecurity or healthcare careers.
items.value: Coordinates employers, training providers and funding (including GI Bill and workforce dollars) into structured pathways into high-demand fields, with an emphasis on getting veterans into CDL and cyber roles quickly.
items.how: Check taskforcemovement.org for current pathway programs and partner employers.
items.hack: The trucking pathway matters because a CDL is one of the fastest credential-to-income conversions available — weeks of training to a $60,000-$90,000 job — and the VA will pay for CDL training under the GI Bill, which most veterans do not realize because they think the GI Bill is only for degrees. The GI Bill covers licensing and certification tests and many non-college degree programs. Verify current TFM program status directly, as this is a coalition initiative whose active pathways change.
items.deadline: Varies by pathway; verify current programs.

items.title: VA Adaptive Sports Grant Program — how to find the funded programs near you
items.org: Department of Veterans Affairs, National Veterans Sports Programs and Special Events
items.who: The grants go to ORGANIZATIONS, not individuals — but the point for a veteran is that these grantees deliver free adaptive sports programming to disabled veterans and service members in your community.
items.value: VA awards grants annually to national, regional and community organizations to expand adaptive sports for veterans and service members with disabilities. For the veteran, this translates into free or heavily subsidized local adaptive skiing, cycling, rowing, climbing, equestrian and team sports programs.
items.how: Ask your VA medical center's Recreation Therapy service which adaptive sports grantees operate in your area, or review VA's published list of current grant recipients at department.va.gov/veteran-sports.
items.hack: Do not apply for the grant — find the grantees. The published recipient list is effectively a directory of vetted, VA-funded, free adaptive sports programs near you, and almost nobody reads it that way. It is the fastest route from 'I want to try adaptive sports' to an actual local program, and it is far denser than the handful of national events.
items.deadline: Grantee programs run year-round; grant cycle is annual for organizations.

items.title: VA Highly Rural Transportation Grants — free rides to VA care in remote counties
items.who: Veterans living in 'highly rural' counties (fewer than seven people per square mile). Grants go to state veterans agencies and veterans service organizations that then provide free transportation.
items.value: Free transportation to VA and VA-authorized medical appointments for veterans in the most remote counties in the country, where a medical appointment can be a 200-mile round trip and the absence of a ride is the actual barrier to care.
items.how: Contact your VA medical center's Veterans Transportation Service or your state department of veterans affairs and ask whether a Highly Rural Transportation Grant operates in your county. Also ask about the Veterans Transportation Service (VTS) and the DAV Transportation Network, which cover non-highly-rural areas.
items.hack: Stack the three transportation options — VTS (VA-operated), the DAV van network (volunteer-driven), and the Highly Rural grant program — because coverage is patchy and different programs run on different days and routes. Separately, if you travel for VA care you may be eligible for Beneficiary Travel mileage reimbursement, which is a cash benefit paid per mile that a large share of eligible veterans never claim.
items.deadline: Ongoing where grantees operate.

items.title: VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) and Special Home Adaptation (SHA) grants
items.who: Veterans and service members with specific severe service-connected disabilities — loss or loss of use of limbs, blindness with loss of use of a limb, severe burns, certain respiratory injuries (SAH); and blindness in both eyes, loss of use of both hands, or severe burns (SHA).
items.value: SAH grants (worth well over $100,000 in FY2026, indexed annually) and SHA grants (a smaller amount, also indexed) to build, buy or modify a home for accessibility. Veterans can use the grant across multiple properties over their lifetime up to the aggregate cap, and there is also a Temporary Residence Adaptation (TRA) grant for modifying a family member's home you are living in temporarily.
items.how: Apply with VA Form 26-4555 at va.gov. You can apply online and a VA Loan Guaranty agent is assigned to you.
items.hack: File for SAH even if you have no plan to build — the letter of eligibility is the prerequisite that unlocks Homes For Our Troops and several other adapted-home charities, and it takes months to obtain. Also, the separate Home Improvements and Structural Alterations (HISA) grant is a DIFFERENT and much more widely available benefit for medically necessary home modifications, available for both service-connected and (at a lower amount) non-service-connected conditions — most veterans who need a grab bar and a roll-in shower qualify for HISA and never hear of it.
items.deadline: No application deadline; grant amounts adjust annually each October.

items.title: LIHEAP and utility assistance — plus Operation Round-Up and Salvation Army
items.org: HHS LIHEAP / electric cooperatives / The Salvation Army
items.who: Low-income households including veterans. LIHEAP eligibility is set by each state, typically keyed to a percentage of the federal poverty level or state median income.
items.value: LIHEAP pays heating and cooling bills and funds crisis assistance for shutoffs, plus weatherization in many states — typically a few hundred to over a thousand dollars per year depending on the state and household. Operation Round-Up (run by many rural electric cooperatives, which round up members' bills to the next dollar) makes small emergency grants for utilities, rent and medical costs. The Salvation Army provides utility assistance, rent assistance, food and emergency shelter.
items.how: Apply for LIHEAP through your state or local community action agency; find yours at acf.hhs.gov/ocs/programs/liheap. Ask your electric cooperative whether it runs Operation Round-Up. Contact your local Salvation Army corps directly.
items.hack: LIHEAP funds are appropriated annually and many states exhaust them within weeks of the application window opening — apply the day the window opens, usually in the fall, not in January when you are cold. Most states also hold back a separate 'crisis' pot available year-round for shutoff notices, so being denied for regular LIHEAP does not mean you are denied for crisis assistance. Ask explicitly for the crisis program.
items.deadline: LIHEAP application windows typically open in autumn and funds are exhausted quickly; crisis funds often available year-round.

items.title: 211 — the single phone number that finds local assistance
items.who: Anyone. Free, confidential, available 24/7 in most of the U.S. and Canada.
items.value: A live specialist who searches a curated local database for rent assistance, utility help, food pantries, free clinics, legal aid, childcare subsidies, transportation and veteran-specific programs in your specific county — including small church and community funds that have no website and appear in no national directory.
items.how: Dial 211, text your ZIP code to 898-211 in many areas, or search 211.org.
items.hack: 211 finds the money that national search cannot: small local funds, single-parish emergency assistance, county-level veteran relief funds. Many states also have a statutory County Veterans Service Officer AND a separate county veterans relief/assistance fund (Wisconsin, Michigan, Ohio, Washington and others) that makes direct emergency grants to veterans and is essentially invisible online. Ask 211 specifically for the county veterans relief fund, not just 'help for veterans.'
items.deadline: None; 24/7.

items.title: Lowe's — 10% military discount, year-round, no annual cap
items.who: Active duty, veterans (any discharge except dishonorable), retirees, reservists, National Guard, NOAA and Public Health Service members, and their immediate family members. Each person needs their own account, including spouses.
items.value: 10% off most purchases, every day, with NO annual cap — this is the key difference from Home Depot. Verified members also get free Silver Key status in Lowe's Rewards, which includes free standard shipping and faster reward earning.
items.how: Enroll in MyLowe's Rewards and verify military eligibility through ID.me at lowes.com/l/military-discount. Once verified it applies automatically in store and online.
items.hack: No annual cap is the entire reason to route a renovation through Lowe's instead of Home Depot — Home Depot caps you at $400 of discount per calendar year, so on a $20,000 kitchen remodel Lowe's saves you roughly $2,000 versus Home Depot's $400. Watch the exclusions though: major appliances and commodity lumber, electrical cable and plywood are excluded, which is where a lot of a renovation budget lives. Buy appliances during a separate military appliance promotion instead.
items.deadline: Ongoing; Lowe's reserves the right to change or cancel the program.

items.title: Home Depot — 10% off but capped at $400 of savings per year
items.who: Active duty, National Guard, reservists, Coast Guard, honorably discharged veterans, and military spouses (spouses must verify with dependent ID and create their own account). Non-married dependents, dishonorably discharged veterans and civilian military employees are NOT eligible.
items.value: 10% off full-priced, non-appliance merchandise, year-round, capped at $400 of total discount per calendar year (the cap resets each January).
items.how: Create a Home Depot account, go to homedepot.com/military/discount or use the app, click Verify Military Status, and verify through SheerID with a military ID, veteran ID card, VA health care card, DD-214, or a driver's license with a veteran designation. In store you must show the live QR code in the app — screenshots do not work.
items.hack: The $400 cap means the discount is fully used up at $4,000 of qualifying spend. Sequence your year: use Home Depot for the first $4,000 and Lowe's (uncapped) for everything after. Exclusions are broad — gift cards, installation services, tool rentals, clearance, most appliances. And a spouse with a separate verified account gets a separate $400 cap, effectively doubling a household's benefit.
items.deadline: Cap resets each calendar year on January 1.

items.title: Free lifetime America the Beautiful pass for veterans and Gold Star families
items.org: National Park Service and five other federal land agencies
items.who: Anyone who served in the U.S. Armed Forces, including National Guard and Reserve — no disability rating, no minimum service, no combat requirement. Also Gold Star Families (next of kin of service members who died in qualifying situations).
items.value: A free Military Lifetime Pass covering entrance fees and standard amenity (day-use) fees at National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management, Bureau of Reclamation, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Forest Service and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers sites. It admits the holder plus everyone in one private vehicle, or the holder plus three adults where per-person fees apply. The paid equivalent annual pass is $80/year — this is free, for life.
items.how: Get it FREE in person at any participating park or federal recreation site by showing a DoD ID card, Veteran Health Identification Card (VHIC), VA-issued Veteran ID Card, or a state driver's license with a veteran designation. Online it costs $7.50 shipping via Recreation.gov (or a free digital pass) or $10 processing via the USGS Store. Gold Star family members present a printed Gold Star Voucher.
items.hack: Get it in person and pay nothing — ordering online adds a shipping or processing fee for the exact same pass. Two more things: camping, tours and concession fees are NOT covered, so budget for those separately. And separately from this federal pass, a majority of states offer free or heavily discounted STATE park passes to resident veterans (often free lifetime for disabled veterans) — check your state's department of natural resources, because state parks are where most people actually camp.
items.deadline: No expiration; lifetime pass.

items.title: Commissary, exchange and MWR access for ALL service-connected veterans — the most underused benefit since 2020
items.org: Defense Commissary Agency, military exchanges, DoD MWR
items.who: Veterans with ANY service-connected disability rating — including 0% and 10% — plus Medal of Honor recipients, Purple Heart recipients, former prisoners of war, and eligible primary family caregivers. Granted by the Purple Heart and Disabled Veterans Equal Access Act of 2018, effective January 1, 2020.
items.value: In-person commissary, exchange and MWR retail privileges, plus online shopping at ShopMyExchange, MyNavyExchange, ShopCGX and the Marine Corps Exchange. Commissaries sell groceries at cost plus a surcharge — typically 20-30% below civilian grocery prices. Exchange purchases are SALES TAX FREE, which is a 6-10% discount on every item in most states, on top of already competitive pricing.
items.how: Present a Veteran Health Identification Card (VHIC) showing 'Service connected,' 'Purple Heart,' 'Medal of Honor,' or 'Former POW.' Without a VHIC, bring a VA service-connected disability letter, a VA caregiver patronage letter, or VA Health Eligibility Center Form H623A. For ONLINE exchange shopping, verify at VetVerify.org — that is a separate process from your VHIC. Note the legislated card fees: 1.43% on credit/signature debit and 0.36% on PIN debit; cash, check, SNAP and eWIC carry no fee.
items.hack: This is the single most valuable and least-claimed benefit for a low-rated veteran. A 10% tinnitus rating pays about $175/month — but it also unlocks tax-free shopping and at-cost groceries for life, which for a family of four is plausibly worth more than the compensation check. Two steps people miss: (1) you need a VHIC, which requires enrolling in VA health care — do that first; (2) online exchange access runs through VetVerify.org and is a separate registration from in-person access. Use PIN debit or cash at the commissary to avoid the 1.43% credit card fee.
items.deadline: Ongoing since January 1, 2020.

items.title: Disney Armed Forces Salute 2026 — and why most veterans do NOT qualify
items.who: ACTIVE or RETIRED members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Space Force, National Guard, Reserves, the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service and NOAA — plus 100% permanently disabled veterans. Ordinary honorably discharged veterans are NOT eligible. You need a valid DEERS/RAPIDS military ID.
items.value: 2026 Walt Disney World: 4-Day Park Hopper $409 + tax, 5-Day $429, 6-Day $449; the Disney Celebrates America Military Salute ticket is $499 (Park Hopper) or $529 (Park Hopper Plus). Disneyland: 1-Day 1-Park $98-$104, 3-Day Park Hopper $314 ($416 with Lightning Lane), 4-Day Park Hopper $369 ($505 with Lightning Lane). Room discounts up to 30% at Deluxe resorts, 25% Moderate, 20% Value. Each eligible member may buy up to 6 tickets.
items.how: Buy through your installation's MWR/ITT ticket office or directly from Disney with military ID. The 2026 offer is valid January 1 – December 18, 2026, with blockout dates March 29 – April 11, 2026 and November 22 – 28, 2026.
items.hack: The eligibility trap is the retiree/veteran distinction — a military RETIREE (20 years, has a DoD ID) qualifies, but a veteran who served four years and got out does NOT, regardless of an honorable discharge. If you are in that second category, look instead at SeaWorld's Waves of Honor (which has historically offered free admission to veterans as well as active duty) and Universal's military ticket offers, which have historically had broader veteran eligibility than Disney. Also: the 6-ticket limit is per eligible member, so a family with two eligible members can bring 12 people.
items.deadline: 2026 offer valid January 1 – December 18, 2026, with blockout dates.

items.title: SeaWorld Waves of Honor and Universal military tickets — better veteran eligibility than Disney
items.org: SeaWorld Parks & Entertainment; Universal Destinations & Experiences
items.who: SeaWorld's Waves of Honor has historically covered active duty, veterans, retirees and dependents. Universal's military offers have historically covered active duty, retirees and, for some promotions, veterans. Verify current-year terms before booking.
items.value: Waves of Honor has historically provided free single-day admission for the service member plus up to three direct dependents at SeaWorld, Busch Gardens, Sesame Place and Aquatica, typically as a once-per-year offer, plus discounted annual passes. Universal Orlando and Hollywood run discounted multi-day military tickets and have offered Freedom Pass style promotions.
items.how: Register and verify at wavesofhonor.com (SeaWorld) and check universalorlando.com/military or your installation's MWR/ITT office for Universal. Verification is typically through ID.me or a similar service.
items.hack: If you are a regular honorably discharged veteran who was shut out of the Disney Armed Forces Salute, start here — SeaWorld's Waves of Honor has historically extended to veterans, not just active duty and retirees, which makes it the best theme park value for the largest group of veterans. Buy Universal tickets through a base ITT office rather than online; ITT pricing often beats the public military rate and ITT offices will sell to eligible veterans.
items.deadline: Offers are annual and terms change each year — verify current eligibility before planning a trip.

items.title: Space-A travel — and the category that opened to 100% disabled veterans
items.who: Active duty, retirees, and their dependents, in a six-category priority system. Critically, veterans with a 100% permanent and total service-connected disability rating became eligible for Space-A travel under the FY2019 NDAA — they travel in Category VI, the lowest priority.
items.value: Free or nearly free seats on military aircraft worldwide. There is no fare; you pay only a small federal inspection fee on some international segments. A CONUS-to-Europe or CONUS-to-Pacific hop that would cost $900-$1,800 commercially costs essentially nothing.
items.how: Register at the passenger terminal of your departure base (most accept email or online sign-up 72 hours in advance), then show up for roll call. Use the AMC Travel page and individual terminal Facebook pages for flight schedules, which change constantly. Priority runs Category I (emergency leave) through Category VI (retirees, 100% P&T disabled veterans, and certain dependents).
items.hack: The 100% P&T eligibility from the FY2019 NDAA is widely unknown among the veterans it covers. The practical technique for low-category travelers: always have a commercial ticket home as a backup, travel with carry-on only, sign up at multiple terminals simultaneously, and treat any specific date as impossible — Space-A rewards flexibility and punishes schedules. Retirees and 100% P&T veterans both sit in Category VI, so you are competing with retirees, and summer PCS season is the worst time to try.
items.deadline: Sign up 72 hours before desired travel; ongoing.

items.title: Armed Forces Vacation Club and Veterans Advantage
items.org: Armed Forces Vacation Club (Travel + Leisure Co.); Veterans Advantage (WeSalute)
items.who: AFVC: active duty, retirees, veterans, Guard, Reserve, DoD civilians and family. Veterans Advantage/WeSalute: veterans, active duty and family members — it is a PAID membership program.
items.value: AFVC offers resort condo stays historically starting around $369 per week for a full unit (not per night) at thousands of resorts worldwide, on a space-available basis. Veterans Advantage (now WeSalute) bundles discounts across travel, retail and services for an annual membership fee.
items.how: Register free at afvclub.com and search available weeks. Veterans Advantage/WeSalute requires a paid annual membership at wesalute.com.
items.hack: AFVC registration is free and there is no obligation — the $369-ish weekly condo rate is genuine but it is space-available inventory, meaning good locations in peak season are rarely there. Check it before booking any vacation; the downside is zero. Veterans Advantage is the opposite: it is a PAID subscription, so do the math on whether you will actually use enough of its partner discounts to beat the fee. Many of its headline benefits (national park pass, home improvement discounts, exchange access) are available to you for free through other channels covered elsewhere on this list.
items.deadline: AFVC inventory is space-available and changes constantly.

items.title: USAA, Navy Federal and PenFed — who can actually join
items.org: USAA; Navy Federal Credit Union; Pentagon Federal Credit Union
items.who: USAA: active duty, Guard, Reserve, veterans who separated with an honorable discharge, precommissioned officers, and their eligible family members (spouses, widows/widowers, and children of USAA members). Navy Federal: all DoD branches active/retired/veteran, DoD civilians and contractors, and family members including grandparents and grandchildren. PenFed: OPEN TO ANYONE — no military affiliation required.
items.value: Materially better rates than most commercial banks on auto loans, mortgages and deposits, plus military-specific features: USAA and Navy Federal both offer early direct deposit of military pay (typically one business day early), and all three understand SCRA benefits, deployment and PCS in a way that a national retail bank does not.
items.how: USAA: usaa.com. Navy Federal: navyfederal.org. PenFed: penfed.org — anyone can join, historically by opening a savings account with a nominal deposit.
items.hack: Two things. First, PenFed is open to everyone, which means you should compare its rates as a baseline even if you qualify for the others. Second, and more valuable: under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, interest on debt you incurred BEFORE entering active duty must be capped at 6%, and USAA and Navy Federal apply it correctly and often proactively — but you must REQUEST it in writing with a copy of your orders, and many servicemembers never do. Also note USAA's family eligibility chains through membership, so joining while you serve preserves eligibility for your children.
items.deadline: USAA eligibility is best established while serving; family eligibility chains from your membership.

items.title: Military and veteran auto insurance — USAA, GEICO and Armed Forces Insurance
items.who: USAA property and casualty eligibility is narrower than its banking eligibility. GEICO offers a military discount to active duty, retirees, Guard and Reserve, and veterans. Armed Forces Insurance serves the military community broadly.
items.value: GEICO advertises a military discount (historically up to 15%) plus additional discounts for emergency deployment. USAA typically prices competitively for the military market and offers a storage/garaging discount when a vehicle is laid up during deployment. Savings of several hundred dollars a year are typical.
items.how: Quote all three plus two or three civilian carriers. Ask specifically about the deployment/storage discount and about state-specific veteran discounts.
items.hack: The deployment storage discount is the one people forget: if your car is garaged and not driven during a deployment, most military-focused insurers will drop you to comprehensive-only coverage for that period, cutting the premium by 60-80%. Nobody applies it automatically — you have to call. Also, do not assume USAA is automatically cheapest; it often is not for drivers with clean records in low-risk states, and the only way to know is to quote it against competitors annually.
items.deadline: Re-shop annually; request deployment discounts before you deploy.

items.title: Car manufacturer military rebates — $500-$1,000+ stacked on top of other incentives
items.org: Ford, General Motors, Toyota, Honda, Nissan, Hyundai, Kia and others
items.who: Varies by manufacturer but typically active duty, Guard, Reserve, retirees, veterans within a defined window of separation (commonly 12-24 months), and often spouses. Some programs (notably Toyota's college/military rebate) require recent separation; others (GM) extend to all veterans.
items.value: Cash rebates historically $500-$1,500 per vehicle depending on manufacturer and model, applied at purchase or lease. These typically STACK on top of advertised consumer incentives, dealer discounts and financing offers.
items.how: Most programs require a verification certificate obtained online before you visit the dealer — through the manufacturer's military site or a verification service like ID.me. Print or save the certificate and present it at signing.
items.hack: Get the certificate BEFORE you negotiate, and do not mention it until the price is final. Negotiate the vehicle price as if the rebate does not exist, agree on an out-the-door number, and only then apply the military rebate — otherwise many dealers quietly absorb it into their discount and you net nothing. Also check whether your manufacturer's window is tied to separation date (Toyota historically) or open to all veterans (GM historically), because that determines whether the clock is running on you.
items.deadline: Manufacturer programs and eligibility windows change frequently — verify current terms before shopping.

items.title: Verizon, T-Mobile and AT&T military plans
items.who: Active duty, veterans, retirees, Guard and Reserve at all three carriers. Verizon and T-Mobile extend their military pricing to veterans; AT&T's military discount has historically applied to active duty, veterans and their families.
items.value: All three carriers run discounted military/veteran versions of their main unlimited plans, typically saving roughly 15-25% off standard multi-line pricing, plus periodic device promotions restricted to military accounts. On a family of four this commonly runs $20-$40/month, or $240-$480/year.
items.how: Verify military or veteran status through the carrier's site — all three use ID.me or a comparable verification service. Existing customers must actively apply the discount; it is not retroactive and it is not automatic.
items.hack: The pricing and plan names at all three carriers change constantly, so quote all three at the moment you are switching rather than relying on any published comparison. The bigger, less obvious move: under the SCRA you can terminate a wireless contract WITHOUT an early termination fee when you receive PCS or deployment orders of 90+ days to a location the carrier does not service, and you can suspend service during deployment at little or no cost. Carriers do not advertise this. Send written notice with a copy of your orders.
items.deadline: Verify and apply the discount manually; not retroactive.

items.title: Amazon, Walmart, Costco, Sam's Club and retail military offers
items.org: Amazon; Walmart; Costco; Sam's Club; various retailers
items.who: Veterans, active duty and military families, with verification typically through ID.me, SheerID or VerifyPass.
items.value: Costco and Sam's Club periodically run military membership promotions that bundle shop cards or gift cards worth $30-$60 with a new membership. Many national retailers offer a standing 10% military discount in store (Michaels, Kohl's on select days, Rack Room, Foot Locker, Bass Pro and others). Amazon and Walmart run recurring military appreciation promotions rather than a standing percentage discount.
items.how: Verify once with ID.me and once with SheerID and VerifyPass — these three services power the large majority of online military verification, and a single verification with each unlocks hundreds of merchants without re-proving your status each time.
items.hack: Doing the three verifications (ID.me, SheerID, VerifyPass) in one sitting is the actual hack — it takes about 30 minutes total and thereafter military pricing appears automatically at checkout across hundreds of sites you would never think to ask. The other thing: always ASK in a physical store even when no discount is advertised, because a large share of local and franchise locations offer an unpublicized military discount at the manager's discretion. And remember the exchange comparison — exchange purchases are sales-tax free, which often beats a 10% retail discount outright.
items.deadline: Promotions are seasonal, concentrated around Memorial Day and Veterans Day.

items.title: Airline military benefits and travel booking
items.who: Active duty primarily, with some benefits extending to veterans and dependents. Baggage waivers are generally tied to active-duty orders.
items.value: Most major U.S. airlines waive checked bag fees for active-duty service members traveling on orders (often for several bags, and frequently for personal travel as well), which is $70-$200 per round trip. Many offer priority boarding for uniformed service members. Priceline and Expedia run military rate channels on hotels, typically 5-15% below public rates.
items.how: Add your military status to your frequent flyer profile so waivers apply automatically. Use the military rate filters on Priceline and Expedia, and compare against direct booking with the hotel's government/military rate.
items.hack: Compare the Priceline/Expedia military rate against the hotel's own GOVERNMENT rate, which is often lower and is frequently available to veterans and retirees traveling on personal business at properties near military installations — you just have to ask for it by name at the front desk or when calling the property directly rather than booking through an aggregator. Also, for active duty, the baggage waiver frequently applies to personal leave travel too, not just travel on orders, but only if the airline knows you are military — put it in your profile.
items.deadline: Ongoing; verify current airline policies, which change.

items.title: Onward to Opportunity — 30+ free industry certifications from Syracuse IVMF
items.org: D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families (IVMF), Syracuse University
items.who: Active-duty service members transitioning within 6 months with an honorable discharge; veterans with 180+ days of service and an honorable discharge; National Guard and Reservists; and military spouses of active duty, veterans or Guard/Reserve members.
items.value: Free training toward 30+ industry certifications. IT and cyber: CompTIA SecurityX, Network+, Security+, A+, Cloud+, Linux+, Server+, Tech+, Project+, CySA+, PenTest+; Cisco CCST (Cybersecurity, Networking, IT Support), CCNA, JavaScript Essentials; ISC2 SSCP; AWS Cloud Practitioner, Solutions Architect Associate, AI Practitioner; Microsoft Azure Fundamentals and Azure AI Fundamentals; Google Professional Cloud Architect; Python Institute PCEP and PCAP; Oracle Java SE8 and Oracle 12c. Business: PMP, CAPM, Six Sigma Green Belt and Yellow Belt, HRCI aPHR, PHR and SPHR. Retail cost of this training plus exams runs $2,000-$6,000+ per certification track.
items.how: Apply at ivmf.syracuse.edu/programs/career-training/. Job placement support is delivered in partnership with Hire Heroes USA.
items.hack: Read the exam fee rule carefully, because it is the trap: O2O covers the TRAINING for everyone eligible, but it covers the certification EXAM FEE only for participants who are currently UNEMPLOYED, plus active-duty members in their final six months. Employed veterans, Guard members, Reservists and military spouses get the training free but must pay their own exam fee (PMP alone is roughly $400-$600). So the optimal sequencing is to complete O2O training and sit the exam either while still on active duty in your last six months, or during a genuine unemployment gap — not after you have started a new job.
items.deadline: Rolling enrollment; exam fee coverage depends on your employment status at the time.

items.title: American Corporate Partners — a free one-year mentor from a Fortune 500 company
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans and active-duty service members nearing separation, and military spouses. Historically requires a minimum period of service (commonly 180 days). Free.
items.value: A year-long, one-on-one mentorship with a professional from one of 100+ participating companies (including major banks, tech firms, defense primes and consultancies), matched to your target industry. Monthly structured conversations on career strategy, resume, networking and negotiation. Also free access to ACP AdvisorNet, an online Q&A platform where veterans get career questions answered by professionals.
items.how: Apply at acp-usa.org. Matching typically takes a few weeks.
items.hack: A year is long enough for the relationship to become a real professional connection rather than a coaching transaction — and the mentor works at a company you want to work for. The highest-value use is not asking for resume edits; it is asking your mentor, around month three, to introduce you to two people in their network and to forward your resume internally. Referred candidates convert at multiples of cold applicants. Also use AdvisorNet immediately even before you are matched, since it requires no waiting.
items.deadline: Rolling; one-year commitment once matched.

items.title: Hire Heroes USA — free career coaching, resumes and a lifetime alumni network
items.who: Transitioning service members, veterans, military spouses and caregivers. Completely free.
items.value: A dedicated volunteer career advisor, professional resume rewriting translated into civilian language, LinkedIn optimization, mock interviews, workshops, a curated job board, and industry connections. Alumni support continues for life — the alumni network exceeds 65,000 veterans. Comparable private career coaching and resume services run $500-$3,000.
items.how: Register at hireheroesusa.org. You are assigned a career advisor who works with you one-on-one until you are placed.
items.hack: Hire Heroes is explicit that it is NOT a placement agency — it gives you tools and connections, not a job. Set expectations accordingly and treat the advisor as a coach you must actively work, not a recruiter who will find you a role. The resume rewrite alone is worth the registration; their writers are specifically trained to convert military experience into the specialized-experience language that both federal HR and corporate ATS systems screen for. Use it together with O2O (which uses Hire Heroes as its placement partner) so the two reinforce each other.
items.deadline: None; lifetime alumni access.

items.title: FourBlock — a semester-long career readiness course with employer site visits
items.who: Transitioning service members, veterans and military spouses. Free. Delivered in cohorts in major metros and virtually.
items.value: A structured multi-week career readiness program run in partnership with universities, combining classroom instruction on career narrative and networking with site visits to partner employers in your city. Free, plus a durable cohort network of local veterans entering the same job market.
items.how: Apply at fourblock.org for a cohort in your metro or the virtual cohort. Cohorts run on a semester schedule.
items.hack: The site visits are the product. Walking into a company's office with a cohort, meeting its veteran employee resource group, and leaving with names is worth more than any number of online applications. Choose the cohort in the city where you intend to LIVE, not where you are currently stationed — FourBlock's value is local network density, and building it in a city you are about to leave wastes the program.
items.deadline: Semester-based cohorts; apply ahead of the term start.

items.title: Microsoft Software & Systems Academy (MSSA) — free technical training with an interview guarantee
items.who: Transitioning service members (typically within 180 days of separation) and, in some cohorts, veterans and spouses. Free.
items.value: A multi-week intensive technical training program in tracks such as cloud application development, server and cloud administration, cybersecurity administration and data analytics — delivered free, with a guaranteed interview with Microsoft or a hiring partner on completion. Historically strong placement rates into roles paying well above the veteran median.
items.how: Apply at military.microsoft.com/mssa. MSSA is a DoD SkillBridge-approved program for eligible active-duty applicants, meaning you can attend while still drawing full military pay.
items.hack: Doing MSSA as a SkillBridge is the whole play: you receive full active-duty pay and benefits while completing free technical training that ends in a guaranteed interview. That is a paid bootcamp with a job interview attached, versus a civilian coding bootcamp costing $15,000-$20,000 with no guarantee. Apply roughly 9-12 months before separation so cohort timing, SkillBridge approval and your 180-day window align.
items.deadline: Cohort-based; apply 9-12 months before separation to align with SkillBridge.

items.title: Amazon, Google and Salesforce veteran programs
items.who: Veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses. Specific programs have their own eligibility.
items.value: Amazon runs a Military Talent program and SkillBridge-approved apprenticeships and fellowships across AWS, operations and corporate roles, and has a large veteran hiring commitment. Google offers free Google Career Certificates (data analytics, IT support, project management, UX, cybersecurity) with scholarships routinely available to veterans and spouses, plus a military skills translator and veteran recruiting channel. Salesforce runs Vetforce, providing free Salesforce training and certification pathways plus a veteran talent community — Salesforce administrator and developer certifications are among the highest-ROI credentials available.
items.how: Amazon: amazon.jobs/military. Google: grow.google/certificates and google.com/about/careers/veterans. Salesforce: vetforce.org (Trailhead-based, free).
items.hack: Vetforce is the sleeper: Salesforce admin certification is a genuine path to $75,000-$110,000 roles, the training on Trailhead is free to anyone, and Vetforce specifically funds veteran and spouse certification vouchers and connects you to a hiring ecosystem of Salesforce partners who are chronically short of certified admins. It requires no degree and no prior technical background. Google Career Certificates are similarly free-to-low-cost for veterans and are recognized by a consortium of employers.
items.deadline: Rolling; scholarship and voucher availability varies.

items.title: RecruitMilitary, Corporate Gray and Orion Talent — veteran job fairs and military recruiting firms
items.who: Veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses. Free to the job seeker — employers pay these firms.
items.value: RecruitMilitary runs the largest network of veteran career fairs (in-person and virtual) plus a job board with millions of registered veterans. Corporate Gray runs military job fairs concentrated around major installations and the DC area and publishes free transition guides. Orion Talent is a military placement firm that recruits junior military officers and technical NCOs into specific client roles, often with structured hiring conferences.
items.how: Register free at recruitmilitary.com, corporategray.com and oriontalent.com. Orion assigns you a recruiter who works your candidacy against specific client openings.
items.hack: Understand the incentive structure: these firms are paid by EMPLOYERS, which means they will push you toward roles their clients are filling, not necessarily the best role for you. That is fine as long as you know it. Orion in particular runs hiring conferences where you interview with six to ten companies in two days — extraordinarily efficient, but heavily weighted toward manufacturing, energy and field operations roles. Use them in parallel with ACP and FourBlock, which have no placement incentive and will give you unbiased advice.
items.deadline: Rolling; job fairs and hiring conferences are scheduled throughout the year.

items.title: Vets2PM — project management certification training for veterans
items.who: Veterans and transitioning service members pursuing PMP, CAPM and related project management credentials. Some offerings are SkillBridge-approved.
items.value: PMP exam preparation and the required 35 contact hours of project management education, with a veteran-specific approach to documenting military experience as qualifying project management experience on the PMP application. PMP holders command a well-documented salary premium; PMI's own salary surveys have consistently shown certified project managers earning materially more than non-certified peers.
items.how: Check vets2pm.com for current SkillBridge and training options. Also compare against free O2O/IVMF PMP training.
items.hack: Before paying anyone for PMP prep, exhaust the free options: O2O offers PMP and CAPM training free, and covers the exam fee if you are unemployed or in your final six months of active duty. The genuinely hard part of PMP for veterans is not the exam — it is documenting 36 months of project experience on the application in language PMI accepts, because military roles do not have civilian project titles. That translation help is what a veteran-specific provider adds. Note that CAPM requires no experience hours and is a legitimate stepping stone if you cannot yet document PMP-qualifying experience.
items.deadline: Rolling; SkillBridge participation requires the usual 180-day window.

items.title: LinkedIn Premium free for one year for veterans
items.who: Veterans and transitioning service members. Historically offered as a free one-year LinkedIn Premium Career subscription, with LinkedIn Learning included.
items.value: One year of LinkedIn Premium (retail roughly $30-$40/month, so $360-$480 of value) including InMail credits to message recruiters directly, visibility into who viewed your profile, applicant ranking against other candidates, salary insights, and unlimited LinkedIn Learning courses.
items.how: Check linkedin.com/help or LinkedIn's military and veteran programs page for the current offer and verification method (historically verified through a military email address or an ID verification partner).
items.hack: Verify the offer is still active before relying on it — LinkedIn has changed the terms and redemption path of this program more than once. If it is available, the highest-value feature is InMail: you can message hiring managers and recruiters directly, bypassing the application pile entirely, and veterans consistently underuse it. Time your redemption for the 12 months when you are actually job searching, not the moment you separate, because the clock starts on redemption.
items.deadline: Verify current availability; redeem when you begin an active job search, not before.

items.title: Veterati mentorship — STATUS UNCERTAIN, verify before relying on it
items.who: Historically: veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses seeking on-demand mentorship calls.
items.value: Historically offered unlimited free mentorship calls with volunteer professionals, booked self-service through a calendar platform — a lower-commitment complement to ACP's year-long matched mentorship.
items.how: Check veterati.com directly for current status before investing time. If it is unavailable, use American Corporate Partners (matched one-year mentorship), ACP AdvisorNet (on-demand Q&A), and Hire Heroes USA (assigned career advisor) as functional replacements.
items.hack: Multiple third-party sources in 2025-2026 describe Veterati as having sunset, and competitor organizations have published 'post-Veterati' migration guidance — but the site itself still presents active service copy, so the signal is genuinely mixed. Treat it as unverified. The practical answer is that ACP plus ACP AdvisorNet covers both the depth (year-long matched mentor) and the breadth (on-demand questions) that Veterati provided, and both are confirmed operating.
items.deadline: Unknown; verify directly.

items.title: Every free certification path for veterans, with what it would otherwise cost
items.org: Multiple (IVMF, Salesforce, Google, CompTIA, VA, DoL)
items.who: Veterans, transitioning service members and in most cases military spouses.
items.value: Free or funded paths and their retail cost: PMP via O2O (retail $500-$2,000 training + $405-$555 exam); CompTIA Security+, Network+, A+ via O2O (retail $400-$1,200 training + $253-$404 per exam); AWS Cloud Practitioner and Solutions Architect via O2O (exam $100-$150); Six Sigma Green Belt via O2O (retail $1,000-$3,000); HRCI aPHR/PHR/SPHR via O2O ($300-$500 exam); Salesforce Administrator via Vetforce/Trailhead (retail $200 exam plus $1,500-$5,000 courses); Google Career Certificates in data analytics, IT support, project management, UX and cybersecurity (retail ~$49/month); Team Rubicon ICS, sawyer and heavy equipment credentials; and CDL, HVAC, welding and IT certifications payable through the GI Bill's licensing and certification benefit.
items.how: Start with O2O at ivmf.syracuse.edu for the broadest catalog, Vetforce at vetforce.org for Salesforce, grow.google/certificates for Google, and va.gov/education for GI Bill licensing and certification reimbursement.
items.hack: The GI Bill licensing and certification benefit is the least-used education benefit in the system: the VA will reimburse you for licensing and certification TESTS — up to $2,000 per test, and taking a test does NOT consume a full month of entitlement the way a semester of school does, it only charges entitlement proportionally. That means you can sit PMP, Security+, a CDL exam and a real estate license exam and barely dent your 36 months. Veterans routinely pay out of pocket for exams while sitting on unused GI Bill entitlement.
items.deadline: GI Bill entitlement generally must be used within applicable delimiting periods; O2O exam fee coverage depends on employment status.

items.title: How to actually find a SkillBridge partner (and create your own)
items.who: Service members within 180 days of separation with command approval.
items.value: Access to 2,000+ authorized organizations, ranging from Fortune 100 companies to small firms, across essentially every industry and geography.
items.how: Use the Partner Program Locator at skillbridge.osd.mil, filterable by state, industry and job family. Cross-reference against the Hiring Our Heroes SkillBridge provider list. Then contact the organization's SkillBridge or military talent point of contact directly — do not apply through their general careers portal, which will not route correctly.
items.hack: Two non-obvious moves. First: a company NOT on the list can become a SkillBridge partner by signing a simple MOU with DoD, so if a company wants to hire you, you can ask them to onboard — it costs them nothing since DoD pays your salary, and companies say yes far more often than veterans expect. Second: target SMALL partners, not the household names. Everyone applies to Amazon and Microsoft SkillBridge; a 200-person defense engineering firm on the list may receive two applications a year and has a much higher probability of converting you to a full-time offer, which is the actual objective.
items.deadline: Begin outreach 9-12 months before separation.

items.title: WWP Project Odyssey and mental wellness programs
items.who: Registered WWP Alumni — post-9/11 veterans and service members with a service-related physical or mental injury, illness or wound. Separate cohorts exist for men, women, couples and veterans with specific experiences including military sexual trauma.
items.value: Project Odyssey is a free multi-day mental wellness retreat combining outdoor challenge activities with clinically informed group curriculum, followed by 90 days of structured follow-up support. Travel, lodging and meals are covered. WWP also funds Warrior Care Network, which provides intensive outpatient PTSD and TBI treatment at four academic medical centers (including Home Base at Mass General, Emory, Rush and UCLA) at no cost including travel.
items.how: Register as a WWP Alumni at woundedwarriorproject.org, then apply for a specific Project Odyssey cohort or request a Warrior Care Network referral.
items.hack: Warrior Care Network is the underpublicized one and it is clinically serious: two to three weeks of intensive, evidence-based PTSD and TBI treatment at a top academic medical center, condensing roughly a year of outpatient therapy, with travel and lodging paid and no cost to you. It is the highest-intensity free mental health treatment available to post-9/11 veterans anywhere. Ask for it by name — a general WWP intake conversation will not necessarily surface it.
items.deadline: Cohort-based; rolling application.

items.title: SGLI to VGLI conversion — the 240-day no-health-questions window
items.org: Department of Veterans Affairs / Office of Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance
items.who: Any service member with SGLI coverage who is separating. SGLI continues free for 120 days after separation.
items.value: You may convert up to your SGLI coverage amount (up to $500,000) to Veterans' Group Life Insurance. If you apply within 240 days of separation, NO health questions are asked and no medical exam is required — you are guaranteed coverage regardless of your health. After 240 days you have up to one year and 120 days total, but you must then prove insurability.
items.how: Apply through the Office of Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance at benefits.va.gov/insurance. Premiums are age-banded and rise as you get older.
items.hack: The 240-day guaranteed-issue window is the most valuable thing in this item, and it matters most for exactly the people who ignore it — veterans with service-connected conditions that make commercial term life expensive or unobtainable. If you are healthy, shop commercial term life, which is usually cheaper than VGLI at younger ages. If you have a significant medical history, convert within 240 days without fail, because VGLI cannot decline you in that window and a commercial insurer absolutely can. Also compare against VA's Veterans Affairs Life Insurance (VALife), a guaranteed-acceptance whole life program for service-connected veterans.
items.deadline: 240 days from separation for guaranteed issue with no health questions; one year and 120 days absolute maximum with proof of insurability.

items.title: Operation Homefront Transitional Homes and Villages
items.who: Wounded, ill and injured post-9/11 service members and veterans and their families, typically while recovering or transitioning. Also runs Permanent Homes for Veterans.
items.value: Rent-free transitional housing (apartments and Villages near major military medical centers) for up to roughly two to three years, paired with financial counseling, budgeting and caseworker support designed to get the family into permanent housing debt-free. Families routinely leave with savings they could not have built while paying market rent.
items.how: Apply at operationhomefront.org. Availability is site-specific and concentrated near major military treatment facilities.
items.hack: This is the program that produces the biggest durable financial change of anything Operation Homefront does, and it is far less known than the emergency grants. Two to three years without a rent payment, with mandatory financial counseling attached, is how a family with $30,000 of debt leaves with a down payment. Apply early in a recovery, not after you have already signed a market lease.
items.deadline: Rolling; availability is site-specific.

items.title: Elizabeth Dole Foundation — the caregiver's organization
items.who: Military and veteran caregivers — the spouses, parents, children and friends caring for a wounded, ill or injured service member or veteran, of ALL eras including Vietnam and Korea.
items.value: Free access to the Hidden Heroes network, respite care initiatives, caregiver peer support, a curated resource campaign connecting caregivers to financial, legal and mental health services, and the Dole Caregiver Fellows leadership program. Also drove the legislation that expanded VA's Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC) to pre-9/11 caregivers.
items.how: Start at elizabethdolefoundation.org and the Hidden Heroes resource hub. Separately, apply for VA's PCAFC at caregiver.va.gov — that is the one that pays a monthly stipend.
items.hack: The real money is the VA's PCAFC, which pays an eligible primary family caregiver a monthly stipend (frequently $1,500-$3,000+ depending on tier and geography), plus health coverage through CHAMPVA for caregivers who lack insurance, plus respite care and travel. PCAFC was expanded to caregivers of veterans of ALL eras, so a spouse caring for a Vietnam veteran can now qualify — an enormous population that still assumes it is post-9/11 only. The Dole Foundation is the best free guide to navigating that application, which has a high denial and appeal rate.
items.deadline: Rolling; PCAFC applications can be appealed if denied.

items.title: Folds of Honor — scholarships for families of the fallen and disabled
items.who: Spouses and children of service members (and, since a 2022 expansion, first responders) who were killed or disabled in service. Disability generally must be service-connected; many awards key to a 10%+ or higher VA rating depending on program year.
items.value: Educational scholarships historically up to $5,000 per year for private K-12 tuition, college, trade school and technical programs. Folds of Honor has awarded well over 50,000 scholarships.
items.how: Apply at foldsofhonor.org during the annual application window, typically opening in the winter and closing in the spring for the following academic year.
items.hack: The disabled-veteran eligibility (not just killed-in-action) is the part families miss — the child of a living veteran with a service-connected disability rating can qualify, which is a vastly larger population than Gold Star families. It also covers K-12 private school tuition, not just college, which almost no veteran education benefit does. And it stacks with the GI Bill, Fry Scholarship and Chapter 35 DEA benefits — it is a private scholarship, so it does not offset VA education entitlement.
items.deadline: Annual application window, typically winter through spring; verify current dates.

items.title: Paralyzed Veterans of America — free accredited advocacy plus architecture and sports
items.who: Veterans with spinal cord injury or disease (including MS and ALS). PVA's accredited service officers, however, represent ANY veteran on a VA claim for free.
items.value: Free VA-accredited claims representation by service officers who specialize in catastrophic disability, free architecture and accessibility consulting for home modifications, an aggressive legal advocacy arm that litigates ADA and accessibility cases, adaptive sports programming, and co-sponsorship of the National Veterans Wheelchair Games.
items.how: Find a PVA National Service Officer at pva.org — most are co-located at VA regional offices and VA spinal cord injury centers.
items.hack: PVA's service officers are widely regarded as the most technically expert in the accredited VSO world on complex, high-rating claims — special monthly compensation, aid and attendance, loss of use determinations, and total disability based on individual unemployability. If you have a catastrophic or complex claim and a general VSO has not gotten it right, PVA is the escalation. And they will represent you for free even if you have no spinal cord injury.
items.deadline: Rolling.

items.title: Travis Manion Foundation — character and leadership programs for veterans and survivors
items.who: Veterans, active duty, and survivors (family members of the fallen). Free.
items.value: Free expeditions, character development and leadership training, and a large mentorship and service community. The Survivor Expedition program specifically serves families of the fallen with funded outdoor and peer experiences. Also runs the national 9/11 Heroes Run series.
items.how: Apply at travismanion.org for expeditions and programs; local chapters run year-round activity.
items.hack: TMF's distinctive feature is that it integrates SURVIVORS and veterans in the same programs rather than siloing them — which addresses a real gap, since surviving family members are usually offered grief services and nothing else. If you are a Gold Star family member who wants purpose and community rather than a support group, this is the organization built for that. Their 'If Not Me, Then Who' mentorship places veterans into schools, which is also a credential-building volunteer experience.
items.deadline: Rolling; expeditions are cohort-based.

items.title: Blue Star Families — spouse employment, support and research
items.who: Military families — active duty, Guard, Reserve, veteran and surviving families. Free membership.
items.value: Free membership providing spouse employment programs and career networking, local chapter events, caregiver and neighborhood support programs, and free or discounted access to museums and cultural institutions through the Blue Star Museums program (free admission at 2,000+ museums for active duty and families, typically Armed Forces Day through Labor Day).
items.how: Join free at bluestarfam.org. Blue Star Museums participation runs each summer; find participating museums through the National Endowment for the Arts.
