items.deadline: Rates change with OPM GS table updates.

items.title: PCAFC reassessments, the 2020-2022 discharges, and the legacy protection through September 30, 2028
items.who: Caregivers in PCAFC, especially legacy participants who entered before the program expanded in October 2020.
items.value: When VA expanded PCAFC to pre-9/11 veterans it also applied new criteria and began reassessing existing participants. Large numbers of legacy families were discharged or downgraded, generating congressional scrutiny and litigation. VA published a final rule extending the legacy transition period through September 30, 2028, under which legacy participants and legacy applicants will not have their stipend decreased during reassessment, with limited exceptions.
items.how: Know your status. Ask the Caregiver Support Line (1-855-260-3274) in writing whether you are classified as a legacy participant or legacy applicant, and get the answer documented.
items.hack: If you are a legacy participant, that classification is worth money and it is worth confirming in writing now rather than discovering after a reassessment that VA has you coded otherwise. Prepare for reassessment the way you would a C&P exam: document the worst days, keep a care log with times and tasks, and have the veteran's treating clinicians put the level of supervision needed into the medical record. Reassessments turn on what the record says, not on what the family says in the interview.
items.deadline: Legacy protections run through September 30, 2028.

items.title: Appealing a PCAFC denial, downgrade or discharge
items.who: Veterans and caregivers who disagree with a PCAFC decision.
items.value: PCAFC decisions are appealable. Because PCAFC is a VHA benefit rather than a VBA benefit, the review path runs through VHA's clinical appeals process and, where applicable, the VHA decision review options — which is different from the VBA supplemental claim and Higher-Level Review lanes most veterans know.
items.how: Request review promptly after the decision letter; the letter states the applicable process and deadline. Call the Caregiver Support Line at 1-855-260-3274 to confirm which review lane applies and to get the claim status — the four stages are Pending Intake, In Queue for Assignment, Assigned and Under Review, and Decision Issued.
items.hack: Do two things on receipt of an adverse decision. One: request the complete record VA relied on, including the assessment worksheets, so you can see which criterion they found unmet — the letters are vague and the worksheets are not. Two: get new clinical evidence that speaks directly to that criterion, from the veteran's treating provider, not a generic letter. And get an accredited representative involved; several VSOs now handle PCAFC appeals specifically because the 2020-2022 discharge wave created the expertise.
items.deadline: Stated in the decision letter — act quickly, the windows are short.

items.title: PCAFC's non-cash benefits — CHAMPVA, travel, counseling, legal and financial planning
items.who: Approved Primary and Secondary Family Caregivers.
items.value: Primary Family Caregivers get: health insurance through CHAMPVA if they have no other coverage; mental health counseling; beneficiary travel benefits when traveling with the veteran to appointments; at least 30 days of respite care per year; and legal and financial planning services. Secondary Family Caregivers get mental health counseling and limited travel benefits. VA also runs the Building Better Caregivers training, a peer support mentoring program, and a virtual psychotherapy program for caregivers.
items.how: Through your local Caregiver Support Program team, or the Caregiver Support Line at 1-855-260-3274.
items.hack: CHAMPVA for the caregiver is the sleeper benefit here — a spouse who left a job to provide care and lost employer coverage gets health insurance out of PCAFC, which is worth more than the stipend in many cases. The legal and financial planning services are also real and almost never used: this is where you get help executing a durable power of attorney, an advance directive and a guardianship plan, which the family will need and which nobody does until there is a crisis.
items.deadline: Respite is an annual allotment.

items.title: PGCSS — the caregiver program with no rating requirement
items.who: Caregivers of veterans enrolled in VA health care who do not meet PCAFC criteria — including caregivers of veterans with no service-connected rating at all.
items.value: The Program of General Caregiver Support Services provides peer support mentoring, caregiver skills training including Building Better Caregivers, a caregiver support line, coaching, and referral to services. There is no stipend and no CHAMPVA, but there is also no 70% rating requirement, no line-of-duty requirement, and no six-month need requirement.
items.how: Call the Caregiver Support Line at 1-855-260-3274 or contact your facility's Caregiver Support Coordinator. The veteran must be enrolled in VA health care.
items.hack: This is where the overwhelming majority of caregivers actually belong, and where the ones denied by PCAFC should land instead of giving up. Enroll in PGCSS, then work the two paths that do carry money: Veteran-Directed Care (no rating requirement, veteran controls a budget and can hire the family member) and, if the veteran is low-income wartime, VA pension with Aid and Attendance. PGCSS plus VDC plus A&A is a real package; PCAFC-or-nothing is how families end up with nothing.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Casualty Assistance Officer — your first military contact, and what to demand from them
items.who: Next of kin and survivors of a service member who dies on active duty.
items.value: A casualty assistance officer (CAO, CACO or casualty assistance representative depending on service) is assigned immediately and serves as the family's primary military point of contact — handling the death gratuity, SGLI, arrangements, the DD-1300, and the initial benefits paperwork. This is a temporary role that ends when the benefits processing is complete.
items.how: The service assigns them; you do not request one. Military OneSource, 800-342-9647, is available 24/7 throughout.
items.hack: Get everything in writing and keep your own file, because the CAO rotates out and the institutional memory goes with them. Specifically demand: multiple certified copies of the death certificate, the DD Form 1300 Report of Casualty, the DD-214 if applicable, and written confirmation of every claim filed and every claim number. Families who rely on the CAO's file rather than their own spend years reconstructing it. Ask explicitly about the Gold Star lapel button and about being transferred to the service's long-term assistance program before the CAO closes the case.
items.deadline: The CAO role is temporary; long-term programs take over after.

items.title: Service long-term survivor programs — the support that lasts after the casualty officer leaves
items.who: Surviving family members after the casualty assistance officer's role ends.
items.value: Each service runs a permanent case management program with dedicated counselors: Army Survivor Outreach Services, 833-313-1960; Navy Long Term Assistance Program, 877-270-2162; Marine Corps Long Term Assistance Program, 866-210-3421 ext. 2; Air Force and Space Force Families Forever, 866-299-0596; Coast Guard Office of Casualty Matters, 571-266-2375. Military OneSource, 800-342-9647, backs all of them 24/7.
items.how: Call the number for your service directly. You do not need a referral and there is no expiration — families reconnect years later.
items.hack: These programs are open-ended, and survivors routinely disconnect in the first year while numb and then have nowhere to go in year three when the benefits problems surface. Reconnect. They handle exactly the things that break later: a DIC problem, an education benefit election that turns out to have been wrong, a change in remarriage status, a child aging into or out of eligibility. Also note the TRICARE cliff — surviving families keep active-duty-rate coverage at no cost for three years, then move to retiree family member rates with premiums. Mark that date on a calendar the day you are told it.
items.deadline: TRICARE active-duty rates for 3 years after the death.

items.title: Gold Star Lapel Button and Next of Kin Lapel Button (DD Form 3)
items.who: The Gold Star Lapel Button goes to next of kin of members who died in qualifying combat-related circumstances. The Next of Kin of Deceased Personnel lapel button goes to next of kin of members who died on active duty in other circumstances. Eligible relations include widows and widowers, parents including step and adoptive parents, children, siblings including half-siblings and, following a policy update, stepsiblings.
items.value: Official recognition and a replaceable emblem, plus it is the document trail that establishes Gold Star status for other programs — installation access policies, the Gold Star Families Memorial programs, and various state benefits and private offers that require proof.
items.how: Apply on DD Form 3, Application for Gold Star Lapel Button, through the service casualty office. Replacements for lost buttons are available through the same channel. The Army processes through HRC.
items.hack: Apply even if you do not intend to wear it, because it is the cleanest proof of status you will have. Families are repeatedly asked to prove Gold Star status for benefits and access programs and find that the DD-1300 alone does not satisfy the requester. And the eligibility list is broader than people assume — siblings and stepsiblings qualify, and siblings almost never apply because nobody tells them they can.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Accrued benefits and substitution — the money families lose when a veteran dies with a claim pending
items.who: Surviving spouse; dependent children including those 18-23 in school; dependent parents. If no eligible relation exists, whoever paid the last illness and burial expenses can be reimbursed.
items.value: Two distinct remedies and families need to know the difference. Accrued benefits (VA Form 21P-601, or 21P-534EZ if filed with DIC, or 21P-535 for parents) pay out benefits that were due and unpaid at death based on the evidence already in the file. Substitution (VA Form 21P-0847) lets the survivor step into the deceased's shoes on a pending claim or appeal and keep litigating it — including submitting new evidence. Substitution is almost always the stronger option, because a claim that was going to be denied on the existing record can still be won with new evidence.
items.how: VA must receive the accrued benefits claim within one year of the beneficiary's death and/or the date of notification. Substitution requests must also be filed within one year of the claimant's death. Priority runs: surviving spouse (full amount), then children in equal shares, then dependent parents.
items.hack: This is real money — often years of retroactive compensation on a claim that was pending at death — and families lose it constantly because nobody tells them the claim survives. File BOTH: request substitution on 21P-0847 AND file the accrued benefits claim, within the one year. Do it even if you are not sure the claim had merit. And if the veteran is currently ill with a pending claim, file the substitution paperwork knowledge into the family's hands now, because the one-year clock starts at death and grieving families do not read VA mail in month eleven.
items.deadline: One year from the beneficiary's death. This deadline is not forgiving.

items.title: Filing the DIC claim — VA Form 21P-534EZ and what to attach
items.who: Surviving spouses, dependent children, and in some cases dependent parents of veterans who died from a service-connected condition or who met the DIC rating-duration rules.
items.value: 21P-534EZ is the combined application for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation, Survivors Pension and accrued benefits — one form covers all three, and VA will consider you for each. It runs under the Fully Developed Claim program, which means submitting complete evidence up front gets it decided faster.
items.how: File 21P-534EZ. Attach the death certificate showing cause of death, the marriage certificate, the veteran's DD-214, birth certificates for dependent children, and any medical evidence linking the cause of death to the service-connected condition. If the veteran had a pending claim at death, file 21P-0847 for substitution at the same time.
items.hack: The cause-of-death link is where DIC is won or lost, and death certificates are written by whoever is on duty, not by anyone thinking about VA. If the immediate cause was pneumonia but the underlying driver was service-connected COPD or ALS, get a physician statement saying the service-connected condition was a contributory cause of death — that is the statutory language and it is a lower bar than principal cause. Also check the DIC rating-duration path: if the veteran was rated totally disabling for 10 continuous years before death, DIC can be payable regardless of what they died of.
items.deadline: No absolute filing deadline for DIC, but file within one year of death to preserve the accrued benefits and substitution rights on the same form.

items.title: Walking into a non-VA emergency room in crisis — what to say, and what it costs
items.who: Veterans as defined in 38 USC 101, and individuals described in 38 USC 1720I — which includes veterans with OTH discharges. Enrollment in VA health care is not required.
items.value: Crisis stabilization care at any VA or non-VA facility, on a Veterans Crisis Line recommendation or by presenting in acute suicidal crisis: up to 30 calendar days of inpatient or crisis residential care and up to 90 calendar days of outpatient care, both extendable when clinically necessary, plus ambulance and air ambulance transport. VA will not charge eligible individuals any costs for that care, at VA or non-VA facilities. If VA cannot confirm eligibility, the individual gets a bill — so confirmation matters.
items.how: Call 988 and press 1, or go to the nearest emergency department. Tell the facility you are a veteran in acute suicidal crisis and that VA should be notified. Notify VA as soon as possible — facilities and veterans are both expected to notify VA promptly so the episode is captured under the authority.
items.hack: Say the words 'veteran' and 'suicidal crisis' at registration, and give them your VA information. The billing problem is almost always an identification problem: the hospital registers you as a commercial or uninsured patient, bills you, and then it takes months to unwind. If a bill arrives anyway, do not pay it and do not ignore it — contact the VA medical center's community care or revenue office and cite emergent suicide care under 38 CFR 17.1200. The regulation says VA will not charge you.
items.deadline: 30 days inpatient / 90 days outpatient per episode, extendable on clinical need. Notify VA promptly.

items.title: inTransition — a DoD mental health coach through any transition, any discharge
items.who: Active duty, National Guard, Reserve, veterans and retirees — regardless of branch, length of service or discharge status. No eligibility verification.
items.value: Free, confidential coaching that keeps mental health care from breaking during a transition — separation, retirement, relocation, deployment, a change in duty status, or moving between providers. Coaches connect you to a new provider, coordinate the handoff and follow up so the continuity does not depend on you making the call while in crisis.
items.how: Call 800-424-7877 in the US, 800-748-81111 from overseas, or email dha.intransition@health.mil.
items.hack: The value is the handoff, which is exactly where people fall out of treatment. If you are separating and currently seeing a military provider, call inTransition before your last appointment, not after — they will get you connected to VA or a civilian provider so there is no gap. And note the eligibility line: no verification, any discharge status. A veteran with bad paper who cannot get into VA can still use this.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Peer support — VA peer specialists and the BeThere peer coaches
items.who: Veterans, service members and military spouses.
items.value: VA employs peer support specialists — veterans in recovery themselves, formally trained and certified — embedded in mental health teams, homeless programs and primary care. Separately, Military OneSource's BeThere program connects you by phone with peer coaches who are veterans, service members or military spouses, 24/7/365, at 800-342-9647.
items.how: Ask your VA mental health team to be connected with a peer support specialist. For BeThere, call 800-342-9647.
items.hack: Ask for a peer specialist by name as a separate request, not as part of a therapy referral — they are a distinct workforce and they get assigned when someone asks. What they do that clinicians cannot: show up, navigate the system alongside you, and tell you what actually happened to them. For veterans who will not engage with a clinician, a peer is often the only bridge that works.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: VA Whole Health and the free Veteran Training self-help portal
items.who: Enrolled veterans; the online training portal is open to anyone.
items.value: Whole Health reorients care around what matters to the veteran rather than only what is wrong with them, and delivers well-being programs — health coaching, peer-led groups, and complementary approaches including yoga, tai chi, meditation, acupuncture and chiropractic care, which VA covers as part of the medical benefits package. Separately, veterantraining.va.gov offers free self-guided tools built on established clinical methods for anger, insomnia, parenting and mood.
items.how: Ask your VA facility for the Whole Health program and a Whole Health coach. The training portal needs no enrollment: veterantraining.va.gov.
items.hack: The concrete, underused piece is the complementary and integrative health coverage — acupuncture, chiropractic, yoga and meditation are covered VA services and veterans pay for them out of pocket in the community because nobody told them. Ask your primary care provider for a referral by name. If your facility does not offer a modality, that is a community care conversation.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Make the Connection — the no-account, no-record resource directory
items.who: Anyone — veterans, family, friends. No enrollment, no login, no record created.
items.value: A VA site built around thousands of first-person video stories from veterans, organized by experience — combat, MST, loss, substance use, transition — paired with a local resource locator that maps VA and community services near a zip code.
items.how: maketheconnection.net.
items.hack: This is the thing to send someone who will not accept help. It creates no record, requires no account, and asks nothing of them. For a veteran whose whole objection is 'I don't want it in my file,' a page of other people describing the same thing is often the only entry point that works. It is also the fastest way for a family member to find what exists near a specific zip code without calling VA.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Vet Center scope — what readjustment counseling actually covers, including bereavement and MST
items.who: Combat veterans, veterans who experienced MST, veterans who provided mortuary services or emergency medical care to casualties, certain drone crews, Vietnam-era veterans, and the families of all of them. Bereavement counseling is available to the families of service members who died on active duty.
items.value: Free counseling with no VA enrollment, no rating requirement, and — importantly — records held separately from the VA medical record. Individual, group, family and couples counseling; MST counseling; bereavement counseling; substance use assessment and referral; employment and benefits referral. Vet Centers do not screen on discharge characterization for counseling.
items.how: Call 877-927-8387 — staffed 24/7 by fellow combat veterans — or walk into a Vet Center. Locate one at va.gov/find-locations with facility type set to Vet Center.
items.hack: Three things almost nobody knows. One: family members can be seen, in their own right, for issues related to the veteran's service — spouses and children get counseling too. Two: bereavement counseling for families of members who died on active duty is available with no connection to any other VA benefit. Three: the record separation is real and it is the reason to use a Vet Center if your concern is a security clearance or a command finding out. Vet Centers are also mobile — Mobile Vet Centers cover rural areas on a scheduled route.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: VA Service Dog Benefit - VA does not buy the dog, it pays for the dog's whole life
items.who: Enrolled veterans whose VA clinician determines a service dog is clinically necessary for a visual, hearing, mobility, or (in limited cases) mental-health impairment.
items.value: VA pays the premiums, copays and deductibles on a comprehensive veterinary health insurance policy for the dog's lifetime: annual wellness visits, immunizations, urgent and emergency care, prescription medication, treatment of chronic illness, and one sedated dental procedure per year. VA also pays for harnesses, leashes and other hardware the dog needs to do its job, and pays travel costs to go get the dog. VA does NOT buy the dog and does not pay for food, treats, OTC meds, grooming, boarding, pet sitting, license tags or non-sedated dental cleanings.
items.how: Ask your VA primary care or mental health provider for a service dog evaluation referral. A VA clinician does a clinical assessment covering the functional goal the dog would serve and your ability to care for an animal. If approved, VA refers you to an accredited provider. The dog MUST come from an organization accredited by Assistance Dogs International (ADI) or the International Guide Dog Federation (IGDF).
items.hack: The accreditation rule is where most veterans lose this benefit. If you already own a dog, or you bought one from an online 'service dog' outfit, or a local trainer certified it, you are NOT eligible - no exceptions, no grandfathering. Before you spend a dollar or accept a dog from anyone, confirm they are on the ADI or IGDF accredited list. Getting the free dog from an accredited org is what unlocks a lifetime of free veterinary care worth far more than the dog.
items.deadline: No deadline - apply any time you are enrolled in VA health care.

items.title: Find an ADI- or IGDF-accredited service dog provider (the gate on every VA dog benefit)
items.org: Assistance Dogs International / International Guide Dog Federation
items.who: Any veteran pursuing a service dog who wants VA to cover the veterinary care.
items.value: A free, searchable public list of every accredited assistance dog program by country, state and dog type (mobility, hearing, guide, PTSD/psychiatric, facility). Accreditation is the exact standard VA uses.
items.how: Search assistancedogsinternational.org member programs by location and dog type, and igdf.org.uk for guide dog schools. Then apply directly to the program - VA does not place you.
items.hack: Accredited programs are free or near-free and have waiting lists measured in years. Non-accredited outfits will sell you a dog in weeks for $15,000-$25,000 - and that dog will never qualify for the VA veterinary benefit. The wait is the price of the benefit.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: PAWS Act pilot - train a service dog at VA as PTSD treatment (five sites, still running)
items.org: VA / PAWS for Veterans Therapy Act
items.who: Veterans with a PTSD diagnosis enrolled at one of the five VA pilot sites, seen by VA primary care or mental health within the last 3 months, and cleared by a VA clinician screening.
items.value: Free 8-week course, roughly 2 hours once a week, in which you help train candidate service dogs. This is therapy, not a dog giveaway - in most cases the dog you train goes to another veteran. The clinical theory is that the altruism and structure raise your sense of purpose and self-worth.
items.how: Ask your VA provider for a PAWS referral. A VA clinician screens you and puts you in the next canine training group.
items.hack: Two things veterans get wrong: (1) you do not leave with the dog, and (2) you do not leave with a trainer certification. Go in for the treatment effect. If you want a dog to keep, that is a separate track - the ADI/IGDF accredited providers below.
items.deadline: Pilot is limited to five VA sites; ask your facility whether it is one of them before you plan around it.

items.title: Canine Companions - free service dogs for veterans, ADI accredited, 45 trained tasks
items.who: Veterans with physical disabilities, and veterans with PTSD. All eras.
items.value: A fully trained service dog at no cost, plus team training and lifetime follow-up support. Dogs are trained in up to 45 tasks including retrieving dropped items, opening doors, pulling a wheelchair, and interrupting nightmares. Canine Companions is ADI accredited, so the dog qualifies for the VA veterinary benefit.
items.how: Apply at canine.org. Veteran-specific contact: Daryl Sager, Veteran Programs Manager, (707) 297-3682, or the main line 1-800-572-BARK (2275).
items.hack: Canine Companions does not publish a wait time, and it varies by dog type and region - ask the veteran programs manager directly for a realistic number before you apply, so you can decide whether to also apply to K9s For Warriors or Patriot PAWS in parallel. Applying to several accredited programs at once is allowed and is what experienced applicants do.
items.deadline: Rolling applications

items.title: Patriot PAWS - free mobility and PTSD service dogs, trained largely by Texas inmates
items.who: Disabled American veterans, with a focus on mobility disabilities and post-traumatic stress.
items.value: A fully trained service dog at no cost. The organization states plainly: 'No Veteran will EVER receive a bill for our services.' Each dog represents 18-24 months of training and more than $45,000 of cost the veteran never sees.
items.how: Apply at patriotpaws.org/applications/. Phone (972) 772-3282, office@patriotpaws.org.
items.hack: Patriot PAWS trains many of its dogs through an inmate training program in Texas correctional facilities, which is why they can produce dogs at volume other programs cannot. Verified operating with a site update dated September 2026.
items.deadline: Rolling applications; expect an 18-24 month pipeline

items.title: Dogs Inc (formerly Southeastern Guide Dogs) - guide and PTSD service dogs, free
items.who: Veterans with vision loss and veterans with PTSD.
items.value: Guide dogs and PTSD service dogs at no cost to the veteran, including training and ongoing support.
items.how: Apply through dogsinc.org. Note the rebrand: guidedogs.org now redirects to dogsinc.org.
items.hack: If you search for 'Southeastern Guide Dogs' you may land on stale third-party pages or dead links. The organization is operating - it changed its name. Confirm current program details and wait times by phone rather than from any aggregator site.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Dogs on Deployment - free pet boarding so you do not surrender your dog for a deployment
items.who: Active duty, Guard, Reserve, veterans and first responders who need temporary pet care because of service obligations, training, deployment, PCS, or emergency.
items.value: Four programs: the Hero Pet Boarding Network (volunteer foster homes that board your pet for the length of your absence at no boarding charge), veterinary assistance grants, Pet PCS relocation assistance, and spay/neuter assistance.
items.how: Register at dogsondeployment.org and post your pet's profile to be matched with a volunteer boarder. Request help through the veterinary, PCS and spay/neuter forms.
items.hack: Start the match early - good boarders get claimed. This is also the answer for a veteran facing a hospitalization or a residential treatment program who would otherwise refuse care because there is nobody to take the dog.
items.deadline: Rolling; match times depend on volunteer availability in your area

items.title: Pets for Patriots - adopt the hardest-to-place shelter pet, get discounted lifetime vet care
items.who: U.S. military veterans of any era and any discharge era, plus spouses of the fallen (Gold Star). This is a companion animal program, not a service dog program.
items.value: Adoption fee support at partner shelters, a discount at a participating veterinarian for the life of the pet, and hardship/hero fund grants for veterinary emergencies. The program deliberately targets the pets nobody adopts - older, larger, special-needs animals.
items.how: Apply at petsforpatriots.org, get approved, then adopt through a partner shelter.
items.hack: This is the right program when you need a companion animal and cannot wait two years for an accredited service dog. It is explicitly NOT a service dog - it will not have public access rights and will not qualify for the VA veterinary benefit. Verified operating with content dated September 2026.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: VA National Veterans Sports Programs - the 2026-27 calendar and how facility sponsorship actually works
items.org: VA National Veterans Sports Programs and Special Events
items.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care who meet each event's disability criteria.
items.value: Confirmed schedule: National Veterans Wheelchair Games, Detroit MI, July 9-14 2026 (registration opened Feb 2, 2026) and Orlando FL, July 14-19 2027. National Disabled Veterans Golf Clinic, Iowa City IA, Sept 13-18 2026 (applications Jan 26 - Mar 20, 2026). National Disabled Veterans Winter Sports Clinic, Snowmass CO, March 27 - April 3 2027 (applications open Aug 1, 2026). National Veterans Golden Age Games, Cleveland OH, June 23-29 2027. National Veterans Creative Arts Festival - competition entries Feb 1 - Mar 15 2027, winners announced June 2027, and only national winners attend. National Veterans Summer Sports Clinic relaunches in 2027.
items.how: Every one of these events runs through a Recreation Therapist or Voluntary Service coordinator at your VA medical center. Call your facility, ask for the Recreation Therapy service, and say you want to be sponsored for the event by name. The coordinator handles the application, the medical clearance and in most cases the travel funding through the facility's sponsorship budget.
items.hack: Do not wait for the application window. Call Recreation Therapy months early and get your name on the facility's internal list, because facility sponsorship slots and travel money are allocated before the public window closes. Veterans who apply cold in the last week routinely get told the facility's slots are already committed.
items.deadline: See per-event windows above; Winter Sports Clinic applications open August 1, 2026

items.title: Move United (formerly Disabled Sports USA) - 257 member chapters, 45 states, Warfighters program
items.who: Veterans and service members with disabilities, plus family members. Also civilians with disabilities.
items.value: Adaptive sports through a network of 257 member organizations in 45 states - skiing, cycling, climbing, water sports, team sports and more. The Warfighters program is the veteran-specific track and has served 21,556+ warfighters and family members. Also runs a Warfighters Ambassador Program and member organization grants.
items.how: Use the chapter finder at moveunitedsport.org/locations/ to find the closest member organization, then contact that chapter directly - they set their own costs and schedules. National office: 301-217-0960, info@moveunitedsport.org.
items.hack: Move United is the umbrella; the money and the equipment are at the local chapter. Many chapters hold VA Adaptive Sports Grant funding, which means the clinic that looks like it costs $400 is free to a veteran who says 'I am a veteran, do you have grant-funded slots.' Always ask that question by name.
items.deadline: Chapter-specific; national org celebrated its 70th anniversary in 2026

items.title: Team River Runner - free adaptive kayaking and whitewater, 2,300+ sessions a year
items.who: Veterans and active duty service members, including those with physical and psychological injuries. Many chapters include family members.
items.value: Adaptive paddle sports instruction from pool sessions through whitewater, run by volunteer chapters in more than half the country. Over 2,300 paddle sessions a year. Equipment is provided by the chapter.
items.how: Find your chapter at teamriverrunner.org/get-involved/chapters/. Contact info@teamriverrunner.org or the national office at 5007 Stone Road, Rockville MD 20853.
items.hack: Chapters typically run free weekly pool sessions in winter at a local rec center - that is the low-commitment entry point and requires zero equipment and zero swimming ability. Cost is set by the chapter; the national organization does not publish a fee, so confirm with your local chapter. Marked medium confidence because current-year cost terms were not published.
items.deadline: Rolling; chapter-driven

items.title: Challenged Athletes Foundation Operation Rebound - grants for adaptive equipment, entry fees and coaching
items.who: U.S. veterans, active duty personnel, law enforcement, firefighters and paramedics with permanent physical disabilities. EMTs are specifically excluded.
items.value: Three grant categories: adaptive equipment (racing wheelchairs, running and sport prosthetics, handcycles), competition expenses (travel, entry fees, coaching), and training (clinics, camps, one-on-one coaching). CAF has awarded millions through the program.
items.how: Apply at challengedathletes.org/grants/us-military-and-first-responder-grants/. You need proof of service and medical verification of the disability.
items.hack: Applications are accepted year-round with no seasonal cutoff, which almost no adaptive equipment grant does. This is the fastest route to a $4,000-$10,000 handcycle or running prosthesis that VA prosthetics will not authorize as 'recreational.' Stack it: apply to CAF for the equipment and to your VA facility for the travel to the event.
items.deadline: Rolling, year-round - no deadline

items.title: Achilles Freedom Team of Wounded Veterans - free race entries, handcycles, travel and guides
items.who: Wounded veterans and adaptive athletes.
items.value: Participation in mainstream endurance events (marathons, road races) with equipment, trained volunteer guides, travel and entry covered by the Freedom Team. Achilles also runs the Cordani Family Grant Program for adaptive athletes.
items.how: Apply through achillesinternational.org - Freedom Team program page. Chapters also run free weekly workouts in many cities.
items.hack: Verified current: The Cigna Group publicly renewed its Freedom Team sponsorship in January 2026, so the program is funded and operating this year. Freedom Team athletes are flown to marquee races - this is one of the very few programs that pays travel and lodging for the athlete AND a support person.
items.deadline: Race-by-race; apply well ahead of major marathons

items.title: Rivers of Recovery - free fly fishing and hunting trips built around a measured treatment protocol
items.who: Physically and psychologically injured U.S. combat veterans.
items.value: Multi-day outdoor therapeutic trips - fly fishing and hunting - delivered free of charge to the veteran, structured around a designed treatment approach rather than a pure recreation outing.
items.how: Contact info@riversofrecovery.org and review the Participate section at riversofrecovery.org.
items.hack: Marked medium confidence: the organization's own program page was last substantively updated in 2024, and 2026 trip schedules and application steps were not published. Email before you plan around it. The free-to-veteran model is clearly stated on their site.
items.deadline: Trip-based; confirm current schedule by email

items.title: Honor Flight Network - free trip to your memorials in Washington DC, plus the Lone Eagle program
items.who: Veterans who served through May 1975 (WWII, Korea, Vietnam) get priority, and terminally ill veterans of ANY era qualify through the TLC program.
items.value: An all-expenses-paid day trip to Washington DC to see the war memorials, at no cost to the veteran. WWII and Korea veterans are prioritized on the waitlist. The Lone Eagle program serves veterans who do not live near a hub, and the TLC program serves critically ill veterans with less than a year to live.
items.how: Find your local hub at honorflight.org/hub-by-county/ or by hub name. If no hub is near you, or you are critically ill, go to loneeagle.honorflight.org. National office: 937-521-2400, info@honorflight.org; Lone Eagle: eagle@honorflight.org, (937) 521-2400 ext. 104.
items.hack: You must bring a guardian aged 18+ who can push a wheelchair and stand for long stretches; hubs will supply a volunteer guardian if you have nobody. Guardians generally pay their own way and hub policies differ, so ask your hub directly. If a veteran is terminally ill, say so on the application - the TLC program is a separate, much faster queue and it is open to all eras.
items.deadline: First-come, first-served waitlist with WWII/Korea priority

items.title: Gary Sinise Foundation WWII Veteran Celebrations (the program formerly called Soaring Valor)
items.who: World War II veterans.
items.value: An all-expenses-paid trip to New Orleans with a VIP tour of The National WWII Museum, a ceremonial dinner, an airport parade with police escort, a Victory Belles performance, and letters of gratitude. Historically the program paired each veteran with a student guardian.
items.how: Contact the Gary Sinise Foundation at (615) 575-3500 or through garysinisefoundation.org to nominate a WWII veteran.
items.hack: The name changed. Searching 'Soaring Valor' surfaces old pages and dead forms; the live program is listed as WWII Veteran Celebrations. Given the age of the remaining WWII population, call rather than wait on a web form.
items.deadline: Rolling nominations; population-limited

items.title: Vet Tix - free tickets to concerts, games and shows; 41 million tickets given away
items.who: Currently serving military of all branches, honorably discharged veterans, and immediate family of troops killed in action.
items.value: Free tickets to sporting events, concerts, performing arts, educational events and family events in all 50 states and DC. As of 2026 there are nearly 5,900 open events at any given time, 41 million+ tickets donated and 2.9 million+ verified members.
items.how: Create an account at vettix.org, complete service verification, then request tickets to events you want. You pay only a small delivery fee per ticket order.
items.hack: Request early and request often - requests are drawn, not first-come. Set your notification radius wide; veterans in secondary markets get far higher hit rates than those in New York or Los Angeles. The delivery fee is typically a few dollars per order and is the only cost.
items.deadline: Rolling; individual events close days before showtime

items.title: State park entry and hunting/fishing licenses - the disabled-veteran discount almost every state has
items.org: State parks and state fish & wildlife agencies
items.who: Typically veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating (thresholds vary widely by state - some at 50%, some at 100%, some any rating), and in many states all honorably discharged veterans get a discount day or a reduced annual pass.
items.value: Free or heavily reduced state park entry and camping, and free or reduced lifetime hunting and fishing licenses. In several states a disabled-veteran lifetime combination hunting and fishing license replaces a recurring cost of $50-$150 a year.
items.how: Two calls: your state parks department and your state fish & wildlife / DNR agency. Ask specifically for the 'disabled veteran' and 'resident veteran' license and pass categories. Your state department of veterans affairs maintains the authoritative list for your state.
items.hack: This is a state benefit, so third-party 'every state' listicles are frequently years out of date and are the single biggest source of bad information in this space. Verify with the state agency itself, not an aggregator. Bring your VA award letter showing the percentage - most states will not accept a VHIC alone as proof of rating.
items.deadline: Varies by state; many licenses run on a calendar or license-year cycle

items.title: Space-A lodging on military bases - the travel benefit nobody outside the military knows about
items.org: DoD Lodging (Air Force Inns, Army Lodging, Navy Gateway Inns & Suites, Navy Getaways, Marine Corps transient housing)
items.who: Anyone with base access - active duty, retirees, NAF and DoD civilians, and sponsored guests. Veterans with base access privileges (including those granted under the Purple Heart and Disabled Veterans Equal Access Act) can use these where the installation admits them.
items.value: Rooms across 89 Air Force Inns locations (27,000+ rooms), 24 Army Lodging locations (4,000+ rooms), and the Navy Gateway/Getaways inventory worldwide, at a fraction of commercial hotel rates in the same city. Navy Getaways in particular includes cabins, RV sites and cottages at resort locations.
items.how: Search by city or airport code at dodlodging.net, which searches every branch's inventory at once, then book through the branch system. Call the front desk directly if the online system shows nothing - unsold rooms open up to Space-A close to the date.
items.hack: Two rules that make this work: (1) official-duty travelers get first call, so book as far out as you can and expect to be bumped; (2) the best value is not near a big city, it is at recreation-area lodging like Navy Getaways sites, where a cabin can run a third of the local commercial rate. Confirm your specific base-access eligibility with the installation before you drive - access rules for veterans differ by installation and are the thing that most often goes wrong.
items.deadline: Rolling; official travel has priority

items.title: Rebuilding Together 'Veterans at Home' - free home repair and accessibility modifications
items.who: Low-income veterans and their families who own their home. Each local affiliate sets its own income and eligibility rules.
items.value: Free home modifications and repairs for safety and accessibility - ramps, grab bars, bathroom modifications, roofing, heating, electrical. The stated goal is to increase independence and let veterans age in place. Rebuilding Together completes about 10,000 rebuild projects a year nationally.
items.how: Find your local affiliate at rebuildingtogether.org/find-your-local-affiliate and apply to that affiliate directly. The national office does not take applications.
items.hack: Stack this with VA's HISA grant. HISA pays for medically necessary in-home improvements but caps out; Rebuilding Together's volunteer labor covers the non-medical structural work HISA will not touch (the deck the ramp has to land on, the roof over it). Affiliates plan their year around National Rebuilding Day in April, so apply in the fall for the following spring. Eligibility and cost details are set locally and were not published nationally - confirm with the affiliate.
items.deadline: Affiliate-driven; apply in autumn for spring build season

items.title: Habitat for Humanity Veterans Build - homeownership, repairs and employment, 350+ affiliates
items.who: Veterans and military families who meet the local affiliate's income and need criteria. Habitat has served 9,097+ veterans and families since 2013.
items.value: Three distinct tracks: build-and-buy homeownership with an affordable mortgage and sweat equity; critical home repair on a home you already own; and financial literacy education. 350+ Habitat affiliates run Veterans Build and 100+ veteran-serving organizations partner with it.
items.how: Contact your local Habitat affiliate, or start at habitat.org/housing-help/apply. Affiliates set income bands, sweat-equity hours and waiting lists.
items.hack: Habitat homeownership is not a giveaway - you buy the house and carry a mortgage, but it is an affordable one and there is no down payment barrier the way there is in the private market. If you already own your home, ask about Repair Corps rather than the homeownership queue; it is a much shorter path.
items.deadline: Affiliate-driven, rolling

items.title: Habitat Repair Corps - Home Depot Foundation-funded critical repairs on veteran-owned homes
items.org: Habitat for Humanity / The Home Depot Foundation
items.who: Veterans who own and occupy their home, in a county served by a participating Habitat affiliate.
items.value: Critical home repair and energy-efficiency work at no or minimal cost to the veteran homeowner. Over 70 Habitat affiliates in 30+ states participate and the program has completed work on 1,997 veteran-occupied properties.
items.how: Ask your local Habitat affiliate specifically whether they hold Repair Corps funding - not every affiliate does. Start at habitat.org/volunteer/near-you/veterans-build/home-depot-repair-corps-program.
items.hack: Ask by program name. If you just call and say 'I need help with my roof,' you go on the general waitlist. Saying 'Do you have Repair Corps funding for veteran-occupied homes this cycle' routes you to a separate, veteran-only funding pot with far less competition.
items.deadline: Funding-cycle driven; ask the affiliate when their cycle opens

items.title: Veterans Community Project - tiny home villages in 7 cities, any discharge status
items.who: Veterans experiencing homelessness. VCP is known for serving veterans other programs turn away, including those with discharge statuses that bar them from VA programs - confirm your situation with the local village.
items.value: A furnished 240-square-foot transitional home (about 127 items provided) plus 1:1 case management on the H.O.M.E.S. framework - health, opportunity for education/training, money management, earnings and income, and support network. Average stay is about 14 months. VCP reports an 85% rate of transitioning residents into sustainable permanent housing.
items.how: Go to vcp.org and use the 'I'm a Veteran looking for assistance' path, or contact the village nearest you. Villages: Kansas City MO, St. Louis MO, Longmont CO, Sioux Falls SD, Milwaukee WI, Dallas TX, Glendale AZ.
items.hack: VCP's outreach center will help ANY veteran who walks in, not only village residents - benefits navigation, transportation, emergency needs. If you are in one of those seven metros and stuck, the outreach center is a same-day door. The village itself has a waitlist.
items.deadline: Rolling intake; village waitlists vary

items.title: Helping A Hero - specially adapted homes for severely injured post-9/11 service members
items.who: Military personnel severely injured in the war on terror. Also runs marriage, caregiver and recreational programs.
items.value: Specially adapted homes built in partnership with builders and developers, plus caregiver and marriage retreat programming and emotional and financial support.
items.how: Download the home application PDF at helpingahero.org or use the 'Nominate a Hero' form. Phone (888) 786-9531, info@helpingahero.org, 2517 N. Frazier Street Suite 2200, Conroe TX 77303.
items.hack: Marked medium confidence on terms: the organization historically required the veteran to contribute toward the home (commonly cited as around $50,000, often covered by a mortgage), which is a real difference from Homes For Our Troops and Tunnel to Towers, where the home is mortgage-free. Ask about the required contribution in your first phone call before you invest months in an application. Site content verified current as of July 2026.
items.deadline: Rolling; build-schedule driven

items.title: Soldiers' Angels - monthly free groceries for veterans in 10+ metros, plus caregiver support
items.who: Service members, Guard and Reserve, veterans and their families. Income-qualifying is generally light-touch - this is a food distribution, not a means-tested benefit program.
items.value: Monthly mobile food distributions of fresh groceries plus year-round pantries. Served 41,873 service members and veterans with food assistance in 2025. Also: deployed care packages, the Women of Valor telehealth program for female caregivers, holiday assistance registration, and card/letter programs.
items.how: Register once at the Soldiers' Angels self-registration portal (linked from soldiersangels.org), then sign up for each monthly distribution.
items.hack: Distribution cities as of 2026 include San Antonio, Dallas, Atlanta, Charleston SC, Charlotte/Salisbury NC, Cincinnati, Denver, Detroit, Orlando and Washington DC. A single distribution is typically a large box of fresh produce and staples - for a veteran on a fixed disability check this is $100-$200 of groceries a month with no caseworker and no means test.
items.deadline: Monthly distributions; register in advance, slots fill

items.title: Code of Support Foundation and PATRIOTlink - free case coordination plus a 40,000-org resource search
items.who: Service members, veterans and military family members. No cost, no eligibility screen to use the resource database.
items.value: PATRIOTlink is a free, curated, searchable database of 40,000+ vetted veteran support services with no sign-up, no login and no fee. Code of Support also provides intensive case coordination for complex cases spanning mental health, caregiving, benefits and financial need.
items.how: Search free at patriotlink.org. For case coordination call (571) 418-6339 or email contact@codeofsupport.org. Office: 4220 King Street, Alexandria VA 22302.
items.hack: PATRIOTlink is curated and verified, which is the whole point - it is the antidote to the affiliate-spam 'veteran resource' sites that list dead programs. Use it as your first filter before you spend a week calling numbers. For a veteran with five problems at once (housing plus benefits plus mental health plus a legal issue), the case coordination service is the thing to ask for by name.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Objective Zero - anonymous peer support by text, voice or video, on demand, free app
items.who: Active duty, veterans, military and veteran families, and caregivers.
items.value: A free app connecting you anonymously to 2,600+ trained peer supporters ('Pathfinders') by text, voice or video, plus mood and symptom tracking, journaling, guided meditation and yoga. 100,000+ text conversations and 6,000+ hours of voice/video connection facilitated.
items.how: Download the Objective Zero app on iOS or Android. Info: (202) 573-9660, contactus@objectivezero.org.
items.hack: Anonymous is the operative word. Nothing goes into a VA record, there is no intake, and you can filter for a Pathfinder who matches your branch, era or experience. It is the right tool for 2am on a Tuesday when the crisis line feels like too big a step. Member of the Face the Fight coalition, verified operating 2026.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Give an Hour - free mental health care from volunteer licensed providers, plus peer support groups
items.who: People affected by human-made trauma, with a longstanding dedicated military and veteran track. Weekly peer support groups run separately for military/veterans and for military families.
items.value: Barrier-free access to mental health care from volunteer licensed clinicians who donate hours, plus free weekly peer support groups. No VA rating, no enrollment and no insurance required.
items.how: Start at giveanhour.org/military/ or use the Contact Us page. Providers are matched from the volunteer network.
items.hack: Marked medium confidence: the organization is clearly operating and the military track is live, but current provider availability and any cost were not published on the site, and the volunteer-clinician model means coverage is thin in some regions. Call before you count on it. If the network has no provider near you, Cohen Veterans Network clinics and Vet Centers are the fallbacks.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Vets4Warriors - 24/7 confidential peer line staffed by veterans, explicitly NOT affiliated with VA
items.who: Every member of the military community - active duty, veterans, family members, caregivers.
items.value: A 24/7 peer support line staffed by veterans. Calls are 100% confidential. The organization states plainly it is 'absolutely not affiliated with the VA or military in any way,' meaning a call cannot affect your status, clearance or benefits.
items.how: Call 855-838-8255, any hour, any day.
items.hack: This is the number for the veteran who will not call the Crisis Line because he is afraid of the record, the commander notification or the clearance. It is not a crisis line - it is an ongoing peer relationship line, and the same peer can follow up with you. Keep 988 press 1 for acute crisis and this number for everything before that.
items.deadline: None - 24/7

items.title: American Red Cross Hero Care Network - the only body that can verify a family emergency for emergency leave
items.who: Active duty, veterans, military families, caregivers and survivors.
items.value: 24/7 emergency communication between a service member and their command - the Red Cross is the only organization chartered by Congress to independently verify a family emergency, which is what starts the emergency leave process. Also connects military families to financial assistance and local resources, and runs a free Hero Care App.
items.how: Call +1 877-272-7337. OCONUS service members can call online at safdial.redcross.org. Text GETHEROCARE to 90999 for the app.
items.hack: Every hour you spend trying to get a commander to approve emergency leave on the strength of a family phone call is an hour wasted - the command needs the Red Cross verification message. Call the Red Cross FIRST, with the hospital or funeral home name and phone number ready, and the message goes to the command through official channels. This is free.
items.deadline: None - 24/7

items.title: Military Saves / Veteran Saves - free savings pledge, coaching content and April savings month
items.who: Service members, veterans and their families.
items.value: Free savings pledge with personalized goal setting, email and text reminders and financial tips, educational content across 10+ savings categories (emergency fund, retirement, housing, debt payoff), and partner resource packets. Military Saves Month runs each April.
items.how: Take the pledge at militarysaves.org. Consumer Federation of America, 1620 Eye Street NW Suite 200, Washington DC 20006, (202) 387-6121, save@americasaves.org.
items.hack: The program has extended into 'Veteran Saves' specifically for transitioning and separated members - the content set differs from the active-duty version. During April, installations and many banks run matched-savings and prize-linked savings promotions tied to the pledge, which is the only time free money is attached to it.
items.deadline: Military Saves Month is April each year

items.title: Veterans Benefits Banking Program - free certified financial counseling and a veteran-friendly bank locator
items.org: VBBP / Association of Military Banks of America / VBA
items.who: Veterans, veteran beneficiaries and veteran caregivers.
items.value: Free, confidential counseling from certified financial counselors; VetCents, a free financial wellness platform for savings, credit, debt and fraud avoidance; a locator for banks and credit unions that have committed to veteran-friendly accounts; and direct-deposit help for VA benefit payments.
items.how: Go to veteransbenefitsbanking.org. Run jointly by VBBP, the Association of Military Banks of America and the Veterans Benefits Administration.
items.hack: The single highest-value use: if you are unbanked and receiving VA compensation by prepaid card or check, the bank locator finds an institution that will open a no-fee, no-minimum account for a veteran with damaged credit, which is what stops the check-cashing fees that eat 3-5% of a disability check every month. The counseling is free and is not a debt-settlement sales funnel.
items.deadline: None

items.title: NFCC nonprofit credit counseling - the legitimate alternative to debt-settlement companies
items.who: Anyone, including veterans. NFCC has no veteran-specific program, but member agencies work with VA income and many have military financial counselors on staff.
items.value: Counseling from 1,500+ NFCC-certified counselors on credit card debt, budgeting, homeowner and foreclosure issues, and student loans. Initial counseling sessions at NFCC member agencies are typically free; debt management plans carry a modest monthly fee that is far below for-profit debt settlement.
items.how: Call 877-360-6322 or 833-746-7578, use the NFCC agency locator at nfcc.org, or request video chat.
items.hack: The test for whether a 'veteran debt relief' outfit is a scam: NFCC member agencies are nonprofit, do not cold-call you, and never ask you to stop paying your creditors. Anyone who finds you through a VA disability lead list and tells you to stop paying is a debt settlement firm and will wreck your credit. Marked medium confidence only because NFCC publishes no veteran-specific program and fees are set per agency.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Military OneSource - you keep it for 365 days after you separate, and most people never use it
items.org: DoD Military Community and Family Policy
items.who: Veterans and their immediate family members for 365 days past their end of tour, retirement date or discharge date (honorable). Medically discharged members in wounded warrior programs, caregivers of wounded/ill/injured service members, and unmarried surviving spouses and children keep access beyond that window.
items.value: Free, 24/7: confidential non-medical counseling (individual, couples, family) with a set number of sessions per issue, financial counseling, MilTax free tax prep and e-filing, legal consultations, specialty consultations on transition, education and special needs, and coaching.
items.how: Call 800-342-9647, 24/7/365, or use secure chat at militaryonesource.mil.
items.hack: The 365-day clock is the point. In your first year out you can get free couples counseling, a free financial counselor and free tax filing without touching VA, without a rating, and without anything entering a medical record. Almost nobody uses it because they assume the benefit ended at the gate. Use it in month two, not month eleven.
items.deadline: 365 days from separation/retirement/discharge date

items.title: Dental Lifeline Network Donated Dental Services - comprehensive free dentistry, veterans prioritized
items.who: People who are 65+, OR have a permanent disability, OR need medically necessary dental care and cannot afford it. Dental Lifeline states that whenever possible it prioritizes veterans who have a disability, are elderly, or need life-saving care.
items.value: Comprehensive donated dental treatment from volunteer dentists and labs - not a cleaning, a full treatment plan, frequently including extractions, restorations and dentures. Free to the patient.
items.how: Apply through dentallifeline.org/help/ for your state program. Denver national office: 1800 15th Street Suite 100, Denver CO 80202, 303.534.5360.
items.hack: This is the program for the veteran who is NOT eligible for VA dental - which is most veterans, since VA Class IV dental requires 100%/TDIU or a service-connected dental condition. Waits are long (often a year or more) and state programs open and close their waitlists, so apply the day you learn about it. Apply in parallel with Everyone For Veterans and an Aspen Dental Day of Service appointment.
items.deadline: State waitlists open and close - check your state's status

items.title: Aspen Dental Day of Service - November 7, 2026, free dental care for any veteran, 550+ offices
items.who: Anyone who has served in any branch of the military. No rating, no income test, no discharge test stated.
items.value: Free dental care at 550+ participating Aspen Dental offices on the day of service: a limited exam and X-rays, then treatment of the most urgent need - fillings, extractions, basic cleanings, denture repairs. Since 2014 the program has served 30,000+ veterans and donated $28 million of dentistry; Aspen announced a goal of up to $100 million in donated care over five years.
items.how: Registration opens September 29, 2026. Book online at aspendental.com/dayofservice or call (800) 277-3633. Appointments are about 30 minutes. Walk-ins are accommodated where possible but appointments are strongly advised.
items.hack: Book on September 29, the morning registration opens. Slots at 550 offices sound like a lot and they are gone in days in metro areas. Go in with ONE urgent problem identified - it is a single 30-minute visit focused on the most urgent need, not a treatment plan. Use it to kill the abscess, then use Dental Lifeline or Everyone For Veterans for the comprehensive work.
items.deadline: Registration opens September 29, 2026; event day November 7, 2026

items.title: Everyone For Veterans - free comprehensive dental care, and it covers the spouse too
items.who: Veterans who completed at least one enlistment, were honorably discharged, and are in financial hardship. Spouses currently living with a qualifying veteran are also eligible with a marriage certificate.
items.value: Free comprehensive dental care from volunteer dentists: X-rays, a full exam and treatment of diagnosed concerns, aimed at long-term oral health rather than a single emergency visit.
items.how: Apply at everyoneforveterans.org. You need your DD214 and your VA award letter. Program Director contact is listed on their site.
items.hack: Spousal eligibility is genuinely rare in veteran dental programs and is the reason to pick this one if your spouse also needs work. Wait times vary entirely by how many volunteer dentists are near you, so apply here AND to Dental Lifeline simultaneously - neither penalizes you for being on both lists.
items.deadline: Rolling; wait depends on local volunteer dentist supply

items.title: Hearing Aid Project - free refurbished hearing aids (currently limited to areas near partner audiologists)
items.who: U.S. residents with audiologist-documented hearing loss and a hearing aid recommendation, who are low income AND either uninsured or have insurance with zero hearing aid coverage. The project cannot cover deductibles.
items.value: Refurbished hearing aids at no cost, fitted through a partner audiologist.
items.how: Complete the contact form at hearingaiddonations.org/contact/ to find out whether there is a partner audiologist near you. If you already see a partner audiologist, they can refer you directly - hap@sertoma.org, 816-895-2410.
items.hack: Important caveat verified in 2026: the project is TEMPORARILY LIMITING new applications to people within reasonable distance of an existing audiology partner. Check geography first. And check VA first - if you are enrolled in VA health care, VA hearing aids are free to a far wider group of veterans than most people realize, including many with no compensable hearing rating. Exhaust VA before you queue here.
items.deadline: Rolling but geographically constrained as of 2026

items.title: VSP Eyes of Hope - free eye exam and a complete pair of glasses (distribution paused as of 2026)
items.who: Any age, household income up to 200% of the Federal Poverty Level, no existing private or government vision coverage for the exam or eyewear, and no VSP Eyes of Hope or VSP care in the prior 12 months.
items.value: A gift certificate good for a comprehensive eye exam and a complete pair of glasses at a VSP network doctor, at no cost.
items.how: Certificates are distributed through partner community organizations, not directly to individuals. Ask a social worker, VSO, food bank or clinic whether they hold Eyes of Hope certificates. VSP member line: 800-877-7195.
items.hack: Verified caveat as of 2026: VSP has TEMPORARILY PAUSED distribution of Eyes of Hope gift certificates to its partner network because of demand, and says it will update its page when certificates return. If you already hold a certificate it is still usable at a network doctor. Meanwhile, if you are enrolled in VA health care, VA eyeglasses are free to a broad group of enrolled veterans - go there first.
items.deadline: Distribution paused as of 2026; check the page for resumption

items.title: Lions Clubs - local-club eyeglass and hearing aid assistance, no national application
items.org: Lions Clubs International and district Lions Vision/Hearing programs
items.who: Low-income individuals including veterans. Every club sets its own rules; there is no national eligibility standard.
items.value: Assistance with prescription eyeglasses and, at some clubs and districts, refurbished hearing aids. Lions also run vision screening and recycled-eyeglass programs worldwide.
items.how: Find your nearest club through the Lions Clubs International club locator and contact the club's sight or hearing chair directly. Some districts run a formal application (for example Lions Vision Services eyewear assistance programs).
items.hack: Marked medium confidence deliberately: this is a decentralized volunteer organization and coverage, forms and funding vary club by club and year by year. Do not trust a downloadable 'Lions Club application for glasses' PDF you found on a form-filling website - go to the local club. The realistic ask is one pair of basic prescription glasses, and the realistic turnaround is weeks, not days.
items.deadline: Club-driven

items.title: Free legal clinics inside VA medical centers - the LSV grant program funded 92 organizations
items.org: VA Homeless Programs - Legal Services for Veterans (LSV / LSV-H)
items.who: Veterans who meet federal service requirements and are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Individual grantees set further limits based on their capacity and expertise.
items.value: Free civil legal representation, frequently delivered on-site at a VA medical center through a medical-legal partnership: eviction defense and housing discrimination, family law, income support and government benefits, criminal matters tied to homelessness, discharge upgrade requests, domestic violence protections, health care access and employment law. VA awarded up to $500,000 each to 92 organizations for the grant period beginning October 1, 2025.
items.how: Ask your VA social worker or the Homeless Program Coordinator at your medical center for the on-site legal clinic schedule, or get the current grantee referral list from the VA Homeless Programs site.
items.hack: The medical-legal partnership model means the lawyer holds a clinic in the hospital, on a set day, and your VA social worker can walk you down the hall to it. That is a completely different experience from calling legal aid and waiting. Discharge upgrade help is on the covered list and is one of the hardest things to find a free lawyer for anywhere else.
items.deadline: Grant year began October 1, 2025; clinics run on fixed weekly or monthly schedules

items.title: Veterans Legal Institute - free legal help for low-income and at-risk veterans, in person and virtual
items.who: Homeless, at-risk, disabled and low-income service members and veterans.
items.value: Free legal clinics (in-person and virtual), benefits and disability claims assistance, housing and employment legal support, discharge upgrades, and referrals. Served 1,550 veterans and families in 2025 and 10,000+ since 2014.
items.how: Apply at vetslegal.org/online-application/, call 714.852.3492 or email info@vetslegal.org. Based at 1231 Warner Avenue, Tustin CA.
items.hack: Note the domain: vetslegal.com now redirects to vetslegal.org. Because VLI runs virtual clinics, veterans outside Southern California can sometimes be served - ask rather than assume you are out of area.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Connecticut Veterans Legal Center - the medical-legal partnership model other states copy
items.who: Low-income veterans in Connecticut. Clinician referrals from across the state are welcomed.
items.value: Free legal help on the four things that block mental health recovery: housing, health care access, income, and recovery-related legal problems. 200+ pro bono volunteer lawyers serving roughly 1,500-1,700 veterans a year. Four-star Charity Navigator. Locations in West Haven, Orange, Newington, New London and Rocky Hill.
items.hack: Worth knowing even if you do not live in Connecticut: CVLC pioneered the model of embedding lawyers in VA mental health care, and it is the template that the VA LSV grantees and law school clinics in other states now follow. If you are trying to get such a clinic started in your area, this is the organization whose model to cite.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Legal Services Corporation - the national legal aid network and its Veterans Task Force
items.who: Low-income people, including veterans. Income eligibility is set by each grantee based on federal poverty guidelines plus state and local rules, so thresholds vary.
items.value: LSC funds civil legal aid programs in every state and territory. The Veterans Task Force works through three working groups (legal issues, collaboration, transition to civilian life) and publishes a Veteran Legal Services Toolkit. LSC also administers the Veterans Pro Bono Grant Program.
items.how: Use the 'Get legal help' locator at lsc.gov to find your local LSC-funded legal aid program, then contact that program directly.
items.hack: LSC-funded programs cannot represent you in a VA benefits claim for a fee and generally do not do VA claims work - for that you want an accredited VSO or the VA-hosted legal clinic. What they DO handle, and handle well, is the eviction, the child support order, the driver's license suspension and the consumer debt that are actually destabilizing your life. Use the right tool for each problem.
items.deadline: None

items.title: 38 CFR 14.636 - what an accredited attorney or agent may legally charge you (and when)
items.who: Any veteran considering paid representation on a VA claim.
items.value: The actual rule. A fee may only be charged AFTER the agency of original jurisdiction has issued notice of an initial decision on the claim - nobody may charge you for filing an initial claim. A fee of 20% or less of past-due benefits is presumed reasonable. A fee above 33-1/3% of past-due benefits is presumed UNREASONABLE, though that presumption can be rebutted. VA will pay the representative directly out of past-due benefits only if the fee is 20% or less, is contingent on a favorable outcome, the representative is accredited, and the award produces a cash payment.
items.how: Read the rule at eCFR 38 CFR 14.636 before you sign any fee agreement. Fee agreements must be filed with VA.
items.hack: Three numbers to hold onto: zero (what anyone may charge for an initial claim), twenty percent (the presumed-reasonable contingency, and the ceiling for VA paying the lawyer directly), and thirty-three and a third percent (above which the fee is presumed unreasonable and you can challenge it). If a company is charging you five times your monthly increase as a flat 'consulting fee' on an initial claim, that is not a legal fee under this rule - and unaccredited consultants are outside this scheme entirely.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA OGC accreditation search - verify in 60 seconds whether the person taking your case is legally allowed to
items.who: Every veteran, before signing anything.
items.value: A free public database of every attorney, claims agent and VSO representative currently accredited by VA. If the person does not appear, they are not currently authorized to represent you before VA. The database refreshes Monday, Wednesday and Friday evenings.
items.how: Search by last name, first name, city, state or ZIP at the VA OGC accreditation search page. Partial names work. Questions: ogcaccreditationmailbox@va.gov.
items.hack: Run the search BEFORE the first meeting, not after. The single most common pattern in claim-shark complaints is a 'consultant' who is not accredited, is therefore not bound by 38 CFR 14.636's fee limits, and cannot actually file anything on your behalf. Thirty seconds in this database prevents it. When a case genuinely needs a lawyer - a complex CUE claim, a denied TDIU with a bad record, a Board appeal with legal error, or a CAVC appeal - hire only from this list, and only on a contingency of 20% of past-due benefits.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The COMMIT Foundation - free one-on-one transition work, not a resume workshop
items.who: Service members, veterans and military spouses transitioning to civilian life. The Foundation describes its participants as high-potential leaders and is selective.
items.value: One-on-one transition assistance with an assigned advisor, the Pursue Your Purpose program, a dedicated spouse program, transformation workshops, employer-connection workshop events, and a digital library of self-assessment and messaging tools.
items.how: Apply at commitfoundation.org/apply/. Contact +1 571-306-1323 or info@commitfoundation.org.
items.hack: COMMIT's value is the opposite of a job board - it is the identity and purpose work most people skip and then regret eighteen months into a job they took for the salary. Do it BEFORE you start applying, ideally 9-12 months from separation. Verified operating 2026 (participated in the July 2026 Resnick Aspen Action Forum). No cost is published; confirm at application.
items.deadline: Rolling applications; selective

items.title: The Honor Foundation - the transition program built specifically for Special Operations
items.who: U.S. Special Operations Forces personnel (and, through THF's ecosystem, SOF spouses at some campuses).
items.value: A structured career transition program that translates elite SOF service into civilian terms - professional development, executive coaching, a large alumni network, and continued mentorship after graduation. Multiple physical campuses plus a virtual option. Also runs Vector Accelerator for SOF entrepreneurs.
items.how: Apply at honor.org/apply. Fall 2026 cohorts have launched across all campuses; the published next deadline is December 1, 2026 for the Spring 2027 cohort.
items.hack: Apply for the cohort a full season ahead of your separation, not after - THF is cohort-based with hard deadlines, and the December 1, 2026 deadline for Spring 2027 is the one on the board right now. The alumni network is the actual asset; the curriculum is the entry fee.
items.deadline: December 1, 2026 for the Spring 2027 cohort

items.title: Vets2Industry - a free curated resource library and a networking machine, open to dependents too
items.who: Veterans and retirees, active duty, Guard and Reserve, military spouses, AND college-age dependents of service members.
items.value: A free curated resource library covering education, career and jobs, mental health and wellness, and financial support; free in-person and virtual networking events (V2I and V2I+); mentorship through a Veterati partnership; a job board and candidate panel.
items.how: Subscribe at vets2industry.org, browse the resource library, and register for events. Contact (202) 738-5633.
items.hack: Including college-age dependents is unusual and underused - if you have a kid in college, they qualify for the library and the networking events on your service. The library is curated rather than scraped, which puts it in the same small category as PATRIOTlink for not wasting your time on dead links.
items.deadline: None

items.title: DAV Patriot Boot Camp - free 3-day entrepreneurship intensive with a non-dilutive pitch prize
items.who: Military members, veterans and military spouses building a company.
items.value: Free three-day events held throughout the year: entrepreneurship education, one-on-one mentorship with business experts, structured networking, and a pitch competition awarding thousands of dollars in NON-DILUTIVE funds (you do not give up equity). 36 programs run and 1,346 alumni.
items.how: Register through the event link at patriotbootcamp.org and join the community list for future dates. Site verified current as of July 2026.
items.hack: Note the name change - it is now DAV Patriot Boot Camp after DAV took it on, so older links and articles under the standalone name may be stale. Non-dilutive prize money is rare; most veteran pitch competitions are equity plays or marketing funnels for an accelerator. Come with a working prototype, not a deck.
items.deadline: Multiple events per year; dates posted on the registration page

items.title: Women Veterans Interactive Foundation - crisis relief plus a women-veteran-specific network
items.who: Women veterans of any era.
items.value: Operation Safety Net provides crisis relief - eviction prevention, safe lodging, utility assistance, food support and medication access. Also: Women Veterans Transition Space, Beyond the Transition, the Pink & White Empowerment Series, the Women Veterans Entrepreneurship Collective, local chapters and an annual national conference. Named Veterans Service Organization of the Year by the National Veterans Council in September 2025.
items.how: Crisis assistance: call (202) 810-2118 or email info@womenveteransinteractive.org, or use the Get Assistance section at womenveteransinteractive.org.
items.hack: Operation Safety Net is the item to ask for by name in an emergency - it explicitly covers safe lodging and medication access, two things most emergency grant programs will not pay for. Membership exists with additional benefits but crisis assistance does not require it.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: PsychArmor - free online courses on military culture, caregiving and suicide prevention
items.who: Service members, veterans, families, caregivers and survivors - and employers, clinicians and educators who work with them.
items.value: On-demand online courses at no charge covering military culture, mental health, suicide prevention, caregiver support and health equity, plus multimedia resources. Over 200,000 courses completed annually. The organization states its no-cost model is a commitment, not a promotion.
items.how: Register free at learn.psycharmor.org. Contact 1-858-755-3006 or info@psycharmor.org.
items.hack: Two high-leverage uses most veterans miss. First: send the employer-facing courses to a hiring manager or a new supervisor - it does more for your working conditions than explaining yourself will. Second: the caregiver track is the best free training available for a spouse or parent who has just become a caregiver and is drowning; pair it with the VA PCAFC application rather than waiting for VA training that may take months.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Farmer Veteran Coalition - Fellowship Fund grants and the Homegrown By Heroes label
items.who: Veterans in the beginning years of farming or ranching.
items.value: The Fellowship Fund provides direct assistance - equipment, infrastructure, livestock, inputs - to veterans starting out in agriculture.
