If something adverse happens, get legal assistance immediately rather than talking your way through it.
items.hack: If you are ever offered the chance to explain yourself in a command investigation or before non-judicial punishment, talk to a defense attorney first, for free, before you say a word. Junior sailors talk themselves into punishment constantly because they thought cooperating and being honest were the same thing as being unrepresented. And read every page 13 before you sign; attach your rebuttal statement the same day, because a year later the entry is all anybody sees.
items.deadline: Immediately, any time an adverse action is initiated

items.title: Audit your own official military personnel record annually
items.org: Navy Personnel Command; branch record systems
items.who: Everyone, especially before any board
items.value: Selection boards, commissioning boards and advancement systems see only what is in your official record. Missing awards, missing schools, missing qualification letters, missing evaluations and unposted decorations are silent, and they cost selections.
items.how: Pull your official record at least annually and before any board or application. Verify every evaluation is present and legible, every award is posted with the correct citation, every school and specialty code is recorded, your photo where required is current and in the correct uniform, and there is no erroneous adverse material. Submit corrections with your own documentation from your binder.
items.hack: Pull your record twelve months before a board, not two weeks before, because posting a missing award or a missing eval takes months and there is a hard cutoff date after which the board sees the record as-is. Every cycle, people get passed over on a record that was missing a decoration they actually earned, and there is no appeal for that; the board saw what the record said. Your binder is what fixes it, which is why you kept one.
items.deadline: Annually, and at least 12 months before any board

items.title: Special programs: recruiting, instructor, independent duty, and command screening
items.who: Mid-career enlisted
items.value: Screened special programs, including recruiting duty, instructor duty, independent duty, career counselor, drill instructor and equivalent billets, produce breadth, visible metrics, frequent personal awards and in some communities preferential advancement. They also carry demanding screening requirements including record, physical readiness, and family and financial stability.
items.how: Find out which special programs exist for your community and what screening they require. Clean up the disqualifiers, which are usually financial, physical readiness, record and medical, at least a year before you apply. Talk to people who have done the tour about what it does and does not do for a record.
items.hack: Look at what the top of your community's chief selectee list has in common, and it will almost always include one screened special program tour. Then look at the screening criteria and notice that most of them are things you can fix in a year: a credit issue, a physical readiness category, a missing qualification. The tour itself is hard; getting eligible for it is mostly paperwork and discipline, and that is where most people fall out.
items.deadline: Screening and application cycles vary; prepare 12+ months ahead

items.title: Meritorious advancement: the quota your command controls
items.org: Navy Meritorious Advancement Program; branch equivalents including Army and Air Force command promotion authorities and Marine Corps meritorious promotion
items.who: High-performing junior and mid-grade enlisted
items.value: Meritorious advancement lets commands advance selected sailors outside the exam cycle. It is the fastest advancement mechanism available, it accelerates everything downstream including time in grade for the next paygrade, and it is decided locally by the leadership who see you every day.
items.how: Understand your command's meritorious advancement process, the season in which quotas are distributed, and who sits on the selection panel. Build the record that panel looks for: quals complete and early, warfare device, top eval ranking, a won board, formally appointed collateral duties with results, strong physical readiness, and education progress.
items.hack: Meritorious advancement is a local popularity contest in the best sense of the phrase: the panel picks the person whose work every chief in the room has personally seen. You cannot study for it and you cannot apply for it. You can only be the obvious answer, which means the work has to be visible outside your own division. Find one command-level problem to solve where other departments see you do it, and do it before the quota season.
items.deadline: Quota seasons are announced by message; build the record well in advance

items.title: Joint and broadening assignments in the second decade
items.org: Joint commands; combatant commands; service staffs
items.who: Senior petty officers, chiefs and above
items.value: Joint duty, combatant command and headquarters staff tours produce exposure to how decisions actually get made, a network outside your community, and record breadth that senior enlisted selection boards weigh heavily. They also translate well to civilian program management roles.
items.how: Identify which joint and staff billets are open to your paygrade and community and what qualifications they require. Pursue joint professional military education where available to enlisted. Sequence a staff tour between operational tours rather than stacking staff duty.
items.hack: Take a staff tour once, early enough that you still have operational tours left after it, because a record that ends in three consecutive staff jobs reads as somebody who left the deckplates. One joint or staff tour is breadth. Three in a row is a reputation, and it is not the one you want when the master chief board convenes.
items.deadline: Best sequenced between operational tours in years 10-16

items.title: Financial readiness protects your clearance, your record and your options
items.org: Personal Financial Management programs; Fleet and Family Support; Military OneSource
items.who: Everyone, especially junior enlisted
items.value: Debt problems are the leading cause of clearance denials and revocations, they generate command financial counseling entries in your record, they disqualify you from screened special programs, and they are the reason many people cannot afford to take the career-building tour or the commissioning program that pays less in the short term.
items.how: Use the free personal financial management counseling available at your command and through Military OneSource. Understand the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act and the Military Lending Act protections. Avoid the predatory lending near every base gate. Build the emergency fund before the car. Contribute to the Thrift Savings Plan from your first paycheck.
items.hack: The used car dealership outside the gate has a business model, and it is you at nineteen with a guaranteed paycheck. A twenty-four percent auto loan is how a promising sailor ends up with a clearance review and a financial counseling entry in their record by year two. Take the free financial counseling in your first month, before you have anything to fix, because at that point it costs you an hour instead of a career option.
items.deadline: First month at your first command; review annually

items.title: Build your spouse's career and credentials in parallel
items.org: Military Spouse Career Advancement Accounts; Spouse Education and Career Opportunities; state licensure reciprocity programs
items.who: Married service members
items.value: A spouse with portable credentials and continuous employment changes the family's financial position, makes hard orders survivable, and removes one of the main reasons people leave the service. Programs exist that fund spouse licensing and credentialing and support license portability across state lines.
items.how: Look into the spouse career advancement funding and education counseling programs, employer partnership programs that hire military spouses, and the license reciprocity provisions that reduce the cost of re-licensing after a move. Choose spouse career fields with portability in mind where possible, and build the credential while you are at a stable duty station.
items.hack: Steer your spouse toward a portable credential early, because the single biggest financial loss in a military family is a spouse's career getting reset every three years. Nursing, teaching with reciprocity, IT certifications, accounting, trades, remote-capable professional work: these move with you. And use the spouse credentialing funds, because most families never find out they exist until the last duty station.
items.deadline: Apply at a stable duty station; funding programs have annual limits

items.title: GI Bill transferability: the election you must make while still serving
items.who: Anyone with dependents who may not need the benefit themselves
items.value: Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits can be transferred to a spouse or children, but the election must be made while still serving and generally requires agreeing to additional obligated service. Once you separate, the window closes permanently.
items.how: Confirm current eligibility rules including the years-of-service window, the additional service obligation, and how to designate and later reallocate months among dependents. Make the election through the DoD system, not the VA, and verify it was recorded. Designate all eligible dependents even with a small number of months, because reallocating later among already-designated dependents is far easier than adding someone new.
items.hack: Make the transfer election while you are still in, even if you are not sure who will use it, and put at least one month on every eligible dependent including newborns. Designating a dependent later, after you separate, is generally impossible; moving months between already-designated dependents afterward is straightforward. That one administrative act, done years early, has been worth a child's entire college education to a lot of families, and it is missed constantly.
items.deadline: Must be elected while serving; service obligation rules apply

items.title: Join the professional associations and veteran networks while you are in
items.org: Rating and community associations; veterans service organizations; industry associations
items.who: Mid-career and senior personnel
items.value: Community associations, chief petty officer associations, industry groups tied to your technical field, and veterans service organizations produce mentorship, job leads, claims assistance and a network that exists independent of your command. The people in them are the ones who hire veterans.
items.how: Join the association for your technical field, not only the veteran-specific groups, because that is where the hiring managers are. Attend the conferences your command will fund. Get involved with a veterans service organization early enough that you know someone before you need help with a claim.
items.hack: Join the civilian professional association for your technical field five years before you get out, and go to one conference on the command's dime. You will meet the people who hire for your skill set while you still have something to offer them, rather than showing up as an unemployed stranger with a resume. And find a veterans service organization representative you trust before you need a claim filed, because the middle of a claim is a bad time to be shopping for help.
items.deadline: Join now; the value compounds over years

items.title: Vets4Warriors 24/7 Peer Support Line
items.who: Veterans, service members, families, caregivers — no VA enrollment or rating needed
items.value: Round-the-clock peer support by phone, text or chat with people who have served; help with crisis, isolation, relationship and benefits questions
items.how: Call 855-838-8255 any time, or use the chat on vets4warriors.com
items.hack: Our founder's own note: put this number in your phone now, before you need it — you may be calling on behalf of a friend, not yourself

items.title: Veterans Crisis Line
items.who: Any veteran, service member, National Guard/Reserve member, or their family — enrollment in VA care not required
items.value: Free confidential crisis support 24/7 by phone, text or chat, staffed by responders trained in military culture
items.how: Dial 988 then press 1, text 838255, or chat at veteranscrisisline.net

items.title: Catch A Lift Fund — Free Gym Membership or Home Gym
items.who: Post-9/11 combat-wounded veterans
items.value: Pays for a gym membership or ships in-home gym equipment, plus remote fitness and nutrition coaching
items.how: Apply through the application form on catchaliftfund.org
items.hack: Our founder flags this as one of the highest-value 'free' programs most vets never hear about

items.title: Project Sanctuary Family Retreats
items.who: Military and veteran families — service member, spouse and children attend together
items.value: Free multi-day therapeutic family retreat plus two years of follow-on case management, focused on mental health and family reintegration
items.how: Submit the retreat application at projectsanctuary.us/retreat-application/
items.hack: It is a whole-family program — bring the spouse and kids rather than treating it as a solo retreat

items.title: Project New Hope (MA) — Retreats and Pantries
items.who: Veterans and military families, strongest coverage in Massachusetts
items.value: No-cost retreats, food pantries, baby pantries, and a veteran peer-support internship program
items.how: Browse programs and apply at projectnewhopema.org

items.title: Operation Heal Our Patriots — Free Marriage Retreat in Alaska
items.who: Post-9/11 wounded, ill or injured service members and veterans, attending with their spouse
items.value: All-expenses-paid week-long couples retreat in Alaska with marriage enrichment and chaplain-led counseling, plus long-term aftercare
items.how: Apply at samaritanspurse.org through the Operation Heal Our Patriots application
items.hack: Our founder's file marks this 'APPLY TO THIS ONE FIRST' — application cycles fill early in the year

items.title: Operation Homefront Transitional Housing / Permanent Homes
items.who: Wounded, ill or injured service members and, for transitional housing, families leaving the military — no injury requirement on some programs
items.value: Rent-free transitional apartments and condos while a family gets on its feet, plus mortgage-free permanent homes awarded through the Homes on the Homefront program
items.how: Apply through operationhomefront.org housing programs
items.hack: Two different doors — transitional housing has a lower bar than the mortgage-free home award; apply to both

items.title: Military Warriors Support Foundation — Homes4WoundedHeroes, Transportation4Heroes, Skills4Life
items.who: Combat-wounded veterans and Gold Star/surviving spouses
items.value: Three stacked programs: mortgage-free homes, donated vehicles, and a recreation-plus-mentorship track
items.how: Review open homes and apply at militarywarriors.org
items.hack: The same application family covers home, car and mentorship — do not stop at the housing page

items.title: Purple Heart Homes
items.who: Service-connected disabled veterans of all eras, with an emphasis on aging veterans
items.value: Home modifications for accessibility and rehabilitated homes made available to disabled veterans
items.how: Apply at purplehearthomesusa.org
items.hack: One of the few housing charities that serves older-era veterans, not only post-9/11

items.title: Tunnel to Towers Foundation
items.org: Stephen Siller Tunnel to Towers Foundation
items.who: Catastrophically injured service members, Gold Star and fallen first responder families, and homeless veterans
items.value: Smart homes for catastrophically injured veterans, mortgage payoffs for Gold Star families, and homeless veteran housing programs
items.how: Apply through the programs page at t2t.org

items.title: Building For America's Bravest / OurBravest Smart Homes
items.org: Building For America's Bravest (Stephen Siller / Gary Sinise partnership)
items.who: Catastrophically injured veterans, typically quadruple amputees and severe TBI cases
items.value: Purpose-built smart homes using adaptive technology so severely injured veterans can live independently
items.how: Learn about eligibility and apply at ourbravest.org

items.title: Helping a Hero
items.who: Severely wounded post-9/11 veterans
items.value: Specially adapted homes provided in partnership with builders and communities
items.how: Apply at helpingahero.org

items.title: Rebuilding Together — Critical Home Repairs
items.who: Low-income homeowners including veterans; run through local affiliates
items.value: Free critical home repairs and safety modifications on a home the veteran already owns
items.how: Find your local affiliate at rebuildingtogether.org
items.hack: This is repairs on a home you already own, not a home giveaway — the right door when the house is the problem, not the mortgage

items.title: Patios for Patriots — Free Concrete or Brick Patio
items.who: Veterans, typically service-connected disabled, at their own residence
items.value: A donated concrete or brick patio installed at the veteran's home at no cost
items.how: Apply at patiosforpatriots.org

items.title: SALUTE Inc. — Adapted Home Renovations
items.who: Severely disabled military members and their families
items.value: Project-by-project adapted home renovations delivered with builders, contractors and local businesses; also emergency financial assistance
items.how: Request assistance at saluteinc.org

items.title: Veterans Community Project — Tiny Home Villages
items.who: Homeless veterans regardless of discharge status or era
items.value: Transitional tiny homes plus wraparound case management, and a walk-in outreach center for any veteran
items.how: Visit veteranscommunityproject.org or walk into a VCP Outreach Center
items.hack: VCP serves veterans with discharge statuses the VA turns away — worth knowing for anyone with a bad-paper discharge

items.title: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
items.who: Veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness, and their families
items.value: Free 24/7 line that connects a veteran directly to local VA homeless coordinators, HUD-VASH vouchers, and emergency housing
items.hack: Homeless veterans can also use VA and base facilities for a shower and gym access while working through the system — Our founder notes many never ask

items.title: Cohen Veterans Network Clinics
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans and their families, including many discharge statuses the VA excludes
items.value: Free or low-cost mental health care at brick-and-mortar clinics and by telehealth, with short wait times
items.how: Find a clinic at cohenveteransnetwork.org
items.hack: Accepts family members and less-than-honorable discharges that VA mental health may not cover

items.title: Headstrong Project
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans, service members and families
items.value: Free, confidential, stigma-free trauma-focused therapy with no cost, no insurance and no VA paperwork
items.how: Request care at getheadstrong.org
items.hack: Treatment is not billed to the VA, so nothing enters a VA record — useful for anyone worried about clearance or career effects

items.title: Give an Hour — Donated Counseling Hours
items.who: Military, veterans, families and caregivers
items.value: Free counseling sessions donated by licensed civilian mental health professionals
items.how: Search the provider network at giveanhour.org

items.title: Military OneSource Non-Medical Counseling
items.who: Service members, retirees within a set window after separation, and family members
items.value: Free confidential non-medical counseling sessions per issue per year with licensed counselors, plus financial, legal, tax and relocation help under one roof
items.how: Call Military OneSource or book at militaryonesource.mil
items.hack: Non-medical counseling is not a medical record entry — Our founder flags it as the low-friction first step before a clinical referral. Session counts change; confirm the current number
items.deadline: Access continues for a limited period after separation — confirm the current window

items.title: Operation Mend (UCLA Health)
items.who: Post-9/11 service members, veterans and families with combat-related injuries
items.value: Advanced reconstructive surgery and comprehensive psychological health treatment at no cost, with travel and lodging provided
items.how: Apply through the Operation Mend program at UCLA Health
items.hack: Travel for the veteran and a caregiver is covered — cost of getting there is not a reason to skip it

items.title: Home Base (Boston) — Invisible Wounds Program
items.org: Home Base, a Red Sox Foundation and Mass General Brigham program
items.who: Post-9/11 service members, veterans and families with PTSD, TBI, anxiety, depression or related conditions
items.value: Intensive clinical care plus fitness and mind-body wellness programming, including a two-week intensive clinical program
items.how: Contact Home Base through homebase.org

items.title: Save A Warrior
items.who: Combat veterans, first responders and service members carrying post-traumatic stress
items.value: Free week-long cohort-based program focused on breaking the cycle of post-traumatic stress and suicidal ideation
items.how: Apply at saveawarrior.org
items.hack: Our founder marks this as his personal favorite of the recreational and healing programs

items.title: Hope For The Warriors
items.who: Service members, veterans, military families and families of the fallen
items.value: Clinical support services, wellness programming, caregiver support and emergency financial assistance
items.how: Request services at hopeforthewarriors.org

items.title: K9s For Warriors — Service Dogs
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans with PTSD, TBI or military sexual trauma
items.value: A trained service dog plus the training program to pair with it, at no cost including lodging during training
items.how: Apply at k9sforwarriors.org

items.title: America's VetDogs
items.who: Veterans and active duty with physical disabilities, PTSD, hearing loss or seizure disorders
items.value: Guide, service, hearing and facility dogs provided free, including training and lifetime follow-up support
items.how: Apply at vetdogs.org

items.title: Freedom Service Dogs of America
items.who: Veterans with PTSD, TBI or mobility limitations
items.value: Custom-trained service dogs placed free of charge, with lifetime support for the team
items.how: Apply at freedomservicedogs.org

items.title: Soldiers' Angels Valour-IT — Adaptive Technology
items.who: Veterans with hand, arm or vision injuries that limit computer use
items.value: Voice-controlled laptops, adaptive tablets and GPS devices provided at no cost
items.how: Request through soldiersangels.org

items.title: SAMHSA Service Members, Veterans and Their Families TA Center
items.org: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
items.who: Veterans, service members and families; also state and community agencies serving them
items.value: Federal technical assistance hub for behavioral health, suicide prevention and substance use resources aimed at the military population
items.how: Browse resources at samhsa.gov/smvf-ta-center
items.hack: Use this to find what exists in your state rather than as a direct service provider

items.title: Operation Second Chance
items.who: Wounded, injured and ill service members and veterans, and their families
items.value: Financial assistance with bills and rent, family retreats, and a maintained resource directory
items.how: Apply through operationsecondchance.org/resources/

items.title: Fields4Valor Farms
items.who: Veteran families facing food insecurity, primarily in the Maryland/DC region
items.value: Free fresh produce and farm-based programming for veteran families
items.how: Sign up at fields4valor.org

items.title: Charlotte Hall Veterans Home — Volunteer Program
items.who: Anyone wanting to volunteer with resident veterans in southern Maryland
items.value: Structured volunteer and activities opportunities with resident veterans — good for community service hours and for MOVSM-type recognition
items.how: Contact the activities/volunteer director at 301-884-8171 (Sandra Johnson, sjohnson@hmrmd.com; Brandi M. Tanner ext. 5141, btanner@hmrmd.com)
items.hack: Our founder pairs volunteer work with awards packages — volunteering at a state veterans home is countable community service

items.title: Wounded Warrior Project Alumni Registration
items.who: Veterans and service members who incurred a physical or mental injury on or after 11 September 2001
items.value: Registering as an Alumni unlocks WWP's benefits services, mental health programs, career counseling and peer events at no cost
items.how: Register at woundedwarriorproject.org
items.hack: WWP's benefits-claims service is members-only — you have to register as Alumni first to use it

items.title: Semper Fi & America's Fund
items.who: Critically ill and injured service members and veterans of all branches, plus caregivers
items.value: Direct financial assistance, adaptive housing and transportation, career transition support and long-term case management
items.how: Request assistance at thefund.org

items.title: PenFed Foundation Emergency Financial Assistance
items.who: Wounded, ill and injured combat veterans and active duty facing a financial emergency
items.value: Grants for emergency expenses such as rent, utilities, car repair and travel for medical treatment
items.how: Apply at penfedfoundation.org/apply-for-assistance/
items.hack: PenFed also runs the Veteran Entrepreneur Investment Program — the same foundation is a funding door for a business, not just an emergency

items.title: USA Cares
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans, service members and families in financial crisis
items.value: Emergency assistance with housing, utilities and basic needs, plus career transition support and combat-injured assistance
items.how: Apply at usacares.org/programs

items.title: Branch Relief Societies — Interest-Free Loans and Grants
items.org: Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society, Army Emergency Relief, Air Force Aid Society, Coast Guard Mutual Assistance
items.who: Active duty, retirees and eligible family members of the matching branch
items.value: Zero-interest emergency loans and outright grants for rent, car repair, funeral travel and emergency needs, plus education grants and interest-free education loans
items.how: Contact your branch society: nmcrs.org, armyemergencyrelief.org, afas.org, cgmahq.org
items.hack: Retirees remain eligible — the door does not close at the DD-214, and NMCRS also runs spouse and dependent education grants

items.title: Vet Tix — Free Event Tickets
items.who: Currently serving, veterans of all eras, and immediate family of those killed in action
items.value: Free tickets to sporting events, concerts, comedy shows, theater and family events; you cover only a small delivery fee
items.how: Create an account and verify service at vettix.org, then request tickets as they post in your area
items.hack: Tickets release on short notice — turn on alerts for your metro rather than checking occasionally

items.title: America the Beautiful Military Annual and Lifetime Passes
items.who: Current military and dependents; separately, a free lifetime pass for veterans and Gold Star families
items.value: Free entry to national parks and federal recreation lands, covering entrance and standard amenity fees
items.how: Obtain at a park entrance with military ID or veteran ID, or order through the USGS store
items.hack: Veterans get a free lifetime version, not just the annual military pass — two different products, ask for the right one

items.title: American Forces Travel
items.who: Service members, retirees, veterans with VA service-connected disability, and DoD ID holders
items.value: Official MWR travel portal running on Priceline inventory with military-only rates on hotels, flights, cars and cruises; revenue goes back to MWR
items.how: Book at americanforcestravel.com after verifying eligibility
items.hack: Compare against the same hotel on a points booking — the portal wins on cash rates but does not always earn hotel status

items.title: Armed Forces Vacation Club
items.who: Active duty, Guard/Reserve, retirees, veterans and DoD civilians
items.value: Flat-rate week-long resort condo stays worldwide from surplus timeshare inventory, plus discounted hotels and cruises
items.how: Register at afvclub.com and search open weeks
items.hack: Inventory is leftover timeshare weeks — flexibility on dates and destination is what makes the pricing work

items.title: Armed Forces Recreation Centers — Hale Koa, Edelweiss, Dragon Hill, New Sanno
items.who: Active duty, retirees, and other DoD ID cardholders; eligibility tiers vary by property
items.value: DoD-owned resort hotels at Waikiki (Hale Koa), Bavaria (Edelweiss), Seoul (Dragon Hill) and Tokyo (New Sanno) with rank-based rates well below market
items.how: Book directly with each resort: halekoa.com, edelweisslodgeandresort.com, dragonhilllodge.com, thenewsanno.com
items.hack: These book out a year ahead in peak season — put the reservation in before the leave chit

items.title: DoD Lodging, Navy Getaways and Navy Lodge
items.who: DoD ID cardholders including retirees
items.value: On-base hotels, cabins, cottages, RV parks and campsites at military rates across the US and overseas
items.how: Search dodlodging.net, navymwr.org/programs/navy-getaways, and navy-lodge.com
items.hack: On-base RV parks and cabins are the cheapest family travel in the system and are almost never fully booked outside summer

items.title: Fisher House Foundation — Free Lodging Near Medical Centers
items.who: Families of patients receiving care at major military and VA medical centers
items.value: Free lodging in a Fisher House beside the hospital for the duration of treatment
items.how: Ask the hospital's Fisher House manager or social worker for a referral; see fisherhouse.org
items.hack: Request placement through the treating facility's social worker, not by cold application — beds are allocated hospital-side

items.title: Hero Miles and Hotels for Heroes
items.who: Wounded, injured and ill service members and veterans in treatment, plus their family or close friends
items.value: Donated airline miles converted into free round-trip tickets, and donated hotel points converted into free hotel rooms, for travel tied to treatment or an authorized event
items.how: Request through the treating medical facility's case manager; details at fisherhouse.org
items.hack: Runs on donated miles and points, so requests go through the medical center — build the ask into the treatment plan

items.title: Veterans Airlift Command — Free Private Air Transport
items.who: Combat-wounded veterans, post-9/11 wounded service members, and their families
items.value: Free flights on donated private aircraft for medical and compassionate travel, including family accompanying the veteran
items.how: Submit a flight request at veteransairlift.org
items.hack: Private aircraft, so it handles routes and timing commercial airlines cannot — good for treatment at a distant specialty center

items.title: Honor Flight Network
items.who: Veterans, with priority to WWII, Korea, Vietnam-era and terminally ill veterans
items.value: Free trip to Washington DC to visit the memorials, with a guardian escort, at no cost to the veteran
items.how: Apply through your regional hub at honorflight.org

items.title: Space-Available (Space-A) Military Air Travel
items.who: Active duty, retirees, 100% service-connected disabled veterans and eligible dependents, in priority categories
items.value: Free or nearly free seats on military aircraft worldwide when space allows
items.how: Sign up through the AMC passenger terminal for your desired destinations; track flights via the terminals' official pages
items.hack: 100% service-connected disabled veterans were added to Space-A eligibility — many disabled veterans do not know they qualify. Confirm current category rules before planning

items.title: TSA PreCheck with DoD ID Number
items.who: Active duty, Guard/Reserve, and DoD civilians; cadets and midshipmen
items.value: TSA PreCheck at no cost by entering your DoD ID number as the Known Traveler Number
items.how: Enter the 10-digit DoD ID number from the back of your CAC as the KTN in each airline profile
items.hack: It does not carry over after you separate — pay for PreCheck or Global Entry (or use a card that reimburses it) before your last day
items.deadline: Benefit ends at separation

items.title: Blue Star Museums
items.org: Blue Star Families / National Endowment for the Arts
items.who: Active duty military and up to five family members
items.value: Free admission to thousands of participating museums during the summer program window
items.how: Show military ID at a participating museum; list at bluestarfam.org
items.hack: Seasonal — runs roughly Armed Forces Day through Labor Day, so plan summer trips around it
items.deadline: Summer program window each year

items.title: Waves of Honor — Free Theme Park Admission
items.who: Active duty, activated Guard/Reserve, and in some years veterans, plus direct dependents
items.value: Free single-day admission to SeaWorld, Busch Gardens and affiliated parks for the service member and several dependents
items.how: Verify eligibility and claim tickets at wavesofhonor.com
items.hack: Eligibility and the number of free dependent tickets change year to year — re-verify each season rather than assuming last year's terms
items.deadline: Offer terms reset annually

items.title: Birdies for the Brave — Free PGA Tickets
items.who: Active duty, retirees, veterans and their dependents
items.value: Complimentary or discounted tickets to PGA TOUR tournaments
items.how: Verify service and claim tickets through the Birdies for the Brave portal

items.title: Margaritaville at Sea — Heroes Sail Free
items.who: Veterans, active duty and first responders; terms vary by sailing
items.value: Promotional cruise offer where the qualifying hero's fare is waived on select sailings (taxes, fees and companion fares still apply)
items.how: Check current terms at margaritavilleatsea.com/offers/heroessailfree/
items.hack: Read the current terms before booking — this is a rotating commercial promotion, not a standing veteran benefit, and port fees are still charged
items.deadline: Promotional, terms change

items.title: Heroes on the Water — Kayak Fishing
items.who: Active duty, veterans, first responders and their families
items.value: Free kayak fishing outings with gear provided, run by local chapters as a low-key therapeutic program
items.how: Find a chapter and register at heroesonthewater.org

items.title: Project Healing Waters Fly Fishing
items.who: Disabled veterans and active military personnel
items.value: Free fly fishing, fly tying and rod building instruction plus outings, with equipment provided, through local programs at VA facilities and military hospitals
items.how: Find a local program at projecthealingwaters.org
items.hack: Many programs meet inside VA medical centers — ask recreation therapy at your VA

items.title: Team River Runner
items.who: Active duty service members, veterans and their families, including those with disabilities
items.value: Free kayaking and paddlesport programs with adaptive equipment and instruction through local chapters
items.how: Find a chapter at teamriverrunner.org

items.title: Team Red, White & Blue
items.who: Veterans, service members and community supporters
items.value: Free local chapter fitness, social and leadership activities that build a post-service community, plus volunteer leadership roles
items.how: Join at teamrwb.org and connect to a local chapter through the app
items.hack: Our founder's note: it is more than running — the chapter leadership roles are a resume line and a network

items.title: Higher Ground (Idaho)
items.who: Veterans and their families, including those with physical injuries, PTSD and TBI
items.value: Therapeutic recreation camps and retreats for warriors and families at no cost
items.how: Apply at highergroundusa.org

items.title: No Barriers Warriors — Outdoor Expeditions
items.who: Veterans, including those with disabilities
items.value: Free multi-day wilderness expeditions built around a curriculum for post-service purpose and resilience
items.how: Apply at nobarriersusa.org

items.title: Outward Bound for Veterans
items.who: Veterans and service members of all eras, especially those readjusting after deployment
items.value: Free wilderness expedition courses designed to support reintegration to civilian life
items.how: Apply at outwardbound.org/veteran-adventures

items.title: R4 Alliance — Vetted Recreational Therapy Network
items.who: Veterans, service members and families looking for therapeutic recreation programs
items.value: A membership network of vetted recreational-therapy providers, usable as a directory so you are not guessing which outdoor program is legitimate
items.how: Browse member programs at r4alliance.org
items.hack: Our founder treats this as a quality filter — the programs in it have been screened, unlike a general web search

items.title: Black Horse Forge — Free Blacksmithing Classes
items.who: Veterans, service members and first responders, primarily around Fredericksburg, Virginia
items.value: Free blacksmithing classes and open forge time used as a peer-support and therapeutic craft community
items.how: Sign up at blackhorseforge.com

items.title: ID.me Shop — Verified Military Discount Portal
items.who: Active duty, veterans, retirees, Guard/Reserve and in many cases spouses
items.value: Single verified identity that unlocks military pricing at hundreds of retailers that will not otherwise honor a discount online
items.how: Create and verify an ID.me account once, then shop through shop.id.me
items.hack: Verifying once with ID.me is also how you get into many VA and state portals — do it before you need it, and keep the DD-214 and rating letter in Google Drive to verify fast

items.title: GovX
items.who: Military, veterans, first responders and government employees
items.value: Members-only pricing on tactical gear, optics, apparel, footwear and event tickets
items.how: Verify service at govx.com

items.title: ExpertVoice Military Program
items.who: Verified military and veterans
items.value: Deep pro-level pricing (often far below retail) on outdoor, athletic and gear brands
items.how: Apply to the military program at expertvoice.com/military
items.hack: Pro pricing here typically beats the public 'military discount' at the same brand's own site — check both

items.title: Outdoor Brand Pro Deals for Military
items.org: Multiple outdoor brands (Helly Hansen, Kelty, Marmot, Merrell, Osprey, Leatherman, Gerber, Benchmade, Thule, Therm-a-Rest, MSR, Mystery Ranch, Scarpa, Smith Optics, Oakley SI, Spyderco, Vortex and others)
items.who: Verified military, veterans and retirees; each brand sets its own eligibility
items.value: Direct-from-brand pro purchase programs, often around half off retail, that accept military service as qualifying for pro status
items.how: Apply on each brand's pro program page individually (for example hellyhansen.com pro, kelty.com pro-purchase-program, osprey.com pro-sales) or through Outdoor Prolink and Guidefitter
items.hack: Apply to several at once during a gear-buying window — approval can take days and each is separate; Oakley Standard Issue and Guidefitter are the fastest wins

items.title: Adidas and Columbia Employee Store Access with CAC
items.who: CAC holders (active duty and DoD civilians) at the Portland, Oregon employee stores
items.value: Admission to invite-only employee stores at employee pricing, typically a steep discount off retail
items.how: Present a CAC at the Portland employee store entrance
items.hack: Geographically narrow and CAC-dependent — plan it around a Pacific Northwest trip while still serving
items.deadline: Requires a valid CAC

items.title: Overstock Club O Free Membership for Military
items.who: Verified military
items.value: Free Club O rewards membership normally sold as a paid subscription
items.how: Verify military status through the retailer's military page
items.hack: Overstock rebranded to Bed Bath & Beyond — verify this program still exists before counting on it

items.title: Thrive Market Free Military Membership
items.who: Verified active duty, veterans and military families
items.value: Free annual membership (normally a paid subscription) to a members-only online grocery with wholesale pricing on natural and organic goods
items.how: Verify service through Thrive Market's military sign-up

items.title: Free Wall Street Journal and Washington Post for Military
items.who: Service members and families; the Post offer keys off a .mil email address
items.value: Free digital subscriptions to major newspapers, plus free access via Military OneSource to ProQuest PressReader (thousands of newspapers), Morningstar investment research, EBSCO e-books and audiobooks, and Kanopy streaming
items.how: WSJ and research databases through militaryonesourceconnect.org; Washington Post via subscribe.washingtonpost.com/specialoffer with a .mil address
items.hack: The WSJ account has to be renewed periodically — set a calendar reminder or it lapses silently
items.deadline: WSJ access requires periodic renewal

items.title: Cash-Back Stacking Play (Rakuten/BeFrugal + Chat Discount + Card Promo)
items.org: Rakuten, BeFrugal, retailer customer service, card issuer offers
items.who: Anyone shopping online, military or not — Our founder teaches it as his 'ballin on a budget' play
items.value: Stacks four savings layers on one purchase: portal cash back, a negotiated military discount, a card statement-credit promo, and the retailer's own reward points
items.how: Start at Rakuten or BeFrugal, click through to the retailer, open the retailer's chat and ask for a military discount or price match, then pay with a card running a statement-credit offer for that merchant
items.hack: Ask for the discount in chat even in uniform and even as a retiree — closed mouths don't get fed. Rebate percentages change daily, so check the portal the day you buy

items.title: Active&Fit Direct Gym Network via USAA
items.who: USAA members and their families
items.value: One low monthly membership covering thousands of participating gyms nationwide plus on-demand workout videos, with no long-term contract
items.how: Enroll through the USAA link at activeandfitdirect.com/fitness/USAA
items.hack: Priced far below a single-gym membership and it travels with you — Our founder calls this out specifically for PCS moves and post-retirement. Prices and gym counts have changed since the file was written; check current terms

items.title: YMCA Military Outreach Memberships
items.org: YMCA of the USA / Armed Services YMCA
items.who: Eligible active duty and military families, especially those geographically separated from a base, through participating Ys
items.value: Free or subsidized YMCA membership funded through the DoD military outreach initiative
items.how: Contact a participating local Y or the Armed Services YMCA; see asymca.org
items.hack: Eligibility is tied to specific DoD-funded categories (often Guard, Reserve and geographically dispersed families) — ask the local Y which category applies

items.title: Headspace and Spiritune Free via Blue Star Families
items.who: Members of Blue Star Families (free to join) — military, veterans and families
items.value: Free subscriptions to the Headspace meditation app and the Spiritune music-therapy app that are otherwise paid annually
items.how: Create a free bluestarfam.org account first, then enroll through their member benefits
items.hack: You must have the Blue Star Families account before the app links will work — do that step first

items.title: Military Lending Act Protections
items.who: Active duty service members and their dependents
items.value: Caps the Military Annual Percentage Rate on covered consumer credit and bars certain fees and terms; in practice this is why premium card issuers waive annual fees for active duty
items.how: Applies automatically to covered credit; raise it with the issuer if a fee appears
items.hack: This is the mechanism behind the premium-card fee waivers below — the waiver is a legal obligation, not a courtesy, so escalate if a rep says no
items.deadline: Active duty only

items.title: Credit Card Annual Fee Waivers for Active Duty
items.org: American Express, Chase, Citi, Capital One, US Bank, Discover
items.who: Active duty service members (and often spouses on joint accounts)
items.value: Annual fees waived on premium cards — including the flagship Amex Platinum and Chase Sapphire Reserve — while retaining lounge access, travel credits, rideshare credits and purchase and cell phone protection
items.how: Amex: americanexpress.com service-members-civil-relief page. Chase: chase.com/digital/military/scra. Citi: call 1-877-804-1082 or email orders to MILITARYORDERS@CITI.COM. Capital One: capitalone.com/military. US Bank: military banking page. Discover: no late fees under SCRA
items.hack: Open the premium cards WHILE on active duty — Citi and US Bank may not apply the waiver to cards opened after your active duty start date. Our founder's related plays: get high-limit cards when your score is strongest and you don't need them, keep utilization under about 33%, and use a 0% balance transfer to kill high-interest debt or fund a venture
items.deadline: Apply before or during active duty; some issuers exclude cards opened after start of active duty

items.title: Free Active Duty Credit Monitoring and Alerts
items.who: Active duty service members
items.value: Free credit monitoring from all three bureaus plus the active duty fraud alert, which requires extra identity verification before new credit is opened in your name
items.how: Enroll at equifax.com/personal/military-credit-monitoring, transunion.com/active-duty-military-credit-monitoring, and experian.com/lp/military.html
items.hack: Enroll at all three, not one — the alert and the monitoring are separate products and each bureau runs its own

items.title: Federal Student Loan Benefits for Military
items.who: Service members and veterans with federal (and in the case of the SCRA cap, private) student loans
items.value: Stacked benefits: SCRA 6% cap on pre-service loans; 0% interest on Direct Loans while serving in a hostile-fire area; military service deferment; Guard/Reserve deferment; HEROES Act documentation waivers; Public Service Loan Forgiveness counting military service; DoD loan repayment programs; and Total and Permanent Disability discharge for service-connected TPD veterans
items.how: Contact your loan servicer for each benefit separately; TPD discharge through the Department of Education's disability discharge process
items.hack: These do not apply automatically — Our founder's line is that if you believe you qualify and haven't received it, call the servicer. Military service counts toward PSLF's 120 qualifying payments, which many separating members never claim

items.title: Student Loan Discharge for Totally and Permanently Disabled Veterans
items.org: US Department of Education / VA data match
items.who: Veterans the VA has rated 100% service-connected totally and permanently disabled, or determined individually unemployable
items.value: Full discharge of federal student loan debt, with no federal tax on the discharged amount under current federal rules (state tax treatment can differ)
items.how: Apply through the Department of Education's TPD discharge site, or via the automated VA data match
items.hack: There is an automated VA match, but it does not catch everyone — apply directly rather than waiting for it. Check your state's tax treatment of the discharged balance

items.title: Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) Election
items.who: Retiring service members with a spouse or dependents
items.value: Converts a portion of retired pay into an inflation-adjusted annuity for a surviving spouse or child; premiums are paid pre-tax from retired pay
items.how: Complete DD Form 2656, signed by the spouse and notarized, and get it to DFAS before retirement; run numbers on the SBP calculator at actuary.defense.gov
items.hack: Two timing traps from Our founder's notes: the notarized DD 2656 must reach DFAS ahead of your retirement date, and there is a one-time window (roughly 25-36 months after retirement) to cancel. Decide SBP against a large term life policy bought while you are young and healthy. Premium percentages and the paid-up rule have changed over time — verify current figures with DFAS
items.deadline: Election before retirement; limited cancellation window after retirement

items.title: SGLI to VGLI Conversion Window
items.who: Separating and retiring service members with SGLI coverage
items.value: Converts military group life insurance to Veterans' Group Life Insurance without a medical exam if you act inside the no-health-questions window; SGLI coverage itself continues for 120 days after separation
items.how: Apply through VA life insurance at va.gov/life-insurance
items.hack: Two clocks: the no-medical-exam window is short (the planner cites 120 days), while the outer enrollment window runs about a year and a half. Miss the first and you may have to prove insurability. Separately, price VGLI against commercial term life and Navy Mutual — VGLI premiums rise with age and are often beaten by term insurance bought while healthy
items.deadline: No-exam window closes ~120 days after separation; outer window ~1 year and 240 days

items.title: TSP Loan Instead of Withdrawal as Transition Cash
items.who: Service members still on active duty who need a cash cushion for transition
items.value: A TSP loan gives you access to your own balance without triggering income tax or the early withdrawal penalty, and you repay yourself at a low rate
items.how: Request through tsp.gov while still serving — loan eligibility depends on being in active pay status
items.hack: Our founder's rule: take the LOAN while you are still in, not a withdrawal after you get out. A withdrawal is taxable and penalized; a loan is not taxed. He also notes rolling a civilian 401(k) into an IRA on the way out and being more aggressive with TSP fund allocation early in a career
items.deadline: Must be initiated while still in active pay status

items.title: Plan for the Final Paycheck and Retired Pay Lag
items.who: Everyone separating or retiring
items.value: Knowing in advance that your last active duty paycheck is not paid on the normal cycle and that first retired pay and first VA disability payment can lag by months
items.how: Download your last 12 months of LESs from myPay before turning in your CAC; confirm all separation paperwork reached DFAS; verify direct deposit in VA.gov and eBenefits
items.hack: Our founder's planning rule: hold three to six months of cash. His files say final pay reconciliation can run six months or longer while DFAS audits the career for over- and underpayments, and that DFAS has a window to act only after it receives corrected documents — trust but verify that your admin shop actually submitted them
items.deadline: Set up myPay password before losing CAC access

items.title: File Your VA Claim Through an Accredited VSO (Form 21-22)
items.org: DAV, VFW, American Legion, AMVETS, state and county veterans service officers
items.who: Any veteran filing an initial claim, a secondary claim, or an appeal
items.value: Free accredited representation that prepares the claim, tracks it, and represents you on appeal — at no cost, unlike paid claim consultants
items.how: Find a representative through the VA accredited representative search, then appoint them with VA Form 21-22 (or 21-22a for an individual)
items.hack: It is unlawful to charge a fee for preparing an initial claim before the VA's first decision — anyone charging up front for that is a red flag. Our founder's guide is blunt: don't file alone and don't pay. Note the Navy guide's caution that some VSOs will not support a claim you filed yourself while still on active duty

items.title: Benefits Delivery at Discharge (BDD)
items.who: Service members between 180 and 90 days from separation or retirement
items.value: Lets you file a disability claim before you separate so the rating decision can land shortly after discharge instead of many months later
items.how: File through VA.gov within the 180-to-90-day window with your service treatment records
items.hack: This one is genuinely contested in Our founder's own files. The BDD pitch is speed. The counter-argument he recorded from a VSO: appealing is harder if you filed while still on active duty (you may need JAG rather than a VSO), you have a full year from separation to file with benefits backdated to your discharge date anyway, and some VSOs will not assist a BDD claim. Decide deliberately, and talk to the VSO you plan to use BEFORE the 180-day mark
items.deadline: Window is 180 to 90 days before separation

items.title: Get Your Complete Medical Record with DD Form 2870
items.who: Anyone separating or retiring — start 6 to 12 months out
items.value: Your DoD health record is government property but you have a right to a copy; DD Form 2870 is how you demand it, usually delivered as a CD or a DoD Safe link
items.how: Submit DD Form 2870 to the facility holding your record; request outpatient, surgical, radiology (X-rays on disk), mental health and dental separately
items.hack: Our founder's rules, repeated across every file: make TWO complete copies, single-sided, one for you and one for the VA; scan everything to Google Drive with an app like Genius Scan; request the record again one last time right before you separate to capture late visits; compress PDFs for the VA's upload size limit. Note the link cannot be emailed to a .mil address — send it to a personal account
items.deadline: Start 6-12 months out; can take up to 3 months to receive

items.title: Document Every Injury From Day One
items.who: Every service member, from the first day of service
items.value: A VA claim is won or lost on whether the condition appears in your service record — an undocumented injury is very hard to service-connect years later
items.how: Go to medical for everything, however minor, and confirm it was entered in the record; review your record annually rather than at the end
items.hack: The single most repeated line in Our founder's book: 'Day 1 document document document.' Related plays from the same file: take the over-40 physical, get the sleep study if there is any question, check the Airborne Hazards and Open Burn Pit Registry and malaria-pill exposure, and do a self-assessment of your medical history 12+ months out to find gaps while you can still fill them
items.deadline: Ongoing; gaps get harder to close as separation approaches

items.title: Airborne Hazards and Open Burn Pit Registry
items.who: Veterans and service members who deployed to Southwest Asia, Afghanistan, Djibouti, Syria, Uzbekistan and other listed areas
items.value: Registers exposure and provides a free registry health evaluation; supports presumptive service connection claims under the PACT Act
items.how: Register at veteran.mobilehealth.va.gov/AHBurnPitRegistry
items.hack: Register while still on active duty — it is on the 12-months-out checklist for a reason. Registration itself is not a claim; you still file separately, but the exposure record helps

items.title: PACT Act Presumptive Conditions
items.who: Veterans with toxic exposure from burn pits, Agent Orange, radiation and other listed hazards; also survivors
items.value: Expands the list of conditions presumed service-connected, removing the burden of proving the link for covered conditions and locations
items.how: File a claim or a supplemental claim at va.gov; previously denied claims can be refiled under the new presumptions
items.hack: If you were denied before the PACT Act for a condition now on the presumptive list, file a supplemental claim — a prior denial is not the end of it

items.title: Build the Claim File: DBQs, Nexus Letters and Buddy Statements
items.who: Any veteran filing or appealing a disability claim
items.value: Three evidence types that move a claim: a completed Disability Benefits Questionnaire from a provider, a nexus letter tying the condition to service, and lay/buddy statements from people who witnessed the condition
items.how: Have your provider complete the relevant DBQ; submit lay evidence on VA Form 21-4138 (also the continuation sheet when you exceed the space on 21-526EZ)
items.hack: Our founder's note: do not let a healthcare provider be vague — vague documentation is one of the ten listed ways to get a claim denied. Buddy letters can satisfy the 'lay evidence' requirement where records are thin

items.title: Never Miss the C&P Exam
items.who: Any veteran with a pending claim
items.value: The Compensation and Pension exam is where the rating is effectively decided; missing it is one of the fastest ways to get denied
items.how: Attend every scheduled C&P exam; expect separate visits for mental health, dental, eye, ear and TBI claims
items.hack: Register for My HealtheVet and complete in-person identity verification so you can read the C&P examiner's notes afterward. And know the difference: a normal appointment treats you, the separation physical clears you, the C&P exam rates you — do not treat them as the same visit
items.deadline: As scheduled by VA

items.title: 38 CFR Part 4 — VA Schedule for Rating Disabilities
items.who: Any veteran who wants to understand or challenge a rating percentage
items.value: The actual regulation that assigns rating percentages to conditions — the criteria the rater is applying to your file
items.how: Read the current text at ecfr.gov title 38, chapter I, part 4
items.hack: Read the criteria for your condition BEFORE the C&P exam so you know which symptoms matter and can describe them accurately. Ratings combine under the 38 CFR 4.25 table, not by simple addition — two 50% ratings are not 100%

items.title: VA Disability Compensation Rate Tables
items.who: Rated veterans and those estimating a claim's value
items.value: Official current monthly tax-free compensation amounts by rating percentage and dependent status
items.how: Check the current year's table at va.gov/disability/compensation-rates/veteran-rates/
items.hack: Always use the live VA table rather than any figure in a circulated PDF — rates are adjusted by Congress most years using the Social Security COLA, so every dollar figure in this document set is stale. Adding dependents increases payment at 30% and above, and dependents must be added to your file or you lose the money
items.deadline: Rates change with annual COLA

items.title: What Each Disability Rating Threshold Unlocks
items.who: Veterans at any rating, including 0%
items.value: Benefits ladder by rating: even a 0% rating can open VA health care priority, dental and vision eligibility, S-DVI/VALife, 10-point federal hiring preference and burial allowance; 10% waives the VA loan funding fee; 10-20% can open VR&E with a serious employment handicap; 30% adds dependents to compensation, VR&E regardless of handicap, higher health care priority and federal direct-hire eligibility; 50% qualifies for free VA health care when enrolled
items.how: Compare your rating letter against the current VA benefit criteria on va.gov
items.hack: Our founder's biggest point: a 0% rating is not nothing — it establishes service connection, which can be increased later if the condition worsens, and it already carries real benefits. The specific thresholds and figures in his 2022-2023 source tables are stale; verify each on va.gov

items.title: Disability Letter Timing Play for Job Applications
items.who: Rated veterans applying for federal or corporate jobs
items.value: A tactic for when to disclose your rating: use the letter for hiring preference when the rating is low, and disclose after hire when the rating is high
items.how: Print your disability rating letter from VA.gov or eBenefits; attach it with the application at lower ratings, or provide it to HR after you have the job at higher ratings
items.hack: Our founder's version: at roughly 0-30% use the letter with the application to claim preference points; at 50%+ upload it to HR only after you already have the job, so the disclosure supports retention rather than screening. Note this is his tactic, not a VA rule, and disclosure rules differ between federal (Schedule A / veterans' preference) and private employers — confirm before relying on it

items.title: Check the DD-214 Before You Sign It
items.who: Everyone separating or retiring
items.value: The DD-214 is the master key to every veteran benefit; errors in name, SSN, dates, awards, schools, RE code or dental block cost you benefits later
items.how: Review the draft in NSIPS (or your service's system) 30 days before terminal leave, verify awards with an awards memo, and sign the final copy only when it is correct
items.hack: Our founder's specific plays: take the MEMBER-1 and MEMBER-4 copies; highlight the original in yellow highlighter and make certified copies (Navy Federal will notarize/certify free); send MEMBER-4 to the VA to apply for benefits; leave DD-214 Block 17 (dental) UNCHECKED if dental work is not complete, because checking it can close the door on post-service dental; scan everything into Google Drive
items.deadline: Verify draft 30 days before terminal leave; sign on last day

items.title: Set Up Every Login Before You Turn In the CAC
items.who: Everyone separating or retiring — do this 3 to 6 months out
items.value: Prevents being locked out of pay, benefits and records the day after separation, when CAC-based access disappears
items.how: Create username/password logins (not CAC-only) for myPay, DS Logon, milConnect, TRICARE Online, VA.gov and My HealtheVet while you still have a CAC
items.hack: Our founder and the Navy guide both flag this as a routine, avoidable disaster. Also download 12 months of LESs and your final records from myPay before the CAC goes away, and note that on eBenefits a 'P' (Premium) account was required to file claims
items.deadline: Before turning in CAC on your last day

items.title: Veteran ID Card (VIC) and Veteran Health Identification Card
items.who: Veterans with honorable or general under honorable conditions discharge
items.value: A wallet card proving veteran status for discounts and identification, without carrying your DD-214 around
items.how: Apply for the VIC at va.gov; the VHIC comes with VA health care enrollment
items.hack: Our founder's alternative for everyday use: keep a scanned DD-214, disability rating letter and a digital business card in Google Drive so you can prove eligibility from your phone. Many states also add a veteran designation to the driver's license

items.title: Re-enroll in TRICARE After Retirement
items.who: Retirees and their families — active duty TRICARE ends on the last day of service
items.value: Continues family health coverage as TRICARE Prime or Select at retiree rates, with no gap if you act inside the window
items.how: Update DEERS with your retiree ID card first, then enroll online at tricare.mil, by phone (East 1-800-444-5445, West 1-844-866-9378), or by mail
items.hack: Sequence matters: you cannot enroll in the retiree plan until DEERS is updated with your retiree ID, so book the ID card appointment ~30 days out. The planner cites a 90-day no-gap window and a 12-month outer limit before you are stuck waiting for open season or a qualifying life event
items.deadline: Enroll within ~90 days of retirement for no break in coverage

items.title: FEDVIP Dental and Vision via BENEFEDS
items.who: Retirees and their families; separate from TRICARE medical
items.value: Dental and vision insurance for military retirees, purchased through the federal FEDVIP program
items.how: Enroll at benefeds.com; the planner cites an enrollment window opening about 31 days before retirement and closing around 60 days after
items.hack: Two cost checks Our founder makes: (1) if your civilian employer's dental/vision is better and cheaper, drop FEDVIP; (2) at a 100% rating the VA covers dental at no copay and can refer you out, which may make FEDVIP redundant. Unlike medical, dental and vision do NOT continue past your last day in service
items.deadline: Roughly 31 days before retirement to 60 days after

items.title: Continued Health Care Benefit Program (CHCBP)
items.who: Those losing TRICARE eligibility, including voluntary separations and former spouses
items.value: Lets you purchase temporary continued TRICARE-like coverage (the file cites up to 18 months) to bridge to civilian insurance
items.how: Enroll through humana-military.com; the file cites a 60-day window after separation
items.hack: This is the military COBRA — it is a paid bridge, not a free benefit, and the enrollment window is short. Compare cost against a marketplace plan before defaulting to it
items.deadline: ~60 days after separation to enroll

items.title: Enroll in VA Health Care (Form 10-10EZ)
items.who: Veterans meeting service and, for some priority groups, income or rating criteria
items.value: Access to the VA medical benefits package; all care for a service-connected condition is free, and the file notes 50%+ ratings qualify for free VA health care when enrolled
items.how: Apply with VA Form 10-10EZ at va.gov/health-care/how-to-apply/
items.hack: Our founder's play: sign up for VA health care while you are still in and upgrade once your rating comes through, rather than waiting until you need care. Priority group placement depends on rating and income, so re-apply when your rating changes

items.title: VA Foreign Medical Program (FMP)
items.who: Veterans with service-connected conditions living or traveling outside the United States
items.value: Pays for care of service-connected conditions received overseas, where regular VA care does not reach
items.how: Register with the VA Foreign Medical Program before you travel or relocate
items.hack: Register BEFORE you go overseas — Our founder lists it as a pre-departure action, not something to sort out after a problem abroad

items.title: CHAMPVA for Dependents
items.who: Spouses and children of veterans rated permanently and totally disabled, or of veterans who died from a service-connected condition — and who are NOT eligible for TRICARE
items.value: Health coverage for family members of totally disabled veterans, cost-shared with the VA
items.how: Apply through va.gov/health-care/family-caregiver-benefits/champva/
items.hack: Our founder's repeated caution: CHAMPVA and TRICARE are mutually exclusive, and dependents cannot simply be added — a retired 100% veteran's family situation determines which applies, and children in particular are not automatically covered. Confirm the current eligibility rules with the VA rather than assuming from a forum answer

items.title: VA Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers
items.who: Seriously injured veterans and the family member — often a spouse — who cares for them
items.value: A monthly stipend paid to the designated family caregiver, plus caregiver training, respite care, counseling and CHAMPVA health coverage for the primary caregiver
items.how: Apply at caregiver.va.gov
items.hack: The caregiver can be your spouse and can be paid for the care they are already giving. Our founder's files cite a rough monthly figure — do not rely on it; the stipend is tied to a VA-set rate that varies by locality and care tier, so get the current amount from the VA

items.title: Stateside Legal — Free Legal Help for Veterans
items.who: Veterans, service members and families
items.value: Free legal education, self-help tools and a directory of free or reduced-cost legal services, including for discharge upgrades, benefits appeals and housing
items.how: Search at statesidelegal.org

items.title: Discharge Upgrade and Record Correction
items.org: Discharge Review Boards / Boards for Correction of Military Records
items.who: Veterans with a discharge characterization that blocks benefits, and anyone with an error on their military record
items.value: Can restore access to VA benefits that a less-than-honorable discharge cut off; corrections also fix missing awards and dates that affect eligibility
items.how: Start with the VA's discharge upgrade tool at va.gov, and use a VSO or a legal clinic rather than filing alone
items.hack: Our founder lists 'apply for a discharge upgrade' among the top ten ways to maximize benefits. Mental health conditions, TBI and MST are recognized bases for reconsideration — a decades-old discharge is not necessarily final

items.title: Transfer Post-9/11 GI Bill Benefits to Dependents
items.who: Service members who meet the service requirement and can complete the additional service obligation — must be done WHILE on active duty
items.value: Moves up to 36 months of education benefits to a spouse and children, as little as one month per dependent
items.how: Submit the transfer request through milConnect (milconnect.dmdc.osd.mil), then the dependent applies to the VA
items.hack: Our founder's key play: transfer at least ONE month to the spouse and to each child at your earliest eligibility, purely to lock the transfer in — you can reallocate months later, but you cannot start a transfer after you separate. Note the different clocks: a spouse's transferred benefit expires roughly 15 years after your separation; a child must generally use it before age 26
items.deadline: Must be initiated while still on active duty; carries an added service obligation

items.title: VA Round-Out Rule — Full BAH in Your Final Term
items.who: GI Bill students in their last quarter or semester who need fewer credits than a full-time load to graduate
items.value: Lets you add non-required classes to reach full-time status and receive full-time education benefits, including full housing allowance, in your final term
items.how: Ask your school certifying official to certify the final term under the Round-Out Rule
items.hack: Our founder files this under 'hidden benefit.' Without it, a 6-credit final semester pays partial housing allowance. It applies only to the LAST term of the program, and you must still be taking the required remaining classes
items.deadline: Applies only to the final quarter/semester

items.title: GI Bill Housing Allowance Location and Format Plays
items.who: Post-9/11 GI Bill students
items.value: Housing allowance is driven by the physical location of the school and by whether your course load counts as in-person
items.how: Check rates with the GI Bill Comparison Tool at va.gov/gi-bill-comparison-tool
items.hack: Our founder's specific plays: the physical campus location sets the housing rate, so a high-BAH metro campus pays more than an online program; a hybrid load (at least one on-campus class) can qualify for the full in-person rate rather than the reduced online rate; and the GI Bill does not pay housing between semesters, so plan cash flow for breaks and consider summer classes. Rules on rate tiers change — verify with the comparison tool before choosing a school

items.title: VA Work-Study Program
items.who: Students using VA education benefits at three-quarter time or more
items.value: Paid part-time work at VA facilities, state veterans agencies or campus veteran offices while you are enrolled, on top of your education benefits
items.how: Apply through va.gov/education/about-gi-bill-benefits/how-to-use-benefits/work-study/
items.hack: Our founder flags this as a path into state and federal jobs, not just income — you build agency experience and contacts while a student. Pay rate follows federal/state minimum wage, so the figure in the old file is stale

items.title: Chapter 35 — Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA)
items.who: Children and spouses of veterans rated permanently and totally disabled, or who died from a service-connected condition
items.value: A monthly education stipend for dependents that is entirely separate from any transferred GI Bill months
items.how: Apply through va.gov education benefits for survivors and dependents
items.hack: Our founder's stacking play: Chapter 35 for the dependents, transferred Post-9/11 months as the backup, and state benefits (CalVet fee waiver, Texas Hazlewood) on top — these are three different programs, and families routinely use only one. His file cites a monthly figure that is now stale; get the current rate from the VA
items.deadline: Dependents have age and time limits — check current rules

items.title: CalVet College Fee Waiver
items.who: Dependents of service-connected disabled California veterans; income limits apply to some plans
items.value: Waives mandatory system fees at University of California, California State University and California community colleges — the files say through the doctorate level
items.how: Apply through your County Veterans Service Office; general info at calvet.ca.gov (800-952-5626)
items.hack: Our founder's caution from the CalVet brief: the child's own income is capped, and a 529 plan can affect that calculation — plan the 529 around the fee waiver rather than assuming they stack cleanly. Verify the current income limit with CalVet, not the old figure in these files
items.deadline: Apply per academic year through the County VSO

items.title: Section 702 In-State Tuition for Recently Separated Veterans
items.org: Choice Act / public colleges and universities
items.who: Recently separated veterans and covered dependents using VA education benefits at public schools
items.value: Requires public schools to charge in-state tuition regardless of residency for a period after separation, which is a large saving at out-of-state public universities
items.how: Present your DD-214 to the admissions or veterans office and request the in-state rate under the Choice Act provision
items.hack: Our founder's file cites 36 months after separation. The window has been modified by later legislation — confirm the current period with the school's VA certifying official before enrolling out of state
items.deadline: Time-limited after separation — verify current window

items.title: Free Credit While Serving: TA, CLEP, DANTES and PACE
items.who: Active duty service members
items.value: Tuition Assistance pays for college credit while you serve, and CLEP and DANTES/DSST exams let you test out of courses free — PACE brings courses aboard ship
items.how: Through your base education office; exam test centers via clep.collegeboard.org and the DANTES program
items.hack: Our founder's sequencing: finish the undergraduate degree on TA while you are in, so the GI Bill and VR&E are untouched for graduate work and dependents. Test out of everything you can with CLEP/DANTES before spending TA dollars. TA caps (per credit hour and annual) change by service and year — get current figures from your education office
items.deadline: Available only while serving

items.title: Branch COOL Programs — Free Civilian Certifications
items.org: Navy COOL, Army COOL, Air Force COOL, USMC COOL
items.who: Service members; program scope varies by branch and sometimes by rank
items.value: Pays exam and credentialing fees for civilian certifications and licenses that map to your military job
items.how: Start at cool.navy.mil (or your branch's COOL site) and use MilGears/Navigator to map your record to credentials
items.hack: Get the certifications while the service pays for them. Our founder's warning from the Navy guide: COOL funding has been suspended for some populations in past budget years — check current funding status rather than assuming. He also notes free certification test vouchers through Navy Federal
items.deadline: Available while serving; funding subject to budget

items.title: USMAP — Turn Military Time Into a DOL Apprenticeship
items.org: United Services Military Apprenticeship Program (Navy-run, multi-service)
items.who: Enlisted Navy, Marine Corps and Coast Guard members
items.value: Converts your on-the-job military hours into a Department of Labor Certificate of Completion of Apprenticeship — a nationally recognized civilian credential at no cost
items.how: Register at usmap.osd.mil and log hours against your trade
items.hack: You are already doing the work; USMAP just documents it. Register early in a tour so hours accrue rather than backfilling at the end
items.deadline: Must be enrolled while serving to accrue hours

items.title: ACT NOW Education — Free Coursera and Transition Training
items.who: Service members, veterans, spouses and caregivers
items.value: Free access to Coursera courses and certificates, plus career planning, resume guidance and interview preparation resources
items.how: Register at actnoweducation.com and follow their weekly rundown of opportunities
items.hack: Our founder and the Navy retirement guide both name ACT NOW specifically for the free Coursera certificates — a low-cost way to add credentials before your resume goes out

items.title: Free Cybersecurity and IT Training Programs for Veterans
items.org: SANS VetSuccess, FedVTE, Vets in Tech, CyberVets USA, Splunk Work+, Microsoft Software & Systems Academy, AWS Educate, Apprenti, NS2 Serves, FortiVets, CBT Nuggets, Cisco Networking Academy, Salesforce VetForce, Code Platoon, WithYouWithMe
items.who: Transitioning service members, veterans and in many cases spouses
items.value: Free or heavily subsidized technical training and industry certifications, several with stipends, room and board, or guaranteed interviews on completion
items.how: Apply to each program directly — SANS at sans.org/cybertalent, FedVTE via CISA, Microsoft MSSA, AWS Educate for veterans, Apprenti at apprenticareers.org, NS2 Serves, Code Platoon at codeplatoon.org, Salesforce Trailhead/VetForce
items.hack: Apply to several in parallel — cohorts are competitive and staggered. NS2 Serves pays a stipend plus room and board during training; Salesforce's program is tied to companies that guarantee interviews to completers. Program names and sponsors churn fast in this space, so verify each is still operating before building a plan around it
items.deadline: Cohort-based; several are limited to a window around separation

items.title: FedVTE — Free Federal Virtual Training Environment
items.who: Veterans, federal employees and government personnel
items.value: Free on-demand cybersecurity training courses, many mapped to certification exams
items.how: Register through the CISA/NICCS training portal
items.hack: No cohort, no application window — purely self-paced, so it is the easiest one to start today

items.title: Warrior-Scholar Project
items.who: Enlisted service members and veterans preparing for or entering undergraduate study
items.value: Free one- to two-week academic boot camp hosted at top universities, covering writing, study skills and the transition to being a student
items.how: Apply at warrior-scholar.org
items.hack: Aimed specifically at enlisted veterans who are strong but have been out of a classroom — it is a confidence and skills bridge before the first semester
