items.deadline: Summer sessions, applications open earlier in the year

items.title: MyCAA and Military Spouse Scholarships
items.org: DoD MyCAA / National Military Family Association
items.who: Spouses of service members in eligible pay grades (MyCAA), and military spouses generally for NMFA scholarships
items.value: Tuition assistance for a spouse's licenses, certifications or associate degrees, plus separate NMFA scholarship funding
items.how: MyCAA at mycaa.militaryonesource.mil; NMFA scholarships at militaryfamily.org
items.hack: MyCAA eligibility is tied to the service member's pay grade and is time-limited — use it while the sponsor is in an eligible grade rather than waiting. Pair with free spouse certification programs (Onward to Opportunity, SANS Women's Immersion Academy, IT-Ready) and free LinkedIn Premium for spouses
items.deadline: Tied to sponsor's pay grade and service window

items.title: Free Tutoring, Libraries and Language Learning
items.org: Military OneSource / Tutor.com / branch MWR libraries
items.who: Service members and their families, including school-age children
items.value: Free online personal tutoring for K-12 and college through Tutor.com, free Mango Languages, Universal Class (500+ courses), and full digital libraries through Navy MWR and MCCS
items.how: Access via militaryonesource.mil and your branch's digital library (navymwrdigitallibrary.org, mccs.ent.sirsi.net)
items.hack: Our founder's family play: the same portal covers the kids' homework help and your own professional courses — most families never log in once
items.deadline: Access tied to service/eligibility status

items.title: Joint Service Transcript and VMET
items.who: Service members preparing to separate or enroll in school
items.value: The JST converts military training and experience into recommended college credit; the VMET (DD Form 2586) translates it for employers
items.how: Print the JST at jst.doded.mil and download the VMET through milConnect
items.hack: Pull both BEFORE you lose CAC access, and check the JST for accuracy — schools award credit off it, so a missing school or qualification is lost tuition. Our founder also stresses validating your record annually, not just at the end
items.deadline: Access easiest while you still hold a CAC

items.title: DoD SkillBridge
items.who: Service members in their last 180 days of service, with command approval
items.value: Work a civilian internship or apprenticeship with a real employer while still drawing full military pay and benefits — often converting directly into a job offer
items.how: Find opportunities at skillbridge.osd.mil, and command approval per your service's instruction (Navy: NAVADMIN guidance, DoDI 1322.29; DON ethics training required within 12 months of start)
items.hack: Two hard-won notes from these files. First, the official SkillBridge site is a poor search tool — use it to harvest company points of contact, then email them directly; search 'DoD SkillBridge' on LinkedIn Jobs and check 50-strong.us/skillbridgelistings, which tracks 80+ authorized partners. Second, if you are hired during terminal leave you can draw military leave pay and a civilian salary at the same time. Complete TAP Capstone at 12 months to clear the way for SkillBridge approval
items.deadline: Last 180 days of service; apply months earlier

items.title: 50 Strong — SkillBridge Listings and Mentorship
items.who: Service members hunting a SkillBridge slot
items.value: A curated, regularly updated list of DoD-authorized SkillBridge employer partners plus on-demand mentorship and networking sessions
items.how: Browse 50-strong.us/skillbridgelistings and follow them on LinkedIn for SkillBridgeConnect sessions
items.hack: The Navy retirement guide's author found his SkillBridge through networking, not the official site — this listing plus LinkedIn is the practical search path

items.title: DoD Transition Assistance Program (TAP) and Capstone
items.who: All separating and retiring service members — mandatory
items.value: Structured pre-separation counseling, a Department of Labor employment workshop, VA benefits briefings, and two-day tracks for employment, education, vocational training or entrepreneurship, closing with the Capstone event
items.how: Register through your installation transition office; start at dodtap.mil and complete DD Form 2648
items.hack: Our founder's advice on TAP: go early (more than 12 months out) and go twice if you can, because the second pass lands differently. And talk to the SME, not the facilitator — many facilitators read slides without having done the process themselves. Capstone completed at 12 months positions you for SkillBridge
items.deadline: Initial counseling more than 365 days out; Capstone no later than 90 days before separation

items.title: Hire Heroes USA — Free Resume and Job Search Support
items.who: Transitioning service members, veterans and military spouses
items.value: A dedicated transition specialist, free professionally rewritten resume, mock interviews, LinkedIn help and a curated job board
items.how: Sign up at hireheroesusa.org and get assigned a specialist
items.hack: Our founder's nuance: use Hire Heroes for the free base resume, then tailor it per posting yourself (or pay for a targeted rewrite) — he is explicit that a tailored resume beats a generic one and that ATS screening rejects untailored resumes automatically. Keep a 5-6 page master resume and cut a 1-2 page tailored version for each job

items.title: American Corporate Partners (ACP) Mentorship
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans and active duty spouses
items.value: A free year-long one-on-one mentorship with a corporate professional matched to your target career, plus career tools and elevator pitch coaching
items.how: Apply at acp-usa.org; requires monthly contact with your mentor
items.hack: Named in both Our founder's book and the Navy retirement guide. It is a year-long commitment with monthly contact — start it 12 months out so the mentorship runs through your actual job search, not after it
items.deadline: Start ~12 months out so the year covers your search

items.title: Veterati — On-Demand Mentor Calls
items.who: Transitioning service members, veterans and military spouses
items.value: Free unlimited mentorship calls with industry professionals you book directly, with no long-term commitment
items.how: Create a profile at veterati.com and book mentors by industry
items.hack: Unlike ACP's year-long single-mentor model, Veterati is built for many short conversations — use it for informational interviews across industries before you commit to a direction. The Navy guide notes the platform had an outage; confirm it is operating

items.title: FourBlock Career Readiness Program
items.who: Transitioning service members, veterans and military spouses
items.value: A 10-week cohort course (about 2 hours a week, online) where a different company presents each week, with small-group breakouts and an assigned coach
items.how: Apply at fourblock.org
items.hack: The value is the weekly company exposure and the cohort network, not just the curriculum — treat every company session as a warm introduction
items.deadline: Cohort-based, runs in terms

items.title: Hiring Our Heroes
items.who: Transitioning service members, veterans, military spouses and caregivers
items.value: Corporate fellowship programs (a SkillBridge pathway), hiring events, a job board and education and networking resources
items.how: Browse programs and events at hiringourheroes.org
items.hack: Their corporate fellowship is one of the most established SkillBridge routes — apply to the fellowship cohort, not just the job board
items.deadline: Fellowship cohorts have fixed start dates

items.title: VETS2INDUSTRY
items.who: Transitioning service members, veterans, spouses and caregivers
items.value: A large free resource repository of veteran service organizations and benefits, plus career webinars and networking events connecting recruiters to transitioning members
items.how: Join at vets2industry.org
items.hack: Named in the retirement checklist alongside ACT NOW as the two LinkedIn groups to follow early — the resource library is the point, not just the events

items.title: USAJOBS and Veterans' Preference
items.who: Veterans applying for federal employment
items.value: Preference points added to federal hiring scores, plus special hiring authorities (VRA, VEOA, 30% or more disabled direct hire) that bypass normal competition
items.how: Build a federal resume and apply at usajobs.gov; obtain a Veteran's Preference Letter from eBenefits/VA.gov
items.hack: Our founder's specifics: a 30% or greater rating supports direct-hire authority, and his file cites 30% as equating to a 15-point hiring advantage. A federal resume is a different document from a civilian one — build both, keep both in Google Drive. Note the 180-day rule restricting retirees taking DoD GS/GG positions right after retirement, and expect slow federal turnaround
items.deadline: 180-day restriction applies to retirees for some DoD civilian jobs

items.title: FedsHireVets.gov
items.who: Veterans and hiring managers
items.value: The official explainer for veterans' preference, special appointing authorities, and how federal vacancy announcements actually work
items.how: fedshirevets.gov
items.hack: Read the appointing-authority pages before applying — knowing which authority you qualify under changes which announcements you should target

items.title: O*NET OnLine and My Next Move for Veterans
items.who: Anyone translating a military job into civilian occupations
items.value: Crosswalks your MOS/rating to civilian occupations with wage data, required skills and local demand
items.how: onetonline.org and mynextmove.org/vets/
items.hack: Use the wage data to set your salary range before an interview — Our founder's rule is to have a number ready and to convert hourly figures by multiplying by 2000 for an annual equivalent

items.title: Military-Focused Recruiting Firms and Job Placement
items.org: Orion Talent, Bradley-Morris, Lucas Group, Cameron-Brooks, CSI Executive Search, Insight Global, RecruitMilitary, Corporate Gray, Shift, SkillMil, Hire GI, Work for Warriors
items.who: Transitioning service members and veterans; several specialize in junior officers or technical enlisted
items.value: No-cost-to-candidate placement services and hiring conferences that put you in front of employers already looking for military talent
items.how: Register with several: oriontalent.com, bradley-morris.com, lucasgroup.com, cameron-brooks.com, recruitmilitary.com, insightglobal.com, shift.org, workforwarriors.org (916-854-4426)
items.hack: These are free to the candidate — the employer pays. Our founder's caution is that placement firms should be one channel, not the whole plan: network and direct referrals remain the highest-yield path. Firm names in this space change; verify each is still operating

items.title: ClearanceJobs — Cleared Roles
items.who: Veterans holding or eligible to reinstate a security clearance
items.value: Job board restricted to cleared positions, where an active clearance is a direct salary premium
items.how: clearancejobs.com
items.hack: Our founder's related play: verify your clearance expiration date and update it while you still can — an active clearance is one of the most valuable things you carry out the door, and it lapses
items.deadline: Clearance eligibility lapses after a period out of a cleared position

items.title: STAR Interview Preparation and Salary Negotiation Plays
items.org: Our founder's transition notes / TGPS and Ruehlin seminar material
items.who: Any veteran interviewing in the civilian market
items.value: A rehearsed set of stories and responses that translate military experience without military jargon
items.how: Prepare 3-4 STAR examples: a time you made a measurable impact, a time a problem arose and you controlled the outcome, and a time your integrity was tested
items.hack: Our founder's specific lines: nobody in the room cares about your rank, so drop it; dress better than the interviewer; have questions ready and research the panel; ask 'do you have any hesitations about moving forward with me as a candidate?'; if salary comes up, answer 'it sounds like you're making me an offer — are you making me an offer?'; follow up with a thank-you that states you can see yourself there. Veterans have documented accountability for budget, personnel and equipment — quantify it

items.title: The Referral Play — Network Before You Need It
items.who: Anyone job hunting after service
items.value: A concrete method for converting LinkedIn connections into referrals, which the files identify as the single highest-yield job search channel
items.how: Look up someone at the target company on LinkedIn, connect, have a real conversation, then list them as a referral on the application; attend veteran networking events (Veteran Beer Club, NDIA, SDMAC, local chamber, job fairs)
items.hack: Our founder's realities check on the job market: many advertised jobs are already filled or unfunded; internal candidates usually have preference; a job search runs two weeks to three months with long silences; even retired O-6s struggle; age and overqualification are real filters. The counter is a referral from inside. His framing: 'it's not what you know, it's who you know' and 'know who's who in the zoo'

items.title: Boots to Business (SBA)
items.who: Service members, veterans and military spouses — a TAP entrepreneurship track
items.value: Free two-day entrepreneurship course plus the follow-on Revenue Readiness and Reboot courses, covering business model, funding and SBA resources
items.how: Register at sbavets.force.com or through your TAP office
items.hack: Take it while still in uniform as the TAP entrepreneurship track — it is the on-ramp to SBA veteran lending and certification, not just a class
items.deadline: Offered through TAP while serving and to veterans afterward

items.title: SBA Veteran Business Support — OSDBU, VOSB/SDVOSB Certification, Lending
items.org: Small Business Administration / VA Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization
items.who: Veteran and service-disabled veteran business owners
items.value: Free business counseling, SBA lending with veteran fee advantages, and VOSB/SDVOSB certification that opens set-aside federal contracting
items.how: Start at sba.gov's veteran business outreach centers and certify through the SBA's Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert)
items.hack: Our founder's business plays around this: form the LLC early and season it at least five years because lenders and contracting officers weight company age; consider the S-corp tax election (Form 2553) to reduce self-employment tax; business credit does not appear on your personal credit report; look for grants alongside loans. Certification moved to the SBA from the VA — verify the current process

items.title: VetFran — Franchise Discounts for Veterans
items.who: Veterans considering franchise ownership
items.value: Directory of franchisors offering veterans reduced franchise fees, financing incentives and dedicated support
items.how: Search participating brands at vetfran.org
items.hack: Incentives vary enormously by brand — use the directory to compare fee reductions before choosing a concept, and pair with SBA veteran lending

items.title: Troops to Teachers and Helmets to Hardhats
items.org: Proud to Serve Again (Troops to Teachers) / Helmets to Hardhats
items.who: Veterans entering K-12 teaching or the building trades
items.value: Two structured second-career pipelines: teacher certification and placement support, and direct placement into union apprenticeships in the construction trades
items.how: proudtoserveagain.com and helmetstohardhats.org (866-741-6210)
items.hack: Helmets to Hardhats feeds union apprenticeships, many of which are VA-approved for GI Bill on-the-job training — you can draw the housing allowance on top of apprentice wages. Verify Troops to Teachers' current federal funding status, as the program has been restructured

items.title: Tech for Troops — Free Refurbished Computers
items.who: Veterans and their children
items.value: Free refurbished computers and basic IT training for veterans who need a machine for job searching or school
items.how: Request at techfortroops.org

items.title: VAREP — Veterans Association of Real Estate Professionals
items.org: Veterans Association of Real Estate Professionals
items.who: Veterans working in or entering real estate, mortgage and housing-adjacent fields, and veteran homebuyers
items.value: Free education on VA loan mechanics, homeownership counseling for veterans, and a professional network and chapter structure for veterans in the industry
items.how: Join a chapter through varep.net
items.hack: Directly relevant if you are a veteran building a real estate or mortgage practice serving veterans — the chapter network is both a referral source and a credibility marker. Several brokerages (Metro Brokers VET to REP, Long & Foster, Century 21, PenFed Realty, Edina Realty) also run veteran real estate license scholarship or training programs

items.title: Military Spouse Professional License Portability
items.org: State licensing boards / Joining Forces initiative
items.who: Military spouses (and in many states veterans) holding a professional license who relocate on orders
items.value: Expedited licensure, temporary licenses, reciprocity or exam waivers so a license does not have to be rebuilt from scratch at every PCS — real estate, nursing, teaching, cosmetology and many others
items.how: Check the destination state's licensing board for 'military spouse,' 'reciprocity' or 'license by endorsement'; DoD also reimburses certain relicensing costs after a PCS
items.hack: Rules are state-by-state and change often; Our founder's file lists roughly two dozen states with real estate provisions for California licensees. Always verify on the destination board's own site, and ask about the DoD relicensing reimbursement, which many spouses never claim
items.deadline: Often tied to PCS date

items.title: VA Home Loan and Certificate of Eligibility
items.who: Eligible service members, veterans and some surviving spouses
items.value: Zero down payment, no private mortgage insurance, and no VA-imposed credit score minimum — the single largest wealth-building benefit in the file
items.how: Request the Certificate of Eligibility through VA.gov or have a VA-approved lender pull it
items.hack: Our founder's core lender insight: the VA sets no credit score minimum, but lenders add their own rules called overlays — the game is finding a lender or broker with few overlays. Also, BAH is tax-free and lenders gross it up (his files say roughly 125%), giving a service member more buying power than a civilian earning the same gross. Get the COE early; it is on the 3-months-out checklist
items.deadline: Obtain COE ~3 months out

items.title: VA Funding Fee Exemption at 10% Disability
items.who: Veterans receiving VA compensation for a service-connected disability (the files cite 10% or more), plus certain surviving spouses and Purple Heart recipients
items.value: Waives the VA loan funding fee entirely — on a large loan this is thousands of dollars saved at closing, on every VA loan you ever use
items.how: The lender applies the exemption once your rating is documented; if the fee was charged before your rating came through, request a refund
items.hack: Our founder flags this twice. Two actions: (1) even a 10% rating pays for itself here, which is an argument for filing the claim; (2) if you closed a VA loan before your rating was granted and the rating is retroactive to before closing, you may be owed a funding fee REFUND — most veterans never ask. The exact percentage varies by down payment and prior use, so do not rely on the 3.15% figure in these files
items.deadline: Refunds can be requested retroactively in some cases

items.title: Second VA Loan Using Remaining Entitlement
items.who: Veterans who already have a VA loan on a property and want to buy again
items.value: You can hold more than one VA loan at once; where entitlement is partly used, you cover 25% of the amount above the county limit rather than a full down payment
items.how: Have a VA-knowledgeable lender calculate remaining entitlement against the new county loan limit
items.hack: Our founder's worked example: a $400k VA loan in Florida, then a $700k purchase in a county with a $1M limit — you are $100k over the guaranteed amount, so you bring roughly $25k (25% of the difference) instead of a conventional down payment, and 75% of the rental income from the first home can help you qualify. Dual-military couples should use BOTH members' entitlements. County limits and entitlement rules change — have the lender run the current numbers, not this example

items.title: Restore VA Entitlement by Refinancing to Conventional
items.who: Veterans who own a home on a VA loan and want to buy again without a county limit
items.value: Refinancing the existing VA loan into a conventional loan releases the entitlement, restoring full VA eligibility for the next purchase with no county cap (subject to qualifying)
items.how: Refinance the existing VA loan to conventional, keeping 20% equity in the property to avoid PMI, then apply for a new VA loan
items.hack: Our founder's sequence: buy with VA at 0% down, live in it, convert it to a rental after roughly two years, refinance to conventional when rates allow (pulling cash out to consolidate debt if it makes sense), which restores 100% of the VA entitlement for the next purchase. Cautions he includes: a cash-out refi resets the amortization clock, lender max LTV on cash-out is often around 90%, and closing costs plus the funding fee can eat the proceeds. This is his strategy, not a VA program — run it past a lender and a tax professional

items.title: Military Capital Gains Exclusion — Extended Ownership Window
items.who: Service members on qualified official extended duty who sell a former primary residence
items.value: Military members can suspend the running of the ownership-and-use test, giving far longer than the civilian 2-of-5-years rule to sell a home and still exclude gain
items.how: Discuss the suspension election with a CPA when you sell; it is claimed on the return, not automatic
items.hack: Our founder's files describe it as 2-of-10 for military versus 2-of-5 for civilians. The statutory suspension period and its conditions are specific — do not rely on the shorthand; have a tax professional confirm it applies to your duty history before you sell. He also notes the exclusion caps (single vs married filing jointly) and a separate, aggressive play of refinancing before a sale to pull cash tax-free — that one is his strategy and warrants real tax advice
items.deadline: Tied to periods of qualified extended duty

items.title: Navy Federal Military Choice and Homebuyers Choice Loans
items.who: Navy Federal members, including veterans and family members
items.value: 100% financing mortgage products for members who have exhausted VA entitlement or do not qualify for a VA loan, plus competitive auto loan rates and free notary and document certification
items.how: Apply through navyfederal.org
items.hack: Our founder's specific uses: Navy Federal as the refinance escape when a dealer wrote a high-interest car loan; a rate reduction for senior enlisted on auto loans; free certification of your DD-214; free certification exam vouchers; and a trust account option. Compare rates rather than assuming the credit union always wins

items.title: Down Payment Assistance and State Veteran Loan Programs
items.org: State housing finance agencies (CalVet, CalHFA, Texas VLB and others) / Down Payment Resource
items.who: Veteran and first-time buyers, varying by state program
items.value: Grants and second-lien programs that cover down payment and closing costs, plus state-run veteran mortgage programs that are separate from the federal VA loan
items.how: Search programs at downpaymentresource.com and your state's veterans and housing agencies
items.hack: Our founder's point for California: CalVet and CalHFA are separate doors from the VA loan and can stack with it or replace it — many veterans never check the state program. Every state differs, so check the destination state before a PCS purchase
items.deadline: Program funds are often first-come and reset by fiscal year

items.title: State Veteran Benefits — Property Tax, Registration, Licenses, Tuition
items.who: Veterans, with benefits keyed to residency and often to disability rating
items.value: State-level benefits stack on top of federal: property tax exemptions (full exemption in some states at 100% disability), free or reduced vehicle registration and veteran plates, free hunting and fishing licenses, state park access, dependent tuition waivers, and state hiring preference
items.how: Start with the VA's state benefit directory and your state department of veterans affairs; county VSOs handle many applications
items.hack: Our founder's two plays: check your state and local veteran tax laws as part of the retirement move decision, and consider relocating to a veteran-friendly state (no income tax states like Texas and Florida; Texas Hazlewood Act and full property tax exemption at 100%). These vary wildly and change by legislature — verify with the state, never from a national summary
items.deadline: Property tax exemptions often have annual filing deadlines

items.title: Final Move (HHG) Benefit and Storage
items.org: Military Surface Deployment and Distribution Command / move.mil
items.who: Separating and retiring service members
items.value: The government moves your household goods after you leave — the planner and Navy guide cite up to one year post-retirement with extensions available
items.how: Schedule household goods transportation counseling 6-12 months out and file through move.mil
items.hack: Our founder's note: you do not have to use it immediately. Retirees can hold the benefit for a year or more (with extensions) while deciding where to settle, and can extend further for schooling in some cases. Also decide early whether to take terminal leave or sell back leave — you cannot do both with the same days
items.deadline: Generally within 1 year of separation, extensions possible

items.title: Permissive TDY (House and Job Hunting) Plus Terminal Leave
items.who: Separating and retiring service members
items.value: Up to 20 days of permissive TDY for house and job hunting, taken alongside terminal leave — paid time to actually find work and housing
items.how: Submit a PTDY request chit separately from your terminal leave request; file the PTDY voucher with DFAS afterward
items.hack: Our founder's planning notes: accrue up to 60 days of leave ahead of transition; request terminal leave explicitly labeled 'terminal' and count back from your official retirement date; PTDY is a separate chit, not part of the leave request; the separation physical must be complete before you go on terminal leave, or you will not be released. And a SkillBridge or civilian job started during terminal leave means drawing both military and civilian pay
items.deadline: Separation physical must be complete before terminal leave starts

items.title: Free Camps and Enrichment Grants for Military Kids
items.org: Camp Corral, Our Military Kids, United Heroes League, Military Teen Adventure Camps (Purdue Extension), Boys & Girls Clubs
items.who: Children of wounded, ill, injured or fallen service members, and military children generally
items.value: Free summer camp (Camp Corral), grants for tutoring, sports and arts (Our Military Kids), free sports equipment and tickets (United Heroes League), free adventure camps for teens, and free Boys & Girls Club membership
items.how: Apply to each: campcorral.org, ourmilitarykids.org/apply, unitedheroesleague.org, ag.purdue.edu adventure camps, bgca.org/about-us/military
items.hack: Apply in winter and early spring — these are summer programs with application deadlines months ahead, and Our founder's family-first theme is that these are the benefits parents most often miss because the deadlines pass quietly
items.deadline: Summer programs — applications close in spring

items.title: United Through Reading
items.who: Deployed or separated service members and their children
items.value: Free recorded video or audio sessions of a parent reading a children's book, sent home to the child
items.how: Record through unitedthroughreading.org or at a participating location
items.hack: Works for weekend duty and TDY, not just deployment

items.title: Free Lawn Care, Snow Removal and Pet Boarding During Deployment
items.org: Project EverGreen GreenCare for Troops, SnowCare for Troops, Dogs on Deployment
items.who: Deployed service members' families, generally enlisted
items.value: Free lawn maintenance, free snow and ice removal, and free volunteer pet boarding while the service member is deployed
items.how: Register at projectevergreen.org/greencare-for-troops, bossplow.com snowcare-for-troops, and dogsondeployment.org
items.hack: Register before the deployment starts — matching to a local volunteer provider takes time
items.deadline: Register ahead of deployment

items.title: Free Photography for Military Families
items.org: Hearts Apart, Operation Love Reunited, Operation We Are Here, JCPenney Portraits
items.who: Deploying and returning service members and their families
items.value: Free professional photo sessions before deployment and on homecoming, plus a free print and discounted package at JCPenney Portraits
items.how: heartsapart.org, operationlovereunited.com, operationwearehere.com, jcpportraits.com military offer
items.hack: Our founder's related note: take lots of pictures, journal the deployments and cruises, and back it all up to Google Drive — the record matters later, both personally and for awards
items.deadline: Book around deployment and homecoming dates

items.title: Brides Across America — Free Wedding Gowns
items.who: Military and first responder brides, and military spouses
items.value: Free wedding gowns given away at participating bridal salons during scheduled events
items.how: Find an event at bridesacrossamerica.com
items.hack: Event-based and location-specific — register for event notifications rather than checking periodically
items.deadline: Event-based giveaways

items.title: Operation Ride Home
items.who: Junior enlisted service members and their families traveling home for the holidays
items.value: Financial assistance with holiday travel home
items.how: Apply through asymca.org when the seasonal application opens
items.hack: Seasonal — the application window opens in the fall for December travel
items.deadline: Seasonal, fall application window

items.title: Cell Phones for Soldiers
items.who: Deployed service members and veterans in need
items.value: Free international calling cards for deployed troops, funded by recycled phone donations, plus emergency communication support for veterans
items.how: Request talk time at cellphonesforsoldiers.com

items.title: MilitaryChildCare.com
items.who: Military families needing childcare
items.value: Single portal to request military-provided and military-affiliated childcare across all services, including fee assistance for off-base care
items.how: Register and request care at militarychildcare.com
items.hack: Waitlists are long — get on the list as soon as PCS orders are known, not after arrival
items.deadline: Waitlists — apply as early as possible

items.title: TAPS — Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors
items.who: Anyone grieving the death of a military loved one, regardless of how or when they died
items.value: Free 24/7 grief support line, peer mentorship, survivor seminars, Good Grief Camps for children, and help navigating survivor benefits
items.how: Call the TAPS national helpline or start at taps.org
items.hack: TAPS serves survivors of any military death — including illness, accident and suicide, not only combat deaths. That eligibility breadth is widely misunderstood

items.title: Elizabeth Dole Foundation — Caregiver Support
items.who: Military and veteran caregivers — spouses, parents and others caring for a wounded, ill or injured veteran
items.value: Free caregiver resources, respite programs, peer networks and a fellows program; advocacy that has expanded VA caregiver benefits
items.how: Start at elizabethdolefoundation.org
items.hack: Pair with the VA Caregiver Program — the foundation handles community and respite, the VA handles the stipend and health coverage

items.title: National Resource Directory (NRD.gov)
items.org: Department of Defense / VA / Department of Labor
items.who: Wounded service members, veterans, families and caregivers
items.value: Federally maintained searchable database of vetted national, state and local resources across benefits, housing, employment, health and family support
items.how: Search by need and location at nrd.gov
items.hack: Our founder marks this as one of two go-to portals when you do not know which program you need — search by state to surface local organizations that never appear in national lists

items.title: Operation We Are Here — Resource Portal
items.who: Military families, warriors and caregivers
items.value: A long-running volunteer-maintained index of military and veteran resources organized by need, including many small programs missing from official directories
items.how: Browse operationwearehere.com
items.hack: Our founder names this and NRD.gov as his 'two best resource portals to date' — use NRD for vetted federal/state programs and Operation We Are Here for the long tail of small nonprofits

items.title: Code of Support Foundation — PATRIOTlink
items.who: Veterans, service members, families, caregivers and the case managers serving them
items.value: A free searchable database of vetted, no-cost direct services for the military community, plus intensive one-on-one case coordination for complex cases
items.how: Search PATRIOTlink at codeofsupport.org
items.hack: Where NRD is broad, PATRIOTlink is filtered to free direct services only — useful when the constraint is money, not information

items.title: Benefits.gov Military Category and VA Benefits A-Z
items.org: US Government / Department of Veterans Affairs
items.who: Any veteran or service member trying to find what they qualify for
items.value: Official eligibility screeners and the VA's own A-Z list of every benefit it administers, plus the VA's list of benefits offered by other federal agencies
items.how: benefits.gov military category, va.gov benefits A-Z, and the VA's other-federal-benefits page
items.hack: Our founder's closing line on benefits: 'As thorough as I have been, keep searching — there are much more benefits available.' Use the official A-Z list as the checklist rather than any circulated PDF, and re-check annually because eligibility rules expand

items.title: Always Ask for the Military Discount
items.who: Every service member, veteran and retiree
items.value: A behavioral habit, not a program: discounts that are never advertised get given when asked, including after retirement
items.how: Ask in person, ask in online chat before purchase, ask customer service after purchase, and ask for a price match if you find it cheaper
items.hack: Our founder's framing: 'Closed mouths don't get fed.' Specific tactics — ask even while in uniform, because the store still needs you to ask; call or use chat when shopping online; request a discount code by email before buying; ask for a retroactive credit after buying; keep asking as a retiree. He pairs this with knowing Costco's extended electronics return policy and Amex purchase, cell phone and payment protections

items.title: Apply Early in the Fiscal Year — Program Funds Run Out
items.who: Anyone applying for any funded military or veteran program
items.value: A timing rule that determines whether an application is funded at all
items.how: Know that the federal fiscal year runs 1 October to 30 September and submit funded applications early in it
items.hack: Our founder's exact point: program money often runs out before the fiscal year ends, so a perfectly eligible application filed in August may be denied for funding while the same application in October is approved. He pairs this with a second rule — be persistent and ask a different person: 'Don't let an opportunity pass you by because someone misinformed you; this happens often'
items.deadline: Federal fiscal year 1 Oct - 30 Sep

items.title: The 'I Love Me' Binder and Digital Backup System
items.who: Every service member, from day one
items.value: A complete, scanned, cloud-backed record of awards, evaluations, certifications, qualifications, orders and medical records — the raw material for promotions, VA claims, federal resumes and discharge corrections
items.how: Scan everything with a phone scanner app (Genius Scan), organize into folders in Google Drive, and keep a rolling brag sheet and professional resume updated continuously
items.hack: Our founder's rule: 'Make copies of EVERYTHING — paperwork always somehow gets lost, cover your six.' Specifics from his files: keep a running professional resume plus a federal resume, scan every set of orders, validate your record annually so it is clean at promotion time, write up your own awards so they are ready to route, and keep the DD-214 and disability rating letter available from your phone for discount verification
items.deadline: Start on day one; do not wait for transition

items.title: The 33% Rule — Build a Three-Layer Mentor Network
items.who: Service members at any stage, and veterans building a civilian network
items.value: A concrete structure for who should be around you: a third above you to mentor, a third at your level to challenge you, a third junior to teach
items.how: Deliberately recruit into each layer — multiple mentors for multiple perspectives, peers who hold you accountable, and juniors you actively pay it forward to
items.hack: Our founder pairs this with finding a 'champion' — someone with the positional power to put you in the roles where you grow, distinct from a mentor who advises. His blunt version: 'As hard a worker as you are, nobody gets where they are without leadership placing them into key positions.' And 'work your boss out of a job' — assume their responsibilities and you get championed

items.title: Talk to the SME, Not the Facilitator
items.who: Anyone navigating military benefits, transition programs or VA claims
items.value: A verification habit that prevents losing benefits to bad information from people reading a script
items.how: When an answer sounds wrong, escalate to someone who has actually done the process — a VSO who files claims, a lender who closes VA loans, a counselor who has transitioned
items.hack: Our founder's version: 'Most times you run into a facilitator who just reads off a PowerPoint without ever having done it.' Paired rules: be persistent, ask a different person, validate from multiple sources and reach your own conclusion; research pros and cons rather than going by rumor; 'trust but verify — it's your career'

items.title: Run the 20-vs-30-Year Retirement Math Before You Re-up
items.who: Career service members deciding whether to stay past 20 years
items.value: A framework showing that staying longer is not automatically the richer choice once retirement pay, VA disability, GI Bill housing allowance and civilian salary are stacked
items.how: Model total compensation from retirement age to 65 under both paths, including pension percentage (High-3 vs BRS), VA disability, GI Bill housing allowance during school, and realistic civilian salary
items.hack: Our founder's own analysis found that for E-7, E-9 and O-4 the 20-year path often wins because you enter the civilian workforce a decade earlier, while for O-6 the 30-year path wins on the much larger pension and active duty pay. His line: at a certain stack, 'staying in the military longer is in fact costing you money — the additional 2.5% per year doesn't match this setup.' CRITICAL CAVEAT: every dollar figure in his model is from 2025 pay tables and assumes 100% VA disability and a specific salary — treat the METHOD as the takeaway and rebuild the numbers with current rates and your own realistic civilian offer. He also flags that concurrent receipt rules limit drawing full retired pay and VA compensation at some ratings, and that GI Bill housing allowance while employed may be constrained
items.deadline: Decision point typically around year 15

items.title: Start Transition Prep at Year 15, Not Year 19
items.who: Career service members
items.value: A timeline rule: the preparation that makes transition work (degree, certifications, network, documented medical record, marketability) takes years, not months
items.how: At year 15, begin treating transition as a project — finish the degree on TA, get the certifications through COOL, build LinkedIn before you need it, and document medical issues
items.hack: Our founder's framing: 'Don't just stay in the military because of job security — after 20 years all good things eventually come to an end. At year 15 really get serious and prep yourself.' A related warning he raises: know whether you will age out of a target career (he cites federal agent age limits) before you decide to stay another tour
items.deadline: Year 15 of a 20-year career

items.title: VA Disability Compensation
items.who: Served on active duty, active duty for training, or inactive-duty training; discharged other than dishonorable; at least 10% disabled by an injury or disease incurred in or aggravated during that service
items.value: Tax-free monthly payment scaled to combined rating; additional allowance for dependents once the combined evaluation reaches 30%
items.how: File on VA.gov (Disability > File a claim for compensation), in person at a VA regional office or a military-installation intake site, or mail VA Form 21-526EZ to Department of Veterans Affairs, Claims Intake Center, PO Box 4444, Janesville, WI 53547-4444
items.hack: There is no deadline to file, but the filing date sets the effective date. File within one year of separation and the award is retroactive to the day after separation; file later and it runs only from the date VA receives the claim. VA Form 21-526EZ has room for 15 conditions; use VA Form 21-4138 as a continuation sheet
items.deadline: File within 1 year of separation to keep retroactivity to the day after discharge

items.title: Notice of Intent to File
items.who: Any veteran or service member preparing a disability or pension claim
items.value: Locks in an effective date for back pay while you gather evidence
items.how: Open the claim on VA.gov, which starts a 12-month clock to submit the completed claim
items.hack: Costs nothing and takes minutes. Do it the day you decide to file, before you have your records together - the back pay accrues from the intent-to-file date, not from the day you finally submit
items.deadline: Complete the claim within 12 months of the intent-to-file date

items.title: Fully Developed Claim (FDC)
items.who: Anyone from 90 days before separation onward, with no time limit after
items.value: Faster decision than a traditional claim
items.how: Submit all evidence in your possession or easily obtainable, certify there are no more records VA needs, and attend any required VA exam
items.hack: Unlike BDD, you can work with a Veterans Service Officer on an FDC. This is the usual recommendation for a veteran who wants both speed and free representation
items.deadline: No filing deadline

items.title: Traditional (Standard) Disability Claim
items.who: Any claimant whose claim does not qualify for BDD or FDC
items.value: Full VA duty-to-assist development; VA gathers the evidence for you
items.how: File on VA.gov or by VA Form 21-526EZ; runs through the standard eight-step claim process
items.hack: Not given priority processing - expect significantly longer timelines than FDC
items.deadline: No filing deadline

items.title: The Eight-Step VA Claim Process
items.who: Every disability claimant
items.value: Knowing which of the eight steps your claim sits at tells you whether VA is still gathering evidence or has moved to decision
items.how: Steps: (1) VA receives claim, (2) claim assigned to a Veterans Service Representative, (3) VSR gathers evidence, (4) VSR reviews evidence, (5) VSR prepares a recommended decision, (6) VA reviews the recommendation, (7) VA prepares the claim packet, (8) VA sends the decision packet
items.hack: Submitting maximum evidence up front collapses step 3, which is where most of the calendar time lives
items.deadline: None

items.title: The Five Ways to Establish Service Connection
items.who: Any claimant
items.value: Each path is an independent route to a grant; a claim denied on one theory may win on another
items.how: Direct (evidence shows the injury or disease was incurred in service); aggravation (a preexisting condition was made worse by service); secondary/proximate cause (a disability proximately due to an already service-connected condition - e.g. cardiovascular disease following a service-connected lower-limb amputation); 38 USC 1151 (disability caused by VA medical care or VA vocational rehabilitation, treated as if service-connected); and statutory presumption (conditions Congress or regulation deems incurred in service without in-service evidence)
items.hack: Secondary service connection is the most underused. If you already hold a rating, map what that condition has caused downstream and claim those separately
items.deadline: None

items.title: Integrated Disability Evaluation System (IDES)
items.who: Active-duty service members who remain in service despite an injury and are being evaluated for fitness for duty
items.value: Produces a proposed VA disability rating before separation, without the member filing a separate claim
items.how: Entered through the medical evaluation board / physical evaluation board process; DoD determines fitness for duty and VA proposes the rating
items.hack: The proposed rating tells you your approximate compensation before you leave, which lets you plan the civilian transition on real numbers rather than guesses
items.deadline: Driven by the MEB/PEB timeline, not by you

items.title: Separation Health Assessment (SHA) vs DoD Separation History and Physical Exam (SHPE)
items.who: Every separating service member gets a DoD SHPE; those filing a BDD claim get VA's SHA instead
items.value: One VA SHA satisfies both VA's disability exam requirement and DoD's separation physical requirement
items.how: File a BDD pre-discharge claim 180-90 days before separation AND request the exam at least 90 days before separation to receive VA's SHA. File later than 90 days, or not at all, and you receive DoD's SHPE
items.hack: This is the single highest-leverage scheduling decision in the whole transition. Getting one exam instead of two, on VA's form, is why the 180-90 day window matters. The SHPE is normally conducted 90-180 days prior to retirement or the start of terminal leave
items.deadline: Request at least 90 days before separation

items.title: Compensation and Pension (C&P) Exam
items.who: Claimants whose claim requires a medical opinion
items.value: The examiner's report is frequently the single document that decides the rating
items.how: VA schedules it after the claim is filed; it is separate from the SHPE and from ordinary treatment visits. Expect additional separate appointments for mental health, dental, eye, ear, and TBI claims
items.hack: Practical guidance drawn from the source documents: read your own military, VA, and private medical records first; review 38 CFR Part 4 for the criteria of your condition; describe your worst day, not your best; explain functional limitation, not just diagnosis; bring hard-copy documents; and ask your accredited VSO to request a copy of the exam report afterward. The examiner is not your treating provider - the appointment exists to rate you, not to treat you
items.deadline: Attend when scheduled; missing it can result in denial

items.title: VA Schedule for Rating Disabilities (VASRD), 38 CFR Part 4
items.who: Anyone with a rated or claimable condition
items.value: The actual legal criteria VA applies; ratings run 0% to 100% in 10% increments, based on average impairment of earning capacity, under authority of 38 USC 1155
items.how: Read the diagnostic code for your condition at the eCFR
items.hack: Look up your condition's criteria BEFORE the C&P exam so you know which specific findings the examiner needs to document. This is the difference between a 10% and a 30% for the same condition
items.deadline: None

items.title: Total Disability based on Individual Unemployability (TDIU)
items.who: Veterans unable to secure or follow substantially gainful employment because of service-connected disabilities
items.value: Paid at the 100% rate without a 100% schedular rating, and carries most of the derivative benefits of a 100% rating
items.how: Claim it; VA also has an obligation to consider it when the record raises it
items.hack: The 2012 checklist in this set gives TDIU its own full page of benefits - CHAMPVA for dependents, all necessary dental care, Chapter 35 DEA for spouse and children, VMLI, Specially Adapted Housing, property tax exemption, supplemental S-DVI, and VA life insurance premium waiver under 65. The 'Additional VA Disability Benefits Chart' by contrast reduces TDIU to a single bullet inside the 60-90% row. Treat TDIU as its own tier
items.deadline: None

items.title: Special Monthly Compensation (SMC)
items.who: Veterans with specific anatomical losses, loss of use, housebound status, or need for aid and attendance
items.value: Compensation above the normal rating schedule for losses the percentage system does not capture
items.how: Claimed with or after the underlying disability claim
items.hack: The 2012 checklist maps which losses become claimable at which rating tier: loss or loss of use of a creative organ at 0%; add loss of a female breast or one eye at 30%; add one foot at 40%; add one hand at 60%; add both buttocks at 80%; at 100% add complete deafness in both ears, complete organic aphonia, and the paired-extremity combinations. Also at 100%: housebound, aid and attendance, and the '100% plus 60% separately ratable' statutory housebound provision. Paired organs where one is service-connected and one is not are covered by 38 CFR 3.383
items.deadline: None

items.title: Statutory Housebound (100% plus separate 60%)
items.who: A veteran with one service-connected disability rated 100% plus additional conditions independently ratable at 60% or more in combination
items.value: Special monthly compensation at the housebound rate, on top of the 100% rate
items.how: VA should apply it automatically when the rating picture qualifies, but it is frequently missed - raise it in writing
items.hack: This is the one benefit the 'Additional VA Disability Benefits Chart' gives its own dedicated row, and it is genuinely commonly overlooked. If you are at 100% for a single condition and hold other ratings, do the 60% math on the remaining conditions
items.deadline: None

items.title: Annual Clothing Allowance
items.who: Veterans whose service-connected condition requires a prosthetic or orthopedic appliance, or a wheelchair, that wears out clothing - or who use a prescribed skin medication that damages clothing
items.value: An annual payment; the checklist shows it claimable from a 0% rating upward
items.how: Apply through VA; a VA clinician certifies the appliance or medication
items.hack: Listed as available at every rating tier from 0% in the 2012 checklist - most veterans with a brace, a prosthesis, or a prescribed topical never claim it
items.deadline: Annual claim cycle

items.title: Automobile Allowance and Adaptive Equipment
items.who: Per the 2012 checklist, possible eligibility begins at a 40% overall rating; the governing rule keys on loss or permanent loss of use of a hand or foot, permanent impairment of vision in both eyes, or severe burn injury
items.value: A one-time payment toward a specially adapted automobile, plus a separate adaptive-equipment allowance
items.how: Apply to VA; the vehicle grant and the adaptive equipment allowance are separate claims
items.hack: The adaptive equipment allowance can be claimed more than once over a lifetime even though the vehicle grant is one-time
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Form 21-22, Appointment of Veterans Service Organization as Claimant's Representative
items.who: Any claimant who wants a VSO to represent them
items.value: A limited power of attorney letting a chartered VSO act for you on VA claim matters only - free of charge
items.how: Complete VA Form 21-22 (the VSO or VA will supply it) and file it with the claim
items.hack: Accredited VSO representation is free by law. It is unlawful for anyone to charge a fee to help prepare a VA claim before VA has issued its initial decision - organizations advertising 'no fee until we win' are charging on the post-decision side
items.deadline: File before or with the claim

items.title: VA Office of General Counsel Accredited Representative Search
items.who: Anyone looking for a VSO representative, accredited claims agent, or accredited attorney
items.value: The authoritative directory of who is actually accredited to represent you
items.how: Search by name, city, state, or ZIP on VA.gov under Veterans Service Organizations
items.hack: Check accreditation before signing anything. Accreditation status is the line between a free chartered VSO and a paid claims consultant
items.deadline: None

items.title: DD Form 2870, Authorization for Disclosure of Medical Information
items.who: Any service member who wants a copy of their own military health record
items.value: Your complete service treatment record - the evidentiary spine of every disability claim
items.how: Submit DD Form 2870 to the facility holding your record; expect a CD or a DoD SAFE link to an electronic copy
items.hack: Two practical notes from the Navy guide: the DoD health record is government property and you are entitled to a copy, not the original; and the DoD SAFE link cannot be sent to a .mil address, so supply a personal address. Request it 6-12 months before separation, not in the final weeks
items.deadline: Start 6-12 months before separation

items.title: DD Form 2807-1, Report of Medical History
items.who: Every separating service member
items.value: Your own sworn account of every condition, and the document VA reads first
items.how: Complete it honestly, then cross-check it line by line against the medical record you obtained with DD Form 2870 and amend it for anything the record shows that you forgot - asbestos exposure is the example the Navy guide gives
items.hack: The single most common self-inflicted wound in the whole process is under-reporting on this form. If a condition is not documented anywhere, make a medical appointment and get it documented before you separate
items.deadline: Completed as part of the separation physical

items.title: VA Forms 21-686c and 21-674, Adding Dependents
items.who: Rated veterans at 30% combined or higher, who are entitled to an additional allowance for a spouse, children, and dependent parents
items.value: An additional monthly amount per dependent, plus a possible aid-and-attendance allowance for a disabled spouse
items.how: VA Form 21-686c for dependents generally; VA Form 21-674 (Request for Approval of School Attendance) for children aged 18-23 in school
items.hack: The 30% threshold is the trigger. Veterans who cross 30% on an increase frequently never file the dependency forms and leave the add-on unpaid. Bring marriage certificate, birth certificates, divorce decrees, Social Security cards, and school information to the appointment
items.deadline: File promptly - the add-on generally runs from when VA receives the dependency claim

items.title: Request Military Service Records / Replace a Lost DD 214
items.who: Any veteran or next of kin
items.value: Replacement DD 214 and other service records
items.how: Request at VA.gov/records/get-military-service-records
items.hack: Corrections are a different process: a DD Form 215 must be issued, and a corrected DD 214 follows. You cannot simply annotate the original
items.deadline: None

items.title: The Eight Versions of the DD 214 (and which ones you keep)
items.who: Every separating member
items.value: Different copies carry different content; the wrong copy can cost you a benefit
items.how: Copies are MEMBER-1, SERVICE-2, VETERANS ADMINISTRATION-3, MEMBER-4, DEPARTMENT OF LABOR-5, STATE DIRECTOR OF VETERANS AFFAIRS-6, SERVICE-7, and SERVICE-8
items.hack: Sign for and physically take the MEMBER-1 and MEMBER-4 copies on your last day. MEMBER-4 is the one VA, VSOs, and most employers want because it carries the narrative reason for separation. The Navy guide's field tip: highlight the original in yellow highlighter and make certified copies (a credit union such as NFCU will certify them). Store the printed originals somewhere your next of kin knows about
items.deadline: Last day of service

items.title: Validation of Awards Before the DD 214 Is Cut
items.who: Every separating member, especially anyone with unit awards
items.value: Awards absent from the DD 214 are effectively lost for employment preference, veteran license plates, and organization membership
items.how: List every award on the separations questionnaire (NPPSC 1900/1 in the Navy), then verify the official military personnel file - for the Navy, BOL at bol.navy.mil, field codes 32 (page 13s) and 37 (awards) - and submit an awards memo with supporting NAVPERS 1070/613 and BOL unit-award printouts as enclosures
items.hack: Unit awards are the ones that go missing. The Navy guide states plainly that if you take no action, awards you earned will not appear on the DD 214
items.deadline: Before the draft DD 214 is finalized, roughly 30-60 days before terminal leave

items.title: Discharge Upgrade / Character of Discharge Review
items.org: DoD discharge review boards, with VA guidance
items.who: Veterans whose character of discharge is blocking benefit eligibility
items.value: Character of discharge is described in the Participant Guide as one of the most important determinants of VA benefit eligibility; an upgrade can unlock the entire benefit set
items.how: Use VA's discharge upgrade instruction tool to identify the right board and application
items.hack: Separately, Vet Center counseling and one year of post-separation mental health care are available regardless of character of discharge - do not wait on an upgrade to get care
items.deadline: Varies by board and by how long since discharge

items.title: VA Health Care Enrollment (VA Form 10-10EZ)
items.who: Generally, served 24 continuous months or the full period called to active duty, without a dishonorable discharge. The minimum-service requirement is waived for those discharged for a service-connected disability or hardship, or who served before September 7, 1980
items.value: Access to the largest integrated health system in the country; enrollment also satisfies the Affordable Care Act minimum essential coverage requirement, and VA mails an annual letter for tax purposes
items.how: Apply online at VA.gov/health-care/apply, by phone at 877-222-8387 option 1 (M-F 8am-8pm ET), in person at a VA medical center, or by mailing VA Form 10-10EZ to the Health Eligibility Center, 2957 Clairmont Road, Suite 200, Atlanta, GA 30329
items.hack: You can apply up to one year before your separation date but no earlier. Gather DD 214 Member-4, most recent tax return, SSNs for you and dependents, current rating information, and the account numbers for any other health insurance. If you have not heard back a week after applying, call 877-222-8387 option 0
items.deadline: Cannot apply more than 1 year before separation; no deadline after

items.title: Enhanced Eligibility Categories for VA Health Care
items.who: Former prisoners of war; Purple Heart or Medal of Honor recipients; veterans with a VA service-connected rating of 10% or more; those discharged for a disability incurred or aggravated in the line of duty; Vietnam service Jan 9 1962 - May 7 1975; certain Navy and Coast Guard ships associated with that service; Persian Gulf service Aug 2 1990 - Nov 11 1998; 30 or more days at Camp Lejeune, NC; veterans VA finds catastrophically disabled; and veterans whose prior-year household income is below VA's national or geographic threshold
items.value: Bypasses the ordinary income-and-priority screening and moves you into a higher priority group
items.how: Identified on the 10-10EZ; supply the supporting documentation
items.hack: Camp Lejeune and the Blue Water Navy ship lists are the two categories veterans most often do not realize apply to them
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Health Care Priority Groups (1 through 8)
items.who: Every enrolled veteran is assigned to one of eight groups
items.value: Determines how quickly VA can enroll you and how much, if anything, you pay in copays
items.how: Assignment is based on service-connected rating, income level, Medicaid qualification, and other benefits received such as pension
items.hack: The structural rule that has held for years: a combined rating of 50% or higher puts you in Priority Group 1 with no copays for any care. Below 50% you land somewhere between 2 and 8, and groups 7 and 8 carry copays. The specific group assigned to a 0% or 10-20% veteran differs between the documents in this set, so confirm yours with VA rather than from any chart
items.deadline: None

items.title: CHAMPVA (Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs)
items.who: Spouse and children of a veteran rated 100% permanently and totally disabled (TDIU-P&T counts), and survivors of a veteran who died of a service-connected condition - unless the dependent is eligible for TRICARE
items.value: Comprehensive health coverage for dependents with no monthly premium
items.how: Download, complete, sign, and mail the application; approval takes roughly eight to twelve weeks
items.hack: This is the highest-value single benefit tied to P&T status, and it is the reason chasing P&T matters more than chasing 100% schedular. The trap: dependents already eligible for TRICARE (i.e. a 20-year retiree's family) cannot use CHAMPVA
items.deadline: None, but allow 8-12 weeks for processing

items.title: VA Dental Insurance Program (VADIP)
items.org: VA, through Delta Dental and MetLife
items.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care, and family members covered under CHAMPVA
items.value: Purchased dental insurance for those who do not qualify for direct VA dental care
items.how: Enroll through the VADIP page on VA.gov
items.hack: There is no enrollment deadline on this one - the Participant Guide's own checklist says 'no time limit associated with this benefit.' It is the fallback for the large majority of enrolled veterans who fall outside the VA dental classes
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Direct Dental Care and the Dental Classes
items.who: Eligibility runs by dental class, not by a single rating threshold; the class depends on military service history, current health, and living situation
items.value: Covered services range from cleaning and X-rays to fillings, crowns, and bridges
items.how: Eligibility is determined at enrollment; ask VA which dental class applies to you
items.hack: Charts that say '100% = free dental care' oversimplify. Former POWs and veterans rated totally disabled (including TDIU) are the categories the source documents identify for full necessary dental treatment. If you are outside a qualifying class, VADIP is the route
items.deadline: For separating members: complete an exit dental exam within 90 days of retirement, and make sure DD 214 block 17 is filled in to record it

items.title: Beneficiary Travel Pay Reimbursement
items.who: Per the charts in this set, available from a 0% service-connected rating for travel to scheduled appointments at a VA medical facility or VA-authorized facility; broader travel pay for all VA health care appears at the 30% tier
items.value: Mileage reimbursement for appointment travel
items.how: Claim through the Beneficiary Travel Self-Service System or at the facility
items.hack: Do not carry forward the cents-per-mile figure in the Navy guide (41.5 cents, 2022) - the rate is set administratively and changes. Claim the mileage; look up the current rate
items.deadline: Claims must be filed within a limited window after the appointment

items.title: VA Vet Centers
items.who: Veterans, active duty service members, members of the reserve components, and their families who meet the eligibility criteria - including those who provided direct emergent medical care or mortuary services while serving
items.value: Free individual, group, marriage, and family counseling, outreach, and referral - with no time limitation
items.how: Walk in or call a Vet Center; find one with the VA facility locator filtered to vet_center
items.hack: Three things make Vet Centers different from a VA medical center: you are eligible regardless of character of discharge, you do not need a disability rating or service connection, and you do not need to be enrolled in VA health care. They keep nontraditional hours, and more than 70% of staff are veterans, most of whom served in combat theaters. Mobile Vet Centers serve areas with no permanent site
items.deadline: None

items.title: One Year of Free Post-Separation Mental Health Care
items.who: Newly separated service members, regardless of discharge status, service history, or eligibility for VA health care
items.value: Free mental health care for one year after separation
items.how: Present at a VA facility or Vet Center
items.hack: This is the benefit with the shortest fuse and the least awareness. The Participant Guide's checklist marks the deadline explicitly as 'within 1 year of separation (for free mental health care)' and adds that you can still file a mental health disability claim after the year has passed. Emergency mental health care is available 24/7 at VA medical centers; a VAMC without a 24-hour ER must arrange 24/7 mental health care through another local hospital
items.deadline: Within 1 year of separation

items.title: Military Sexual Trauma (MST) Care and Claims Support
items.who: Female and male veterans who experienced sexual assault or sexual harassment during service
items.value: Free, confidential counseling and treatment for mental and physical health problems linked to MST, regardless of whether the incident was reported
items.how: Ask at any VA medical center; VA regional offices have MST coordinators, and all regional offices have Women Veterans Coordinators who assist male and female veterans filing MST claims
items.hack: VBA acknowledges MST evidence is hard to locate and will help develop it. Hold onto anything that could serve as evidence - copies of reports to authorities, treatment records, or documentation of difficulties during service - even if you do not intend to file now
items.deadline: No time limit on filing an MST-related claim

items.title: VA Caregiver Support Program
items.who: Primary caregivers of eligible service members and veterans
items.value: Education, resources, and support services for the caregiver
items.how: Apply through the Caregiver Support Program; VA Forms 10-10CG and related
items.hack: Some service members and veterans are eligible for both TSGLI and the Caregiver Support Program - the programs do not offset each other. Caregiver support has its own help line and local Caregiver Support Coordinators at each VA medical center
items.deadline: None

items.title: Fisher House Program
items.org: VA Social Work Service / Fisher House Foundation
items.who: Families and caregivers of veterans and active-duty service members receiving treatment at a participating medical center; eligibility varies by location
items.value: Free lodging near the treating facility - 'a home away from home'
items.how: Request through the social worker or Fisher House manager at the treating medical center
items.hack: Ask the day admission is scheduled, not after the family has already paid for a hotel. Locations are listed on the VA social work site
items.deadline: None

items.title: Women Veterans Health Care and the Women Veterans Call Center
items.who: Women veterans - described in the Participant Guide as the fastest-growing group in the veteran population
items.value: General care plus female-specific services (birth control, preconception counseling, maternity), screenings including Pap smears and mammograms, and care from a female provider on request
items.how: Every VA medical center has a Women Veterans Program Manager who advises, advocates, and coordinates services; the Women Veterans Call Center is staffed entirely by women
items.hack: Call 1-855-829-6636. The Program Manager at your facility is a named human being whose job is to unstick your care - ask for them by title
items.deadline: None

items.title: Transition and Care Management (TCM) / OEF-OIF-OND Case Management
items.who: Combat veterans returning from deployment
items.value: Assigned case managers who connect you to VA care and benefits and advocate inside the system; combat veterans have access to cost-free medical care for any condition related to service in theater
items.how: Ask for the TCM program manager at your local VA medical center
items.hack: The cost-free in-theater-related care window is time-limited after separation, which is exactly why the Navy guide sequences VA health registration immediately post-retirement rather than 'whenever'
items.deadline: Combat-veteran cost-free care has a limited post-separation eligibility period

items.title: VA Health Care Liaison Program (VA Liaisons at Military Treatment Facilities)
items.who: Service members being treated at a military treatment facility who will transfer to VA care
items.value: An on-site VA representative who educates you on VA health care and communicates your needs to the receiving VA facility
items.how: Ask at the MTF; VA Liaisons are posted at named installations
items.hack: This is a warm handoff that exists specifically so the transfer from DoD to VHA does not drop you. Most members never learn the liaison exists
items.deadline: While still in DoD care

items.title: Veteran Community Care (VA MISSION Act)
items.who: Enrolled veterans who meet access or eligibility standards for care outside a VA facility
items.value: Hospital care and medical services from a community provider, paid by VA
items.how: Coordinated through your VA care team; see VA.gov/communitycare
items.hack: Community care triggers automatic sharing of your record through the Veterans Health Information Exchange - which you can opt out of, and back into, if you would rather control that flow
items.deadline: None

items.title: My HealtheVet
items.who: Veterans and VA patients
items.value: Secure messaging with your care team, appointments, lab results, medication history, admission and discharge summaries, and prescription refills
items.how: Register at myhealth.va.gov; accounts come in Basic, Advanced, and Premium tiers, with Premium unlocking the full feature set through in-person or online identity authentication
items.hack: Create the Basic account before you separate and upgrade to Premium after - that is the sequence the Participant Guide's own checklist prescribes. My HealtheVet also hosts an anonymous, confidential substance-use screening tool that routes you to your provider, your TCM manager, or your local Vet Center
items.deadline: None

items.title: Veterans Health Information Exchange (VHIE)
items.who: Any veteran whose record VA shares with community providers
items.value: Control over whether VA automatically shares your electronic health information with non-VA providers
items.how: Opt out, or opt back in, by mail or in person; VA notifies you when automatic sharing begins
items.hack: Most veterans never realize this is a switch they can flip. If you are seeing community providers under the MISSION Act, sharing is usually what you want; if you are not, opting out is a privacy lever
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Health Benefits Explorer
items.who: Anyone deciding whether to enroll
items.value: Shows what you may be eligible for based on your service, before you apply
items.how: Answer a short questionnaire at VA.gov/healthbenefits/apps/explorer
items.hack: Useful as a pre-enrollment reality check, but it is an estimator, not a determination
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Solid Start Program
items.who: Every newly separated service member
items.value: Three proactive outreach calls during the first year after separation, at roughly 90, 180, and 365 days
items.how: VA calls you - the Navy guide identifies the outbound number as 1-800-827-0611
items.hack: Answer it. Solid Start representatives will not ask for financial information and only discuss topics you are comfortable with. Because the program was created by executive order, the calls happen whether or not you have enrolled in anything - it is a free second chance at every deadline you missed
items.deadline: Calls occur in the first 365 days post-separation

items.title: Make the Connection
items.who: Any veteran or family member
items.value: Hundreds of first-person veteran video stories about mental health, organized by experience - preparing for deployment, transitioning, maintaining relationships, managing PTSD
items.how: Browse at maketheconnection.net
items.hack: Built as a doorway for veterans who will not call a clinician but will watch someone who sounds like them
items.deadline: None

items.title: AboutFace
items.who: Veterans experiencing PTSD and their families
items.value: Personal video stories aimed at helping people recognize PTSD and engage with evidence-based care
items.how: ptsd.va.gov/apps/aboutface
items.hack: Pairs with the National Center for PTSD's clinical material at ptsd.va.gov, which is the authoritative source on which PTSD treatments actually have evidence behind them
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Mobile App Store (PTSD Coach, Mindfulness Coach)
items.who: Anyone
items.value: Free clinically designed self-management apps; no VA enrollment required
items.how: Browse mobile.va.gov/appstore
items.hack: PTSD Coach and Mindfulness Coach are the two the Participant Guide singles out. They work as a bridge for a veteran who is not yet willing to make an appointment
items.deadline: None

items.title: BeThere Peer Assistance Program
items.org: Veterans Crisis Line in partnership with Military OneSource
items.who: Service members including reserve components, their families, and transitioning veterans up to 365 days after separation or retirement
items.value: Private conversation with a peer coach who may be a veteran, service member, or military spouse
items.how: veteranscrisisline.net/support/be-there
items.hack: The 365-day window after separation is the operative limit, and it is the same window as free post-separation mental health care and Military OneSource access - three benefits with one clock
items.deadline: Up to 365 days after separation or retirement

items.title: Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) Assistance Program
items.who: Veterans, and others in VA care, experiencing physical, sexual, or psychological harm by a current or former partner or spouse - across heterosexual and same-sex relationships, and not requiring sexual intimacy
items.value: Coordinated safety planning and support
items.how: Talk to the IPV coordinator at your VA medical center, a VA social worker, or any VA health care provider; the National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233
items.hack: Every VA medical center has a designated IPV coordinator - a specific role, not a general referral
items.deadline: None

items.title: Objective Zero Foundation
items.who: Service members, veterans, and their families
items.value: On-demand peer connection and mental health resources by videoconference, voice, or text
items.how: objectivezero.org
items.hack: Listed by VA itself in the Participant Guide's mental health resource table, which is a meaningful vetting signal for a nonprofit
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Chaplain Services and the Center for Faith-Based and Neighborhood Partnerships
items.who: Any veteran in VA care, and families affected by a suicide
items.value: Faith-based counseling for mental health, grief and loss, and conflict resolution; support for those in crisis and those bereaved by suicide; and training for community clergy in suicide prevention
items.how: Ask for chaplain services at the VA medical center
items.hack: An option for veterans who will accept help from a chaplain before they will accept it from a mental health clinic
items.deadline: None

items.title: GI Bill Feedback Tool
items.who: Any GI Bill student with a concern about a school or training facility
items.value: A formal channel to report recruiting and marketing practices, student loan issues, accreditation problems, refund issues, transcript release, transfer of credit, degree plan changes, and post-graduation job claims
items.how: Submit at benefits.va.gov/gibill/feedback.asp
items.hack: Complaints feed VA's oversight of school approval. This is the lever when a school is stonewalling on transcripts or refunds
items.deadline: None

items.title: Marine Gunnery Sergeant John David Fry Scholarship
items.who: Children and surviving spouses of service members who died in the line of duty after September 10, 2001
items.value: Up to 36 months of benefits at the 100% Post-9/11 GI Bill level
items.how: Apply with VA Form 22-5490
items.hack: Children become eligible at 18 (or earlier on high school graduation). A surviving spouse loses eligibility on remarriage. A beneficiary eligible for both Fry and Chapter 35 DEA must pick one - Fry pays at the Post-9/11 rate, which is usually higher. Members of the reserve components who died on weekend drill or annual training can create Fry eligibility
items.deadline: Spouse eligibility ends on remarriage

items.title: Transfer of Post-9/11 GI Bill Entitlement to Dependents (TEB)
items.who: Service members who have served, or agree to serve, at least ten years - the Participant Guide's checklist states the transfer must be executed prior to departing the military
items.value: Moves unused Post-9/11 entitlement to a spouse or children
items.how: Request through milConnect while still serving; VA Form 22-1990E for the dependent
items.hack: Two hard rules that catch people: you must complete the transfer request while still in uniform - it cannot be done after separation - and you do not need all ten years banked first. Six years served plus a four-year reenlistment commitment lets the transfer go through now
items.deadline: Must be executed before leaving the military

items.title: VA Work-Study Allowance (VA Form 22-8691)
items.who: Students in a college degree, vocational, or professional program at three-quarter time or more, using Chapter 30, 31, 32, 33, 35, or 1606 benefits, or transferred entitlement
items.value: Tax-advantaged hourly pay on top of your education benefit, at the greater of the federal or state minimum wage
items.how: Complete VA Form 22-8691 and mail it to the VA Regional Processing Office, P.O. Box 8888, Muskogee, OK 74402-8888; or submit through Ask VA at ask.va.gov. Phone 1-888-GI-BILL-1 (1-888-442-4551); Federal Relay 711
