items.hack: Two mechanics worth knowing. The contract cap is 25 times the number of weeks in the enrollment period. And you can request an advance payment of the lesser of 40% of the total contract or 50 hours at your hourly rate - money up front, before you have worked the hours. Qualifying work includes VA outreach, VA facility work, processing VA paperwork, work at a VA-approved school, work at a state or national cemetery or a state approving agency, and helping veterans in DoD hospitals, nursing homes, or domiciliaries. Chapter 1606 (MGIB-SR) claimants are restricted to a narrower list. Do not begin work before VA approves you
items.deadline: Apply before the enrollment period you want covered

items.title: Veteran Employment Through Technology Education Courses (VET TEC)
items.who: Not on active duty; qualify for VA education assistance under the GI Bill; have at least one day of unexpired GI Bill entitlement; and are accepted by a VA-approved training provider
items.value: High-tech training - the program's focus areas include computer programming, computer software, media applications, data processing, and information science
items.how: Apply through VA.gov's VET TEC page
items.hack: The key structural feature: you need only one day of remaining GI Bill entitlement to qualify, but you cannot draw GI Bill and VET TEC simultaneously. For a veteran with almost no entitlement left, this converts a nearly worthless remainder into a full coding bootcamp
items.deadline: Program authorization has been renewed periodically - confirm current status before relying on it

items.title: On-the-Job Training and Apprenticeship under the GI Bill
items.who: Veterans; spouses and children receiving benefits through the Fry Scholarship or Chapter 35 DEA; and children using transferred Post-9/11 entitlement. Not available to active-duty service members, nor to spouses using a transferred benefit
items.value: Learn a trade while being paid by the employer, with a GI Bill housing allowance on top, instead of sitting in a classroom
items.how: Enter a training contract with an employer or union for a set period, ending in job certification or journeyman status; confirm the program is VA-approved first
items.hack: The excluded groups are the surprise - active-duty members and spouses on transferred benefits cannot use it, while children on transferred benefits can. Also note: if the training establishment is run by a federal, state, or local government, the pay rules differ
items.deadline: None

items.title: VetSuccess on Campus (VSOC)
items.who: Anyone currently eligible for or receiving a VA education benefit, or VR&E (Chapter 31) training, at a participating school
items.value: An on-campus VA counselor providing benefits assistance, career counseling, and orientation support
items.how: Check whether your school participates; see VA.gov/careers-employment/vetsuccess-on-campus
items.hack: Make participation in VSOC or VITAL one of your school-selection criteria, alongside Yellow Ribbon. A VA counselor physically on campus resolves certification and payment problems that otherwise take months by phone
items.deadline: None

items.title: Veterans Integration to Academic Leadership (VITAL)
items.who: Student veterans at participating campuses
items.value: College success coaching, transition support, resource referral, and behavioral health services delivered on campus
items.how: mentalhealth.va.gov/studentveteran/vital.asp
items.hack: VITAL is the clinical counterpart to VSOC - VSOC is benefits-side (VBA), VITAL is health-side (VHA). A campus with both is a materially better environment for a struggling student veteran
items.deadline: None

items.title: Total and Permanent Disability (TPD) Discharge of Federal Student Loans
items.org: U.S. Department of Education (with VA data match)
items.who: Veterans with a 100% P&T VA rating, or TDIU status; the source also asserts eligibility for veterans rated 100% who are neither P&T nor TDIU
items.value: Complete discharge of federal student loan debt - the single largest dollar benefit in the source material
items.how: Start at DisabilityDischarge.com; ED and VA run a data match that can identify eligible borrowers automatically
items.hack: Since the VA-ED data match was automated, many eligible veterans are discharged without applying - but do not assume. If you hold federal student loans and a P&T or TDIU rating, verify your status directly rather than waiting for a letter
items.deadline: None

items.title: GI Bill 'Rounding Out' Policy
items.who: GI Bill students in a term where required courses do not fill a full-time schedule
items.value: Lets you add courses to reach full-time enrollment - which protects the full monthly housing allowance in your final terms
items.how: Coordinate with your School Certifying Official, who certifies the rounding-out courses
items.hack: The policy evolved in stages and the current form is the generous one. A student may round out with any additional class included in the approved program curriculum, even if it is not required for that beneficiary to graduate, provided it is named in the approved curriculum and not already completed. And if the student has taken or is enrolled in every class the program offers, they may round out with ANY class the institution offers, inside or outside the degree plan. Section 4 of the REMOTE Act codified VA's practice of rounding out. Timeline from the source: historical practice before Aug 1 2021; policy advisory 'Revision of the VA Education Service Practice of Rounding Out' issued Jun 1 2021, effective Aug 1 2021; REMOTE Act Section 4 Dec 21 2021; final expansion Jul 5 2022
items.deadline: Must be certified for the term in question

items.title: Section 702 of the Choice Act - In-State Tuition for Covered Individuals
items.who: 'Covered individuals' at public institutions: veterans using Post-9/11 or MGIB-AD living in the state where the school is located; anyone using transferred benefits living in that state while the transferor is on active duty; Fry Scholarship recipients living in that state; and those continuously enrolled thereafter
items.value: Public schools must charge in-state tuition and fees, or VA disapproves their programs for GI Bill use
items.how: Assert covered-individual status with the school's residency office; the authority is 38 USC 3679(c)(2)
items.hack: This kills the out-of-state tuition problem at public universities for most GI Bill users, which is a far cleaner fix than relying on Yellow Ribbon. It applies to enrollments in terms beginning after July 1, 2015. If a public school tries to bill you out-of-state rates, cite the statute and the Section 702 fact sheet
items.deadline: Requires continuous enrollment to retain the status

items.title: Colonel John M. McHugh Tuition Fairness for Survivors Act of 2021 (PL 117-68)
items.who: Chapter 35 (DEA) beneficiaries at public institutions
items.value: Extends the in-state tuition requirement to Chapter 35 beneficiaries - VA may disapprove courses at a school that does not charge in-state rates to them
items.how: Assert it with the school's residency office
items.hack: Signed November 30, 2021, effective for enrollments beginning on or after August 1, 2022. Chapter 35 was originally left out of the covered-individual protections; this law closed that gap. Survivors and dependents billed out-of-state rates after Aug 2022 have a statutory argument. VA reported all states either in compliance or operating under an approved waiver
items.deadline: Applies to enrollments beginning on or after August 1, 2022

items.title: Section 103, Veterans Benefits and Transition Act of 2018 (PL 115-407) - No Penalty While Awaiting VA Payment
items.who: GI Bill students, including Chapter 35 beneficiaries since PL 117-68
items.value: Schools may not penalize or prohibit a GI Bill student from attending or participating in courses while awaiting VA payment, for up to 90 days
items.how: Cite it to the bursar; schools are required to comply as a condition of program approval
items.hack: Effective August 1, 2019. This is the answer to a registration hold, a late fee, or being dropped from classes because VA has not paid the school yet. Chapter 35 students were added later via PL 117-68 - a detail most bursars' offices do not know
items.deadline: Protection runs up to 90 days from the certified payment date

items.title: Section 1009, Isakson and Roe Act - MHA While on Active Duty
items.who: Individuals pursuing a program of education while on active duty
items.value: Clarifies that you must be serving at least 30 days on active duty before losing GI Bill monthly housing allowance eligibility - because DoD is paying a housing allowance
items.how: Applies automatically; effective August 1, 2022
items.hack: Matters for reservists and Guard members on short activations: a period of active duty under 30 days no longer switches off the GI Bill housing allowance
items.deadline: Effective August 1, 2022

items.title: Digital GI Bill (DGIB) and the Enhanced Post-9/11 Application
items.who: Veterans and service members applying for Post-9/11 education benefits
items.value: A rebuilt application with pre-filled personal information, faster electronic eligibility decisions, and documents accessible online
items.how: Apply at VA.gov
items.hack: If you started an application under the old system and abandoned it, the rebuilt flow is materially shorter - worth restarting rather than resuming
items.deadline: None

items.title: Ask VA (AVA) and the Debt Management Center
items.who: Veterans and school officials disputing a VA education debt
items.value: The routing channel that actually reaches DMC instead of a general queue
items.how: Submit at ask.va.gov; select 'Veterans Affairs - Debt' as the category. School officials select 'A School Official' as the topic and, under 'My inquiry is,' select 'On behalf of a Veteran,' which surfaces School Certifying Official or Other (Business) as the relationship. You must log in to receive a response containing specific debt information. DMC phone: 1-800-827-0648
items.hack: The category and topic selections are what route the inquiry to DMC - the Office Hours deck calls this 'critical.' For a dispute, include one student per inquiry, identifying information outside the subject line, school name and facility code, the debt amount, and supporting details such as the front and back of a cashed check or the date an amended certification was sent
items.deadline: Debt collection timelines run regardless - dispute early

items.title: School Certifying Official Handbook, ELRs and SAAs
items.who: School certifying officials, and indirectly every GI Bill student whose certification is stuck
items.value: Tells you which office owns which problem, so you escalate to the right one
items.how: Education Liaison Representative (ELR) owns: updating certifying officials (VA Form 22-8794), enrollment reporting assistance, VA-ONCE access and technical guidance, 85/15 reporting, and WEAMS 1998 report clarification. The Certifying Official Hotline owns: status of tuition, fee, or Yellow Ribbon payments, school debt creation, and individual student benefit and hardship cases. The State Approving Agency (SAA) owns: program revisions and new, suspended, or cancelled programs, updated catalogs, school address and branch updates, accreditation status changes, and change of ownership
items.hack: For a student, the practical takeaway is that 'my tuition payment has not arrived' is a Certifying Official Hotline question, while 'my program is not approved' is an SAA question. Sending it to the wrong one costs weeks
items.deadline: None

items.title: Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance (SGLI)
items.who: Active duty; Ready Reserve and National Guard members scheduled to perform at least 12 periods of inactive training a year; commissioned members of NOAA and the Public Health Service; cadets and midshipmen at the four service academies; ROTC members in authorized training; and members who volunteer for a mobilization category in the IRR
items.value: Low-cost group term life coverage while serving
items.how: Managed through SGLI Online Enrollment System (SOES); beneficiary designations on SGLV forms
items.hack: Coverage ends 120 days after separation. That 120-day window is the single most missed insurance deadline in the transition - the Navy guide flags it explicitly in the post-retirement block. Questions: SGLI/VGLI call center 1-800-419-1473
items.deadline: Coverage terminates 120 days after separation

items.title: Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI)
items.who: Anyone who had full-time SGLI and is separating, retiring, being released from the Ready Reserve, or placed on the Temporary Disability Retirement List; also those with part-time SGLI who became uninsurable from an injury incurred on duty
items.value: Renewable term life coverage converting your SGLI, with no medical underwriting if you apply inside the early window
items.how: Apply within 1 year and 120 days of separation
items.hack: The rule that decides whether this is cheap or expensive: apply within the first 240 days and there is NO health review. Apply after 240 days but within 1 year and 120 days and you must prove insurability. A healthy veteran is usually better off with commercial term life; VGLI's real value is for people who are hard to insure - and that is exactly the group that must not miss the 240-day no-underwriting window
items.deadline: 1 year and 120 days from separation; no health review if applied within the first 240 days

items.title: Family Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance (FSGLI)
items.who: Spouses and dependent children of service members insured under SGLI - regardless of whether the spouse is themselves active duty, a retired veteran, or a civilian. Not available to those insured under VGLI
items.value: Spousal coverage in increments, and automatic dependent child coverage
items.how: Elect through SOES
items.hack: FSGLI spouse coverage ends 120 days after separation and can be converted to an individual policy with a participating commercial insurer within that window (also within 120 days of a divorce). Dependent child coverage CANNOT be converted and simply ends. The list of participating insurers is published at benefits.va.gov/insurance/forms/SGL_133_ed2019-07.pdf
items.deadline: Convert no later than 120 days after separation

items.title: SGLI Traumatic Injury Protection (TSGLI)
items.org: VA Insurance Service; branch of service determines eligibility
items.who: Anyone insured under full-time SGLI is automatically covered; also members of reserve components and individuals on funeral honors or one-day muster duty
items.value: A lump-sum payment for a qualifying traumatic loss - not limited to combat injuries
items.how: Apply through your branch of service using SGLV-8600
items.hack: Four conditions must all be met: insured by SGLI when the injury occurred; a qualifying loss directly resulting from the traumatic injury; the injury occurred before midnight of the day SGLI coverage terminated; the scheduled loss occurred within two years (730 days) of the injury; and you survived at least seven full days from the injury. TSGLI cannot be declined unless you also decline basic SGLI. Critically, a veteran can be eligible for both TSGLI and the VA Caregiver Support Program - they do not offset. The Participant Guide checklist explicitly says to apply after separation if you did not apply while in service and are eligible
items.deadline: Qualifying loss must occur within 730 days of the traumatic injury

items.title: SGLI Disability Extension (SGLI-DE)
items.who: Members totally disabled at separation, or who have permanent loss of use of a hand or foot, total loss of hearing in both ears, or loss of speech
items.value: Free SGLI coverage extended up to two years past separation at no cost
items.how: Apply to VA; the Participant Guide checklist sets the window at within 2 years of the separation date
items.hack: Free coverage for a totally disabled separating member - and it preserves the option to convert to VGLI at the end of the extension. Most people in this category are dealing with the disability and never file for it
items.deadline: Within 2 years of separation

items.title: Service-Disabled Veterans Insurance (S-DVI, 'RH') - CLOSED TO NEW ENROLLMENT
items.who: Historically: released from active duty after April 25, 1951 under other than dishonorable conditions, rated for a service-connected disability (even 0%), in good health except for service-connected conditions, and applying within 2 years of VA granting a NEW service-connected disability
items.value: Basic policy issued at a maximum of $10,000, with a premium waiver available for those totally disabled for 6 consecutive months before age 65 due to service-connected disability, plus supplemental coverage for policyholders granted the waiver
items.how: Historical - no longer open
items.hack: IMPORTANT STALENESS FLAG: S-DVI stopped accepting new enrollments on 31 December 2022 and was replaced by VALife effective 1 January 2023. Both the 2012 checklist and the Participant Guide v3.3 still present S-DVI as an available benefit; the Navy guide (Nov 2022) correctly flags the sunset. Existing S-DVI policyholders keep their policies. Also note the historical trap: an INCREASE in an existing service-connected disability, or a grant of TDIU on an already-rated condition, never opened a new 2-year S-DVI window
items.deadline: Closed to new applicants after 31 December 2022

items.title: VALife (Veterans Affairs Life Insurance)
items.who: All veterans aged 80 and under with a VA disability rating of 0% to 100%
items.value: Whole life, guaranteed acceptance - no medical underwriting - up to $40,000 in $10,000 increments
items.how: Apply through VA.gov; premium depends on age and coverage amount
items.hack: Two features that make this different from everything that came before: there is NO time limit to apply, and a 0% rating qualifies. The catch is a two-year waiting period - coverage takes effect two years after enrollment provided premiums are paid throughout, with premiums refunded plus interest if you die during the waiting period. Because there is no deadline, the correct move for a newly 0%-rated veteran is to enroll early and start the two-year clock
items.deadline: No application deadline; 2-year waiting period before coverage takes effect

items.title: Veterans' Mortgage Life Insurance (VMLI)
items.who: Service members and veterans with severe service-connected disabilities who have received a Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) or Special Housing Adaptation (SHA) grant, hold title to the home, and have a mortgage on it
items.value: Mortgage life insurance paid directly to the lender, wiping out the mortgage if you die
items.how: Apply with VA Form 29-8636; a premium calculator is at insurance.va.gov/vmli/calculator
items.hack: Two constraints: it pays only the mortgage lender, never a named beneficiary, and you must apply before your 70th birthday. The Participant Guide's checklist pairs it directly with the SAH/SHA grant - if you receive one of those grants, VMLI is the immediate follow-on action
items.deadline: Must apply before age 70

items.title: Combat-Related Special Compensation (CRSC)
items.org: Your military service branch (application) and DFAS (payment)
items.who: Military retirees who are eligible for retired pay, have a disability the branch has deemed combat-related and VA has deemed service-connected, and have retired pay offset by VA compensation
items.value: A monthly tax-free entitlement paid alongside retired pay, restoring pay lost to the VA waiver
items.how: Apply to your branch of service - CRSC is NOT automatic, unlike CRDP
items.hack: 'Combat-related' is broader than combat: it includes the direct result of armed conflict, hazardous duty, duty under conditions simulating war, or an instrumentality of war. Training injuries and parachute or dive injuries frequently qualify. And unlike CRDP there is no 50% rating floor - any compensable combat-related rating can qualify. The rating charts in this upload set list concurrent receipt only at 50%+ and never mention CRSC, which is a genuine gap. You must choose between CRSC and CRDP; DFAS runs an annual open season to switch
items.deadline: No deadline, but payment is generally retroactive only six years

items.title: Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay (CRDP)
items.who: Retirees based on length of service, or Reserve Retirees with 20 qualifying years who have reached retirement age, who are eligible for retired pay offset by VA payments - at a VA rating of 50% or higher
items.value: Restores retired pay that would otherwise be waived to receive VA compensation
items.how: No application needed - qualified retirees are enrolled automatically
items.hack: Crossing from 40% to 50% is worth far more than the compensation-table difference, because it switches CRDP on. If you retire on a disability retirement rather than length of service, CRDP is offset by the amount disability retired pay exceeds length-of-service retired pay. You cannot receive CRDP and CRSC at the same time
items.deadline: None - automatic

items.title: Disability Severance and Separation Pay Recoupment
items.who: Veterans who received disability severance pay, separation pay, or a separation incentive and are later awarded VA disability compensation
items.value: Understanding this prevents a nasty surprise: VA withholds all or part of your compensation until the separation payment is recouped
items.how: VA applies recoupment automatically based on information from your branch of service
items.hack: Plan for it. A veteran who took an early separation package and then wins a rating may see months of withheld compensation. This is not a denial and not an error. Note also that separately, disability severance pay attributable to combat-related injury or received after certain dates may not be recoupable and may have been improperly taxed - worth a specific inquiry
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Pension (Wartime Veterans Pension)
items.who: No dishonorable discharge; net worth below an annually adjusted limit; a qualifying wartime service period (pre-Sept 8 1980: 90 days active with at least one day during wartime; enlisted entering after Sept 7 1980: 24 months or the full called period with one day during wartime; officers entering after Oct 16 1981 with no prior 24 months); AND at least one of: age 65 or older, permanent and total disability, a nursing home patient for long-term care due to disability, or receiving SSDI or SSI
items.value: A monthly payment for low-income wartime veterans whose disabilities are NOT service-connected
items.how: Apply on VA.gov with supporting financial and dependency documentation
items.hack: The structural point: pension is needs-based and does not require service connection, while compensation is service-connection-based and ignores income and net worth entirely. You cannot receive both - if you qualify for both, compensation almost always pays more. Net worth counts your spouse's income and retirement accounts but excludes your home and car; VA also wants the value of household contents such as art and furniture. The net worth limit adjusts each fall with the SSA COLA - do not carry any stated figure forward
items.deadline: None

items.title: Aid and Attendance / Housebound (Special Monthly Pension)
items.who: Veterans (and survivors) receiving a VA pension who either need another person to help with daily activities like bathing, feeding, and dressing; must stay in bed or spend a large part of the day in bed due to illness; are a nursing home patient due to loss of mental or physical abilities related to a disability; or have limited eyesight (5/200 or less in both eyes with correction, or visual field contracted to 5 degrees or less). Housebound applies to those who spend most of their time at home because of a permanent disability
items.value: An increased pension rate earmarked for paying a nurse or home care provider
items.how: Apply with the pension application or separately; be ready to describe daily life, mobility, home layout, and specific care needs
items.hack: You cannot receive Aid and Attendance and Housebound at the same time - A&A is the higher benefit. Both are also available to surviving spouses, which is the version almost nobody claims. Note this is distinct from SMC aid-and-attendance under compensation
items.deadline: None

items.title: Survivors Pension
items.who: Surviving spouses and unmarried dependent children of deceased wartime veterans, subject to income and net worth limits and the veteran's qualifying service
items.value: A monthly needs-based payment to the survivor
items.how: Apply with VA Form 21-534EZ
items.hack: The service test mirrors the veteran's pension test: 90 days active (or 24 months for post-1980 entrants), at least one day during a wartime period. If the veteran died on active duty under circumstances precluding DIC, the requirement becomes at least two years of honorable service with one day during wartime
items.deadline: None

items.title: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC)
items.who: A surviving spouse who married the veteran within 15 years of discharge, OR was married at least 1 year, OR had a child with the veteran and is not currently remarried; surviving children who are unmarried and under 18 (or under 23 if in school); and surviving parents who are the biological, adoptive, or foster parent and have income below a threshold
items.value: A tax-free monthly payment to survivors of a service-connected death
items.how: Apply with VA Form 21-534EZ (spouse or child) or VA Form 21-535 (parents)
items.hack: There is NO minimum length-of-service requirement for DIC. Separately, DIC can be payable on a non-service-connected death if the veteran was rated totally disabled (100% or TDIU) for 10 continuous years immediately preceding death - or 5 continuous years if out of service less than 10 years - or 1 year if a former POW. That 10-year clock is why the date a total rating was granted matters enormously to a surviving spouse
items.deadline: None, but file promptly

items.title: SBP Withdrawal After 10 Years of Total Service-Connected Disability
items.who: Military retirees rated service-connected totally disabled for 10 continuous years - or, if out of service less than 10 years, rated totally disabled for at least 5 continuous years from the date of last active duty
items.value: Allows withdrawal from SBP participation, ending the premium, because the surviving spouse would instead receive DIC
items.how: Coordinate with DFAS and VA
items.hack: This is a real and rarely used lever. The same 10-year / 5-year total-disability clock that creates the survivor's DIC entitlement is what makes continued SBP premiums arguably redundant. Run the numbers carefully with a counselor before withdrawing - it is not reversible
items.deadline: Available once the 10-year (or 5-year) total-disability period is met

items.title: Thrift Savings Plan Options After Separation
items.who: Separating service members with a TSP balance
items.value: Three paths: leave the funds in TSP (no new contributions, but you can still change the investment mix); purchase a single-life or joint-life annuity through the TSP annuity vendor (minimum purchase applies, and traditional and Roth balances are treated separately); or withdraw all or part
items.how: Manage at tsp.gov
items.hack: Mechanics worth knowing from the source: a minimum balance is required to keep the account open; you can transfer traditional TSP to a Roth IRA but you pay tax on the transferred amount that year; you cannot move Roth money to a traditional IRA; and while you can choose whether a withdrawal comes from traditional or Roth, you cannot choose which fund it comes from - TSP withdraws a proportional slice of every fund. Traditional withdrawals carry a mandatory 20% federal withholding and a 10% early-withdrawal penalty before 59.5 unless you separate from service in or after the year you turn 55. Once an annuity is purchased it cannot be cancelled or changed
items.deadline: Required minimum distributions apply beginning in the year set by current law

items.title: Social Security Special Extra Earnings Credits for Military Service
items.who: Anyone on active duty (including active duty for training) between 1957 and 2001
items.value: Extra wage credits added to your Social Security earnings record, raising your eventual benefit
items.how: SSA applies them; verify your earnings record at ssa.gov
items.hack: From 1978 through 2001, for every $300 in active-duty basic pay you were credited an additional $100 in earnings, up to $1,200 per year. Public Law 107-117 ended the credits for service after January 2002. Check your SSA earnings statement - if the credits are missing, bring your DD 214
items.deadline: None, but verify before claiming Social Security

items.title: DFAS Retired Pay, myPay, and the Retiree Account Statement
items.who: Military retirees
items.value: Your retired pay account, statements, tax documents, and withholding controls
items.how: myPay at DFAS; DFAS Cleveland Center at (800) 321-1080, 0800-1700 Eastern
items.hack: Sequencing details that cause real problems: your final active-duty paycheck will likely not arrive on the normal pay date because DFAS audits the account first, and a flagged debt can stretch that to 120 days or more. Your first retired paycheck arrives the first business day of the month after retirement only if DFAS has your completed package including a signed DD Form 2656. Your annual tax statement becomes a 1099-R instead of a W-2. Set up a password login for myPay, DS Logon, and milConnect BEFORE you turn in your CAC - the Navy guide puts this at 3 months out, and it is the mistake that locks people out of everything at once. Retired pay COLA is effective December 1 and paid in the January payment. DFAS publishes a quarterly retiree newsletter at dfas.mil/retnews
items.deadline: Set up non-CAC logins before turning in your CAC

items.title: Terminal Leave vs. Lump-Sum Leave Sellback
items.who: Separating and retiring service members with an accrued leave balance
items.value: A decision worth thousands of dollars either way
items.how: Terminal (separation) leave expires on the day of separation and does not require returning to the command, but all pre-separation counseling and administrative processing must be completed before departing. Lump-sum sellback is generally capped at 60 days of basic pay over a career
items.hack: Decide at 4-6 months out, per the Navy guide's timeline, because the paperwork feeds the DD 214. Terminal leave keeps you on full pay and benefits including health coverage; sellback pays basic pay only, no allowances. One legal trap: a military OFFICER engaged in off-duty employment while on terminal leave is prohibited by 18 USC 203 and 205 - criminal statutes - from representing a non-federal employer back to the government. That restriction does not apply to enlisted members
items.deadline: Decide 4-6 months before separation

items.title: Post-Government Employment Opinion Letter (DD Form 2945)
items.who: Service members taking civilian employment with a defense contractor or firm that does business with the government
items.value: A 'Letter of Opinion,' '30-Day Letter,' or 'Safe Harbor Letter' documenting what post-service employment restrictions apply to you
items.how: Submit DD Form 2945 to your legal office before accepting employment
items.hack: Not always required - consult JAG to determine whether it is. But for anyone moving into a role touching their former program office, the safe harbor letter is the document that protects you later
items.deadline: Before accepting post-service employment

items.title: VA Home Loan Guaranty and Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
items.who: Service members and veterans who separated after September 7, 1980 with 24 continuous months or the full period called (at least 181 days, unless discharged for a service-connected disability); 6 years in the Selected Reserve or National Guard; those discharged for a service-connected disability; and eligible surviving spouses. You must agree to personally occupy the home
items.value: No down payment, no mortgage insurance, competitive rates, and easier qualification than conventional financing. Also usable to refinance an existing loan to a lower rate, or to add energy-efficient improvements such as solar heating
items.how: Obtain the COE through VA.gov or have your lender pull it, then complete the loan application with a VA-experienced lender
items.hack: VA itself sets no minimum credit score - private lenders do, and most require around 620. Use a lender that does VA purchase volume rather than a general mortgage broker. Regional Loan Centers are listed at benefits.va.gov/homeloans/contact_rlc_info.asp. Note the source book recommends a specific commercial lender the author owns - disregard that; shop it
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Funding Fee Waiver and Retroactive Refund
items.who: Veterans with a service-connected disability rated 10% or higher; also surviving spouses receiving DIC. The charts in this set show the waiver available even at a compensable 0% rating (multiple 0% conditions paid at the 10% rate under 38 CFR 3.324)
items.value: Waives the funding fee, which runs roughly 1.4% to 3.6% of the loan amount depending on down payment and whether it is a first use
items.how: Provide your VA benefits letter to the lender at closing
items.hack: The highest-value move in the whole home-loan section: if you closed a VA loan, paid the funding fee, and are LATER awarded a 10%+ rating with an effective date before the closing, VA refunds the fee. That is thousands of dollars people simply never claim. Do not wait for a rating before buying - buy, then claim the refund
items.deadline: Claim the refund once the rating is granted; refund depends on the rating's effective date relative to closing

items.title: Native American Direct Loan (NADL)
items.who: Native American veterans (and certain non-Native veterans married to a Native American) buying, building, or improving a home on federal trust land
items.value: A loan directly from VA rather than a private lender, typically on better terms than the private market
items.how: Apply through VA; requires a Memorandum of Understanding between VA and the tribal government
items.hack: Because VA is the lender rather than a guarantor, the terms can beat anything a private lender offers. Requires the tribe to have an MOU with VA in place
items.deadline: None

items.title: Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) Grant
items.who: Veterans and service members with specific severe service-connected disabilities - the 2012 checklist shows it becoming possible at the TDIU and 100% tiers
items.value: A grant to build, buy, or modify a home to accommodate the disability
items.how: Apply with VA Form 26-4555
items.hack: Receiving SAH or SHA is what makes you eligible for VMLI, so treat them as a pair. The Participant Guide checklist prompts you to apply for VMLI as soon as you have title and a mortgage, and before age 70
items.deadline: Apply once eligible; VMLI must follow before age 70

items.title: Special Housing Adaptation (SHA) Grant
items.who: Veterans with qualifying severe service-connected disabilities, including certain blindness and loss of use of both hands or severe burn injuries
items.value: A grant to adapt a home you or a family member owns
items.how: Apply with VA Form 26-4555
items.hack: SHA is the smaller sibling of SAH and applies to adapting an existing home, including one owned by a family member you live with - a fact that surprises veterans living with relatives
items.deadline: Apply once eligible

items.title: Home Improvement and Structural Alteration (HISA) Grant
items.who: Per the 2012 checklist, possible eligibility begins at a 0% service-connected rating and continues at every tier - available for both service-connected and, at a lower amount, non-service-connected conditions
items.value: A medically-driven grant for home modifications such as ramps, widened doorways, and bathroom accessibility
items.how: Apply through your VA medical center's prosthetics department with a physician's prescription
items.hack: HISA is the most accessible of the three housing grants because it runs through VHA prosthetics on a clinical prescription rather than through the Loan Guaranty Service on a severe-disability finding. It appears at the 0% tier in the checklist and is almost never claimed at low ratings
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Loan Technicians and Foreclosure Avoidance
items.who: Any borrower with a VA-backed loan having trouble making payments - and, per VA, borrowers on non-VA loans can sometimes get help too
items.value: VA loan technicians intervene with servicers to arrange repayment plans, forbearance, and alternatives to foreclosure
items.how: Contact VA through VA.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/trouble-making-payments or a Regional Loan Center
items.hack: Call VA before you call the servicer. VA has leverage with servicers that borrowers do not, and the Participant Guide frames this as an active advocacy service rather than a referral
items.deadline: Call at the first missed payment, not after default

items.title: Recognizing Predatory VA Refinance Offers
items.who: Any veteran with a VA-backed mortgage
items.value: Protection against churning and equity-stripping refinance schemes aimed specifically at VA borrowers
items.how: The Participant Guide includes a red-flag exercise on a sample advertisement targeted at veterans
items.hack: Standard tells: unsolicited mail that mimics a government notice, promises of skipped payments or cash back, pressure to act immediately, rates quoted without disclosing fees, and repeated refinance offers within months of closing. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Office of Servicemember Affairs takes complaints at 1-855-411-CFPB (2372)
items.deadline: None

items.title: Burial in a VA National Cemetery
items.who: Veterans who met active duty service requirements and were discharged other than dishonorably; reservists who died on active duty under certain circumstances; service members and former members eligible for retired pay; and in some cases surviving family members
items.value: Opening, closing, and perpetual care of the grave; a government headstone, marker, or medallion including faith-based emblems; and a burial flag
items.how: Arrange through the funeral home or contact NCA; find cemeteries via the VA facility locator filtered to cemetery
items.hack: VA will make and deliver a headstone or marker anywhere in the world, including to a private cemetery - you do not have to be buried in a national cemetery to receive one. Of the 136 operating national cemeteries, roughly 100 are still accepting new interments, so location availability is a real planning constraint. The full list of authorized faith-based emblems is published at cem.va.gov
items.deadline: None

items.title: Pre-Need Burial Eligibility Determination Program
items.who: Service members, veterans, spouses, and unmarried dependent adult children - and authorized representatives acting for them
items.value: A written determination of national cemetery burial eligibility made in advance, so your family is not litigating eligibility during a funeral
items.how: Apply with VA Form 40-10007 at VA.gov/burials-memorials/pre-need-eligibility
items.hack: Both the Navy guide and the Participant Guide put this in the immediate post-retirement block, and the Navy guide adds a practical instruction: print the determination and give it to your next of kin. A determination letter sitting in a VA database that nobody knows about helps no one
items.deadline: None, but do it while healthy

items.title: VA Burial and Plot-Interment Allowance
items.who: Generally, survivors of veterans who were receiving VA pension or compensation, died of a service-connected condition, died while hospitalized by VA, or died with no next of kin. The rating charts show a burial and plot allowance at every tier
items.value: A payment toward burial and funeral expenses, plus a separate plot-interment allowance if not buried in a national cemetery; a higher amount when death is service-connected
items.how: Apply with VA Form 21P-530EZ (the 2012 checklist references the older 21-530)
items.hack: Two timing rules that differ sharply: for a NON-service-connected death, survivors have two years from burial to file and need proof of death, receipts, and a statement from the funeral home or cemetery. For a SERVICE-CONNECTED burial, plot, or interment allowance there is NO time limit. Since 2014 many burial payments are automatic for a surviving spouse already on record with VBA - but verify rather than assume. DO NOT rely on any dollar figure in these documents; the amounts cited ($300, $796, $2,000) are tied to specific historical date ranges and have been superseded
items.deadline: 2 years from burial for non-service-connected death; no limit for service-connected

items.title: Burial Flag (VA Form 27-2008) and Headstone or Marker (VA Form 40-1330)
items.who: Eligible veterans' next of kin, funeral directors, or authorized representatives
items.value: A United States flag for burial purposes, and a government-furnished headstone, grave marker, niche cover, or medallion
items.how: VA Form 27-2008 for the flag; VA Form 40-1330 for the headstone, marker, or niche cover (VA Form 40-1330M for the medallion affixed to a privately purchased headstone)
items.hack: The medallion option exists specifically for veterans already buried under a private headstone - families who think they missed the window often have not
items.deadline: None

items.title: Presidential Memorial Certificate (VA Form 40-0247)
items.who: Next of kin, other relatives, friends, or authorized service representatives acting for them, of a deceased veteran eligible for burial in a national cemetery
items.value: An engraved certificate bearing the current president's signature
items.how: Apply with VA Form 40-0247
items.hack: Anyone can request it - friends included, not just next of kin - and more than one certificate can be issued. Costs nothing
items.deadline: None

items.title: Veterans Legacy Memorial (VLM)
items.who: Anyone
items.value: A digital memorial page for every veteran interred in a VA national cemetery
items.how: vlm.cem.va.gov
items.hack: Families can add tributes and biographical detail. Free, and a place to point relatives who want to do something
items.deadline: None

items.title: Burial at Sea
items.org: Navy and Marine Corps Mortuary Affairs
items.who: Eligible service members, retirees, and veterans - for cremated remains or intact remains
items.value: Committal at sea aboard a U.S. Navy vessel, performed by the ship's crew
items.how: Contact the Navy and Marine Corps Mortuary Affairs Office at 1-866-787-0081
items.hack: Family members cannot be present for the ceremony, but the command sends the family the flag, photographs, and the chart of the committal position. Coordination is done in advance and requires specific documentation
items.deadline: None

items.title: Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E, Chapter 31)
items.who: Service members and veterans with both a service-connected disability and an employment handicap. Two thresholds: a 20% or higher rating (including a pre-discharge memorandum rating) with an employment handicap, or a 10% rating with a SERIOUS employment handicap. Discharge must be other than dishonorable
items.value: VA typically pays for everything - tuition, fees, books, equipment, and a subsistence allowance - and assigns a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor who builds an individualized plan
items.how: Apply through VA.gov. Service members with a disability that began or worsened on active duty who do NOT yet have a rating can apply without waiting, using VA Form 28-0588
items.hack: VR&E runs five tracks, and most veterans only know about the school one. The source names: reemployment with a former employer, rapid access to employment, self-employment (VA can fund a small business plan), employment through long-term services, and independent living services for veterans too disabled to work yet. The self-employment track is the most underused benefit in this entire document set. Also note VR&E entitlement is separate from and in addition to the GI Bill's 36-48 months
items.deadline: The old 12-year basic period of eligibility was eliminated by the Isakson-Roe Act for most veterans - confirm current rules

items.title: Personalized Career Planning and Guidance (PCPG, Chapter 36)
items.who: Transitioning service members and veterans eligible for a VA education benefit - notably, this program does NOT require a service-connected disability
items.value: Free career counseling, benefits coaching, and personalized academic or adjustment counseling to remove barriers to training success
items.how: Apply at VA.gov/careers-employment/education-and-career-counseling
items.hack: This is the one to use if you do not qualify for VR&E. No rating needed, no cost, and it includes academic and adjustment counseling - not just resume help. Most veterans have never heard of Chapter 36
items.deadline: Tied to education benefit eligibility windows

items.title: Veterans' Preference for Federal Jobs (5 and 10 point)
items.who: Veterans discharged or released from active duty under honorable conditions. The charts in this set show 10-point preference available from a 0% rating (for a non-compensable 0% the disability must have been incurred in combat or have ascertainable residuals, 38 CFR 3.357)
items.value: 5-point preference for qualifying veterans; 10-point preference for disabled veterans - meaning an equally qualified veteran must be selected over a non-veteran. Also confers retention preference in a reduction in force
items.how: Obtain a Veterans' Preference letter from VA.gov; claim preference on the USAJOBS application
items.hack: Preference extends beyond the veteran: the 10-point preference is also available to the spouse and to the natural mother of a permanently and totally service-disabled veteran, and to widows and widowers of veterans who died in service. Get the preference letter at 3 months out, per the Navy guide's timeline - not when you find a job posting. Special hiring authorities are listed at fedshirevets.gov/job-seekers/special-hiring-authorities
items.deadline: Obtain the letter before applying; some authorities have time limits after separation

items.title: Non-Competitive Hiring Authorities for Disabled Veterans (VRA, 30% or More Disabled, Schedule A)
items.org: Office of Personnel Management and federal agencies
items.who: The 2012 checklist notes that at 30% and above a veteran 'may be employed on a noncompetitive basis under certain circumstances'; the Additional VA Disability Benefits Chart calls this 'direct hire authority' starting at 30%
items.value: An agency can appoint you without going through competitive examination
items.how: Identify yourself to the agency's hiring officials and supply the VA letter documenting the rating
items.hack: Terminology matters here and the source charts get it wrong. The real authorities are the 30 Percent or More Disabled Veteran appointing authority (5 CFR 315.707), the Veterans Recruitment Appointment (VRA), and Schedule A for individuals with disabilities. 'Direct hire authority' is a different OPM concept entirely. Use the correct name when talking to an agency HR office or they will not know what you mean. The author of You Deserve It got hired this way (via Expedited Hiring Authority) about two weeks after separating, by contacting the installation hiring agency roughly three months before taking off the uniform
items.deadline: Some authorities have post-separation time limits

items.title: Veteran Employment Services Office (VESO) / VA for Vets
items.who: Veterans seeking employment at VA or another federal agency
items.value: A military skills translator, employment and career management resources, and help identifying tools to find federal work
items.how: vaforvets.va.gov; connect with a VESO representative
items.hack: VA is one of the largest federal employers and actively recruits veterans. The Participant Guide checklist pairs this with obtaining the Veterans' Preference letter - do both before you start applying
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Intermediate Care Technician (ICT) Program
items.who: Former military corpsmen and medics
items.value: Direct hire into skilled clinical positions at VA medical centers, with a defined career pathway toward academic degrees leading to advanced clinical roles
items.how: vacareers.va.gov/careers/technicalfield
items.hack: This converts combat medicine experience into a paid clinical job immediately, while you work toward the credential - rather than starting from scratch in a civilian nursing program. Almost no separating corpsman knows it exists
items.deadline: None

items.title: USERRA Reemployment Rights for Reserve and Guard
items.org: Department of Labor, Veterans' Employment and Training Service (VETS)
items.who: Reserve and National Guard members called to duty
items.value: Your full-time employer must hold your position, and cannot revoke seniority-based benefits including pay increases and promotions
items.how: Give advance notice of service to your employer, keep records, and formally apply for reemployment on return
items.hack: Two limits: with exceptions, cumulative absence cannot exceed five years, and you must actually submit a reemployment application - the right is not self-executing. If the employer stalls, contact DOL VETS at dol.gov/vets
items.deadline: Reemployment application deadlines scale with length of service

items.title: Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act (VEVRAA)
items.who: Protected veterans in four subcategories (you can be in more than one): disabled veteran (entitled to VA compensation, or would be but for retired pay, or discharged for a service-connected disability); recently separated veteran (within 3 years of discharge); active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran; and Armed Forces service medal veteran (an operation for which an AFSM was awarded under EO 12985)
items.value: Prohibits federal contractors and subcontractors from discriminating against protected veterans, and requires affirmative action to recruit, hire, promote, and retain them
items.how: Self-identify as a protected veteran on applications with federal contractors
items.hack: Despite the name, this is not limited to Vietnam-era veterans - it was amended in 2014 under 38 USC 4212. The 'recently separated' category has a hard three-year clock, so self-identify aggressively in your first three years out
items.deadline: 'Recently separated' status lasts 3 years from discharge

items.title: Transition Assistance Program (TAP) and the Capstone Event
items.who: All separating and retiring service members
items.value: The mandatory curriculum that includes the VA Benefits and Services course, plus one-on-one assistance with a VA Benefits Advisor
items.how: Register through your command; the Navy guide places initial pre-separation counseling and TAP registration at more than 12 months prior, with the Capstone event at 3 months prior (it can be completed earlier)
items.hack: The single highest-leverage thing in TAP is the One-On-One Assistance session with your Benefits Advisor - the Participant Guide's checklist says to set it up 'before I leave this course.' Also complete DD eForm 2648 (pre-separation counseling) and the Transition Assistance Curriculum Participant Assessment at dodsurveys.mil/tgpsp
items.deadline: Capstone no later than 90 days before separation

items.title: Verification of Military Experience and Training (DD Form 2586) and the Joint Services Transcript
items.who: Every separating service member
items.value: VMET translates your training and experience into civilian-readable terms; the JST is an accredited transcript of military training for college credit
items.how: Pull the VMET from milConnect; request the JST from jst.doded.mil. Both are due with your terminal leave submission package
items.hack: Give the JST to the school's registrar BEFORE you enroll. Credit awarded for military training reduces the number of months of GI Bill entitlement you burn, which is the same as adding entitlement
items.deadline: Pull both roughly 60 days before terminal leave

items.title: Veteran ID Card, VHIC, and the Retired ID Card (DD Form 2 / DD Form 1173)
items.who: Veterans (VIC), enrolled VA patients (VHIC), and retirees and their families (DD 2 / DD 1173)
items.value: Proof of service for discounts and identification; the VHIC is required for VA medical care access; the DD Form 2 (Retired) blue card and the DD Form 1173 family card authorize commissary, exchange, theater privileges, and medical care
items.how: Apply for the Veteran ID Card at VA.gov; get the VHIC photo taken at your local VA medical center after enrollment; make the ID card appointment 30 days before retirement
items.hack: The DD Form 2 (Retired) is issued to retirees entitled to retired pay EVEN IF they have waived military retired pay in favor of VA compensation - a point retirees routinely get wrong. Make the ID appointment before you turn in your CAC
items.deadline: Make the ID appointment 30 days before retirement

items.title: Household Goods Storage, Transportation, and Home of Selection Travel
items.who: Separating and retiring service members
items.value: Non-temporary storage of household goods for one year, HHG transportation within three years of termination of active duty, and travel for the member and dependents to a Home of Selection within three years of the last permanent duty station
items.how: Schedule Household Goods Transportation Counseling 6-12 months out; see JTR sections 0510 and 0518B
items.hack: The three-year clock on both the HHG move and the Home of Selection travel is generous and widely forgotten. Extensions are available annually for HHG transportation, and the HOS travel window can extend to six years with a certified ongoing medical condition. Storage extensions are authorized for members undergoing hospitalization or medical treatment
items.deadline: HHG transportation within 3 years; HOS travel within 3 years (extendable to 6 for medical)

items.title: Permissive Temporary Duty (PTDY) for Job and House Hunting
items.who: Retiring service members
items.value: Up to 20 days of non-chargeable leave for job and house hunting in CONUS; up to 30 days OCONUS
items.how: Submit PTDY orders or an approved request to personnel 60 days before terminal leave; see MILPERSMAN 1320-22 for the Navy
items.hack: PTDY can be combined with chargeable leave and terminal leave, effectively extending your paid transition runway by three to four weeks. You must return to the command after PTDY, unlike terminal leave
items.deadline: Submit 60 days before PTDY or terminal leave begins

items.title: TRICARE Enrollment After Retirement
items.who: Retirees from a full career of 20 or more years of service, and their dependents. Veterans who separate short of retirement do not qualify, and neither do their dependents
items.value: Continued military health coverage: TRICARE Prime, TRICARE Select, the US Family Health Plan (managed by Brighton Marine Health Center in New England), and TRICARE For Life
items.how: Enroll by website, phone (East 1-800-444-5445, West 1-844-866-9378), or mail
items.hack: You have 90 days after your retirement date to enroll with no break in coverage, and it must be done within 12 months or you wait for open season or a qualifying life event. TRICARE For Life requires no enrollment - it is automatic once you have Medicare Parts A and B, though you pay the Part B premium, and it works worldwide. Do not carry forward the enrollment fees, deductibles, or copays quoted in the Navy guide; those are FEB 2022 Group A figures
items.deadline: 90 days after retirement for unbroken coverage; 12 months absolute

items.title: Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP) for Retirees
items.who: Military retirees and their families
items.value: Dental coverage from 7 national carriers (Aetna, Blue Cross, Delta, GEHA Connection, MetLife, United Concordia, United Healthcare) and 5 regional carriers (Dominion National, EmblemHealth, HealthPartners, Humana, Triple-S); vision from Aetna, Blue Cross, MetLife, United Healthcare, and VSP
items.how: Enroll at benefeds.com; eligibility starts 31 days before and runs 60 days after retirement, otherwise you wait for open season (Monday of the second full work week in November through the Monday of the second full work week in December)
items.hack: The asymmetry that traps people: you can ENROLL in that 31-days-before-to-60-days-after window, but you can only DISENROLL during open season. If you take dental through a new civilian employer in February, you are stuck paying FEDVIP premiums until November
items.deadline: Enroll 31 days before to 60 days after retirement; disenroll only during open season

items.title: Read your LES: which parts of your pay are taxed and which are not
items.who: All active duty, Guard and Reserve on orders
items.value: Understanding that a large share of your pay is already tax-free changes every budgeting and investing decision you make.
items.how: Pull up your Leave and Earnings Statement. Base pay is taxable and is the number your pension and TSP match are calculated from. Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH) and Basic Allowance for Subsistence (BAS) are excluded from gross income by law, so they are not subject to federal income tax and not subject to Social Security or Medicare tax. Special and incentive pays vary - some are taxable, some are not. Compare Box 1 of your W-2 to your total annual pay and you will see the gap. Tax treatment depends on your individual facts - confirm with a CPA or tax attorney before acting.
items.hack: When a civilian friend says they make more than you, compare after-tax dollars, not gross. A civilian needs meaningfully more gross pay to match a service member's take-home once allowances and TRICARE are counted.
items.deadline: Review every January when the new pay tables take effect

items.title: Budget on base pay, invest the allowances
items.who: Anyone receiving BAH and BAS
items.value: Turns a structural tax advantage into actual accumulated assets instead of lifestyle.
items.how: Build your monthly budget around base pay alone. Housing costs come out of BAH, food out of BAS, and whatever is left over from those allowances goes straight to TSP, an IRA, or a brokerage account before you ever see it. The mechanism that makes this work is automation: set the contribution percentage in myPay so the money never lands in checking. Every promotion and every longevity raise gets split - part to lifestyle, the majority to the savings rate.
items.hack: Raise your TSP contribution percentage by one point the same week every promotion hits. You never feel the loss because you never had the higher paycheck.
items.deadline: Set it up now; revisit at every promotion and every PCS

items.title: Emergency fund before anything else
items.who: Everyone
items.value: Keeps a broken transmission or an emergency flight home from turning into a payday loan or a 25% credit card balance.
items.how: Target three to six months of essential expenses in a high-yield savings account at a separate bank from your checking, so it is one transfer away but not one swipe away. Military families can often run at the lower end of that range while on active duty because pay is stable and TRICARE covers medical - but build toward the higher end in the two years before you separate, because that transition is when income gets unpredictable.
items.hack: Use a split direct deposit in myPay so a fixed dollar amount lands in savings every payday automatically. Allotments and split deposits beat willpower.
items.deadline: Before you start any investing beyond the TSP match

items.title: Pay off high-interest debt in a deliberate order
items.who: Anyone carrying consumer debt
items.value: Eliminating a 24% credit card balance is a guaranteed 24% return. No investment offers that with certainty.
items.how: List every debt with its balance and interest rate. Two valid methods: the avalanche (highest interest rate first, mathematically optimal) and the snowball (smallest balance first, psychologically easier to stick with). Either beats paying minimums on everything. Keep making the TSP contribution that earns your full match while you do this - declining the match to pay debt faster usually costs more than it saves.
items.hack: If your debt predates your active duty service, invoke the SCRA 6% interest rate cap first - it can cut the balance you are attacking before you attack it.
items.deadline: Ongoing

items.title: SCRA 6% interest rate cap on pre-service debt
items.who: Active duty; often activated Guard and Reserve
items.value: Caps the interest rate at 6% on debts you took out before entering active duty, and the excess is forgiven, not deferred.
items.how: The cap applies to obligations incurred before you entered active duty - credit cards, car loans, student loans (federal loans have their own separate provisions), mortgages. Send the creditor a written request with a copy of your orders. The creditor must reduce the rate retroactively to the start of your active duty and forgive the excess interest rather than tacking it on. They cannot report you adversely for invoking it. SCRA also provides protections against default judgments, evictions and foreclosures during service.
items.hack: It applies to your spouse's jointly-held pre-service debt too in many cases. Ask - most creditors will not volunteer it.
items.deadline: Request anytime during active duty and up to a period after; do not wait

items.title: Military Lending Act 36% rate cap on consumer credit
items.who: Active duty service members and their dependents
items.value: Caps the all-in cost of most consumer credit at a 36% Military Annual Percentage Rate and bans several predatory contract terms.
items.how: Unlike SCRA, the MLA applies to new credit taken out while you are on active duty. Covered credit cannot exceed a 36% MAPR (which includes fees and credit insurance, not just the stated rate), cannot require mandatory arbitration, and cannot require an allotment as a condition of the loan. It covers payday loans, vehicle title loans, tax refund anticipation loans, credit cards and most installment loans; purchase-money vehicle and residential mortgage loans are excluded.
items.hack: Lenders clustered outside the gate exist because the model works on young service members. If an offer is only available to military, treat that as a warning, not a benefit.
items.deadline: Protection is automatic while on active duty

items.title: Free accredited financial counseling you already paid for
items.org: Military OneSource / installation Personal Financial Managers
items.who: Active duty, Guard, Reserve, spouses, and recently separated veterans
items.value: Free one-on-one sessions with accredited financial counselors who do not sell products and earn no commission.
items.how: Every installation has Personal Financial Managers through the Family Center, and Military OneSource provides free telephone and video consultations plus free tax filing through MilTax. These counselors hold AFC or CFP credentials and are prohibited from selling you anything - which is the opposite of the insurance agent who set up a table at your unit.
items.hack: Use them before any major purchase or any pitch for an insurance or investment product. Ask the counselor to review the actual contract, not the sales sheet.
items.deadline: Available anytime; access continues for a period after separation

items.title: Credit cards used as a tool, not a income source
items.who: Anyone with reliable income and no revolving balance
items.value: Rewards on spending you would do anyway, plus the payment history that builds the credit score behind your mortgage rate.
items.how: The only rule that matters: pay the statement balance in full every month. Interest at typical card rates overwhelms any rewards program by an order of magnitude. Beyond that, keep utilization low relative to your limits, keep your oldest account open because length of history helps your score, and pick one or two cards whose rewards match what you actually spend on - not the ones with the flashiest signup offers. SCRA and MLA can waive or cap fees and interest on some cards for active duty; several issuers waive annual fees for service members. Ask your issuer directly. Alongside this, pull all three credit reports free at annualcreditreport.com, and use the free credit monitoring nationwide bureaus must provide to active duty members. Anyone can place a free security freeze; active duty members can also place a free active duty alert. Dispute errors in writing - one wrong collection can cost you a quarter point on a mortgage rate.
items.hack: Ask your card issuer in writing whether they apply SCRA benefits to the account. Several major issuers waive annual fees entirely for active duty members but do not apply it unless you request it. And freeze your children's credit - minor identity theft usually is not discovered until they apply for their first loan at 18.
items.deadline: Ongoing

items.title: SGLI while you serve, and the VGLI decision when you leave
items.who: Active duty, Guard, Reserve, separating veterans
items.value: Group term life insurance at rates no individual policy can match, with a guaranteed-issue conversion option on separation.
items.how: SGLI enrolls you automatically in term life coverage in increments up to the program maximum, at a flat premium per thousand of coverage regardless of your age or health. Coverage continues free for a period after separation, and you can convert to VGLI without a medical exam if you apply within the VA's stated window. VGLI premiums rise with age; a healthy veteran under about 45 will usually find a 20- or 30-year level term policy cheaper. A veteran with a health condition that would hurt civilian underwriting should take VGLI, because it does not ask.
items.hack: Apply for civilian term coverage while you are still in uniform and still healthy. Compare the quote to VGLI before you separate, not after the window closes.
items.deadline: VGLI application window runs from separation - check current VA deadlines and apply early

items.title: How to evaluate an insurance or investment pitch aimed at service members
items.who: Everyone in uniform
items.value: Avoiding one badly-sold whole life or indexed universal life policy can be worth six figures over a career.
items.how: The military community is a heavily targeted sales market, and GAO and DoD have documented it for decades. Before signing anything: ask for the total commission being paid on the sale, in writing. Ask for an in-force illustration showing guaranteed values, not projected ones. Ask what the surrender charge is in years 1 through 10. Take the paperwork to a free installation financial counselor before you sign. A legitimate product survives that review; a bad one is sold under time pressure specifically to avoid it.
items.hack: If the pitch includes the phrase 'be your own bank' or promises tax-free retirement income from an insurance contract, that is a sales script for a permanent life policy. Permanent insurance has real uses in estate planning at high net worth; it is almost never the right first or second investment for an E-5.
items.deadline: Before signing anything

items.title: Traditional TSP vs Roth TSP - how to choose
items.who: All uniformed service members and federal employees
items.value: The TSP has among the lowest expense ratios of any retirement plan in the world, and the traditional/Roth choice changes your lifetime tax bill.
items.how: Traditional contributions come out before federal income tax, lowering your taxable income now; withdrawals in retirement are taxed as ordinary income. Roth contributions are made with after-tax dollars; qualified withdrawals, including all the growth, come out tax-free. The rule of thumb: choose Roth when your current tax rate is low relative to what you expect in retirement, traditional when it is high. Most junior enlisted are in low brackets now and should lean Roth. A senior officer in a high bracket with a large pension coming may lean traditional. You can split between both. Contribution limits are set by the IRS and change annually - look up the current elective deferral limit, catch-up amounts, and annual additions limit at tsp.gov or irs.gov. Tax treatment depends on your individual facts - confirm with a CPA or tax attorney before acting.
items.hack: Remember that your pension and, if you have a rating, your VA compensation are already going to fill up the low brackets in retirement. That pushes the argument toward Roth for more service members than most generic advice assumes.
items.deadline: Change your election anytime in myPay; limits reset each calendar year

items.title: Capture the full BRS TSP match - it is an immediate 100% return
items.who: Members under the Blended Retirement System (generally those who joined on or after 1 Jan 2018, plus opt-ins)
items.value: The government automatically contributes 1% of your base pay whether you contribute or not, and matches your contributions dollar-for-dollar on the first 3% and fifty cents on the dollar on the next 2%. Contribute 5% and a total of 10% of base pay goes in every pay period.
items.how: Set your contribution to at least 5% of base pay in myPay. Anything less leaves free money on the table permanently - there is no catch-up on a match you did not capture in a prior year. Check that automatic and matching contributions have begun; there are service-entry waiting periods before the match starts. Agency contributions vest after a required period of service - confirm your vesting status before separating early.
items.hack: 5% is the floor, not the goal. The match is a reason to contribute at least 5%; it is not a recommendation to stop there.
items.deadline: Every pay period you do not contribute 5% is permanently lost match

items.title: Combat Zone Tax Exclusion - what it covers
items.who: Service members serving in an IRS-designated combat zone or qualified hazardous duty area
items.value: Military pay earned during any month you serve even one day in a designated zone can be excluded from federal income tax.
items.how: For enlisted members and warrant officers, all military pay for the qualifying month is excluded. For commissioned officers, the exclusion is capped at the highest enlisted pay rate for that month plus hostile fire or imminent danger pay. It covers basic pay, hostile fire/imminent danger pay, reenlistment bonuses signed while in the zone, and certain other pays. Excluded pay does not appear in Box 1 of your W-2. The zone designations and the officer cap amount change - check irs.gov for the current list and figures. Tax treatment depends on your individual facts - confirm with a CPA or tax attorney before acting.
items.hack: Combat zone service also extends your deadline to file, pay, and contribute to an IRA - generally for the period of service in the zone plus additional days after. You cannot be penalized for a late filing you were deployed through.
items.deadline: Applies automatically to qualifying months; filing extensions run from your return date

items.title: Roth TSP contributions from combat-zone pay - the most powerful move in the military tax code
items.who: Deployed service members receiving tax-excluded pay
items.value: Money that was never taxed going in, invested in an account where growth and qualified withdrawals are also never taxed.
items.how: Normally a Roth contribution costs you tax - you pay income tax on the dollar first, then contribute it, and in exchange growth and withdrawal are tax-free. Combat-zone pay is already excluded from federal income tax. Contributing that pay to the Roth TSP means you paid no tax on the way in, the growth compounds untaxed, and qualified withdrawals come out tax-free. There is no other common situation in the U.S. tax code where a dollar can be untaxed at all three stages. Set your Roth TSP election before or at the start of the deployment so contributions flow from the excluded pay. Tax-exempt pay also interacts with the higher annual additions limit rather than the ordinary elective deferral limit - the current figures are at tsp.gov. Tax treatment depends on your individual facts - confirm with a CPA or tax attorney before acting.
items.hack: Set the election in myPay BEFORE you deploy. Changing it from a forward location with intermittent connectivity is how people miss an entire deployment's worth of this.
items.deadline: Set before deployment; contributions must be made from qualifying pay during the qualifying months

items.title: Saver's Credit (Retirement Savings Contributions Credit)
items.who: Lower- and moderate-income taxpayers who contribute to a TSP, IRA, or 401(k)
items.value: A tax credit - a dollar-for-dollar reduction of tax owed - for money you were putting into retirement anyway. Junior enlisted incomes frequently fall in the qualifying range.
items.how: Contribute to a TSP, traditional IRA, or Roth IRA, then claim the credit on Form 8880. The credit is a percentage of your contribution (the percentage steps down as income rises) up to a maximum contribution amount. The income thresholds and the maximum credit change every year, and filing status matters - look up the current figures at irs.gov. Note that this is a credit, not a deduction, which makes it worth substantially more per dollar. Tax treatment depends on your individual facts - confirm with a CPA or tax attorney before acting.
items.hack: Most junior service members never claim this because nobody tells them it exists. If you contributed to the TSP and your income was modest, check Form 8880 - and check whether you can amend a prior year's return to claim it.
items.deadline: Claimed with your annual return; amended returns generally allowed within the IRS statutory window

items.title: VA disability compensation is tax-free at every rating level
items.who: Veterans with a service-connected disability rating
items.value: A monthly, COLA-adjusted, lifetime payment that is excluded from federal gross income and is not taxed by any state.
items.how: VA disability compensation is excluded from gross income under federal law. It is not reported on your 1040, and because states start from federal gross income, no state taxes it either. It is also generally not counted as income for certain federal means-tested programs. Ratings run from 0% to 100% in 10% increments, and multiple disabilities combine using the VA's combined ratings table rather than simple addition. Additional amounts are paid for dependents at 30% and above. Current rate tables are published at va.gov and change with each COLA. Tax treatment depends on your individual facts - confirm with a CPA or tax attorney before acting.
items.hack: Because it is tax-free and inflation-adjusted for life, VA compensation functions in a portfolio like a large inflation-protected bond position. That is a reason a rated veteran can often hold a higher stock allocation in the rest of their portfolio than a civilian with the same net worth - not a reason to buy an annuity that duplicates what you already have.
items.deadline: File your claim; effective dates generally relate back to the claim date, so filing early matters

items.title: State of legal residence under SCRA and MSRRA
items.org: SCRA / Military Spouse Residency Relief Act
items.who: Active duty members and their spouses
items.value: You can keep one state of legal residence across every PCS, and choosing a state without an income tax can be worth thousands a year for an entire career.
items.how: Under SCRA, a service member does not lose or acquire a state of legal residence solely by being stationed somewhere on orders. MSRRA and later amendments extend comparable treatment to the spouse, and current law generally allows the spouse to elect the service member's residence for tax purposes. Establishing residence is a factual matter - where you register to vote, title and register vehicles, hold a driver's license, own property, and where you intend to return. You cannot simply declare a state you have no connection to. Changing your state of legal residence is done with DD Form 2058 through your finance office. Tax treatment depends on your individual facts - confirm with a CPA or tax attorney before acting.
items.hack: The time to establish residence in a no-income-tax state is when you are actually stationed there and can genuinely build the connections. Doing it from a duty station 2,000 miles away, with no real ties, is the fact pattern state revenue departments audit.
items.deadline: Anytime you have a legitimate basis; DD 2058 through finance

items.title: State taxation of military retired pay varies enormously
items.who: Military retirees choosing where to settle
items.value: Military retired pay is taxable federally but a large and growing majority of states exempt some or all of it. Where you establish domicile at retirement directly changes the after-tax value of your pension for life.
items.how: Distinguish three things: VA disability compensation (never taxed by any state), military retired pay (taxable federally; state treatment varies), and civilian second-career income (taxed normally). States with no income tax at all obviously do not tax the pension. Many states with income taxes fully exempt military retired pay, and others offer partial exemptions capped by dollar amount, age, or income. The list changes every legislative session - verify your target state's current law before you commit. Establishing domicile requires real steps, not just a mailing address. Tax treatment depends on your individual facts - confirm with a CPA or tax attorney before acting.
items.hack: Run the comparison on total cost of living, not the income tax line alone. A state with no income tax but very high property tax and insurance can cost a retiree more than a state that exempts the pension.
items.deadline: Decide before you separate; establishing domicile takes time and documentation

items.title: IRA alongside the TSP - a second tax-advantaged bucket
items.who: Anyone with earned income; spouses can use a spousal IRA
items.value: An additional annual contribution on top of your TSP, in an account where you choose the investments and which follows you out of the service.
items.how: You can contribute to an IRA in the same year you contribute to the TSP. Traditional IRA contributions may be deductible depending on income and whether you are covered by a workplace plan; Roth IRA contributions are not deductible but qualified withdrawals are tax-free. A non-working spouse can contribute to a spousal IRA based on the working spouse's earned income. Annual contribution limits, catch-up amounts, deduction phase-outs, and Roth income phase-outs are all set by the IRS and change annually - look them up at irs.gov. Tax treatment depends on your individual facts - confirm with a CPA or tax attorney before acting.
items.hack: You can contribute for a tax year up until the filing deadline of the following April. If you deployed and money was tight, you often still have a window after the year ends.
