items.hack: The entry-point trap is real and recurring: the same software is free through the IRS Free File portal and paid through the company's own site. And if your AGI is above the threshold, Free File FILLABLE FORMS has no income limit at all — bare-bones, but for a simple return with military retirement and tax-free VA compensation it is often perfectly adequate and completely free.
items.deadline: Federal filing deadline, typically mid-April; Free File typically opens in January.

items.title: What 'VA compensation is tax-free' actually means for every other benefit's income test
items.org: IRS / VA / HHS / Social Security Administration
items.who: Every veteran receiving VA disability compensation, DIC or VA pension who also applies for an income-tested benefit. This is the most consequential and least-explained interaction in the whole system.
items.value: VA disability compensation, DIC and VA pension are excluded from federal gross income, so they do not appear on a tax return, do not count toward adjusted gross income or modified AGI, and do not affect the taxability of Social Security benefits. But income-tested PROGRAMS each define income their own way, and several count VA compensation anyway.
items.how: Expect roughly this pattern, and verify each program's current rule before applying. ACA marketplace subsidies use MAGI, so VA compensation is NOT counted. FAFSA relies on tax data, so service-connected VA disability compensation is generally NOT counted. SNAP COUNTS it as unearned income. SSI COUNTS it as unearned income and reduces the SSI payment dollar for dollar above the exclusion. Medicaid for the MAGI-based adult group generally does NOT count it, but Medicaid for aged, blind and disabled categories often DOES. HUD rental assistance COUNTS it as annual income. VA's own health care means test counts it in some calculations.
items.hack: The rule to carry: tax-free does not mean invisible. Before applying for any income-tested benefit, ask the program in writing whether VA compensation counts, because the staff answer and the regulation sometimes differ. Where it is counted and pushes you over a line — SSI especially — the planning question is whether VA PENSION versus VA COMPENSATION, or SSI versus SSDI, produces the better combined result. Take that to an accredited VSO or a benefits counselor BEFORE you file, not after a denial.
items.deadline: None, but ask before each application rather than after a denial.

items.title: Multi-state tax filing for military families — MSRRA and the 2018 spouse residency election
items.org: IRS / state revenue departments / Military OneSource
items.who: Service members and spouses living in a state other than their state of legal residence. SCRA protects the member's residency; the Military Spouses Residency Relief Act and the Veterans Benefits and Transition Act of 2018 extend protections to the spouse.
items.value: The member keeps their state of legal residence for income tax purposes regardless of duty station. The spouse may ELECT to use the same state of legal residence as the service member for income tax and voting purposes — even if the spouse never lived there — which can eliminate state income tax entirely when the member's domicile is a no-income-tax state.
items.how: File the member's resident return with the state of legal residence; file a nonresident return in the duty state only for unprotected non-military income. The spouse claims the election by filing in the member's domicile state and submitting a withholding exemption certificate to their duty-state employer. Use a MilTax consultant — this is exactly what MilTax specializes in.
items.hack: The 2018 spouse election remains underused years later: a spouse working in a high-tax state whose service member is domiciled in a no-income-tax state can elect that domicile and stop paying state income tax. File the employer withholding exemption as early in the tax year as possible, and consider amended returns for prior open years if the election was available and not taken. Confirm with a MilTax consultant before amending.
items.deadline: File withholding exemption certificates early in the tax year; amended returns are generally limited to three years.

items.title: VALife operational detail — the two-year waiting period, the increments, and who it is actually for
items.who: Veterans aged 80 or under with ANY service-connected disability rating from 0 to 100 percent, plus veterans over 80 with a new service-connected rating within a limited window of that rating. Guaranteed acceptance: no medical exam, no health questions.
items.value: Whole life coverage purchased in $10,000 increments up to a program maximum, with level premiums based on age at application and cash value that builds over time. The critical structural feature: a TWO-YEAR WAITING PERIOD during which death pays only the premiums paid plus interest, not the face amount.
items.how: Apply online through VA.gov's life insurance pages. Confirm the current maximum coverage, the per-increment premium at your age, and the exact waiting-period terms at the official page before deciding.
items.hack: Two things determine whether VALife is right. First, the two-year waiting period means VALife is NOT a solution for a veteran with a terminal diagnosis today — but it is an excellent purchase for a healthy 45-year-old with a 10% rating who expects to become uninsurable later. Second, buy it EARLY: premiums are set by age at application and never increase, so a 0%-rated 35-year-old locks a rate for life. Guaranteed acceptance plus a locked premium plus any-rating eligibility makes VALife the most broadly useful insurance product VA has, and most 10%-rated veterans have never heard of it.
items.deadline: Apply before age 81; veterans over 80 have a limited window after a new service-connected rating.

items.title: VGLI's age-banded premiums — the trap that makes it unaffordable exactly when you need it
items.who: Veterans who converted SGLI to VGLI, or who are still inside the conversion window. VGLI is renewable term life with no health questions at conversion within the window.
items.value: Term coverage up to the amount of SGLI held at separation. Premiums are set by five-year age bands and increase at each band — modest in a veteran's thirties, severe in their sixties and seventies. No cash value.
items.how: Apply through VA.gov. Confirm the CURRENT premium table by age band and coverage amount at the official VGLI page before making any comparison; rates are periodically adjusted and figures in guides go stale fast.
items.hack: Run the arithmetic at 50, not at 70. VGLI's structure means a healthy veteran almost always does better converting to level-premium commercial term or permanent coverage while still insurable, keeping VGLI only if health makes commercial coverage impossible. Two companion facts: VGLI lets you INCREASE coverage in increments at defined intervals up to the maximum without health questions, valuable if you took less than full coverage; and VGLI can be converted to a commercial individual policy with participating insurers without health questions — a little-known escape hatch.
items.deadline: Convert from SGLI within 240 days of separation with no health questions, or up to one year and 120 days with evidence of insurability.

items.title: TSGLI claim mechanics — SGLV 8600, the branch office, and the ADL clock that decides the claim
items.who: Service members insured under SGLI who suffered a qualifying traumatic injury, including off-duty and non-combat injuries. Certain retroactive claims are available for qualifying injuries in defined earlier periods.
items.value: A lump-sum payment on a schedule of losses — amputation, loss of sight or hearing, burns, paralysis, coma, hospitalization, and inability to perform activities of daily living for a specified number of consecutive days — scaled by severity and duration. The ADL-based losses are the most commonly claimed and most commonly denied.
items.how: File SGLV Form 8600 with YOUR BRANCH's TSGLI office, not with VA. The form has a member section and a MEDICAL PROFESSIONAL section that a licensed provider must complete. Appeals go to the branch and then to the service's board.
items.hack: Most TSGLI denials are documentation failures on the ADL clock, not eligibility failures. The schedule pays by CONSECUTIVE DAYS of inability to perform activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, transferring, continence), so the claim lives or dies on contemporaneous records showing which ADLs required assistance and for how long. Pull the inpatient nursing notes, physical therapy notes and home health records, and have the provider complete the medical section against those exact dates. If denied, appeal with a day-by-day ADL timeline rather than a narrative. And note that TBI and non-combat accidents qualify — this is not a combat-wounds-only program.
items.deadline: File as soon as possible; retroactive windows and appeal deadlines are branch-specific — ask the branch TSGLI office in writing.

items.title: FSGLI spouse coverage — it ends shortly after separation, and the conversion right is use-it-or-lose-it
items.who: Spouses of service members insured under SGLI, and dependent children (children are covered at no cost). Spouse coverage is paid for by the member via payroll deduction.
items.value: Term coverage on the spouse up to a statutory maximum not exceeding the member's own SGLI amount, plus automatic no-cost coverage on dependent children. Spouse coverage terminates a set number of days after the member separates, and the spouse then has a CONVERSION right to an individual commercial policy with a participating company, without health questions.
items.how: Verify the current spouse coverage maximum and the exact termination and conversion deadlines at the official FSGLI page. The conversion is executed with a participating commercial insurer, not with VA — request the list of participating companies from the Office of Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance.
items.hack: The conversion right is the whole value and it evaporates fast. A spouse with a health condition that would fail commercial underwriting can convert FSGLI to a permanent individual policy with no health questions — but only inside the post-termination window. Put that deadline on the calendar at the moment of separation, next to the member's own SGLI-to-VGLI deadline. And note that unlike the member, a spouse has NO VGLI equivalent: there is no group product waiting. It is conversion or nothing.
items.deadline: Spouse coverage terminates a defined number of days after separation; conversion must be exercised within the stated window after termination.

items.title: FEGLI for veterans who take federal jobs — the 31-day no-medical window and Living Benefits
items.who: Veterans employed in eligible federal civilian positions, including those hired under Veterans Recruitment Appointment, the 30 Percent or More Disabled Veteran authority, or Schedule A.
items.value: Basic life insurance tied to salary plus Accidental Death and Dismemberment, with Option A (standard), Option B (multiples of salary, up to five) and Option C (family). Basic is automatic on appointment unless waived. FEGLI also offers a LIVING BENEFITS option allowing a terminally ill employee or annuitant to receive the Basic face amount while alive.
items.how: Basic FEGLI is automatic at appointment — do nothing and you have it. Optional coverage (A, B, C) must be ELECTED within 31 days of becoming eligible, with no medical exam. After 31 days, enrollment generally requires a qualifying life event or an infrequently held open season.
items.hack: The 31-day window is the trap, and newly hired veterans miss it constantly in onboarding chaos. Option B at five times salary with no medical questions is extraordinary coverage for a veteran who would fail commercial underwriting — available for 31 days and then effectively gone. Two more points: FEGLI continues into retirement if you meet the five-year rule, and the 75 percent reduction election dramatically changes retirement cost, so understand it early. And the Living Benefits option is a real lever for a terminally ill veteran that is almost never requested.
items.deadline: 31 days from eligibility to elect optional coverage without medical underwriting; five years of continuous coverage to carry FEGLI into retirement.

items.title: On-installation solicitation rules — DoD Instruction 1344.07 and the protection you can invoke by number
items.who: All service members, especially junior enlisted in training and first-term status, approached by insurance and financial product salespeople on or near an installation.
items.value: DoD Instruction 1344.07 governs personal commercial solicitation on DoD installations. Its protections include no solicitation in barracks, dormitories, dining facilities or other unauthorized areas; no mass or door-to-door solicitation; appointments only, by individual request; no use of command or official endorsement to generate sales; no solicitation during duty hours or in settings implying command sponsorship; and required disclosures. A soliciting company's installation privileges can be WITHDRAWN for violations.
items.how: If a salesperson appears in your barracks or at a mandatory formation, report it to your chain of command, the installation commander's office and the installation legal assistance office. Ask for DoD Instruction 1344.07 by number. You can also report to the state insurance commissioner and the DoD Inspector General.
items.hack: The two highest-risk settings are the end of initial entry training and the payday briefing, and both are covered by the no-mass-solicitation rule. Say out loud: 'Is this a command-sponsored briefing or a commercial solicitation under 1344.07?' The question alone frequently ends the pitch. And never sign a financial product the same day it is pitched — take it to the installation Personal Financial Manager and the legal assistance office first, both free.
items.deadline: Report violations promptly; insurance contracts typically carry a state free-look cancellation period of 10 to 30 days.

items.title: The insurance products sold to young enlisted — the pattern, and the three questions that kill them
items.org: FTC / CFPB Office of Servicemember Affairs / state insurance regulators
items.who: Junior enlisted service members, especially in a first enlistment, targeted with high-cost life insurance, 'military-specific' whole life or modified-premium policies, and insurance bundled with investment or savings features.
items.value: The pattern to recognize: pitched as savings or investment rather than insurance; very low initial premiums that escalate sharply after a few years; an allotment or recurring bank draft set up at signing; a small death benefit relative to premium; heavy front-loaded commissions meaning near-zero cash value in the early years; and the claim that SGLI is insufficient. The product is almost never better than SGLI plus low-cost term plus the Thrift Savings Plan.
items.how: Three questions, asked in writing: (1) What is the total premium I will pay over twenty years, year by year? (2) What is the GUARANTEED cash surrender value at years 1, 5 and 10? (3) Are you a fiduciary, and how are you compensated on this sale? Then take the answers to a free Accredited Financial Counselor via Military OneSource at 1-800-342-9647 before signing.
items.hack: The decisive fact: a healthy 20-year-old already has substantial SGLI at a very low payroll cost, and additional need is met far more cheaply by level term insurance. Any product pitched as doing insurance AND investing does both worse than doing them separately. If you already signed, check immediately whether you are inside the state free-look period, cancel the allotment, and file complaints with the CFPB at consumerfinance.gov/complaint, the state insurance commissioner, and installation legal assistance.
items.deadline: State free-look cancellation periods are typically 10 to 30 days from policy delivery — act immediately.

items.title: Auto, homeowners and renters insurance for military — the deployment, garaging and barracks angles
items.org: USAA / Armed Forces Insurance / GEICO Military and other military-market carriers
items.who: Service members, veterans and eligible family members. Membership eligibility differs sharply by carrier — USAA eligibility runs through service and family lineage, while others sell to anyone with a military affiliation.
items.value: Military-specific features worth asking for by name: deployment or storage endorsements that cut premiums while a vehicle is stored; garaging-location pricing updated at each PCS; coverage that follows the vehicle OCONUS; renters coverage written for barracks and dormitory living; military uniform and equipment coverage; and policy suspension during deployment.
items.how: Shop at least three carriers at each PCS and again at separation — not once. Ask every carrier four questions: do you offer a deployment or storage discount; do you re-rate for the new garaging ZIP code; do you cover personal property in transit during a PCS; and do you write a military renters policy covering government-issued gear.
items.hack: Three concrete savings. A vehicle stored during deployment can usually be reduced to comprehensive-only, yet people pay full liability on a car sitting in a garage for a year. Renters insurance for barracks residents costs very little, and the government is NOT liable for your stolen property while the claim against a PCS mover is separate and partial. And the SCRA caps interest on pre-service debt but does NOT cap insurance premiums, so shopping is the only lever — re-shop at separation specifically, because military rates and veteran rates are priced differently.
items.deadline: Re-shop at each PCS, at each deployment, and at separation.

items.title: How to actually get into the VA legal clinic — ask the Homeless Program Coordinator, not the front desk
items.org: VA Legal Services for Veterans (LSV) grant program / VA Homeless Programs
items.who: Veterans receiving care at a VA medical center that hosts a legal clinic. VA funds legal services organizations through the Legal Services for Veterans grant program, and many medical centers host law school clinics, legal aid organizations or bar association clinics on site.
items.value: Free civil legal REPRESENTATION — not just advice — on the issues that most threaten housing and health: eviction and landlord disputes, child support and family law, driver's license restoration, benefits appeals, consumer debt defense, expungement and record relief, and estate documents.
items.how: Ask three people at your medical center: the Homeless Program Coordinator, the social work department, and the Patient Advocate. Use the words 'legal clinic' or 'medical-legal partnership.' If your facility has none, ask the Homeless Program Coordinator which LSV grantee covers your region and call them directly. Also check the ABA's veteran legal services directory and your state bar's military and veterans committee.
items.hack: Legal clinics at VA medical centers are almost always administered through the HOMELESS program office regardless of whether the veteran is homeless, because that is where the grant money sits. Veterans asking at the front desk get nowhere; veterans asking the Homeless Program Coordinator get an appointment. That single routing fact is the item.
items.deadline: Clinic sessions are often weekly or monthly with limited slots — call early in the month.

items.title: The medical-legal partnership model — why a lawyer in the clinic improves health outcomes
items.org: National Center for Medical-Legal Partnership / VA / legal aid organizations
items.who: Veterans with health-harming legal needs: unsafe or unstable housing, benefits denials causing income loss, utility shutoff threatening life-sustaining equipment, family instability, or employment discrimination.
items.value: An embedded legal team treated as part of the clinical care team. The clinician screens for health-harming legal needs and refers internally, the lawyer takes the case, and the legal outcome — housing stabilized, benefits restored, utilities reconnected — is understood and measured as a health intervention.
items.how: Ask your VA social worker or primary care provider to screen you for health-harming legal needs and refer to the on-site legal partner. If you are seen at a community health center rather than VA, ask whether the center has a medical-legal partnership — many FQHCs do.
items.hack: The referral works better coming from the clinician than from you, because the lawyer's intake prioritizes clinician-referred cases and the clinical note supplies documentation the lawyer needs. So the move is to tell your doctor or social worker about the eviction notice, not just a lawyer. Say the words 'this is affecting my health' and let them route it.
items.deadline: None, but eviction answer dates and appeal windows move fast — raise it at the first appointment after any legal notice.

items.title: Armed Forces Legal Assistance — free attorneys for active duty, Guard, Reserve and usually retirees
items.org: Service judge advocate general legal assistance offices
items.who: Active duty service members and dependents, Guard and Reserve on qualifying status, and at most offices military RETIREES and their dependents — a category that routinely does not know it still has a free lawyer.
items.value: Free legal advice and document preparation: wills, trusts and estate planning, advance medical directives, powers of attorney, free NOTARY service, family law advice, consumer and landlord-tenant advice, SCRA and USERRA advice, tax advice at many offices, and limited representation in some matters.
items.how: Find the nearest office through the Armed Forces Legal Assistance locator at legalassistance.law.af.mil, which covers all services. Call for an appointment; walk-in notary is often available. Bring your ID and any documents.
items.hack: Retirees keep legal assistance eligibility at most installations for life, and almost nobody uses it. A retiree can get a will, a durable power of attorney, an advance directive and a healthcare proxy drafted and notarized for free — the same package a civilian attorney charges well into four figures for. Do it the month you retire, and update after any move, marriage, divorce or birth. The free notary alone is worth knowing about.
items.deadline: None; appointment availability varies.

items.title: CFPB Office of Servicemember Affairs — what filing a complaint actually does
items.org: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Office of Servicemember Affairs
items.who: Service members, veterans, military spouses, survivors and families with a problem involving a consumer financial product or service — mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, student loans, debt collection, credit reporting, bank accounts, prepaid cards or money transfers.
items.value: The CFPB complaint system routes your complaint to the company, which is expected to respond substantively within a defined period (commonly cited as 15 days for an initial response, up to 60 days for complex matters). You can review and dispute the response, and the complaint is retained in the Bureau's database and used in supervision. OSA specifically tracks servicemember and veteran complaints and publishes findings.
items.how: File at consumerfinance.gov/complaint and identify yourself as a servicemember, veteran, spouse or survivor so the complaint routes to the servicemember data set. CFPB consumer line: 855-411-2372 (TTY/TDD 855-729-2372).
items.hack: The honest value proposition: a CFPB complaint is not an adjudication and will not order a company to pay you, but it is the most effective way to reach a company's executive-level regulatory response team. Front-line customer service says no; the unit that answers CFPB complaints has authority to make exceptions and a strong incentive to resolve. File the complaint AND keep your own paper trail. Note that CFPB structure and resourcing have been subject to significant change, so verify current operations and response times at the official site rather than assuming.
items.deadline: No filing deadline, but file while you still have documents and the account is open.

items.title: MilitaryConsumer.gov — and the three federal reporting sites that do three different jobs
items.org: Federal Trade Commission / Department of Defense / Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
items.who: Service members, veterans, military families and survivors. MilitaryConsumer.gov is jointly operated by the FTC, DoD and CFPB as the official military consumer education site.
items.value: Plain-language guidance organized around financial life stages — spend, earn, borrow, save and invest, protect, and life events including first duty station, deployment, PCS, transition and veteran life — plus a downloadable toolkit, scam alerts, and routing to the federal complaint systems.
items.how: Start at militaryconsumer.gov. To report fraud or a scam, use ReportFraud.ftc.gov. For identity theft, use IdentityTheft.gov, which generates a personalized recovery plan and an FTC Identity Theft Report. For financial products, use consumerfinance.gov/complaint.
items.hack: The three reporting sites do different jobs and people use the wrong one. ReportFraud.ftc.gov feeds law enforcement intelligence but will not get your money back. IdentityTheft.gov is the one that produces a LEGAL DOCUMENT — the FTC Identity Theft Report — which creditors and credit bureaus must accept as the basis for blocking fraudulent accounts and information. CFPB is the one that makes a company respond to YOU. If you have been defrauded, file all three.
items.deadline: None, but identity theft recovery is far easier in the first weeks.

items.title: Active duty alerts and free credit freezes — the FCRA protections nobody activates
items.org: Equifax, Experian, TransUnion / Fair Credit Reporting Act
items.who: Active duty service members deployed away from their usual duty station are entitled to an ACTIVE DUTY ALERT. Everyone — including every veteran and family member — is entitled to free credit freezes and free credit reports. Service members and dependents also have free credit MONITORING rights under federal law.
items.value: An active duty alert requires creditors to take extra identity-verification steps before extending credit, lasts one year, is renewable, and removes your name from prescreened credit offer lists for two years. A SECURITY FREEZE blocks new credit from being opened at all, is free to place and lift at every bureau, and is the stronger protection. Free credit reports are available at AnnualCreditReport.com.
items.how: Place an active duty alert with ONE of the three bureaus, which must notify the other two. Place freezes at each of the three bureaus separately — each is free. Get reports only at annualcreditreport.com, the sole federally authorized source. If you are a fraud victim, also freeze at the secondary and specialty reporting agencies.
items.hack: Freeze, do not merely alert: an alert asks creditors to be careful, a freeze stops the account from being opened. A deployed service member should freeze all three bureaus before deployment and also freeze any MINOR CHILDREN's credit, since child identity theft is typically discovered years later. Freezing and thawing is free and takes minutes online, so the old inconvenience objection no longer holds. Free credit monitoring for service members is a separate federal entitlement — request it from each bureau.
items.deadline: Active duty alerts last one year and must be renewed; freezes last until you lift them.

items.title: Debt collection rights — the 30-day validation window, and the VA overpayment path nobody uses
items.org: CFPB / Fair Debt Collection Practices Act / VA Debt Management Center
items.who: Any veteran or service member contacted about a consumer debt — medical, credit card, auto deficiency, an old charge-off, or a VA benefit overpayment.
items.value: Under the FDCPA and Regulation F: the right to a written validation notice; the right to DISPUTE the debt in writing within 30 days of the initial notice, which requires the collector to stop collection until it verifies; limits on call frequency and times; a prohibition on contacting you at work once you say not to; a prohibition on third-party disclosure; and the right to demand the collector cease communication entirely.
items.how: Send a written DEBT VALIDATION request within 30 days of first contact, by a provable method. Keep a log of every call. File complaints with the CFPB at consumerfinance.gov/complaint, the FTC, and your state attorney general.
items.hack: Three military-specific points. A collector contacting your command or implying military discipline is applying illegitimate pressure — tell them in writing to stop third-party contact and report it to the CFPB and legal assistance immediately. Servicemembers file debt collection complaints at disproportionately high rates, so the CFPB pays attention to them. And most important: a VA BENEFIT OVERPAYMENT is handled by VA's Debt Management Center, not a private collector, and you can request a WAIVER, a COMPROMISE offer, or a dispute using VA Form 5655 (Financial Status Report). Do that on the FIRST notice, before it is referred for Treasury offset, which can take your tax refund and reduce your benefit check.
items.deadline: 30 days from the first written collector notice to trigger the verification requirement. VA overpayment waiver requests have their own timelines — act on the first notice.

items.title: Identity theft recovery for veterans — and the VA-specific exposure civilians do not have
items.org: Federal Trade Commission / VA / Social Security Administration
items.who: Any veteran whose identity has been misused. Veterans are disproportionately targeted because benefit payments are predictable, the VA file number was historically the SSN, and benefit-related phishing is widespread.
items.value: IdentityTheft.gov generates a personalized recovery plan, pre-filled dispute letters, and an FTC IDENTITY THEFT REPORT — a legal document that entitles you to block fraudulent information from your credit reports, obtain an extended fraud alert, and compel businesses to stop collecting on fraudulent accounts.
items.how: File at IdentityTheft.gov. Then freeze all three credit bureaus, file a police report, contact each affected institution's fraud department in writing, and notify VA. For benefit-related fraud or a compromised VA account, contact VA at 800-827-1000 and report to the VA Office of Inspector General hotline at 800-488-8244. Report Social Security misuse to SSA at 800-269-0271.
items.hack: Veterans have an exposure civilians do not: older VA records used the SSN as the claim number, so a single leaked VA document exposes it directly. Two protective moves — ask VA to change your file number to a non-SSN identifier if it is still your SSN, and enable multi-factor authentication on VA.gov and DFAS myPay. Then watch the DIRECT DEPOSIT field: redirecting a benefit payment is a common attack, so turn on bank alerts and check your VA.gov payment information monthly.
items.deadline: Act within days; extended fraud alerts last seven years and require an FTC Identity Theft Report.

items.title: DOJ Servicemembers and Veterans Initiative — where SCRA and USERRA violations go when the company says no
items.org: U.S. Department of Justice, Servicemembers and Veterans Initiative
items.who: Service members, veterans and families whose rights under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act, or the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act have been violated.
items.value: DOJ investigates and brings enforcement actions, including pattern-or-practice suits that have produced large settlements over improper foreclosures, repossessions, interest-rate violations and improper default judgments against deployed service members. DOJ can also represent individual federal-employee USERRA claimants and intervene in private cases.
items.how: Report SCRA and USERRA violations to DOJ at servicemembers@usdoj.gov or through justice.gov/servicemembers. For USERRA, also file with the Department of Labor Veterans' Employment and Training Service, which investigates first and can refer to DOJ. Use installation legal assistance in parallel.
items.hack: Escalate past the company. SCRA violations — a repossession during deployment, a foreclosure without a court order, refusal to reduce a pre-service loan to the 6 percent cap, refusal to allow lease termination on PCS or deployment orders — are frequently resolved by a single letter from legal assistance invoking the statute. Send the interest-rate-reduction request IN WRITING with a copy of your orders, keep proof of delivery, and note that the 6 percent cap applies to PRE-SERVICE obligations and the excess interest must be FORGIVEN, not merely deferred.
items.deadline: SCRA interest rate relief can generally be requested up to 180 days after the end of military service — do not let that lapse.

items.title: The first 72 hours after a veteran dies — the call list, in order
items.org: VA / DFAS / Social Security Administration / service casualty offices
items.who: The surviving spouse, adult child, executor or next of kin of a veteran or military retiree. This is the operational checklist no single agency publishes.
items.value: Doing these in order prevents the three most common and most expensive failures: losing the burial and plot allowances, creating a months-long overpayment that DFAS and VA will claw back, and missing a time-limited survivor election.
items.how: Hours 0-24: order at least 10 CERTIFIED copies of the death certificate, because every agency wants an original and you will run out; tell the funeral home the veteran's status and ask them to request national cemetery interment or the burial flag and headstone, which funeral homes do routinely and free; if the death was on active duty, the branch Casualty Assistance Officer comes to you. Days 1-3: call DFAS Retired and Annuitant Pay to report a retiree death and START the SBP annuity — do not let retired pay keep depositing, it will be recovered; call VA at 800-827-1000 to report the death and stop compensation or pension; call Social Security at 800-772-1213; locate the DD-214 or DD Form 1300, the marriage certificate and all insurance policies; and do NOT close the joint bank account receiving benefit deposits until every agency confirms the stop.
items.hack: The two errors families make in week one are closing the receiving bank account — which makes returning overpayments a nightmare and can delay the SBP annuity for months — and spending a benefit payment that arrived for the month of death. Report the death to every paying agency within days, keep the account open, and set aside any post-death deposit until each agency states in writing what it is owed.
items.deadline: Report to DFAS, VA and SSA within days. Burial allowance deadlines and survivor elections run from the date of death.

items.title: DD Form 1300 Report of Casualty — the master document, and why you read it carefully
items.who: Survivors of a service member who died on active duty, and in some circumstances a retiree. DD Form 1300 is issued by the service casualty office.
items.value: DD Form 1300 is the authoritative official record of the death and the document that unlocks nearly everything else: it is accepted by VA, SSA, DFAS, insurers and state agencies, and it documents duty status, cause and circumstances — which in turn determine service-connected death status for DIC and burial purposes.
items.how: The service casualty office prepares it and provides it through the Casualty Assistance Officer. Request MULTIPLE certified copies at the outset. If years have passed, request a copy from the service's casualty office or through the National Personnel Records Center.
items.hack: Ask for at least ten copies when it is first issued; requesting it later takes weeks and every agency wants its own. Then READ it: the duty status and line-of-duty determination it records drives whether the death is treated as service-connected, which controls DIC eligibility, the burial allowance amount, Arlington eligibility and dependents' education benefits. If you believe the duty status or line-of-duty finding is wrong, raise it with the casualty office immediately — correcting it later is far harder and the downstream consequences are enormous.
items.deadline: Request copies at issuance; corrections are vastly easier in the first weeks.

items.title: Death gratuity and SGLI — the two fastest payments, and the forms that override your will
items.org: Defense Finance and Accounting Service / Office of Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance
items.who: Survivors of a service member who dies on active duty or in certain other qualifying statuses. The death gratuity is a statutory lump sum paid quickly to cover immediate expenses; SGLI is the life insurance proceed.
items.value: A statutory death gratuity lump sum (long set at $100,000 and typically paid within days) plus SGLI proceeds up to the member's elected coverage amount. Both are paid to the DESIGNATED beneficiaries, and both are controlled by the member's own designation forms, not by a will. Verify the current death gratuity amount and SGLI maximum at the official sources.
items.how: The member designates death gratuity and SGLI beneficiaries on SGLV Form 8286 (and 8286A for FSGLI) in the service's personnel system. Survivors claim SGLI on SGLV Form 8283, Claim for Death Benefits, submitted to the Office of Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance. The Casualty Assistance Officer walks survivors through both.
items.hack: The planning action belongs to the LIVING service member: pull up your SGLV 8286 today and confirm the designations are current. These forms OVERRIDE your will. Divorce, remarriage, new children and the death of a named beneficiary routinely leave stale designations in place, and the result is money going to an ex-spouse or into a probate fight. Review at every life event and every PCS. Also understand that a member can designate a portion of the death gratuity outside the default statutory order — that election exists and is rarely used deliberately.
items.deadline: No claim deadline for SGLI, but update designations now — they control, and cannot be fixed after death.

items.title: SF 1174 — claiming a retiree's arrears of pay, and the month-of-death trap
items.org: Defense Finance and Accounting Service, Retired and Annuitant Pay
items.who: The designated beneficiary or eligible survivor of a deceased military retiree. Arrears of pay is retired pay earned but unpaid as of the date of death, prorated for the month of death.
items.value: Payment of the prorated retired pay owed for the month of death plus any other unpaid amounts, paid to the person the retiree designated on DD Form 2656 for arrears of pay, or in the statutory order of precedence if no valid designation exists.
items.how: Report the death to DFAS Retired and Annuitant Pay immediately. DFAS then sends SF 1174, Claim for Unpaid Compensation of Deceased Member of the Uniformed Services, to the designated beneficiary, who completes and returns it with a certified death certificate. The SBP annuity is claimed separately — DFAS issues that application to the surviving spouse.
items.hack: Two things collide here. DFAS pays retired pay in arrears, so the deposit arriving after death is usually for the PRIOR month and belongs to the estate — but DFAS will also recover any amount paid for the period after death. The result is a confusing sequence of a recovery followed by a payment, which is why you do not spend post-death deposits and do not close the account. Separately, the living retiree should check the arrears-of-pay designation on DD Form 2656 now: like SGLI, it overrides the will, and a stale designation sends the final check to the wrong person.
items.deadline: File SF 1174 promptly; report the death to DFAS within days to limit the overpayment that must be returned.

items.title: VA Form 21P-530EZ — the burial allowance application, and the exceptions that erase the deadline
items.who: Surviving spouses, children, parents, estate executors, other family members or friends who paid burial costs, and in some cases funeral home representatives. The veteran must not have a dishonorable discharge and must meet a qualifying condition: a service-connected death, death while in VA care, a VA claim pending at death, or receipt of VA benefits at death.
items.value: The burial and funeral allowance, the plot or interment allowance, and transportation reimbursement for moving the remains to a national cemetery. Amounts are adjusted annually — verify current figures at the official page rather than relying on any published number.
items.how: File VA Form 21P-530EZ online at VA.gov or by mail, attaching the death certificate, proof of the burial expenses you paid (the itemized funeral bill marked paid), and the DD-214.
items.hack: The deadline structure is where money is lost. For a NON-service-connected death you generally have 2 YEARS from the date of burial — but there is NO deadline if the veteran died while in VA care, at a VA or VA-contracted facility, and NO deadline for the plot, interment or transportation allowances. For a SERVICE-CONNECTED death there is no deadline at all. So a family past the two-year window should still file: ask whether death occurred in VA care, and file for the plot and transportation allowances regardless, because those have no time limit. Note too that a claim pending at death can itself establish burial eligibility.
items.deadline: 2 years from burial for non-service-connected deaths, with exceptions; no deadline for service-connected deaths, deaths in VA care, or plot and transportation allowances.

items.title: VA Form 21P-0847 substitution — the one-year deadline that is worth years of retroactive pay
items.org: VA Pension and Fiduciary Service / Veterans Benefits Administration
items.who: Survivors of a veteran who died while a VA claim or appeal was pending, or who was owed money VA had not yet paid. There are two distinct remedies and they are not the same thing.
items.value: ACCRUED BENEFITS (VA Form 21P-601, Application for Accrued Amounts Due a Deceased Beneficiary) pays amounts due and unpaid at death, limited to the evidence already in the file, to a limited class of survivors in statutory order. SUBSTITUTION (VA Form 21P-0847, Request for Substitution of Claimant Upon Death of Claimant) lets an eligible survivor STEP INTO the veteran's pending claim or appeal, submit NEW evidence, keep the veteran's original effective date, and pursue the full retroactive award.
items.how: File VA Form 21P-0847 for substitution within ONE YEAR of the veteran's death, and VA Form 21P-601 for accrued benefits within one year as well. Where both are available, file BOTH.
items.hack: Substitution is the one that matters and the one nobody files. Accrued benefits are frozen to the evidence already in the file; substitution lets the survivor DEVELOP the claim — obtain the nexus letter, respond to development letters, go to the Board — while preserving the veteran's effective date, which can mean years of retroactive compensation rather than a few months of unpaid benefits. The one-year deadline from the date of death is absolute. If a veteran dies with ANY claim or appeal pending, file 21P-0847 in the first month and get an accredited VSO or attorney involved immediately.
items.deadline: ONE YEAR from the date of the veteran's death, for both substitution and accrued benefits. Strictly enforced.

items.title: The survivor notification list — every agency to call, and the beneficiary forms that distribute more money than the will
items.org: VA / DFAS / SSA / OPM / Thrift Savings Plan / insurers
items.who: Any surviving spouse, executor or next of kin. Each entry has a distinct benefit, a distinct phone number and a distinct failure mode.
items.value: What each call produces: DFAS Retired and Annuitant Pay stops retired pay, starts the SBP annuity and issues SF 1174. VA (800-827-1000) stops compensation or pension and opens the DIC claim (VA Form 21P-534EZ) and the burial claim (21P-530EZ). Social Security (800-772-1213) stops benefits, pays the statutory lump-sum death payment to an eligible spouse or child, and starts survivor benefits. The Thrift Savings Plan pays per the TSP-3 designation. OPM handles a federal civilian annuity and FEGLI. The Office of Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance handles SGLI, VGLI and FSGLI claims on SGLV 8283. Then private insurers, employers, the state veterans agency and the county recorder.
items.how: Work the list in writing as well as by phone and request written confirmation of each stop and each claim number. Keep one log with date, agency, person, number and reference number. Order more death certificates than you think you need.
items.hack: The TSP beneficiary designation is the most commonly missed item on this list and often the single largest asset — TSP pays according to form TSP-3 on file, which supersedes any will, and stale designations are extremely common. Living service members and retirees should verify TSP-3, SGLV 8286, the DD Form 2656 arrears designation, and every IRA and bank beneficiary line THIS WEEK. Those four forms distribute more money than most wills do, and none of them is updated by getting divorced.
items.deadline: Report deaths within days. DIC, burial and substitution claims each carry their own deadlines, the tightest being one year for substitution.

items.title: The FTC Funeral Rule — itemized pricing, no required packages, and the casket you bought elsewhere
items.who: Every family arranging a funeral, including every veteran's family. The Funeral Rule is federal law binding on funeral homes nationwide.
items.value: Enforceable rights: a GENERAL PRICE LIST you may keep, given to you at the start of any in-person discussion of arrangements or prices; itemized pricing so you buy only what you want; prices over the telephone on request; a casket price list and outer burial container price list BEFORE being shown the merchandise; the right to supply your own casket or urn bought elsewhere with NO handling fee; no requirement to buy a package; a written statement of goods and services selected with the total; and disclosure of any legal requirement the funeral home claims applies.
items.how: Ask for the General Price List in writing at the first conversation and get prices by phone before visiting. Compare at least three funeral homes — price variation for identical services routinely runs into thousands of dollars. Report violations to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and to your state funeral board.
items.hack: The casket provision is the biggest single saving and the most resisted: you can buy a casket from a third party for a fraction of funeral home pricing, and the funeral home may not charge a handling fee or refuse to use it. Embalming is rarely legally required, and a funeral home may not tell you it is when it is not. And for a veteran being buried in a national cemetery, the grave, opening and closing, liner, headstone and perpetual care are provided at no cost — so you are buying far less from the funeral home than the package assumes. Say so, and ask them to re-price against a national cemetery interment.
items.deadline: None, but request the General Price List before any discussion of merchandise.

items.title: VA Patient Advocate and the White House VA Hotline — the two escalation levers inside VA health care
items.org: VA Veterans Experience Office / facility Patient Advocates / VA Office of Inspector General
items.who: Any veteran, family member or caregiver with a problem in VA health care — access, a denied item, a rude encounter, a scheduling failure, a billing error, or a clinical concern.
items.value: Every VA medical center has a Patient Advocate whose job is to resolve complaints and who can convene service chiefs. Above that, the White House VA Hotline (855-948-2311) operates 24/7 and creates a tracked inquiry routed to the facility with reporting back up the chain. The VA Office of Inspector General hotline (800-488-8244) handles fraud, waste, abuse and patient safety concerns.
items.how: Ask the facility operator for the Patient Advocate by title and get a written case number. If unresolved, call the White House VA Hotline at 855-948-2311 and get the inquiry number. For patient safety or integrity issues, contact the VA OIG hotline at 800-488-8244.
items.hack: Use them in order and collect numbers at each step. The Patient Advocate resolves most things quietly and fast, and skipping them wastes the one lever with local authority. But when a facility simply is not responding, the White House VA Hotline is genuinely effective because it generates a tracked item the facility director must answer — veterans routinely report that something which sat for three months moved in a week. And if a prosthetic, dental or travel denial is the issue, name the specific item and the specific rule in the complaint; generic complaints get generic answers.
items.deadline: None, but complain while the record is current.

items.title: Federal Voting Assistance Program — the FPCA, the backup ballot, and why military ballots get rejected
items.org: Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP), Department of Defense
items.who: Active duty service members and their eligible family members, and U.S. citizens residing overseas, voting absentee under the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act.
items.value: UOCAVA rights: register and request absentee ballots for a full election cycle using ONE form, the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA, Standard Form 76); receive ballots electronically where the state allows; and use the FEDERAL WRITE-IN ABSENTEE BALLOT (FWAB) as a backup if the state ballot does not arrive in time.
items.how: Complete the FPCA at fvap.gov each January — it covers all federal elections that calendar year. Use the state-by-state guide at fvap.gov for your state's deadlines and transmission options. Installation Voting Assistance Officers help in person.
items.hack: Two mechanics prevent most rejections. First, file a fresh FPCA every January and after every PCS — a stale address is the leading cause of a ballot never arriving. Second, if the state ballot has not arrived about 30 days before the election, send the FEDERAL WRITE-IN ABSENTEE BALLOT immediately; if the state ballot later arrives and you return it, the state counts the state ballot and discards the FWAB, so there is no downside to sending the backup. Also check whether your state requires a witness or notary signature — a missing signature is the second-biggest rejection cause, and installation legal assistance notarizes free.
items.deadline: FPCA each January and after every move; FWAB about 30 days out if no ballot has arrived; state receipt deadlines vary and are strict.

items.title: Vehicle buying protections for service members — and the Military Lending Act gap nobody mentions
items.org: FTC / state attorneys general / installation legal assistance
items.who: Service members buying vehicles, especially junior enlisted at first duty stations and at dealerships clustered outside installation gates that market specifically to military buyers.
items.value: The applicable protections: the FTC Used Car Rule requires a BUYERS GUIDE window sticker disclosing warranty status; FTC rules and state unfair-and-deceptive-practices statutes prohibit deceptive pricing and add-on practices; state lemon laws cover new and in some states used vehicles; the SCRA caps interest on PRE-service loans at 6 percent; and the Military Lending Act's 36 percent MAPR cap applies to many consumer credit products but NOT to a loan secured by the vehicle being purchased.
items.how: Before signing, take the deal sheet to installation legal assistance and the Personal Financial Manager — both free, both usually same-day. Get your own financing pre-approval from a credit union first. Demand the Buyers Guide and a vehicle history report. After a bad deal, file with the CFPB at consumerfinance.gov/complaint, the state attorney general, the state DMV dealer board, and the installation commander, who can bar a dealer from the installation.
items.hack: The Military Lending Act exclusion is the single most important and least-known fact here: purchase-money vehicle loans are NOT covered by the 36 percent MAPR cap, so the protection service members believe they have on a car loan does not exist. That is exactly why add-ons — GAP, service contracts, window etching, credit insurance — get stacked into vehicle financing. Refuse all add-ons at signing and buy any you actually want separately later. And watch for the yo-yo sale, where you drive off before financing is final and are called back to re-sign at worse terms: do not take delivery until the financing is final in writing.
items.deadline: State lemon law notice periods and cancellation rights are short and vary — act within days. Add-on product free-look periods are typically 10 to 30 days.

items.title: VA Form 10-10EZR — the annual update that quietly controls your copays and travel pay
items.org: VA Veterans Health Administration Health Eligibility Center
items.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care, particularly those in Priority Groups 5, 7 and 8 whose enrollment and copay status depend on income, and anyone whose household size, dependents or other insurance has changed.
items.value: VA Form 10-10EZR, the Health Benefits Update Form, updates income, household size, dependents and insurance. It controls your priority group, whether you owe copays, your income-based beneficiary travel eligibility, and your eligibility for cost-free care for certain conditions.
items.how: Submit 10-10EZR online at VA.gov, by mail, or in person at the enrollment office whenever income or household changes, and review it at least annually. Veterans can also consent to automatic income verification using IRS and SSA data in place of annual self-reporting.
items.hack: This is the quiet lever on a lot of money. An income DROP — retirement, job loss, a spouse leaving work — moves you to a lower copay tier and can open income-based beneficiary travel eligibility, but only if you report it, and VA will not come asking. Conversely, adding a dependent raises your income threshold, which helps you. Three prompts to file a 10-10EZR: any income drop, any new dependent, any change in other health insurance. Veterans sit in Priority Group 8 paying copays for years after their income fell below the threshold, purely because nobody told them the form existed.
items.deadline: Report changes when they happen; review annually.

items.title: Free communication equipment and device loans — iCanConnect, state TEDPs and AT Act programs
items.org: FCC National Deaf-Blind Equipment Distribution Program / state assistive technology programs
items.who: Veterans with a disability affecting communication. Three distinct programs: iCanConnect (the National Deaf-Blind Equipment Distribution Program) for people with combined vision and hearing loss; state Telecommunications Equipment Distribution Programs for people with hearing, speech, vision or mobility disabilities; and state Assistive Technology Act programs, which serve anyone.
items.value: iCanConnect provides communication equipment and training at no cost to income-eligible people with combined hearing and vision loss — braille displays, screen readers, amplified phones, tablets. State TEDPs provide amplified, captioned and specialized telephones, often free or nominal and usually with no income test. State AT Act programs provide free device DEMONSTRATION, short-term LOAN, and reuse or exchange of used equipment.
items.how: iCanConnect: find your state program at icanconnect.org. State TEDP: search your state's name plus 'telecommunications equipment distribution program,' or ask your state commission for the deaf and hard of hearing. State AT program: find yours at at3center.net.
items.hack: The state Assistive Technology Act program is the most useful and least known of the three, because it lets you TRY equipment before anyone buys it. A veteran unsure whether a particular magnifier, communication device or environmental control will actually help can borrow it for several weeks free. Do that BEFORE asking VA PSAS to purchase it — the loan period produces exactly the functional evidence the VA clinician needs for the consult, and it prevents VA buying the wrong device.
items.deadline: None; iCanConnect has an income test, most TEDPs and AT Act programs do not.

items.title: Durable medical equipment reuse and loan closets — free wheelchairs, walkers, beds and ramps
items.org: Local DME reuse programs / Area Agencies on Aging / veteran service organizations / Habitat ReStore
items.who: Any veteran or family member needing durable medical equipment quickly, including while a VA prosthetics consult is pending or when VA will not issue a particular item.
items.value: Free or nearly free refurbished durable medical equipment: wheelchairs, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, bedside commodes, hospital beds, patient lifts, ramps, and sometimes power chairs and scooters. Many programs also accept donations and sanitize and repair equipment before reissue.
items.how: Call 211 or your Area Agency on Aging (eldercare.acl.gov, 800-677-1116) and ask for a DME reuse program or 'loan closet.' Also ask your County Veteran Service Officer, local VFW, American Legion, DAV chapter, Lions Club, and faith-based medical lending ministries, plus Habitat for Humanity ReStore for ramp materials.
items.hack: Loan closets solve the timing problem VA cannot: the prosthetics consult takes weeks, and the veteran needs a shower chair tonight. Borrow from a loan closet now and let the VA consult run in parallel for the permanent, properly fitted item. Loan closets are also where you find the odd item VA declined — a second walker for upstairs, a transport chair for travel — and nobody tracks them nationally, so the phone call to 211 is the only way in.
items.deadline: None; inventory is first-come.

items.title: VA prescription copays, the annual cap and the exemptions nobody claims
items.org: VA Veterans Health Administration Pharmacy Benefits Management
items.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care who receive outpatient medications. Copays vary by priority group and medication tier, and several categories of veterans and medications are EXEMPT.
items.value: Outpatient medication copays are tiered by medication class, are subject to an ANNUAL CALENDAR-YEAR CAP after which no further medication copays are owed that year, and are waived entirely for several categories — including Priority Group 1 veterans (50 percent or more disabling, unemployable due to service-connected conditions, or Medal of Honor recipients), veterans rated 40 percent or less whose income falls at or below the national income limits, medications for conditions covered by a special treatment authority (combat service, Agent Orange, Camp Lejeune, military sexual trauma and others), former POWs, and Purple Heart recipients. Verify the current copay tiers, the dollar amount of the annual cap and the full exemption list at the official VA copay rates page.
items.how: Confirm your copay status with the VA enrollment office and the pharmacy, and ask whether you have hit the annual cap. If your income dropped, file VA Form 10-10EZR. If a medication treats a service-connected condition, ask the provider to document that linkage in the record so the copay is waived.
items.hack: The service-connected medication exemption is the one left on the table most often, because it depends on how the prescription is linked in the record rather than on your overall rating. If you are rated for a condition and taking medication for it, ask the provider and the pharmacy to flag it as treating the service-connected condition. Second: ask whether you have reached the ANNUAL CAP — once reached, further copays stop for the rest of the calendar year, and veterans keep paying without knowing the cap exists.
items.deadline: Copay caps run by calendar year; file a 10-10EZR as soon as income drops.

items.title: VA copay exemption and debt relief — hardship waivers, repayment plans and the catastrophic disability determination
items.org: VA Veterans Health Administration / VA Health Resource Center
items.who: Veterans who owe VA copays or medical debt, or who face copays they cannot afford. Separately, veterans whose clinical condition may qualify them for a CATASTROPHICALLY DISABLED determination, which eliminates inpatient and outpatient copays regardless of rating.
items.value: Three distinct remedies: a hardship determination that prospectively exempts you from copays based on projected current-year income; a waiver, compromise or extended repayment plan for copay debt already incurred; and a CATASTROPHICALLY DISABLED determination under 38 CFR 17.36, a clinical finding that places the veteran in Priority Group 4 and removes inpatient and outpatient care copays. Verify how each remedy currently affects medication copays specifically, since medication and care copays follow different rules.
items.how: Request a hardship determination through the VA enrollment office using the current-year projected income process. For existing debt, contact the VA Health Resource Center and request a waiver, compromise or extended repayment plan, supported by VA Form 5655 (Financial Status Report). For catastrophic disability, ask a VA clinician to request the clinical evaluation.
items.hack: The CATASTROPHICALLY DISABLED determination is the hidden one. It is a CLINICAL determination based on functional dependency — not on your disability percentage — so a veteran rated well below 50 percent who is clinically dependent in activities of daily living can qualify for Priority Group 4 and lose the care copays. It must be requested and evaluated; VA does not screen for it. Ask the clinician directly. And for existing debt, request the hardship determination and the waiver in the SAME letter, because the hardship stops the bleeding going forward while the waiver addresses what already accrued.
items.deadline: Hardship determinations are generally made for the current year and must be requested; address copay debt on the first billing notice.

items.title: The VA Caregiver Support Line and Caregiver Support Coordinator — the whole menu in one call
items.who: Family members and friends caring for a veteran of any era, including caregivers of veterans who are not enrolled in the comprehensive stipend program.
items.value: The Caregiver Support Line (1-855-260-3274, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern) and every VA medical center's Caregiver Support Coordinator provide: eligibility information for both caregiver programs (PGCSS, open to caregivers of enrolled veterans from ANY era, and PCAFC, the comprehensive stipend program with a service-connection threshold); peer support mentoring; caregiver skills training and coaching; self-care programs; telephone support; referral to respite care; and connection to community aging and disability resources.
items.how: Call the VA Caregiver Support Line at 1-855-260-3274, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern, or ask your VA medical center for the Caregiver Support Coordinator by title.
items.hack: One call to the Caregiver Support Coordinator should produce the whole menu rather than one program, so ask the question that forces it: 'Walk me through every program a caregiver in my situation can access — stipend, respite, skills training, peer mentor, Veteran-Directed Care, Adult Day Health Care, Homemaker and Home Health Aide — and what each requires.' The programs sit in different offices with different eligibility rules, and caregivers routinely learn about one, are found ineligible, and never hear about the other six.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: TRICARE Dental Program — the dental plan for Guard, Reserve and active duty FAMILIES
items.org: Defense Health Agency / TRICARE Dental Program
items.who: Family members of active duty service members, and Selected Reserve and Individual Ready Reserve (mobilization-only) members AND their families. Active duty members themselves get dental through military dental facilities, not TDP. Retirees are NOT eligible for TDP — retirees and their families use FEDVIP dental through BENEFEDS instead.
items.value: Voluntary, premium-based dental insurance with cost shares: diagnostic and preventive care typically at no cost share, with cost shares on restorative, endodontic, periodontal, prosthodontic and orthodontic services, subject to an annual maximum and a separate lifetime orthodontic maximum. The government pays a share of the premium for eligible sponsors.
items.how: Enroll through the TDP contractor and manage enrollment through milConnect. Confirm current premiums, cost-share percentages, the annual maximum and the orthodontic maximum at the official TRICARE dental page rather than relying on published figures.
items.hack: Two things families get wrong. First, TDP has a 12-month minimum enrollment commitment, so enroll when a dependent is added rather than waiting for a problem. Second, and the big one: TDP ENDS AT RETIREMENT. At the retirement transition you must move to FEDVIP dental through BENEFEDS, and that is a separate enrollment with its own window — families discover the gap when a child's orthodontic treatment is mid-course. Line up the FEDVIP enrollment before the retirement date.
items.deadline: 12-month minimum enrollment commitment; TDP terminates at retirement and FEDVIP enrollment has its own window — act before the retirement date.

items.title: Funeral Consumers Alliance — the nonprofit that publishes what local funeral homes actually charge
items.org: Funeral Consumers Alliance and local affiliate societies
items.who: Any family planning or arranging a funeral, including veterans' families. Funeral Consumers Alliance is a nonprofit consumer federation with local affiliate societies in many states.
items.value: Local affiliates conduct PRICE SURVEYS of funeral homes in their area and publish the results, which is the only practical way to see side-by-side pricing without calling a dozen funeral homes while grieving. FCA also publishes guides on state law, body donation, home funerals, green burial, cremation and what is and is not legally required, plus consumer complaint help.
items.how: Find your local affiliate at funerals.org. Many affiliates offer a low-cost lifetime membership that includes the local price survey and a pre-planning document file. Request the survey BEFORE you need it.
items.hack: This is the single best preparation step a family can take in advance, and it takes twenty minutes while nobody is grieving. Pull your local price survey, identify the two or three funeral homes with reasonable pricing, and write their names into the same file as the DD-214 and the pre-need burial eligibility letter. Families overpay by thousands not because they are careless but because they are making a purchasing decision in the worst 48 hours of their lives, from a single vendor, with no price reference.
items.deadline: None, but do it in advance — the value evaporates once you are in the arrangement conference.

items.title: IRS Identity Protection PIN — the free control that stops a fraudulent tax return in your name
items.who: Any taxpayer, including every veteran and service member. The IP PIN program is open to anyone who can verify their identity — it is no longer limited to confirmed identity theft victims.
items.value: A six-digit Identity Protection PIN, issued annually, that must appear on your federal return for the IRS to accept it. Without the PIN, an electronically filed return in your name is rejected and a paper return receives additional scrutiny — which blocks the refund-theft scheme outright.
items.how: Enroll through the 'Get an IP PIN' tool at irs.gov using IRS online identity verification. A new PIN is issued each year and is available through the same tool; taxpayers unable to verify online can use an alternative paper process. Keep the PIN with your tax documents and give it to whoever prepares your return, including a VITA or MilTax preparer.
items.hack: Deployed and PCSing service members are uniquely exposed to refund theft because they file late, mail changes constantly, and may not notice a fraudulently filed return for a year. The IP PIN is free, takes about ten minutes, and makes refund fraud in your name essentially impossible. Enroll before filing season, not during it, and note that the PIN changes annually — retrieve the new one each January so it does not derail your filing.
items.deadline: Retrieve a new IP PIN each year before filing; enroll before filing season opens.

items.title: Adult Day Health Care and VA respite — the two benefits that keep a caregiver employed
items.who: Enrolled veterans who need supervision or assistance during the day, and the family members caring for them. Adult Day Health Care and respite care are separate authorizations with separate eligibility and separate approval paths.
items.value: ADULT DAY HEALTH CARE provides a structured daytime program — nursing oversight, therapies, meals, social and recreational activity, and often transportation — at a VA site, a community site under VA contract, or a Veteran-Directed arrangement. RESPITE CARE provides short-term relief for the caregiver, delivered in the home, at an adult day program, or as a short inpatient or community living center stay.
items.how: Ask your VA social worker or the Geriatrics and Extended Care program for an evaluation for BOTH Adult Day Health Care and respite care, by name, in the same conversation. Copays may apply depending on priority group — ask what they are before the first authorization. Also ask the Caregiver Support Coordinator (1-855-260-3274) what respite the caregiver programs add on top.
items.hack: Frame the request around the CAREGIVER's employment and health, not just the veteran's needs — 'I cannot keep my job without daytime coverage' and 'I have not slept in a week' are the clinical facts that move these authorizations. And ask about them TOGETHER: ADHC covers weekdays so a caregiver can work, respite covers the gaps so a caregiver can have surgery, attend a funeral, or simply stop. Families take one and never learn about the other, because they are approved by different staff.
items.deadline: No application deadline, but respite authorizations are typically granted in limited periods per year — ask how many and use them.

items.title: Why the SAH/SHA/TRA numbers you just read are already wrong — the October 1 re-index
items.org: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Loan Guaranty Service
items.who: Any veteran or service member researching VA adaptive housing grants, and anyone writing or reading a 'VA grant amounts' article.
items.value: The SAH, SHA and TRA maximums are not fixed dollar figures. Under 38 U.S.C. 2102(e), VA raises them every fiscal year by the change in a residential cost-of-construction index — the Turner Building Cost Index, specified at 38 CFR 36.4411(a). The FY2026 increase was 3.87%, measured from Q2 2024 to Q2 2025, producing FY2026 maximums of $126,526 under section 2101(a), $25,349 under 2101(b), $116,084 for a 2102(b) grant, and TRA caps of $50,961 and $9,099. A new set of numbers took effect on 1 October 2026 for FY2027. Do not budget off any FY2026 figure, including the ones in older entries in this reference.
items.how: Pull the current number from VA's own SAH page or from the Federal Register notice for the current fiscal year before you sign anything. Search the Federal Register for 'Cost-of-Construction Index for Fiscal Year' plus the year. VA has published the notice as late as November for a cycle that began 1 October, so between 1 October and publication the only authoritative source is the VA Regional Loan Center handling your case — ask them in writing what the current cap is and keep the answer.
items.hack: The index has a floor of zero: if construction costs fall or stay flat, the grant does not go down. That means the maximum only ratchets upward. If your adaptation project can wait a few months and you have not yet used any of your lifetime entitlement, starting the project after 1 October gives you the new, higher cap — a swing that has run $4,000 to $5,000 a year recently. Conversely, if you are mid-project and your approval was issued under last year's cap, ask the Regional Loan Center whether your remaining entitlement can be recalculated at the new rate.
items.deadline: Re-indexes every 1 October. FY2027 figures effective 1 October 2026.

items.title: The SAH prior-approval trap — buy or build first and VA owes you nothing
items.org: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Loan Guaranty Service
items.who: Veterans and service members approved or applying for SAH, SHA, TRA, or the automobile/adaptive equipment benefits.
items.value: Protects the entire grant — six figures in the SAH case. VA's adaptive housing and automobile benefits are prior-approval programs: VA must approve the specific plan, the specific equipment, or the specific vehicle purchase before the money is spent. VA's own automobile allowance page states the requirement flatly: you must have prior VA approval before purchasing an automobile or adaptive equipment. The same logic governs adaptive housing — an unapproved adaptation is an adaptation you paid for.
items.how: File VA Form 26-4555 (Application in Acquiring Specially Adapted Housing or Special Home Adaptation Grant) and wait for the determination and the approved scope of work. For adaptive equipment, VA Form 21-4502 or VA Form 10-1394. Get the approval in writing, with the dollar figure and the approved items named, before a contractor breaks ground or a dealer takes a deposit.
items.hack: If you have already spent the money, do not assume it is over — ask the Regional Loan Center about a retroactive determination in writing and get the denial in writing too, because a written denial is an appealable decision and a verbal 'no' is not. Separately: your SAH entitlement can be used up to six separate times across your life, so a small unapproved project that VA refuses to reimburse does not destroy the remaining entitlement. Protect the remaining uses by never starting another project without the paper.
items.deadline: No application deadline; approval must precede the spending.

items.title: VA's own automobile allowance page shows a 2018 number — how to get the real one
items.org: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Benefits Administration
items.who: Veterans and service members with service-connected loss or loss of use of a hand or foot, severe permanent vision impairment in both eyes, burn-related contractures, or ALS.
items.value: A one-time payment toward a vehicle, plus adaptive equipment that is NOT one-time and can be provided repeatedly over the life of the benefit. The statutory allowance under 38 U.S.C. 3902 is adjusted over time, but as of this writing VA's benefits.va.gov automobile allowance page still prints 'not more than $21,058.69, beginning 10-01-18.' Other VA and third-party sources carry substantially higher current figures. Treat every published number, including the one elsewhere in this reference, as unverified until you confirm it.
items.how: Apply with VA Form 21-4502 for the vehicle allowance and adaptive equipment; VA Form 10-1394 if you qualify for adaptive equipment only. Ask the VA Regional Office or the Prosthetics service at your VA medical center to state the current allowance in writing before you shop. Get prior approval.
items.hack: The adaptive equipment side is where the real recurring money is and almost nobody works it. The vehicle allowance is once per lifetime; adaptive equipment — power steering, power brakes, power windows and seats, lifts, hand controls, entry and exit assists — can be reauthorized as equipment wears out or your condition changes, and it is not capped at the vehicle-allowance figure. Ankle immobility of the knees or hips qualifies you for adaptive equipment even if you do not qualify for the vehicle allowance itself.
items.deadline: No deadline; prior approval required before purchase.

items.title: The SAH Assistive Technology grant — $200,000 a year, and an authorization you must check
items.org: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Loan Guaranty Service
items.who: Any person or entity developing new assistive technology for SAH grant recipients — under 38 U.S.C. 2108 this is open to individuals as well as organizations, not just corporate developers.
items.value: Up to $200,000 per applicant per fiscal year to develop assistive technology that helps SAH-eligible veterans live independently at home. VA has stated plainly that the program is administered annually and does not guarantee subsequent awards, and the 2024 rulemaking described statutory authority running through 30 September 2024 — meaning continuation depends on Congressional reauthorization. Confirm the program is authorized and funded for the current fiscal year before you invest time in an application.
items.how: Watch for the Notice of Funding Availability in the Federal Register and the opportunity listing on grants.gov. Applications go through grants.gov, which requires a SAM.gov registration and Unique Entity ID first — start that weeks early, it is the usual reason people miss the window.
items.hack: For veterans rather than developers: the reason to watch SAHAT is that it tells you what adaptive technology VA considers legitimate and fundable. A product funded by a SAHAT award is a product you can point to when you ask VA Prosthetics or your SAH agent to approve something unusual. The award announcements are a short list of VA-endorsed solutions, published annually and read by almost nobody.
items.deadline: Annual NOFA; cycle and authorization must be confirmed for the current fiscal year.

items.title: If SAH is denied: 'medically feasible' is a decision you can appeal
items.who: Veterans denied SAH, SHA, TRA or HISA, or whose approved scope of work was cut below what their clinician recommended.
items.value: The full grant, on reconsideration. An SAH determination is a VA benefit decision, and benefit decisions are appealable through the standard review lanes — not a customer-service complaint to be argued over the phone.
items.how: Get the denial in writing with its reasons. Then pick a lane: a Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) if you can add new and relevant evidence such as a specialist's letter tying the adaptation to your service-connected condition, or a Higher-Level Review (VA Form 20-0996) if you believe the existing record was misread. Board appeal (VA Form 10182) after that.
items.hack: The strongest new evidence in an adaptive housing appeal is almost never from you — it is a letter from the VA or private clinician who treats the qualifying condition, written in the statute's own language, explaining why the specific adaptation is medically necessary for you to live independently in that dwelling.
