items.title: SAH can pay down the mortgage on a home you already own and are adapting
items.who: SAH-eligible veterans and service members
items.value: Grant money for building, buying, adapting, OR reducing indebtedness on a currently owned home being adapted
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "VA may approve a grant to assist with the cost of building, buying, adapting existing homes or paying to reduce indebtedness on a currently owned home that is being adapted, up to a maximum benefit amount."
items.hack: The debt-reduction use is the least known of the four. If the home is already adapted and already yours, the grant can go against the loan balance instead of construction.
items.deadline: None

items.title: SAH qualifying disability: loss or loss of use of more than one limb
items.who: Veterans and service members with loss, or loss of use, of more than one limb
items.value: SAH grant eligibility
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: SAH eligibility includes "The loss, or loss of use, of more than one limb."
items.hack: "Loss of use" is a functional finding, not an amputation requirement - paralysis or a non-functional limb counts.
items.deadline: None

items.title: SAH qualifying disability: one lower extremity plus residuals of an organic disease or injury
items.who: Veterans with loss or loss of use of a lower extremity together with residuals of an organic disease or injury
items.value: SAH grant eligibility
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "The loss, or loss of use, of a lower extremity along with the residuals (lasting effects) of an organic (natural) disease or injury."
items.hack: This combination route is how many single-amputee veterans qualify - the second condition does not have to be another limb.
items.deadline: None

items.title: SAH qualifying disability: blindness in both eyes at 20/200 or less
items.who: Veterans blind in both eyes with 20/200 central visual acuity or less
items.value: SAH grant eligibility
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "Blindness in both eyes (with 20/200 central visual acuity or less)."
items.hack: The handbook states the acuity standard explicitly - 20/200 central visual acuity or less - so get the exact acuity documented in the eye exam, not a general 'legally blind' note.
items.deadline: None

items.title: SAH qualifying disability: certain severe burns
items.who: Veterans with certain severe burns
items.value: SAH grant eligibility
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: SAH eligibility includes "Certain severe burns."
items.hack: The handbook says 'certain' without defining them, so a burn case turns entirely on the regulation and the medical evidence - ask the SAH agent which criteria they are applying.
items.deadline: None

items.title: SAH qualifying disability: post-9/11 loss of use of ONE lower extremity that destroys balance or gait
items.who: Veterans with loss or loss of use of one lower extremity after September 11, 2001 who cannot balance or walk without braces, crutches, canes or a wheelchair
items.value: SAH grant eligibility on a single-limb basis
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "The loss, or loss of use, of one lower extremity (foot or leg) after September 11, 2001, which makes it so that you cannot balance or walk without the help of braces, crutches, canes, or a wheelchair."
items.hack: This is the single-limb door into SAH, and it only exists for post-9/11 injuries. The test is assistive-device dependence for balance or walking - document the device use, not just the diagnosis.
items.deadline: Injury must be after September 11, 2001

items.title: SAH ownership test: you own or WILL own the home
items.who: SAH applicants
items.value: Eligibility where purchase or construction has not closed yet
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "Both must be true: You own or will own the home, and You have a qualifying service-connected disability."
items.hack: "Will own" is doing real work here - you can line the grant up with a purchase or build rather than having to own first.
items.deadline: None

items.title: SHA: the grant for adapting or buying a home to live more independently
items.who: Veterans and service members entitled to compensation for permanent and total service-connected disability from a qualifying condition
items.value: Grant toward adapting or purchasing a home
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "VA may approve a grant to assist with the cost of adapting or purchasing a home to live more independently."
items.hack: SHA is the smaller sibling of SAH with a different, narrower disability list - if you miss SAH, test yourself against SHA before giving up.
items.deadline: None

items.title: SHA requires PERMANENT AND TOTAL service-connected disability from one of three conditions
items.who: Veterans entitled to compensation for permanent and total service-connected disability due to anatomical loss or loss of use of both hands, certain severe burn injuries, or certain severe respiratory injuries
items.value: SHA grant eligibility
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "Service members and Veterans must be entitled to compensation for permanent and total service-connected disability due to one of the following: Anatomical loss or loss of use of both hands; Certain severe burn injuries; Certain severe respiratory injuries."
items.hack: SHA carries a permanent-and-total requirement that SAH's bullet list does not state - that P&T element is the usual reason an otherwise-qualifying SHA claim fails.
items.deadline: None

items.title: TRA: adapt a FAMILY MEMBER's home you are temporarily living in
items.who: Eligible veterans and service members temporarily residing in a home owned by a family member
items.value: A TRA grant to adapt the family member's home
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "Eligible Veterans and Service members who are temporarily residing in a home owned by a family member may also receive a TRA grant to adapt the family member's home to meet his or her specific needs."
items.hack: TRA exists precisely for the recovery period when you are staying with family and own nothing - the usual ownership requirement does not block it.
items.deadline: None

items.title: TRA does NOT count against your SAH or SHA maximum
items.who: Veterans who use a TRA grant and later pursue SAH or SHA
items.value: Preservation of the full SAH/SHA dollar ceiling
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "NOTE: TRA grant amounts do not count against SAH or SHA grant maximum amounts."
items.hack: Use TRA while living with family and your SAH ceiling stays whole for the house you eventually buy or build. The handbook flags this as a NOTE because people assume the opposite.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Supplemental financing: a VA-guaranteed loan on top of the housing grant
items.who: Veterans and service members with available VA Home Loan Guaranty entitlement who are using a housing grant
items.value: A guaranteed loan to supplement the grant when acquiring an already-adapted home
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: "Veterans and Service members with available VA Home Loan Guaranty entitlement may also obtain a guaranteed loan to supplement the grant to acquire a specially adapted home that has already been adapted."
items.hack: Grant plus VA loan on the same transaction, specifically for a home somebody else already adapted - the cheapest path to an accessible house is often buying one that is already done.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Housing grant phone line: 877-827-3702
items.who: Anyone pursuing SAH, SHA or TRA
items.value: Direct access to the housing grant program
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: the Housing Grants for Disabled Veterans section lists 877-827-3702.
items.hack: A dedicated number beats the general line for grant questions - the SAH agents are a small specialized staff.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA's own 2026 handbook prints NO dollar amount for SAH, SHA or TRA
items.who: Anyone trying to confirm a current SAH/SHA/TRA maximum
items.value: Knowing no FY2027 figure exists in the handbook
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 3: for SAH, SHA and TRA alike the handbook says only "Rates can be found by visiting www.va.gov/housing-assistance/disability-housing-grants" - no figures and no fiscal year are printed.
items.hack: The handbook is useless as a grant-amount source. The annual cost-of-construction notice and the disability-housing-grants page are the only places the number exists.
items.deadline: Amounts re-index each October 1

items.title: VR&E eligibility: 20% with an employment handicap, OR 10% with a SERIOUS employment handicap
items.who: Veterans with a service-connected rating of at least 20% plus an employment handicap, or rated 10% with a serious employment handicap
items.value: Access to Chapter 31 training, education and employment services
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "A Veteran must have a VA service-connected disability rating of at least 20% and be determined to have an employment handicap, or rated 10% and determined to have a serious employment handicap."
items.hack: At 10% you are not shut out - you need the heavier 'serious employment handicap' finding instead. Most 10% veterans never apply because they think 20% is the floor.
items.deadline: See the period-of-eligibility rules

items.title: What an "employment handicap" actually means
items.who: VR&E applicants
items.value: The finding that unlocks Chapter 31
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "An employment handicap exists if a Veteran's service-connected disability impairs his/her ability to prepare for, obtain, and maintain suitable employment."
items.hack: Three verbs - prepare for, obtain, maintain. Failing at any one of them is an impairment, so a veteran who can get hired but cannot hold a job still fits the definition.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VR&E's basic period of eligibility is 12 years, from the LATER of two dates
items.who: Veterans using VR&E under the basic rule
items.value: A 12-year window to use Chapter 31
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "The basic period of eligibility in which VR&E benefits may be used is 12 years from 1) A Veteran's date of separation from active military service or 2) the date VA first notified a Veteran that they have been granted a compensable service-connected disability, whichever is later."
items.hack: 'Whichever is later' can buy years. A rating granted long after discharge restarts the 12-year clock from the notification date, not the separation date.
items.deadline: 12 years from the later of separation or first compensable-rating notice

items.title: The 12-year VR&E limit does NOT apply if you were discharged on or after January 1, 2013
items.who: Claimants discharged or released from active military service on or after January 1, 2013
items.value: No time limit at all on using VR&E
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "As of January 5, 2021, the 12-year eligibility period does not apply to claimants who were discharged or released from active military service on or after January 1, 2013."
items.hack: This is the single most valuable line in the chapter. If you left service in 2013 or later, VR&E has no expiration date - so a veteran told in year 13 that they are too late is being told something false.
items.deadline: None - no delimiting date for post-2013 separations

items.title: VR&E entitlement: up to 48 months full-time, or the part-time equivalent
items.who: Veterans in an approved VR&E rehabilitation plan
items.value: Up to 48 months of services
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "Veterans may be provided with up to 48 months of full-time services or the part-time equivalent based on the extent of services needed."
items.hack: 48 months is a third longer than the GI Bill's 36, and it is scaled to need rather than granted flat - part-time study stretches it further.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Service members can apply BEFORE discharge with a 20% memorandum rating
items.who: Service members expecting an honorable discharge with a memorandum rating of 20% or more
items.value: VR&E access before leaving active duty
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "Service members are eligible to apply if they expect to receive an honorable discharge upon separation from active duty; and obtain a memorandum rating of 20% or more from VA."
items.hack: A memorandum rating is not a final rating - you can start VR&E while still in uniform, which is how people have a plan running on day one as a civilian.
items.deadline: Apply before separation

items.title: IDES gives AUTOMATIC VR&E entitlement
items.who: Service members going through the Integrated Disability Evaluation System
items.value: Automatic entitlement to VR&E, without the usual handicap determination
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: service members are eligible via "automatic entitlement through the Integrated Disability Evaluation System."
items.hack: If you are in IDES you do not have to prove an employment handicap - entitlement is automatic. Anyone being medically separated should open a VR&E case during the board, not after.
items.deadline: Apply during the IDES process

items.title: VR&E Track 1 - Reemployment with your pre-service employer
items.who: Veterans and service members returning to an employer they worked for before activation, including Guard and Reserve
items.value: Help getting back into the job you left
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: Reemployment "targets Veterans and Service members who served on active military service or in the National Guard or Reserves and are now returning to employers for whom they worked prior to going on active duty."
items.hack: Pair this track with USERRA. VR&E can fund the accommodation or retraining that makes your reemployment right actually workable.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VR&E Track 2 - Rapid access to employment
items.who: Veterans who want work quickly and already have the skills for a suitable job
items.value: Job placement support without a training program
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: Rapid access to employment "targets Veterans who express a desire to obtain employment as soon as possible and already have the necessary skills to qualify for competitive employment in a suitable job."
items.hack: You do not have to go back to school to use Chapter 31. If you are already qualified, this track is placement help - and it barely touches your 48 months.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VR&E Track 3 - Self-employment, built for people who need flexibility
items.who: Veterans with limited access to traditional employment, or who need flexible schedules or a more accommodating work environment because of their disabilities or life circumstances
items.value: Support toward running your own business
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: Self-employment "targets Veterans who have limited access to traditional employment, need flexible work schedules, or need a more accommodating work environment due to their disabling conditions or other life circumstances."
items.hack: The handbook's criteria are about access and accommodation, not about having a business plan already. 'Other life circumstances' is deliberately broad - caregiving and rural isolation both fit.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VR&E Track 4 - Employment through long-term services, including degrees
items.who: Veterans needing remedial or refresher courses, specialized training, or post-secondary education to obtain or maintain suitable employment
items.value: Funded education and training, plus a subsistence allowance
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: this track "targets Veterans who need long-term services such as remedial or refresher courses, specialized training and/or post-secondary education, to obtain and/or maintain suitable employment."
items.hack: This is the track people mean when they say Chapter 31 beats the GI Bill - it covers remedial and refresher coursework the GI Bill treats as a waste of entitlement.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VR&E Track 5 - Independent living when work is not yet realistic
items.who: Veterans who may be unable to immediately return to work but can improve their independence in daily living with VR&E help
items.value: Independent living services rather than an employment plan
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: Independent living "targets Veterans who may be unable to immediately return to work, but with assistance of VR&E services, they are able to improve their independence in daily living."
items.hack: Note the word 'immediately'. The independent living track is not a declaration that you will never work - it is a stepping stone, and people do move from it into an employment track.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VR&E pays training costs AND a subsistence allowance
items.who: Veterans in an approved VR&E program of training
items.value: Cost of approved training and services, plus a subsistence allowance
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "If a program of training is selected, VA pays the cost of the approved training and services that are outlined in the Veteran's rehabilitation plan (except those coordinated through other providers), as well as a subsistence allowance."
items.hack: Watch the parenthetical - services 'coordinated through other providers' are carved out, so confirm who is paying for anything VR&E routes to an outside agency.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The handbook publishes NO VR&E subsistence allowance amounts
items.who: Anyone trying to confirm a Chapter 31 subsistence rate
items.value: Knowing the handbook is not a source for the figure
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: the chapter states a subsistence allowance is paid but prints no rate table, no dollar amounts and no effective date.
items.hack: Chapter 31 subsistence rates have to come from VA's VR&E rate page, and they vary by training time and dependents - never quote a single flat number.
items.deadline: Rates change annually (October 1)

items.title: The VR&E 2101B housing adaptation grant - a second, separate adaptation route
items.who: Veterans and service members not currently able to work because of their service-connected disabilities, or who require adaptations to achieve a vocational goal
items.value: Home adaptations delivered through VR&E rather than the SAH/SHA program
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "VR&E may provide home adaptations to Veterans and Service members who are not currently able to work because of the effects of their service-connected disabilities or who require adaptations to achieve a vocational goal."
items.hack: Almost nobody knows this exists. If you fail the SAH and SHA disability lists but need adaptations to reach a vocational goal, 2101B is a completely different door with a completely different test.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The 2101B grant amount changes yearly and is not printed in the handbook
items.who: Veterans pursuing a 2101B adaptation grant
items.value: Knowing where the current maximum lives
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "The maximum amounts may change from year-to-year and are located at www.va.gov/housing-assistance/disability-housing-grants."
items.hack: 2101B maximums sit on the same page as SAH and SHA, so check all three at once - the 2101B figure is much smaller and easy to confuse with the SAH number.
items.deadline: Re-indexed annually

items.title: VetSuccess on Campus (VSOC) - VA benefits help delivered at your school
items.who: Veterans, service members and eligible dependents attending participating campuses
items.value: Coordinated on-campus benefits assistance and counseling
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "The VSOC program aims to help Veterans, Service members, and eligible dependents succeed through a coordinated delivery of on-campus benefits assistance."
items.hack: Eligible dependents are included - a GI Bill transferee or Chapter 35 student can use the VSOC counselor too, not just the veteran.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VR&E employment services cover military SPOUSES too
items.who: Veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses
items.value: Career advice, resume building and access to veteran-friendly employers
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 4: "VA provides support to Veterans and transitioning Service members at all stages of their job search, including career advice, resume building, and access to employers who want to hire Veterans and military spouses."
items.hack: The employer network is explicitly framed as hiring veterans AND military spouses - worth naming when a spouse asks what VA has for them.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Pension brings total income up to a level set by Congress
items.who: Low-income wartime veterans and surviving family members
items.value: Supplemental income through the Veterans Pension and Survivors Pension programs
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "Payments are made to bring the Veteran's or survivor's total income, including other retirement or Social Security income, to a level set by Congress."
items.hack: Pension is a top-up, not a flat check. Every dollar of countable income reduces it - which is why the medical-expense deduction below matters so much.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Unreimbursed medical expenses reduce countable income for pension
items.who: Pension applicants and recipients with out-of-pocket medical costs
items.value: A lower countable income, and therefore a larger pension payment
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "Unreimbursed medical expenses may reduce countable income for VA purposes."
items.hack: This is the lever that makes pension work for people who look 'too wealthy' on paper. Nursing home, in-home care and insurance premiums come off income before VA does the math.
items.deadline: Report expenses annually

items.title: Pension tests BOTH income and net worth against a congressional limit
items.who: Pension applicants
items.value: Eligibility determination
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "Yearly family income and net worth must be less than the amount set by Congress to qualify for the Veterans pension benefit."
items.hack: Two separate tests. Passing the income test does not help if assets exceed the net worth limit - and the handbook does not print either number.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Pension wartime service: 90 days active duty with at least ONE day during a wartime period
items.who: Veterans with at least 90 days of active military service including at least one day during a recognized wartime period
items.value: The service gateway to Veterans Pension
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "at least 90 days of active military service, with at least one day during a recognized wartime period."
items.hack: One day inside the wartime window is enough - you do not need to have deployed or served in combat. Check the wartime period dates against your service dates before assuming you are out.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Pension service rule for later enlistees: 24 months or the full period called up
items.who: Veterans subject to the minimum active duty service requirement
items.value: The alternative service test for Veterans Pension
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "served at least 24 months or for the full period for which they called or ordered to active duty."
items.hack: 'The full period for which you were called' rescues Guard and Reserve members whose activation was shorter than 24 months - serving the whole mobilization satisfies the rule.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Pension age test: 65 or older - no disability needed
items.who: Wartime veterans aged 65 or older who meet the income and net worth tests
items.value: Veterans Pension without any disability requirement
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: qualifying conditions include "Age 65 or older."
items.hack: At 65 the disability question disappears entirely. A healthy low-income wartime veteran qualifies on age alone, which is the fact most often missed.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Pension disability test: permanently and totally disabled
items.who: Wartime veterans under 65 who are permanently and totally disabled
items.value: Veterans Pension eligibility before age 65
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: qualifying conditions include "Permanently and totally disabled."
items.hack: The disability does NOT have to be service-connected for pension - that is the fundamental difference from compensation.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Nursing home residents receiving skilled nursing care qualify for pension
items.who: Wartime veterans who are a patient in a nursing home receiving skilled nursing care
items.value: Veterans Pension eligibility without a separate P&T finding
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: qualifying conditions include "A patient in a nursing home receiving skilled nursing care."
items.hack: Nursing home placement is itself a qualifying condition. Combine it with the unreimbursed medical expense deduction and the arithmetic usually favors filing.
items.deadline: None

items.title: A VA-approved medical foster home also qualifies
items.who: Wartime veterans residing in a VA-approved medical foster home
items.value: Veterans Pension eligibility
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: qualifying conditions include "VA-approved medical foster home."
items.hack: Medical foster homes are listed alongside nursing homes here - residents should not assume the cheaper setting costs them pension eligibility.
items.deadline: None

items.title: SSDI or SSI receipt is a qualifying condition for pension
items.who: Wartime veterans receiving Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income
items.value: Veterans Pension eligibility without proving P&T to VA separately
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: qualifying conditions include "Receiving Social Security Disability Insurance" and "Receiving Supplemental Security Income."
items.hack: An existing SSDI or SSI award substitutes for the disability finding. Bring the Social Security award letter and skip a whole evidentiary fight.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Apply for pension online or on VA Form 21P-527EZ
items.who: Veterans Pension applicants
items.value: A filed pension claim
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "To apply for Veterans Pension, apply online at www.va.gov/pension or download and complete VA Form 21P-527EZ, Application for Veterans Pension."
items.hack: The EZ form is a fully developed claim - submit it with your evidence and VA is supposed to decide faster than on a general application.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Mail pension claims to the Janesville, Wisconsin intake center
items.who: Veterans filing a paper pension claim
items.value: Correct routing of the claim
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "Department of Veterans Affairs Pension Intake Center, P.O. Box 5365, Janesville, WI 53547-5365."
items.hack: Pension has its own intake center, separate from the compensation intake center. Mailing a pension claim to the wrong P.O. box costs weeks.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Aid and Attendance / Housebound is claimed on VA Form 21-2680
items.who: Pension recipients seeking the Aid and Attendance or Housebound increase (Special Monthly Pension)
items.value: The higher Special Monthly Pension rate
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "VA Form 21-2680, Examination for Housebound Status or Permanent Need for Regular Aid and Attendance."
items.hack: The form is an examination form - a physician completes it. Handing your doctor 21-2680 and the handbook's evidence list is the whole trick to a clean A&A claim.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Exactly what the A&A examination must document
items.who: Veterans and survivors claiming Aid and Attendance or Housebound
items.value: Evidence sufficient to support the increase
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: evidence must show "whether there is disease or injury producing physical or mental impairment, loss of coordination, or conditions affecting the ability to dress and undress, to feed oneself, to attend to sanitary needs and to keep oneself ordinarily clean and presentable, or whether confined to the immediate premises due to disability."
items.hack: That sentence is a checklist. Dressing, feeding, sanitary needs, grooming, and confinement to the premises - make sure the examining physician addresses each one by name rather than writing 'needs assistance'.
items.deadline: None

items.title: You cannot draw Aid and Attendance AND Housebound at the same time
items.who: Pension recipients
items.value: Clarity that these are alternatives, not additive
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "A Veteran may not receive aid and attendance benefits and housebound benefits at the same time."
items.hack: They do not stack. Claim the higher one you can actually prove - Aid and Attendance pays more than Housebound, so lead with A&A if the evidence supports it.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Medicaid-covered nursing home residents are capped at $90 per month of pension
items.who: Veterans with no dependents who are in a Medicaid-approved nursing facility and covered by a Medicaid plan for the nursing facility services
items.value: Pension limited to $90 per month
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: "Veterans with no dependents who are in a Medicaid-approved nursing facility and covered by a Medicaid plan for services furnished by the nursing facility are limited to receiving $90 per month in pension benefits."
items.hack: The cap is written for veterans with NO dependents. A veteran with a dependent spouse is outside this limitation - which is exactly the fact that changes long-term-care planning for married couples.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The handbook publishes NO pension MAPR, net worth limit or look-back figure
items.who: Anyone verifying a pension rate, net worth ceiling or transfer penalty
items.value: Knowing the handbook cannot confirm any pension dollar figure
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 5: Chapter 5 gives no Maximum Annual Pension Rate, no Aid and Attendance or Housebound amount, no net worth limit, and no asset-transfer look-back or penalty period - only "the amount set by Congress" and www.va.gov/pension.
items.hack: The handbook is silent on the look-back entirely, so the 36-month rule and any penalty period must be cited to 38 CFR 3.276 or the pension rate page, never to the handbook.
items.deadline: MAPR adjusts each December 1

items.title: What the education chapter actually promises
items.who: Veterans, service members and their qualified family members
items.value: Help with tuition, choosing a school or training program, and career counseling
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "Education and Training Benefits help Veterans, Service members and their qualified family members with needs like paying college tuition, finding the right school or training program, and getting career counseling."
items.hack: Career counseling is named as a benefit in its own right, not just a wrapper around tuition money - worth asking for explicitly.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Post-9/11 GI Bill: 90 aggregate days of active duty after September 10, 2001
items.who: Service members and veterans who served at least 90 aggregate days on active duty after September 10, 2001
items.value: Post-9/11 GI Bill entitlement
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "Service member or Veteran must serve at least 90 aggregate days on active duty after September 10, 2001."
items.hack: "Aggregate" means it adds up across separate periods. Several short mobilizations can clear 90 days together even if no single one did.
items.deadline: None - the Post-9/11 GI Bill has no delimiting date for post-2013 separations

items.title: Every Purple Heart recipient gets the Post-9/11 GI Bill
items.who: Purple Heart recipients whose award was made during service occurring after September 10, 2001
items.value: Post-9/11 GI Bill entitlement regardless of length of service
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "All Purple Heart award recipients are eligible for Post-9/11 GI Bill entitlement providing the award was made during service occurring after September 10, 2001."
items.hack: No service-length test at all. A Purple Heart recipient who served well under 90 days is still fully entitled - and at the 100% rate.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Discharged for a service-connected disability after 30 days? You still qualify
items.who: Veterans honorably discharged for a service-connected disability after serving 30 continuous days after September 10, 2001
items.value: Post-9/11 GI Bill entitlement on 30 days instead of 90
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "Veterans may also be eligible if they were honorably discharged from active duty for a service-connected disability after serving 30 continuous days after September 10, 2001."
items.hack: Note 'continuous', not aggregate, for this route - and note that it takes the 90-day bar down to 30. A medical separation early in a first enlistment is often still a GI Bill case.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Post-9/11 GI Bill: up to 36 months of entitlement
items.who: Eligible service members and veterans
items.value: Up to 36 months of education benefits
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "Service members or eligible Veterans may receive up to 36 months of entitlement under the Post-9/11 GI Bill."
items.hack: 36 months is roughly four academic years, because summers usually do not consume entitlement - plan the calendar, not just the credit count.
items.deadline: None

items.title: How tuition is paid: a percentage of in-state public cost, or a national cap at private and foreign schools
items.who: Post-9/11 GI Bill students
items.value: Tuition and fees paid directly to the school
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "Tuition and fees are paid to the institution on the student's behalf" - "a percentage of the cost of in-state tuition and fees at public institutions, or the tuition and fees capped at a national maximum rate for private or foreign schools."
items.hack: Two different mechanisms. Public schools are covered by percentage of actual in-state cost with no dollar ceiling; private and foreign schools hit a flat national cap, which is what Yellow Ribbon exists to bridge.
items.deadline: None

items.title: MHA requires MORE than half-time enrollment
items.who: Post-9/11 GI Bill students attending more than half-time
items.value: Monthly housing allowance paid directly to the student
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "A monthly housing allowance (MHA) is paid directly to the student, provided the student is attending more than half-time."
items.hack: Exactly half-time pays nothing. Dropping one class can cross that line and zero out the housing money for the whole term - check the rate of pursuit before you withdraw.
items.deadline: Verify enrollment monthly

items.title: MHA is set by the ZIP code where you physically attend most classes
items.who: Post-9/11 GI Bill students
items.value: A housing allowance keyed to campus location, not to where you live
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "MHA is calculated based on the ZIP code of the campus location where the student physically attends most of their classes."
items.hack: Campus ZIP, not home ZIP, and specifically the campus where you attend the majority of classes. For multi-campus systems that choice is worth real money.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Online-only students get HALF the national average housing rate
items.who: Post-9/11 GI Bill students taking only online courses
items.value: MHA at half the national average
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "If a student is only taking online courses, their MHA is half the national average."
items.hack: 'Only' is the trigger. A single in-person class above half-time pursuit moves you from the online rate to the campus ZIP rate - often a large difference.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Four situations where MHA is not payable at all
items.who: Flight and correspondence students; students at half-time or less; individuals on active duty and their spouses
items.value: Knowing in advance that no housing allowance will come
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "MHA is not payable to individuals enrolled in flight or correspondence training; to individuals pursuing training at half-time or less (regardless of the type of training); or to individuals on active duty or their spouses."
items.hack: Active duty members AND their spouses are excluded from MHA. A spouse using transferred entitlement while the sponsor is still serving gets tuition and books but no housing money - budget for that before the transfer.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The $500 rural relocation payment almost nobody claims
items.who: Certain individuals relocating from highly rural areas to attend school
items.value: A one-time payment of $500
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "A one-time payment of $500 paid to certain individuals relocating from highly rural areas."
items.hack: This is the rural benefit tied to counties with very low population density where you had to physically relocate or fly to reach a school. It is one-time, it is small, and it goes unclaimed constantly.
items.deadline: One-time; claim at relocation

items.title: Yellow Ribbon now explicitly includes ACTIVE-DUTY service members
items.who: Veterans, active-duty service members, post-9/11 Purple Heart recipients, Fry Scholarship recipients, and transfer-of-entitlement dependents receiving benefits at the 100% rate
items.value: School funding above the national tuition cap
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "The student must be a Veteran, active-duty Service member, individual awarded a Purple Heart on or after September 11, 2001, Fry Scholarship recipient, or a transfer-of-entitlement-eligible dependent receiving benefits at the 100% benefit rate."
items.hack: Active duty used to be shut out of Yellow Ribbon entirely. The handbook now lists active-duty service members among the eligible - so older guidance telling an active-duty student they cannot use Yellow Ribbon is out of date.
items.deadline: Apply through the school each academic year - school slots are limited

items.title: Yellow Ribbon math: VA matches the school, up to 50% of the difference
items.who: Students at participating Yellow Ribbon schools
items.value: School contribution plus a VA match against tuition above the national cap
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "The institution can contribute a specified dollar amount of those expenses and VA will match the contribution not to exceed 50% of the difference."
items.hack: Because VA matches rather than covers, the school's pledge is the real variable. Compare schools on their Yellow Ribbon dollar amount and the number of slots, not just on whether they participate.
items.deadline: School slots fill - apply early each year

items.title: Fry Scholarship: for children and surviving spouses of those who died after September 10, 2001
items.who: Children and surviving spouses of service members who died after September 10, 2001
items.value: Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits at the 100% level
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "The Fry Scholarship provides Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits to the children and surviving spouses of Service members who died after September 10, 2001."
items.hack: Fry pays at the 100% rate, which is why it usually beats Chapter 35 - but you generally have to choose between them, so run the comparison before electing.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Fry also covers deaths in the Selected Reserve and within 120 days of discharge
items.who: Survivors of members who died on duty other than active duty, from a service-connected disability while in the Selected Reserve, or from a service-connected disability within 120 days of discharge
items.value: Fry Scholarship eligibility beyond active-duty deaths
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: qualifying deaths include "While serving on duty other than active duty as a member of the Armed Forces," "From a service-connected disability while a member of the Selected Reserve," and "From a service-connected disability within 120 days of being discharged."
items.hack: The 120-day post-discharge window is the one families never hear about. A veteran who died shortly after separating from a service-connected condition can still generate Fry eligibility for the children.
items.deadline: Death within 120 days of discharge for that route

items.title: Fry children: age 33 cutoff for pre-2013 deaths, NO expiration for 2013 and later
items.who: Surviving children using the Fry Scholarship
items.value: Either a deadline at age 33 or no deadline at all, depending on the date of death
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "If the qualifying parent's death occurred before January 1, 2013, the child's eligibility ends on their 33rd birthday. If the qualifying parent's death occurred on or after January 1, 2013, the child's eligibility never expires."
items.hack: January 1, 2013 is the pivot. A child on the pre-2013 side has a hard 33rd-birthday wall and should plan backwards from it; a child on the post-2013 side can wait indefinitely.
items.deadline: 33rd birthday if the parent died before January 1, 2013

items.title: Fry surviving SPOUSES have no time limit
items.who: Surviving spouses eligible for the Fry Scholarship
items.value: Unlimited time to use the benefit
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "Surviving spouses who are eligible have no timeline on when they can use the benefit."
items.hack: The handbook states this flatly with no 15-year caveat. A spouse who set school aside for a decade to raise children has not lost anything.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Fry children can start school BEFORE turning 18
items.who: Surviving children eligible for the Fry Scholarship
items.value: The ability to begin an approved program of education before age 18
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "Surviving children who are eligible may begin an approved program of education before the age of 18."
items.hack: This is a real difference from Chapter 35, which generally makes a child wait. A dual-enrolled or early-college student can start on Fry.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Fry pays full tuition and fees straight to the school, for 36 months at the 100% level
items.who: Fry Scholarship recipients
items.value: Up to 36 months of benefits at the 100% level, with tuition and fees paid directly to the school
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "up to 36 months of benefits at the 100% level" and "The Fry Scholarship pays full tuition and fees directly to the school."
items.hack: Because Fry pays at 100%, it also opens Yellow Ribbon - the handbook lists Fry recipients among eligible Yellow Ribbon students.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Rogers STEM Scholarship: nine extra months, up to $30,000
items.who: Veterans and Fry Scholars in qualifying STEM programs who have exhausted or will exhaust their entitlement
items.value: Up to nine months of additional benefits, to a maximum of $30,000
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "provide up to nine months of additional benefits (to a maximum of $30,000)."
items.hack: This is extra entitlement beyond the 36 months - genuinely additional money, not a reshuffling. The $30,000 is the ceiling, so a high-tuition program hits the cap before the nine months run out.
items.deadline: Apply as entitlement nears exhaustion

items.title: Rogers STEM requires 60 semester or 90 quarter credit hours already completed
items.who: Rogers STEM Scholarship applicants
items.value: Eligibility for the extension
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: applicants "must have completed at least 60 semester credit hours (or 90 quarter credit hours) toward their degree already."
items.hack: You must be past the halfway mark before you can apply. Front-load your GI Bill months and you may hit 60 hours with entitlement still left, which is the ideal position for a STEM extension.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Three different ways to qualify for Rogers STEM
items.who: Veterans and Fry Scholars pursuing a STEM undergraduate degree, a covered clinical training program, or a teaching certification after a STEM degree
items.value: Rogers STEM eligibility by any of three routes
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "Seeking a qualifying undergraduate STEM degree alone or as part of a dual-degree program; or... Have earned a qualifying post-secondary degree or graduate degree and are enrolled in a covered clinical training program for health care professionals; or... Have earned a qualifying STEM degree and are seeking a teaching certification."
items.hack: The clinical-training and teaching-certification routes are widely missed. A nurse in a clinical program or a STEM graduate going for a teaching credential can both reach this money.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Rogers STEM is for people who have run out - or are about to
items.who: Veterans or Fry Scholars who have exhausted or will exhaust their Post-9/11 GI Bill entitlement
items.value: Eligibility for the STEM extension
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: "To be eligible, Veterans or Fry Scholars must have exhausted or will exhaust" their entitlement.
items.hack: "Will exhaust" means you apply before you are empty, not after. Waiting until the last month is how people lose a term.
items.deadline: Apply before entitlement runs out

items.title: The GI Bill call center: 888-GI-BILL-1 (888-442-4551)
items.who: Anyone with a GI Bill or education benefit question
items.value: Direct access to the Education Call Center
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: the Education and Training chapter lists 888-442-4551 (888-GI-BILL-1).
items.hack: Education claims are handled by regional processing offices, not your local VA - the call center is the only phone route that reaches them.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA's 2026 handbook prints almost no education dollar figures - and no entitlement tier table
items.who: Anyone trying to verify a GI Bill rate against the handbook
items.value: Knowing which figures the handbook does and does not support
items.how: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 6: the only education dollar figures printed are the $1,000 yearly books stipend, the $500 rural relocation payment and the $30,000 Rogers STEM maximum. The private/foreign tuition cap, the online-only MHA dollar rate and the entitlement percentage tier table (e.g. 90 days = 50%) are NOT printed.
items.hack: Quote the handbook for the rules and the GI Bill rate tables for the money. Attributing the private-school cap or the percentage tiers to the handbook is a citation error.
items.deadline: Education rates change each August 1 for the academic year

items.title: Filing a Supplemental Claim within 1 year preserves your effective date
items.who: Anyone who received a VA decision letter and intends to keep pursuing the claim
items.value: Protects retroactive pay back to the original claim date instead of restarting it
items.how: VA.gov, Decision reviews FAQs [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: This is the single most valuable date in the appeals system. Even if you are not ready to argue the case, filing the Supplemental Claim inside 12 months keeps the original effective date alive; filing at month 13 resets it to the new filing date.
items.deadline: 1 year from the date on the decision letter

items.title: The HLR informal conference - a one-time phone call with the reviewer
items.who: Anyone who files a Higher-Level Review and requests the conference on the form
items.value: A direct call with the higher-level reviewer handling your case, at no cost
items.how: VA.gov, Choosing a decision review option / Decision reviews FAQs [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Almost nobody checks this box. It is your one chance to tell a decision-maker out loud exactly which page of the file was misread. Request it on the 20-0996 itself - you generally get one.
items.deadline: Request it when you file the 20-0996

items.title: Board Appeal (VA Form 10182) - a Veterans Law Judge, three dockets
items.who: Claimants who want a Veterans Law Judge at the Board of Veterans' Appeals to decide the case
items.value: Review by a Veterans Law Judge; the fastest docket averages about 365 days
items.how: VA.gov, Choosing a decision review option [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Choosing the docket is the whole decision. Picking 'Hearing' when you have nothing new to say can add years; picking 'Direct Review' when you still need to submit a nexus letter locks the evidence out.
items.deadline: 1 year from the date on the decision letter

items.title: Board docket 1 - Direct Review: fastest, but the record is frozen
items.who: Board appellants who need no new evidence and no hearing
items.value: Averages roughly 365 days, the fastest of the three dockets
items.how: VA.gov, Choosing a decision review option [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: No new evidence and no hearing are allowed on this docket. Choose it only when you are certain the existing record already proves the claim and the error is purely legal.
items.deadline: Select the docket on the 10182 when you file

items.title: Board docket 2 - Evidence Submission: new evidence, no hearing
items.who: Board appellants who have new evidence but do not want to testify
items.value: Lets you add evidence to the Board record without waiting for a hearing slot
items.how: VA.gov, Choosing a decision review option [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: This is the middle path most people overlook: you get the new nexus letter into the record without taking on the multi-year hearing queue.
items.deadline: Select on the 10182; evidence must be submitted within the window stated on VA's instructions (commonly 90 days from filing)

items.title: Board docket 3 - Hearing: testify before the judge, longest wait
items.who: Board appellants who want to appear before a Veterans Law Judge, with or without new evidence
items.value: A hearing before the judge; the longest of the three docket timelines
items.how: VA.gov, Choosing a decision review option [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Worth it when credibility or lay testimony is the contested issue - a judge hearing you describe the symptom can carry weight a paper file cannot.
items.deadline: Select on the 10182 when you file

items.title: Which lanes accept new evidence - and which forbid it
items.who: Anyone choosing among the three decision review options
items.value: Avoids the most common fatal lane-selection mistake
items.how: VA.gov, Decision reviews FAQs [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: New evidence is ALLOWED in: Supplemental Claim, Board Evidence Submission docket, Board Hearing docket. New evidence is NOT allowed in: Higher-Level Review, Board Direct Review docket. Match your lane to what you are holding.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Miss the one-year window and the Supplemental Claim is your ONLY option
items.who: Claimants more than one year past their decision letter
items.value: Keeps a path open indefinitely after HLR and Board appeal rights lapse
items.how: VA.gov, Decision reviews FAQs [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA states plainly that once the year runs, the Supplemental Claim is all that is left. You lose the effective date, not the claim - so file anyway, then argue the effective date separately.
items.deadline: After 1 year from the decision letter, HLR and Board appeal are no longer available

items.title: Some VA benefits have a SHORTER review deadline than one year
items.who: Claimants in non-compensation programs (the decision letter states the shorter period)
items.value: Prevents assuming a 12-month clock that does not apply
items.how: VA.gov, Decision reviews FAQs [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA says the one-year rule is the general case and that some benefits carry shorter timeframes specified in the decision letter itself. Read the letter's deadline line rather than assuming 365 days.
items.deadline: As stated on your decision letter

items.title: VA's 125-day goal for Supplemental Claims and Higher-Level Reviews
items.who: Anyone deciding whether to use a VBA-level lane or go straight to the Board
items.value: A published expectation you can measure VA against
items.how: VA.gov, Choosing a decision review option [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Both VBA lanes target roughly 125 days versus about 365 days for the fastest Board docket. If the legal error is simple, the VBA lanes are usually a year faster.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Duty-to-assist errors can be corrected without starting over
items.who: Claimants whose decision rests on a record VA failed to develop properly
items.value: VA can fix its own development failure rather than denying on an incomplete record
items.how: VA.gov, Decision reviews FAQs (reviewers may identify errors) [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: If VA never ordered the exam, never requested the service treatment records, or never got the private records it promised to get, that is a VA error - raise it explicitly in the HLR or Supplemental Claim narrative.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Fiduciary decisions have their own decision review path
items.who: Beneficiaries and fiduciaries contesting a VA fiduciary determination
items.value: A review route for fiduciary matters distinct from ordinary benefit claims
items.how: VA.gov, Decision reviews - fiduciary claims [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Fiduciary appointments, removals and misuse determinations are reviewable - most people do not realise these are appealable decisions at all.
items.deadline: As stated on the fiduciary decision notice

items.title: Online filing is available for all three decision review lanes
items.who: Claimants with disability compensation decisions
items.value: Faster filing and a timestamped receipt
items.how: VA.gov, Choosing a decision review option [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Filing online produces a dated confirmation - critical proof when the whole case turns on whether you filed inside the one-year effective-date window.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Burial allowance for a SERVICE-CONNECTED death: $2,000
items.who: Whoever paid the burial/funeral costs when the Veteran's death was service-connected
items.value: $2,000 if the Veteran died on or after September 11, 2001
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance (page updated 1 Oct 2026) [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: This figure is NOT indexed annually like the non-service-connected allowance - it has sat at $2,000 since 2001. It is also the one with no filing deadline at all.
items.deadline: No time limit for a service-connected death

items.title: Service-connected burial allowance is $1,500 for deaths BEFORE 11 Sep 2001
items.who: Survivors filing on an older service-connected death
items.value: $1,500 where death occurred before September 11, 2001
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance (page updated 1 Oct 2026) [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Because there is no deadline on service-connected burial claims, a 1990s death can still be claimed today - at the $1,500 rate in force by date of death.
items.deadline: No time limit for a service-connected death

items.title: Non-service-connected burial allowance: $1,032 effective 1 October 2026
items.who: Whoever paid burial costs for a Veteran whose death was not service-connected but who meets one of VA's qualifying circumstances
items.value: $1,032 for deaths on or after October 1, 2026 (was $1,002 for deaths on or after 1 Oct 2025)
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance (page updated 1 Oct 2026) [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The rate is set by DATE OF DEATH, not date of filing. A death on 30 September 2026 pays $1,002; a death on 1 October 2026 pays $1,032.
items.deadline: Generally 2 years after the Veteran's burial

items.title: Plot or interment allowance: $1,032 effective 1 October 2026
items.who: Whoever paid for the burial plot or interment when the Veteran is not buried in a national cemetery
items.value: $1,032 for deaths on or after October 1, 2026 (was $1,002 for deaths on or after 1 Oct 2025)
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance (page updated 1 Oct 2026) [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The plot allowance is a SEPARATE payment stacked on top of the burial allowance - $2,064 combined at the current rate - and unlike the burial allowance it carries NO filing deadline.
items.deadline: No time limit for the plot or interment allowance

items.title: The burial allowance rate table runs back to 2013 - look up YOUR date of death
items.who: Survivors filing on a death from any prior year
items.value: Published rates by date-of-death band, e.g. $978/$978 (FY2025), $948/$948 (FY2024), $893 (from 5 Jan 2023)
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance (page updated 1 Oct 2026) [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Note the 5 January 2023 break: before it the non-service-connected burial allowance was stuck at $300 while the plot allowance was already $893. Deaths just either side of that date pay very differently.
items.deadline: Deadline depends on which allowance you claim

items.title: VA Form 21P-530EZ - the application for burial benefits
items.who: Survivors, estate representatives, friends, funeral homes, cemeteries or organizations that paid the costs
items.value: Claims the burial allowance, plot/interment allowance and transportation reimbursement on one form
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: One form covers all three allowances - but you must claim each one. People routinely leave the plot allowance unclaimed because they did not tick it.
items.deadline: Generally 2 years after burial for the non-service-connected burial allowance

items.title: The exceptions that erase the 2-year burial filing deadline
items.who: Survivors who are past the two-year mark
items.value: Four situations VA states carry NO time limit at all
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: No deadline applies if: (1) the death was service-connected; (2) the death occurred while in VA care or a VA-contracted facility; (3) you are claiming the plot/interment allowance; (4) you are claiming transportation reimbursement. State or tribal organizations claiming the state plot allowance also have no limit.
items.deadline: No time limit in these four situations

items.title: Discharge upgraded AFTER death? A fresh 2-year clock starts
items.who: Survivors of a Veteran whose dishonorable discharge was corrected after death
items.value: Restores burial benefit eligibility with a new filing window
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA states that where it changed the discharge from dishonorable after death, you file within 2 years AFTER the change - not after the burial. A posthumous discharge upgrade therefore reopens burial benefits decades later.
items.deadline: 2 years after the discharge change

items.title: VA pays some surviving spouses automatically - no application at all
items.who: Surviving spouses already recorded on the Veteran's VA profile
items.value: A set amount paid automatically for plot, interment or transportation on notice of death
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: If you are the spouse of record, VA says it pays automatically once it learns of the death. Check whether the automatic payment arrived BEFORE filing - but if nothing came within a few months, file the 21P-530EZ anyway.
items.deadline: No application required for the automatic payment

items.title: The six circumstances that qualify a non-service-connected death
items.who: Survivors of a Veteran who died of a non-service-connected cause
items.value: Eligibility for the burial and plot allowances
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Any ONE of these qualifies: death from a service-connected disability; death while in VA or VA-contracted care; death while travelling at VA expense to authorized care; an original or reopened claim pending at death with entitlement established; actively receiving VA pension or compensation at death; or the Veteran had elected military retired pay instead of compensation.
items.deadline: Generally 2 years after burial

items.title: Transportation of remains reimbursement - keep the itemized receipt
items.who: Survivors where the Veteran died in VA care or while travelling to VA-authorized care
items.value: Reimbursement of the cost of transporting the remains for burial in a national cemetery
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA requires an ITEMIZED transportation receipt - a funeral home's lump-sum invoice often gets this denied. Ask the funeral director to break out the transport line separately. There is no filing deadline on this one.
items.deadline: No time limit for transportation reimbursement

items.title: Funeral homes, estates and even friends can claim the burial allowance
items.who: Surviving spouse or partner, children, parents, estate executor, an unrelated friend, or a funeral home, cemetery or organization that paid
items.value: The allowance goes to whoever actually bore the unreimbursed cost
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans burial allowance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: You do NOT have to be next of kin. A neighbour who paid for a Veteran's funeral out of pocket can claim - the test is who paid and was not reimbursed from another source.
items.deadline: Generally 2 years after burial

items.title: Burial in a VA national cemetery - what is included at no cost
items.who: Veterans discharged under other than dishonorable conditions, and service members who died on active duty, ACDUTRA or INACDUTRA
items.value: Gravesite, opening and closing of the grave, a grave liner, a headstone or marker, a burial flag, a Presidential Memorial Certificate, and perpetual care - no charge to the family
items.how: VA Welcome Kit burial benefits quick start guide; NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Inside a national cemetery the headstone and the Presidential Memorial Certificate require NO application - the cemetery orders them. The application burden only exists for private-cemetery burials.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: 155 national cemeteries - space availability decides where
items.who: Any eligible Veteran or eligible family member
items.value: A gravesite in any national cemetery with available space
items.how: VA Welcome Kit burial benefits quick start guide [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: You are entitled to a national cemetery burial, not to a specific cemetery. Popular cemeteries close to new casket interments while still accepting cremated remains - ask about both when you call.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Spouses and minor children may be buried in a national cemetery - even if they die FIRST
items.who: Spouse, surviving spouse, and minor dependent children of an eligible Veteran; some unmarried adult children with disabilities
items.value: Full national cemetery interment at no cost to the family
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits; VA Welcome Kit burial benefits guide [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA states eligible spouses and children may be buried even if they PREDECEASE the Veteran. Families wrongly assume the Veteran must go first and buy a private plot unnecessarily.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Unmarried adult dependent children with disabilities are eligible too
items.who: Unmarried adult children of an eligible Veteran who are dependent due to disability
items.value: National cemetery interment alongside the Veteran
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits; VA Welcome Kit burial benefits guide [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: This category is routinely missed. An adult child who never married and is dependent because of a disability is eligible - get a pre-need determination on file to settle it in advance.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: One gravesite per family - and the two-Veteran couple exception
items.who: Veterans and their eligible family members
items.value: VA typically provides one shared gravesite and one headstone for the family
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans headstones and markers [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA normally gives the family ONE gravesite and ONE headstone, inscribed on both sides. But two married Veterans may request separate side-by-side gravesites - each then gets their own headstone and their own full honors.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: National Cemetery Scheduling Office - fax first, then call
items.who: Families arranging a burial in a VA national cemetery
items.value: Burial scheduling, 7 days a week
items.how: VA Welcome Kit burial benefits guide; NCA FAQ [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The sequence matters: FAX the discharge documents to 866-900-6417 (or email NCA.Scheduling@va.gov), THEN call 800-535-1117. Calling first without the paperwork in their hands just adds a round trip. Open daily, 8:00 a.m.-7:30 p.m. ET.
items.deadline: Arrange at time of need

items.title: Arlington National Cemetery is Army-run with stricter rules
items.who: Those seeking burial at Arlington National Cemetery or the U.S. Soldiers' and Airmen's Home National Cemetery
items.value: Separate eligibility criteria set by the Department of the Army, not VA/NCA
items.how: NCA FAQ [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA's NCA runs most national cemeteries, but Arlington and the Soldiers' and Airmen's Home are Army. NCA eligibility does NOT transfer - contact the Army directly before assuming Arlington is available.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: VA does NOT provide burial at sea - the Navy does
items.who: Veterans and families wanting committal of remains at sea
items.value: Burial at sea performed by the U.S. Navy at no cost to the family
items.how: NCA FAQ [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: NCA states flatly that VA does not provide burial at sea. Call Navy Mortuary Affairs at 1-833-330-6622. Note you can still get a MEMORIAL headstone from VA for a Veteran buried at sea.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Green burial is available at three VA pilot cemeteries
items.who: Eligible Veterans and family members choosing a chemical-free interment
items.value: Natural burial with no embalming chemicals, in a natural manner or a fully biodegradable receptacle
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Almost nobody knows this exists. The three pilot sites are the National Memorial Cemetery of Arizona (Phoenix), Pikes Peak National Cemetery (Colorado Springs) and Florida National Cemetery (Bushnell). Same interment process as a standard burial.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: VA Form 40-10088 - casket or urn reimbursement for unclaimed Veteran remains
items.who: The person or organization that paid to bury a Veteran whose remains went unclaimed, and indigent Veterans' burials
items.value: Reimbursement for the casket or urn, on top of the burial and plot allowances
items.how: VBA, Indigent Veterans and Unclaimed Remains [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: This form is almost invisible in the public guides. For a national cemetery burial VA may reimburse casket/urn PLUS transportation to the nearest national cemetery PLUS the burial allowance. Annotate the application 'unclaimed remains' to state your relationship.
items.deadline: Deadline follows the burial allowance rules

items.title: Every VA regional office has an Unclaimed Remains Outreach Coordinator
items.who: Funeral homes, coroners, medical examiners and county officials holding unclaimed Veteran remains
items.value: A named VA point of contact to establish Veteran status and arrange interment with honors
items.how: VBA, Indigent Veterans and Unclaimed Remains [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Coroners and funeral directors sitting on unidentified cremated remains can call the Benefits Hotline at 1-800-827-1000 and ask for the Indigent Veterans and Unclaimed Remains Outreach Coordinator - a dedicated role most callers never hear about.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: What VA pays for an indigent Veteran differs by cemetery type
items.who: Those arranging burial for a Veteran with insufficient estate resources
items.value: National cemetery: casket/urn + transportation + burial allowance. State/tribal VA-funded cemetery: casket/urn + burial allowance + plot allowance. Private cemetery: burial allowance + plot allowance (plus a government headstone if eligible)
items.how: VBA, Indigent Veterans and Unclaimed Remains [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Routing an indigent Veteran to a national cemetery unlocks transportation reimbursement that a private burial does not - the choice of cemetery changes what VA will pay.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: State and tribal Veterans cemeteries have their own eligibility rules
items.who: Veterans and families considering a VA-grant-funded state, tribal or territory Veterans cemetery
items.value: Interment at a state or tribal cemetery, often with a state plot allowance paid to the cemetery
items.how: VA Welcome Kit burial benefits quick start guide [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Requirements differ from national cemeteries - many impose a state residency rule. Contact the specific cemetery, not NCA. The upside: a state cemetery is often far closer to family than the nearest national cemetery.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Bereavement counseling through Vet Centers - free, for survivors
items.who: Surviving spouses, children and parents of service members who died on active duty; survivors of Reservists/Guard on active duty; families of Veterans who were receiving Vet Center services at death; and families of Veterans or service members who died by suicide
items.value: Free outreach, counseling and referral through Vet Centers
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: No enrollment in VA health care is needed and it is not limited to the spouse - parents and children qualify too. Walk into any Vet Center.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Government headstone or marker (VA Form 40-1330) - free, including for private graves
items.who: Eligible Veterans and deceased active-duty service members not discharged dishonorably
items.value: A granite, marble or bronze headstone or marker at no charge to the applicant
items.how: NCA Headstones, Markers and Medallions; VA.gov headstones and markers [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Free for the stone itself - but in a PRIVATE cemetery you arrange and pay for setting it. Get the cemetery's installation quote before ordering, because that cost is yours.
items.deadline: No deadline

items.title: The two date rules for a government headstone in a private cemetery
items.who: Veterans buried in private cemeteries
items.value: Determines whether a government stone can be furnished at all
items.how: NCA Headstones, Markers and Medallions; VA.gov headstones and markers [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: If the grave is UNMARKED, any date of death qualifies. If the grave already has a PRIVATELY PURCHASED marker, the Veteran must have died on or after 1 November 1990. That single date decides many claims.
items.deadline: No filing deadline, but the 1 Nov 1990 date-of-death rule is absolute for privately marked graves

items.title: Bronze medallion (VA Form 40-1330M) for a privately purchased headstone
items.who: Veterans who served on or after April 6, 1917 and have a privately purchased headstone or marker
items.value: A bronze medallion affixed to the existing private stone, at no charge
items.how: NCA Headstones, Markers and Medallions; NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The medallion solves the problem families hit when they already bought a beautiful headstone and do not want a government slab beside it - and it dodges the 1 Nov 1990 restriction.
items.deadline: No deadline

items.title: Medallion sizes - three Veteran sizes and two Medal of Honor sizes
items.who: Families ordering a medallion for a privately purchased headstone
items.value: Veteran medallion in three sizes; Medal of Honor medallion in two sizes
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Measure the available flat face on the existing stone before ordering - picking the wrong size means a second application. Medal of Honor recipients have their own distinct medallion.
items.deadline: No deadline

items.title: Headstone OR medallion - the choice cannot be undone
items.who: Families of Veterans buried in private cemeteries
items.value: One memorial item per Veteran
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA provides either a traditional headstone/marker or a medallion, NOT both. Decide before applying, because the law provides no way to swap later.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Memorial headstones for Veterans whose remains were never recovered
items.who: Families of Veterans whose remains were not recovered or identified, were buried at sea, were donated to science, or were cremated and scattered
items.value: A memorial headstone or marker placed in a cemetery, at no charge
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans headstones and markers; NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: This is how a family gets a physical place to visit when there is no grave - MIA cases, scattered ashes, burial at sea, or remains donated to a medical school all qualify.
items.deadline: No deadline

items.title: Headstone and marker types - upright, flat, and niche markers for columbaria
items.who: Families ordering a government memorial item
items.value: Upright headstones in granite or marble; flat markers in granite, marble or bronze; bronze niche markers for columbaria
items.how: NCA Headstones, Markers and Medallions [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: You do not get a free choice - the cemetery's own officials decide which styles are permitted at that location. Ask the cemetery what it allows BEFORE filling in the form.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: A spouse or child in a PRIVATE cemetery can still get an inscription
items.who: Spouses and dependent children buried in private cemeteries
items.value: An inscription added to the Veteran's privately purchased marker, though not a separate government stone
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans headstones and markers [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Spouses and dependents cannot get their own government headstone in a private cemetery - but VA will add their inscription to the Veteran's stone. Most families never ask.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Emblems of belief and optional inscription items
items.who: Anyone applying for a government headstone or marker
items.value: A choice from VA's list of accepted emblems of belief, plus optional inscription text
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans headstones and markers; NCA Headstones, Markers and Medallions [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA maintains a formal list of accepted emblems of belief, including non-religious options. If the emblem you want is not on the list there is a process to request a new one - but it takes time, so start early.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Replacement headstone for damage or an engraving error - block 27
