items.who: Families with a damaged government headstone or one engraved incorrectly
items.value: A replacement stone at no charge
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans headstones and markers [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The mechanism is a second VA Form 40-1330 with the reason explained in BLOCK 27. Without that explanation the application reads as a duplicate and gets rejected.
items.deadline: No deadline

items.title: Submit memorial applications by QuickSubmit, mail or fax
items.who: Applicants for headstones, markers, medallions and urns/plaques
items.value: Free submission by the AccessVA QuickSubmit tool, mail or fax
items.how: VA.gov, Veterans headstones and markers; VA Welcome Kit burial benefits guide [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Mail goes to NCA FP Evidence Intake Center, PO Box 5237, Janesville, WI 53547. The Memorial Products Service address (41B, 5109 Russell Road, Quantico, VA 22134-3903) and fax 800-455-7143 also appear in VA's guides - use the address printed on the form version you have. Phone 800-697-6947 (TTY 711), Mon-Fri 8-5 ET. Send a COPY of the DD214; originals are not returned.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: United States burial flag (VA Form 27-2008)
items.who: Next of kin or a close friend of an honorably discharged Veteran or service member
items.value: One flag at no cost, to drape the casket or accompany the urn - the family keeps it
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits; VA Welcome Kit burial benefits guide [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: You can get the flag at a U.S. POST OFFICE as well as a VA regional office or through the funeral director - the post office route is the one nobody mentions. One flag per Veteran, and it is not replaced if lost.
items.deadline: Request at time of need

items.title: Spouses and dependents get NO burial flag and NO Presidential Memorial Certificate
items.who: Families planning a spouse's or dependent's interment
items.value: Clarifies what does and does not come with a family member's burial
items.how: VA Welcome Kit burial benefits quick start guide [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VA states it plainly: spouses and dependents are not eligible for a PMC or a burial flag, and get no headstone/marker/medallion if buried in a private cemetery. Plan and budget for that gap.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Presidential Memorial Certificate (VA Form 40-0247) - request more than one
items.who: Next of kin, other family members and close friends of a Veteran or Reservist eligible for national cemetery burial
items.value: A gold-embossed certificate bearing the current President's signature, at no cost
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits; VA Welcome Kit burial benefits guide [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: MULTIPLE certificates may be requested - so every child and grandchild can have one rather than the family fighting over a single copy. Close friends, not just relatives, may request. PMC questions: 202-632-7300, Mon-Fri 8-4 ET.
items.deadline: No deadline

items.title: In a national cemetery, the headstone and PMC arrive with NO application
items.who: Families burying a Veteran in a VA national cemetery
items.value: Headstone or marker and Presidential Memorial Certificate furnished automatically
items.how: VA Welcome Kit burial benefits quick start guide [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The quick start guide states both come with 'no application needed' for a national cemetery interment. Families waste weeks filing 40-1330 and 40-0247 that were never required.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Commemorative urns and plaques (VA Form 40-1330UP) - an irreversible trade
items.who: Families holding the cremated remains of a Veteran who served on or after April 6, 1917 and will NOT be interred
items.value: A commemorative urn or plaque furnished by VA at no cost
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Read the warning before applying: VA states the decision CANNOT be undone and 'the law does not provide a method to restore these benefits.' Accepting the urn or plaque forfeits national cemetery interment and the headstone/marker benefit for that Veteran.
items.deadline: No deadline, but the choice is permanent

items.title: Veterans Legacy Memorial - a free online memorial for 10+ million Veterans
items.who: Anyone; covers Veterans and service members in VA national cemeteries, state/tribal/territory Veterans cemeteries, DoD cemeteries, and private cemeteries since 1996
items.value: A permanent free digital memorial page where family can post tributes, photos and history
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Over 10 million pages already exist - your relative probably has one you have never seen. Search the name and claim the page to add photos and tributes at no cost.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: 'Your Story, Your Legacy' - write your own memorial while you are alive
items.who: Living Veterans who have been APPROVED for pre-need burial eligibility
items.value: Private upload of images, an autobiography, a military timeline and documents, published publicly after death
items.how: NCA burial and memorial benefits [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: This is the hidden payoff of the pre-need determination: once approved, you can write your own Veterans Legacy Memorial page yourself - in your own words - instead of leaving it to whoever survives you. Get the 40-10007 approved first.
items.deadline: Apply after pre-need approval; no deadline

items.title: Military funeral honors - the two-person legal minimum
items.who: Every eligible Veteran, upon the family's request
items.value: An honor guard of at least two members of the armed forces, one from the Veteran's own branch; the playing of Taps; and the folding and presentation of the flag to next of kin
items.how: NCA Military Funeral Honors [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Two people is the floor set by law, not the ceiling. A rifle detail, pallbearers and escort are NOT in the statutory minimum - those come from Veterans Service Organizations and Authorized Provider Partnership Programs, so ask a VSO directly if you want full honors.
items.deadline: Request 48 to 72 hours before the service

items.title: How to actually request military funeral honors - and when
items.who: Families of eligible Veterans
items.value: Honors arranged through the Veteran's service branch at no cost
items.how: NCA Military Funeral Honors [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The funeral director or a personal representative requests honors on the family's behalf, direct to the service branch - VA does not arrange them. VA advises contacting the branch at least 48 to 72 HOURS before the service. NCA staff can help at their own cemeteries. Program questions: Military OneSource, 800-342-9647.
items.deadline: 48 to 72 hours before the scheduled service

items.title: Military funeral honors are a statutory right under Public Law 106-65
items.who: Every eligible Veteran whose family requests honors
items.value: Honors upon request, as mandated by law since the program began 1 January 2000
items.how: NCA Military Funeral Honors [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: If a service branch tells a family honors are unavailable, the entitlement is statutory - escalate rather than accept the refusal, and in parallel ask a VSO honor guard to cover the detail.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: VSOs and Authorized Provider Partnership Programs fill the honors gap
items.who: Families who want more than the two-person statutory minimum
items.value: Rifle details, pallbearers, escorts and additional ceremonial support, generally at no cost
items.how: NCA Military Funeral Honors [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The American Legion, VFW, AMVETS and local honor guards do this work routinely. Call the local post directly - this is the practical route to a rifle volley and a full flag detail.
items.deadline: Arrange alongside the branch honors request

items.title: Commissary, exchange and MWR privileges for Veterans with a service-connected rating
items.who: Honorably discharged Veterans with ANY service-connected disability rating, military retirees, former prisoners of war, and Purple Heart and Medal of Honor recipients
items.value: Full in-person commissary, exchange and MWR retail privileges
items.how: VA.gov, Commissary and exchange privileges for Veterans [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: A 0% or 10% service-connected rating is enough - there is no minimum rating. And there is NO application: you just present the right ID at checkout.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: PCAFC primary family caregivers get commissary and exchange privileges
items.who: Primary family caregivers formally recognized under the Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers
items.value: Commissary, exchange and MWR privileges in their own right
items.how: VA.gov, Commissary and exchange privileges for Veterans [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The caregiver's privilege is independent - they can shop without the Veteran present. One of the most concrete and least-publicized PCAFC perks.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Unmarried surviving spouses and dependents keep commissary and exchange access
items.who: Unmarried surviving spouses, dependents and survivors of eligible service members, and dependents of eligible Reserve members
items.value: Continued commissary, exchange and MWR privileges
items.how: VA.gov, Commissary and exchange privileges for Veterans [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The privilege survives the Veteran but is lost on remarriage - worth knowing before a later marriage, since it is not restored.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: The ID that gets you through the gate: VHIC, or a VA letter plus photo ID
items.who: Veterans using commissary, exchange and MWR privileges
items.value: Base and store access with no application process
items.how: VA.gov, Commissary and exchange privileges for Veterans [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Either a Veteran Health Identification Card (VHIC) OR a letter from VA together with your passport or driver's license. If you have a service-connected rating but no VHIC, request the VA letter rather than assuming you are shut out.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: Overseas commissary privileges vary country by country
items.who: Veterans with commissary privileges travelling or living abroad
items.value: Access that depends on the host nation's agreement
items.how: VA.gov, Commissary and exchange privileges for Veterans [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Status-of-forces agreements, not VA, control this. Confirm with the specific overseas installation before relying on commissary access abroad.
items.deadline: n/a

items.title: VALife - guaranteed life insurance for service-connected Veterans up to age 80
items.who: Veterans aged 80 and under with any service-connected disability rating
items.value: Up to $40,000 of whole life coverage in $10,000 increments, with no medical underwriting
items.how: VBA Life Insurance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: There is no health question and no rating minimum, which makes it the backstop for Veterans who cannot buy commercial cover. But coverage takes effect TWO YEARS after enrollment and you must pay premiums throughout that wait - so enroll early, not when you are ill.
items.deadline: Apply before age 81; two-year waiting period before coverage takes effect

items.title: VGLI (SGLV 8714) - converting SGLI after you separate
items.who: Veterans who had full-time SGLI coverage on separation
items.value: Renewable term life insurance converted from SGLI
items.how: VBA Life Insurance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: The conversion window is short and there is a health-question-free period early on - apply as soon as you separate. Waiting means answering medical questions you may not pass.
items.deadline: Apply promptly after separation (SGLV 8714)

items.title: VMLI (VA Form 29-8636) - mortgage life insurance tied to the SAH grant
items.who: Severely disabled Veterans who received a Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant, hold title to the home, and have a mortgage on it
items.value: Mortgage life insurance that pays off the adapted home's mortgage on death
items.how: VBA Life Insurance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: VMLI is bolted to the SAH grant - if you got an SAH grant and still carry a mortgage, you are likely eligible and probably were never told. It protects the family from losing the adapted house.
items.deadline: Apply while you hold the mortgage

items.title: TSGLI (SGLV 8600) - traumatic injury protection, automatic with SGLI
items.who: All service members covered by SGLI
items.value: A lump-sum payment for qualifying traumatic injuries
items.how: VBA Life Insurance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: TSGLI is a TRAUMA benefit, not a death benefit, and it is retroactive for some injury periods - Veterans who lost a limb or suffered severe burns years ago sometimes still have an unfiled claim. File SGLV 8600.
items.deadline: File SGLV 8600 after a qualifying traumatic injury

items.title: FSGLI (SGLV 8286A) - spouse and child coverage, children free
items.who: Spouses and children of SGLI-covered service members
items.value: Spouse coverage up to the service member's own amount; dependent children covered at no charge
items.how: VBA Life Insurance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Children are covered automatically at NO cost - families paying for separate child life policies are duplicating a free benefit. Spouse coverage cannot exceed the member's own SGLI amount.
items.deadline: Enroll via SOES or SGLV 8286A

items.title: SGLI enrollment runs through SOES on milConnect
items.who: Active duty, Ready Reserve, National Guard, service academy cadets and midshipmen, ROTC members, NOAA Commissioned Corps and Public Health Service
items.value: Automatic maximum SGLI coverage, adjustable online
items.how: VBA Life Insurance [Source is VA.gov primary page, NOT the handbook: 2026 handbook Ch.12-15 body text was unreachable - see notes]
items.hack: Coverage is automatic, but beneficiary designations are NOT - stale beneficiary data is the single most common SGLI failure. Check SOES at milconnect.dmdc.osd.mil after every marriage, divorce or birth. Members without SOES access use form SGLV 8286.
items.deadline: Review at every life event

items.title: Basic eligibility for VA health care now names space service explicitly
items.who: Anyone who served in the active military, naval, space or air service, discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable, including qualifying Reserve and National Guard members
items.value: Eligibility for VA health benefits
items.how: The handbook's basic-eligibility sentence reads: 'A person who served in the active military, naval, space or air service, and who was discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable' may qualify, including 'qualifying Reserve and National Guard members.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Space Force service is covered by the same sentence as every other branch — do not let a clerk tell you otherwise. 'Other than dishonorable' is a far wider door than 'honorable': OTH and general discharges are not automatically out.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The 24-month minimum duty requirement and the five ways around it
items.who: Veterans who enlisted after September 7, 1980, or entered active duty after October 16, 1981
items.value: Must serve 24 continuous months or the full period called to active duty — waivable
items.how: The handbook requires '24 continuous months or the full period for which they were called to active duty,' and says this 'may be waived' for those 'discharged for hardship, early out or a disability incurred or aggravated in the line of duty, or those accessing care under certain special treatment authorities, such as treatment related to military sexual trauma (MST).' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: If you were separated short of 24 months, find your separation code. Hardship, early-out and line-of-duty-disability discharges all waive the rule, and MST care bypasses the minimum-duty test entirely under a special treatment authority.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Ten-year extended health care eligibility for theater-of-operations service after 2001
items.who: Veterans who served in a theater of operations after November 11, 2001
items.value: Cost-free health care and nursing home care for conditions possibly related to service, for 10 years after discharge
items.how: The handbook states these Veterans 'are eligible for an extended period of eligibility for health care for ten years after their discharge,' including 'cost-free health care services and nursing home care for conditions possibly related to military service.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: This is 10 years, not 5 — the old post-9/11 window was 5 years and many veterans still believe that. The clock runs from discharge, so enroll inside the window even if you feel fine; enrollment placement sticks after it closes.
items.deadline: 10 years from date of discharge

items.title: Four groups urged but not required to enroll in VA health care
items.who: Veterans rated 50%+; those with line-of-duty conditions not yet rated; those seeking service-connected-only or special-authority care; those seeking registry exams
items.value: Enrollment not required to receive care
items.how: The handbook lists Veterans 'urged to do so' but not required to enroll: those with 'service-connected disability rated at 50% or more'; those seeking care for disabilities 'the military determined was incurred or aggravated in the line of duty, but which VA has not yet rated, within 12 months of discharge'; those seeking care for service-connected disabilities only or under special treatment authorities like MST; and those seeking 'registry examinations.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Not required still means you should enroll — enrollment is what gets you the medication benefit, community care and urgent care. Use the exemption to get seen now, then file the 10-10EZ.
items.deadline: Line-of-duty-but-unrated route: within 12 months of discharge

items.title: Priority Group 1 — 50% or more, unemployable, and Medal of Honor
items.who: Veterans with service-connected disabilities rated 50% or more; those VA determines unemployable due to service-connected conditions; Medal of Honor recipients
items.value: Highest enrollment priority
items.how: Group 1 is 'Veterans with service-connected disabilities rated 50% or more'; those 'determined by VA to be unemployable due to service-connected conditions'; and 'Medal of Honor' recipients. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: TDIU lands you in Group 1 even if your combined rating is below 50% — the handbook's test is unemployability, not percentage.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Priority Group 2 is exactly 30% and 40% — nothing else
items.who: Veterans with service-connected disabilities rated 30 or 40%
items.value: Second enrollment priority
items.how: Group 2 is 'Veterans with service-connected disabilities rated 30 or 40%.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Group 2 is the narrowest group in the system — two percentages only. If you are at 20% you are Group 3, not Group 2.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Priority Group 3 — where 10% and 20% veterans actually land, plus POWs and Purple Hearts
items.who: Former POWs; Purple Heart recipients; veterans discharged for a line-of-duty disability; veterans rated 10 or 20%; those whose compensation is suspended for military retired pay; 10%-rate multiple non-compensable awards; 38 U.S.C. 1151 awardees
items.value: Third enrollment priority
items.how: Group 3 is: former prisoners of war; 'Purple Heart medal' recipients; those discharged 'for a disability incurred or aggravated in the line of duty'; veterans with 'service-connected disabilities rated by VA at 10 or 20%'; those whose 'disability compensation is suspended because of the receipt of military retired pay'; veterans receiving 'compensation at the 10% rate based on multiple non-compensable service-connected disabilities that clearly interfere with normal employability'; and those 'awarded special eligibility classification under 38 U.S.C. 1151.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Waiving VA compensation to take military retired pay does not drop you out of Group 3 — the handbook keeps suspended-compensation veterans in. Say 'my compensation is suspended for retired pay' at enrollment.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Priority Group 4 — aid and attendance, housebound, and catastrophically disabled
items.who: Veterans receiving increased compensation or pension for regular aid and attendance or permanent housebound status; veterans VA determines to be catastrophically disabled
items.value: Fourth enrollment priority
items.how: Group 4 is Veterans receiving 'increased compensation or pension based on their need for regular aid and attendance or by reason of being permanently housebound' and those 'determined by VA to be catastrophically disabled.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Catastrophically disabled is a clinical determination made by a VA provider, not a rating decision — ask your VA physician to evaluate you for it. It moves you to Group 4 without any change to your percentage.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Priority Group 5 — 0% non-compensable, pension recipients, and Medicaid eligibility
items.who: Non-service-connected and non-compensable 0% veterans with income below the geographically adjusted limit; VA Pension recipients; veterans eligible for Medicaid
items.value: Fifth enrollment priority
items.how: Group 5 is 'Nonservice-connected Veterans and non-compensable service-connected Veterans rated by VA as 0% disabled' with 'annual income below the VA's geographically adjusted income limit'; those 'receiving VA Pension benefits'; and those 'eligible for Medicaid benefits.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Medicaid eligibility alone puts you in Group 5 regardless of the income arithmetic — if you are on Medicaid, say so on the 10-10EZ and skip the means-test argument.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Priority Group 6 — compensable 0%, toxic exposure, and the ten-year post-discharge slot
items.who: Compensable 0% veterans; atmospheric-testing and Hiroshima/Nagasaki radiation-exposed; Project 112/SHAD participants; WWII veterans; Vietnam service Jan 9 1962-May 7 1975; toxic-exposed veterans; Southwest Asia Aug 2 1990-Nov 11 1998; those discharged on or after September 11, 2001
items.value: Sixth enrollment priority — includes the ten-year post-discharge enrollment slot
items.how: Group 6 covers 'Compensable 0% service-connected Veterans'; those exposed to 'ionizing radiation during atmospheric testing or during the occupation of Hiroshima and Nagasaki'; 'Project 112/SHAD participants'; 'World War II Veterans'; those who 'served in the Republic of Vietnam between January 9, 1962, and May 7, 1975'; toxic exposed Veterans in specific locations; those in 'Southwest Asia theater of operations from August 2, 1990, through November 11, 1998'; and Veterans 'discharged from active duty on or after September 11, 2001, for ten years post-discharge.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: A compensable 0% rating — 0% that still pays, usually under a special monthly award — is Group 6, a full priority band above a non-compensable 0%, which is Group 5. The distinction is worth asking your enrollment clerk to check.
items.deadline: Post-9/11 slot: 10 years post-discharge

items.title: Camp Lejeune service of 30 days between 1953 and 1987 places you in Priority Group 6
items.who: Veterans who served at Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, NC for at least 30 days between August 1, 1953, and December 31, 1987
items.value: Priority Group 6 placement and enhanced benefits for ten years post discharge
items.how: The handbook groups with Post-9/11 Veterans those who 'served at Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, NC, for at least 30 days between August 1, 1953, and December 31, 1987,' receiving 'enhanced benefits for ten years post discharge.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The 30 days do not have to be consecutive in practice, and MCAS New River counts as Camp Lejeune. Bring any orders, pay record or dependent record that puts you there.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Priority Group 7 — below the geographic income limit, copayments agreed
items.who: Veterans with gross household income below the geographically adjusted VA income limit for their resident location who agree to pay copayments
items.value: Seventh enrollment priority
items.how: Group 7 is 'Veterans with gross household income below the geographically adjusted VA income limit for their resident location and who agree to pay copayments.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The geographic limit is higher than the national limit in expensive counties. A veteran over the national limit can still be Group 7 on the geographic figure — ask for the geographic test by name.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Priority Group 8 sub-priorities a through d — who can still enroll above the income limit
items.who: Veterans with gross household incomes above both VA's national income limit and the geographically adjusted limit, who agree to pay copayments
items.value: Sub-priorities 8a, 8b, 8c and 8d are eligible for enrollment
items.how: Group 8 is 'Veterans with gross household incomes above VA's national income limit and the geographically adjusted income limit for their resident location and who agree to pay copayments.' Eligible for enrollment: sub-priority a, non-compensable 0% service-connected 'enrolled as of January 16, 2003, and who have remained enrolled since that date'; sub-priority b, non-compensable 0% 'enrolled on or after June 15, 2009, whose income exceeds the current VA national income limits or VA national geographic income limits by 10% or less'; sub-priority c, nonservice-connected 'enrolled as of January 16, 2003, and who remained enrolled since that date'; sub-priority d, nonservice-connected 'enrolled on or after June 15, 2009, whose income exceeds the current VA national income limits or VA national geographic income limits by 10% or less.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The 10%-or-less overage rule in 8b and 8d is the single most useful line in the priority table: if you are barely over the limit, you are still enrollable. Run your income against both the national and the geographic limit and use whichever you clear.
items.deadline: Legacy enrollment dates: January 16, 2003 and June 15, 2009

items.title: Priority Group 8 sub-priorities e and g — enrolled only for service-connected care, or not at all
items.who: Non-compensable 0% service-connected veterans above the limit (8e) and nonservice-connected veterans who do not meet 8c or 8d (8g)
items.value: Not eligible for enrollment; 8e may still receive care for the service-connected condition only
items.how: Listed as not eligible for enrollment: sub-priority e, non-compensable 0% service-connected Veterans '(eligible for care of their service-connected condition only)'; and sub-priority g1, nonservice-connected Veterans not meeting the sub-priority c or d criteria. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Even in 8e you keep care for the service-connected condition itself. File a claim on anything plausibly service-connected: one granted 0% condition converts a closed door into a standing appointment.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Financial assessment on initial application — and the annual reporting VA dropped
items.who: Most veterans not receiving VA disability compensation or pension payments
items.value: One financial assessment at initial application; no annual re-reporting for non-service-connected and 0% veterans
items.how: 'Most Veterans not receiving VA disability compensation or pension payments must provide a financial assessment upon initial application to determine their eligibility for free medical care.' VA no longer requires annual reporting for non-service-connected and 0% service-connected Veterans; IRS and Social Security information is used for verification instead. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: You do not have to send VA an income update every year any more. VA pulls IRS and SSA data. If VA sends a letter demanding an annual update on a non-service-connected enrollment, cite this change.
items.deadline: Initial application only

items.title: Declining the financial assessment means agreeing to copayments
items.who: Veterans whose income exceeds VA income limits and those who choose not to complete the financial assessment
items.value: Must agree to pay required VA copayments
items.how: 'Veterans whose income exceeds the VA income limits as well as those who choose not to complete the financial assessment at the time of enrollment must agree to pay required VA copayments.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Refusing to disclose income is a legitimate choice, but it is treated as a copay election — it does not get you free care by default. If your income is actually low, completing the assessment is the cheaper path.
items.deadline: At time of enrollment

items.title: Indian and Urban Indian Veterans are copay-exempt for all hospital care and medical services
items.who: Indian and Urban Indian Veterans
items.value: Full copay exemption for all hospital care and medical services
items.how: The handbook's note reads: 'NOTE: Indian and Urban Indian Veterans are copay-exempt for all hospital care and medical services.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: This is a blanket exemption with no income test and no rating requirement, and it is printed as a NOTE that is easy to miss. Bring tribal enrollment documentation or Urban Indian Organization confirmation to your enrollment appointment.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA bills your private insurance but you are not responsible for what it refuses
items.who: Enrolled veterans with private health insurance receiving care for non-service-connected conditions
items.value: No liability for unpaid or uncovered balances; insurance payments offset copayments dollar for dollar
items.how: VA bills private health insurance for non-service-connected condition treatment. The beneficiary is not responsible for unpaid or uncovered balances, and insurance payments offset copayments 'dollar for dollar.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Give VA your insurance card even if you think it will cost you — the payment reduces your own copay dollar for dollar and you can never be balance-billed. Withholding the card only costs you money.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The handbook prints no copay dollar figures — it points to one live rate page
items.who: All enrolled veterans subject to copayments
items.value: Current rates published only at va.gov/healthcare/copay-rates
items.how: For copayment amounts the handbook says only: 'For more information on medical services and VA copayments, visit www.va.gov/healthcare/copay-rates.' No inpatient, outpatient, specialty, urgent care or medication tier dollar figures appear in Chapter 2. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Any copay figure you are quoted from a chart or a forum is unsourced as of this edition. Check the live rate page before you budget, and screenshot it with the date — rates change by calendar year.
items.deadline: Rates change annually

items.title: VA health care income limits change annually and are geographically adjusted
items.who: Veterans whose enrollment priority depends on income
items.value: Published annually at va.gov/health-care/income-limits
items.how: 'VA's income limits change annually, and current levels can be found at www.va.gov/health-care/income-limits/introduction.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: There are two numbers, national and geographic, and you only need to clear one of them. Look up your county's geographic limit before concluding you are over.
items.deadline: Annual change

items.title: Four ways to apply for VA health care with Form 10-10EZ
items.who: Any veteran applying for VA health care
items.value: Phone, online, mail or in person
items.how: Apply by phone at '877-222-VETS (877-222-8387) Monday through Friday between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. ET.' or '1-800-MyVA411 (1-800-698-2411)'; online, where 'VA will search for your supporting documentation through its electronic information systems'; by mail to the Health Eligibility Center; or in person — 'Veterans can also apply in person at most VA medical centers and some clinics.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Applying by phone or online makes VA find your DD-214 itself through its electronic systems. Mailing a paper form is the slowest route and the only one where a missing discharge document stalls you.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The mailing address for a paper VA health care application
items.who: Veterans mailing Form 10-10EZ or 10-10EZR
items.value: Health Eligibility Center, ATTN: Enrollment Eligibility Division, P.O. Box 5207, Janesville, WI 53547-5207
items.how: The handbook gives the mailing address as 'Health Eligibility Center, ATTN: Enrollment Eligibility Division, P.O. Box 5207, Janesville, WI 53547-5207.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Send it certified with return receipt and keep the receipt — the postmark is your application date if the file is later rebuilt.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Once enrolled, you can use any VA facility in the country
items.who: Enrolled veterans
items.value: Care at VA health care facilities anywhere in the country
items.how: 'Once enrolled, Veterans can receive health care at VA health care facilities anywhere in the country.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Enrollment is national, not local. Moving states does not require re-enrolling — it requires transferring your primary care assignment, which is a phone call.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Health Connect — a real person on the phone or chat, 24/7
items.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care
items.value: Nurse advice, appointment scheduling, urgent-issue consultation and medication refills by phone, video or chat
items.how: 'VA Health Connect gets you to the right care, right now. Talk on the phone or chat online with a real person in real time 24/7 about your health care needs.' Services include talking 'to a medical provider about an urgent or developing medical issue via phone or video' and refilling medications with pharmacy assistance. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Before you drive to an emergency room or pay an urgent care copay, call VA Health Connect — a nurse can authorize care, book you same-day, or tell you it can wait, which is also worth knowing.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA Health Chat app — the same access without a phone call
items.who: Enrolled veterans
items.value: Chat with VA clinical staff; hours vary by site, some locations 24/7
items.how: Access by calling your local VA medical facility or using the VA Health Chat app, 'Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-4 p.m. local time, some locations 24/7.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Check whether your facility is one of the 24/7 chat sites — coverage is uneven, and the app will tell you before you need it at 2 a.m.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Telehealth is available to any enrolled veteran as an addition to in-person care
items.who: Anyone enrolled in VA health care
items.value: Telehealth visits in addition to in-person services
items.how: 'Anyone who is enrolled in health care through VA can choose telehealth visits in addition to in-person services.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Telehealth does not replace your in-person care or your travel benefit — it is additive. Use it for follow-ups and keep in-person slots for anything that needs hands on you.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Veterans Community Care Program — the six doors to a community provider
items.who: Enrolled veterans whose health care needs meet one of six criteria
items.value: Care from a local community provider at VA expense
items.how: The six criteria are service unavailable ('You need a service that is not available at any VA health care facility'); facility unavailable; grandfathered choice status; best medical interest ('You and your VA provider agree it is in your best medical interest to be referred'); quality standards (VA determines the service 'is not providing care that complies with VA's quality standards'); and access standards. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: You only need one of the six. 'Best medical interest' is the most flexible and the least used — it needs nothing but your VA provider agreeing in writing, so ask them to document it in the note.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The 'facility unavailable' community care criterion names seven states and territories
items.who: Veterans residing in Alaska, Hawaii, New Hampshire, Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, or the U.S. Virgin Islands
items.value: Automatic community care eligibility on the facility-unavailable criterion
items.how: The facility-unavailable criterion 'applies to Veterans in Alaska, Hawaii, New Hampshire, Guam, American Samoa, Northern Mariana Islands, and U.S. Virgin Islands.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: If you live in one of these seven, you do not argue drive times — you are eligible on residence alone. New Hampshire is the one mainland state on the list and veterans there routinely do not know it.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Grandfathered Choice Program distance eligibility survives from before June 6, 2018
items.who: Veterans who still reside in a location that qualified them under the Veterans Choice Program's distance criteria before June 6, 2018
items.value: Continued community care eligibility on legacy distance grounds
items.how: 'You continue to reside in a location that qualified you for community care under the Veterans Choice Program's distance criteria prior to June 6, 2018.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: If you were eligible under the old 40-mile rule and have not moved, you keep that eligibility regardless of today's drive-time standard. Say 'I am grandfathered under the Choice distance criteria' at the referral desk.
items.deadline: Must have resided there prior to June 6, 2018 and still reside there

items.title: Emergency care in a community facility — the 72-hour notification is the whole ballgame
items.who: Veterans who cannot receive timely emergency care from a VA facility
items.value: Emergency department care at community facilities, possibly at VA expense
items.how: 'You may receive emergency care at a community emergency department, possibly at VA expense, when you cannot receive timely emergency care from a VA facility.' Notification: 'the community provider, you or your representative must contact the closest VA medical facility within 72 hours of the emergency.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Any of three people can make the call — the provider, you, or your representative. Do not assume the hospital did it. Make the call yourself from the bed, and write down who you spoke to and when.
items.deadline: 72 hours from the emergency

items.title: The 72-Hour Emergency Care Notification Line and the online reporting portal
items.who: Veterans, their representatives, and community providers reporting an emergency episode
items.value: Call 844-724-7842 or file through the emergency care reporting portal
items.how: Notification may be made by calling '844-724-7842 or submit an emergency care online portal notification at emergencycarereporting.communitycare.va.gov.' The front matter lists the same number as the '72-Hour Emergency Care Notification Line.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Save 844-724-7842 in your phone under 'VA 72-hour line' today. It is the single number that decides whether an emergency room bill becomes VA's problem or yours.
items.deadline: 72 hours from the emergency

items.title: Two separate routes to community emergency care eligibility
items.who: Veterans who received VA health care in the previous 24 months, or who meet 38 U.S.C. 1728 requirements
items.value: Eligibility for VA payment of community emergency care
items.how: Eligibility requires either: 'You received VA health care within the previous 24 months; or You meet one the 38 U.S.C. 1728 reimbursement requirements: seeking treatment of a service-connected conditions or a condition aggravating it; you have a VA rating of permanently and totally disabled; or you meet the 1728 requirements for participants in a VA vocational rehabilitation program.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The 24-month rule is the trap: a veteran who has not used VA in over two years can lose emergency coverage entirely. Book one appointment — any appointment — every couple of years purely to keep this alive.
items.deadline: 24 months since last VA care

items.title: Emergency suicidal crisis care at any facility, plus 90 days of follow-up
items.who: Veterans at imminent risk of self-harm who seek help at a non-VA emergency department
items.value: VA may cover the emergency care and care for up to 90 days
items.how: 'VA may be able to cover the cost of your emergency care and care for up to 90 days if you meet at least one of these requirements.' Eligibility: Veterans who were sexually assaulted or harassed during service, served 24 or more months honorably, or served 100 or more days deployed in combat or contingency operations. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: This covers follow-up care for 90 days, not just the emergency night — most veterans use the first visit and never claim the follow-up. Enrollment is not required and the eligibility routes include MST with no minimum service.
items.deadline: Up to 90 days of follow-up care

items.title: Urgent care in the community — enrolled, seen within 24 months, and in network
items.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care who received VA care within the previous 24 months
items.value: Walk-in treatment for non-life-threatening injuries and illnesses
items.how: 'Veterans must be enrolled, must have received VA Care within the 24 months before seeking urgent care, and must go to an urgent care provider in VA's network.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: All three conditions must hold at once. The in-network requirement is absolute — a non-network urgent care visit is yours to pay, so check the locator before you walk in, not after.
items.deadline: Must have had VA care within 24 months

items.title: What to say at the urgent care desk — and the eligibility check they run
items.who: Veterans using the VA urgent care benefit
items.value: Provider verifies your eligibility before providing care
items.how: 'Upon arriving, tell them you are using your VA urgent care benefit. The urgent care provider will verify your eligibility before providing care.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Say the words 'I am using my VA urgent care benefit' before you hand over any other insurance card. If you let them bill your private insurance first, untangling it afterwards is on you.
items.deadline: None

items.title: What the urgent care benefit actually covers, and the limits on medications
items.who: Veterans using in-network community urgent care
items.value: Diagnostic services such as X-rays, some lab testing, and some medications and prescriptions with limitations
items.how: 'Treatment may include diagnostic services like X-rays, some lab testing, and some medications/prescriptions (with limitations).' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Prescriptions from an urgent care visit are limited — expect a short course only, and plan to move anything ongoing to the VA pharmacy. Ask the urgent care provider to send the record to VA so the refill is not a fight.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Urgent care eligibility support lines by VA community care region
items.who: Veterans or providers verifying urgent care eligibility during a visit
items.value: 888-901-6609 for Regions 1, 2 and 3; 866-620-2071 for Regions 4 and 5
items.how: '888-901-6609 if located in Region 1, 2 or 3' and '866-620-2071 if located in Region 4 or 5.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: If the clinic says it cannot verify you, hand them the regional number rather than leaving. Most refusals are a front-desk system problem, not an eligibility problem.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Women Veterans Health Services — privacy, dignity, and the full care range
items.who: Women veterans enrolled in VA health care
items.value: Women's health screening, disease prevention, maternity care, fertility care, gynecologic services and mental health services
items.how: 'VA staff delivers the highest quality health care in a setting that ensures privacy, dignity, and sensitivity.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Ask for a designated Women's Health Primary Care Provider by name rather than a general primary care slot — it is a distinct assignment and it changes what gets screened for.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Women Veterans Call Center — call or text 855-VA-WOMEN
items.who: Women veterans with any benefits or health care question
items.value: Dedicated call and text line, 855-829-6636
items.how: 'Call or text 855-VA-WOMEN (855-829-6636) or visit www.womenshealth.va.gov.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: It takes texts, which matters if you are calling about something you would rather not say out loud in a shared house. The staff are trained on the full benefits picture, not just health care.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA assisted reproductive technology and IVF for service-connected infertility
items.who: Enrolled veterans with a VBA-adjudicated service-connected condition resulting in infertility, and their lawful spouses
items.value: IVF, embryo transfer, gamete and embryo cryopreservation, and genetic testing
items.how: 'VA may authorize specialized fertility benefits for Veterans who have a VBA-adjudicated service-connected condition that results in the inability to procreate without fertility treatments.' Coverage 'includes single, unmarried, and married Veterans and their lawful spouses.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The 2026 edition says single and unmarried veterans qualify — the old marriage requirement is gone. You need the service connection adjudicated by VBA first, so file the claim on the underlying condition before you start a fertility workup.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Free MST treatment with no rating, no service connection, and bad paper accepted
items.who: Veterans, service members, and former service members with Other Than Honorable or uncharacterized discharges; National Guard and Reserve members with federal active-duty service
items.value: Free treatment for physical and mental health conditions related to MST
items.how: 'VA provides free treatment for physical and mental health conditions related to MST. These services are available to individuals with Veteran status.' Service connection and a disability rating are not required. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: An Other Than Honorable or uncharacterized discharge does not block MST care. No claim, no rating, no copay, no minimum service period — walk in and ask for the MST Coordinator by title.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Mammography screening for all veterans 40 to 74, and at any age after toxic exposure
items.who: All veterans aged 40-74; veterans exposed to toxic substances who deployed in contingency operations, at any age
items.value: Breast cancer screening; risk assessment and screening for younger toxic-exposed veterans
items.how: The handbook sets screening for 'all Veterans aged 40-74,' and provides that 'Veterans exposed to toxic substances and deployed in contingency operations' are eligible for risk assessment and screening at any age. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Toxic exposure removes the age floor entirely. If you deployed to a burn pit area, ask for a risk assessment at 30 — you do not wait until 40.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Post-9/11 Military2VA (M2VA) case management at every VA medical center
items.who: Transitioning service members and Post-9/11 era veterans
items.value: Proactive outreach, advocacy and clinical case management, including screening for risk factors
items.how: 'Each VA medical center has a Post-9/11 Military2VA Case Management Program that provides proactive outreach and clinical case management services.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Every medical center has one and almost nobody asks for it. A case manager cuts through scheduling and referral problems that take a veteran months alone — ask for the M2VA Case Manager by name at intake.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Veteran Health Registries — a free environmental health evaluation that is not a claim exam
items.who: Veterans exposed to specific hazards: ionizing radiation, Agent Orange, Gulf War/OEF/OIF/OND, depleted uranium, airborne hazards and open burn pits
items.value: Free environmental health evaluation and exposure information
items.how: 'A health registry evaluation is not a disability compensation exam.' The registries cover ionizing radiation, Agent Orange, Gulf War/OEF/OIF/OND, depleted uranium, airborne hazards, and the Open Burn Pit Registry. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Because it is not a compensation exam, a registry evaluation cannot hurt a claim — and the findings become medical evidence you can later cite. Ask for the Environmental Health Coordinator at your facility, or call MyVA411.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Registry examinations do not require enrollment in VA health care
items.who: Veterans seeking ionizing radiation, Agent Orange, Gulf War/OEF/OIF/OND, depleted uranium, airborne hazards or Open Burn Pit Registry examinations
items.value: Registry exam without enrolling
items.how: The handbook lists veterans seeking 'registry examinations (ionizing radiation, Agent Orange, Gulf War/Operation Enduring Freedom/Operation Iraqi Freedom/Operation New Dawn (OEF/OIF/OND) depleted uranium, airborne hazards, and Open Burn Pit Registry)' among those not required to enroll. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: You can get the exposure exam before you ever file a 10-10EZ. It is the cheapest way to start building an exposure record if you are undecided about enrolling.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Electronic health information sharing with your non-VA providers, and how to opt out
items.who: Enrolled veterans whose care team includes non-VA providers
items.value: Secure sharing of VA electronic health information with participating community providers
items.how: VA securely shares electronic health information with participating non-VA providers on a Veteran's health care team for coordinated care. Opt-out options: online via My HealtheVet, by mail using Form 10-10164, or in person at the Release of Information (ROI) Office. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Sharing is on by default for participating providers. If you want it off, Form 10-10164 is the opt-out; Form 10-10163 is the opt-in. Do it through the ROI office in person if you want a stamped copy.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Vet Centers — confidential community counseling without time limitation
items.who: Combat veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve members, and their families
items.value: Confidential community-based counseling, outreach and referral, with no time limit
items.how: 'Vet Centers provide confidential, community-based counseling without time limitation.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: No time limitation is the key phrase — Vet Center counseling does not expire, does not need a rating, and sits outside your VA medical record. For a veteran worried about a security clearance, that separation is the entire point.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The full list of who qualifies for Vet Center services
items.who: Combat theater veterans; MST survivors; those who provided mortuary or medical care in service; UAV crew members; Vietnam-era veterans with pre-2013 access; national emergency and disaster responders; Coast Guard drug interdiction participants; Reserve component members with behavioral health needs; educational assistance beneficiaries
items.value: Vet Center eligibility
items.how: The handbook lists eligibility as combat theater service, MST experience, mortuary or medical care provision during service, UAV crew service, Vietnam-era Veteran (pre-2013 access), national emergency or disaster response, Coast Guard drug interdiction, Reserve component members with behavioral health needs, and educational assistance beneficiaries. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Drone crews, mortuary affairs and medical personnel are on this list — three groups that routinely assume Vet Centers are for infantry only. So are GI Bill beneficiaries, which quietly covers a lot of students.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Bereavement counseling through Vet Centers, including families bereaved by suicide
items.who: Families of deceased military personnel, reservists and National Guard members, and families of veterans or service members who died by suicide
items.value: Grief counseling at no cost through Vet Centers
items.how: Bereavement counseling is 'available to families of deceased military personnel, reservists, National Guard members, and Veterans/service members who died by suicide.' Vet Center Call Center, available 24/7: 1-877-927-8387. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: This reaches families who were never themselves in the military and have no other VA benefit. One call to 877-927-8387 opens it — there is no application and no eligibility packet.
items.deadline: None

items.title: HISA grants — $6,800 service-connected, $2,000 non-service-connected, lifetime
items.who: Veterans needing home modifications to continue treatment or access their home
items.value: Up to $6,800 lifetime for service-connected veterans; up to $2,000 lifetime for non-service-connected veterans
items.how: 'Service-connected Veterans receive up to $6,800 lifetime; non-service-connected Veterans receive up to $2,000 lifetime.' Apply by contacting the prosthetic representative at the nearest VA medical center. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: HISA runs through the prosthetics department of your medical center, not through Loan Guaranty — veterans lose months calling the wrong office. It stacks with SAH and SHA grants, which are a separate program entirely.
items.deadline: Lifetime limit, not annual

items.title: Spina Bifida Health Care Benefits Program for children of Korea, Vietnam and Thailand veterans
items.who: Birth children of Korea, Vietnam and Thailand veterans diagnosed with spina bifida, excluding spina bifida occulta
items.value: Comprehensive health care: outpatient, inpatient, pharmacy, prosthetics, medical equipment and supplies
items.how: The program provides comprehensive health care for birth children of Korea, Vietnam, and Thailand Veterans diagnosed with spina bifida, excluding spina bifida occulta, covering 'outpatient, inpatient, pharmacy, prosthetics, medical equipment, and supplies.' Program line: 833-930-0816. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Thailand and Korea service both count, not just Vietnam — the Korea DMZ and Thailand base perimeters were added years after the original program and many families never rechecked.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Lifetime care coordination for blind and visually impaired veterans
items.who: Veterans with visual impairments
items.value: Lifetime care coordination plus inpatient and outpatient blind and vision rehabilitation programs
items.how: The handbook describes 'lifetime care coordination and inpatient/outpatient VA blind and vision rehabilitation programs' for Veterans with visual impairments. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The word is lifetime — a Visual Impairment Services Team coordinator stays assigned to you. Ask for VIST by name; it is not something the eye clinic offers unprompted.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Mental health treatment across every setting, in person or by telehealth
items.who: Enrolled veterans needing general or specialty mental health care
items.value: Individual, group and family therapy in primary care clinics, outpatient clinics, residential programs and inpatient units
items.how: The handbook describes general and specialty mental health treatment including individual, group, and family therapy in primary care clinics, outpatient clinics, residential programs, and inpatient units, delivered by telehealth and in person. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Family therapy is on the list. If your spouse or kids are carrying the condition with you, VA can treat the family unit, not just you — ask the mental health clinic for family services specifically.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Veterans Crisis Line — 988 then 1, text 838255, or chat, with no enrollment
items.who: All veterans, service members, and concerned family or friends
items.value: 24/7 access to qualified VA responders; enrollment not required
items.how: 'The Veterans Crisis Line connects Veterans, Service Members, and concerned parties in crisis with qualified, caring VA responders.' Contact by dialing 988 then Press 1, texting 838255, or chatting at VeteransCrisisLine.net/chat. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Concerned parties means you can call about someone else. Enrollment, rating and discharge character are all irrelevant — there is no eligibility screen on this line.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Crisis Line access for National Guard, Reserve and overseas veterans
items.who: National Guard and Reserve members, and veterans living outside the continental United States
items.value: Regional contact information published for OCONUS access
items.how: The handbook notes that National Guard, Reserve, and OCONUS Veterans can find regional contact information at VeteransCrisisLine.net. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: 988 does not work from every overseas number. If you live abroad, look up and save your region's direct line now rather than discovering it fails at the worst moment.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Where VADIP is available — the states and territories list
items.who: Enrolled veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries residing in the U.S., District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa or the Northern Mariana Islands
items.value: VADIP coverage availability
items.how: VADIP is available in the 'U.S., District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, Northern Mariana Islands.' Enrollment questions: 877-222-VETS (877-222-8387), Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-8 p.m. ET. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The territories are explicitly included — a Guam or USVI veteran who was told dental insurance is stateside-only was told wrong.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Long-term services and supports — three national programs plus care at home
items.who: Enrolled veterans needing long-term care
items.value: Home and community-based services plus facility-based nursing home care through VA Community Living Centers, State Veterans Homes and the community nursing home program
items.how: The handbook describes home and community-based services (primary care at home, home health aide, respite services) and facility-based nursing home care through three national programs: VA Community Living Centers, State Veterans Homes, and the community nursing home program. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Respite is listed inside the home and community-based services, which means it does not require the caregiver program. Ask geriatrics for respite directly if PCAFC is not in play.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VA pays the full cost of nursing home care at 70% or more, or for a service-connected need
items.who: Enrolled veterans needing nursing home care for a service-connected disability; veterans rated 70% or greater; veterans rated totally disabled based on individual unemployability
items.value: VA pays the full cost of nursing home services
items.how: 'VA is obligated to pay the full cost of nursing home services for enrolled Veterans who need nursing home care for a service-connected disability or Veterans who have a 70% or greater service-connected disability and Veterans with a rating of total disability based on individual unemployability.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: 70% is the threshold, and TDIU counts as total disability for this purpose even at a lower combined rating. This is the single largest dollar benefit in the chapter and it turns on a number most veterans never check against their rating letter.
items.deadline: None

items.title: State Home Per Diem Program — federal money behind State Veterans Homes
items.who: Veterans using state-operated Veterans Homes for nursing, domiciliary or adult day health care
items.value: Federal grant assistance and daily per diem payments to state homes
items.how: The program provides 'federal grant assistance and daily payments to state-operated Veterans Homes for nursing, domiciliary, and adult day health care.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Adult day health care is on this list, which makes a state home a daytime option rather than only a residential one — often the difference between a caregiver keeping a job or not.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Foreign Medical Program — VA pays for service-connected care abroad
items.who: U.S. veterans living or traveling abroad who need care for a VA-rated service-connected disability
items.value: Payment or reimbursement of claims for treatment of service-connected disabilities overseas
items.how: 'VA's Foreign Medical Program pays/reimburses health care claims for treatment of the U.S. Veteran's VA-rated service-connected disability while the Veteran is living or traveling abroad.' Submit VA Form 10-7959f-1 by fax to 303-331-7803 or by mail. Contact 833-930-0816 (TTY 711). Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Register with FMP before you travel, not after you need it — the program issues a benefits authorization letter that foreign providers will actually accept. It also covers conditions that aggravate a service-connected disability.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Traveling Veteran Coordination — notify your PACT four to six weeks before you go
items.who: Enrolled veterans who will need care at a different VA facility while traveling
items.value: Coordinated care at the alternate VA facility
items.how: Notify your Patient Aligned Care Team (PACT) 4-6 weeks prior with destination, address, phone, dates, and care needs. The PACT then contacts the Traveling Veteran Coordinator for care coordination. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Four to six weeks, and there is a named Traveling Veteran Coordinator at every facility. Snowbirds who do this once stop having their prescriptions and infusions interrupted every winter.
items.deadline: 4-6 weeks before travel

items.title: Veteran Health Identification Card (VHIC) — check in without exposing your SSN
items.who: Enrolled veterans
items.value: Secure ID card for check-in at VA medical centers
items.how: The VHIC is a 'secure ID card used for check-in at VA medical centers, protecting personal information while enabling health record access.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The VHIC is not the Veteran ID Card and not a VA benefits card — it is specifically for medical check-in, and it replaces reading your Social Security number out loud at a crowded desk.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Caregiver Support Program — two programs, one office
items.who: Caregivers of veterans
items.value: Individual and group support, skills training, peer mentoring, respite care, mental health counseling, legal and financial planning, monthly stipends and health care coverage access
items.how: 'VA provides support to caregivers of Veterans through its Program of General Caregiver Support Services and Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: PGCSS and PCAFC are run by the same Caregiver Support Program team at your medical center. If PCAFC turns you down, PGCSS has no rating requirement and no application — ask the same coordinator to move you across.
items.deadline: None

items.title: CHAMPVA — who the veteran has to be for the family to qualify
items.who: Dependents and survivors of a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled, who died from a service-connected disability, or who died in the line of duty not due to misconduct
items.value: Reimbursement for inpatient, outpatient, mental health, prescription medications, skilled nursing care and medical equipment
items.how: 'Under CHAMPVA, certain dependents and survivors can receive reimbursement for most medical expenses.' The veteran must be 'rated permanently and totally disabled, died from a service-connected disability, or died in line of duty (not misconduct).' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Permanent and total is the trigger, not 100% — a 100% rating that is not P&T does not open CHAMPVA. Check your rating letter for the words 'permanent and total' before telling your spouse they are covered.
items.deadline: None

items.title: CHAMPVA and TRICARE are mutually exclusive
items.who: Spouses and dependents of eligible veterans
items.value: Must not be eligible for TRICARE to use CHAMPVA
items.how: Spouse and dependent eligibility requires that they 'must not be eligible for TRICARE (Department of War program).' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Eligibility for TRICARE disqualifies you even if you never use it. A military retiree's spouse is almost always TRICARE-eligible and therefore almost never CHAMPVA-eligible — know which one you are before you apply.
items.deadline: None

items.title: CHAMPVA remarriage rules turn on age 55
items.who: Surviving spouses with CHAMPVA
items.value: Remarriage after 55 does not affect eligibility; remarriage before 55 ends it, with reinstatement if the later marriage ends
items.how: 'Age 55+ spouse remarriage doesn't affect eligibility; age 55- spouse loses eligibility at remarriage unless marriage ends and re-establishes within specified timeframe.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: 55 is the line, the same age that governs DIC remarriage. A surviving spouse weighing remarriage before 55 is weighing away health coverage, not just a monthly check.
items.deadline: None

items.title: CHAMPVA is always the secondary payer, and Medicare Part B is mandatory
items.who: CHAMPVA beneficiaries with other health insurance or Medicare
items.value: CHAMPVA pays second; Medicare beneficiaries must maintain Part B enrollment
items.how: 'CHAMPVA is secondary when other health insurance exists; Medicare beneficiaries must maintain Part B enrollment.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Dropping Part B to save the premium kills CHAMPVA. This is the most expensive avoidable mistake in the program — if you are on Medicare and CHAMPVA, keep Part B paid no matter what.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Camp Lejeune Family Member Program — 15 conditions, reimbursed
items.who: Family members of veterans stationed at Camp Lejeune between August 1, 1953 and December 31, 1987
items.value: Reimbursement of medical care costs for 15 specified illnesses and conditions
items.how: The program provides 'medical care cost reimbursement for family members of Veterans stationed at Camp Lejeune (August 1, 1953-December 31, 1987) for 15 specified illnesses/conditions.' Contact 866-372-1144. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: This is reimbursement to the family member, paid after other insurance, and it is a separate program from the veteran's own Camp Lejeune eligibility and from the Justice Act lawsuits. Keep every explanation of benefits.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Beneficiary travel — the six ways to qualify for mileage
items.who: Veterans with a 30% or greater service-connected rating; those traveling for service-connected treatment; those traveling to obtain a service dog; VA pension recipients or those whose income does not exceed the maximum annual rate; those traveling for a scheduled compensation or pension exam; those traveling for inpatient care under a VA special disability rehabilitation program
items.value: Mileage reimbursement eligibility
items.how: The handbook lists eligibility as: service-connected disability rating of 30% or more; traveling for treatment of a service-connected condition; traveling to obtain a service dog; receives VA pension or income does not exceed the maximum annual rate; traveling for a scheduled compensation or pension examination; and traveling for care through a VA special disability rehabilitation program on an inpatient basis. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Travel to obtain a service dog is a listed category in its own right. So is travel to a C&P exam — which means VA pays you to attend the exam it ordered, and almost nobody claims it.
items.deadline: File within VA's claim window after each trip

items.title: The travel mileage rate, the per-trip deductible, and the monthly cap
items.who: Veterans eligible for beneficiary travel
items.value: 41.5 cents per mile; $3 one-way or $6 round-trip deductible; maximum deductible $18 per calendar month
items.how: 'Mileage reimbursement is currently 41.5 cents per mile and there is a deductible of $3 one-way or $6 round-trip for each trip. The maximum deductible is $18 per calendar month.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The $18 monthly cap means the deductible stops after three round trips — every trip after that in the same month reimburses in full. If you can cluster appointments into one month, you keep more of the money.
items.deadline: Deductible caps per calendar month

items.title: Four situations where the travel deductible is waived entirely
items.who: Veterans traveling for compensation or pension exams; those using special mode transport; non-Veteran beneficiaries; veterans in severe financial hardship
items.value: Travel deductible waived
items.how: The deductible is waived for compensation and pension exams, special mode transport, non-Veteran beneficiaries, and severe financial hardship cases. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Severe financial hardship is a waiver you have to ask for — it is not applied automatically. Raise it with the travel office in writing, and the C&P exam waiver should never be charged to you at all.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Special mode transportation — ambulance and wheelchair van at VA expense
items.who: Veterans for whom special mode transport is medically indicated
items.value: Ambulance or wheelchair van transport, with the travel deductible waived
items.how: Special mode transport, including ambulance and wheelchair van, is 'available when medically indicated.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The test is medical indication, documented by a VA provider, and it must usually be authorized in advance except in an emergency. Get the standing authorization into your chart before you need it.
items.deadline: Prior authorization generally required except emergencies

items.title: The PACT Act is the largest expansion of VA benefits in 30 years
items.who: Veterans exposed to burn pits and other toxic substances, and their survivors
items.value: Expanded VA health care and benefits
items.how: 'On August 10, 2022, the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics Act of 2022, referred to as the PACT Act, was signed into law. The law expands VA health care and benefits for Veterans exposed to burn pits and other toxic substances, providing generations of Veterans-and their survivors-with the care and benefits they have earned and deserve. The enactment of the PACT Act marks the largest expansion of VA benefits in 30 years.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Survivors are named in the statute's own framing. If a veteran died of a condition now presumptive, the family has a claim even though the veteran never filed one.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Project 112/SHAD participation is its own Priority Group 6 category
items.who: Veterans who participated in Project 112/SHAD
items.value: Priority Group 6 placement
items.how: The handbook lists 'Project 112/SHAD participants' among the Priority Group 6 categories. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Project 112 and Shipboard Hazard and Defense testing ran in the 1960s and participants were often never told. If you served aboard a test vessel, ask VA to check the SHAD participant list against your service number.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Atmospheric nuclear testing and Hiroshima/Nagasaki occupation duty place you in Priority Group 6
items.who: Veterans exposed to ionizing radiation during atmospheric testing or during the occupation of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
items.value: Priority Group 6 placement
items.how: Group 6 includes those exposed to 'ionizing radiation during atmospheric testing or during the occupation of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Occupation duty counts, not just the tests. A veteran who was in Japan on occupation orders in 1945-46 is a radiation-exposed veteran for enrollment purposes.
items.deadline: None

items.title: World War II veterans are a named Priority Group 6 category
items.who: World War II veterans
items.value: Priority Group 6 placement
items.how: The handbook lists 'World War II Veterans' among the Priority Group 6 categories. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Status alone qualifies — no income test and no rating needed. Worth knowing for the last cohort of WWII veterans and for the family members managing their care.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Vietnam service between January 9, 1962 and May 7, 1975 places you in Priority Group 6
items.who: Veterans who served in the Republic of Vietnam between January 9, 1962 and May 7, 1975
items.value: Priority Group 6 placement
items.how: Group 6 includes those who 'served in the Republic of Vietnam between January 9, 1962, and May 7, 1975.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The window opens in January 1962, earlier than the date most charts use, and closes in May 1975. Check your orders against those exact dates.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Southwest Asia service from August 2, 1990 through November 11, 1998 places you in Priority Group 6
items.who: Veterans who served in the Southwest Asia theater of operations from August 2, 1990 through November 11, 1998
items.value: Priority Group 6 placement
items.how: Group 6 includes those in the 'Southwest Asia theater of operations from August 2, 1990, through November 11, 1998.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: The theater period runs to November 1998, well past Desert Storm's end. Service in Kuwait or Saudi Arabia in the mid-1990s still counts.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Special eligibility under 38 U.S.C. 1151 puts you in Priority Group 3
items.who: Veterans awarded special eligibility classification under 38 U.S.C. 1151
items.value: Priority Group 3 placement
items.how: Group 3 includes those 'awarded special eligibility classification under 38 U.S.C. 1151.' Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Section 1151 covers injury caused by VA care itself. It is treated as if service-connected for enrollment, which lands you in Group 3 alongside Purple Heart recipients.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The dental chapter is one line and a web address — the classes are not in this edition
items.who: Veterans seeking VA direct dental care
items.value: Eligibility criteria published only at va.gov/dental
items.how: Chapter 2 says only that 'VA is limited to providing dental benefits to those Veterans who meet certain eligibility criteria' and directs readers to www.va.gov/dental. The Class I through Class VI dental classification table does not appear in this edition. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
items.hack: Do not rely on a dental class chart that cites the handbook — this edition does not print one. Get the class determination in writing from your facility's dental service, and check the live page for the current criteria.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Homeless veteran health programs route through one national call center
items.who: Veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness
items.value: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans, 877-424-3838
items.how: Chapter 2 directs readers to 'Contact the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at 877-424-3838' and to department.va.gov/homeless. The chapter does not itself describe HUD-VASH, HCHV, HCRV or Grant and Per Diem. Source: 2026 VA handbook, Chapter 2.
