items.hack: One day of wartime service inside a 90-day enlistment is enough for pre-1980 entrants — the veteran never had to deploy or see combat. This is why Survivors Pension reaches far more widows of Korea- and Vietnam-era veterans than families expect.
items.deadline: No filing deadline, but the award runs from the filing date

items.title: Survivors Pension: the continuous cohabitation rule that defeats more claims than income does
items.who: Surviving spouses applying for Survivors Pension
items.value: The spouse must not have remarried after the veteran's death; the veteran must not have received a dishonorable discharge; the spouse must meet the income and net worth limits set by Congress; and the spouse must have 'lived with the Veteran from the time you were married until the Veteran's death, with no time living apart' — with limited exceptions.
items.how: VA, 'Survivors Pension' — eligibility, va.gov
items.hack: The exceptions to continuous cohabitation are real and they matter: separation caused by the veteran's misconduct, or by medical or employment necessity, does not defeat the claim. If a couple lived apart because he was in a nursing home or she moved for work, say so explicitly in the application rather than hoping it goes unnoticed.
items.deadline: Tested as at the date of death

items.title: Survivors Pension for children, and the one form that covers DIC, Pension and accrued benefits together
items.who: Unmarried surviving children of wartime veterans
items.value: An unmarried child qualifies if under 18, or under 23 and attending a VA-approved school, or unable to care for themselves due to a disability that arose before age 18. Apply on VA Form 21P-534EZ, Application for D.I.C., Survivors Pension, and/or Accrued Benefits — online, by mail to Janesville, Wisconsin, in person at a VA regional office, or through an accredited representative.
items.how: VA, 'Survivors Pension' — eligibility and how to apply, va.gov
items.hack: 21P-534EZ is three claims on one form. File it and you have simultaneously claimed DIC, Survivors Pension and accrued benefits — which matters enormously when a claim was pending at the veteran's death and the one-year accrued-benefits clock is running.
items.deadline: File within 1 year of death to preserve accrued benefits (38 CFR 3.1000(c))

items.title: CHAMPVA eligibility: four categories, and the TRICARE bar
items.who: Spouses, dependent children and survivors of permanently and totally disabled or deceased veterans
items.value: You may qualify if at least one applies: spouse or dependent child of a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability; surviving spouse or dependent child of a veteran who died from a service-connected disability; surviving spouse or dependent child of a veteran who was at the time of death rated permanently and totally disabled; or, in certain cases, a survivor of a service member who died in the line of duty, not due to misconduct. 'If you're eligible for or enrolled in TRICARE, you can't get CHAMPVA benefits.'
items.how: VA, 'CHAMPVA benefits', va.gov
items.hack: The bar is eligibility for TRICARE, not enrolment in it. A surviving spouse who is eligible for TRICARE through a military retiree's status cannot elect CHAMPVA instead, even if TRICARE is worse for them. Determine TRICARE eligibility first — the CHAMPVA question depends on it.
items.deadline: No deadline, but coverage is not retroactive before application in most cases

items.title: CHAMPVA requires Medicare Part A AND Part B once you are Medicare-eligible
items.who: CHAMPVA beneficiaries approaching or over 65, and those on Medicare through disability
items.value: 'If you're eligible for Medicare, you must have Medicare Part A and Part B in order to get or keep CHAMPVA benefits.'
items.how: VA, 'CHAMPVA benefits', va.gov
items.hack: Declining Part B to save the premium terminates CHAMPVA. This hits people under 65 who become Medicare-eligible through SSDI and do not realise Medicare has arrived. Enrol in both parts and keep CHAMPVA as the wraparound — losing it is far more expensive than the Part B premium.
items.deadline: Enrol in Part B during your Medicare initial enrolment period to avoid both a gap and a late-enrolment penalty

items.title: CHAMPVA costs: $50 deductible, 25% cost share, $3,000 catastrophic cap
items.who: CHAMPVA beneficiaries budgeting for the year
items.value: The calendar year deductible is '$50 per person or up to $100 per family each calendar year.' After the deductible, beneficiaries 'pay 25% of the CHAMPVA allowable amount' — CHAMPVA covers the remaining 75%. The annual catastrophic cap is '$3,000. After your household reaches this limit, you won't pay a cost share for covered services for the rest of the year.'
items.how: VA, 'CHAMPVA care' — costs, va.gov
items.hack: A $3,000 household out-of-pocket maximum is better than most employer plans and far better than a Medicare Advantage plan's cap. Track the cap deliberately — once a family hits $3,000 in a calendar year, every remaining covered service that year is free, which argues for front-loading elective care into the back half of a heavy year.
items.deadline: Deductible and catastrophic cap reset every January 1

items.title: What CHAMPVA covers — and the two exclusions that catch families out
items.who: CHAMPVA beneficiaries planning care
items.value: Covered: 'Family planning and maternity care, Hospice care, Inpatient care, Mental healthcare, Outpatient care and procedures, Skilled nursing care, Ambulance services, Medical equipment, Organ transplants, Prescription medications.' CHAMPVA 'doesn't cover eyeglasses or contact lenses except in certain cases' and does not cover 'prescription GLP-1 medications for weight loss.'
items.how: VA, 'CHAMPVA care' — covered and excluded services, va.gov
items.hack: Skilled nursing care and organ transplants being covered surprises people; routine vision not being covered surprises them more. And the GLP-1 weight-loss exclusion is specific — the same drug prescribed for diabetes is a different question from the same drug prescribed for weight loss.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Fry Scholarship: 36 months of Post-9/11 benefits, and the four qualifying death circumstances
items.who: Children and surviving spouses of service members who died on or after September 11, 2001
items.value: Eligible: the child or surviving spouse of a service member or Selected Reserve member who died on or after September 11, 2001 and who died in the line of duty while on active duty; died from a service-connected disability within 120 days of discharge; was a Selected Reserve member who died in the line of duty other than active duty; or was a Selected Reserve member who died from a service-connected disability. The benefit is 'up to 36 months' covering tuition, housing, books and other education costs.
items.how: VA, 'Fry Scholarship', va.gov
items.hack: 'Died from a service-connected disability within 120 days of being discharged' is a route almost nobody knows exists. A service member who separated and died of a service-connected condition four months later leaves Fry eligibility behind — and that is Post-9/11 rates, not Chapter 35 rates.
items.deadline: Death must have occurred on or after September 11, 2001; the 120-day rule applies to post-discharge deaths

items.title: Fry age and time limits: age 33 if the parent died before 2013, no limit after
items.who: Children eligible for the Fry Scholarship
items.value: Children must be 'at least 18 years old or you graduated from high school.' If the parent died before January 1, 2013, eligibility extends 'until you're 33 years old.' If the parent died on or after January 1, 2013, or was a Selected Reserve member, 'there's no time limit.'
items.how: VA, 'Fry Scholarship' — eligibility, va.gov
items.hack: January 1, 2013 is the hinge. A child whose parent died in 2012 has a hard wall at 33; a child whose parent died in 2013 has none at all. For the pre-2013 group, plan the degree backwards from the 33rd birthday — and use Chapter 35 for the overflow.
items.deadline: Age 33 for pre-2013 deaths; no limit for deaths on or after January 1, 2013

items.title: Fry for surviving spouses: remarriage does not end it, and DIC keeps paying
items.who: Surviving spouses using or considering the Fry Scholarship
items.value: Remarriage preserves eligibility, and expired benefits can be restored after January 2, 2025. Surviving spouses retain Dependency and Indemnity Compensation payments while using Fry benefits.
items.how: VA, 'Fry Scholarship' — surviving spouse rules, va.gov
items.hack: This is the decisive difference from Chapter 35: Fry lets a spouse keep DIC AND draw education benefits, and remarriage does not destroy it. A remarried surviving spouse who was told years ago their education benefit was gone should re-check — restoration of expired benefits opened after January 2, 2025.
items.deadline: Restoration of expired benefits applies after January 2, 2025

items.title: Fry versus Chapter 35: one at a time, and a combined cap of 81 or 48 months
items.who: Children eligible for both Fry and Chapter 35 DEA
items.value: Children may use both programs but 'only 1 program at a time,' with combined benefits capped at 81 months if the parent died before August 1, 2011, or 48 months if the death was on or after August 1, 2011.
items.how: VA, 'Fry Scholarship' — choosing between Fry and DEA, va.gov
items.hack: Order matters. Fry pays Post-9/11 rates — full in-state tuition at a public school plus a housing allowance — while Chapter 35 pays a flat monthly stipend. Spend Fry on the expensive years (the four-year degree) and Chapter 35 on the cheap ones (community college, a certificate), not the other way round.
items.deadline: Combined cap of 81 months (pre-Aug 1 2011 deaths) or 48 months (on/after Aug 1 2011)

items.title: Chapter 35 DEA: 36 months since August 1, 2018 — it used to be 45
items.who: Dependents using Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance
items.value: Training started before August 1, 2018: 'up to 45 months.' Training started on or after August 1, 2018: 'up to 36 months.'
items.how: VA, 'Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35)', va.gov
items.hack: The nine-month cut is permanent and it is driven by when training STARTED, not by when eligibility arose. Anyone who began training before August 1, 2018 and stopped out still has the 45-month entitlement — check the original start date before accepting a 36-month figure.
items.deadline: The 45-month entitlement applies only where training began before August 1, 2018

items.title: Chapter 35 eligibility is broader than death: MIA, captured, and detained all count
items.who: Dependents of veterans and service members in six distinct situations
items.value: The qualifying veteran or service member must be: permanently and totally disabled due to a service-connected disability; have died from a service-connected disability; have died in the line of duty; be missing in action or captured for 90+ days; be forcibly detained by a foreign entity for 90+ days; or be hospitalised for a service-connected permanent total disability and likely to be discharged for it.
items.how: VA, 'Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35)' — eligibility, va.gov
items.hack: The living-veteran route is the one that matters most in volume: a veteran rated permanently and totally disabled generates Chapter 35 for every dependent child and the spouse, while the veteran is alive and drawing compensation. Families treat Chapter 35 as a death benefit; it is not.
items.deadline: The 90-day thresholds apply to the MIA, captured and detained routes

items.title: Chapter 35 for children: since August 1, 2023 there is no age floor and no time limit
items.who: Children eligible for Chapter 35 DEA
items.value: Before August 1, 2023, a child had to be 18 or hold a high school diploma or GED to start. On or after August 1, 2023, any age is permitted. There is no time limit if eligibility occurred on or after August 1, 2023; otherwise, generally 'up to 8 years' before turning 26 if eligible before that date, with extensions where eligibility arose between ages 18 and 26, where the parent died in that window, or for military service (8 years from discharge, under 31).
items.how: VA, 'Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35)' — children's benefits, va.gov
items.hack: August 1, 2023 removed both the age floor and the 26-year wall for new eligibility. A dual-enrolled 16-year-old can now use Chapter 35, and a 40-year-old whose eligibility arose in 2024 has no deadline at all. For pre-2023 eligibility the 26th birthday is still the cliff — calendar it.
items.deadline: Age 26 cliff for eligibility arising before August 1, 2023; no limit after

items.title: Chapter 35 for spouses: 10 years, 20 years, or no limit — and the remarriage carve-out
items.who: Surviving and current spouses eligible for Chapter 35 DEA
items.value: Eligibility arising before August 1, 2023: generally ends 'after 10 years'; 'after 20 years' if the service member died on active duty. Eligibility arising on or after August 1, 2023: no time limit. Remarriage ends eligibility unless the wedding occurred 'on or after January 1, 2004, and you were at least 57 years old' or the new marriage ends by death or divorce. Apply on VA Form 22-5490.
items.how: VA, 'Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35)' — spouses' benefits, va.gov
items.hack: The 20-year window for an active-duty death is double the standard one and routinely misquoted as ten. And eligibility that ended through remarriage can revive if that marriage ends by death or divorce — a spouse in that position should reapply rather than assume the benefit is gone forever.
items.deadline: 10 years (standard), 20 years (active-duty death), or no limit if eligibility arose on/after August 1, 2023

items.title: ★ THE ONE-YEAR DEADLINE: accrued benefits must be claimed within 1 year of death
items.who: Any survivor of a veteran or beneficiary who died with money owed or a claim pending — this is the most irreversible deadline in the entire benefits system
items.value: The regulation states: 'Application for accrued benefits must be filed within 1 year after the date of death.' VA's own survivor page says the same: 'You must apply for accrued benefits within 1 year of the beneficiary's death.'
items.how: 38 CFR 3.1000(c), Entitlement to accrued benefits — ecfr.gov; and VA, 'Accrued benefits', va.gov
items.hack: Treat the date of death as day zero and file inside twelve months, no exceptions and no waiting for the death certificate to be perfect. There is no equitable tolling, no good-cause extension and no CUE remedy for a missed accrued-benefits deadline — the money owed for years of a pending claim simply ceases to exist. File VA Form 21P-534EZ or 21P-601 immediately and supplement later.
items.deadline: 1 year after the date of death — absolute

items.title: ★ SUBSTITUTION: also 1 year, quoted verbatim from 38 CFR 3.1010
items.who: Survivors who want to step into and continue a veteran's pending claim, decision review or appeal
items.value: 'A person may not substitute for a deceased claimant under this section unless the person files a request to substitute with the agency of original jurisdiction no later than one year after the claimant's death.' The written request must state the intent to substitute and include the deceased claimant's claim, Social Security or appeal number and the names of both the deceased claimant and the person requesting substitution.
items.how: 38 CFR 3.1010(c), Substitution in case of death of a claimant — ecfr.gov
items.hack: Substitution and accrued benefits are different things on the same one-year clock. Accrued benefits are limited to the evidence already in VA's hands at death; a SUBSTITUTE can keep developing the claim, submit new evidence and continue the appeal — which is usually worth far more. Where a claim was pending, request substitution, do not merely claim accrued benefits.
items.deadline: No later than one year after the claimant's death — absolute

items.title: ★ VA Form 21P-0847 is the substitution request — and the form page states no deadline
items.who: Survivors continuing a deceased claimant's claim or appeal
items.value: 'Request for Substitution of Claimant Upon Death of Claimant (VA Form 21P-0847)' is used when 'someone you're connected to dies before we finish processing their VA claim, decision review, or appeal — and you want to continue their claim.' It can be submitted online instead of on paper. The form page itself gives no deadline.
items.how: VA, 'About VA Form 21P-0847', va.gov — deadline from 38 CFR 3.1010(c)
items.hack: This is the trap: the form page is silent on the deadline, so families reasonably assume there isn't one. The one-year limit lives in 38 CFR 3.1010(c), not on the form page. Never rely on a VA form page for a deadline — go to the regulation.
items.deadline: 1 year after the claimant's death, per 38 CFR 3.1010(c) — not stated on the form page

items.title: ★ VA Form 21P-601 is the accrued-amounts claim — and 21P-534EZ does the same job plus DIC
items.who: Survivors claiming money VA owed a beneficiary at death
items.value: 'You should fill out an Application for Accrued Amounts Due a Deceased Beneficiary (VA Form 21P-601).' A spouse or child of a veteran may instead use VA Form 21P-534EZ, Application for D.I.C., Survivors Pension, and/or Accrued Benefits, which claims all three at once.
items.how: VA, 'Accrued benefits', va.gov
items.hack: For a spouse or child, file 21P-534EZ — it covers DIC, Survivors Pension and accrued benefits on one form, so a single timely filing protects everything. Use 21P-601 for claimants outside the spouse/child line, such as a person seeking reimbursement for last-sickness and burial expenses.
items.deadline: 1 year after the date of death

items.title: ★ CONFLICT TO WATCH: VA's page states a separate 5-year rule for 'lump sum' accrued benefits
items.who: Survivors and advocates working an accrued-benefits claim
items.value: VA's accrued-benefits page carries two deadlines: 'You must apply for accrued benefits within 1 year of the beneficiary's death' and, separately, 'If you're applying for lump sum accrued benefits, you must do so within 5 years of the Veteran's death.' The governing regulation, 38 CFR 3.1000(c), states only: 'Application for accrued benefits must be filed within 1 year after the date of death.'
items.how: VA, 'Accrued benefits', va.gov (both sentences); and 38 CFR 3.1000(c) — ecfr.gov
items.hack: Do not plan around the 5-year sentence. The regulation knows only a one-year limit, and the regulation is what an adjudicator applies. File within one year and treat the 5-year language as, at best, a narrow situation to raise if you are already late — never as your deadline.
items.deadline: File within 1 year. The 5-year language is on VA's page only and is not in 38 CFR 3.1000(c)

items.title: ★ The rule that saves a late family: a DIC or pension claim is 'deemed to include a request to substitute'
items.who: Survivors who filed for DIC or Survivors Pension but never filed a substitution request
items.value: A claim for accrued benefits, survivors pension or dependency and indemnity compensation by an eligible person 'is deemed to include a request to substitute' if a related claim or appeal was pending when the claimant died.
items.how: 38 CFR 3.1010 — ecfr.gov
items.hack: This is the safety net, and it is why filing 21P-534EZ fast matters so much. A surviving spouse who filed for DIC inside the year has already requested substitution by operation of the regulation, even if nobody ever sent a 21P-0847. If VA says the substitution request was late, check whether a timely DIC or pension claim was filed — it counts.
items.deadline: The underlying DIC, pension or accrued-benefits claim must itself be within 1 year of death

items.title: ★ Missing the deadline in a preferred category does NOT pass the right down the line
items.who: Children and parents of a deceased claimant whose surviving spouse did not act in time
items.value: 'Failure to timely file a request to substitute... by a person of a preferred category... will not serve to vest the right to request substitution in a person in a lower category.'
items.how: 38 CFR 3.1010 — ecfr.gov
items.hack: A surviving spouse who sits on their hands does not hand the claim to the children — they destroy it for everyone. If the spouse is grieving, incapacitated, estranged or simply unwilling, the children cannot wait out the year and then step in. Get the spouse to file, or get the whole family to file inside the same twelve months.
items.deadline: 1 year after the claimant's death for every category

items.title: The order of payees for accrued benefits — and what 'evidence in the file at date of death' means
items.who: Survivors determining who is entitled to a deceased beneficiary's unpaid benefits
items.value: Accrued benefits are paid to the living person first listed as: 'His or her spouse'; 'His or her children (in equal shares)'; 'His or her dependent parents (in equal shares) or the surviving parent.' 'Evidence in the file at date of death' means 'evidence in VA's possession on or before the date of the beneficiary's death, even if such evidence was not physically located in the VA claims folder on or before the date of death, in support of a claim for VA benefits pending on the date of death.'
items.how: 38 CFR 3.1000(a) and (d) — ecfr.gov
items.hack: That definition of 'in VA's possession' is a weapon. VA medical records, records VA had requested and received, and anything else VA held anywhere count — even if the claims folder itself was thin. Argue constructive possession of VHA treatment records; on an accrued-benefits claim it is often the whole case.
items.deadline: 1 year after the date of death to file

items.title: Bereavement counselling through Vet Centers — free, and it covers suicide loss explicitly
items.who: Surviving spouses, children and parents of service members and veterans
items.value: You qualify if you are a 'surviving spouse, child, or parent' of: a service member who died while serving; a Reservist or National Guard member who died on active duty; a veteran who was receiving Vet Center services at the time of death; or a veteran or service member who died by suicide. Services include outreach, counselling and referrals, delivered at Vet Centers, in community locations or by telehealth — all free of charge. Request it through your nearest Vet Center.
items.how: VA, 'Bereavement counseling', va.gov
items.hack: The suicide-loss category stands alone — it does not require that the veteran was enrolled in VA care or that the death was service-connected. Any surviving spouse, child or parent of a veteran or service member who died by suicide can walk into a Vet Center and be seen, at no cost, with no eligibility paperwork.
items.deadline: No stated time limit

items.title: Medal of Honor pension for surviving spouses — a distinct survivor benefit on VA's own list
items.who: Surviving spouses of Medal of Honor recipients
items.value: VA lists 'Medal of Honor pension for surviving spouses' as a separate survivor compensation program alongside DIC, Survivors Pension, accrued benefits and bereavement counselling.
items.how: VA, 'Survivor compensation benefits' program list, va.gov
items.hack: This sits outside DIC and outside Survivors Pension and is easy to miss because it is a one-line entry on a landing page. If a Medal of Honor recipient's spouse is in the picture, pursue it alongside DIC rather than instead of it — and check the current rate directly with VA.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: The ESGR Ombudsman: free, neutral, informal — and DOL itself points to resolution before complaint
items.org: Employer Support of the Guard and Reserve (DoD)
items.who: Reservists and Guard members with an employment problem they would rather not litigate
items.value: DOL VETS guidance is to attempt informal resolution with the employer before filing a formal complaint; ESGR provides free neutral ombudsman services for employer-employee disputes under USERRA. Mechanism verified; no current ESGR figures or response times were read on an official page this session.
items.how: DOL VETS, 'File a Claim' (informal resolution guidance), dol.gov — ESGR service described generally; confirm current ESGR contact details at esgr.mil
items.hack: Run ESGR mediation in parallel with documenting everything for a VETS complaint, not instead of it. Ombudsman mediation is non-binding and most employer violations are ignorance rather than malice — but keep your 1002.115 deadlines and your written reemployment application on track regardless of how friendly the mediation feels.
items.deadline: USERRA has no statute of limitations, but mediation does not pause your reporting and application deadlines

items.title: ACT NOW Education (ANE) — the free-resource clearinghouse for the whole military community
items.who: Active duty, veterans, reservists, National Guard, military spouses, and dependents
items.value: Advertises 'over 40,000 free resources and opportunities'; no cost and no obligation to members. ANE reports helping 24,000+ military members and families, 200+ master's degrees earned at no cost, and 300+ certifications awarded.
items.how: Start at actnoweducation.org, sign up for the free newsletter, and register for a Weekly Rundown. Everything flows from the Rundown.
items.hack: ANE is a broker, not a school. Its real value is that it aggregates partner seats and vouchers you would never find alone — and it hands out codes that unlock them. Treat it as the front door, not the destination.
items.deadline: None — ongoing organization

items.title: Verify ANE before you trust it: EIN 87-4345131, 501(c)(3), IRS ruling 2022
items.who: Anyone vetting the organization
items.value: Confirmed 501(c)(3) public charity. Legal name 'Act Now Education Organization Inc', Ellicott City, Maryland. Tax exemption issued March 2022.
items.how: Look up EIN 87-4345131 on ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer or Candid/GuideStar before handing over ID documents.
items.hack: ANE asks you to email a photo of your ID for Coursera verification. Confirming the 501(c)(3) and the EIN first is basic hygiene — do this before you send identity documents to any 'free benefits' group.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Reality check on ANE's size: a volunteer-run charity with a sub-$100K budget
items.org: ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer / ANE strategic goals
items.who: Anyone deciding how much to rely on ANE
items.value: IRS filings: FY2024 revenue $80,655 / expenses $79,160; FY2023 revenue $297,180 / expenses $300,670; FY2022 (990-EZ) revenue $3,354 / expenses $2,160. ANE's own strategic plan cites roughly $200,000 in annual expenses against $240,000 projected income, and says full implementation of its plan would cost a little over $1 million.
items.how: Set expectations accordingly: small team, volunteer labor, slow email, offers that appear and disappear with partner funding.
items.hack: This is the single best explanation for why ANE's offers are so volatile. Revenue dropped roughly 73% from FY2023 to FY2024. When a partner's funding lapses, the offer vanishes from the Rundown with no announcement. Never build a transition plan around one ANE offer.
items.deadline: FY2025 Form 990 was not yet posted as of late September 2026

items.title: ANE is volunteer-run — eight board members, ~4,000 volunteer hours each
items.org: ACT NOW Education strategic goals document
items.who: All members
items.value: No paid staff model; the organization describes itself as 'a group of volunteers that want to be the change we want to see.' Board of eight.
items.how: Be patient with response times and do not expect case management. Use the Rundown's live chat for answers rather than email.
items.hack: Because it is volunteer-run, the live Saturday Rundown chat is dramatically faster than email. Ask your question live in the chat — the team answers in real time and posts links there that never make it onto the website.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Founder and executive director: Navy LCDR Jai Salters, founded 2021
items.who: Context for all members
items.value: Founded in 2021 while Salters was still on active duty. Mission: upskilling and reskilling the military community through education so 'no opportunity goes to waste.'
items.how: Follow Jai Salters on LinkedIn — several ANE offers are released only through his personal LinkedIn posts.
items.hack: Some ANE benefits are claimed by direct-messaging a keyword on LinkedIn rather than through any form. The veteran teaching scholarship was distributed by messaging the word 'TEACHER' in caps. Watching the founder's LinkedIn is a genuine access channel.
items.deadline: None

items.title: ANE's stated three-year goals — and what they tell you about what is coming
items.org: ACT NOW Education strategic goals document
items.who: Members planning more than a few months ahead
items.value: Published goals: grow to 100,000 members in three years; run 3 CERT at least four times a year; place at least 75% of 3 CERT participants in certification-related jobs; expand certifications into other in-demand fields; add government, nonprofit and corporate partners; deepen the Coursera and Splunk partnerships.
items.how: Read the strategic goals document on ANE's Candid/GuideStar profile.
items.hack: The stated goal of running 3 CERT 'at least four times a year' is aspirational, not a schedule. The program's own page showed applications closed in March 2025. Use the goal document to see where ANE is heading, never as a calendar.
items.deadline: Three-year plan; no dated milestones published

items.title: The '40,000+ free resources' figure — how to read it honestly
items.who: All members
items.value: ANE's own description across its site, podcast and press coverage claims 'over 40,000 free resources and opportunities.'
items.how: Treat the number as a count of catalogued links and partner offerings, not 40,000 funded seats.
items.hack: The 40,000 figure counts resources in a database, not vouchers available to you. The genuinely scarce items — exam vouchers, cohort seats, master's scholarships — are rationed in batches of 20 to 50 and gated behind the weekly code. Chase the gated items; ignore the headline number.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Two domains, one organization: actnoweducation.org and actnoweducation.com
items.who: All members
items.value: ANE publishes links under both .org and .com, and its own podcast notes contain typo variants. Both resolve to the same organization.
items.how: Prefer actnoweducation.org. If a link fails, swap the TLD before assuming the offer is gone.
items.hack: ANE's own show notes contain misspelled domains ('actnowednucation.org', 'acnoweducation.org'). A dead ANE link is usually a typo, not a dead program — fix the spelling and try the other TLD before giving up.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Donations: ANE says 100% goes back to community members in need
items.who: Donors and supporters
items.value: ANE states that 100% of donations are returned to community members in need. It is registered with Benevity and PayPal for giving, and reports some recurring donors at about $10 per month. A summit fundraiser reportedly raised about $100,000 earmarked for certifications.
items.how: Give via the supporter page, Benevity (employer matching) or PayPal.
items.hack: If your employer uses Benevity for workplace giving, ANE is already registered — your match can be routed to certification vouchers for other veterans at no extra cost to you.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The Weekly Rundown — the free Saturday webinar that is the gateway to everything
items.who: Active duty, veterans, reservists, National Guard, military spouses, dependents
items.value: Free live webinar, roughly 1-2 hours, covering current job leads, scholarships, certification giveaways, cohort openings and partner resources. ANE reports orientations drawing roughly 200 to 500 people each week.
items.how: Register through the Weekly Rundown page on actnoweducation.org and attend live.
items.hack: This is not optional content — it is the access gate. Most of ANE's scarce benefits (Career Compass, cohort seats, voucher batches) require a code announced only during the live session. Reading the website alone gets you almost nothing.
items.deadline: Recurring weekly; register before each session

items.title: Weekly Rundown timing: Saturdays, 1:00-3:00 PM ET
items.who: All members
items.value: The 3 CERT requirements page specifies the Weekly Rundown runs Saturdays 1:00-3:00 PM Eastern. Independent coverage in June 2025 confirmed it runs 'live every Saturday.'
items.how: Block the recurring slot and register ahead; sessions have run about 1 to 2 hours.
items.hack: Confirm the current time on the registration page each week — ANE has published both a 2-hour window and shorter sessions, and the podcast archive shows episodes from 1:00 to 2:05 in length. Treat 1:00 PM ET Saturday as the anchor and verify.
items.deadline: Weekly; recurring

items.title: The weekly code — the single most important mechanic in the whole ecosystem
items.who: Anyone wanting Career Compass, cohort seats or vouchers
items.value: A code is announced in a survey during each live Weekly Rundown. It changes every week and is only valid for that week. Without it, the applications do not process.
items.how: Attend the live Rundown, complete the in-session survey, capture the code, then submit it on the relevant ANE application form.
items.hack: The code is the whole trick. It is deliberately not published anywhere, which is why people browse the site, find nothing claimable, and conclude ANE is hype. Attend one Saturday session, grab the code, and the gate opens the same week.
items.deadline: Code expires at the end of that week

items.title: Use the SAME email address for the Rundown and every application
items.who: All applicants
items.value: ANE's 3 CERT requirements state explicitly that you must use the same email for the Weekly Rundown registration and your program application, or the application will not move forward.
items.how: Pick one personal email address (not a .mil address you are about to lose) and use it everywhere with ANE.
items.hack: This silently kills applications. ANE matches your application to your Rundown attendance by email string. A mismatch is not flagged — it is simply dropped. Also: never use your .mil address, because you lose it at separation and with it your account recovery.
items.deadline: None — applies to every application

items.title: The Tuesday 7:00 PM processing deadline
items.who: Career Compass and cohort applicants
items.value: Applications submitted with the weekly code are batch-processed on Tuesdays; accounts are created by the following Tuesday. The Rundown team cited a Tuesday 7:00 PM cutoff and warned late submissions get missed.
items.how: Submit your form with the weekly code before Tuesday evening, not at the end of the week.
items.hack: The code lasts the week but the processing run is Tuesday. Submit Saturday night or Sunday. Submitting Wednesday means your code is burned and you wait for the next Rundown to get a fresh one.
items.deadline: Tuesday ~7:00 PM each week

items.title: The ANE Advantage newsletter — free monthly digest of certifications and deadlines
items.who: Anyone in the military community
items.value: Free newsletter covering upskilling and reskilling resources, free certification opportunities, deadlines, training and career tools. Described in Rundowns as monthly.
items.how: Sign up via the pop-up or newsletter form on actnoweducation.org.
items.hack: The newsletter is where ANE announced certification programs before they appeared anywhere else (an AI compliance certification and a Certified ScrumMaster batch were both pre-announced there). If you cannot make Saturdays, the newsletter is the minimum viable subscription.
items.deadline: None — ongoing

items.title: The podcast archive — the searchable record of what ANE actually gave away
items.org: ACT NOW Education Podcast (Weekly Rundown & Transition with Us)
items.who: Anyone researching ANE's offerings
items.value: Free podcast on Buzzsprout, Apple Podcasts, Spotify and Amazon Music. Episode pages carry full transcripts naming partners, seat counts, eligibility rules and deadlines.
items.how: Browse podcast.actnoweducation.org, or the RSS feed at feeds.buzzsprout.com/2461350.rss.
items.hack: Because ANE's main website is JavaScript-rendered and largely unreadable to search engines and AI tools, the podcast transcripts are the best public record of what ANE offers. Search the transcripts for a certification name to learn its real eligibility rules and seat counts.
items.deadline: None

items.title: 'Transition with Us' — ANE's newer transition-planning series
items.who: Transitioning service members and spouses
items.value: Episode 1 published April 28, 2026 (~51 minutes). Covers SkillBridge timelines, cash buffers for pay delays and overpayment clawbacks, life insurance/wills/beneficiaries, medical documentation, BDD claim timing, loss of community, and a '3-2-1' networking framework (three industry conversations, two events, one goal per month).
items.how: Listen via the ANE podcast feed.
items.hack: The 3-2-1 framework is the most portable thing in the series: three industry conversations, two events and one concrete goal per month. It converts vague 'networking' advice into a countable monthly quota.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The private Facebook group — 77,000+ members
items.who: Military community members
items.value: ANE's private Facebook community was cited at over 77,000 members in its own program materials and Rundowns.
items.how: Request to join the ACT NOW EDUCATION group on Facebook.
items.hack: Offers with tiny seat counts get posted in the group between Rundowns. If you can only monitor one asynchronous channel, the group moves faster than the website.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Career Compass — free premium access to the Careerflow job-search platform
items.who: Military community; Rundown reports indicated approvals were running for veterans, with spouse access less certain
items.value: ANE-branded free access to Careerflow, a for-profit platform. Features cited: AI resume building, LinkedIn profile optimization and scoring, job tracking, recruiter Boolean search, and a job board cited at 12 million-plus listings (one Rundown cited 19-21 million, refreshed often). ANE staff cited Careerflow's own paid tier at roughly $8.99/week or about $20/month — an approximate figure quoted live, not an official price.
items.how: Attend the Weekly Rundown, get the weekly code, submit the Career Compass form before Tuesday, then log into Careerflow with the same email you applied with.
items.hack: Career Compass is Careerflow premium, free. The accounts must be created by the ANE team so they link to the program — if you sign up at Careerflow directly you get the free consumer tier instead and cannot be migrated easily. Always go through the ANE form.
items.deadline: Weekly; processed Tuesdays

items.title: Career Compass results ANE reported: 338 roles saved, 18 members interviewing
items.who: Prospective Career Compass users
items.value: In a July 2025 Rundown, ANE reported 338 people had saved roles through the platform and 18 were interviewing.
items.how: Use the job tracker and LinkedIn scorer, not just the resume builder.
items.hack: The LinkedIn profile scorer gives a percentage plus specific fixes (one live demo scored 81%). It is the fastest high-value use of the account — run it the day you get access, fix what it flags, then start applying.
items.deadline: None

items.title: MilMentor — free mentorship with 1,000+ mentors at major employers
items.who: Service members, veterans and military spouses
items.value: Free mentorship platform connecting the military community with mentors at top companies. Mentor counts cited between 1,000 and 1,200-plus across industries. Includes mentor calls, one-click job applications and member events.
items.how: Access via milmentor.com or the MilMentor link from ANE.
items.hack: There is no cap on sessions and no penalty for switching. If a mentor cannot answer your question, book another — the Rundown team explicitly told members to re-book with a different mentor rather than settle. Treat it as unlimited informational interviews, which is exactly what the 3-2-1 framework needs.
items.deadline: None

items.title: 3 CERT Cohort — eight weeks, three industry certifications, free
items.who: Transitioning service members (3 months or less to separation), veterans, spouses of active-duty members, veteran military spouses, reservists, National Guard
items.value: Eight weeks of instructor-led virtual training toward three certifications, with exam vouchers included. ANE's flagship program; its strategic plan targets 75%+ job placement into certification-related roles.
items.how: Attend a Weekly Rundown to receive the registration code, then complete the application form using the same email address.
items.hack: 3 CERT bundles the three credentials that together read as 'IT project lead' on a resume: a security cert, an agile cert and a project management cert. That combination is worth far more than any one of them alone, and ANE pays for all three exams.
items.deadline: Applications stopped being accepted 03-03-2025; ANE said it would announce any reopening

items.title: What the three certifications in 3 CERT actually are
items.who: 3 CERT applicants
items.value: Cert 1: CompTIA Security+ or a Splunk certification (Core User, Power User, Cloud, or Advanced). Cert 2: Professional Scrum Master. Cert 3: PMI Project Management Professional (PMP) or CompTIA Project+, depending on your eligibility.
items.how: Confirm which track you qualify for during the application.
items.hack: The third slot forks on PMP eligibility: PMP requires documented project experience, so if you cannot meet PMI's experience requirement you are routed to CompTIA Project+ instead. Know which one you qualify for before you apply, and gather project hours early if you want the PMP.
items.deadline: Tied to cohort openings

items.title: 3 CERT includes a tailored business suit, a professional headshot and job placement help
items.who: 3 CERT participants
items.value: Beyond training and exam vouchers: resume help, mentorship from industry professionals, mock interview preparation, a tailored business suit, a professional headshot, an employment readiness workshop, and job placement assistance.
items.how: Included automatically for accepted cohort members.
items.hack: The suit and the headshot are the overlooked part. Interview clothing and a professional photo are real out-of-pocket costs at exactly the moment your income stops. ANE covering both, alongside the vouchers, is a large practical subsidy that no other certification program bundles in.
items.deadline: Tied to cohort participation

items.title: Cert2Success — three-week instructor-led course toward CISSP, PMP, Scrum Master or cloud security
items.who: Military community
items.value: A three-week instructor-led program covering CISSP, PMP, Scrum Master and cloud security certifications, plus job readiness training and placement support aimed at IT and cybersecurity roles.
items.how: Ask about current Cert2Success openings during a Weekly Rundown.
items.hack: Cert2Success is the shorter, higher-level sibling of 3 CERT — it reaches CISSP, which 3 CERT does not. If you already hold Security+ and have the CISSP experience requirement, ask about this rather than 3 CERT.
items.deadline: Cohort-based; confirm current status

items.title: Service to Success — a cohort that ends in a hiring fair
items.who: Military community members seeking employment
items.value: A cohort program covering resumes, personal branding, interviews, mentorship, training and job search strategy, concluding with a hiring fair. Length cited variously as four, six and seven weeks across ANE materials.
items.how: Request access through the ANE website or during a Weekly Rundown.
items.hack: The hiring fair at the end is the point. Unlike open job boards, you arrive already vetted by ANE and in front of employers who came specifically for military-affiliated candidates. Ask whether the fair is included before committing the weeks.
items.deadline: Cohort-based; recurring

items.title: SkillBridge Plus — ANE's certification-plus-placement SkillBridge track
items.who: Active-duty service members eligible for DoD SkillBridge, located in the DMV / Northern Virginia area; must be authorized to work in the U.S. or have a pending status
items.value: A SkillBridge pathway pairing three certifications with a job placement. Amazon was named as an employer for a Northern Virginia opportunity.
items.how: Raise it during a Weekly Rundown and apply when a cohort is announced.
items.hack: This one is genuinely geography-locked: the Rundown team said being willing to relocate is not enough — you must already be in the DMV area. Do not burn a SkillBridge application cycle on it from elsewhere.
items.deadline: Tied to announced cohorts

items.title: ACT NOW Coursera — free Coursera certificates, specializations and courses
items.who: Active duty, veterans, reservists, National Guard and military spouses; dependents were historically excluded
items.value: Free Coursera access through ANE's partnership. Catalog cited at over 12,000 courses, with 27-plus professional certificates highlighted. Some certificates carry college credit.
items.how: Register through the ANE Coursera page or the Eventbrite registration ANE distributes, then complete military-affiliation verification.
items.hack: Verification takes roughly one to three weeks (commonly quoted as about two) and is handled by a partner organization, not ANE. Start the Coursera request the moment you hear about it and work on something else while it processes — people miss cohort deadlines waiting on this.
items.deadline: Rolling; verification takes 1-3 weeks

items.title: Coursera identity verification: send only the front of your ID, by email
items.who: Coursera applicants
items.value: ANE instructs applicants to email a photo of the front of their ID only for military-affiliation verification.
items.how: Email the front of the ID as instructed; do not send the reverse side or additional documents.
items.hack: Front only. Any 'free benefits' process asking for the back of your ID, your SSN or your DD-214 in full for a course signup deserves a hard stop and a direct question to the team in the live Rundown chat.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Coursera for dependents — historically excluded, with a family program planned
items.who: Military dependents
items.value: ANE stated Coursera access was not normally offered to dependents, and described a planned IT certification program in which a dependent could enroll alongside a military-affiliated parent or family member.
items.how: Ask about dependent eligibility in the live Rundown chat before applying on a dependent's behalf.
items.hack: Eligibility differs sharply by group across ANE's catalog, and dependents are the most often excluded. Always confirm the specific group — service member, veteran, spouse, dependent — before investing time. The planned 'enroll with a parent' structure is the workaround to ask about.
items.deadline: Program was in planning; confirm current status

items.title: ACT NOW Splunk — free Splunk eLearning through SplunkWork+ and the Splunk Pledge
items.org: Splunk (SplunkWork+ / Splunk Pledge) + ACT NOW Education
items.who: Current service members, veterans and spouses, referred through ACT NOW Education as a skills development partner
items.value: Free access to Splunk's eLearning courses. SplunkWork+ is part of the $100 million Splunk Pledge. Splunk does not publish the normal course price on the ANE partner page.
items.how: Create a Splunk account via the SplunkWork+ ACT NOW Education page, verify your email, wait 24 hours, then register for courses on the Splunk Pledge training page and apply the coupon code at checkout.
items.hack: Two steps break people: you must wait a full 24 hours after verifying your email before the coupon will work, and you must be logged into the same account you created. Also note the coupon path runs through 'Buy Now' or 'Add to Cart' and then 'Apply Coupon Code' — the price only drops to zero at that final step, which looks alarming until you apply the code.
items.deadline: None stated — ongoing partner program

items.title: Splunk certifications reachable through the partnership: Core User, Power User, Cloud, Advanced
items.who: Service members, veterans, spouses
items.value: ANE's 3 CERT program lists Splunk Core User, Power User, Cloud and Advanced certifications as an alternative to CompTIA Security+ for its security slot.
items.how: Access the eLearning through SplunkWork+; pursue the certification through 3 CERT or an announced voucher batch.
items.hack: Splunk skills map directly onto SOC analyst and SIEM engineer job postings, and Splunk certifications are far less saturated among veterans than Security+. If you already hold Security+, taking the Splunk branch in 3 CERT differentiates you more.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Free master's degree program — an $18,000 scholarship from the partner school
items.who: Military community
items.value: ANE's strategic goals document lists a master's program carrying an $18,000 scholarship from the school. ANE reports 200-plus master's degrees earned at no cost through the organization.
items.how: Watch the ANE free-master's page and the newsletter, and ask in the Weekly Rundown when the next intake opens.
items.hack: The $18,000 figure is the school's scholarship against tuition, which is how the degree becomes free — it is not cash to you. Crucially, this can preserve your GI Bill entitlement for something else, which is the real financial win: a funded master's that costs you no months of Chapter 33.
items.deadline: Intake-based; confirm current availability

items.title: Scholarship America partnership — scholarships for veterans becoming teachers
items.who: Veterans pursuing teaching careers
items.value: ANE partners with Scholarship America on scholarships for veterans entering teaching. No dollar amount was published in the coverage reviewed.
items.how: Watch for ANE announcements; one distribution round was run by messaging the word 'TEACHER' in capitals to ANE on LinkedIn.
items.hack: This is the clearest example of ANE's informal access channels. A funded scholarship was distributed by LinkedIn direct message with a keyword — not through any application portal. If you want the teaching path, follow ANE and the founder on LinkedIn.
items.deadline: Round-based; no published deadline

items.title: JROTC instructor certification support
items.who: Retiring and retired service members
items.value: ANE lists support for transitions into JROTC instructor roles among its services, including certification guidance.
items.how: Ask about the JROTC pathway during a Weekly Rundown or via the newsletter.
items.hack: JROTC instructor pay is structured around your retired pay, and the certification requirements are service-specific. Pairing this with the teacher scholarship route gives retirees two parallel paths into schools.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: College-level certificate programs in development, including data center operations
items.who: Military community
items.value: As of June 2025 ANE described planned college-level certificate programs still in development, citing data center operations as a focus area. No launch dates, costs or formats were published.
items.how: Monitor the newsletter for launch announcements.
items.hack: Data center operations is where the hiring is: AWS was described in ANE Rundowns as actively hiring veterans and military spouses into data center roles, some with security clearance opportunities. A clearance plus data center training is an unusually strong combination.
items.deadline: In development as of mid-2025

items.title: The $100 nonprofit discount on PMI and CompTIA vouchers
items.who: Military community members buying their own vouchers through ANE
items.value: ANE staff stated that because ANE is a nonprofit, members can get $100 off any certification through PMI, CompTIA and similar bodies — available unless you are taking one of ANE's free courses, which cover the exam outright.
items.how: Ask the Rundown team for the nonprofit voucher rate if you are paying for your own exam.
items.hack: Even when the free cohorts are closed, the nonprofit rate stays available. If you missed a cohort, do not pay retail — ask for the discounted voucher. It is the consolation prize nobody asks for.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: The assessment gate: score 70 to receive a voucher
items.who: Voucher applicants
items.value: ANE staff stated a score of 70 on the program assessment is required to receive an exam voucher.
items.how: Take the practice assessment seriously; hit 70 or above before the voucher is issued.
items.hack: This gate exists because ANE pays for the exam and tracks pass rates. Treat the assessment as the real application. Using the included study resources to clear 70 comfortably is the difference between getting a funded exam and being passed over.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Use-it-or-lose-it: unused vouchers can get you banned from the community
items.who: Anyone awarded a voucher or seat
items.value: ANE stated that voucher recipients must act on the voucher or formally decline it, and that non-use may result in being banned from the community.
items.how: If you cannot use a voucher or seat, decline it promptly so it can be reassigned.
items.hack: This is the etiquette rule with teeth. Seats and vouchers are scarce and funded by donations, and ANE reassigns declined ones. Declining costs you nothing and keeps you eligible; silently sitting on one can end your access permanently.
items.deadline: Act or decline promptly

items.title: Seat counts are tiny — expect 20 to 50 per offer, and cohorts that fill
items.who: Anyone planning around an ANE offer
items.value: Representative counts from Rundowns: PMP 36 seats (11 September, 25 October); SHRM-CP 20 total with 10 reserved for military spouses; AI/ML course 25-30 seats; AWS course at least 25; Python course 50-plus; Scrum cohorts of 30. An August Certified ScrumMaster class was full and the October cohort was mostly filled.
items.how: Apply the same week you hear the announcement, not later.
items.hack: Scarcity, not eligibility, is the real constraint. With 20-50 seats against a 77,000-member community, speed beats qualifications. Attend the Rundown live, submit before Tuesday, and have a second choice ready.
items.deadline: Rolling; cohorts fill within weeks

items.title: Credly — where your ANE-earned credentials actually live
items.who: Anyone earning certifications through ANE partners
items.value: ANE directs members to Credly as the digital credential platform holding their badges and certification transcripts.
items.how: Create a Credly account with the same email you used for the certification, and claim badges when issued.
items.hack: Claim the badge the week it is issued and add it to LinkedIn from Credly directly — it posts with a verification link recruiters can click. An unclaimed badge is invisible to employers and expires out of your inbox.
items.deadline: Claim promptly after issuance

items.title: Vets in Tech — free certification tracks with exam vouchers included
items.who: Veterans and military spouses
items.value: Free courses with testing vouchers. ANE-cited tracks: PMP (36 seats, voucher included), Security+, a four-week basic Python course (four nights a week, two hours a night, ~32 hours, 50+ seats), an AI/ML course (25-30 seats), and an AWS course (25+ seats).
items.how: Apply through VetsinTech or via the openings announced in ANE's Weekly Rundown.
items.hack: The PMP track includes the exam voucher, which is the expensive part of PMP. But it requires an approved PMI application first, with three to five years of project experience documented — start the PMI application before the cohort opens or you will not make the cut.
items.deadline: Cohort-based; September and October intakes cited in 2025

items.title: Vets in Tech pitch contest — $40,000 in non-diluting funds
items.who: Veteran-owned small businesses
items.value: A pitch competition with $40,000 total in non-diluting funds: $25,000 first place, $10,000 second, $5,000 third.
items.how: Enter through VetsinTech when the contest cycle opens; ANE announces rounds in the Weekly Rundown.
items.hack: Non-diluting means you keep all your equity — this is a grant, not an investment. For a veteran-owned business that is strictly better than the same amount from an investor, and veteran-only pools are far less competitive than open startup competitions.
items.deadline: Cycle-based; a 2025 round had an August 12 event with submissions due August 16

items.title: Empower — free CompTIA A+ and Google IT Support training with job placement
items.who: Veterans, military spouses, transitioning service members, National Guard, Reservists; a dependent/college-student track was cited for ages 18-24
items.value: Free tech training, certifications and job placement. ANE-cited tracks: CompTIA A+ and Google IT Support.
items.how: Apply through Empower; ANE's Rundown team makes referrals.
items.hack: Empower is state-restricted. ANE cited roughly ten states: California, New York, Texas, Maryland, New Jersey, Virginia, Michigan, North Carolina, Missouri, Ohio and Oregon — and specifically noted Florida is not among them. Check your state before investing time.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Empower's 18-24 track — one of the few routes open to dependents
items.who: Military dependents and college students aged 18-24 (Ohio and North Carolina cited)
items.value: ANE cited an Empower opportunity open to children aged 18-24 and college students, in Ohio and North Carolina.
items.how: Ask the ANE Rundown team for the current dependent-eligible referral.
items.hack: Dependents are excluded from most of ANE's catalog, including Coursera historically. This age-banded track is a genuine exception — if you have a college-age child in a covered state, this is one of the few ANE-adjacent doors actually open to them.
items.deadline: Rolling; state-limited

items.title: Per Scholas — free tech training for the military community
items.who: Veterans and military-affiliated adults
items.value: Named repeatedly in ANE Rundowns as a free certification and training provider in tech, alongside CompTIA, AWS and PMP pathways.
items.how: Apply directly to Per Scholas; ANE refers members to it.
items.hack: Per Scholas is a long-established national nonprofit with physical campuses and employer hiring partners, which makes it more durable than many of the offers that cycle through the Rundown. Worth applying to independently of ANE.
items.deadline: Rolling cohorts

items.title: Vets Transition Support — the gateway to free Coursera, plus Lean Six Sigma and OSHA
items.who: Military community
items.value: Described in ANE Rundowns as the gateway organization for free Coursera access, and as offering Lean Six Sigma and OSHA certifications.
items.how: Register through the Coursera path ANE distributes; ask about the Six Sigma and OSHA tracks separately.
items.hack: This is the organization actually doing the Coursera verification behind ANE's offer, which explains the one-to-three-week wait. Its own Lean Six Sigma and OSHA certifications are separate offers most ANE members never notice — ask about them while your Coursera request processes.
items.deadline: Rolling; Coursera verification 1-3 weeks

items.title: Cloud Veterans — free cloud certifications, open to family members
items.who: Service members, spouses and family members
items.value: Free cloud certifications. ANE cited a wait of roughly six months.
items.how: Apply through Cloud Veterans; expect a queue.
items.hack: Two things make this notable: family members are explicitly eligible, which is rare, and the roughly six-month wait means you apply now for a certification you will start next year. Get in the queue early and pursue something else meanwhile.
items.deadline: Rolling; ~6-month wait cited

items.title: Onward to Opportunity (IVMF) — still free, but the catalog has shrunk
items.who: Service members, veterans and military spouses
items.value: ANE's Rundown team said the O2O certification catalog had contracted from roughly 70 offerings to about 35-40.
items.how: Apply through IVMF's Onward to Opportunity.
items.hack: This is a concrete, dated warning worth heeding: guides still advertising '30+ free certifications' through O2O may be describing a larger catalog than exists today. Verify the specific certification you want is still offered before building a plan on it.
items.deadline: Rolling cohorts

items.title: SANS Academy, Climb Higher and Scrum Booster — additional free training partners
items.org: SANS Institute Academies / Climb Higher / Scrum Booster
items.who: Veterans and military spouses (varies by provider)
items.value: Named in ANE Rundowns among free certification and training providers. Climb Higher was cited alongside Vets in Tech and Empower as offering free CompTIA A+ or Security+ routes.
items.how: Ask the ANE Rundown team which of these is currently accepting applications.
items.hack: SANS Academies are the highest-value item in this group by a wide margin — SANS/GIAC training is among the most expensive in cybersecurity, and its veteran academies are full-scholarship but highly competitive with fixed application windows. Set a calendar reminder rather than waiting for ANE to mention it.
items.deadline: Application windows vary by provider

items.title: Modern States — free CLEP exam funding, and it covers spouses and dependents
items.who: Military members, spouses and dependents
items.value: ANE cites Modern States as funding CLEP exams for the military community including dependents, provided most of the associated coursework is completed.
items.how: Take the free Modern States course, then request the voucher that covers the CLEP exam fee.
items.hack: This is the cheapest college credit in existence and one of the very few ANE-promoted resources that explicitly includes dependents. Each CLEP can retire a whole course — stacking several before enrolling preserves GI Bill months for upper-division work.
items.deadline: Rolling; complete coursework first

items.title: Boots to Books — scholarship up to $1,000 toward certifications such as CISSP
items.who: Veterans and military community members
items.value: ANE cited a scholarship of up to $1,000 for certifications including CISSP, and also mentioned Google Analytics certification support. Offered only periodically.
items.how: Apply when a cycle opens; ANE announces rounds in the Weekly Rundown.
items.hack: CISSP is the expensive certification ANE's free cohorts mostly do not cover — the Rundown team said CISSP costs roughly two to three times other certifications and that a voucher-only path was still being raised with the board. Boots to Books is the practical workaround while that remains unresolved.
items.deadline: Periodic cycles; no standing deadline

items.title: American College — financial services certifications
items.org: The American College of Financial Services
items.who: Military community members entering financial services
items.value: Named in ANE Rundowns as a source of financial services certifications for the military community.
items.how: Ask the ANE team for the current referral path.
items.hack: The American College runs well-known military scholarship programs for designations like ChFC and CFP coursework. For anyone moving into financial planning — a common second career for veterans — this is a far cheaper route than self-funding the designations.
items.deadline: Varies

items.title: The MWR Digital Library — the free benefit ANE calls the one you are sleeping on
items.who: Active duty, reserves, National Guard, retirees, Medal of Honor recipients and eligible family members
items.value: Free access to a bundle ANE describes as worth 'thousands of dollars': ebooks, audiobooks, newspapers and magazines (Wall Street Journal, National Geographic, The Economist), genealogy, language learning, live tutoring and technical certification prep.
items.how: Log in to the MWR Digital Library with your military credentials.
items.hack: ANE devoted an entire Rundown to this because almost nobody uses it. It costs nothing, requires no application, no code, no cohort and no waitlist — the only ANE-promoted resource with zero gatekeeping. Retirees are explicitly included.
items.deadline: None — standing benefit

items.title: MWR's O'Reilly Media access — certification prep with practice labs and exams
items.org: O'Reilly Media via MWR Digital Library
items.who: MWR-eligible: active duty, reserves, Guard, retirees and eligible family members
items.value: Full O'Reilly library covering data, databases, analytics, cybersecurity, AI and technology, including certification prep with practice labs and practice exams.
items.how: Access O'Reilly through the MWR Digital Library portal.
items.hack: This is the highest-value item hiding inside MWR. An O'Reilly individual subscription is a substantial recurring cost, and the practice labs are the part that actually gets people through cloud and security exams. Use it to prepare for the exams ANE's vouchers will pay for.
items.deadline: None — standing benefit

items.title: Tutor.com military edition — free live tutoring for military families
items.who: Military families: children and adults, elementary through college level
items.value: Free live, on-demand tutoring, available 24/7, from elementary through college level.
items.how: Access the military edition of Tutor.com through the MWR Digital Library or Military OneSource.
items.hack: It covers adults too, not just children. If you are taking a certification course or college class and stall on the math, you have free 24/7 tutoring already paid for. Members routinely use it for their kids and never realize it works for them.
items.deadline: None — standing benefit

items.title: Mango Languages — 70+ languages free through MWR
items.org: Mango Languages via MWR Digital Library
items.who: MWR-eligible members and families
items.value: Free access to Mango Languages covering more than 70 languages.
items.how: Access via the MWR Digital Library.
items.hack: Pair this with a PCS. Starting the language three to six months before an overseas move, for the whole family, costs nothing and is one of the few genuinely useful things you can do during the waiting phase of orders.
items.deadline: None — standing benefit

items.title: Ancestry.com and Fold3 — free military records research through MWR
items.org: Ancestry.com and Fold3 via MWR Digital Library
items.who: MWR-eligible members and families
items.value: Free access for researching family and military service records.
items.how: Access via the MWR Digital Library.
items.hack: Fold3 holds digitized military service records. Beyond genealogy, it can surface documentation of a relative's service that helps with survivor benefits, cemetery eligibility or a lineage-based organization application.
items.deadline: None — standing benefit

items.title: Candorful — free mock interviews with real practice rounds
items.who: Veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses
items.value: Free interview preparation; ANE cited three practice interviews with feedback.
items.how: Register with Candorful directly, or through ANE's referral.
items.hack: Three recorded practice rounds with working professionals is the fastest fix for the single biggest veteran interview problem: translating military work into civilian language. Do this before, not after, you start applying.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: VetSec — a 7,000+ member veteran cybersecurity community
items.who: Veterans and military spouses in or entering cybersecurity
items.value: A free community of roughly 7,000-8,000 veterans and spouses, organized around a Slack workspace with channels for cyber intelligence, cloud and AI.
items.how: Join VetSec and get into the Slack workspace.
items.hack: The Slack is where unadvertised cyber roles and voucher offers circulate first. For anyone pursuing Security+, Splunk or CISSP through ANE, VetSec is the peer network that turns the certification into an actual job referral.
items.deadline: None — ongoing

items.title: The Commit Foundation — one-on-one transition mentorship
items.who: Transitioning service members and veterans
items.value: Free one-on-one transition mentorship, named in ANE Rundowns among mentorship resources.
items.how: Apply directly to The Commit Foundation.
items.hack: Commit runs intensive one-on-one workshops rather than group webinars, and is selective. It suits senior enlisted and officers with a specific target industry better than the broad platforms — a different tool than MilMentor, not a duplicate.
items.deadline: Application-based

items.title: American Corporate Partners (ACP) — free year-long mentorship
items.who: Veterans and military spouses
items.value: Free mentorship platform connecting the military community with industry professionals; named alongside MilMentor in ANE's transition episode.
items.how: Apply through ACP.
items.hack: ACP assigns one mentor for a full year, which is structurally different from MilMentor's one-off calls. Run both: ACP for sustained guidance, MilMentor for breadth across companies.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Vetforce / VertForce — military spouse and veteran-owned remote job board with employer events
items.who: Military spouses and veterans
items.value: A remote-focused job board, military spouse and veteran-owned, with recurring employer events. ANE cited employers including Imagine360, CVS Health, Intuit TurboTax and Travelers Insurance, plus live streams on Tuesdays at noon Pacific.
items.how: Register on the VertForce job board and attend its employer events.
items.hack: The employer events are the real product — each one is a named company showing up specifically for military-affiliated candidates, which beats cold-applying. The Tuesday noon Pacific live stream is where new openings are announced.
items.deadline: Recurring; events announced per employer

items.title: NLx — the job board for overseas and national labor exchange roles
items.who: Service members, veterans and spouses, including those stationed overseas
items.value: A job board named in ANE's transition episode as a source for overseas roles.
items.how: Search NLx directly.
items.hack: NLx aggregates verified employer-direct postings rather than scraped reposts, which cuts out the ghost-job problem. It is one of the few places to find legitimate postings for jobs located overseas, useful for spouses PCSing abroad.
items.deadline: None

items.title: MSEP Career Accelerator — 90-day paid fellowship placements for military spouses
items.who: Military spouses
items.value: A 90-day fellowship placement program for military spouses, named in ANE's transition episode alongside MSEP.
items.how: Apply through the DoD MSEP Career Accelerator.
items.hack: A 90-day fellowship solves the military spouse resume gap problem directly: it gives you a current, name-brand employer on your resume and frequently converts to a permanent offer. Among the highest-leverage spouse programs ANE points to.
items.deadline: Cohort-based

items.title: Free professional headshots and interview wardrobe
items.who: ANE members, particularly cohort participants
items.value: ANE provides free professional headshots, and a tailored business suit for 3 CERT participants, alongside resume help and mock interviews.
items.how: Ask at the Weekly Rundown or through your cohort.
items.hack: A current professional headshot measurably lifts LinkedIn profile response, and ANE gives them away. Combine the free headshot with the Career Compass LinkedIn optimizer in the same week for the largest single improvement to your online presence.
items.deadline: Event and cohort-based

items.title: Free LinkedIn Premium access
items.who: Cited for active duty in an ANE Rundown; confirm current eligibility
items.value: ANE listed free LinkedIn Premium among the resources it surfaces, described in a July 2025 Rundown as being for active duty.
items.how: Ask in the Weekly Rundown for the current LinkedIn Premium path.
items.hack: LinkedIn has long run a free Premium year for service members and veterans through Military OneSource. If ANE's route is closed, go to Military OneSource directly rather than paying — and time the free year to start when you begin job hunting, not before.
items.deadline: Confirm current availability

items.title: Military Influencer Conference — ANE has covered the ticket cost
items.org: Military Influencer Conference + ACT NOW Education
items.who: ANE members selected for sponsorship
items.value: ANE covered MIC ticket costs for members for a September 21-24 event in Atlanta; attendees paid their own airfare, lodging and food.
items.how: Watch for the sponsorship announcement in the Weekly Rundown or newsletter.
items.hack: Note exactly what is and is not covered: the ticket only. Budget airfare, hotel and meals before accepting, and share a room with another sponsored member — several ANE members coordinate this in the Facebook group.
items.deadline: Annual; tied to conference dates

items.title: ANE Summit — where certifications are given away at scale
items.who: ANE members who attend
items.value: ANE's summits are its largest giveaway events. A 2025 summit distributed a reported 535 certifications and certificates total, including 262-263 personal certificates, plus four laptops, Visa gift cards, a PlayStation and a MacBook. ANE separately reported 504 certifications issued in a single week, mostly AWS and CompTIA. ANE said roughly $100,000 was raised toward certifications.
items.how: Register for the summit when announced; ANE has run winter and annual summits.
items.hack: The summit is the single highest-expected-value event ANE runs — hundreds of certifications issued at once instead of 20-seat cohorts. If you attend nothing else all year, attend the summit.
items.deadline: Event-based; a 2026 summit was referenced as upcoming

items.title: Self-directed IRA benefit — offered to roughly 50 members
items.who: ANE members who requested it
items.value: ANE announced self-directed IRA funding for about 50 people, with a first-year annual fee covered by the provider. No dollar amount was published.
items.how: Request it on the ANE form when announced; wait for ANE to coordinate rather than contacting the provider directly.
items.hack: ANE specifically told members not to contact the provider directly — doing so breaks the coordinated batch. This pattern holds across ANE's partner offers: always go through ANE, never around it, or you forfeit the nonprofit rate.
items.deadline: Capped at ~50; batch-based

items.title: Virtual hiring fairs with employers recruiting military-affiliated candidates
items.who: Military community members seeking employment
items.value: ANE runs virtual hiring fairs; an August 29 fair was cited featuring employers actively hiring military-affiliated candidates. The Service to Success cohort concludes in a hiring fair.
items.how: Register through ANE when a fair is announced.
items.hack: Employers at these fairs are pre-filtered for wanting military-affiliated hires, so your background is an asset rather than something you must explain. Bring the ANE headshot, the Career Compass-optimized resume and the Candorful practice rounds — the three together are what the fair is designed to convert.
items.deadline: Event-based

items.title: Dog Tag Inc — veteran entrepreneurship fellowship taught by Georgetown faculty
items.who: Veterans, military spouses and caregivers
items.value: An entrepreneurship program ANE names among its business resources, delivered in person at Washington, DC facilities with instruction from a Georgetown University professor.
items.how: Apply directly to Dog Tag Inc.
items.hack: Dog Tag's fellowship carries a Georgetown business certificate, which is a credential rather than just a workshop. It is in-person in DC, so it is realistic only for the National Capital Region — but for those there it is among the strongest veteran entrepreneurship programs.
items.deadline: Cohort-based; in-person DC

items.title: Service to Schools, Warriors to Scholars and Posse — the selective-college route
items.org: Service to School / Warrior-Scholar Project / Posse Foundation
items.who: Enlisted veterans and transitioning service members pursuing degrees
items.value: Named in ANE Rundowns as college access and opportunity programs.
items.how: Apply directly to each; all are free to applicants.
items.hack: These exist to get enlisted veterans into selective colleges, which is a different goal than finishing a degree cheaply. Service to School provides free application mentorship, the Warrior-Scholar Project runs academic boot camps on campus, and the Posse Veterans Program places veterans at top universities with full scholarships. Use them before applying, not after.
items.deadline: Application cycles vary; generally annual

items.title: AWS is actively recruiting veterans and spouses into data center roles
items.who: Veterans and military spouses
items.value: ANE reported AWS actively hiring veterans and military spouses for data center roles, with some positions offering security clearance opportunities. AWS also ran in-person and monthly virtual training, with Seattle cited as a hub.
items.how: Apply through AWS military recruiting; pursue AWS certification vouchers through ANE's partner challenges.
items.hack: The clearance angle is the differentiator. If you are leaving with an active clearance, data center roles that sponsor or require one let you monetize the clearance immediately — pair it with a free AWS associate certification and you are an unusually strong candidate.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Security clearance pathways — ANE dedicated a Rundown to positioning for cleared work
items.who: Service members and veterans with or eligible for clearances
items.value: A March 2025 Weekly Rundown (about 1 hour 54 minutes) in which the founder broke down clearance levels, requirements and how to position for clearance-eligible roles. ANE cited a cleared full-stack developer role in Maryland at $200,000-$240,000.
items.how: Listen to the Security Clearance Pathways episode in the ANE podcast archive.
items.hack: Your clearance is a depreciating asset — it stays reinstatable for a limited window after you separate. The cleared salary premium is real, and ANE's own example was a $200,000-$240,000 Maryland role. Target cleared work first, while the clearance is current.
items.deadline: None; archived episode

items.title: AI tools ANE teaches members to use for translating military experience
items.who: Transitioning service members and veterans
items.value: ANE Rundowns coach members to use ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Google NotebookLM to translate military experience into civilian job requirements, and shared NotebookLM tutorials with the community.
