items.how: Free tiers of each tool suffice; ANE shared written tutorials and a video walkthrough.
items.hack: The specific technique is the useful part: paste a civilian job description alongside your evaluations or award citations and have the model map one onto the other. NotebookLM is the better choice because it grounds answers in the documents you upload rather than inventing accomplishments.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Branch COOL programs — the government-funded route ANE points members back to
items.org: Army COOL / Navy COOL / Air Force COOL / Marine Corps COOL
items.who: Active duty service members (and in some cases reservists and Guard)
items.value: ANE's transition episode directs members to their service's COOL program for funded civilian credentials mapped to their military occupation.
items.how: Search your branch's COOL site for credentials mapped to your rating, MOS or AFSC, and apply through your command for funding.
items.hack: COOL pays for the exam and often the training while you are still in uniform, with no cohort, no lottery and no weekly code. Exhaust COOL before chasing ANE's scarce 20-seat batches — ANE's own team sends people here first.
items.deadline: While still serving; before separation

items.title: How to actually use ANE: the five-step sequence
items.who: Anyone new to ANE
items.value: The access path ANE and independent coverage both describe: (1) join the free Weekly Rundown, (2) build a roadmap in Career Compass, (3) connect with a mentor through MilMentor, (4) attend action-based events such as resume reviews, certification workshops and career fairs, (5) use partner college and university career centers.
items.how: Work the steps in order, starting with one Saturday Rundown.
items.hack: Step one is load-bearing and the rest are not reachable without it. Browsing the website first is the mistake almost everyone makes — the site is largely a set of landing pages, and the substance lives in the live session, the newsletter and the Facebook group.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Partner college and university career centers — access without enrolling
items.who: Military-affiliated professionals
items.value: ANE describes strategic partnerships with colleges and universities giving military-affiliated members access to campus career centers and internal job boards, plus joint events and workshops.
items.how: Ask ANE which institutions are currently partnered and how to get access.
items.hack: Internal university job boards are not public and carry postings that never reach Indeed or LinkedIn. Getting access without being an enrolled student is a genuinely unusual benefit — ask explicitly which schools are live, because ANE does not publish the list.
items.deadline: Varies by institution

items.title: Navy Federal membership — the full eligible list, including veterans of any era and their grandparents
items.who: Active duty Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard, National Guard and Space Force; Delayed Entry Program enlistees; DoD Officer Candidate/ROTC participants; DoD Reservists; veterans, retirees and annuitants (no era limit and no minimum time in service stated); DoD civilian employees; U.S. Government employees assigned to DoD installations; DoD contractors assigned to U.S. Government installations; DoD civilian retirees and annuitants. Family: parents, grandparents, spouses, siblings, children (including adopted and stepchildren), grandchildren, and household members of anyone in any category above.
items.value: Access to the largest credit union in the world, with no-fee checking, ATM rebates and military-specific loan products. Membership costs $5 and is permanent once established.
items.how: Apply online or at a branch. Open a Membership Savings Account with a $5 minimum balance, which must be maintained to keep membership. You need the sponsoring relative's or your own service details.
items.hack: The family path is the widest in military banking: because veterans of any era qualify and eligibility flows up to parents and grandparents as well as down to grandchildren, a single veteran in a family makes three generations eligible. Most people assume it is active-duty-only and never check.
items.deadline: None — open enrollment

items.title: If one relative served, you can join Navy Federal — the veteran family-member route
items.who: Parents, grandparents, spouses, siblings, children (including adopted children and stepchildren), grandchildren, and household members of a veteran. The veteran does not have to be a Navy Federal member themselves and does not have to be living, per the published family-member categories.
items.value: Full membership for civilians with no service of their own — the same rates, the same ATM network, the same no-fee accounts.
items.how: Use the 'Family Members of Veterans' application path and supply the veteran relative's service information. $5 opens the membership savings account.
items.hack: 'Household member' is a separate and broader category than 'family member' — a roommate or domestic partner sharing the residence of an eligible member can qualify without any blood relation.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Navy Federal Free Active Duty Checking — $240 a year in ATM rebates and pay a day early
items.who: Active duty, retired service members and reservists who are Navy Federal members and set up qualifying military direct deposit. A qualifying military direct deposit must post within 180 days of opening or the account converts to Free EveryDay Checking; if military direct deposits stop for more than 180 days it also converts.
items.value: No monthly service fee, no minimum balance, ATM fee rebates of up to $20.00 per statement period (Navy Federal states this adds up to $240 a year), free personalized military checks, 0.05% dividend rate / 0.05% APY, and military pay available a full business day before the regular posting date.
items.how: Open Free Active Duty Checking and route your DFAS net pay to it via myPay. Check Navy Federal's Military Active Duty posting calendar for the exact early-availability date each month.
items.hack: The $20-per-statement-period rebate is per account, so it is worth more to a heavy out-of-network ATM user than almost any 'free ATM network' claim. If you withdraw cash on a base without a Navy Federal ATM, the rebate is effectively a $240 annual raise.
items.deadline: Direct deposit must post within 180 days of opening

items.title: Navy Federal's 0.25% APR military discount is not automatic — you have to ask for it
items.who: Active duty and retired military members of Navy Federal with military direct deposit to a Navy Federal account.
items.value: A 0.25% APR discount on select loans. On a $35,000 five-year auto loan that is roughly a couple of hundred dollars of interest, and more on larger balances.
items.how: Navy Federal states that members must call or visit a branch to receive the discount — it is not applied to a straight online application. Ask for it by name before the loan is funded. The offer may expire at any time.
items.hack: This is the single most commonly forfeited benefit at Navy Federal, because the online application path does not surface it. Apply online to get the decision, then phone before closing and ask for the active-duty rate reduction.
items.deadline: Offer may expire at any time; must be requested before funding

items.title: Navy Federal Emergency Relief Loan — up to $5,000 for members deployed to conflict regions
items.who: Navy Federal members who are service members, or members living in conflict regions overseas, per Navy Federal's deployment page.
items.value: An Emergency Relief Loan of up to $5,000. This is a loan, not a grant — it is repaid. Navy Federal also states it is waiving certain account fees for eligible members on request.
items.how: Apply at a branch, by phone, or using Navy Federal's international phone number list. Request fee waivers separately by phone, at a branch, or by eMessage.
items.hack: The fee waiver is request-only. Deploying members routinely eat wire, stop-payment and statement fees that Navy Federal will waive if asked by eMessage — which works from a ship or a forward location where a phone call does not.
items.deadline: Tied to deployment/conflict-region status

items.title: Navy Federal Career Kickoff Loan — 0.75% APR up to $36,000 for service academy juniors and seniors
items.who: Juniors and seniors at the Air Force Academy, Coast Guard Academy, Merchant Marine Academy, West Point or the Naval Academy who are Navy Federal members. Graduates are not eligible, so the window closes at commissioning.
items.value: 0.75% APR on a 60-month loan of up to $36,000, with repayment deferrable until 90 days after graduation. Navy Federal's own disclosure example: a $36,000 loan carries a $1,218 total finance charge, a $620.30 monthly payment and $37,218 total repaid.
items.how: Apply as a Navy Federal member while still a junior or senior. You must keep a Navy Federal checking account with direct deposit of military pay for the life of the loan — otherwise the rate converts to the prevailing personal loan rate.
items.hack: At 0.75% this is below the risk-free rate on a Treasury bill in most environments, which makes it one of the few genuinely positive-carry consumer loans in existence. The trap is the direct-deposit condition: let the DFAS deposit lapse and the rate repricing wipes out the advantage.
items.deadline: Must apply before graduation; junior/senior years only

items.title: Navy Federal Dollars for Doers goes to nonprofits, not to members — do not apply expecting cash
items.who: Nonprofit organizations nominated by Navy Federal employees who volunteer there. Not members, and not individuals.
items.value: $1,000 per nominated nonprofit. Navy Federal has reported 100 organizations supported in a year, totalling $100,000.
items.how: A Navy Federal employee nominates the nonprofit. There is no member-facing application.
items.hack: If you run or sit on the board of a military-family nonprofit, the lever is not an application form — it is finding a Navy Federal employee who already volunteers with you, or recruiting one. Navy Federal gives employees 8 hours of paid volunteer leave, so the supply of volunteers is real.
items.deadline: Annual employee nomination cycle

items.title: USAA membership — narrower than Navy Federal, and it does not pass to in-laws or grandparents
items.who: Historically: active, retired and honorably separated officers and enlisted of all U.S. service branches; officer candidates in commissioning programs (service academies, ROTC, OCS/OTS); and the spouses, widows, widowers and children of USAA members. The key structural difference from a credit union is that USAA eligibility descends from a member — children of USAA members qualify — but it does not ascend to the member's parents or grandparents, and it does not reach siblings. USAA's own eligibility page could not be read in this session (it returns a cookie-wall error to automated requests), so confirm your exact category at usaa.com/membership or by phone before assuming.
items.value: Banking, insurance, investments and retirement under one roof, with the military-specific underwriting that makes USAA auto and renters insurance competitive for a population that moves and deploys. Membership itself has no fee.
items.how: Apply at usaa.com/membership with your DD-214, orders or commissioning documentation; family members apply by naming the member they descend from.
items.hack: Because eligibility flows down from a member and not up, enrolling an eligible veteran parent or grandparent first is what unlocks it for the children. Families that skip a generation of USAA membership permanently lose the path for everyone below them — so get the eligible service member enrolled even if they will never use the accounts.
items.deadline: None, but the descent rule means delay can foreclose the family path

items.title: USAA Educational Foundation — free financial education with no membership and nothing sold to you
items.who: The Foundation describes itself as serving military families and does not state a membership or eligibility requirement, so treat it as open. It is a separate nonprofit from USAA the insurer and bank.
items.value: Free financial education resources from experts in personal finance and military life. The Foundation explicitly states it does not endorse or sell any product — which makes it one of the few military financial-education sources with no sales motive attached.
items.how: Use the resources and learning management system at usaaef.org. No account, membership or purchase required.
items.hack: Because the Foundation is prohibited from selling, its material is safe to hand to a junior service member whom you do not want steered into a product. Contrast that with the 'free financial seminar' on base that ends in a life insurance application.
items.deadline: None

items.title: PenFed is open to literally anyone — no military affiliation required
items.who: Anyone of age. PenFed states in its own FAQ: 'Anyone of age can join. No military affiliation required.' Its membership application lists military, DoD, DHS, NOAA, USPHS, Reserve/National Guard, immediate family of a member, American Red Cross volunteers and employees, and association routes (ASMC, CGAuxA, MOAA, NAUS, VFW, ROA, Navy League, USAWOA) — but the catch-all 'anyone' route means none of those are necessary.
items.value: Nationwide credit union membership with military-grade rates for a $5 share deposit, available to a civilian with no connection to the military at all. PenFed reports over 1.4 million members worldwide.
items.how: Apply at penfed.org and fund a Regular Share (savings) account with a $5 minimum balance. PenFed also creates membership automatically if you apply for and take a loan — you do not need to be a member to apply.
items.hack: PenFed's 'Pentagon Federal' name does more to deter eligible people than any membership rule. Civilians, contractors with no DoD tie, and family members who assume they are shut out are PenFed's own largest missed market. The $5 share is refundable when you close.
items.deadline: None

items.title: PenFed Access America Checking — a $15 monthly fee that is trivially easy to kill
items.who: Any PenFed member. Opening requires a minimum balance of $25.
items.value: Dividend-earning checking on balances up to $50,000. The $15 monthly fee is waived by either a monthly direct deposit of $500 or more, or a daily balance of $500 or more — one or the other, not both. Dividends require recurring direct deposits of $500 or more.
items.how: Open with $25, then either set a $500+ recurring direct deposit (a single military pay deposit clears this easily) or park $500. Fee-free access at PenFed, Allpoint and Co-op ATMs; the ATM owner may still surcharge out-of-network.
items.hack: A junior enlisted member's semi-monthly DFAS deposit clears the $500 direct-deposit test on its own, so the $15 fee should never be paid by anyone on military pay. Verify the current APY tier before you move money — PenFed's rate did not render on the page in this session and it is variable.
items.deadline: Fee assessed monthly until a waiver condition is met

items.title: PenFed's actual fee schedule — the numbers to compare against your current bank
items.who: All PenFed members; fees vary by account type.
items.value: Verified from PenFed's published service fees: foreign transaction fee up to 2% of the transaction amount on most checking and savings accounts; non-PenFed ATM withdrawal $1.50; non-PenFed ATM balance inquiry $1.00; non-sufficient funds $30.00; uncollected funds $10.00; domestic wire $30.00; international wire $35.00; stop payment on an individual check $20.00. Free: Free Checking monthly service charge, first 40 checks, official checks of $500 or more, ACH transfers initiated at PenFed.org, and PenFed ATM use for Complete Access, Access America and Free Checking.
items.how: Compare line by line against your current institution's schedule. Route recurring ACH transfers through PenFed.org rather than the receiving bank's pull to land in the $0 column.
items.hack: The 2% foreign transaction fee is the figure OCONUS members miss. If you are stationed in Europe or Japan, a PenFed debit card is the wrong card at the point of sale — pair it with a no-foreign-fee card and use PenFed for the domestic side. Fees change; confirm at the link before relying on any number here.
items.deadline: None — schedule changes without notice, verify current

items.title: PenFed Foundation Veteran Entrepreneur Program — free, pays your travel, and gives you no money
items.who: A veteran or military spouse who is the majority owner of the business. Up to two founders may participate. Industry agnostic, with priority to national security and defense businesses. Non-veteran co-founders may attend but must cover their own expenses. Three tracks: Incubator (idea stage, no minimum viable product or customers needed — explicitly including lifestyle, franchise and local service businesses), Accelerator (established companies with customers, traction or scalable potential), and Bootcamp (short intensive for active-duty members or spouses considering entrepreneurship before transition).
items.value: No cost to participate in either program. For the Accelerator the Foundation covers travel including economy flights, hotel and meals; the Incubator covers all meals. What you get is mentorship and access to an investor network — more than 120 founders supported since 2018, with alumni raising early capital through that network. The program page does not state that the Foundation itself grants or invests money, and does not mention taking equity.
items.how: Apply through penfedfoundation.org/our-programs/vep/. Pick the track honestly — applying to the Accelerator without customers wastes a cycle when the Incubator is the designed entry point.
items.hack: The Incubator explicitly accepts franchise and local service businesses, which almost every other veteran accelerator screens out in favour of tech. If you are opening a trades business, a franchise or a local services company, this is one of the few serious programs that will take you.
items.deadline: Cohort-based — check current application windows

items.title: PenFed Foundation Military Heroes Program — money moves to nonprofits, not to you directly
items.who: The Foundation describes the program as partnering with nonprofits serving military communities to meet service members' and families' needs and ease the transition to civilian life. The money flows to partner nonprofits, which then serve individuals; the program page does not publish individual eligibility criteria.
items.value: The Foundation reports over $50 million in total support to the military community over 25 years. Named grants to partner organisations are the delivery mechanism.
items.how: As an individual, find which partner nonprofit in your area receives Military Heroes funding and apply to that nonprofit. As an organisation, approach the Foundation about partnership.
items.hack: Distinguish this from the Foundation's separate emergency-assistance channel. People apply to the Military Heroes Program for rent money and get nowhere, because it is a grants-to-grantees program. Ask the Foundation which downstream partner handles direct individual assistance in your region.
items.deadline: Rolling partner cycles

items.title: Armed Forces Bank is a bank, not a credit union — and civilians can open accounts too
items.who: Not restricted to the military. Armed Forces Bank states it serves 'active and retired military and civilian clients' in all 50 states and those deployed worldwide. There is no membership, no field of membership and no share to buy — it is an FDIC-insured national bank, so you simply open an account.
items.value: On-base and near-base branch presence combined with nationwide account opening, FDIC insurance rather than NCUA share insurance, and military-specific products (early pay, recruit checking) without any eligibility gate.
items.how: Open online or at a branch. Products have their own minimums — Access Freedom Checking opens with $25.
items.hack: Because it is a bank with no field of membership, Armed Forces Bank is the fallback when a service member's family member cannot establish credit-union eligibility anywhere. It is also the answer for a recruit at basic training who needs an account opened before they have orders or a DoD ID.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Armed Forces Bank Military Early Pay — one business day, no paperwork, no fee
items.who: Anyone with an Armed Forces Bank checking or savings account receiving military direct deposit. If you already have one, no further steps are needed.
items.value: Military direct deposit funds available one business day before the set pay date. No paperwork and no charge. Maximum ACH credit of $15,000.
items.how: Set up direct deposit through your servicing payroll office or myPay using Armed Forces Bank routing number 101108319. The early release then happens automatically.
items.hack: Early pay is not a product you sign up for anywhere — it is a consequence of the bank releasing the DFAS ACH file as soon as it arrives rather than waiting for the settlement date. Any institution that chooses to can do it; the ones that do not are simply keeping a day of float. That is the real question to ask a prospective bank.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Armed Forces Bank Access Freedom Checking — $0 monthly, but watch the paper statement and early-closure fees
items.who: Marketed to military members and their families; the product page does not state a restrictive eligibility requirement. Requires eStatements.
items.value: $0 monthly service charge, no minimum balance, $25 minimum opening deposit, 40,000+ no-fee ATMs nationwide, and no fees for withdrawals, transfers, balance inquiries or denied transactions at MoneyPass Network ATMs in the U.S. with a MoneyPass-logo card. Free overdraft protection when linked to a savings account.
items.how: Open with $25 and keep eStatements on. Link a savings account to get the free overdraft protection transfer.
items.hack: Two fees bite people here: $5 a month if you switch to paper statements, and a $25 early closure fee if you close within 90 days of opening. If you are account-shopping, open and test for more than 90 days before you move on, or the $25 cancels out the first few months of savings.
items.deadline: Early closure fee applies within 90 days of opening

items.title: Service Credit Union — anyone can join free via the American Consumer Council, promo code 'Service'
items.who: Active duty military members and veterans plus their families; current and former Department of Defense employees plus their families; employees or members of a Workplace Partner (select employer group); OR anyone who joins the American Consumer Council for free (promo code 'Service') or the Financial Fitness Association, which Service CU says it will help you join for free if you are not already a member. The association routes mean there is no real eligibility barrier.
items.value: A credit union with 37 U.S. branches, branches on 14 military bases in Germany, and access to more than 5,000 shared branches worldwide — reachable by any American through a free association membership. $5 initial deposit.
items.how: Apply at servicecu.org, select the American Consumer Council route and use promo code 'Service', or take the Financial Fitness Association route and let Service CU enrol you. Fund the share account with $5.
items.hack: The ACC promo code is the whole trick. Service CU's distinctive products — the 10% APY deployed savings account and the German on-base branch network — are reachable by a civilian spouse or a veteran with no current affiliation, for free, in minutes.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Service Credit Union's 10% APY Deployed Warrior Savings — a second combat-zone 10% account beyond SDP
items.who: Active duty service members deployed to a combat zone as Service CU defines it, who provide deployment orders and have net military pay direct deposited to a Service CU account. eCommunications required. No minimum balance to open.
items.value: 10% APY on balances up to $10,000. Balances above $10,000 earn a variable rate stated as 10% down to 0.10%. Monthly deposits cannot exceed your monthly net military pay and may come from direct deposit, an allotment, or a transfer from a Service CU account. The 10% APY stops at the end of the month of your return date plus 120 days. Rates were stated as accurate 07/01/2025 and are subject to change — confirm before enrolling.
items.how: Contact Service CU with your deployment orders, route DFAS net pay to a Service CU checking account, and open the Deployed Warrior / Military Savings account. No withdrawals are permitted — withdrawing before redeployment date plus 120 days moves the funds to a Primary Savings account and closes the Deployed Warrior account.
items.hack: This is the item almost nobody knows: the DoD Savings Deposit Program pays 10% on up to $10,000, and this is a separate, privately offered 10% account with its own $10,000 ceiling. A member who runs both during the same deployment is earning 10% on up to $20,000 of combat-zone pay. The monthly-deposit-capped-at-net-pay rule is the binding constraint, so start the allotment the first month you are eligible rather than trying to lump-sum it later.
items.deadline: Interest ends at end of the month of return date plus 120 days

items.title: Service Credit Union pays military members up to two business days early — and why that can be more than two calendar days
items.who: Military members with DFAS direct deposit into a Service CU account (checking account specified for related loan discounts).
items.value: Pay available up to two business days early. Service CU explains the mechanism: DFAS electronically transmits each paycheck's information up to two business days before the official 1st and 15th paydays, giving the credit union roughly 48 hours to release the funds.
items.how: Set DFAS direct deposit to a Service CU account in myPay. Check Service CU's early payday chart for the dates.
items.hack: Because weekends and federal holidays do not count as business days, when the 1st or 15th falls on a Monday after a holiday weekend your pay can land four or five calendar days early. But Service CU states it cannot assume liability if funds are not deposited early — so set automatic bill payments to the official 1st and 15th, not the early date. People who moved their autopay to the early date got burned when the December 2020 early payday slipped.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Service Credit Union rebates ATM surcharges AND foreign transaction fees — up to $30 a month
items.who: Members on the Direct Deposit Checking tier (up to $15 per month) or Direct Deposit+ tier (up to $30 per month). The Basic checking tier is excluded.
items.value: ATM surcharge and foreign transaction fees rebated up to $15 or $30 per month depending on tier. Surcharge-free withdrawals through Allpoint, CO-OP and Dolphin networks — Service CU cites nearly 85,000 surcharge-free ATMs worldwide. Daily ATM withdrawal limit $1,000, including foreign currency withdrawals, with case-by-case increases.
items.how: Hold a Direct Deposit or Direct Deposit+ checking tier, which requires qualifying direct deposit. Rebates post monthly.
items.hack: Rebating the foreign transaction fee, not just the ATM surcharge, is rare and is the reason this account works for a member stationed in Germany or Japan. At $30 a month that is $360 a year of OCONUS card fees reimbursed. The Basic tier gets none of it, so the direct deposit is not optional.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Service Credit Union Military Relocation Loan — for OCONUS PCS, with a 120-day application window
items.who: Military members with PCS or deployment orders to overseas duty stations. Temporary duty assignments do not qualify. Requires direct deposit into a Service CU account; underwriting and creditworthiness apply. Only one Relocation Loan at a time.
items.value: A purpose-built loan to cover the out-of-pocket gap on an overseas move — the deposits, the car, the household goods you have to buy on arrival — before travel and dislocation allowances reimburse you.
items.how: Apply within 120 days before or after your reporting date to the new assignment.
items.hack: The window runs both directions — 120 days after you report, not just before. Most members who get hammered by an OCONUS move only realise the cash gap once they are in country, and assume they are too late. They are not.
items.deadline: Within 120 days before or after reporting date

items.title: Service Credit Union has branches on 14 military bases in Germany — and sells foreign currency before you fly
items.who: Any member. For members PCSing to Germany this is the practical reason to join before departure.
items.value: Branches on 14 military bases in Germany plus 37 U.S. branches and 5,000+ shared branches worldwide. Foreign currency banknotes can be ordered before travel and picked up at a U.S. branch. Daily published exchange rates for Euro, British Pound and Canadian Dollar, typically updated by 4 p.m. CET. A V PAY debit card for shopping across Europe. International Bill Pay at $1.00 per online or mobile transaction, or $2.00 in-branch, by phone or chat, covering bills in 17 local currencies in more than 40 countries.
items.how: Join before you PCS, order currency for pickup at a U.S. branch, and request a V PAY card for Europe.
items.hack: V PAY matters because large parts of the German retail and transit system run on local debit rails that decline a plain U.S. Visa or Mastercard debit card. Members arrive in Germany, find their card rejected at the grocery store, and conclude their bank is broken. Order the V PAY card before you fly.
items.deadline: Order currency before travel

items.title: Andrews Federal Credit Union — free American Consumer Council route, plus the only Europe-wide CAC path
items.who: Must be 18+. Paths: active duty or reserve members, retired military, and military spouses, dependents and dependent survivors (some military-affiliated paths also require a DoD ID and an assignment or location tied to Joint Base Andrews or Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst); certain DoD civilians and contractors and their dependents at those two joint bases; living, working, attending school or worshipping in Washington, D.C.; employees of Select Employer Groups; a household member or immediate family member of a current member (spouses, children, siblings, parents, grandparents, grandchildren); OR joining the American Consumer Council, which is free and gives immediate eligibility. In Europe: Germany and the Netherlands require a DoD CAC with individual logistical support (ILS); Belgium requires a DoD CAC with ILS or proof of military retiree status; elsewhere in Europe, membership comes through the American Consumer Council. SOFA agreements in some countries may render members ineligible.
items.value: A credit union that will bank you anywhere in Europe, through an association route that is free and takes under five minutes, with a $5 minimum in the Base Share Savings account.
items.how: Apply at andrewsfcu.org/joinnow and select the American Consumer Council as your eligibility option — Andrews enrols you in the ACC automatically, with no separate application and no fee. To qualify for ACC you must be an American consumer who currently uses or has bought a major consumer product or service within the three years before applying. Applying for a loan also puts you up for membership.
items.hack: Andrews is the credit union for Americans in Europe who are not on a base with a Service CU branch. The ACC path means you do not need a CAC, ILS or SOFA status to be a member — it is the fallback when the DoD-ID routes do not fit. Keep the membership open after you rotate back; it is yours until you close the account.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Security Service FCU — geography-based, and the household rule is broader than people think
items.who: You live, work, worship, attend school or volunteer in Texas, Colorado or Utah, or your business is located there; OR you belong to select military branches or units, or are a DoD employee at specific military bases within those service areas; OR you are a family or household member of an existing member. Family includes spouse, child, sibling, parent, grandparent, grandchild, and step and adoptive relationships. Household means someone who shares your residence and helps maintain a single economic unit. The published ways-to-join page does not list employer groups or association routes.
items.value: A large military-origin credit union concentrated in three states with heavy military populations (Fort Cavazos, Lackland, Fort Carson, Hill AFB). Power Protected Checking has no minimum balance and no direct deposit requirement.
items.how: Apply for a product; Security Service confirms eligibility as the first step. If you have ever worked, worshipped, studied or volunteered in TX, CO or UT, that is enough — you do not have to live there now.
items.hack: 'Volunteer in' is an eligibility trigger most applicants skip over. A single documented volunteer role with an organisation in Texas, Colorado or Utah satisfies the geographic test. And the household rule lets a roommate of a member join with no family relationship at all.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Langley Federal Credit Union — 'No Military Affiliation Required', $5 to join
items.who: Langley's join page states plainly: 'No Military Affiliation Required!' The application needs only a Social Security number, proof of name, address and birthday, and $5 to open the account. Langley reports over 400,000 members nationwide. The page does not spell out the formal field-of-membership categories (geographic, employer, family, association), so if an application is declined, call 800-826-7490 or 757-827-5328 and ask which route applies to you.
items.value: A military-origin credit union (Langley AFB) that has opened its doors to civilians, with a $5 entry cost and nationwide membership.
items.how: Apply at langleyfcu.org/join with SSN, ID and $5.
items.hack: Langley is worth joining purely for the free medallion signature guarantee and free notary (see the separate item) — services that cost $50 to $100 at a commercial bank if they will do them at all, and which banks increasingly refuse to non-customers. A $5 membership buys permanent access.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Free medallion signature guarantee and free notary at Langley FCU — the service commercial banks have quietly dropped
items.who: Langley members only — but Langley membership requires no military affiliation and costs $5, so this is effectively open to anyone. For a medallion, all owners of the security must be members and must be present to sign.
items.value: Notary service free of additional cost at any branch or by virtual appointment. Medallion signature guarantee free of charge, in person at any branch, by appointment. A medallion is required to transfer or re-register stocks, bonds and mutual fund shares, and to settle many inherited accounts — and most large banks now provide it only to long-standing deposit customers, or not at all.
items.how: For a medallion, book a branch appointment and bring proof of your most recent 30-day statement showing the security's value and ownership, plus valid ID. Death claims, beneficiary cases and power-of-attorney situations may require additional supporting documents. Langley will not certify true copies of birth, death or marriage certificates or court-issued documents, and will not notarize I-9 forms.
items.hack: This is the hidden reason to hold a small credit union membership you otherwise never use. A surviving spouse trying to retitle a deceased service member's brokerage account will be told by three banks that they cannot help, then charged by a fourth. Join a credit union that does it free, before you need it — the 30-day statement requirement means you cannot walk in cold anyway.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Tower Federal Credit Union — a $35 foundation donation buys lifetime eligibility
items.who: Four paths: employees or retirees of the sponsor agency; employees of Tower partner companies (searchable list on the site); relatives of a current Tower member; OR a $35 donation to The TowerCares Foundation, which requires no other qualification. Tower's membership page invites applicants in MD, DC and VA but does not state residency as a requirement. Tower's heritage is the NSA/Fort Meade community; the page does not itself name the sponsor agency, so confirm by phone at 301-497-7000 if you are relying on that route.
items.value: Membership for a $35 charitable donation. An initial $15 deposit opens a free checking account and a Prime Share savings account and establishes lifetime membership.
items.how: Apply, select the TowerCares Foundation route, donate $35, and fund with $15.
items.hack: $35 to a foundation that supports military and first-responder families, and you are in for life — and the donation is to a charity, not a fee to the credit union. This is the cleanest 'buy your way in' route in military-adjacent banking, and it is the one to use when no family or employer path exists.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Chartway — a $10 donation to the Chartway Promise Foundation is the whole eligibility test
items.who: Five paths: a relative who is already a member (parent, spouse, child, grandparent); sharing a home with a current member, explicitly including domestic partners and roommates; living, working, worshipping or studying in a primary market — Virginia, Utah or Texas; a $10 donation to the Chartway Promise Foundation; or a Select Employer Group partnership covering you and your family.
items.value: Membership in a credit union with deep military roots (Norfolk/Hampton Roads) for a $10 charitable donation, with no military affiliation needed.
items.how: Apply at chartway.com and select the Chartway Promise Foundation route with a $10 donation.
items.hack: $10 is the lowest buy-in of any donation-route credit union found here, and Chartway's emergency relief loan programme (0% for 90 days) is a genuine payday-loan alternative worth having pre-positioned. Join in calm weather; the relief loans require roughly 90 days of membership before you can draw on them.
items.deadline: None, but relief loans generally require 90+ days of membership

items.title: Chartway emergency relief loans — 0% APR for 90 days, up to $5,000, and they are loans not grants
items.who: Chartway members, available only when Chartway declares an eligible emergency event. Applicants generally need at least 90 days of membership or qualifying credit, proof of income and hardship, and either direct deposit or $500 in monthly deposits over the past three months. One hardship loan at a time.
items.value: Three options, all loans and none grants: a 90-Day Relief Loan at 0% APR for up to 3 months, borrowing up to one month's net pay capped at $5,000, full balance due within 90 days; a 12-Month Relief Loan at 4.99% fixed APR for up to 12 months, borrowing up to two months' net pay capped at $10,000, with the first payment deferred 90 days and interest accruing during the deferral; and a one-month Loan Payment Extension on qualifying loans due to a government furlough, covering auto loans, personal loans, lines of credit and credit cards, but excluding first mortgages, student loans, HELOCs and equity loans.
items.how: Call 866-605-7656, use video banking, or visit a branch. Rates and caps change — confirm current terms when you apply.
items.hack: The 0% 90-day loan is the direct structural competitor to a payday loan: same speed, same size, 0% instead of 400%. The catch is that it only exists when Chartway declares an emergency event (shutdown, hurricane, furlough), and it requires 90 days of prior membership. That makes joining for $10 now a cheap option on a future shutdown — which is the whole point for a federal or defence-contractor household.
items.deadline: Only during a declared emergency event; 90-day membership prerequisite

items.title: Chartway for veterans — free membership, free checking, early direct deposit and VBBP participation
items.who: Chartway states it serves veterans of all U.S. armed forces and offers its benefits to active and retired military and their families. Formal eligibility still runs through the five routes above (including the $10 foundation donation), so a veteran with no Virginia/Utah/Texas connection still uses the donation or family path.
items.value: Free membership, free checking, early access to direct-deposited funds, financial education, access to financial advisors, and 24/7 access to funds through the Credit Union Shared Branch and ATM network. Chartway participates in the Veterans Benefits Banking Program, a partnership with VA and the Association of Military Banks of America. The page lists no veteran-specific rate discount.
items.how: Join via any eligibility route, open free checking, and route VA compensation or pension by direct deposit.
items.hack: VBBP participation is the signal that matters for a veteran receiving VA benefits by paper check or prepaid card: VBBP institutions have committed to opening an account for veterans who have been turned away elsewhere, including those with past banking problems. Ask for the VBBP desk by name rather than applying through the standard online funnel.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Redstone Federal Credit Union — 1,800+ membership partner organisations is the real door
items.who: Government employees and contractors, active or retired military, and military dependents on Redstone Arsenal and throughout Madison County, Alabama; Reserve members in Madison County; National Guard members in Madison, Morgan and Limestone Counties (AL) and Lincoln County (TN); employees or members of any of 1,800+ Membership Partner organisations, including organisations, clubs, churches and businesses; immediate family of a Redstone member (spouse, parent, sibling, child, grandparent, grandchild, or step-relative); or anyone living in the same house as a member and sharing household expenses, related or not.
items.value: A large, well-capitalised credit union serving the Army aviation and missile community, reachable through 1,800+ partner organisations rather than only geography. $5.00 minimum balance required to open and maintain the share savings account.
items.how: Check the Membership Partner list first — Redstone says to contact them about other options if your organisation is not listed. Then apply and fund the share account with $5.
items.hack: With 1,800+ partner organisations including clubs and churches, the partner list is the path for anyone with no Alabama connection. Do not self-screen on geography; search the list for anything you already belong to, including a church. Redstone also explicitly invites inquiries about organisations not yet on the list.
items.deadline: None

items.title: America First Credit Union — a county-by-county field of membership across seven states
items.who: Live, work, worship, volunteer or attend school in eligible areas of: Utah (Salt Lake, Utah and Juab Counties in full, plus eligible areas of Cache, Davis, Iron, Rich, Washington and Weber); Nevada (Clark and Lincoln Counties except within 25 miles of the Alamo post office, plus eligible areas of Churchill, Douglas, Esmeralda, Lyon, Mineral, Nye, Storey, Washoe and Carson City); Arizona (Maricopa County, plus eligible areas of Mohave and Pima and parts of Page and St. Johns); Idaho (eligible areas of Ada, Bannock, Bear Lake, Bingham, Boise, Bonneville, Canyon, Caribou, Clark, Elmore, Franklin, Gem, Jefferson, Madison, Owyhee and Power); Oregon (eligible areas of Malheur); New Mexico (eligible areas of Bernalillo, Chaves, De Baca, Guadalupe, Harding, Mora, Quay, Sandoval, San Miguel, Santa Fe, Torrance and Valencia); California (eligible areas of San Bernardino). Also: employees or members of a Select Employer Group or affiliated association; immediate family or household members of an existing member; spouses of members who died within the field of membership; owners, employees or suppliers in the Utah food industry; and existing America First Federal Credit Union members. The become-a-member page does not describe a military eligibility route — it links to a separate Military Offers page.
items.value: A very large credit union serving Hill AFB, Nellis AFB, Luke AFB, Kirtland AFB and the Mountain West defence corridor, with a geographic footprint broad enough that most members of those communities qualify.
items.how: Check the published geographic map, then the SEG list, then the family and household routes in that order. Confirm the opening deposit when you apply — the become-a-member page does not state one.
items.hack: The 'spouses of members who died within the field of membership' clause is a survivor benefit hiding in a membership rule: a surviving spouse who has since moved out of state keeps eligibility that geography would otherwise have taken away. Surviving spouses are routinely told they no longer qualify. They do.
items.deadline: None

items.title: First Command — advice-first, commission-funded, and the one to read the fine print on
items.org: First Command Financial Services / First Command Bank
items.who: First Command describes itself as focused on helping U.S. service members and their families and does not publish a restrictive eligibility rule on its FAQ page, so treat it as open to the military community. Its FAQ does not state who may open a First Command Bank account; call to confirm.
items.value: Comprehensive financial planning and coaching with advisors who specialise in military careers; investment advisory through First Command Advisory Services under a fiduciary standard; brokerage, insurance and trust services through affiliates; and First Command Bank (FDIC member) for accounts, cards, bill pay and transfers, with a Command Center app consolidating accounts, investments and insurance. The FAQ page does not disclose fees or identify which services are free.
items.how: Request an advisor appointment. Before signing anything, ask in writing: is this recommendation made under the fiduciary standard through First Command Advisory Services, or under a suitability standard through the brokerage or insurance affiliate — and what is the commission or fee on each product.
items.hack: First Command's advice sits across a fiduciary advisory arm and a commission-paying brokerage and insurance arm. That question above is not hostile, it is the only question that matters, and the answer determines whether the recommendation is advice or a sale. First Command has a documented regulatory history around military sales practices; this is the firm where 'read the fine print' is the entire benefit note. A no-cost alternative for the same planning work is the free, credentialled counselling at your installation PFM office or Military OneSource.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Why some institutions pay you early and others do not — the DFAS ACH file, explained
items.who: Anyone receiving military pay by direct deposit through DFAS. Also applies to VA compensation and federal civilian pay.
items.value: One to two business days of earlier access to your own money, at no cost. Verified ranges: Armed Forces Bank one business day; Navy Federal a full business day; Service Credit Union up to two business days. Chartway advertises early access without stating a day count.
items.how: The mechanism is not a product. DFAS transmits the payment file electronically one to two business days before the official settlement date of the 1st and 15th. Institutions that choose to post on receipt make the funds available early; institutions that wait for settlement date keep the float. Ask a prospective bank directly: 'Do you post the DFAS file on receipt or on settlement date?'
items.hack: Because weekends and federal holidays are not business days, a two-business-day early release can land four or five calendar days ahead when the 1st or 15th follows a holiday weekend. That matters for a household whose rent is due on the 1st: early pay can convert a chronic late fee into an on-time payment, permanently.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Never schedule a bill on your early pay date — the one rule nobody tells you
items.who: Anyone relying on early military pay.
items.value: Avoiding the cascade of overdraft, NSF and late fees that follows a single missed early deposit. Service Credit Union states plainly that early credit depends on when it receives payroll and that it cannot assume liability if funds are not deposited early — and cites the December 2020 early payday that slipped as the cautionary case.
items.how: Set every autopay, allotment and scheduled transfer to the official 1st and 15th, not the early date. Treat early pay as a buffer, not a payday. A 'pending' deposit has not posted — do not spend against it.
items.hack: Build the habit of keeping one pay period of float behind the early date rather than spending into it. The households that get destroyed by a delayed early payday are the ones whose rent autopay, car payment and insurance all fire on the early date with no cushion. Three NSF fees at $30 each is a $90 penalty for a convenience that was never guaranteed.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Compare ATM rebate programs, not ATM network size — the rebate is what pays you
items.who: Anyone who withdraws cash outside their institution's own network — which describes almost every service member who deploys, PCSes or trains away from home station.
items.value: Verified rebate figures from this session: Navy Federal Free Active Duty Checking rebates up to $20.00 per statement period, which Navy Federal states totals $240 a year. Service Credit Union rebates ATM surcharges and foreign transaction fees up to $15 per month on Direct Deposit Checking or $30 per month on Direct Deposit+, excluding the Basic tier. Armed Forces Bank Access Freedom gives fee-free use of 40,000+ ATMs and no fees at MoneyPass ATMs but does not advertise rebates of other banks' fees. PenFed waives its own ATM fees on Access America, Complete Access and Free Checking but charges $1.50 for a non-PenFed ATM withdrawal and $1.00 for a non-PenFed balance inquiry, and the third-party operator's surcharge is separate.
items.how: Add up your out-of-network withdrawals for a typical month, multiply by the typical $3-$5 combined surcharge, and compare against each institution's monthly rebate ceiling. Then check whether the rebate also covers foreign transaction fees.
items.hack: Network size is marketing; the rebate ceiling is money. An institution with a small network and a $30 monthly rebate beats one with 85,000 ATMs and no rebate if your cash comes out of a machine in a barracks lobby or a bazaar. And only Service CU among those verified here rebates foreign transaction fees alongside the surcharge, which is the figure that decides an OCONUS tour.
items.deadline: None — all figures subject to change, verify current

items.title: The foreign transaction fee is the quiet tax on an OCONUS tour — and it is avoidable
items.who: Anyone stationed, deployed or travelling outside the United States, and anyone buying online from a foreign merchant.
items.value: A foreign transaction fee of 2% to 3% on every purchase compounds into real money over a three-year tour. Verified: PenFed charges up to 2% of the transaction amount on most checking and savings accounts. Service Credit Union rebates foreign transaction fees up to $15 or $30 a month depending on checking tier. On $2,000 a month of local spending, a 2% fee is $480 a year; a $30 monthly rebate covers $1,500 a month of it.
items.how: Before an OCONUS PCS, audit the foreign transaction fee on every card and debit card you hold. Keep one no-foreign-fee card for local spending and use the fee-charging debit card only for ATM withdrawals covered by a rebate.
items.hack: The fee is charged on the debit card too, not just the credit card, and it applies to ATM withdrawals in local currency as well as purchases. Members who carefully pick a no-fee credit card then pay 2% on every cash withdrawal for three years. Check both, and check whether your institution's ATM rebate explicitly includes the foreign transaction fee or only the surcharge.
items.deadline: Audit before OCONUS PCS

items.title: NCUA share insurance — $250,000 per ownership category, which means far more than $250,000 total
items.who: Every member of a federally insured credit union. The parallel at a bank is FDIC deposit insurance at the same $250,000 limit.
items.value: The Share Insurance Fund covers individual accounts up to $250,000, and a member's interest in all joint accounts combined up to a further $250,000. Coverage is calculated per ownership category, so each category carries its own limit: single ownership $250,000 per member-owner; joint ownership $250,000 per owner provided the primary owner is a member; IRAs and certain other retirement accounts $250,000 per member-owner insured separately from other accounts; revocable trusts $250,000 per member-owner for each eligible beneficiary; irrevocable trusts $250,000 per owner for each beneficiary if all owners or all beneficiaries are members.
items.how: Run your actual accounts through the NCUA's Share Insurance Estimator on MyCreditUnion.gov, which handles personal, business and government accounts. Do not guess.
items.hack: A married couple with a joint account, two single accounts and two IRAs at one credit union is insured well past $1 million without moving a dollar — the categories stack. Survivors and retirees who split a lump-sum SGLI or TSP payout across three institutions 'for safety' usually did not need to, and gave up yield to do it. Run the estimator first.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The $5 share is the cheapest permanent financial option you can buy
items.who: Anyone who qualifies for membership at a federal credit union — which, via association and donation routes, is nearly everyone.
items.value: Verified minimums from this session: Navy Federal $5 membership savings minimum, Andrews Federal $5 base share savings, Service Credit Union $5 initial deposit, Redstone $5 share savings minimum maintained at all times, PenFed $5 par value regular share, Langley $5 to open. Tower requires a $35 TowerCares Foundation donation plus a $15 initial deposit for lifetime membership; Chartway requires a $10 Promise Foundation donation.
items.how: Join while you are eligible and in no hurry. Keep the $5 in place. Membership at most credit unions survives losing the original qualifying relationship — Andrews states membership continues until you close the account.
items.hack: Eligibility is a moment in time; membership is permanent. A service member separating, a spouse divorcing, a contractor leaving a DoD installation — each loses the qualifying relationship but keeps membership if the account was already open. Open the account the day you become eligible, even if you have no use for it, because you cannot open it later and you can never get the eligibility back. This is the single highest-return five dollars in this entire reference.
items.deadline: Open while you still qualify — eligibility does not come back

items.title: Payday Alternative Loan (PAL I) — $200 to $1,000 at a federal credit union, with a $20 maximum fee
items.who: Members of a federal credit union that offers PALs. Under 12 CFR 701.21(c)(7)(iii) the credit union must impose a minimum membership requirement of at least one month, so you cannot walk in and get one the same day. State-chartered credit unions are not bound by this federal rule and may differ.
items.value: Principal of not less than $200 and not more than $1,000. Minimum maturity one month, maximum six months. The application fee must reflect actual processing costs and in no case may exceed $20. No rollovers permitted — though extending within the maximum term is allowed if no additional fees are charged and no new credit extended. A credit union may not make more than three PALs loans to one borrower in any rolling six-month period, and only one at a time. Fully amortising.
items.how: Ask your federal credit union whether it runs a PAL programme — not every one does, and the product is often not advertised on the website. Call and use the words 'payday alternative loan'.
items.hack: This is the most underused regulated consumer product in America. A storefront payday loan on $500 commonly costs $75 in fees for two weeks, which annualises past 390%. The same $500 as a PAL costs at most a $20 application fee plus interest capped at 28%, repaid over up to six months. The one-month membership rule is the reason to join a credit union now rather than when you are desperate.
items.deadline: Minimum one month of membership before you can borrow

items.title: PAL II — up to $2,000, up to 12 months, and available the day you join
items.who: Members of a federal credit union offering PALs II. Critically, NCUA's 2019 final rule permits a credit union to make a PALs II loan immediately after the borrower becomes a member — there is no one-month waiting period as there is under PAL I. A member may hold only one type of PALs loan at a time.
items.value: A federal credit union may offer a PALs II loan for any amount up to $2,000, with a term of at least one month and at most 12 months. Rollovers remain prohibited and full amortisation is required.
items.how: Ask specifically for 'PALs II' — credit unions that offer only the older PAL I will quote you the $1,000 / six-month limits. Confirm the application fee and APR in writing before signing.
items.hack: PAL II is the emergency product to ask for by name: double the principal, double the term, and no waiting period. A member can join a federal credit union and borrow $2,000 at a capped rate the same week, which is exactly the scenario that otherwise ends at a title lender. Very few borrowers know PAL II exists as a distinct product from PAL I, and frontline staff sometimes do not either — ask for a lending officer.
items.deadline: None — available immediately on becoming a member

items.title: The PAL rate cap is the federal credit union ceiling plus 1,000 basis points — currently 28%
items.who: Borrowers at federal credit unions. This cap is separate from and lower than the Military Lending Act's 36% MAPR.
items.value: NCUA's rule permits a PALs rate of 1,000 basis points above the general interest rate ceiling the NCUA Board sets for non-PALs loans. The NCUA Board has extended the temporary 18-percent interest rate ceiling through September 10, 2027 — which puts the PALs ceiling at 28%. Compare a storefront payday APR commonly above 390%.
items.how: When a credit union quotes you a small-dollar loan rate above 28% APR, ask whether it is being offered as a PAL. If it is a PAL, the rate is out of compliance. If it is not a PAL, ask whether a PAL is available instead.
items.hack: The 18% general ceiling is itself a benefit worth knowing: no federal credit union may charge more than 18% APR on an ordinary consumer loan while the ceiling is in force, which is well below what a subprime credit card or a near-prime auto lender will quote the same borrower. A service member with damaged credit should be shopping federal credit unions specifically because of that statutory ceiling, not because of any marketing.
items.deadline: 18% ceiling extended through September 10, 2027

items.title: Credit-builder loans — up to 60 points for a thin-file borrower, and slightly negative for everyone else
items.who: Best suited to borrowers with no existing debt and no credit score — a first-term service member, a military spouse with no credit in their own name, a recently naturalised family member. CFPB's study found it is the wrong product for borrowers who already carry debt.
items.value: Typically $300 to $1,000. Mechanism: unlike a secured credit card, the borrower makes no opening deposit. The lender places an amount equal to the loan into a locked savings account using its own funds, the borrower makes monthly payments, and the lender releases each payment back to the borrower minus interest and fees. Payments are reported to all three major bureaus as an installment loan. CFPB's study of 1,531 participants at a midwestern credit union found that for borrowers with no existing debt the loan significantly increased the likelihood of having a score and raised scores by up to 60 points on average against a starting score of 560 — while for borrowers with existing debt it appeared to slightly lower scores on average. Estimated savings increase across all participants was about $253.
items.how: Ask your credit union for a 'credit builder loan' or 'fresh start loan'. Confirm it reports to all three bureaus, confirm whether payments are released as you go or as a lump sum at the end, and set up autopay before the first payment is due.
items.hack: The finding that should change behaviour: about 40 percent of CBL borrowers made at least one late payment on the loan itself, and for borrowers with existing debt the CBL appeared to increase late payments on their other loans too. A credit-builder loan you pay late is worse than no loan at all. Only take one if you can autopay it from the account your military pay lands in, and only if you do not already carry other debt — if you do, pay that down instead.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Share-secured loans — borrow against your own savings at a rate barely above what the savings earns
items.who: Any credit union member with funds in a share savings account or share certificate. There is effectively no credit underwriting, because the loan is fully collateralised by your own deposit — which makes this the product for a member with no credit, damaged credit, or a security-clearance-sensitive need to avoid a hard decline.
items.value: The credit union pledges your shares as collateral and lends against them, typically at a spread of a few percentage points over the dividend rate the shares are earning. Because the deposit keeps earning while pledged, the true cost is the spread, not the full stated APR. Payments report to the bureaus as an installment loan. Federal credit union rates are bounded by the 18% general ceiling in any case.
items.how: Ask for a 'share secured loan' or 'certificate secured loan'. Specify the amount and term, and ask what the net cost is after the dividend your pledged shares continue to earn.
items.hack: The clearance angle matters for this audience: a share-secured loan is approved on collateral, not credit, so it does not generate the pattern of hard inquiries and denials that shows up on a financial-responsibility review. It also converts dead savings into an active, reporting tradeline without spending the savings. The limitation is that it does not create liquidity you did not already have — for that you need a PAL or a relief society loan.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Military auto loan rate discounts — small, stackable, and almost always request-only
items.who: Active duty and in some cases retired members with military direct deposit to the lending institution.
items.value: Verified examples: Navy Federal offers a 0.25% APR discount on select loans to active duty and retired military members with direct deposit, and states members must call or visit a branch to receive it. Service Credit Union offers loan discounts on auto, motorcycle and personal loans to military members with DFAS direct deposit into a Service CU checking account, with the discount depending on checking tier and requiring that tier be maintained for the life of the loan.
items.how: Get the online decision first, then phone before closing and ask for the military rate reduction by name. Confirm in writing what happens to the rate if the direct deposit or checking tier lapses.
items.hack: The condition is the trap, not the discount. Both verified programmes require the direct deposit or checking tier to persist for the life of the loan — so a member who separates, changes institutions, or drops to a Basic checking tier mid-loan can have the rate repriced upward on a five- or six-year note. Before accepting the discount, ask exactly what the rate becomes if the condition fails, and decide whether 0.25% is worth that option you are handing the lender.
items.deadline: Must be requested before loan funding

items.title: VA sets the loan's rules; the lender sets the rate and the fees — so shop the lender, not the benefit
items.who: Any veteran, service member or surviving spouse using VA home loan entitlement. This applies to purchase, cash-out refinance and IRRRL alike.
items.value: VA states directly: 'VA does not set the interest rate that lenders must offer borrowers.' The rate is lender-, borrower- and market-determined and varies between lenders, and VA advises that 'Veterans should shop around to find the lender that offers the best loan terms that fits their needs.' VA-guaranteed loans are facilitated by non-VA-affiliated private lenders who charge their own closing costs, which VA notes can add up to thousands of dollars.
items.how: Get Loan Estimates from at least three VA-experienced lenders on the same day, because rates move daily. Compare the interest rate, the discount points, the lender's origination charge and the total of section A fees side by side — not the monthly payment, which can be manipulated by points and by the term. Your entitlement, funding fee exemption and eligibility do not change between lenders; only price does.
items.hack: The entire marketing industry around VA loans is built on the confusion between the benefit and the lender. 'VA-approved', 'the VA lender', 'specialising in VA' are statements about marketing, not price. Two lenders quoting the same VA loan on the same day can differ by half a point in rate and several thousand dollars in fees. Because the guaranty makes the loan equally safe for every lender, there is no quality trade-off in choosing the cheapest one — which is exactly why shopping is pure gain here and why high-volume VA lenders spend so heavily to prevent it.
items.deadline: Rate locks are time-limited; collect quotes same-day

items.title: What a VA lender may not charge you — commissions, buyer-broker fees and the termite report
items.who: VA home loan borrowers. These are VA's restrictions on the lender and the transaction, binding regardless of which lender you choose.
items.value: From VA's published loan fee guidance: no commissions, brokerage fees or 'buyer broker' fees may be charged to the veteran buyer. The veteran is not allowed to pay for the termite report unless the loan is a refinance. Closing costs including the VA appraisal, credit report, state and local taxes and recording fees may be paid by the buyer, the seller, or split. Sellers may pay certain items — pre-paid closing costs, the VA funding fee, payoff of the veteran's credit balances or judgments, and temporary buydown funds — subject to a 4% cap on the loan amount, with discount points not counted against that cap. The funding fee may be financed or paid in cash but must be paid at closing. VA also limits the lender's flat charge in lieu of itemised origination costs; that specific percentage did not render on the page read in this session, so confirm the current figure in the VA Lender's Handbook or with your lender before relying on it.
items.how: Read your Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure line by line against this list. If a prohibited fee appears, challenge it in writing with the lender, and if it is not removed, escalate to VA Home Loans and to the CFPB complaint system.
items.hack: Discount points sit outside the 4% seller-concession cap. That is the lever to use in a tight negotiation: a seller who has maxed out the 4% on your closing costs can still buy down your rate with points, which is often worth more over the life of the loan than the same dollars applied to closing costs. Buyers and agents routinely stop negotiating at the 4% cap without knowing points are excluded from it.
items.deadline: Challenge improper fees before closing

items.title: Credit union no-down-payment mortgages as a VA loan alternative — and the arithmetic that decides between them
items.org: Navy Federal Credit Union and other credit unions
items.who: Members who either have no VA entitlement left, want to preserve entitlement for a later purchase, or are buying a property type VA will not take. Navy Federal's Military Choice requires at least one active duty, Reservist or Veteran borrower; members may have one active Choice loan at a time.
items.value: Navy Federal's published Military Choice terms: 100% financing for active duty and veterans, with a 1% origination fee waivable in exchange for a 0.25% rate increase, and a 1.75% funding fee waivable in exchange for a 0.375% rate increase or with a 3% down payment. Purchase loans require no down payment in most states. Navy Federal also offers 100% financing on VA-guaranteed loans, where a VA funding fee may apply and can be financed.
items.how: Price both: the VA loan with its funding fee against the credit union product with its 1% origination plus 1.75% funding fee, including the rate-increase alternatives to each. Then ask the decisive question — do you expect to use VA entitlement on a different property later?
items.hack: The real case for the credit union product is not price, it is entitlement preservation. A service member who will PCS in three years and wants to buy again at the next duty station can use the credit union's 100% product now and keep full VA entitlement in reserve. And a veteran exempt from the VA funding fee because of a service-connected disability rating should almost always take the VA loan instead, because the exemption deletes the single largest cost the credit union product cannot waive without a rate increase.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The relief societies are the fastest zero-interest money in the military — and they are not charities you have to beg
items.org: Army Emergency Relief / Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society / Air Force Aid Society / Coast Guard Mutual Assistance
items.who: AER: Soldiers, with assistance delivered through the Secure Online Portal or an office. NMCRS: active duty or retired Sailors and Marines, eligible family members with military ID, surviving spouses, and Reservists on extended duty of 30 or more days. Each service's society has its own rules — verify yours.
items.value: AER states it does not charge interest on loans and never charges late fees. NMCRS provides interest-free loans and grants for everyday living costs (food, rent, utilities), car repairs, registration and insurance, PCS moves and setting up a new household, medical and dental costs not covered by insurance, and funeral expenses; its services are free and confidential. Neither society's public page read in this session published maximum amounts or the loan-versus-grant decision rule, so the amount is determined case by case at the office.
items.how: AER: create an account and submit a request through the Secure Online Portal, or walk into an office — AER states 'You are not required to complete this online form to receive assistance.' Help with the portal is at 866-878-6378. NMCRS: contact your nearest office; find it through their Locations page.
items.hack: The structural insight: a zero-interest relief society loan and a storefront payday loan solve the same problem on the same timeline, and the only reason service members choose the payday lender is that they think the relief society means an inspection of their finances and a note to their chain of command. It does not — NMCRS explicitly describes its services as confidential. AER's walk-in route also bypasses the online form entirely. Go to the society first, every time, before any commercial lender.
items.deadline: None

items.title: AER will pay down your loan balance for finishing financial training — up to $200
items.who: Soldiers with an AER loan balance who complete Financial Frontline training and score 80 or higher within three attempts. Specialists and corporals and below may receive up to $200; sergeants and above up to $100. Credits cannot exceed the current loan balance.
items.value: A direct reduction of an existing AER loan balance — up to $200 for junior enlisted, up to $100 for NCOs and above — for completing training and passing an assessment.
items.how: Take the Financial Frontline training, score 80 or higher within three attempts, and the credit applies against your AER loan balance. AER accepts DFAS allotments for loan repayment.
items.hack: This inverts the usual incentive: most institutions charge you for financial education or make it a condition of a hardship loan. AER pays you up to $200 of principal forgiveness for passing a test. For a junior enlisted Soldier with a $600 AER loan, that is a third of the balance erased for an afternoon of coursework — the highest hourly return available to an E-4 anywhere in this reference.
items.deadline: Must have a current AER loan balance; three attempts to score 80+

items.title: Free financial counselling through Military OneSource and your installation PFM office
items.org: Military OneSource / installation Personal Financial Management programmes
items.who: Service members and their families. Military OneSource describes counselling as free through installation programmes and Military OneSource. The page read in this session did not state eligibility for veterans or any post-separation time limit, so confirm your window directly if you have separated.
items.value: Free, confidential, short-term financial counselling delivered in person, by video or by telephone through Military OneSource, plus classes, seminars and one-on-one counselling through the installation Personal Financial Management (PFM) programme and the Military and Family Life Counseling Program. No cost, and no product is sold to you.
items.how: Contact Military OneSource to schedule, or use the 'Find an Installation' directory to reach your installation's PFM contacts. The page read did not list a phone number — use the installation directory or militaryonesource.mil.
items.hack: This is the direct substitute for a commission-paid financial advisor, and the comparison is not close for the questions most military households actually have: whether to take the TSP loan, how to handle the car note before a deployment, whether the on-base insurance pitch is a good deal. The counsellor has nothing to sell you. Take the free session before you take the free steak dinner.
items.deadline: None stated; confirm post-separation eligibility

items.title: Veterans Benefits Banking Program — the route to an account when you have been turned down before
items.org: VA / Association of Military Banks of America
items.who: Veterans and VA beneficiaries, particularly those currently receiving benefits by paper check or prepaid card, and those who have been declined an account elsewhere. VBBP is a partnership between the Department of Veterans Affairs and the Association of Military Banks of America; participating institutions include banks and credit unions — Chartway confirms its own participation.
items.value: Access to a checking account at a participating institution that has committed to serving veterans, including veterans with past banking problems, plus free financial counselling and a veteran-friendly institution locator. Moving VA compensation or pension from paper check to direct deposit eliminates mail theft risk and check-cashing fees, which can run several percent of each payment.
items.how: Use the VBBP institution list, then contact the institution and say you are coming through the Veterans Benefits Banking Program — do not apply through the standard online funnel, which runs the same automated screening that declined you before.
items.hack: The reason this works is that a prior involuntary account closure sits in a shared database that most banks screen against automatically, and an online application will be declined without a human ever seeing it. VBBP exists precisely to put a human in that loop. Saying the programme's name to a branch employee is the whole technique, and most veterans have never heard of it.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Community Development Financial Institutions — mission lenders that will look at a file a bank declines
items.who: CDFIs are mission-driven lenders certified by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's CDFI Fund, whose main purpose is serving low-income communities. They come in four types: banks, credit unions, loan funds and venture capital funds. Borrowers are individuals and small businesses in the communities each CDFI serves — there is no veteran-specific gate, but many CDFIs prioritise veteran borrowers.
items.value: Depending on type, a CDFI may offer financial services, financial education and affordable loans in its community. The practical value is underwriting: a CDFI loan fund will consider a borrower a commercial bank's credit model rejects, and will spend time on a file a bank will not.
items.how: The CDFI Fund does not lend to individuals — you apply to a CDFI directly. Two official ways to find one: open the published list of certified CDFIs and sort by name, location or institution type, using the contact information in each entry to ask what assistance it offers; or use the Searchable Award Database on the CDFI Fund awards page, select your state and filter for the 'CDFI Program' (Native American, Alaskan Native and Native Hawaiian applicants can also search the 'NACA Program'), then review awardee profiles.
items.hack: If no CDFI is in your area, do not stop — the CDFI Fund itself advises checking nearby communities, because some CDFIs serve neighbouring counties or entire states. The awards database is the better of the two tools for this, because an awardee profile tells you the service area and what the award was for, which the plain certified list does not.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Download the full list of certified CDFIs — the lender directory nobody uses
items.who: Anyone looking for a mission lender: a veteran starting a business, a household in a bank-desert, a borrower rebuilding after a foreclosure or a bankruptcy.
items.value: The CDFI Fund publishes and maintains the complete list of currently certified CDFIs, downloadable and sortable by name, location and institution type, with contact information for each entry. That is a national directory of every Treasury-certified mission lender in the country, free.
items.how: Download the certified CDFI list from the CDFI Fund (linked from cdfifund.gov/faq as cdfifund.gov/media/8018641/download), sort by your state, filter to the institution type you need (credit union for a consumer account, loan fund for business capital), and call them.
items.hack: Sort the list by institution type before you sort by location. If you need a deposit account, you want a CDFI credit union or CDFI bank. If you need business capital with flexible underwriting, you want a CDFI loan fund — and loan funds are the entries borrowers skip because the names are unfamiliar, which is exactly why they have capacity. The list is updated periodically, so re-download rather than relying on a cached copy.
items.deadline: None — list is updated periodically
