items.title: Community Development Credit Unions — and why the NCUA low-income designation is the one to look for
items.who: A community development credit union (CDCU) is one focused on serving low- and moderate-income people and communities, especially those with limited access to safe, affordable financial services. Credit unions serving these communities self-designate as CDCUs when they join Inclusiv. Separately, the NCUA (or occasionally a state regulator) grants a low-income designation when a majority of members are low income — earning less than 80% of the average wage earner's pay per BLS, or having income at or below 80% of national median household income.
items.value: The low-income designation, not the CDCU label, is what confers extra powers: the credit union may accept non-member deposits, receive secondary capital investments, is exempt from the 12.25% cap on member business lending, and can access the NCUA Community Development Revolving Loan Fund plus certain Community Reinvestment Act funds and some Treasury CDFI Fund money. Inclusiv states plainly that CDCU status alone does not grant these powers — low-income designation is still required.
items.how: Find credit unions near you using the NCUA credit union locator at mapping.ncua.gov, then ask each whether it holds the NCUA low-income designation and whether it is an Inclusiv member or a certified CDFI.
items.hack: The business-lending exemption is the one that matters to a veteran entrepreneur. An ordinary credit union is capped at 12.25% of assets in member business loans and will ration that capacity to its best commercial relationships. A low-income-designated credit union is exempt from the cap entirely, which means it has room to lend to a first-time veteran-owned business that a capped credit union would decline for portfolio reasons rather than credit reasons. Ask the question before you apply: 'Do you hold the low-income designation?'
items.deadline: None

items.title: SBA fee relief for veteran-owned businesses — tell the lender you are a veteran early, or lose it
items.who: Qualified veterans and military members, including spouses, borrowing under select SBA 7(a) loan programmes. SBA describes this as reduced upfront guaranty fees under the Veterans Entrepreneurship Act of 2015. The specific fee percentages and eligible loan sizes change by fiscal year — SBA publishes them in an annual information notice, and the notice page did not load in this session, so confirm the current year's figures with your lender or at sba.gov before relying on any number.
items.value: Reduced or waived upfront guaranty fees on select SBA 7(a) loans. SBA reports the relief saved veteran borrowers about $4.8 million in FY17 and $37 million overall. On a seven-figure 7(a) loan the guaranty fee runs into tens of thousands of dollars, so the relief is material.
items.how: SBA's own guidance is explicit: tell the lender your veteran or military status during early conversations, before the loan is packaged. Use SBA Lender Match to find a lender. Veterans Business Outreach Centers (VBOCs) and SBA District Offices provide local advisors who can refer you within the SBA network, and Boots to Business and Boots to Business Reboot cover financing options in their curriculum.
items.hack: The fee relief is applied by the lender at packaging, not claimed by you afterwards. A lender who does not know you are a veteran at the point of packaging will simply charge the standard fee, and there is no retroactive refund process to appeal to. Say it in the first meeting, put it in writing, and ask the lender to confirm in writing which fee tier they are applying. Veterans also typically need less than $50,000 to start, per SBA — which puts most of them in microloan territory where a CDFI may be a better fit than a 7(a).
items.deadline: Fee relief figures reset each fiscal year; must be raised before loan packaging

items.title: What the Military Lending Act does NOT cover — the gap that swallows car loans and mortgages
items.who: Active-duty service members including those on active Guard or active Reserve duty, National Guard members mobilised under federal orders for more than 30 consecutive days, and their covered dependents and spouses. These are 'covered borrowers'.
items.value: Knowing the exclusions is what prevents the mistake. MLA DOES cover payday loans, deposit advance products, vehicle title loans, overdraft lines of credit (but not traditional overdraft services), installment loans subject to exceptions, and credit cards. MLA does NOT cover: residential mortgages used to buy or build the home that secures the loan; mortgage refinances; home equity loans and HELOCs; reverse mortgages; loans to buy a motor vehicle when the vehicle being bought secures the loan; and loans to buy personal property such as jewellery or a home appliance when that item secures the loan. The pattern is simple — if the loan is secured by the very thing you are buying, MLA does not apply.
items.how: Before signing, ask which protection actually applies. If MLA does not cover the loan, SCRA may still cap the rate at 6% on pre-service debt, and state usury law and the Truth in Lending Act still apply. A military legal assistance office can tell you which regime governs your specific contract.
items.hack: This is the single most dangerous misunderstanding in military consumer finance. Service members believe the 36% MAPR cap protects them at the car dealership — it does not, because a purchase-money auto loan secured by the car is excluded. That exclusion is precisely why the aggressive lending concentrates on car sales near bases: the industry knows the cap does not reach it. Treat a dealership finance office as entirely unregulated by MLA and bring your own pre-approved credit union financing to the table.
items.deadline: None

items.title: What goes into the 36% MAPR — it is not the APR on your statement
items.who: Covered borrowers under the Military Lending Act and anyone reviewing a covered credit contract for compliance.
items.value: The Military Annual Percentage Rate cap is 36%, and the MAPR calculation is broader than the Truth in Lending APR. It includes finance charges, credit insurance premiums or fees, add-on credit-related products sold with the credit, and other fees such as application or participation fees, with some exceptions. MLA also bars prepayment penalties, bars requiring arbitration to settle disputes (which normally means surrendering the right to join a class action), and bars requiring repayment by military pay allotment.
items.how: Add the add-ons back in. A loan quoting 29% APR that bundles a credit insurance premium, a debt-cancellation product and a participation fee can exceed 36% MAPR even though its disclosed APR looks compliant. Enforce by submitting a complaint to the CFPB at consumerfinance.gov/complaint or (855) 411-2372, reporting to the Department of Justice at civilrights.justice.gov/report, and taking the contract to a military legal office — find one at legalassistance.law.af.mil.
items.hack: The add-on products are the whole game. Lenders near bases comply with the 36% headline by pricing the loan itself under the cap and making their margin on the bundled credit insurance, GAP product or membership fee — which MLA counts in the MAPR but which the borrower reads as separate purchases. If a lender insists an add-on is required, that is both a MAPR problem and a sign to walk. The no-arbitration and no-allotment-repayment clauses are also worth checking: a covered contract containing either is defective on its face.
items.deadline: None

items.title: The 2015 allotment ban — and why a seller still pushing allotment repayment is telling you something
items.who: Active-duty service members. Military retirees and DoD civilian employees were not affected by the change.
items.value: DoD announced changes to the allotment system in 2014, effective January 2015, barring new allotments used to purchase, lease or rent personal property such as vehicles, appliances and consumer electronics. Allotments remain allowed for savings, insurance premiums, mortgage or rent, dependent support, and investments. CFPB subsequently wrote to companies selling retail goods to service members, warning that still advertising repayment by allotment may violate the law, that offering misleading payment information could violate the Dodd-Frank prohibition on unfair, deceptive or abusive practices, and that letting service members pay by allotment where DoD rules prohibit it is itself a problem.
items.how: If a retailer or lender near a base offers allotment repayment on a TV, a car, furniture or electronics, that offer is outside DoD rules for a new allotment. Decline it, and report it to the CFPB at consumerfinance.gov/complaint and to your installation's legal office.
items.hack: CFPB notes the deeper reason to refuse: a service member paying by allotment instead of an option like ACH gives up certain legal protections — the allotment is a pay instruction, not a payment you can stop, dispute or reverse the way you can an ACH debit or a card charge. So even where an allotment is still permitted, choosing ACH preserves your ability to fight back. A seller who insists on allotment is choosing the payment method you cannot stop, which tells you what they expect to happen.
items.deadline: Ban effective January 2015 for new allotments on personal property

items.title: How to actually file with the CFPB Office of Servicemember Affairs — and the email address that routes it
items.who: Any consumer, with a dedicated route for service members, veterans and their families through the Office of Servicemember Affairs.
items.value: A complaint submitted to the CFPB is forwarded to the company with a response obligation, and the company's answer comes back to you through the portal — which converts a dead-end customer service loop into a documented regulatory record. Verified contact points: submit online at consumerfinance.gov/complaint/, or mail to CFPB, PO Box 27170, Washington, DC 20038. Phone (855) 411-2372; TTY/TTD (855) 729-2372, weekdays 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern excluding federal holidays. The Office of Servicemember Affairs is reachable at military@cfpb.gov.
items.how: File the complaint through the online portal, not the email — the portal creates the tracked record and the company response obligation. Use military@cfpb.gov in addition, to flag the servicemember dimension and to raise a pattern of conduct rather than a single account. Attach the contract, the correspondence and the dates.
items.hack: Two complaints are better than one: the portal complaint gets your individual problem answered, and the email to the Office of Servicemember Affairs feeds the pattern analysis that produces enforcement actions. OSA's published work includes recoveries for service members from auto lenders and retailers. For an SCRA or USERRA violation, also report to the Department of Justice at civilrights.justice.gov/report — DOJ has independent authority the CFPB does not, and DOJ settlements with auto lenders and retailers over SCRA repossessions are the enforcement history that makes a company's compliance office take a servicemember complaint seriously.
items.deadline: File promptly — document retention and limitations periods both run

items.title: Check a lender's SCRA track record before you borrow — the public enforcement trail
items.who: Any service member or family member choosing a lender, servicer or dealership — particularly for an auto loan or a loan that will still be outstanding when you deploy.
items.value: SCRA compliance varies enormously between institutions, and the record is public. DOJ's Servicemembers and Veterans Initiative publishes its SCRA settlements and consent orders, and CFPB publishes its enforcement actions — including orders requiring auto lenders to refund service members and actions over repossessions and aggressive collection against service members. Separately, DMDC's SCRA website lets a lender (and you) verify active-duty status for SCRA purposes, which is the mechanism a compliant servicer is supposed to use before repossessing or foreclosing.
items.how: Search the company name against justice.gov SCRA settlements and against the CFPB enforcement actions list before you sign. Then, once the loan exists, confirm your own active-duty record is correct at the DMDC SCRA site — a wrong date there is what lets a servicer legitimately claim it had no notice.
items.hack: A lender with a prior DOJ consent order is, counter-intuitively, often the safer choice on SCRA specifically — the order forces a compliance programme, trained staff and audit. The dangerous institution is the small one with no enforcement history and no SCRA desk, which has never been made to build the process and will simply repossess. Ask any prospective lender one question: 'What is your process for checking DMDC before a repossession?' A compliant shop answers immediately; the rest do not understand the question.
items.deadline: Check before signing; verify DMDC record annually

items.title: How to spot the bad deal marketed on and near a base — the five tells
items.who: Every service member, and particularly first-term members in their first year, who are the target market.
items.value: Five tells, each grounded in verified enforcement history: (1) repayment by military pay allotment on a vehicle, appliance or consumer electronics — barred for new allotments since January 2015 and the subject of CFPB warning letters; (2) a purchase-money auto or personal-property loan pitched as MLA-protected, when those are precisely MLA's exclusions; (3) required add-on products (credit insurance, debt cancellation, GAP, membership fees) which inflate the MAPR past 36% while the disclosed APR looks compliant; (4) a mandatory arbitration clause or an allotment-repayment requirement in a covered contract, both of which MLA prohibits outright; (5) a free seminar, meal or prize drawing whose purpose is a product application — contrasted with installation PFM counselling and the USAA Educational Foundation, which state they sell nothing.
items.how: Before signing anything within ten miles of a gate: take the contract to your installation legal assistance office (find one at legalassistance.law.af.mil) or the PFM office. Both are free and neither earns a commission on your decision. If a seller will not let the contract leave the building for a day, that is the sixth tell.
items.hack: The structural point to internalise: the heavy marketing near bases is not targeting service members because they are gullible. It is targeting them because military pay is stable, garnishable, allotment-accessible and backed by a federal employer who will not fire you for debt — which makes a service member the single most reliable subprime borrower in the economy. That is why the offers cluster at the gate, and why the right default answer at the gate is 'I will take this to legal and come back.'
items.deadline: None

items.title: Savings Deposit Program — 10% guaranteed on up to $10,000, and the best risk-free return in America
items.who: Service members receiving Hostile Fire Pay who are deployed to a designated combat zone for either 30 consecutive days, or one day in each of three consecutive months. That second test is the one people miss — three brief trips across the line in three consecutive calendar months qualifies you without ever spending 30 straight days there.
items.value: Deposited funds earn 10% interest annually. You may deposit up to $10,000.00. There is no credit risk and no market risk — it is a Treasury-backed government obligation. Interest continues to accrue for up to 90 days after you leave the combat zone: if that period ends on the last day of a month interest accrues for that month, otherwise it accrues through the last day of the preceding month.
items.how: Enrol through your finance office while deployed — the SDP Help Line is 1-888-332-7411 toll free within the U.S., 216-522-5096 commercial, or DSN 580-5096. Fund it by allotment or deposit up to the $10,000 ceiling.
items.hack: Compare 10% guaranteed against anything else available to a retail investor and the comparison is absurd — it beats every FDIC-insured product, every Treasury, and the long-run average of the stock market, with none of the risk. The $10,000 cap and the deployment window are the only limits, which means the correct play is to hit the $10,000 ceiling as fast as the deployment allows rather than contributing evenly over the tour. A member who funds it in month one and a member who funds it in month six of the same deployment can differ by several hundred dollars for no reason other than timing. Rate and cap are set by statute and regulation but confirm both at the official page before you enrol.
items.deadline: Must enrol while deployed; interest runs up to 90 days after departure from the combat zone

items.title: The two SDP eligibility tests — and the one that catches short in-and-out deployments
items.who: Service members receiving Hostile Fire Pay. Two alternative tests: 30 consecutive days deployed to a designated combat zone, OR one day in each of three consecutive months.
items.value: The three-consecutive-months test means aircrew, liaison officers, inspection teams, courier runs and anyone doing short repeated trips into a designated area can qualify for a 10% account without ever completing a 30-day stretch. One day in March, one day in April, one day in May is sufficient.
items.how: Keep documentation of every entry into the designated area and your Hostile Fire Pay entitlement. Take it to finance and ask specifically about the one-day-in-three-consecutive-months test — the 30-day test is the one finance clerks quote by default.
items.hack: This is the most overlooked eligibility rule in military pay. Members who fly in and out of a designated zone assume SDP is for people on a year-long tour and never ask. They are leaving a guaranteed 10% on up to $10,000 on the table because a clerk quoted them the wrong one of two tests. Bring the regulation reference with you.
items.deadline: The three qualifying months must be consecutive

items.title: Getting money out of SDP — the rules that trap people, and the order of operations on return
items.who: SDP participants during and after deployment.
items.value: While in the combat zone you may withdraw accrued interest above the $10,000 principal quarterly. Principal can be withdrawn only if your own or a dependent's health or welfare is at risk without access to the funds, and an emergency withdrawal must be authorised by your commanding officer. Accounts can be closed only after departing the combat zone. Requests go through myPay at mypay.dfas.mil, or by mail to DFAS-Cleveland Center, ATTN: SDP, Special Claims, 1240 East 9th St., Cleveland, OH 44199-2055.
items.how: The order matters: make sure the allotment has stopped before requesting any distribution. Include your name, Social Security number and departure date from the combat zone. For EFT, supply the bank name, routing number, account number and account type; for a cheque, a complete mailing address.
items.hack: Two failure modes account for most SDP horror stories. First, people request the distribution while the allotment is still running, which creates a loop of new deposits against a closing account — stop the allotment first, confirm it stopped, then file. Second, people close the account the week they land, forfeiting up to 90 days of continued 10% accrual. Leave the money in for the full post-deployment accrual window; the end-of-month rule means the exact closing date is worth checking, because closing one day into a month versus one day before it can change which month's interest you keep.
items.deadline: Cannot close until after departing the combat zone; interest accrues up to 90 days after

items.title: Stack SDP with a credit union combat-zone account — two 10% buckets, $20,000 total
items.who: A deployed service member who qualifies for the DoD Savings Deposit Program and is a member of a credit union offering its own combat-zone savings account. Verified example: Service Credit Union's Deployed Warrior / Military Savings pays 10% APY on up to $10,000 for active duty members deployed to a combat zone as Service CU defines it, with deployment orders and net pay direct deposit required.
items.value: SDP: 10% on up to $10,000, government-guaranteed. Service CU: 10% APY on up to $10,000, with balances above that earning a variable rate. Run concurrently, a member can earn 10% on up to $20,000 of combat-zone pay. Service CU's rate was stated accurate as of 07/01/2025 and is subject to change — verify before relying on it.
items.how: Enrol in SDP through finance and open the credit union account with your deployment orders before or early in the deployment. Note Service CU's constraint: monthly deposits cannot exceed your monthly net military pay, so both buckets fill out of the same pay stream and must be started early to reach both ceilings.
items.hack: Almost nobody runs both, because almost nobody knows the second one exists. The binding constraint is not the ceilings, it is time — monthly deposits capped at net pay mean a six-month deployment on E-5 pay cannot fill $20,000 unless the allotments start in month one. Open both accounts before you leave, not after you arrive. And note the different end dates: SDP interest runs up to 90 days after you leave the combat zone, Service CU's 10% runs to the end of the month of your return date plus 120 days — so the credit union bucket should be the last one you close.
items.deadline: Start both allotments in the first month of deployment; different post-deployment accrual windows

items.title: TSP versus a credit union IRA — the expense ratio comparison that settles it for the core holding
items.who: Any service member or federal employee with a TSP account who is also considering an IRA at a credit union or brokerage.
items.value: TSP's published 2025 total expense ratios (net administrative plus investment): G Fund 0.034% (3.4 bps, $0.34 per $1,000), F Fund 0.035%, C Fund 0.035%, S Fund 0.051% (5.1 bps, $0.51 per $1,000), I Fund 0.048%. Net administrative expense alone is 0.034% for G, F, C and S and 0.033% for I. A credit union IRA invested in share certificates has no expense ratio but earns certificate rates; a credit union IRA invested through an affiliated broker-dealer may carry fund expense ratios and advisory fees an order of magnitude above these.
items.how: Use TSP for the low-cost core equity and bond exposure. Use an IRA for what TSP cannot do — holding a specific asset, a Roth conversion, or a beneficiary structure. Before opening an IRA through a credit union's investment affiliate, ask for the total expense ratio of the recommended funds plus any advisory fee, and compare it against 3.5 basis points.
items.hack: At 3.5 basis points the C Fund is cheaper than almost any retail index fund in existence, and dramatically cheaper than the actively managed funds a commission-paid advisor will recommend. The practical rule: never move money out of TSP into a higher-cost wrapper for the same exposure. The one genuinely good reason to hold a credit union IRA alongside TSP is the G Fund's mirror image — a share certificate IRA inside an NCUA-insured credit union gives you a principal-protected sleeve with its own $250,000 insurance category, separate from your other accounts there.
items.deadline: None

items.title: You can contribute to TSP and an IRA in the same year — but Roth TSP can affect Roth IRA eligibility
items.who: Any TSP participant who also wants to use an IRA.
items.value: TSP states plainly: 'Your participation in the TSP does not affect your eligibility to contribute to an IRA.' Both are subject to their own IRS dollar limits, which change yearly. However, TSP also notes that 'contributing to the Roth TSP may affect your eligibility to contribute to a Roth IRA' — so check the interaction before you max both. Rollover rules: traditional IRA money can move into the TSP by direct rollover or by indirect rollover deposited within 60 days; Roth IRA money cannot move into the TSP even if you have a Roth TSP; TSP money can generally roll into an IRA; and your spouse's IRA generally cannot receive your TSP account.
items.how: Contribute to TSP first up to any matching, then to an IRA, then back to TSP. Check the current year's limits at tsp.gov and irs.gov — they change annually. Consult a tax advisor before any rollover out of TSP, because the tax rules are complex and the move is often irreversible.
items.hack: The one-directional rollover rule is the planning trap. Traditional IRA money flows into TSP, but nothing flows from a Roth IRA into a Roth TSP — and once TSP money leaves for an IRA, the 3.5-basis-point expense ratios are gone for good. That asymmetry argues for consolidating stray traditional IRAs into TSP rather than the reverse, which is the opposite of what most rollover advice (which earns a fee on assets leaving TSP) will tell you.
items.deadline: Contribution limits are annual and reset each tax year

items.title: Savings bonds — $10,000 a year each in I and EE, and payroll purchase is gone
items.who: Anyone with a TreasuryDirect account. Purchases for a child or as gifts count separately from your own limit.
items.value: You may buy up to $10,000 in Series EE electronic savings bonds AND up to $10,000 in Series I electronic savings bonds in one calendar year as owner — $20,000 combined, not $10,000 total. Electronic bonds start at $25 and can be bought in amounts to the penny up to $10,000. Note for service members: payroll purchases are no longer available; TreasuryDirect stated this option was discontinued on January 31, 2025.
items.how: Open a TreasuryDirect account and buy directly. Current I bond and EE bond rates are set by Treasury on a published schedule and change — look them up at treasurydirect.gov before buying, because neither rate was readable in this session and both move.
items.hack: Three points most buyers miss. The limits are per series, so a couple can place $40,000 a year between them across I and EE. Gift and child purchases are outside your own limit, which is how larger allocations get made. And the loss of payroll purchase matters specifically for military savers who had been building savings bonds by allotment — that channel is closed, so the habit has to be rebuilt as a TreasuryDirect bank transfer or it simply stops, which is exactly what happened to many allotment savers who never noticed.
items.deadline: Limits are per calendar year; payroll purchase discontinued January 31, 2025

items.title: The Series EE 20-year doubling guarantee — a floor rate nothing else offers
items.who: Anyone buying Series EE savings bonds and willing to hold for 20 years. Commonly used for a child's or grandchild's education fund.
items.value: Series EE bonds carry a Treasury guarantee that the bond will be worth at least double its purchase price if held for 20 years — Treasury makes a one-time adjustment at the 20-year mark if the accrued interest has not got there. Doubling over 20 years is an effective annual return of roughly 3.5%, guaranteed, regardless of what the stated rate does in the interim. The current stated EE rate could not be read in this session (TreasuryDirect's EE page blocked automated access), so verify the rate and confirm the guarantee's current terms at treasurydirect.gov before buying.
items.how: Buy Series EE electronic bonds through TreasuryDirect and hold for the full 20 years. Selling earlier forfeits the guarantee and leaves you with whatever the stated rate accrued.
items.hack: The guarantee is a put option on interest rates that Treasury hands you for free, and it is worth most precisely when stated rates are low — in a low-rate environment, a 3.5% guaranteed floor for 20 years is better than any 20-year instrument available to a retail buyer. It is worth least when rates are high. That makes EE bonds a rate-environment-dependent purchase rather than an always-good one, and makes the 20-year hold commitment the real cost. Verify the current stated rate first; if it is near the 3.5% implied by the doubling, the guarantee is adding nothing.
items.deadline: Must hold 20 years for the guarantee

items.title: Association of Military Banks of America — the trade body behind on-base banking and VBBP
items.org: Association of Military Banks of America
items.who: AMBA is a trade association of banks serving the military community, including those operating on-installation branches under DoD arrangements. It is not a consumer service, but its membership list functions as a screen for institutions that have committed to military-community banking. Its own site redirected to militarybanking.org in this session and the content could not be read, so treat the detail below as directional and confirm at militarybanking.org.
items.value: AMBA is a partner with the Department of Veterans Affairs in the Veterans Benefits Banking Program — Chartway's own veterans page names the partnership. For a veteran who has been declined an account elsewhere, the AMBA-VBBP channel is the practical route in. AMBA also engages DoD on on-installation bank solicitations, which is why some installations have a designated on-base bank and others do not.
items.how: Use militarybanking.org to identify AMBA member institutions and the VBBP participant list, then contact the institution naming the programme.
items.hack: Knowing that the on-base bank holds a DoD arrangement rather than a commercial lease changes how you treat a complaint about it: an on-installation financial institution operates under agreements with the installation commander, which gives you an escalation path through the installation — legal assistance, the commander's office, the PFM programme — that does not exist for a strip-mall lender outside the gate. Use it.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Debt consolidation at a credit union — bounded by the 18% ceiling, which is the whole point
items.who: Members of a federal credit union carrying high-rate revolving debt. Particularly relevant to a service member with a subprime credit card or near-prime auto loan, and to anyone whose debt load is becoming a security-clearance issue.
items.value: No federal credit union may charge more than the NCUA general interest rate ceiling on an ordinary consumer loan — currently 18%, extended through September 10, 2027. A consolidation loan at or below 18% replacing cards at 25% to 30% produces a real and immediate reduction in interest cost, with a fixed payoff date instead of a revolving balance. Credit unions also commonly offer share-secured and signature consolidation loans, and some offer skip-a-payment and hardship extensions (Chartway's verified Loan Payment Extension covers auto loans, personal loans, lines of credit and credit cards, excluding first mortgages, student loans, HELOCs and equity loans).
items.how: Ask a credit union lending officer for a debt consolidation loan and bring a list of every balance and its APR. Close nothing until the consolidation funds. Then stop using the cards — consolidating and re-running the balances is the standard failure mode.
items.hack: The clearance angle is the reason to act early rather than at the point of crisis. A consolidation loan with a fixed payoff date is a demonstrably managed debt; revolving balances at 29% that grow month over month are what adjudicators read as financial irresponsibility. Consolidating is not just cheaper, it changes the documentary picture — and a credit union that is statutorily barred from charging above 18% cannot put you in a worse product while doing it. Beware the for-profit 'debt relief' firms advertising to the military community: a nonprofit credit counselling agency and your credit union's own lending officer cost nothing by comparison.
items.deadline: 18% ceiling in force through September 10, 2027

items.title: Join before you need it — the single operating rule for all of the above
items.who: Everyone in the military community, and the family members who are eligible through them.
items.value: Nearly every genuinely valuable product in this section has a waiting period or an eligibility window that closes: PAL I requires at least one month of membership; Chartway's relief loans generally require 90 days of membership and only exist during a declared emergency; Navy Federal's Free Active Duty Checking requires a qualifying direct deposit within 180 days of opening; the Career Kickoff Loan is gone at graduation; Service CU's Deployed Warrior account needs to be open and funded in the first month of a deployment to reach the ceiling; SDP must be enrolled while you are in the zone; and credit union eligibility itself evaporates on separation, divorce, or leaving a DoD installation — but membership already established survives.
items.how: Today, while nothing is wrong: open a $5 share at one federal credit union that offers PALs, and at one that offers free medallion and notary service. Confirm your institution posts the DFAS file on receipt. Verify your DMDC SCRA record is correct. That is an afternoon's work and under $50.
items.hack: Every item in this section is cheap to arrange in advance and impossible to arrange in a crisis. The payday lender's entire business model is that it is the only option available to someone who needed an option last week. The $5 shares, the 90-day membership clocks and the one-month PAL waiting periods are not bureaucratic friction — they are the reason the alternatives are cheap, and the reason they are useless to people who wait. Treat credit union membership as insurance you buy before the fire.
items.deadline: Every waiting period in this section runs from the day you join, not the day you need it

items.title: Veterans Upward Bound (TRIO) - free college-prep program for veterans
items.who: Veterans, per the program's purpose, who need academic help to enter and finish postsecondary education; grantee must document why each participant qualifies
items.value: Free academic tutoring, help with college entrance exams and applications, financial aid guidance, GED or high-school re-entry guidance, financial literacy, basic-skills refreshers, and referrals to other veterans services. ED's FAQ page does not state a participant cost; confirm with the local grantee.
items.how: Programs are run by individual colleges under 5-year ED grants. Search 'Veterans Upward Bound' plus your state, or ask your college veterans office, and contact the local grantee to confirm it is funded this cycle.
items.hack: Use it BEFORE you spend GI Bill months: remedial math or English refreshers here protect your entitlement. Grantee sites are scattered (community colleges, universities), so check neighbouring counties too.
items.deadline: Rolling by site; the federal competition repeats every four years

items.title: Armed Forces Retirement Home - federally run retirement community (Washington DC and Gulfport MS)
items.who: Retired enlisted/warrant/LDO veterans with 20+ years, certain Guard/Reserve retirees, and some veterans with service-connected disability or war-theater/hostile-fire injury. Must be honorably released, no felony convictions, able to live independently at admission, and have major medical coverage or a 100% VA rating.
items.value: Independent living, assisted living, memory support and long-term care in a DoD-affiliated retirement community. Resident fees exist; I did not verify the current fee schedule, so check afrh.gov.
items.how: Mail the application to AFRH Public Affairs Office, Box 584, Washington DC 20011-8400 or fax 202-541-7519. Needs DD-214, medical exam form, negative TB test, 2 years of tax records, VA benefits letter. Spouses apply together and file separate medical packets.
items.hack: The eligibility checklist I read is dated April 2022; confirm current rules. Beneficiary spouses must have been married before the veteran became retirement-eligible, so check marriage dates early.
items.deadline: Rolling; wait for an official report date before arranging a move

items.title: Computer/Electronic Accommodations Program (CAP) - free assistive tech for wounded service members
items.org: Department of Defense (CAP, Defense Human Resources Activity)
items.who: Wounded, ill and injured Service members with cognitive, communication, dexterity, hearing or visual limitations. After separation, responsibility passes to VA.
items.value: Free needs assessment, assistive technology and training. CAP's page says it provides solutions free of charge and that equipment given to members leaving active duty for medical reasons stays their personal property to support civilian employment.
items.how: Work through your military treatment facility, transition unit, recovery program or commander/clinical provider. Help line on cap.mil: 833-227-3272 or cap@mail.mil.
items.hack: If you are in the medical separation pipeline, ask for CAP evaluation BEFORE separation so the equipment becomes yours; after discharge the page says VA takes over provision.
items.deadline: Must be requested before separation

items.title: Priority of Service - veterans and spouses go first in every DOL-funded job training program
items.org: Department of Labor (Jobs for Veterans Act, 38 USC 4215)
items.who: Veterans and eligible spouses (including widows and widowers) seeking any Department of Labor-funded job training program
items.value: Covered persons get priority access in DOL-funded employment and training programs, including WIOA programs. DOL's page does not explain the order of service in practice; it points to TEGL 10-09 and TEGL 19-16.
items.how: Tell the American Job Center up front that you are a veteran or eligible spouse and ask for priority-of-service enrollment in WIOA training, dislocated-worker and other DOL-funded programs.
items.hack: It applies to waitlisted or capped programs, so invoke it explicitly in writing; it also reaches programs run by private operators using DOL money, not only the job center itself.
items.deadline: None; ongoing statutory right

items.title: Disabled veteran leave - 104 hours of paid leave in your first year as a federal employee
items.who: Federal employees (also USPS and Postal Regulatory Commission employees) who are veterans with a service-connected disability rated 30% or more
items.value: Up to 104 hours of paid leave, without loss of pay, for medical treatment of the service-connected disability, available during the 12 months from your first day of employment. Unused hours are forfeited at the end of that period.
items.how: Request it from your agency; you certify in OPM's prescribed form that the leave was used for treatment by a health care provider.
items.hack: It does not touch your sick leave balance, so schedule VA appointments and C&P-related care in your first year. Use-it-or-lose-it.
items.deadline: 12-month window from first day of employment

items.title: SCSEP - paid community-service jobs for low-income veterans age 55+, with enrollment priority
items.org: Department of Labor Senior Community Service Employment Program (via state aging agencies)
items.who: Age 55+, family income at or below 125% of the federal poverty level. Veterans (and in some cases veterans' spouses) get enrollment priority.
items.value: Part-time subsidized community-service assignment averaging 20 hours a week, paid the highest of the federal, state or local minimum wage, plus training, annual physicals and job-search help. Limited to 48 months unless extended.
items.how: Apply through your state's SCSEP office (for example New York's state aging office) or your American Job Center.
items.hack: The veteran priority puts you ahead of other eligible seniors on the waitlist; say you are a veteran on the first call.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: FMCSA military CDL skills-test waiver, now with a temporary two-year window
items.who: Current and former military drivers who held a qualifying position operating a commercial vehicle
items.value: State agencies may substitute your safe military commercial-vehicle experience for the CDL skills test. A temporary FMCSA waiver extends the application window from one to two years and says recipients are not subject to Entry-Level Driver Training requirements. States are encouraged, not required, to adopt the extension.
items.how: Apply at your state driver licensing agency with proof of the qualifying military position; check whether your state adopted the two-year extension.
items.hack: The waiver page I read lists an effective date of July 30, 2026 and an expiration of October 29, 2026, so anyone between one and two years out should move now.
items.deadline: Waiver expires October 29, 2026; standard program window is one year

items.title: FAA military competency path - civilian commercial and instrument ratings from your military flying
items.who: U.S. military pilots and former military pilots (not removed from flying status for proficiency or discipline); military instructor pilots for CFI
items.value: Apply for a commercial pilot certificate, instrument rating, type rating (where a civilian equivalent exists) or flight-instructor certificate based on military qualification, using a military competency knowledge test instead of the standard path. Saves flight-training time and cost; I did not verify test fees.
items.how: Present official military records of pilot status, undergraduate pilot training graduation and a passed pilot/instrument proficiency check, or 10 logged hours in the relevant military aircraft. Contact an FAA FSDO.
items.hack: Flight instructor applicants must have passed the knowledge test within 24 calendar months of application, so time it close to your CFI application.
items.deadline: None stated in the rule beyond the 24-month CFI knowledge test window

items.title: National Library Service talking books - free braille and audio library with veterans preference
items.org: Library of Congress NLS via state Talking Book Libraries
items.who: People unable to read standard print because of low vision, blindness, physical limitation or a reading disability; Rhode Island's program page says veterans get preference by law
items.value: Free braille and talking-book service, with a download portal (BARD) of more than 99,000 titles per the Rhode Island page. Page calls the service free; it does not mention postage.
items.how: Apply through your state Talking Book Library (the Rhode Island page links to its application and eligibility requirements); a certifying professional is typically needed.
items.hack: Veterans with TBI, vision loss or PTSD-related reading difficulty often qualify and never ask; the NLS network is nationwide even though the page I read is Rhode Island's.
items.deadline: None

items.title: USDA/NRCS beginning-farmer priority for veterans in EQIP
items.who: Veterans (service with other-than-dishonorable discharge) with no farm operation or one for not more than 10 consecutive years
items.value: A state NRCS fact sheet I read says veteran farmers receive the highest priority for funding within beginning-farmer and socially-disadvantaged ranking pools of EQIP, a cost-share program for conservation practices. It did not say veterans automatically get higher payment rates or advance payments.
items.how: Apply at your local USDA Service Center; self-certify as a veteran farmer on the application and ask how your state ranks pools.
items.hack: The 10-year clock counts years operating a farm, so a veteran starting a small farm late in life is still a beginning farmer. Ask your Service Center whether your state has a veteran set-aside.
items.deadline: State application cutoffs vary; ask your NRCS office

items.title: HUD Veterans Housing Rehabilitation and Modification Pilot Program - grants to nonprofits that fix homes for disabled veterans
items.who: Low-income veterans with disabilities; the grant goes to nonprofit organizations, not individuals
items.value: Funds nonprofits to rehabilitate or modify veteran homes: repairs, energy efficiency, ramps, bathroom fixtures, special lighting. One summary page lists $700,000 to $1,000,000 per grant over 3 years with no match, but its page was last modified in 2020.
items.how: Ask local home-repair nonprofits whether they hold a HUD VHRMP award; Federal Register notices in 2025 show the program is still being noticed.
items.hack: Individual veterans cannot apply to HUD. Find grantees via HUD Exchange and approach them directly.
items.deadline: Per HUD NOFO

items.title: IRS forgiveness of income tax for service members who die in a combat zone or from terrorist or military action
items.who: Estates and survivors of service members killed in a combat zone or by terrorist/military action
items.value: Publication 3 (2025) says income tax is forgiven for the year of death and earlier years (combat zone: back to the first day of combat zone service; terrorist/military action: from the year before the injury), with refunds of tax already paid.
items.how: File a paper Form 1040/1040-SR (no return filed) or Form 1040-X (already filed), one per year, and write the operation name and KIA in bold across the top of page 1 (e.g. Iraqi Freedom - KIA).
items.hack: The estate trustee or beneficiary also does not pay tax on income of the decedent for the year of death. Needs a paper return; e-file will not carry the notation.
items.deadline: See Pub 3 for the claim-filing deadline (I did not read that section)

items.title: Segal AmeriCorps Education Award transferable to your children or grandchildren if you serve at 55+
items.who: Anyone who was 55 or older when starting an approved national service term and completed it
items.value: The Segal Education Award can be transferred to a child, stepchild, foster child, grandchild or step-grandchild; recipient must use it within 10 years of your service completion and cannot exceed two full-time awards in total.
items.how: Complete the term, then transfer through your AmeriCorps member portal.
items.hack: Retired veterans who spend a year in AmeriCorps Seniors-age service can convert it into a grandchild's tuition fund. Confirm which programs carry an award.
items.deadline: Recipient must use within 10 years of your completion

items.title: Hmong and Laotian 'secret war' veterans national cemetery eligibility
items.org: VA National Cemetery Administration (Hmong Veterans' Service Recognition Act)
items.who: Certain Hmong and Laotian-American veterans of the Vietnam-era secret war in Laos who die on or after the law's enactment (March 23, 2018)
items.value: Burial in U.S. national cemeteries other than Arlington. NBC reporting did not specify exact criteria; a 2015 veterans-group estimate said 6,900 to 9,700 people could qualify.
items.how: Contact the National Cemetery Scheduling Office and ask for an eligibility determination; I did not verify which documents are accepted.
items.hack: Families should assemble service evidence now (pre-need determination) rather than at time of death.
items.deadline: Applies to deaths on or after March 23, 2018

items.title: VA Compensated Work Therapy - paid vocational program run by VA health care
items.who: Veterans with barriers to employment, referred through VA; the Fargo VA page did not list eligibility rules
items.value: Transitional Work in real settings (community, federal or VA) with vocational counseling every two weeks, and Supported Employment that helps veterans find and keep paid jobs. Page says transitional participants are not federal employees and does not state pay for that track.
items.how: Ask your VA medical center's vocational rehabilitation or mental health team for a CWT referral; each medical center has a point of contact.
items.hack: CWT work history can serve as a bridge for veterans with long gaps and is separate from VR&E Chapter 31.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Operation Warfighter - internships at federal agencies for wounded service members
items.org: DoD Warrior Care / federal host agencies
items.who: Wounded, ill or injured service members in recovery (not yet separated)
items.value: Unpaid-by-host internship placements at federal agencies while on military pay, building resumes and civilian experience. I did not fetch the DoD page; status inferred from recent DLA and DOI program pages.
items.how: Contact your recovery care coordinator or Recovery Care Program; see the DoD Warrior Care OWF page.
items.hack: Intern at the agency you eventually want to be hired into; many hosts hire OWF interns via noncompetitive authorities (30% disabled veterans, Schedule A).
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: ABLE account age-of-onset now 46 - tax-advantaged savings that protect SSI for disabled veterans
items.who: People whose disability began before age 46 (raised from 26 effective January 1, 2026); meets Social Security's disability definition. Veterans on VA disability, SSI or SSDI may already meet it.
items.value: Tax-free growth and withdrawals for qualified disability expenses. One source says balances up to $100,000 generally do not count toward the $2,000 SSI resource limit; $20,000 annual contribution limit in 2026. Medicaid effects were not addressed.
items.how: Open an account in any state plan that accepts out-of-state residents.
items.hack: Eligibility turns on when the disability began, not when it was diagnosed - TBI and PTSD that began in service but were diagnosed later can qualify.
items.deadline: None

items.title: DoD reimbursement of military spouse relicensing and business-move costs after a PCS
items.who: Spouses of service members of any rank who PCS across state lines and held a license or owned a business at a prior duty station
items.value: Up to $1,000 for relicensing/certification costs per move plus up to $1,000 for qualified business costs, per the Air Force benefits page. Business costs apply to orders authenticated on or after December 23, 2022.
items.how: Get the new license first, then file within 24 months of PCS order authentication with receipts, orders, licenses from both stations and business-ownership proof at your finance office.
items.hack: Costs must be paid after orders are authenticated; keep every receipt. Not authorized for accession, retirement or separation moves.
items.deadline: 24 months from PCS orders authentication

items.title: Wisconsin Subsistence Aid and Health Care Aid - state-paid dental, vision, hearing and income-loss grants
items.who: Wisconsin veterans in need who have exhausted other aid; also unremarried surviving spouses/dependent children of eligible veterans and families of activated or deployed Wisconsin service members (loss-of-income test)
items.value: Per WDVA's page: dental up to $800 per 12 months (or $4,000 per 24 months extended dental), vision up to $400 per 12 months, hearing up to $200 per 12 months plus up to $1,875 per hearing aid per 24 months, and subsistence aid up to $3,000 in any 12 months. Combined lifetime cap $7,500.
items.how: Apply through your County or Tribal Veterans Service Office; WDVA pays providers directly under a Description of Benefits. Subsistence applications within 12 months of the income loss.
items.hack: Because aid pays providers directly, get a dental or hearing estimate first, then ask the CVSO to submit. Check funding with your CVSO before applying.
items.deadline: Ongoing; subsistence aid within 12 months of verified income loss

items.title: Oregon Veterans' Emergency Financial Assistance Program (OVEFAP) - one-time bill payment
items.who: Oregon-resident veterans discharged under honorable conditions, or their unremarried surviving spouse, dependent child or stepchild, with immediate financial need
items.value: One-time payment of emergency housing and related costs (utilities, insurance, house repairs), mortgage or rent, emergency medical or dental, and emergency transportation. State of Oregon pays the creditor directly; award amounts vary. Cannot pay credit cards, taxes or fines.
items.how: Complete form VS1024 with a cover letter, submit through a Veteran Service Office or Veteran Advocate by the 10th of the month. Phone ODVA 503-373-2085.
items.hack: Incomplete applications are returned, so use the completion checklist; the cover letter must say what other support you have already tried.
items.deadline: 10th of every month

items.title: New Jersey Catastrophic Entitlement for permanently disabled veterans and surviving spouses
items.org: New Jersey Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (N.J.S.A. 38:18A-1)
items.who: New Jersey veterans with a VA-rated permanent service-connected catastrophic disability: loss of sight; amputation of both hands, both feet or a hand and a foot; hemiplegia; paraplegia; quadriplegia; and specified combinations with loss of use of legs. Surviving spouses covered.
items.value: A state entitlement for catastrophic service-connected disability. The application form I read does not state the payment amount.
items.how: Submit the NJ DMAVA Catastrophic Entitlement application with proof of residency; surviving spouses add the marriage and death certificates.
items.hack: Ask whether the veteran was already receiving it at death - the form uses that to determine the surviving spouse's route.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: New York Lifetime Liberty Pass - free state park access now open to ALL New York veterans
items.who: New York resident veterans and Gold Star family members (a 2023 law, S.3309A, removed the old disability requirement)
items.value: Free access to state parks, historic sites and recreation facilities. A 2014 release also mentioned boat launches; scope today should be confirmed with State Parks.
items.how: Apply through NY State Parks' Lifetime Liberty Pass page with veteran verification.
items.hack: Many New York veterans still believe it requires a 40% rating; that applied before the 2023 change.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Connecticut free veteran bus pass (launched July 31, 2026)
items.org: Connecticut Departments of Veterans Affairs and Transportation
items.who: Connecticut veterans verified by a VA Veteran Health ID card, Connecticut license with veteran flag, or non-driver ID with veteran indicator
items.value: Free bus travel on CTtransit (including CTfastrak), Greater Bridgeport Transit, HART, Milford Transit, Northeastern and Northwestern CT Transit, Norwalk Transit, River Valley Transit, SEAT and WRTD. Buses only, not rail.
items.how: Apply online, verify identity, select the routes you need. Passes last about 30-31 days and renewals are mailed. Questions: DVABusPasses@ct.gov.
items.hack: Request only the routes you need; renew early since replacement passes are mailed.
items.deadline: Monthly renewal

items.title: Sun Metro 'Vets Ride Free' - El Paso fixed route, Brio and paratransit
items.org: Sun Metro (El Paso, TX), funded by a Texas Veterans Commission grant
items.who: Veterans, eligible dependents and surviving spouses in the El Paso service area
items.value: 30-day free passes for Fixed Route, Brio and LIFT paratransit. Program runs September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027 'or until funding is available', first-come, first-served.
items.how: Online Application for Texas Veterans or call 915-212-3333. Past participants do not need to reapply.
items.hack: Funds are first-come, so apply early in the program year.
items.deadline: Through August 31, 2027 or until funds run out

items.title: Florida waives initial professional license fees for veterans AND their spouses
items.org: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation / Health (Fla. Stat. 456.024)
items.who: Honorably discharged veterans and their spouses; also health care practitioners who served in the Armed Forces/Guard/Reserve/USPHS and active-duty spouses seeking licensure
items.value: The statute waives initial licensing, initial application and initial unlicensed activity fees for veterans and spouses. It does not mention examination fees or waive them.
items.how: Apply to the relevant Florida board; claim the veteran/spouse waiver on the application.
items.hack: The waiver applies to the spouse of a veteran, not only active duty; exam fees still apply.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Maryland Conroy Memorial Scholarship - tuition aid including disabled veterans with 25%+ rating who exhausted GI Bill
items.who: Maryland residents: children or surviving spouses of service members who died from service or are 100% permanently disabled; veterans with 25%+ service-connected disability who have exhausted federal education benefits; certain 9/11, POW/MIA and public-safety families
items.value: Maximum 2026-27 award $14,086, capped at in-state tuition and mandatory fees at the highest-cost USM four-year institution; subject to funding.
items.how: Apply through your school's financial aid office by July 15 each year.
items.hack: The 25% veteran category is easy to miss; it is for veterans who ran out of or cannot use federal benefits.
items.deadline: July 15 annually

items.title: Ohio county Veterans Service Commission emergency aid (rent, utilities, food) - example: Lake County
items.who: Lake County example: veterans with honorable discharge and DD-214, residents 3+ months, plus survivors and dependent children, with financial need; no VA rating mentioned
items.value: Emergency, temporary assistance with rent or mortgage, utilities and food from a Soldiers' & Sailors' Relief Fund mandated by Ohio law. Not for income supplement or major home improvement. Other Ohio counties differ.
items.how: Call your county VSC (Lake County: 440-350-2904); packet and appointment required; Lake County stopped accepting email/fax applications August 1, 2023.
items.hack: Each of Ohio's 88 counties has its own commission and rules; call your own rather than relying on a neighbor's.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: California county recorders issue certified copies of recorded DD-214s at no fee
items.who: Veterans, family members, legal representatives and benefit agencies, with notarized application and ID
items.value: Monterey's page states there is no fee for a certified copy of a recorded military discharge. Search is by name and discharge or recording year.
items.how: Mail a notarized, sworn application with photo ID photocopy to the county recorder; each county has its own form.
items.hack: If you recorded your DD-214 years ago, the county copy is a free backup if NPRC is slow. The page did not say why or whether recording itself is free.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Indiana Military Family Relief Fund
items.who: Indiana service members and families, per IDVA's application; I read only the search listing, not the eligibility rules
items.value: Grant program with a current 2026 application revision published by IDVA. Amounts not read.
items.how: Use IDVA's MFRF application (revised July 2026) via your county veterans service officer.
items.hack: Verify eligibility rules on the form before applying; I did not verify them.
items.deadline: Unknown

items.title: AgrAbility - state university projects helping farmers and ranchers with disabilities
items.org: USDA NIFA-funded AgrAbility projects at state land-grant universities
items.who: Farmers, ranchers and farm workers with disabilities, including injured veterans; project list varies
items.value: On-farm assessments and assistive technology guidance via state AgrAbility projects. I saw listings but did not read program rules.
items.how: Search 'AgrAbility' with your state; contact your state land-grant extension project.
items.hack: Veteran-farmer overlap with NRCS and FSA lanes - ask the project for referrals.
items.deadline: Varies

items.title: UA Veterans in Piping (VIP) - no-cost welding, HVACR and fire-suppression training on base
items.org: United Association of Plumbers and Pipefitters
items.who: Active-duty personnel preparing to transition; the page does not address whether separated veterans can apply
items.value: Page says 'No cost to participants', training on-base, GI Bill not required; graduates are guaranteed direct entry into a UA-registered apprenticeship and placement with a signatory contractor after discharge. Sites named include Camp Pendleton, JBLM, Fort Carson, Fort Cavazos, Camp Lejeune, Fort Campbell and Naval Station Norfolk.
items.how: Apply via uavip.org for the nearest installation program; coordinate with your command for SkillBridge or similar release.
items.hack: Nearby-installation members are encouraged to apply to the closest site. Program length not stated on the page.
items.deadline: Cohort dates on uavip.org (not confirmed)

items.title: IBEW Veterans Electrical Entry Program (VEEP) - free pre-apprenticeship with direct-entry agreements
items.who: Servicemembers in their final months and veterans, any MOS, per Local 1547 organizer
items.value: A free seven-week pre-apprenticeship; participants rank four IBEW programs and organizers secure direct-entry agreements. Article is from 2019; later coverage shows expansion including California locations.
items.how: Check ibew.org VEEP pages and your nearest IBEW JATC; Anchorage's version is at alaskaelectricalapprenticeship.org/veep.
items.hack: Even a participant who did not finish got a direct-entry agreement in the first class, per the article.
items.deadline: Cohorts vary

items.title: NPower Tech Fundamentals - free 20-week virtual IT training for veterans and military spouses
items.who: Veterans and military spouses over 21 and authorized to work in the U.S., in or near listed cities; veterans must be in SkillBridge, honorably discharged or in Guard/Reserve
items.value: Free instructor-led virtual training up to 20 weeks with chances at CompTIA A+, IT Fundamentals+, Google IT Support Certificate and an apprenticeship credential, plus paid internship or project opportunities. No stipend stated.
items.how: Apply at npower.org/apply-vet. Cities listed: Baltimore, Dallas, San Antonio, Houston, Detroit, Jersey City, Newark, St. Louis, Kansas City, Raleigh, Dayton.
items.hack: The page I read said the next cohort began February 2025, so it is stale; confirm current start dates.
items.deadline: Cohort-based

items.title: Tuck Next Step - Dartmouth business program for veterans at a fraction of the usual price
items.who: Recently separated veterans (about 9 months) with 3+ years service wanting a business career; not for existing MBA holders
items.value: Not free: AGI-based fee of $2,500 (AGI under $70,000) up to $6,000 (AGI $120,000+) for a program the page says compares to about $32,000. Covers tuition, accommodation and most meals; need-based aid for first-round applicants. Post-9/11 GI Bill cannot currently be used.
items.how: Apply via Tuck's Next Step page; 85 hours of instruction, two virtual weeks plus one on-campus week in Hanover NH (2027 dates March 8-12, March 22-26, April 4-9).
items.hack: Apply in the first round to be eligible for need-based aid.
items.deadline: First-round applications for aid; 2027 cohort

items.title: Warrior PATHH (Boulder Crest) - free posttraumatic growth program with travel and lodging covered
items.org: Boulder Crest Foundation and partner sites
items.who: Military, veterans and first responders; partner pages did not list detailed criteria
items.value: Page says participants receive travel, lodging, food and services at no personal expense. Partner sites: GratitudeAmerica (FL), Camp Southern Ground (GA), Travis Mills Foundation (ME), Big Red Barn Retreat (SC), Sheep Dog Impact Assistance (AR/MO), Permission to Start Dreaming (WA).
items.how: Contact Boulder Crest or a partner listed on bouldercrest.org.
items.hack: Several partners are separate organizations with their own intake - try more than one.
items.deadline: Cohorts vary

items.title: Warrior Care Network - intensive outpatient PTSD/TBI treatment at academic medical centers
items.org: Wounded Warrior Project with Emory, Rush, MGH/Home Base, UCLA and others
items.who: Post-9/11 veterans with PTSD or TBI; I did not fetch eligibility details
items.value: Search results describe a free multi-week intensive program; Emory announced an expansion for Texas veterans in June 2026. I did not read cost or travel terms.
items.how: Start at woundedwarriorproject.org Warrior Care Network page.
items.hack: Self-referral is possible through the partner clinic; verify.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Project EverGreen GreenCare for Troops - donated lawn care, now extending to disabled veterans in six states
items.who: Military families during deployment nationwide; from March 2026 also disabled veterans in Georgia, Massachusetts, Michigan, New York, Pennsylvania and Texas
items.value: Free lawn, landscape and snow-removal services by local professional volunteers for the length of a deployment, often 6-12 months; eligible veterans can receive up to one year and reapply annually, subject to volunteer availability.
items.how: Visit ProjectEverGreen.org; the release gave no application steps.
items.hack: Availability depends on a local volunteer, so apply early and ask which pros serve your ZIP.
items.deadline: Ongoing

items.title: Progressive Keys to Progress - a donated vehicle for veterans, nominated by a sponsor
items.who: Veterans (DD-214), active-duty E-4 and below, spouses of overseas E-4 and below, Gold Star; household income below 250% of the federal poverty guidelines; license with no major infractions in 7 years; no vehicle or hardship
items.value: A free vehicle through a yearly giveaway; a sponsor (nonprofit, veteran organization or professional who knows your need) must submit the application. 2026 giveaway event was set for November 10, 2026.
items.how: Email KeysToProgress@progressive.com during the entry period to request an application, then have a qualified sponsor submit it.
items.hack: Line up a sponsor before the next entry period (2026's ran April 3 to August 7). Incomplete applications are not flagged to you.
items.deadline: 2026 entry period closed August 7, 2026; watch for the spring 2027 window

items.title: VFW National Home for Children - on-campus housing and programs for military and veteran families
items.org: VFW National Home for Children, Eaton Rapids MI
items.who: Military and veteran families with children
items.value: Eaton Rapids campus homes in a 'goal oriented program of support and services', plus nationwide support, referrals and events. Page does not say housing is free or give length of stay.
items.how: Contact info@vfwnationalhome.org or the phone numbers on vfwnationalhome.org (the page listed 800-424-8360 and 866-483-9642 without labels).
items.hack: Ask about nationwide support if you cannot relocate to Michigan.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: American Legion Legacy Scholarship - children of those who died on duty since 9/11 or post-9/11 veterans rated 50%+
items.who: Children of military members who died on active duty on or after September 11, 2001, or children of post-9/11 veterans with a combined VA rating of 50% or more; high school senior or graduate accepted to an accredited college; needs-based
items.value: Needs-based scholarship; the 2026 cycle awarded over $1.7 million to 669 children per Legion news. Per-student amount not read.
items.how: Apply on legion.org; applications opened January 1 in the past cycle.
items.hack: Legion membership was not stated as required; verify.
items.deadline: 2026 cycle closed March 25, 2026; next cycle expected to open January 1

items.title: Camp Corral - free summer camp for children of wounded, injured or fallen military parents
items.who: Children of wounded, injured, ill or fallen service members; DAV published a 2026 registration memo
items.value: Free summer camp. Terms read from search listings only.
items.how: Register via campcorral.org camps page.
items.hack: Registration opens early in the year; check state camp sites.
items.deadline: Spring registration

items.title: Our Military Kids - grants for children's activities when a parent is deployed or wounded
items.who: Children of deployed National Guard/Reserve and of combat-wounded or fallen service members; recent 2026 releases mention toddler and pre-K activity funding
items.value: Grants for sports, arts and tutoring. Amounts not read.
items.how: Apply at ourmilitarykids.org/apply.
items.hack: Ask which activity categories are currently funded; they changed in 2026.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Starkey Hear Now - hearing aids for an application fee
items.who: Low-income people who cannot afford hearing aids; income limits not printed in the brochure
items.value: Hearing aids for only an application fee: a $300 fee invoiced after approval, per the brochure.
items.how: Apply online; clinic orders aids after approval and fee payment; (855) 686-2202.
items.hack: Compare with VA hearing aids first (free for enrolled veterans); this suits veterans outside VA care or family members.
items.deadline: Rolling

items.title: Heroes to Hives - free beekeeping training for veterans (Missouri and other states)
items.org: University of Missouri Extension (also Michigan State, others)
items.who: Military veterans; Missouri's 2026 sign-up was announced as open
items.value: Beekeeping education aimed at veterans in agriculture. Cost terms not read.
items.how: See Missouri Extension Heroes to Hives page.
items.hack: Check your own state's extension office for a sister program.
items.deadline: Missouri 2026 sign-up closed February 28

items.title: Veterans Fire Corps - paid AmeriCorps wildland fire crews for veterans
items.who: Veterans; positions listed in Arizona, West Virginia and elsewhere
items.value: AmeriCorps crew member and crew leader roles in partnership with agencies such as the US Forest Service. Pay and award terms not read.
items.how: Search the Corps Network or Conservation Job Board for 'Veterans Fire Corps'.
items.hack: Fire crew experience helps with later federal wildland firefighter hiring.
items.deadline: Seasonal

items.title: Warrior Expeditions - free long-distance thru-hike, bike or paddle for veterans
items.who: Veterans; 2026 coverage shows an active program with trail communities welcoming hikers
items.value: Support for multi-month thru-hikes. Details of gear and stipend not read.
items.how: Apply through warriorexpeditions.org.
items.hack: Applications are seasonal.
items.deadline: Seasonal

items.title: Knights of Columbus Warriors to Lourdes - military pilgrimage to Lourdes, France
items.who: Wounded, ill and injured military members and veterans; 2026 brochure published
items.value: A Catholic-led annual international pilgrimage, reported by the Catholic Telegraph headline as at no cost for veterans in 2025. I did not read the 2026 terms.
items.how: See the K of C 2026 press release and brochure.
items.hack: The event is open to those of other faiths; confirm in the brochure.
items.deadline: Annual (spring)

items.title: Wounded Warriors in Action - hunting and fishing trips for combat-wounded Purple Heart recipients
items.who: Purple Heart recipients and wounded veterans
items.value: Local news covers annual hunting and fishing weekends; terms not read.
items.how: Apply through the foundation's website.
items.hack: Events are regional; ask about your state.
items.deadline: Annual events

items.title: Veterans Curation Program - paid archaeology curation jobs for veterans
items.who: Veterans; sites in several cities per coverage
items.value: Paid training in artifact curation and archives work. I did not verify current openings.
items.how: Search the Veterans Curation Program and USAJOBS.
items.hack: Short training stints can lead to federal archival and museum technician roles.
items.deadline: Per posting

items.title: ABA Military Pro Bono Project - volunteer attorneys for junior enlisted service members
items.who: Financially eligible junior-enlisted active-duty members and families; referral comes from a military attorney, not self-referral
items.value: Placement with a volunteer civilian attorney for civil legal issues. ABA staff do not provide representation.
items.how: Ask your installation legal assistance office to submit a referral to the ABA Military Pro Bono Project.
items.hack: Operation Stand-By is a separate service where civilian attorneys advise military lawyers; it does not take direct clients.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Limbs for Life Foundation - free prosthetic leg for uninsured or denied amputees
items.who: Lower-extremity amputees (veterans included, not veteran-only) who are U.S. citizens or green-card holders, at or near the federal poverty level, with no coverage or a denial, and who pass a background check
items.value: Free prosthetic components and financial support paid directly to your clinic; partner clinics supply the leg, sockets and lifetime free adjustments on that socket
items.how: Apply on the printable form or online portal at limbsforlife.org/get-help/forms/ with proof of citizenship and a current physician prescription; you need a partnering prosthetic clinic willing to take the contracted rate. Phone 888-235-5462.
items.hack: If VA prosthetics or insurance already denied you, include the denial; the program is built for denials. One application only, since multiple applications do not improve odds. Arms, hands, partial-foot and swim legs are excluded.
items.deadline: Rolling, year-round; approval can take 1 to 6 months and is not guaranteed

items.title: Posse Veterans Program - team-based full-tuition scholarship at partner colleges
items.who: U.S. Armed Forces veterans who want a bachelor's degree at a top college; selected through a three-stage interview process and attend as a team (a Veterans Posse)
items.value: Partner colleges provide supplemental funding to cover full tuition; one-month pre-collegiate training in New York City, weekly faculty mentoring in the first two years, and a Career Program
items.how: Candidates come through the Veteran Nominations route, then the Dynamic Assessment Process (group interview with college representatives). Start at possefoundation.org/veterans-program.
items.hack: Stack with Post-9/11 GI Bill and Yellow Ribbon for living costs; ask your school's veterans office or a veteran-serving nonprofit to nominate you early. Verify the current partner college list and cycle dates on Posse's nomination page; the main page names Wesleyan, Vassar and Dartmouth only in stories.
items.deadline: Nomination-based; cycle dates not stated on the program page, check Posse's Veteran Nominations page

items.title: Remote Area Medical pop-up clinics - free dental, vision and medical care, no insurance needed
items.who: Anyone, including uninsured and underinsured veterans and families (the page has no veteran-specific program)
items.value: Free dental, vision and general medical care at volunteer-run pop-up clinics; a telehealth program in Tennessee pairs an on-site nurse with a remote volunteer physician
items.how: Check the clinic schedule at ramusa.org/schedule/ and walk in; clinics run first-come, first-served. Phone (865) 579-1530.
items.hack: Arrive very early; first-come, first-served clinics fill by dawn. Useful for dental and vision gaps the VA does not cover at your rating.
items.deadline: Clinic-by-clinic; check the schedule page for current dates

items.title: Semper K9 Assistance Dogs - free service dogs for wounded service members and their families
items.who: Wounded service members and their families; page tags PTS/PTSD and TBI; a Family Integration Program serves caregivers and children in the DMV area who already have a dog from an accredited provider
items.value: Service dog trained to the recipient's needs at no cost, and no fee to participate
items.how: No application steps are listed on the page; contact info@semperk9.org or (571) 494-5144.
items.hack: Ask about the Family Integration Program if your spouse or child already has a service dog; DMV area only.
items.deadline: Not stated

items.title: GRID Alternatives Troops to Solar - no-cost solar installation training for veterans
items.who: Veterans who want solar installation experience (the source article describes it as no-cost and aimed at transitioning military skills)
items.value: No-cost solar installation training, on-the-job training, and hiring help through job fairs and solar contractor partners
items.how: Contact GRID or its regional office; the source is a July 2015 article from GRID's Inland Empire region, so program availability and the application route need confirming.
items.hack: Ask your regional GRID office whether Troops to Solar cohorts are currently running and whether the training is SkillBridge eligible.
items.deadline: Unverified; the page read is dated 2015

items.title: Navy SEAL Foundation - one-time Veterans Assistance Fund grant and family support
items.who: Active-duty NSW members and families (via the Special Operations Warrior Care Program), SEAL and SWCC veterans regardless of years of service, wounded/ill/injured members, and surviving families
items.value: Education grants and scholarships, medical support not covered by TRICARE, NSW kids' camps, respite childcare, a one-time Veterans Assistance Fund grant, tragedy assistance, and surviving-family help (mortgage and home-maintenance stipends, counseling, school grants, retreats)
items.how: Veterans apply at nsw.navysealfoundation.org/veteran-support/; active duty, family and wounded members use the online form on the Request Support page; surviving families email the contact listed there. General line 757-744-5326.
items.hack: The foundation also routes SEAL/SWCC veterans to the Headstrong Project (mental health, any discharge) and to Soteria for cancer. The page states no fees and no deadlines.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Green Beret Foundation - free casualty, health, family and VA-claims support for Special Forces families
items.who: Pre- and Post-9/11 Special Forces-qualified soldiers and their immediate families, caregivers and Gold Star families (documents showing SF qualification required)
items.value: Casualty support (the page cites a $2,500 check for family travel the Army does not cover), alternative therapies and adaptive equipment, scholarships for spouses and children, grief counseling and funeral help, and free VA claims help
items.how: Submit a request at greenberetfoundation.org/request-support/ with a redacted ERB, ORB, Soldier Talent Profile or DD214; staff contact you within 3 business days. Active duty goes through Care Coalition first (1-877-672-3039).
items.hack: Upload every required document with the first submission to speed things up. For VA claims, start about two years before separation; anyone charging to guarantee a rating is a fraud.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Marine Raider Foundation - one-time transition grants and certification costs for transitioning Raiders
items.who: Active-duty Marine Raiders who are transitioning out of the military
items.value: Mentorship, certification/license/test-prep costs the GI Bill does not cover, and one-time transition grants for civilian job-search costs such as work attire, travel, education and technology (a testimonial cites a $2,000 grant; no standard amount is stated)
items.how: The page does not describe the process; it points to marineraiderfoundation.org/get-support/.
items.hack: Ask for certification and test-prep costs specifically; they are for items the GI Bill does not pay.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Guardian Angels Medical Service Dogs - service dogs for PTS, TBI and MST
