items.who: Applicants with conditions including PTS, TBI, military sexual trauma, seizure, diabetic and mobility disabilities; veterans are featured (no separate veteran program stated)
items.value: A trained medical service dog at no cost per the site description; dogs placed in 33 states. Travel and other expenses to Williston are not addressed on the page
items.how: Submit the online Service Dog Application request form, an inquiry team member emails you, then a full qualification process follows; approved applicants travel to Williston, FL to be paired. Phone 800-398-6102. Falsified information can lead to refusal. The page lists no veteran-specific rules.
items.hack: Ask about waitlist length and travel costs; the page states neither.
items.deadline: Not stated

items.title: NEADS Service Dogs for Veterans - mobility and hearing dogs, service connection not required
items.who: U.S. veterans with a permanent physical disability or hearing loss, or MS or another progressive condition; the condition does not need to be service-related
items.value: A service dog that fetches, opens doors, braces for transfers and more, or a hearing dog that alerts to sounds
items.how: Take the Prequalifying Questionnaire on the NEADS veterans page; further steps follow. Cost and wait times are not stated on the page.
items.hack: The non-service-connected eligibility is the gap: veterans below the VA rating cutoff can still qualify here.
items.deadline: Not stated

items.title: Dolphin Scholarship Foundation - college awards for children and spouses of Navy submariners
items.who: Sons, daughters and spouses of Navy submariners facing financial obstacles in undergraduate or vocational education
items.value: Annual awards of $3,000 to $4,500 and up to $18,000 in total over up to eight semesters (as stated on the foundation page)
items.how: See the Eligibility and Application FAQ pages on dolphinscholarship.org; dates are not on the page read.
items.hack: Apply every year of eligibility; the page shows the multi-semester total.
items.deadline: Not stated on the page read; check dolphinscholarship.org

items.title: Hap Arnold Education Grant - need-based college grant for Air Force and Space Force children and spouses
items.who: Children (under 24 during the award year) and spouses of active, extended-active-duty Guard/Reserve, retired or deceased Airmen and Guardians, with a 2.0 GPA, full-time undergraduate or vocational study
items.value: Need-based grant (amount varies yearly by applicants, budget, Student Aid Index and cost of attendance; no fixed amount stated)
items.how: File the FAFSA and the Air Force Aid Society application; instructions and a timeline are on afas.org/haparnoldgrant/. Contact the Education Department at (703) 972-2647 or by email.
items.hack: Excludes veterans, Guard/Reserve and other-branch members as applicants. The grant is for dependents; file the FAFSA first because the award depends on your Student Aid Index.
items.deadline: 2026-27 applications are closed; 2027-28 applications open in early January 2027

items.title: Army Scholarship Foundation undergraduate scholarships for soldiers' children and spouses
items.who: Children and spouses of active, Reserve or National Guard Army members in good standing, and children of former members honorably or medically discharged or killed while serving; 2.0 GPA, U.S. citizen, family AGI $160,000 or less, no prior bachelor's degree
items.value: Undergraduate scholarship (amount not stated on the page)
items.how: Submit the online application with proof of service, transcripts, IRS Form 1040, FAFSA summary, photo and an essay of 325 words or fewer.
items.hack: Pull the FAFSA Submission Summary and the Form 1040 early; they are the slowest items.
items.deadline: Due April 15 each year; the 2026-27 window is closed, 2027-28 dates not yet posted

items.title: Dog Tag Inc. Fellowship - 5-month business and leadership program in Washington, DC
items.who: Veterans, military spouses and caregivers
items.value: A 5-month fellowship; the page does not state tuition, stipend or cost
items.how: Use the Apply Now link on dogtaginc.org/fellowship; phone (202) 407-9609.
items.hack: Ask what the fellowship costs and what support it pays before relying on it; the page does not say.
items.deadline: Not stated

items.title: Stop Soldier Suicide ROGER - free confidential counseling and safety planning for any veteran
items.who: All U.S. veterans and service members regardless of branch, generation or discharge status; proof of service not required; loved ones can also reach out
items.value: Free confidential virtual counseling, crisis intervention and safety planning; also a veteran firearm safety program
items.how: Call 844-647-1354 or use Get Help at goroger.org/get-help. The FAQ lists a different line, 984-207-3260 for immediate support; the page does not explain the difference.
items.hack: No VA rating or enrollment required, so it fills the gap for bad-paper veterans.
items.deadline: None; ongoing

items.title: NAMI Homefront - free 6-session course for family and friends of service members and veterans
items.who: Families, caregivers and friends of service members and veterans with mental health conditions, including those currently serving
items.value: Free 6-session educational program based on NAMI Family-to-Family; 2026 classes meet Tuesdays or Thursdays 6:30 to 8:30 PM ET in quarterly sessions
items.how: Use the 'Find the NAMI Homefront nearest to you' link at nami.org/Homefront, or call the NAMI HelpLine 800-950-6264 (M-F, 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. ET) or text NAMI to 62640.
items.hack: If no class is near you, ask your local NAMI affiliate to start one.
items.deadline: Quarterly sessions in 2026; check the finder

items.title: Operation Homefront Back-to-School Brigade - free backpacks and school supplies for military kids
items.who: DEERS-enrolled military dependent children in grades K-12
items.value: Free back-to-school supplies including backpacks, handed out at events, first-come, first-served
items.how: Register through the events page at operationhomefront.org/events/ or the organization's Facebook page; the page lists no specific dates.
items.hack: Supplies are limited; register as soon as your local event posts.
items.deadline: Summer events; no specific 2026 dates on the page

items.title: NCOA Scholarship Fund - $900 per year for children and spouses of NCOA members
items.who: Children (under 25 for the initial grant) and spouses of current NCOA members, in undergraduate study at an accredited school
items.value: $900 per school year paid to the school for tuition, room and board, fees and books (per the fact sheet read)
items.how: Complete application packages must reach NCOA headquarters by March 31; a committee selects recipients in June and notifies only those chosen.
items.hack: Membership is the gate; the fact sheet read is an older PDF, so confirm current dollar amount and form before you rely on it.
items.deadline: March 31 each year

items.title: Home Depot Foundation Path to Pro - free 12-week skilled trades training at 10 bases
items.org: Home Depot Foundation with Home Builders Institute
items.who: Transitioning service members and veterans with a valid driver's license and a computer with internet (per a Military.com article, not the official page)
items.value: Free training for construction, remodeling, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, roofing, welding and more; HBI course runs 12 weeks, about 75% hands-on; SkillBridge eligible
items.how: The article points to the Military section of the Home Depot Foundation site and to HBI for enrollment; training sites include Camp Pendleton, Fort Bliss, Fort Bragg, Fort Campbell, Fort Carson, Fort Hood, Fort Riley, Fort Stewart, NAS Jacksonville and Naval Station Norfolk.
items.hack: Use SkillBridge to train while still drawing military pay, up to 180 days before separation. Confirm sites and dates with the Home Depot Foundation; only a news article was read.
items.deadline: Unverified

items.title: WAVES Project - scuba diving trips for veterans with service-connected injuries (Temecula, CA based)
items.who: American veterans with service-connected injuries (amputations, spinal cord or neurological injuries, PTSD) and their families
items.value: Group scuba trips led by experienced divers; the annual trip to CocoView Resort in Roatan, Honduras is the most popular, and the March 2027 trip includes limited training toward new certifications
items.how: Email info@wavesproject.com (the page notes the .com domain differs from the .org site) or call 951-308-0049. Space is limited. Office: Temecula, CA.
items.hack: The page lists no trip price, so ask whether trips are fully sponsored before booking travel.
items.deadline: Space limited; March 2027 trip is the one the page names

items.title: Boot Campaign - Health and Wellness program and Seasons of Service gifts at zero cost
items.who: Veterans of any era and every branch, and active-duty military families facing financial or medical hardship (Seasons of Service)
items.value: Health and Wellness programming aimed at TBI, PTSD, chronic pain and insomnia, plus curated gifts and services for families in hardship; the 2025 fact sheet says programs served 2,410 people in 2024 at zero cost to them
items.how: The fact sheet gives no application steps; contact (214) 233-6519 or info@bootcampaign.org.
items.hack: Ask which program fits when you call; the fact sheet does not list formal eligibility criteria.
items.deadline: Not stated

items.title: Veterans Yoga Project - 100+ free weekly yoga, breathwork and yoga nidra classes
items.who: Veterans, active-duty members, reservists, family members and supporters
items.value: Free weekly online and in-person yoga and breathwork classes at all levels, including chair yoga and yoga nidra (the class flyer marks them FREE)
items.how: Online classes at veteransyogaproject.org/vyp-classes; in-person classes by region at veteransyogaproject.org/regions. No sign-up process is described.
items.hack: Try the yoga nidra and chair classes if you have pain or sleep problems; they are free.
items.deadline: None; weekly

items.title: Project Hero (Ride 2 Recovery) - free rehabilitation bike rides, example hub in Pinellas, FL
items.who: Injured veterans and first responders; the local ride page says anyone is welcome to ride
items.value: Weekly group rehab rides (Mon, Thu, Sat on the Pinellas schedule); bike repair labor is free and veterans get free parts when available; loaner bikes can be arranged
items.how: The page read is a St. Petersburg College hub page: join the Project Hero Pinellas Facebook group or contact the hub representative listed on the page. Other hubs exist elsewhere; check Project Hero's own site.
items.hack: Ask your nearest hub about handcycles and adaptive bikes before buying equipment.
items.deadline: None; weekly rides

items.title: Avalon Action Alliance - single point of contact to match veterans with TBI, PTS and substance-abuse programs
items.org: Avalon Action Alliance (via The Warrior Alliance)
items.who: Veterans and first responders
items.value: Integrative assessment and a single point of contact matching clients to a network of 7 TBI centers, 11 posttraumatic growth programs and 2 substance-abuse treatment centers
items.how: Use the Get Assistance link at thewarrioralliance.org/register or call (404) 210-1776. The page states no costs, fees or intake process.
items.hack: Ask early whether the network program you are matched to bills TRICARE, VA Community Care or nothing, since the page does not say.
items.deadline: Not stated

items.title: Owens Corning Roof Deployment Project - donated roofing materials and contractor labor for veterans in need
items.who: Veterans in need of a roof (no formal criteria in the article read; contractors can also join)
items.value: Owens Corning donates materials and a contractor donates labor; a local article cites over 775 roofs donated nationally
items.how: A 2023 Owens Corning press release names owenscorning.com/roofdeployment for more information but describes no selection or application process; labor comes from its Platinum Preferred Contractors network.
items.hack: A participating roofing contractor can nominate you; ask local roofers whether they take part.

items.title: Tennessee THDA: veterans and their spouses skip the three-year first-time buyer rule
items.who: Veterans and their spouses buying in Tennessee with a THDA bond-financed mortgage
items.value: Waives the 'no ownership in the past three years' test, so a veteran who already owns or recently owned a home can still use THDA's below-market bond mortgage and its assistance products
items.how: THDA's First-Time Homebuyer Rule states veterans and their spouses do not have to meet the three-year requirement. 'Veteran' is defined by reference to 38 U.S.C. 101 (released under conditions other than dishonorable). The exception does not cover a veteran who has already received a bond-financed mortgage under this exception. Apply through a THDA-participating lender; the page does not give rates or amounts, so confirm current terms with the lender.
items.hack: If a lender tells you that you are disqualified because you 'already own a home,' ask specifically for the THDA veteran exception and have your DD-214 ready.

items.title: North Carolina: $15,000 down payment help and a mortgage tax credit open to eligible military veterans
items.who: First-time buyers OR eligible military veterans buying in North Carolina
items.value: NC 1st Home Advantage Down Payment: $15,000 as a 0% deferred second mortgage forgiven over years 11 to 15; NC Home Advantage Tax Credit: can reduce federal taxes by up to $2,000 per year (both as stated by NCHFA)
items.how: NCHFA's down payment page lists three alternative paths: first-time buyers, military veterans, or a targeted census tract; veterans do not need to be first-time buyers. The $15,000 is a 0%, deferred second mortgage forgiven 20% per year at the end of years 11 to 15, with complete forgiveness at the end of year 15. Requirements: NC Home Advantage Mortgage, credit score 640 or higher (660 for manufactured homes), income and sales price limits, principal residence within 60 days of closing. The page does not define 'military veteran,' so confirm with the lender.
items.hack: You must stay about 15 years to keep all of it; if you will sell sooner, the unforgiven portion comes due.
items.deadline: None stated; confirm funds availability with the lender

items.title: Florida Housing 'Salute Our Soldiers': forgivable down payment help for veterans and active duty
items.who: Florida veterans and active-duty service members buying a home
items.value: Per the Feb 2020 announcement: SOS PLUS forgivable DPA of 3%, 4% or 5% of purchase price forgiven 20% a year over five years; Florida Assist $7,500 at 0% (due on sale/refinance); HLP $10,000 at 3% over 15 years; reduced fees and no documentary stamp or intangible taxes on the note and mortgage
items.how: The press release says veterans are exempt from the first-time homebuyer requirement; active duty must not have owned a primary residence in the prior three years. Apply through a Florida Housing participating lender. This is a 2020 announcement with an up-to-$8 million allocation, so the program may have changed or be funded in rounds; verify it is open before relying on it. A November 11, 2021 Florida Housing release says it was offered exclusively to veterans and active-duty members across all 67 counties, with $8 million available and over 800 users by then; no end date or per-buyer maximum is stated.
items.hack: Compare SOS PLUS (forgivable) to Florida Assist (repayable at sale) with the lender; the forgivable one is usually cheaper if you stay five years.
items.deadline: Original program start March 2, 2020; current availability not verified

items.title: Texas TDHCA: veterans get a first-time buyer exception and are eligible for the Mortgage Credit Certificate
items.org: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)
items.who: Qualified veterans buying in Texas (separate from the Veterans Land Board loan)
items.value: My First Texas Home: down payment assistance with a 30-year mortgage, with qualified veterans eligible for exceptions to the first-time buyer requirement in targeted areas; Texas MCC: dollar-for-dollar reduction of federal tax liability, open to veterans on both the combined and stand-alone options
items.how: TDHCA's programs page names veterans for MFTH exceptions and for the TMCC. A homebuyer education course is required. The stand-alone MCC has no minimum credit score per the page, and supply is limited. The page does not mention Homes for Texas Heroes. Call 1-800-792-1119 or ask a TDHCA-participating lender.
items.hack: If you are not buying in a targeted area, ask about My Choice Texas Home, which does not require first-time buyer status.
items.deadline: MCC supply is limited; no date stated

items.title: MaineHousing Salute ME: 0.50% rate discount, and 'Salute Home Again' waives first-time buyer status
items.who: Maine veterans, active duty and retired military (honorably discharged; 180 days on active duty or in a war zone; National Guard who meet that test)
items.value: Salute ME: 0.50% discount off the First Home Loan 30-year fixed rate; Salute Home Again: waives the first-time homebuyer requirement for veterans who previously owned; optional Advantage feature up to $5,000 toward closing cash with a hoMEworks class and minimum 1% borrower contribution
items.how: Apply through a MaineHousing lender; income and purchase price limits apply and cannot be used to refinance a home you already own. Combines with FHA, RD, VA and others (Salute Home Again excludes the United Guaranty pilot). Questions: (207) 626-4663. MaineHousing's Salute ME FAQ (2022) adds: non-first-time buyers must provide discharge papers (DD Form 214) and/or an LES, must not have had a prior mortgage revenue bond loan, and must sell their current home by closing.
items.hack: Pair with the VA insurer option so you get both the state rate cut and no down payment.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Georgia Dream Peach Select Veterans Assistance: a state-set low-rate VA loan with 100% LTV
items.who: Georgia VA-loan borrowers who qualify for a traditional Georgia Dream VA loan (income under county limit, minimum credit score 640)
items.value: 30-year fixed at a low rate instead of down payment assistance; page shows an initial rate of 5.00%, reset weekly by DCA, with $500 minimum borrower investment and up to 100% loan-to-value. Price and income limits on the page are dated July 8, 2024.
items.how: Contact a Georgia Dream participating lender or call 1-800-359-HOME (4663). You cannot use this and the traditional Georgia Dream program together. Other non-Georgia-Dream down payment programs may be layered with DCA approval. Dollar and rate figures are as read on the page and may have been updated since.
items.hack: Compare against the traditional Georgia Dream DPA product: this one trades the assistance for a lower rate.
items.deadline: Open since March 15, 2024; those with a pending Georgia Dream application before that date had to cancel and reapply

items.title: Connecticut CHFA Military Homeownership Program: rate reduction plus down payment help
items.who: Veterans, full-time active duty, Reserve and National Guard; also unmarried surviving spouses of those who died of military service or service-connected disability
items.value: Adds a .125% rate reduction to CHFA's published rate (.25% in a Targeted Area); CHFA assistance loans available alongside the first mortgage with a $3,000 minimum assistance amount (per the brochure)
items.how: Must be a first-time buyer or not have owned in three years unless buying in a Targeted Area; sales price and income limits apply; free homebuyer education class required. The brochure revision is dated 7-27-2022, so confirm current terms. Apply via a CHFA participating lender or call 844-CT1-HOME.
items.hack: Check whether your target address is in a Targeted Area first; it doubles the rate reduction and removes the first-time test.
items.deadline: None stated; brochure dated 2022

items.title: Pennsylvania PHFA Keystone Home Loan: discharged veterans qualify even if not first-time buyers
items.who: Discharged U.S. Armed Forces veterans buying in Pennsylvania
items.value: Non-first-time buyers can use the Keystone Home Loan if they buy in a Targeted area or are a discharged veteran; VA loans under Keystone Government/Flex require no downpayment in most cases
items.how: Go through a PHFA participating lender; not every lender offers the VA/RD-backed options. The page does not provide rates or amounts.
items.hack: Ask the lender to price Keystone Government with a VA loan against a plain VA loan; PHFA assistance loans can sometimes cover closing costs.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: South Carolina Palmetto Heroes: $10,000 forgivable down payment help for veterans, reservists and active duty
items.who: At least one borrower who is active duty, reservist, National Guard or a veteran (active duty service other than training, discharge other than dishonorable) who meets first-time buyer rules
items.value: $10,000 down payment assistance as a 15-year forgivable zero-percent no-payment second mortgage, usable for down payment, closing costs and prepaids only
items.how: Program guide effective March 16, 2026; the rate is published daily by SC Housing. Needs an executed sales contract before locking; documented statement of service for military; cannot own another principal residence at closing. Apply through an SC Housing participating lender. CAUTION: SC Housing's homebuyers page describes Palmetto Heroes (2026) as now closed, so check whether funds remain before relying on it.
items.hack: Get a statement of service or DD-214 into the file at application; documentation is the usual cause of delay.
items.deadline: All loans must close and be purchased by SC Housing no later than December 31, 2026

items.title: Missouri MHDC First Place Loan: a 'qualified veteran' does not have to be a first-time buyer
items.who: Qualified veterans buying in Missouri
items.value: Exception to the first-time homebuyer requirement for the First Place Loan and the Mortgage Credit Certificate
items.how: MHDC's homebuyer programs overview says 'Qualified Veterans do not have to be first-time homebuyers' for the First Place Loan and defines a qualified veteran as 'any Veteran who served active duty and who applies for financing within 25 years after leaving active service.' Lender training material lists the same exception for the MCC. VA, FHA and USDA-Rural Development loans are eligible loan types.
items.hack: Check your separation date: the 25-year window is the test that quietly disqualifies older veterans.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Indiana IHCDA: an 'Eligible Veteran' is exempt from the first-time homebuyer requirement
items.org: Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority (IHCDA)
items.who: Eligible Veterans: served in the active military, naval or air service or the Indiana National Guard without a dishonorable discharge, or otherwise eligible for VA health benefits, verified by DD-214
items.value: Lets a veteran who is not a first-time buyer use IHCDA programs outside targeted areas
items.how: IHCDA's FAQ says outside targeted areas buyers must be first-time buyers 'unless purchasing in a targeted area, or you are a Qualified Veteran.' The IHCDA program guide (2/2026) uses the term 'Eligible Veteran,' defines it in Appendix E, and waives the three-year prior-ownership restriction for Eligible Veterans. Apply through an IHCDA participating lender with a DD-214.
items.hack: Ask the lender which IHCDA product (First Home, Next Home) fits and whether it layers with your VA loan.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Louisiana Housing Corporation MCC: a Qualified Veteran is exempt from the three-year no-ownership rule
items.who: Louisiana homebuyers; a Qualified Veteran is a 'veteran' under 38 U.S.C. 101 who has not previously used the bond-financed veteran exception
items.value: Federal tax credit of up to 40% of annual mortgage interest, capped at $2,000 per year per the page, for the life of the loan while it is your primary residence; claimed on IRS Form 8396; can combine with LHC down payment assistance
items.how: LHC's MCC manual says 'A Qualified Veteran is exempt from the three-year no prior home ownership requirement.' Documentation: certification that the veteran has not used the exception before, the Military Veteran's Eligibility Affidavit (Exhibit I), and copies of discharge papers if applicable; Qualified Veterans need only the prior year's federal tax return and Tax Return Affidavit. Occupy within 60 days of MCC issuance. The MCC page's credit is up to 40% of annual interest capped at $2,000 per year, claimed with IRS Form 8396.
items.hack: Complete Exhibit I with the lender at the start; it is the document most often missing at closing.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: FHLB Dallas HAVEN: grant of up to $25,000 for disabled veterans and Gold Star families, through a member bank
items.org: Federal Home Loan Bank of Dallas (via member banks)
items.who: Households with a service-related-disabled veteran, reservist, active-duty or Guard member, or Gold Star Families; income at or below 165% of area median; property in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, New Mexico or Texas
items.value: Up to $25,000 per household (as read on the program page) for down payment/closing costs (first-time buyers with counseling), construction of an adapted new home, or modifications such as ramps, grab bars and wider doorways; inspection/intermediary fees capped at $750
items.how: You cannot apply to FHLB Dallas directly: ask a participating member bank to request the funds, then sign the application forms; the member emails the request to ahp@fhlb.com. First-come, first-served. The program page showed 'Available Funds as of July 1, 2026: $0', so funds may already be gone; the 2026 bulletin listed two offerings (Jan 15 and Jul 1, 2026) and $1 million total.
items.hack: Ask your own bank or credit union whether it is an FHLB Dallas member BEFORE the next offering date; only member institutions can pull the money.
items.deadline: Funds available until exhausted or December 31, 2026, whichever is first (watch for the 2027 offering dates)

items.title: FHLBank Atlanta Community Partners Product: home purchase help for veterans, active duty and surviving spouses
items.who: Veterans, active-duty members or their surviving spouses buying a home in the Atlanta district (AL, DC, FL, GA, MD, NC, SC, VA); first-time and repeat buyers can qualify
items.value: Down payment/closing cost assistance via a member lender; the page gives no dollar amount, so confirm the current figure with the lender
items.how: FHLBank Atlanta's affordable housing page lists the Community Partners Product as the one product covering veterans and military. Funds flow through participating member lenders, not direct to buyers. I could not open the product sheet itself (robots-blocked), so details are from the program overview page only.
items.hack: Ask your lender to confirm it is an FHLBank Atlanta member and request the Community Partners Product explicitly.
items.deadline: None stated on the page

items.title: VyStar Credit Union Military Heroes Mortgage: no down payment, no PMI and closing help
items.who: Active duty, veterans and surviving spouses (membership open to past and present military and their families worldwide)
items.value: Per the Nov 2021 announcement: no down payment, no PMI; up to $5,000 toward closing costs or a 0.25% rate discount; up to $10,000 grant toward down payment/closing costs subject to availability and approval; up to $7,500 in retailer discounts
items.how: Call VyStar at the number in the release and ask for the Military Heroes mortgage. Pricing depends on underwriting. This is a 2021 press release; the program may have changed, so verify terms before relying on them.
items.hack: Compare the $5,000 closing credit against the 0.25% rate cut on your actual loan size; the credit usually wins on a short horizon.
items.deadline: None stated; announced November 4, 2021

items.title: Space Coast Credit Union Hero Loans: 0.25% off, a no-closing-cost option, and a military-only no-PMI loan
items.who: Military, educators, first responders, medical professionals, law enforcement, DoD/government contractors (verified by employment); the no-PMI option is for active, veteran and retired Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force and Space Force members and spouses (Guard and Reserve excluded)
items.value: No Closing Costs option (SCCU pays third-party closing costs and waives lender origination fees) with 0.25% off those rates; Reduced Rate option 0.25% off; auto loans with up to 90 days to first payment; Affordable Housing Program grant assistance available with each home loan option
items.how: Apply for a Hero Loan at SCCU and show proof of eligibility. The discount is applied after approval; offers can change or be withdrawn. No dollar figures from the page are repeated here because they were sample payments.
items.hack: Military-only No PMI option trades PMI for a rate adjustment and skips the VA funding fee, so price it against a VA loan.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: RBFCU (San Antonio): commissary access at Randolph, Fort Sam Houston or Lackland is a route to membership
items.who: People who can access the commissary at JBSA-Randolph, JBSA-Fort Sam Houston or JBSA-Lackland
items.value: Membership eligibility without a residence or employer test; RBFCU was established as a military credit union in San Antonio
items.how: RBFCU's membership article states 'If you can access the commissary at these military posts, you can join.' It does not list a veteran-specific perk. Retired and disabled veterans with commissary privileges should qualify; confirm with RBFCU at 210-945-3300.
items.hack: A 100% disabled veteran with commissary privileges can use that as the eligibility test even when living outside Texas.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Huntington Bank: pays up to $5,500 of your VA mortgage closing costs in its footprint states
items.who: VA loan borrowers with a certificate of eligibility buying or refinancing in Huntington's footprint states
items.value: Per the page: borrower pays a minimum of $500 of certain Huntington closing costs, Huntington pays up to $5,500 of the remainder, and you pay any amount above $6,000 total; plus Huntington Perks Checking with no monthly maintenance fee for current and former service members regardless of balance
items.how: Apply for a VA purchase or refinance through Huntington and supply the COE; documentation of military status may be required for the checking waiver. Huntington also offers a 6% interest cap on eligible loans for active-duty (SCRA) and help accessing SBA loans for veterans.
items.hack: Do the closing-cost math against the lender's rate: a fee-credit is only a win if the rate is competitive.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Military Housing Assistance Fund: free closing-cost gift funds for military and veterans (not in AK, OH, NY)
items.who: Military, Guard, Reserve, military civilian employees and veterans buying a home with credit strong enough for a mortgage; not available in Alaska, Ohio or New York
items.value: Closing-cost gift funds applied to your remaining closing costs after seller concessions, usually paid as a reimbursement check after purchase; the page gives no fixed amount; no cost to use
items.how: Apply on the MHAF website, complete an orientation conversation, MHAF assigns a lender and then a real estate agent from its network. You must use MHAF's agent and lender, and you still pay your own down payment, prepaids, inspection and earnest money. Private nonprofit, not a government program.
items.hack: Because you must use its network, compare the network lender's rate and fees to your own quotes before committing.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Armed Forces Bank waives the lender origination fee on VA loans and guarantees closing on time or pays $1,000
items.who: Borrowers who qualify for the VA loan product at Armed Forces Bank
items.value: Lender origination fee waived for VA-qualified borrowers (the VA funding fee may still apply); closing-date guarantee stated as 'close your loan on time or pay you $1,000'
items.how: Per the page footnote the waiver applies to the VA loan product; the page does not say whether the $1,000 guarantee is limited to VA loans and the full guarantee terms were not on the page, so confirm both with the lender.
items.hack: Ask for the guarantee terms in writing and set your contract closing date with margin so the guarantee is meaningful.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Macon-Bibb County (GA): honorably discharged veterans 65+ ride fixed-route buses free for life
items.who: Honorably discharged veterans residing in Bibb County, Georgia, aged 65 or older
items.value: Free, lifetime fixed-route bus service
items.how: MBCTA's page shows the Ride Forever card for veterans but does not give enrollment steps; the enrollment page is linked as mbcta.net/ride-forever/ and you can call (478) 803-2521. Bring proof of residency, age and discharge.
items.hack: Ask MBCTA whether paratransit for eligible riders is covered too.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Las Vegas RTC: 50% off fixed-route fares for Clark County veterans, plus free medical rides
items.org: Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada
items.who: Veterans living in Clark County (VA ID card, DD214 or retiree ID, plus a Nevada ID/DMV card with veteran status)
items.value: 50% off fixed-route fares (single ride, 2-hour, 24-hour, 15-day and 30-day passes); Veterans Medical Transportation Network rides to VA-approved medical appointments
items.how: Get an RTC Veterans ID card at the Bonneville Transit Center in downtown Las Vegas and swipe it at the fare box or show it when buying passes. VMTN requires eligibility at VA Southern Nevada Healthcare System and an application with ID and DD214/VA card.
items.hack: Put the veteran designation on your Nevada ID first; it is one of the documents RTC wants.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Westchester County (NY): free Veterans parks pass for pools, beaches and golf discounts, valid three years
items.who: Honorably discharged U.S. veterans who are Westchester County residents
items.value: Access to county parks, pools, beaches, golf courses and other facilities; discounted admission and parking where applicable and discounted greens fees; valid for three years
items.how: Apply in person only (Parks Department, 450 Saw Mill River Rd, Ardsley; Croton Point Park; Ward Pound Ridge Reservation). Bring photo ID, proof of county residency and proof of veteran status (DD-214, VA ID or NYS licence with Veteran designation). Call 914-231-4575 to confirm hours.
items.hack: Add the 'Veteran' designation to your NYS driver license, then use it as your proof of status.
items.deadline: Renew every three years

items.title: Volusia County (FL): Patriot Pass library card, building-permit discount and park perks listed as veteran initiatives
items.who: Veterans in Volusia County, Florida
items.value: The county page lists: Patriot Pass library card (complimentary copies/printouts per visit), 10% discount on building permit fees for veteran property owners, free Marine Science Center admission, 10% off park pavilions/camping/community-center rentals, free primitive camping in November
items.how: The page frames several items as planned initiatives and gives no enrollment steps, so call Veterans Services (DeLand 386-740-5102) to confirm which are active.
items.hack: Ask for the permit discount before you pull a renovation permit; it is the one that saves real money.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Gardiner, Maine: quarterly sewer bill discount for veterans, seniors or disabled residents under an income limit
items.who: Gardiner households with a resident who is 65+, a veteran or disabled and household income under the limit on the page
items.value: Quarterly sewer billing discount (page says $25 or $45; it does not say which applies to whom)
items.how: Bring the Sewer Discount Program application to Gardiner City Hall (6 Church Street) with proof of residency, age and income. Renew every year; there are no retroactive adjustments for late renewals. The page does not define 'veteran.' Contact (207) 582-4200.
items.hack: File the Sewer Discount and the Property Tax Assistance application together; they share the deadline.
items.deadline: October 15 each year (also for the Property Tax Assistance application); first-time applications accepted any time, starting with the next bill

items.title: Liberty Utilities (Black Mountain Sewer, Arizona): 15% wastewater discount for disabled veterans
items.who: Honorably discharged veterans with a permanent service-related disability rating, income within 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, bill in the applicant's name at a primary residence
items.value: 15% discount on the residential wastewater bill
items.how: The tariff says approval is first-come, first-served, limited to 225 customers combined across the CAT programs with a waiting list, reapply yearly, and notify Liberty within 30 days if you become ineligible. Proof of income required. Tariff date not shown, so check with Liberty Utilities.
items.hack: Apply early; the 225-customer cap means a waiting list can form.
items.deadline: Reapply annually

items.title: Cook County (IL): disabled veterans rated 70%+ get a $250,000 assessed-value reduction, possibly total exemption
items.org: Cook County Assessor / Cook County, Illinois
items.who: Homeowners with a VA-certified service-connected disability; separate Returning Veterans exemption for those returning from active duty in armed conflict
items.value: Homestead Exemption for Veterans with Disabilities reduces equalized assessed value by an amount tied to disability level (70% or more: $250,000 reduction, 'can be totally exempt'); Returning Veterans Exemption: $5,000 reduction in EAV for the year of return
items.how: The county page does not list steps or deadlines; it points to the Assessor's pages for the Returning Veterans Exemption and the Homestead Exemption for Veterans with Disabilities. Amounts for lower disability levels are on the Assessor's page.
items.hack: Ask whether the exemption applies to the current and the prior tax year; exemptions are year-specific.
items.deadline: Filing deadlines are set by the Assessor each year; not on this page

items.title: Fairfax County (VA): exemption from local real estate tax for 100% P&T disabled veterans, plus one vehicle
items.org: Fairfax County Department of Tax Administration
items.who: Veterans rated 100% service-connected and permanently and totally disabled (or paid at the 100% rate via IU), and certain surviving spouses
items.value: Exemption from local real estate tax on the principal residence up to one acre; since 2021 a vehicle tax exemption on one car or pickup used for personal purposes
items.how: Apply online and submit the VA Summary of Benefits letter; the county will not process without it. Surviving spouses supply the death certificate and proof of residence. Page last modified March 2022, so verify requirements. Veterans buying a home can request a pre-certificate of approval at taxrelief@fairfaxcounty.gov.
items.hack: Request the pre-certificate before you make an offer so you know your tax bill ahead of time.
items.deadline: No deadline listed; contact 703-222-8234

items.title: Wisconsin Veterans and Surviving Spouses Property Tax Credit: refundable credit for 100% of primary-residence property tax
items.org: Wisconsin DVA and Department of Revenue
items.who: Wisconsin veterans with honorable service and a 100% service-connected rating (or IU), and unremarried surviving spouses via several pathways
items.value: Refundable credit that covers 100% of property taxes paid on a primary residence including up to one acre; second homes and vacation properties do not qualify
items.how: Contact the Wisconsin DVA first to get verification of eligibility (a County or Tribal Veterans Service Officer can help), claim the credit on your Wisconsin income tax return and attach the WDVA verification the first year plus property tax bills and proof of payment. Claims are due within four years of the unextended due date of the return; if your VA decision is pending, you can request an extension (DORIncome@wisconsin.gov, 608-266-2486). You cannot also claim the school property tax, homestead or farmland preservation credit for that year. Call (800) 947-8387.
items.hack: It is a credit on the state tax return, so you can still benefit if the property tax was paid through escrow.
items.deadline: Four years from the unextended return due date (for example the 2022 credit must be claimed by April 15, 2027)

items.title: Maryland SDAT: 100% disabled veteran exemption, and refunds only reach back three years
items.org: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
items.who: Owner-occupants rated 100% service-connected, permanent and total (or permanently unemployable per an Attorney General opinion); surviving spouses; disabled active-duty members
items.value: Property tax exemption on the dwelling; refund requests within 3 years, starting with the calendar year first eligible, not before tax year 2018-2019
items.how: Submit the right SDAT application to the local assessment office with a VA certification or the final rating decision (SDAT does not accept the Summary of Benefit letter), DD-214 and proof of residency. Active-duty members must submit the Certification of Active-Duty Status yearly.
items.hack: If your rating became P&T years ago, file now; the three-year refund window is the clock.
items.deadline: Refund requests within 3 years of first eligibility; no general filing deadline on page

items.title: New Jersey: 100% P&T disabled veterans exempt from property tax on their dwelling (File D.V.S.S.E.)
items.org: NJ Division of Taxation / local assessor
items.who: Honorably discharged New Jersey residents with a VA-certified 100% permanent and total service-connected disability who own and live in the home; qualifying unremarried surviving spouses
items.value: Full property tax exemption on the dwelling
items.how: File Form D.V.S.S.E. with all supporting documents with your local assessor (VA certification, DD 214, ID). If denied, file Form A-1 with the County Board of Taxation on or before April 1 following the denial; January 15 for Burlington, Gloucester and Monmouth counties. Page does not give an application deadline or say if retroactive; call 609-292-7974.
items.hack: Ask the assessor about back taxes in writing on the day you file.
items.deadline: Appeal: April 1 (January 15 for Burlington, Gloucester, Monmouth) after a denial

items.title: Michigan disabled veterans property tax exemption: affidavit Form 5107 through your local assessor
items.org: Michigan State Tax Commission / local assessor
items.who: Michigan resident disabled veterans honorably discharged with a 100% permanent and total service-connected rating, a specially adapted housing certificate, or an individual unemployability rating, and unremarried surviving spouses of qualifying veterans
items.value: Property tax exemption on the primary residence
items.how: File Form 5107 with the city or township assessor (not Treasury) with VA documentation; a County Department of Veterans Affairs letter alone is insufficient. Submit before December 31 of the tax year (a December 30 postmark counts). From January 1, 2025 the exemption continues until rescinded; file Form 6054 within 45 days if you stop qualifying. Denials can be appealed to the Michigan Tax Tribunal within 35 days. No asset test.
items.hack: File with your local assessor and ask about proration for the first year.
items.deadline: Form 5107 before December 31 of the tax year

items.title: Maryland Mortgage Program: honorably discharged veterans get a one-time first-time homebuyer exemption
items.who: Honorably discharged veterans who have not previously used the first-time homebuyer exemption
items.value: Lets a veteran who is not a first-time buyer use the Maryland Mortgage Program; the fact sheet cites the Heroes Earnings Assistance and Relief Tax Act of 2008 as the basis
items.how: Submit a DD-214 and complete a Veteran First Time Homebuyer Exemption form through a participating lender. It is a one-time use, so do not burn it on a program you do not need.
items.hack: Because it is usable once, ask the lender which MMP product gives the most value before you invoke it.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Florida Hometown Heroes: military and veterans employed full-time by a Florida employer are on the eligible list
items.who: Active duty or reserve service members of all branches (and FL National Guard); veterans discharged under other than dishonorable conditions and employed FULL TIME by a Florida-based employer; only ONE borrower must qualify
items.value: Access to the Hometown Heroes home purchase assistance; the occupations list itself states no benefit amounts
items.how: Per the July 2026 eligible occupations list, participants must be currently and full-time employed by a Florida-based employer. Apply through a participating lender; get program amounts and funding status from Florida Housing or the lender because the list does not state them.
items.hack: A veteran who works for a Florida employer may qualify under Hometown Heroes even if the Salute Our Soldiers set-aside is not open.
items.deadline: Check funding status; none on the list

items.title: Alamo Call-A-Ride 4 Vets: rides for any honorably discharged veteran in the 13-county San Antonio region
items.org: Alamo region veterans transportation program (listed on TexVet)
items.who: Any honorably discharged veteran (also certain family members, surviving spouses and caregivers); no disability rating needed
items.value: Up to three rides depending on funding, for medical appointments (priority), groceries, prescriptions, worship, bills; the page says rides are free in one place and up to $12 one way in another
items.how: Call 210-362-5254 or 1-800-960-5201. Covers Atascosa, Bandera, Bexar, Comal, Frio, Gillespie, Guadalupe, Karnes, Kendall, Kerr, McMullen, Medina and Wilson counties; availability depends on local providers.
items.hack: Book medical appointments first; they get priority.
items.deadline: None; depends on funding

items.title: Virginia Housing Closing Cost Assistance Grant: up to 2% of price, no repayment, for a Virginia Housing VA loan
items.who: Qualified first-time buyers (or repeat buyers in Areas of Economic Opportunity) with a bond RHS or VA loan from Virginia Housing, within income and price limits
items.value: Grant that 'may be worth up to 2% of your home's purchase price'; can go to closing costs and VA funding fees; 'you never have to pay it back'
items.how: Talk with an approved lender. Virginia Housing's VA loan: $0 down, credit scores as low as 620 per the loan page, and it is eligible for the CCA grant (bond loans only). Call 877-843-2123.
items.hack: Ask the lender to pay the VA funding fee from the grant so you keep cash for the down payment on a second property.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Loudoun County (VA) Granting Freedom: grants up to $10,000 for disability home modifications
items.org: Loudoun County Department of Housing and Community Development with Virginia Housing
items.who: Veterans and service members with a line-of-duty service-connected disability who are homeowner-occupants or renters, at or below 80% of area median income
items.value: Grants up to $10,000 (as read on the county page) for owner-occupied and rental unit modifications tied to the disability
items.how: Need a VA rating or award letter (service members: MEB/PEB documents). The application opens a couple of times a year until the closing date or funds are exhausted; the county submits applications to Virginia Housing. Ask the county for the next window: 703-737-8323.
items.hack: Get a clear nexus letter from the treating clinician tying each modification to the disability; the county requires the link.
items.deadline: Rolling windows twice a year; ask the county

items.title: New Jersey $250 Veterans Property Tax Deduction: claim with Form V.S.S. at your local assessor
items.who: New Jersey resident property owners with honorably discharged active-duty service (reservists and Guard only if called to active duty; training doesn't count); qualifying unremarried surviving spouses
items.value: Annual $250 property tax deduction
items.how: All requirements must be met as of October 1 of the pretax year. File Form V.S.S. and proof (DD 214, deed, NJ ID) with your local assessor or tax collector. Denials are appealed with Form A-1 by April 1 after the denial (Jan 15 in Burlington, Gloucester, Monmouth). Questions: 609-292-7974.
items.hack: Check whether a 100% disabled veteran exemption would replace it; the two are separate claims.
items.deadline: Qualifying date: October 1 of the pretax year; appeal April 1 (Jan 15 in three counties)

items.title: Michigan 100% disabled veterans: free-fee plate, a property tax credit for filing MI-1040CR-2, and free licenses
items.who: Michigan veterans rated 100% (or individually unemployable); the plate needs a total and permanent rating
items.value: Disabled veteran plate with no recurring fee (one-time $5 administrative fee when first issued); state credit for property tax paid via Form MI-1040CR-2, refundable even if no income tax is owed; free hunting and fishing licenses; property tax waiver via Form 5107 filed annually
items.how: Form 5107 and support go to the local government that issues the tax bill. Michigan's State Tax Commission FAQ adds: file with the city or township assessor before December 31 of the tax year (a December 30 postmark counts); from January 1, 2025 the exemption stays in effect until rescinded; no asset test; eligibility is a 100% permanent and total rating, a specially adapted housing certificate or IU. Surviving-spouse rules are in the FAQ.
items.hack: File the 5107 and the MI-1040CR-2 together: one removes the tax, the other refunds what was already paid.
items.deadline: Form 5107: before December 31 of the tax year

items.title: Washington Lifetime Disabled Veteran Pass: free state parks, free camping site, boat launch and DNR/WDFW lands
items.org: Washington State Parks and Washington DVA
items.who: Qualified disabled veterans (the DVA page does not list the criteria)
items.value: No Discover Pass needed on state parks, DNR and DFW lands; free state park admission, one free camping or moorage site per night, free boat launching and trailer dumping; the page does not state a fee for the pass
items.how: Use the Lifetime Disabled Veteran Pass application linked from the DVA page, keep the wallet card with you and fill out a fee envelope with your pass number when parking. Call State Parks at (360) 902-8844; for DFW or DNR lands contact those agencies.
items.hack: Get this before buying a Discover Pass; it replaces it.
items.deadline: None

items.title: VEDC Veteran Small Business Loan Fund: $50,000 to $250,000 for veteran-owned firms in Southern California, Chicago and North Carolina
items.org: Veterans Entrepreneurship Development Corporation (VEDC), a CDFI program (hosted by City of Chicago)
items.who: Veterans of all five branches including Guard and Reserve (anything but dishonorable discharge); business 2+ years old, 51%+ veteran-owned, 1 to 200 employees, revenue up to $2 million
items.value: Term sheet: loans of $50,000 to $250,000; rate WSJP plus up to 6%; fees up to 3% paid from proceeds; no prepayment penalty; no balloon; term capped at five years
items.how: Complete the online intake form at vedc.org; inquiries are answered within 48 hours, with a letter of intent within five days of a completed application. DD214 required. The term sheet is undated, so confirm the fund is still open and the pricing.
items.hack: Ask whether the interest-rate spread can be cut with a larger down payment or collateral before you sign.
items.deadline: None stated; term sheet undated

items.title: vet.loan: three CDFIs (California, North Carolina, Texas) pooling loans and free training for veteran entrepreneurs
items.org: Main Street Launch, Carolina Small Business Development Fund, PeopleFund
items.who: Veterans starting or growing a business in California, North Carolina or Texas
items.value: Small business loans and technical assistance; free online training modules; the page gives no loan sizes
items.how: Per a June 2018 PeopleFund post, use vet.loan to connect with the local community lender. Details on eligibility were not in the post, and the portal may have changed since 2018, so verify before relying on it.
items.hack: Ask each CDFI whether it counts a military spouse as a veteran owner.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Veteran Loan Fund: below-market loans and free coaching from 12 CDFIs across 12 states
items.org: Veteran Loan Fund (Bank of America lead investor) with DreamSpring and member CDFIs
items.who: Military veterans and their spouses starting or growing a business; eligibility details are on veteranloanfund.com
items.value: Per a Nov 2023 article: loan capital at below-market interest rates and free business coaching; fund described as $25 million with a goal of $100 million by 2027; loan sizes not stated
items.how: Use the online platform at veteranloanfund.com or contact a member CDFI: Access to Capital for Entrepreneurs (GA), Appalachian Community Capital (VA), Black Business Investment Fund (FL), Business Impact Northwest (WA), Colorado Enterprise Fund (CO), DreamSpring (NM), ECDI (OH), Pathway Lending (TN), Justine Petersen (MO), PeopleFund (TX), Pursuit (NY), WWBIC (WI).
items.hack: Pick the CDFI in your own state; each underwrites locally.
items.deadline: None

items.title: New York Lifetime Liberty Pass: since April 1, 2024 open to all NY resident veterans, not just disabled ones
items.org: New York State Parks (announced by Livingston County Veteran Services)
items.who: All veterans and Gold Star families who are New York State residents (per the county announcement)
items.value: Free lifetime access: free park vehicle entry, free greens fees at state-operated golf courses, free state park pool entrance, discounted camping and cabin rentals at most state parks; also National Parks Lifetime Pass
items.how: Apply on the NYS Parks website or at a county veteran services walk-in event with a DD-214 or equivalent, valid NYS ID showing veteran status, and a VA disability statement if you have one. The announcement is from August 2024; confirm current rules with NYS Parks.
items.hack: Add the 'Veteran' designation to your NYS ID first; the walk-in events ask for it.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Pennsylvania DMVA state veterans programs: real estate tax exemption, Trust Fund grants, temporary assistance and more
items.org: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs
items.who: Pennsylvania veterans and military families (rules differ by program)
items.value: The page names: Disabled Veterans' Real Estate Tax Exemption, Amputee/Paralyzed and Blind Veteran's Pensions, Educational Gratuity, Veterans' Temporary Assistance, Military Family Relief Assistance, Veterans' Trust Fund Grants, VSO Grants, free notarization, plus a registration/title fee waiver and disabled veteran plates through PennDOT and disabled veteran camping discounts and fishing licenses
items.how: This overview lists programs and links but does not state eligibility, amounts or steps; open each program page at pa.gov/agencies/dmva or call DMVA.
items.hack: Start with the Disabled Veterans' Real Estate Tax Exemption and the PennDOT fee waiver; they pay back every year.
items.deadline: Varies by program

items.title: Wisconsin Assistance to Veterans in Need: state grants for low-income veterans, capped at $5,000 lifetime
items.org: Wisconsin Department of Veterans Affairs (via County Veterans Service Office)
items.who: Low-income Wisconsin veterans; spouses and dependents in limited circumstances
items.value: As read on Dodge County's page: subsistence aid in 30-day periods up to three months, capped at $2,000 per 12 months; dental up to $2,500, vision up to $500, hearing up to $1,500 per ear per 12 months; lifetime maximum $5,000
items.how: Contact your County Veterans Service Officer (Dodge County: 920-386-3799) with a DD-214. The county page says the DD214 is the key to all benefits; the same page also lists WI GI Bill tuition waiver, VetEd reimbursement and the Veteran driver's license identifier.
items.hack: Ask the CVSO to screen you for the property tax credit and other state benefits in the same visit.
items.deadline: None stated; VetEd pre-application within 30 days of semester start

items.title: Fairfax County: disabled veteran vehicles taxed at $0.01 per $100 of assessed value
items.org: Fairfax County Department of Tax Administration
items.who: Qualifying disabled veterans in Fairfax County, Virginia
items.value: Vehicles owned and regularly used by a qualifying disabled veteran get a reduced tax rate of $0.01 per $100 of assessed value (per the county page); also out-of-state vehicle exemptions for active-duty and a leased-vehicle credit on the first $20,000 of assessed value
items.how: The page links to separate application pages and does not describe certification steps. Call 703-222-8234 or email DTAAdmin@fairfaxcounty.gov. Note the Fairfax real estate page describes a separate exemption on one personal vehicle for 100% P&T veterans; ask which applies to you.
items.hack: Apply for the vehicle and the real estate exemption at the same visit.
items.deadline: Not stated on the page

items.title: Wichita Transit (KS): veterans with ID ride any bus or Q-line free
items.org: Wichita Transit (promoted by United Way of the Plains)
items.who: Any veteran with proper ID: a Kansas driver license or ID with a veteran designation, a veteran health ID, veteran ID or retired military ID
items.value: Free fares on any Wichita Transit bus or Q-line for any purpose
items.how: No separate sign-up is described; show the ID when boarding. The page is from United Way of the Plains rather than the transit agency, so confirm on wichitatransit.org.
items.hack: Add the veteran designation on your Kansas license so you never have to carry other papers.
items.deadline: None

items.title: NJHMFA: veterans are exempt from the three-year ownership rule for the first mortgage and the Smart Start down payment product
items.org: New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency (NJHMFA)
items.who: Qualified veterans (retired, discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable) and active-duty borrowers who completed their initial obligation; buyers in Urban Target Areas get the same exemption
items.value: Per the Oct 19, 2026 Seller's Guide change log (changes effective July 1, 2025): qualified veterans and Urban Target Area buyers need not be first-time buyers for the first mortgage or the down payment assistance product, and the same applies to Smart Start DPA
items.how: Evidence: a copy of the veteran's Certificate of Eligibility or Title 38 letter, and a DD-214 or Statement of Service. Veterans cannot retain an existing primary residence. All other product requirements still apply. The excerpt available to me was a change log and definitions page, not the full sections, so ask the lender for the full rule.
items.hack: Bring the COE and DD-214 to the first lender call so they can run the exemption and the VA loan together.
items.deadline: Guide effective October 19, 2026

items.title: Colorado CHFA: a Qualified Veteran skips the first-time buyer test, using Form 719 and a DD-214
items.who: Veterans (38 U.S.C. 101) discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable who have not already used a veteran exception for a mortgage-revenue-bond loan or MCC
items.value: Exception to the first-time homebuyer requirement for CHFA loans (including FirstStep) and the MCC; the Seller's Guide (Aug 2026) also requires the full amount of the veteran's available VA guaranty to be applied to the first mortgage
items.how: Sign CHFA Form 719, an affidavit submitted to a private lender with the application, attach a DD-214. The veteran's VA guaranty requirement and the rule that a DPA second mortgage cannot count toward the 25 percent guaranty cash down payment are in the Seller's Guide. I did not see the Guide's definition of Qualified Veteran, only the Form 719 attestation.
items.hack: Use it only once: Form 719 attests that you have not used the veteran exception before.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: San Diego County parks: free day-use and up to 7 free camping nights for disabled, POW and Medal of Honor veterans
items.org: County of San Diego Parks and Recreation
items.who: Veterans disabled during service, prisoners of war and Medal of Honor winners, via the California Distinguished Veteran Pass
items.value: Discounts at day-use parks and eight county camping parks; free use of county parks and campsites up to seven nights a year; standard $5 fee still applies to reserve campsites in advance (per the 2012 announcement)
items.how: Apply for the state Distinguished Veteran Pass through California State Parks; the announcement does not describe a separate county application. It is a March 2012 Board of Supervisors vote, so confirm that the benefit is still current with County Parks before travelling.
items.hack: The state pass also covers California State Parks; apply once and use it at both.
items.deadline: None; announced March 14, 2012

items.title: Florida Housing Mortgage Credit Certificate: veterans exempt from first-time buyer rule, no tax returns, and generally no education class
items.who: Veterans who served in the active military, naval or air service and were discharged under conditions other than dishonorable
items.value: MCC credit of 10% to 30% depending on loan size (30% on loans up to $100,000, 20% to $200,000, 10% above, per the 2018 guideline); veterans need not be first-time buyers
items.how: Certify on the Mortgagor Affidavit and provide a valid DD-214 through the lender; tax returns or transcripts are not required for veterans, and the homebuyer education requirement generally does not apply to them. The guideline is from 2018, so the tiers and process may have changed.
items.hack: Ask the lender for the current credit tier schedule before relying on the 2018 numbers.
items.deadline: None

items.title: South Carolina MCC: a veteran can use a one-time exception to the first-time buyer rule
items.who: Veterans (served in active duty or Reserves, discharged under conditions other than dishonorable) buying under a one-time exception
items.value: MCC federal income tax credit; the Authority offers a 30% credit up to a maximum of $2,000 annually per the Dec 2024 program manual; veterans need only the prior year's tax return
items.how: The lender applies the veterans' exemption; MCC income and acquisition cost limits still apply. The manual does not say which document proves veteran status, and it is dated December 2024, so confirm with SC Housing that MCCs are currently being issued and what the credit rate is today.
items.hack: Use the one-time exception on the loan where it saves the most; it can't be reused.
items.deadline: Confirm current availability with SC Housing

items.title: Ohio enhanced homestead exemption for disabled veterans: no income test, bigger reduction, file with the county auditor by December 31
items.org: Ohio Department of Taxation / county auditor
items.who: Disabled veterans and surviving spouses who own and occupy their principal residence as of January 1 of the application year
items.value: Larger reduction in taxable value than the standard homestead; the FAQ lists $58,000 for tax year 2025 and $59,400 for tax year 2026 on real property (as read, and indexed annually); no income requirement
items.how: Complete Form DTE 105I and file with your county auditor (paper always accepted). Real property applications are due on or before December 31 of the year for which the exemption is sought. Continuing recipients get a form (DTE 105B) each January and return it only if circumstances change. Denials can be appealed on Form DTE 106B within 60 days. Some counties add a local matching exemption.
items.hack: If you move, reapply at the new address; it does not follow you automatically.
items.deadline: December 31 for real property; December 31 of the prior year for manufactured homes

items.title: New Jersey property tax deferment while deployed: pay 90 days after deployment ends (Form AMSPTD)
items.who: Active service members deployed or mobilized in wartime (someone can apply on their behalf)
items.value: Defers a property tax bill, not a reduction; deferred taxes are due within 90 days after deployment or mobilization ends; late deferred payments accrue interest back to the original due date
items.how: File Form AMSPTD with deployment or mobilization orders (and a DD 214 if applicable). It does not cover taxes already delinquent before deployment. If you have a mortgage escrow account, tell the lender. Contact Taxation.propadmin@treas.nj.gov or 609-292-7974.
items.hack: File before the bill's due date, since delinquent taxes are excluded.
items.deadline: Before the tax due date

items.title: New Jersey: no sales tax on a vehicle bought with VA or NJDVA funds, and a deferment for service members stationed away
items.who: Disabled veterans who received funds from the VA or NJDVA to buy a car; resident service members stationed out of state who buy a vehicle outside New Jersey
items.value: Amount received for the vehicle is not subject to sales tax (fully exempt only if the funds equal the total purchase price); service members may defer sales tax until the vehicle is brought to New Jersey (one vehicle at a time)
items.how: The page lists the rules but not the forms; follow the NJ Division of Taxation links on the military tax page. The sales tax is due if the Letter of Deferment is not received.
items.hack: Ask the dealer to structure the VA payment so it equals the full price; otherwise part of the price is taxed.
items.deadline: Not stated

items.title: NC Home Advantage Tax Credit: an MCC worth up to $2,000 a year, 30% of interest on existing homes and 50% on new builds
items.who: Buyers using an NC Home Advantage Mortgage or their own product, with a 30-year fixed-rate FHA, USDA, VA or conventional loan; NCHFA's press release lists eligible military veterans alongside first-time buyers
items.value: Could reduce federal income tax by up to $2,000 per year; up to 30% of annual interest on existing homes; 50% credit on newly built homes (page wording)
items.how: Must be approved for the MCC before the home purchase; lenders reserve MCCs in NCHFA's Online Lender Services. The lender page does not address veteran eligibility, which comes from NCHFA's press release.
items.hack: Ask the lender to pair an MCC with a VA loan: the credit offsets income tax, and VA removes PMI.
items.deadline: Reserve before purchase

items.title: Huntington Honors: Perks Checking with no monthly maintenance fee for current and former service members and veterans
items.who: Current or former service members and veterans (documentation of military status may be required)
items.value: Perks Checking with no monthly maintenance fee regardless of balance; the page also describes a 6% interest rate cap on eligible loans and lines of credit for active-duty members and help accessing SBA small business loans
items.how: Open Perks Checking and provide military documentation if asked. Call 855-480-4748 (US) or 614-480-4748 (outside the US), 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. ET.
items.hack: Ask when the waiver is verified; some banks check once a year.
items.deadline: None stated

items.title: Cook County (IL) Returning Veterans Exemption: $5,000 off assessed value for veterans back from armed conflict
items.org: Cook County Assessor / Cook County, Illinois
items.who: Veterans returning from active duty in armed conflict who own property in Cook County
items.value: $5,000 reduction in the equalized assessed value of the property for the taxable year in which they return (as stated by the county)
items.how: The county page links to the Assessor's Returning Veterans Exemption page for application steps; steps and deadlines were not on the county page. Ask the Assessor whether it can be combined with the Homestead Exemption for Veterans with Disabilities.
items.hack: File in the year you return; it is tied to that taxable year.
items.deadline: Set by the Assessor each year; not on this page

items.title: Southern Nevada Veterans Medical Transportation Network: rides to VA-approved appointments, plus ADA paratransit option
items.org: Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada
items.who: Veterans eligible for care at the VA Southern Nevada Healthcare System; the paratransit version also needs RTC ADA Paratransit certification
items.value: Transportation between home and VA-approved medical appointments within the RTC service area (medical trips only); paratransit trips can be booked up to three weekdays in advance
items.how: Register online, by email or by mail to RTC Specialized Services (600 S. Grand Central Pkwy, Ste. 350, Las Vegas) with front and back copies of a Nevada ID and a VA health card, VIC card or DD214 showing an honorable discharge. Paratransit scheduling: (702) 678-VETS (8387), Monday to Friday 7 AM to 6 PM. Misuse can suspend service.
items.hack: If you are not yet ADA-certified, start that application at the same time: (702) 676-1815.
items.deadline: None

items.title: Washington Lifetime Disabled Veteran Pass - free state parks, free camping and Discover Pass-free state lands
items.org: Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission
items.who: Washington residents who are veterans with a combined service-connected rating of at least 30%
items.value: Free day-use parking, boat launch and trailer dump at state parks, plus free camping or moorage for one site per night; also free day-use parking on Fish and Wildlife and Natural Resources lands in place of a Discover Pass. Applying is free (a replacement card costs $15 per the page).
items.how: Download the application from the state parks pass page; attach proof of Washington residency and your VA award letter showing 30% or more (copies, not originals). Email passes@parks.wa.gov, mail to the Information Center in Olympia, or fax.
items.hack: The pass does NOT cover roofed shelters (cabins, yurts), group camps, extra-vehicle fees or hook-up fees, and only one campsite per night. Cancel reservations you will not use. While waiting 6-8 weeks for the card you still need a Discover Pass or day-use fee on state lands, so apply well before camping season.
items.deadline: No application deadline on the page; processing is delayed - allow at least 6-8 weeks by mail.

items.title: Colorado Free Lifetime Veteran Combo License - small game hunting and fishing for 60%+ disabled veterans
items.org: Colorado Parks and Wildlife (via Colorado Division of Veterans Affairs)
items.who: Colorado resident veterans with a VA-rated service-connected disability of 60% or more; Purple Heart recipients with documentation also qualify
items.value: A free lifetime combined small-game hunting and fishing license (a fishing-only option is also available).
items.how: Get a VA disability letter (eBenefits or 800-827-1000), then apply through the CPW website or call 303-291-7235. Anyone born on or after Jan 1, 1949 must first complete a hunter's safety course.
items.hack: Separate from the Independence Parks Pass: a disabled Colorado veteran can hold both. Big-game licenses are not included.
items.deadline: None stated on the page.

items.title: Colorado Independence Parks Pass and disabled-veteran plate park entry - free Colorado state parks
items.who: Colorado resident disabled veterans (Independence Parks Pass); Colorado residents with Disabled Veterans or Purple Heart license plates (plate entry)
items.value: Free state park entry. The Independence Parks Pass is free, and holders over age 64 also get discounted camping Sunday-Thursday excluding holidays. Disabled Veterans/Purple Heart plate holders get free entry without a windshield pass (camping rates excluded; the veteran must be in the vehicle).
items.how: Apply for the Independence Parks Pass through Colorado Parks and Wildlife (the veterans page gives no process - check the CPW site); plates are issued by the DMV.
items.hack: Also on the veterans page: a free Nov 11 entry day and a 'Military August Pass' (free entry during August, entry only, picked up in person at any CPW office or park starting in July) - both need proof of service.
items.deadline: August pass: pick up starting in July (page does not state a 2026 date); Nov 11 day each year.

items.title: Michigan free hunting and fishing licenses for totally and permanently disabled veterans
items.org: Michigan Department of Natural Resources / Michigan Veterans Affairs Agency
items.who: Michigan residents rated totally and permanently disabled or individually unemployable by the VA
items.value: Hunting and fishing licenses at no cost.
items.how: Apply through the DNR eLicense site (mdnr-elicense.com) with documented proof of disabled-veteran status; carry that proof while using the license.
items.hack: Michigan also gives free Recreation Passport-equivalent entry to Medal of Honor recipients, 100% disabled veterans and ex-POWs - but you must have the specialty license-plate designation to get in free.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Georgia one-time free Sportsman's License for post-July 2005 veterans
items.org: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Division
items.who: Georgia resident veterans with 90+ days of active federal service, honorably discharged on or after July 1, 2005
items.value: A free full-privilege sportsman's license for hunting and fishing, valid one year from date of issue; issued only once. After it expires, a 20% discount applies to the adult lifetime sportsman's license for veterans ages 16-49 (per the Georgia veterans page).
items.how: Download an application from georgiawildlife.com (licenses-permits-passes) or apply at a retail license agent.
items.hack: Start the clock deliberately: the free year runs from date of issue, so request it just before the season you most want to hunt.
items.deadline: None stated; one-time only.

items.title: Texas Military Parklands Passports - free state park entry for active duty, veterans, disabled veterans and Gold Star family
items.who: Active duty/Reserve/Guard; honorably discharged veterans; veterans 60%+ service-connected or with loss of a lower extremity; Gold Star family (spouse, parent, child, sibling)
items.value: Free entry to Texas state parks for the pass holder. Disabled-veteran passes also admit one free companion. Gold Star family members each apply separately.
items.how: Obtain the pass at any state park with photo ID plus proof (service ID; DoD veteran ID, Texas DL with veteran designation, DD-214 or VHIC; award letter, Disabled Veterans plate receipt or Texas tax-exemption letter; DD 1300 and proof of relationship for Gold Star).
items.hack: Entry is not guaranteed when a park reaches capacity; the passport gives entry only, not free camping.
items.deadline: None listed.

items.title: Ohio free hunting and fishing licenses for 100% disabled veterans and former POWs - five-year approval
items.org: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife / Ohio Department of Veterans Services
items.who: Ohio residents of six consecutive months who are honorably discharged and permanently and totally disabled (a 100% rating meets it), hold Disabled Veterans plates, or are former POWs
items.value: At no cost: fishing license, hunting license, fur taker permit, deer permit, wild turkey permit and wetlands habitat stamp. Approval lasts five years, but you must obtain the free licenses each license year (they end in late February).
items.how: Complete form DNR9032-B and send it to the Ohio Department of Veterans Services in Cleveland for certification (mail, fax or email); the Division of Wildlife sends an approval or denial letter. Processing about 4 to 12 weeks.
items.hack: VA paperwork does not replace the form. Apply in the off-season - processing takes up to 12 weeks. Confirm the certified-application email address on the form before sending.
items.deadline: Re-obtain licenses annually; approval valid five years from notification.

items.title: Louisiana free hunting and fishing licenses for 50%+ disabled veterans (foundation pays the fee)
items.org: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries / Louisiana Wildlife and Fisheries Foundation
items.who: Veterans with a permanent service-connected disability rating of 50% or more
items.value: Free: Basic and Saltwater Fishing; Basic, Deer, Waterfowl and Turkey Hunting; and the WMA Access Permit (Federal Duck Stamp not included). The foundation covers the $4 fee. Free hard cards are available.
items.how: Submit the Disabled Veterans application (PDF) with proof of rating and a Louisiana driver's license or OMV ID - in person at LDWF headquarters, by email to lifetime@wlf.la.gov, or by mail. Phone 225-765-2887.
items.hack: Louisiana also sells a $20 combination hunt/fish license to any honorably discharged resident veteran (DD-214 or NGB-22), and gives Purple Heart recipients resident rates even if nonresident.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Wisconsin free one-time returning-veteran license and free Honor Admission Pass for state parks
items.org: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources / Wisconsin Department of Veterans Affairs
items.who: Returning Wisconsin resident veterans (qualifying war periods, certain Reserve/Guard); veterans rated 70%+ or former POWs for the Honor Admission Pass
items.value: A free one-time small game, archery, gun deer or annual fishing license for a returning veteran, and a free Honor Admission Pass (2 years or lifetime) that waives vehicle admission and trail fees.
items.how: Returning-veteran license: contact WDVA first for a voucher code, then redeem at a DNR Service Center or by phone 1-888-936-7463. Honor pass: present VA decision letter, DD-214 and Form 2500-123 to your County Veteran Service Officer.
items.hack: Voucher must be redeemed within 365 days of discharge. Wisconsin also sells a $7 Disabled Veteran Recreation Card (50%+) and $3 disabled-veteran fishing license (70%+), but those are reduced-cost, not free.
items.deadline: Returning-veteran voucher: 365 days from discharge.

items.title: Idaho Disabled Veterans Special Big Game Tag Program - five sponsored tags a year
items.org: Idaho Department of Fish and Game / Idaho Division of Veterans Services
items.who: Resident or nonresident disabled veterans sponsored by a qualifying nonprofit or government agency whose mission serves disabled veterans
items.value: Five special big-game tags per year (deer, elk, pronghorn, black bear, mountain lion) valid for any open general hunt or any controlled hunt with at least 10 tags. The page lists no fee for the tags.
