items.how: Use the official application and submit it between Jan 2 and Jan 31 of the hunt year by mail to the Executive Assistant at IDFG or email SpecialBigGameTag@idfg.idaho.gov. Idaho Division of Veterans Services screens and ranks applicants.
items.hack: The sponsor does not need to be Idaho-based and there is no cap on applicants per sponsor - ask a veteran service organization you already belong to.
items.deadline: Application window Jan 2 - Jan 31 each hunt year; late applications not accepted.

items.title: Idaho DAV resident license - $5 hunting license and very low tag fees for 40%+ disabled veterans
items.org: Idaho Department of Fish and Game
items.who: Veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 40% or more, verified by a VA Benefits Summary letter
items.value: Reduced-fee (not free) DAV license of $5 and DAV tags (deer $10.75, elk $16.50, bear $6.75, turkey $10.75 per the page). Nonresident DAV hunting license is $31.75 with 3-day fishing.
items.how: Email the VA letter to Licenses@idfg.idaho.gov, bring it to a regional office, or mail it to the Boise licensing section. Resident documentation is needed only for the first application.
items.hack: Do not send the multi-page medical report; the one-page percentage letter is enough.
items.deadline: Nonresident draw documentation was due 12/12/25 at 2pm for the 2026 draw; check the next cycle.

items.title: North Carolina lifetime hunting and fishing license for 50%+ disabled resident veterans
items.who: North Carolina residents rated 50% or more disabled by the VA
items.value: A lifetime hunting and fishing license that stays valid as long as the rating remains 50% or more. The page lists no fee - verify cost before applying.
items.how: Mail or in-person only (documentation required): submit the disabled veteran application PDF with VA certification. Customer Service 833-950-0575.
items.hack: Download the form from the Commission's License Types and Fees page under Forms & Applications.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Kentucky Disabled Sportsman's License for veterans 50%+ disabled - covers hunting, fishing, deer and turkey
items.org: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
items.who: Kentucky resident veterans at least 50% disabled from a service-connected disability
items.value: The Disabled Sportsman's License covers the combination hunting and fishing license, all deer permits, spring and fall turkey permits, migratory bird/waterfowl permit and trout permit. The page gives no price - verify the fee.
items.how: Obtain a VA letter showing your Kentucky address and rating; submit via My Profile 'Disability Authorization', by mail, fax (502-564-9845) or in person in Frankfort. Authorization is valid three years.
items.hack: Disability authorization cards are no longer issued - print from My Profile. Still need the HIP survey and a Federal Duck Stamp for waterfowl.
items.deadline: License valid through end of February each year; authorization renews every three years.

items.title: Oregon free Resident Disabled Veteran License - hunting, angling and shellfish for 25%+ rated veterans
items.org: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife
items.who: Oregon residents (6 consecutive months of physical residence) with a VA disability rating of at least 25% from any branch
items.value: Free hunting, fishing and shellfish licenses including Columbia Basin and Ocean endorsements. Resident disabled veterans can also buy one elk tag at a reduced $29 (per the page). Veterans rated 65%+ may also apply for an Oregon Disabilities Hunting and Fishing Permit.
items.how: Print and complete the ODFW disabled-veteran form and mail or deliver it in person with a copy of your most recent VA letter showing the rating.
items.hack: Oregon also holds a statewide Veterans and Active Military Waterfowl Hunt Day - February 6, 2027 - bag limits as normal; licenses, validations and a Duck Stamp are still required.
items.deadline: None for the license; waterfowl day is Feb 6, 2027.

items.title: Oklahoma Stars & Stripes License Project - donor-funded free hunting and fishing license for veterans and Gold Star next of kin
items.who: Oklahoma resident military veterans (annual license); veterans 60%+ disabled (lifetime combination license per the page); Gold Star lapel recipients and next of kin of deceased personnel (annual license)
items.value: Free annual combination hunting/fishing license, or a free lifetime combination license for veterans 60%+ disabled. Donor-funded, no cost to the sportsman. Oklahoma also sells a discounted lifetime combination license to VA-certified disabled veterans (price not shown on the page).
items.how: Apply online through the GoOutdoorsOklahoma licensing system (Customer Lookup page).
items.hack: The page lists a 60% threshold for the free lifetime license but the general disabled-veteran page requires only VA certification - confirm with the Wildlife Department before applying.
items.deadline: None stated; donor funded so availability may be limited.

items.title: Nebraska free lifetime Disabled Veteran Park Entry Permit
items.who: Nebraska residents rated 50%+ service-connected disabled, or 100% non-service-connected disabled and receiving a VA pension
items.value: A free lifetime annual park entry permit for more than 70 state park areas.
items.how: Print the application from a service center or download it, then mail it to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs office in Lincoln for certification. If you already qualified for the disabled veteran hunt/fish permit, send it to the Game and Parks Permit Section.
items.hack: Lost or stolen permits are not eligible for replacement; defective permits or trade-ins need the replacement form and the sticker.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Nebraska free lifetime Disabled Veteran Hunt/Fish/Fur Harvest Permit
items.who: Nebraska residents meeting the same disability criteria as the park permit (50%+ service-connected, or 100% non-service-connected with VA pension)
items.value: A free lifetime hunt/fish/fur harvest permit including all state stamps.
items.how: Mail the application to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, 3800 Village Drive, Lincoln, NE 68516-4737.
items.hack: Nebraska also has a free one-day Veterans Day (Nov 11) hunt permit, Habitat Stamp and waterfowl stamp for honorably discharged resident veterans, plus bonus waterfowl days for veterans and active duty open to nonresidents.
items.deadline: Free Veterans Day hunt: Nov 11 each year (Nov 11, 2026 is upcoming).

items.title: Illinois free hunting and fishing license for veterans rated 10% or more, any state of residence
items.org: Illinois Department of Veterans' Affairs / Illinois DNR
items.who: Veterans rated 10% or greater for service-connected compensation, or receiving a total disability pension, regardless of state residency (per the Illinois veterans page)
items.value: A free fishing and hunting license so no purchase is required.
items.how: Contact your local Veteran Service Officer for a Disability Affidavit. You need the DD-214, current verification of VA compensation or pension, and the affidavit, which you present on request while hunting or fishing.
items.hack: Illinois DNR parks also waive camping and admission fees for certain disabled veterans and former POWs - ask the same VSO. The page links a DNR digest reflecting SB153 changes that was not reviewed, so verify current rules.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Illinois DNR parks - free camping and admission for certain disabled veterans and former POWs
items.org: Illinois Department of Veterans' Affairs / Illinois DNR parks
items.who: Illinois residents who are certain disabled veterans or former prisoners of war
items.value: Free camping and admission at Illinois Department of Natural Resources parks.
items.how: Contact your local Veteran Service Officer; documentation is required (the page does not list which).
items.hack: Ask the VSO which disability threshold applies - the page says only 'certain' disabled veterans.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Pennsylvania free lifetime resident fishing license for 100% disabled veterans
items.who: Pennsylvania residents certified in writing by the VA as 100% service-connected disabled (60% to 99% get a reduced-fee license)
items.value: A free 'lifetime' resident fishing license plus a combination Trout/Lake Erie permit at no charge. Reduced-license holders pay full permit price.
items.how: Get the license initially from a county treasurer, the PFBC Harrisburg office or a regional law enforcement office with proof of residency and written VA certification; then buy annual licenses from agents or huntfish.pa.gov.
items.hack: VA certification is the only acceptable documentation; the page does not list the reduced fee amount.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Utah State Parks Veterans with Disabilities Honor Pass
items.org: Utah State Parks / Utah Department of Veterans and Military Affairs
items.who: Utah residents who were honorably discharged with a service-related disability and a current VA benefits summary letter
items.value: State park access for the veteran; the veterans page does not state the cost or exactly what it covers - verify before relying on it.
items.how: Pick up at Utah State Parks region offices or most state parks. Excluded parks: Flight Park, Piute, Jordan River OHV, Utahraptor, Lost Creek and This is the Place Heritage Park.
items.hack: Utah also listed an Adventure Pass Pilot Program (free day-use for one year for veterans holding an Interagency Military Lifetime Pass, capped at 1,600, first-come) - confirm it is still open.
items.deadline: Adventure Pass pilot capped at 1,600 veterans.

items.title: New Mexico free lifetime hunting and fishing license for 100% disabled veterans
items.org: New Mexico Department of Game and Fish
items.who: New Mexico residents who are 100% disabled veterans
items.value: Free lifetime game-hunting and fishing license covering fishing, small game and a free deer hunting license; no Habitat Stamp needed for fishing, small game or deer (needed for trapping, turkey or other big game).
items.how: Apply to NMDGF for a Disabled Veteran card (processed through headquarters in Santa Fe).
items.hack: Veterans under 100% pay $10 for the game-hunting and fishing license, and all resident veterans and active duty (90+ days) get 50% off licenses, permits and stamps - ask at purchase.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: New Mexico free Military Rehabilitation Fishing License
items.org: New Mexico Department of Game and Fish
items.who: Members or veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces enrolled in a federally sponsored (or federally authorized nonprofit) rehabilitation program that teaches fishing, run under a military or VA rehabilitation center
items.value: A free fishing license with no Habitat Management & Access Validation or Habitat Stamp required.
items.how: The page does not specify the application process - contact NMDGF.
items.hack: Useful for Project Healing Waters-type programs; ask the program coordinator for the paperwork.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: South Dakota Disabled Veteran Lifetime Park Entrance License - free park entry plus half-price camping
items.org: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks
items.who: South Dakota residents with a K award or VA letter showing 100% total service-connected disability, documented POWs, or Purple Heart recipients (per SDCL 41-17-13.4)
items.value: Free vehicle entry at South Dakota state parks via a lifetime billfold card (holder must be present), plus a 50% discount on camping and electrical fees for campsites and camping cabins on online reservations.
items.how: Create or log in to a Go Outdoors South Dakota profile, choose Purchase Park Entrance Licenses, add the Disabled Veteran Lifetime PEL Application to the cart, upload verification documents and check out. Status in about two weeks; the email confirmation works as a temporary license until the card arrives.
items.hack: If you lack the VA letter, the VA can send documents directly to GF&P. Questions 605-773-3391. The page does not state the application cost.
items.deadline: Status update expected within two weeks; no deadline.

items.title: North Dakota free lifetime state park entrance permit for 50%+ disabled veterans, POWs and spouses of deceased qualifying veterans
items.org: North Dakota Parks and Recreation Department
items.who: North Dakota residents who are veterans rated 50%+ service-connected, former POWs, or spouses of deceased veterans who had a 50% rating or were POWs
items.value: A free lifetime entrance permit (wallet card) admitting the holder and companions to North Dakota state parks and recreation areas; the park issues a daily exempt pass for the windshield when you show the card and photo ID.
items.how: Complete the Disabled Vet form, attach your VA benefit summary letter showing 50%+ (or POW proof) and mail to North Dakota State Parks and Recreation Department, 1600 E Century Ave, Suite 3, PO Box 5594, Bismarck, ND 58506.
items.hack: Surviving spouses are covered - an easily missed group. The VA can mail a benefit letter if you lack a copy.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Wyoming free lifetime game bird, small game and fishing licenses for Purple Heart recipients
items.who: Wyoming residents who are Purple Heart recipients
items.value: Free lifetime game bird, small game and fish licenses while the holder remains a Wyoming resident.
items.how: Proof: DD-214, a VA Veteran ID card with a Purple Heart designation, or a Purple Heart certificate; application forms are on the Game and Fish veterans licensing page.
items.hack: The same page lists separate applications for 100% disabled resident veterans (game bird, fish, small game) and 50% disabled veterans (fishing) - the page did not summarize eligibility, so read the information sheets.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Wyoming complimentary elk, deer, game bird and fishing licenses for combat-zone-deployed residents home on leave
items.who: Wyoming residents on active duty deployed to a combat zone who are home on military leave during the season and returning to duty
items.value: Complimentary resident general elk, general deer, game bird/small game and daily fishing licenses at no fee.
items.how: Issued only at the Cheyenne headquarters or regional offices. Bring a valid military ID, military leave orders, a current LES showing hostile fire compensation, and proof of residency.
items.hack: Plan the leave around the season; the licenses are issued in person only, so budget a day at the regional office.
items.deadline: Valid during the season while on leave; no separate deadline stated.

items.title: Maine free lifetime Veteran Park and Museum Pass
items.org: Maine Department of Conservation / Maine Bureau of Veterans' Services
items.who: Maine-resident veterans with an honorable or general-under-honorable discharge (veterans 65+ are not issued the pass because they get free senior admission)
items.value: Free day use at Maine state parks and historic sites plus the Maine State Museum; non-transferable, never expires. Not valid at Acadia National Park, Baxter State Park, Allagash Wilderness Waterway, Penobscot Corridor, Penobscot Narrows Observatory or Maine Wildlife Park.
items.how: The page does not describe how to apply - ask the Bureau of Veterans' Services or the Department of Conservation.
items.hack: The pass covers only the veteran, not family.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Maine free complimentary lifetime hunting and fishing license for 50%+ disabled veterans, plus the Disabled Veterans' Controlled Moose Hunt
items.org: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife / Maine Bureau of Veterans' Services
items.who: Veterans with a service-connected disability of 50% or more who are residents of Maine, New Hampshire or Vermont
items.value: A complimentary license to fish, trap and hunt (including archery, muzzleloader, crossbow, bear, migratory bird, turkey, coyote night hunt, one expanded archery antlerless permit and one either-sex permit) for the holder's life. Eligible disabled veterans can also enter a free-chance controlled moose hunt in Aroostook County in August and September, hunting with a registered Maine Guide.
items.how: Apply through the IFW disabilities page (www1.maine.gov/ifw/hunting-trapping/disabilities.html). Moose hunt applications are posted on the Bureau of Veterans' Services website around the beginning of April; in-state participants are chosen by lottery in May.
items.hack: Maine residents need the complimentary license in hand to enter the moose hunt; a veteran who already tagged a moose through this hunt is ineligible.
items.deadline: Moose hunt application opens around early April; lottery in May.

items.title: New Hampshire free lifetime fish and game license for permanently and totally disabled veterans
items.org: New Hampshire Fish and Game / New Hampshire Office of Veterans Services
items.who: Honorably discharged New Hampshire residents who are permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability (RSA 214:13)
items.value: A free lifetime license. Veterans at least 80% service-connected with a non-dishonorable discharge can apply for a lifetime license at 50% of the standard cost. Patients at the Manchester VA Medical Center and residents of the NH Veterans' Home get free fishing permits under conditions.
items.how: The page says veterans 'may apply' but does not describe steps - check the cited RSA sections or contact Fish and Game.
items.hack: The same page lists free or fee-waived plates, registration and driver's license for certain disabled veterans, former POWs and blind veterans.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Vermont free permanent fish and wildlife license for veterans ever rated 60% disabled
items.who: Vermont residents who are veterans who are, or ever have been, 60% disabled from a service-connected condition, with a specific VA letter; nonresidents from reciprocal states (the page lists NH and ME) who would qualify as Vermont residents
items.value: A free permanent license for Vermont residents (the page does not say whether it covers fishing, hunting or both); nonresident qualifying veterans get a free one-year fishing, hunting or combination license.
items.how: Call the VA Veterans Benefits Section at 1-800-827-1000 for the letter or certificate, download the Permanent License application under Special Licenses, and contact the department at 802-828-1000 or fwinformation@vermont.gov (the page does not say how to submit).
items.hack: 'Ever' 60% counts - a veteran whose rating later dropped may still qualify.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Maryland complimentary lifetime hunting license for POWs and 100% disabled veterans
items.who: Maryland residents certified as former POWs or as 100% service-connected disabled veterans, with VA documentation
items.value: A free lifetime license including the bow stamp, muzzleloader stamp and furbearer permit. Not included: the Maryland Migratory Game Bird Stamp; the federal migratory bird stamp and the Big Game Harvest Record are required annually.
items.how: Visit a DNR Licensing and Registration Service Center with VA documentation. Questions 410-260-3220.
items.hack: The same Maryland page says veterans (resident and out-of-state) and active duty/Maryland National Guard get state park day-use entrance fees waived with ID; a $75 annual passport (listed on the page) covers up to 10 people but is not free.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Maryland state park day-use fee waiver for all veterans, active duty and Maryland National Guard
items.org: Maryland Department of Natural Resources / Maryland Park Service
items.who: Active duty military and Maryland National Guard (show active duty ID); veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces, resident and out-of-state (the page does not specify the proof)
items.value: Day-use entrance charges, or the per-vehicle fee where applicable, are waived for the cardholder; other facility fees still apply.
items.how: Show your active duty military ID to the gate attendant; for veterans the page does not specify a process.
items.hack: Out-of-state veterans qualify too - rare among state park perks.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Alaska free permanent disabled-veteran hunting, fishing and trapping identification card
items.org: Alaska Department of Fish and Game / Alaska Office of Veterans Affairs
items.who: Alaska residents (per ADF&G's residency definition) certified 50% disabled or greater; must be physically present in Alaska to apply
items.value: A free permanent ID card allowing the veteran to hunt, sport fish or trap; the card becomes void immediately if the holder stops being an Alaska resident. A free Sport Fishing Harvest Record Card is needed for fisheries with annual limits.
items.how: Use the Department of Fish and Game military license page ('disabled_vet'); the veterans page does not describe the steps.
items.hack: Do not move away and keep the card - residency loss voids it immediately.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Montana Purple Heart and Legion of Valor Conservation License; free fishing permits for VA hospital patients
items.org: Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks / Montana Military Affairs Division
items.who: Purple Heart recipients (residents and nonresidents, any age); Legion of Valor members; patients at VA hospitals and residents of state institutions
items.value: A Conservation License allowing fishing and upland game bird hunting for Purple Heart recipients (cost not stated on the page); free fishing permits for VA hospital patients at the facility. Veterans with certain combat-connected injuries get half-priced deer and antelope licenses.
items.how: Purple Heart: bring proof and DD-214 to FWP offices (nonresidents must apply at FWP headquarters in Helena). Disabled licenses: fwp.mt.gov/buyandapply/hunting-licenses/disabled-licenses or (406) 444-2950.
items.hack: Legion of Valor card holders qualify too. Verify the license fee before relying on it as free.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: New Mexico Lifetime Veteran Pass - free day use, camping and utilities for every New Mexico resident veteran (effective July 1, 2025)
items.org: New Mexico State Parks Division / New Mexico Department of Veterans' Services
items.who: All New Mexico resident veterans (out-of-state veterans do not qualify); it replaced the 50%-disabled Veterans Annual Day Use and Camping Passes
items.value: Free day-use fee, camping fee and utility fees for the pass holder, plus entry at Living Desert Zoo and Gardens State Park. Not covered: central reservation fees ($3-$10 per reservation per the page), group shelters/camping, cabins and yurts, Rio Grande Nature Center parking, Smokey Bear Historical Park.
items.how: Apply through NMDVS (dvs.nm.gov or 1-866-433-8387) with a completed application, DD-214 (or equivalent) and proof of New Mexico residency. Walk-ins with a complete packet can get the pass the same day; mail/electronic takes up to 14 days after documents are received.
items.hack: Holders of the old disabled-veteran passes can use them through their 2026 expiration date, then must contact NMDVS for the lifetime pass.
items.deadline: Old disabled-veteran passes honored through their 2026 expiration; then convert.

items.title: Virginia State Parks Veteran Disability Passport - free parking, admission and half-price camping for 100% rated veterans
items.org: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
items.who: Veterans with a 100% service-connected disability rating (a separate free Disability Passport exists for people with an SSA or VA disability verification letter)
items.value: Free vehicle parking and admission for the holder and any assistant needed at parks with per-person admission; boat launch and horse-trailer parking free; 50% off camping, swimming, shelters, two-or-more-night yurts and park-operated equipment rentals (one-night yurts 25% off).
items.how: Complete form DCR199-036 and email it to resvs@dcr.virginia.gov with VA paperwork showing the 100% rating (you may redact payment and medical details).
items.hack: Replacement of a lost passport costs $15. Virginia National Guard members also get a free annual pass for the member and up to three immediate family members in the same vehicle, issued through the Guard chain of command.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Virginia National Guard free annual pass - all Virginia state parks for the member plus three family members
items.org: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation / Virginia National Guard
items.who: Active Virginia National Guard members
items.value: Free entry to all Virginia state parks for the member and up to three immediate family members traveling in the same vehicle.
items.how: Issued through the Virginia National Guard, not State Parks - go through your chain of command.
items.hack: Ask your unit; the pass is not available at park gates.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Louisiana Disabled State Park Pass, free disabled veteran plates and veteran license designation
items.org: Louisiana Department of Veterans Affairs / Louisiana Office of State Parks
items.who: Veterans with a VA disability rating of 50% or higher (100% for the 100% DAV plate)
items.value: Exemption from the day-use entrance fee at any Louisiana state park, a disabled veterans or military honors license plate at no charge, and possible driver's license/ID fee waivers (not at privatized OMV offices). 'Support Our Veterans/Troops' plates cost a one-time $25 and are not free.
items.how: Apply for the Disabled State Park Pass through lastateparks.com special rates and discounts; contact your local OMV for plates; use a Veterans Assistance Counselor via the service office locator for ID fee waivers.
items.hack: Vehicle use tax for new residents is reduced to $90 for a qualifying vehicle (registered within 90 days) - reduced, not free.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Indiana free Gold Star Families Pass and Golden Hoosier Passport for former POWs
items.who: Indiana-resident Gold Star families; Indiana-resident former POWs and their surviving spouses
items.value: Free annual entrance pass to Indiana State Parks. Former POWs receive the Golden Hoosier Passport mailed automatically at the start of each year. The page says general veterans typically do not receive free admission; the Disabled Hoosier Veteran Pass costs $25 (discounted, not free).
items.how: Gold Star: complete the Gold Star Families Pass form and email PermitApplication@dnr.IN.gov. POWs: automatic mailing; questions to jplanck@dnr.IN.gov.
items.hack: DAV1/DAV2 plate holders can buy the Golden Hoosier Passport regardless of age.
items.deadline: Passes renew annually.

items.title: New Jersey free hunting and fishing licenses for veterans with ANY service-connected disability
items.org: New Jersey Division of Fish and Wildlife
items.who: Honorably discharged New Jersey resident veterans with a service-connected disability of any degree as declared by the VA
items.value: Free licenses, permits and stamps; license agents charge no transaction fee (online orders incur a small shipping and handling fee).
items.how: Mail a Disabled Veteran License Application to NJ Fish and Wildlife in Trenton with a VA certification letter or wallet card, a DD-214 and NJ driver's license or residency proof, including your CID number; then buy licenses online or at agents. Questions: (609) 292-2965.
items.hack: Certification cannot be done online or at agents - mail only, so start well before the season.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Alabama Parks for Patriots - free state park day-use entry for veterans and active duty
items.who: Veterans and active-duty military from any branch (per a May 25, 2026 report; the Oak Mountain rates page also says active, retired and veterans are free)
items.value: Free admission to participating Alabama State Parks day-use areas that normally charge entry; 15% off lodges, cabins and campgrounds for veterans and active military (not combinable with group rates or other discounts).
items.how: The report describes no sign-up; the park page does not state proof required - bring ID and discharge/military ID and confirm at alapark.com.
items.hack: Alabamians can sponsor free entry for veterans through the program. Disabled veterans also get discounted hunting and fishing license fees (the 50% disabled license is $15.65 per the license manual - discounted, not free).
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Florida free lifetime military pass for veterans with service-related injuries and surviving spouses and parents of combat dead
items.who: Veterans with service-related injuries; surviving spouses and parents of veterans who died in combat
items.value: A free lifetime military pass that waives park entrance fees. Current and retired service members also get 25% off annual entrance passes.
items.how: The page does not say how to apply or what proof is needed; call the Florida State Parks call center at 1-800-326-3521 or 850-245-2157.
items.hack: Ask for the lifetime military pass by name; the 25% discount is a separate, smaller benefit.
items.deadline: None listed.

items.title: Massachusetts state parks - free daily parking and no annual pass for Purple Heart and disabled veteran plates
items.org: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation
items.who: Vehicles carrying a Purple Heart Recipient or disabled veteran license plate
items.value: Daily parking fees are waived and an annual parking pass is not needed. Some libraries and recreation centers also lend a DCR annual pass free of charge.
items.how: The page does not explain how to obtain the plates; ask the RMV or your veterans' services officer. Parking pass line: (617) 626-1420.
items.hack: Libraries lending passes help any veteran who lacks the plates.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Military OneSource free document translation - certified, notarized if needed, in 150+ languages
items.who: People eligible for Military OneSource: service members, spouses, family, survivors and others on the eligibility guide
items.value: Free certified translation (notarized if necessary, with a certificate of authenticity) of leases, marriage licenses, USCIS adoption paperwork, birth and death certificates and school transcripts. Medical documents and event flyers are not covered.
items.how: Call 800-342-9647 (24/7) with the document in hand; the consultant completes a Request for Translation Services form and gives a case number, then you send form and document to the translation provider.
items.hack: Each authorized case number covers one document only; documents under 5,000 words take a few business days, longer for bigger or nonstandard files. Ideal for foreign-spouse immigration paperwork.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Military OneSource free real-time interpretation in 150+ languages
items.who: People eligible for Military OneSource (service members, spouses, parents, Reserve and Guard, survivors)
items.value: Free written and real-time interpretation for English to other-language conversations, in more than 150 languages.
items.how: Call 800-342-9647 or log in for a secure live chat; overseas users should use the international calling options.
items.hack: Use it on a three-way call with a landlord, school or doctor's office - the page lists no usage cap.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: New Parent Support Program - free home visits and parenting classes for expecting parents and children up to 3 (5 for Marines)
items.org: Department of Defense / installation Family Advocacy Programs
items.who: Active-duty service members and their spouses/partners with military medical facility access who are expecting a child or have a child age 3 or younger (5 or younger for Marine Corps)
items.value: Free voluntary home visits on sleep, nutrition, behavior, breastfeeding and siblings; referrals; parenting classes and playgroups where offered.
items.how: Enroll through your installation's Family Advocacy Program, Military and Family Support Center or New Parent Support Program.
items.hack: Classes are not offered everywhere. If you are not near an installation, the page suggests a New MilParent Specialty Consultation through Military OneSource.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Military and Family Life Counseling (MFLC) - free confidential non-medical counseling in person, phone or video
items.who: Service members and immediate family members
items.value: Free confidential counseling with licensed counselors on relationships, stress, adjusting to change, parenting and grief; also briefings and presentations. In person, by phone or by video, on and off the installation.
items.how: Use the MFLC Locator tool on Military OneSource to find a counselor.
items.hack: The page was marked as a testing site - confirm on the public site; the page does not describe confidentiality exceptions, so ask the counselor up front.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Military OneSource health and wellness coaching - including coaching for teens
items.who: Service members, National Guard, spouses, survivors, transitioning members and leaders; teens 13+ with a parent at the first session
items.value: Coaching for weight management, fitness, nutrition and stress, and help planning through deployment, moving and new parenthood. The page says free consultations are available but does not state whether ongoing sessions cost anything.
items.how: Call 800-342-9647 or log in for secure live chat.
items.hack: The page was marked as a testing site and gives no session limits - ask how many sessions are included when you book.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Boys & Girls Clubs of America military partnership - free or reduced membership for military kids ages 6-18
items.org: Boys & Girls Clubs of America / Military OneSource
items.who: Children of active-duty, National Guard and Reserve service members
items.value: Free or reduced memberships at traditional clubs near installations for off-base families; on-installation families join BGCA-affiliated programs through the military youth center. The page does not state the discount value.
items.how: On-installation: ask the military youth center. Off-installation: use the BGCA military outreach page (bgca.org/about-us/military) to find a club.
items.hack: The page was a testing-site copy - confirm the current membership fee waiver with your local club.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: TurboTax Online free federal and state filing for enlisted service members with a DFAS W-2
items.who: Enlisted active-duty and Reserve members (the post says E-1 to E-9) with a DFAS W-2; a spouse can be included on a joint return. Not officers, warrant officers, retirees or veterans; National Guard only under qualifying active reserve orders through DFAS
items.value: Federal and state filing through TurboTax Online Free Edition, Deluxe or Premium at $0 after the military discount applies automatically (no promo code, per the post).
items.how: Start a standard TurboTax Online product, enter your DFAS W-2 and verify military status and pay grade. The post dated Jan 2024, updated Jan 2026 does not state the tax year - confirm current terms.
items.hack: MilTax is free for the whole military community and has no pay-grade limit; use it if you do not qualify here. The post's headline says E1-E5 but its body says E-1 to E-9 - verify before relying on it.
items.deadline: Confirm the current tax year's terms before filing.

items.title: Sesame Street for Military Families - free videos, articles and activities in English and Spanish
items.who: Military service members and their families, including providers
items.value: Free everyday-parenting articles, videos with Sesame Street characters and printable activity handouts, plus online activities to help children cope with big feelings (page dated January 15, 2025).
items.how: Go to sesamestreetformilitaryfamilies.org (everyday parenting section) - no sign-up described.
items.hack: Use the printable handouts for deployment and PCS conversations with young children.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: USO Support for Transitioning Service Members (Pathfinder) - free one-on-one transition specialist and Coursera/Skillsoft certifications
items.who: Active duty, Reserve and National Guard members and military spouses (SkillBridge session limited to those within 180 days of release)
items.value: Free one-on-one support from a USO Specialist, a personalized career/education/financial plan, resume and interview help, free Coursera and Skillsoft certifications, and mentor access.
items.how: Click 'Connect with a USO Transition Specialist' on the program page and complete the online registration form.
items.hack: The page did not use the name Pathfinder - it is the program page that the old Pathfinder URLs now redirect to. Event sign-ups are separate.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: MySECO spouse career coaching - free coaching, resume reviews and a year of LinkedIn Premium
items.who: Military spouses, new and experienced, who need help with careers
items.value: Free career coaching on education options, funding, job search, networking, mock interviews and entrepreneurship; self-assessments, resume builder, scholarship finder, on-demand resume reviews, customized job leads, specialty coaching tracks (health care, IT, federal, K-12, freelancing), and a free year of LinkedIn Premium.
items.how: Call 800-342-9647 or use Live Chat on the MySECO website.
items.hack: Ask for a specialty coaching package that matches your field instead of general coaching.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: Wounded Warrior Project Physical Health and Wellness coaching - free multi-day expo plus personal coaching
items.who: Registered WWP warriors (post-9/11 veterans, active duty and transitioning members) and family members for select programs
items.value: Free tailored wellness plan, in-person and virtual events, personalized coaching starting with a multi-day expo, movement, nutrition and sleep skill-building, and referral to adaptive sports. No gym memberships or gym equipment.
items.how: Register through WWP's registration page, or call the WWP Resource Center (888.WWP.ALUM / 904.405.1213) or use live chat.
items.hack: Already-registered warriors connect through the MyWWP app or portal.
items.deadline: None stated.

items.title: Texas free Disabled Veteran Super Combo Hunting and All-Water Fishing Package
items.who: Disabled veterans (Texas residents or nonresidents) as defined by VA: loss of use of a foot or leg, or a rating of 50% or more, receiving federal disability compensation
items.value: Free (item 502): resident hunting and fishing licenses plus archery, freshwater, saltwater (with red drum tag), upland game bird and migratory game bird endorsements. The Federal Duck Stamp is not included.
items.how: In person only at a license retailer (not online). Show proof each year: VA documentation or a Texas driver license with a 'Disabled Veteran' designation, stating your rating and issued within the last 12 months.
items.hack: Update your Texas license with the Disabled Veteran designation once so you can show it every year instead of fetching a new VA letter.
items.deadline: Proof must be renewed every year.

items.title: Kansas free permanent hunting and fishing license for disabled veterans rated 30% or more
items.org: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks / Kansas Commission on Veterans Affairs Office
items.who: Kansas residents who separated under honorable conditions with a service-connected rating of 30% or higher certified by the Kansas Commission on Veterans Affairs Office
items.value: A permanent hunting and fishing license issued free of charge; the law also exempts qualifying residents from the hunting and fishing license fees in the fee schedule.
items.how: Based on the text of HB 2039 (2023), not an agency application page - ask Kansas Wildlife and Parks and your Kansas veterans office how to apply and which certification form to use.
items.hack: Because the source is the enacted bill, confirm the current process and any hunter-education requirement with the department.
items.deadline: The bill text gives no separate start date.

items.title: Tennessee State Parks expanded veteran discounts - free Veterans Day night and half-price camping for 100% disabled veterans
items.org: Tennessee State Parks (announced by Tennessee House Republican Caucus)
items.who: Tennessee-resident veterans; 100% disabled residents keep a 50%-off benefit year-round
items.value: One free night of camping on Veterans Day (premium sites excluded); 25% off campsites and cabins March-November and 50% off December-February; 25% off lodge rooms year-round; 20% off park golf green fees; 15% off gift and golf shop purchases. 100% disabled residents keep 50% off campsite and cabin rentals year-round.
items.how: The press release does not describe the claim process - see TNStateParks.com/about/discounts for documentation and exclusions.
items.hack: Source is a legislative caucus press release dated November 2025 with no stated start date - confirm on the state parks site before booking. Most of this is discount, not free.
items.deadline: Veterans Day (Nov 11) for the free night.

items.title: Thrive online parenting program - free modules for every age from 0 to 18
items.who: Open to the public per Military OneSource; aimed at military parents; shareable with family members and caregivers
items.value: Four free interactive modules: Take Root (0-3), Sprout (3-5), Grow (5-10) and Branch Out (10-18), covering positive discipline, stress, healthy meals and screen time; supplemental modules include exceptional families, grandparents as caregivers and mental health.
items.how: Use the Access Thrive link (thrive.psu.edu) from the Military OneSource page; help at 800-342-9647.
items.hack: Sessions can be paused at any time - good for deployments and PCS gaps; caregivers and grandparents can use it too.
items.deadline: None.

items.title: National WWII Museum - free admission year-round for active servicemembers in uniform, WWII veterans and branch-birthday days
items.who: Active servicemembers in uniform (US and international), WWII veterans plus one companion; free days for active, reserve, retired and veteran members on their branch's birthday, Armed Forces Day and Veterans Day
items.value: Free admission year-round for uniformed active servicemembers; free admission on Armed Forces Day, Veterans Day and the member's own branch birthday (Army June 14, Coast Guard Aug 4, Air Force Sept 18, Navy Oct 13, Marine Corps Nov 10, National Guard Dec 13, Space Force Dec 20). Year-round $10 off for active, retired and veteran members and spouses (per the page).
items.how: The page does not specify the proof required - bring military ID or DD-214.
items.hack: Check your branch's birthday date for a free day; the Navy birthday is Oct 13 and the Marine Corps birthday is Nov 10 - both upcoming.
items.deadline: Navy birthday Oct 13, 2026; Marine Corps birthday Nov 10, 2026.

states.name: Alabama
states.headline: Military retirement is fully untaxed and a 100% P&T rating wipes out property tax on the home plus 160 acres, while the GI Dependent Scholarship is one of the most generous dependent education benefits in the country.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. The Alabama Department of Revenue lists 'military retirement pay' outright on its Income Exempt from Alabama Income Taxation schedule, with no age, dollar or income condition.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxed. Resident service members pay Alabama income tax on base pay. Exempt: allowances for quarters, subsistence, uniforms and travel, and all compensation for active service in a presidentially designated combat zone.
incomeTax.notes: VA disability compensation and all other VA-disbursed benefits are exempt. Survivor Benefit Plan annuities are also untaxed. Alabama's top individual rate is 5%, so the retirement exemption is worth roughly 5 cents on the dollar.

states.propertyTax: Alabama's Homestead Exemption 3 gives a total exemption from all state, county and municipal ad valorem taxes on the principal residence plus up to 160 adjacent acres, with no cap on value. It is available to anyone who is permanently and totally disabled regardless of age or income — which a 100% P&T VA rating establishes — or to residents 65+ whose taxable income is under $12,000. Separately, any home acquired or adapted with a VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant is exempt from all Alabama property taxes regardless of the property's value, and that exemption follows the home. There is no sliding scale by rating percentage: below P&T status a veteran gets no veteran-specific property tax break, which is the sharp edge of this system. Vehicles all or partly paid for with VA grant funds are exempt from both license fees and ad valorem tax when used solely by the disabled veteran.
states.education: The Alabama G.I. Dependent Scholarship Program is the headline benefit and is unusually deep: dependents of a veteran rated 40% or higher (or a former POW, MIA, or a veteran who died of a service-connected disability) receive $400 per credit hour plus up to $1,000 per year for textbooks at Alabama public institutions. Children and stepchildren get five standard academic years (10 semesters) and must begin before their 26th birthday (extendable to 30 in defined circumstances); spouses of 100% disabled veterans get 10 semesters, and spouses of veterans rated 40–90% get three years (six semesters). Note the program was converted from an open-ended full-tuition waiver to this capped per-credit-hour formula, so it no longer covers 100% of cost at the more expensive campuses — this is the recent tightening to watch. Purple Heart recipients get a separate full waiver of tuition and fees at Alabama public institutions covering up to 125% of required credit hours, undergraduate only, applied after other education benefits. The Alabama National Guard Education Assistance Program (ANGEAP) pays $6,277.00 per semester or $4,151.33 per quarter toward costs not covered by VA benefits, requiring a 2.0 undergraduate / 3.0 graduate GPA. Operation Recognition awards high school diplomas to WWII, Korea and Vietnam era veterans who left school to serve.
states.employment: State hiring preference adds points to passing exam scores: 5 points for honorable discharge, 10 points for veterans receiving VA disability compensation, 10 points for spouses of disabled veterans who cannot work, and 10 points for surviving spouses of service members killed in the line of duty. Preference-eligible employees must be the last discharged in a reduction in force. State employees in reserve components receive 168 working hours of paid military leave per calendar year. A genuinely useful and little-known item: disabled veterans rated 25% or higher with wartime service who are self-employed with no more than one employee pay a flat reduced $25 fee for state business and occupational licenses. Alabama honors the CDL military skills test waiver for service members with 30+ days operating military vehicles (the knowledge test is still required). USERRA protections apply, including health coverage continuation up to 24 months at up to 102% of premium.
states.vehicleRec: The 'Veteran' designation on a driver license is free at first issuance or renewal for anyone with an honorable or general discharge. Vehicle privilege/license tax and registration fees are waived for Alabama National Guard members (active and retired), Reserve component members, veterans rated 10% or higher, and Gold Star Families. There are 43 distinctive military and veteran plate options: Medal of Honor and Gold Star Family plates are exempt from registration fees and taxes on the first plate; Purple Heart and Disabled Veteran (10–50%) plates are exempt from registration fees on the first plate; at 51%+ the first plate is free and additional plates are $5 a year; a VA-funded vehicle gets all plates exempt from fees and taxes. Hunting and fishing is well-tiered: reduced-price lifetime fishing licenses at 20% disability, reduced-price lifetime hunting at 40%, a $17.30 annual hunting license at 50%, and a $3.60 annual hunting license at 100%. Resident active duty on leave need no license at all, and nonresident active duty stationed in Alabama 30+ days pay resident prices. The Parks for Patriots program gives resident veterans and active duty free admission to Alabama State Parks (nonresidents only on state and federal holidays), proven with a military ID, a veteran-designated Alabama license, or a DD214.
states.cash: Alabama has no state wartime service bonus and no general state-funded emergency financial assistance fund for veterans — a real gap relative to neighboring states. The only cash item identified is the Alabama National Guard J.E.E.P. recruiting incentive, which pays $1,000 per successful recruit referral (up to 10 per fiscal year) to active members O4 and below and to retirees of all ranks. There is no state supplement to the VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Five state veterans homes, all skilled nursing with 24-hour coverage, physician on call, physical/occupational/speech therapy, pharmacy, dietary and social services: Bill Nichols (Alexander City, 256-329-3311), Floyd E. 'Tut' Fann (Huntsville, 256-851-2807), William F. Green (Bay Minette, 251-937-8049), Colonel Robert L. Howard (Pell City, 205-338-6487), and Command Sergeant Major Bennie G. Adkins (Enterprise, 334-470-2443). Admission requires 90+ days active duty with honorable discharge (24 months for post-9/7/1980 enlistees), VA medical eligibility, and 12 months of Alabama residency before applying. One state cemetery: the Alabama State Veterans Memorial Cemetery at Spanish Fort (251-625-1338), offering in-ground burial, cremation, columbarium niches and a scattering garden — free for the veteran, $375 for a dependent — requiring Alabama residency at death, at entry to service, or 10 cumulative years. Six VA national cemeteries also operate in Alabama.
other: Reduced $25 flat state business/occupational license fee for self-employed veterans rated 25%+ with wartime service and no more than one employee
Free public records: one copy of any record needed for a VA benefit determination, at no charge
Free recording of discharge papers by probate judges, with access restricted to the veteran, attorney, spouse, next of kin or designated representative
180-day foreclosure delay for service members who die overseas
Uniform Veterans Guardianship Act allows court appointment of guardians for incapacitated veterans and dependents
Courts may commit an incompetent veteran directly into VA Medical Center treatment
Purple Heart tuition waiver covers 125% of required credit hours — more headroom than most states' 100% or 110% caps
states.topHack: Get the VA to designate your disability permanent and total, then file for Homestead Exemption 3 at the county revenue office — not the standard homestead exemption. Exemption 3 is granted on 'permanent and total disability' with no age test and no income test, and it zeroes out state, county AND city property tax on the residence plus 160 acres with no value cap. Most veterans default into Exemption 2 or the ordinary $4,000 homestead and quietly overpay for years. Second-order: if you ever receive a VA Specially Adapted Housing grant, the resulting home is exempt from all Alabama property tax regardless of value or your later rating status.

states.name: Alaska
states.headline: No income tax at all, a $150,000 property tax exemption that starts at a 50% rating rather than requiring 100%, and the Permanent Fund Dividend on top — undercut only by thin veteran-specific tuition benefits.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Not taxed — Alaska has no individual income tax, so military retired pay, Survivor Benefit Plan annuities and TSP distributions are all free of state tax.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Not taxed. No state income tax applies to active duty, Guard or Reserve pay.
incomeTax.notes: Alaska also has no statewide sales tax, though municipalities may levy local sales taxes. There is no state-level add-on for VA disability because there is no income tax to exempt it from.

states.propertyTax: Under AS 29.45.030 the first $150,000 of assessed value on a primary residence is exempt for veterans with a service-connected disability rated 50% or higher — notably a much lower threshold than the 100% P&T requirement most states impose. The same $150,000 exemption independently covers residents 65 and older, so an older disabled veteran does not stack two exemptions but is certain to qualify under one. The exemption transfers to a surviving spouse only if that spouse is at least 60 years old. This is a state mandate that municipalities must honor, but municipalities may and sometimes do exempt additional value above $150,000 at local option, so the effective benefit is larger in some boroughs (Matanuska-Susitna and Fairbanks North Star each publish their own supplements). Because Alaska property is assessed and taxed only by organized boroughs and cities, veterans in the unorganized borough may owe no property tax at all.
states.education: Alaska is weak here and it is the main thing holding the state back. There is no broad tuition waiver for veterans themselves and no dependent tuition program comparable to Illinois, Alabama or Indiana. What exists: the Alaska National Guard tuition program covers up to 100% of tuition at University of Alaska System schools, or up to $2,500 per year at other in-state post-secondary institutions, for current Guard members. Operation Recognition awards high school diplomas to WWII-era veterans who left school to serve. Alaska participates in the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children (MIC3), which smooths enrollment, records transfer and graduation requirements for military kids. Veterans using federal VA education benefits receive in-state tuition rates at University of Alaska campuses.
states.employment: State hiring preference gives 5 points to veterans and 10 points to disabled veterans and former prisoners of war; preference also extends to National Guard members and eligible family members. Professional licensing is handled well: temporary licenses valid 180 days are available, boards accept military education and training toward licensure requirements, deployed service members may defer renewal requirements without penalty, and Military Family Life Counselors get expedited processing. Alaska honors military occupational credentials toward civilian licensure on a board-by-board basis.
states.vehicleRec: The 'Veteran' designation is available on Alaska driver licenses. Special plates include Purple Heart, Disabled Veteran, standard Veteran and Gold Star Family designs, with optional unit symbols. Hunting and fishing licenses are free for Alaska National Guard and Reserve members and for disabled veterans rated 50% or higher — a substantial benefit in a state where nonresident tags run into the hundreds of dollars; nonresident active duty stationed in Alaska pay discounted rates. Disabled veterans receive a free annual state park camping pass. Distinctively, qualified veterans get a one-time 25% discount on purchases of state residential or recreational land (some state sources describe this as 20%; the discount percentage has changed over time and should be confirmed with the Department of Natural Resources before relying on it).
states.cash: The Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend is the big one and it is not veteran-specific but is unusually valuable to veterans who establish residency: every eligible Alaska resident, including veterans and service members who meet the residency test, receives an annual dividend (the 2025 payment was $1,000, and the amount is set annually by the legislature). The application window runs January 1 through March 31. Beyond the PFD, Alaska offers the Alaska Housing Finance Corporation Veterans Mortgage Program, which reduces the interest rate by 1% on the first $50,000 of a loan — effectively a recurring cash benefit rather than a lump sum. There is no wartime service bonus and no dedicated state veterans emergency relief fund identified.
states.homesHealth: Alaska does not operate a conventional multi-site state veterans home system. The Alaska Veterans and Pioneers Home in Palmer is a long-term care facility serving veterans aged 60 and over who need nursing care and meet residency requirements, providing meals, medication management, nursing care and specialized Alzheimer's care; it is part of the state Division of Pioneer Homes. The Interior of Alaska Veterans Cemetery serves the Fairbanks region, and two VA national cemeteries operate in the state. Long-term care capacity is a genuine constraint given Alaska's geography, and many veterans travel out of state for specialized care.
other: Permanent Fund Dividend paid annually to every eligible resident — a de facto cash benefit that stacks with everything else
50% reduction on passenger fares on the Alaska Marine Highway System ferries for disabled veterans
20% discount on Alaska Railroad fares for veterans, active duty and dependents
AHFC Veterans Mortgage Program: 1% interest rate reduction on up to $50,000 of the loan
Free recording of DD214 separation documents at state recorder offices
One-time discount on state land purchases for qualified veterans
Property tax exemption triggers at a 50% rating, not 100% — among the lowest thresholds of any state

agency.name: Alaska Office of Veterans Affairs, Department of Military and Veterans Affairs

states.topHack: The $150,000 exemption starts at a 50% rating, not 100% — this is the single most underused fact about Alaska. A veteran at 50%, 60% or 70% who assumes property tax relief requires P&T status is leaving the full exemption on the table, and in most Alaska boroughs $150,000 of exempt assessed value covers a large share of a typical home. Then check your specific borough separately: Mat-Su and Fairbanks North Star add municipal exemptions on top of the state-mandated $150,000, and those local supplements are granted only on separate application to the borough assessor.

states.name: Arizona
states.headline: All military retired pay and active duty pay are fully exempt from income tax, but the disabled veteran property tax exemption is so small and so tightly income- and value-capped that in practice almost no homeowner qualifies.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Arizona has excluded 100% of military retired pay since tax year 2021, with no dollar cap, age condition or income limit. This replaced the prior $3,500 subtraction.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Arizona does not tax military compensation for members of the active or reserve components.
incomeTax.notes: Arizona levies a flat 2.5% individual income tax, so the value of the exemption is modest per dollar but applies to the entire pension. Survivor Benefit Plan annuities and VA disability compensation are also untaxed.

states.propertyTax: This is Arizona's clear weak point and the figures should be checked before relying on them because they are indexed annually. The disabled veteran exemption reduces assessed value by up to approximately $4,748 scaled by disability percentage, and it is subject to both an income test (roughly $39,865 with no dependents, $47,826 with dependents) and a total property value cap of roughly $36,454. Because the property value cap is far below the assessed value of a typical Arizona home, the overwhelming majority of disabled veteran homeowners are disqualified outright, and the ones who do qualify receive a few hundred dollars. Veterans rated 100% may receive a complete exemption but remain subject to the same income and value limitations. Arizona voters approved Proposition 130 in 2022 restoring constitutional authority for a veterans' property tax exemption, and the legislature has debated expanding it in subsequent sessions; verify with the county assessor and the Arizona Department of Revenue whether the caps have been raised for the 2026 tax year, because the 2026 figures were not independently confirmed.
states.education: Arizona grants immediate in-state residency for tuition purposes to recent veterans and dependents using VA Chapters 30, 31, 33 or 35 — a meaningful benefit at Arizona's three public universities. Tuition waivers are available for Purple Heart recipients, service members rated 50% or higher, and survivors of fallen service members at Arizona public institutions. The Arizona National Guard State Tuition Reimbursement program pays up to $5,250 annually. Arizona does not have a broad dependent tuition waiver on the scale of Illinois, Texas or Alabama; the dependent benefit is restricted to survivors of the fallen. Honorary high school diplomas are issued to WWII, Korean War and Vietnam War veterans who left school to serve.
states.employment: State hiring preference gives 5 points to eligible veterans and 10 points to disabled veterans. Arizona has been among the more aggressive states on licensure portability — it recognizes out-of-state occupational licenses broadly under its universal licensure recognition law, which disproportionately helps military spouses arriving on PCS orders, and boards accept military training and experience toward licensure. The CDL skills test waiver is honored for service members with recent military vehicle experience. Arizona@Work centers provide priority of service and DVOP/LVER specialists.
states.vehicleRec: Veteran license plates cost $25 initially plus $25 annually. Veterans rated 100% disabled receive a full exemption from the vehicle license tax and registration fee. Deployed service members get a one-year exemption from registration fees. Driver licenses remain valid six months past discharge. Hunting and fishing is strong: free licenses for veterans rated 100%, a reduced $42 fee for partially disabled veterans, and $28 for Purple Heart recipients. Arizona State Parks give active duty and retired veterans a 50% discount on day-use entrance fees, and veterans rated 100% receive free annual passes.
states.cash: Arizona has no wartime service bonus and no broad state-funded emergency cash assistance program for veterans identified in official sources. The Arizona Department of Veterans' Services administers a Veterans' Donation Fund supported by a voluntary income tax check-off that makes small grants to veterans in crisis, but per-grant amounts and eligibility were not verified. There is no state supplement to the VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Four state veterans homes, all skilled nursing: Phoenix (4141 North Silvestre Herrera Way, 602-248-1550), Tucson (555 East Ajo Way, 520-638-2150), Yuma (6051 E 34th Street, 928-247-8300) and Flagstaff (2100 N Gemini Drive, 928-637-0600). Three state veterans memorial cemeteries: Sierra Vista (Southern Arizona Veterans Memorial Cemetery), Bellemont (at Camp Navajo) and Marana. This is an unusually well-distributed network for a state of Arizona's population, and the Flagstaff and Yuma homes are recent additions that cut travel distance considerably for rural veterans.
other: Universal licensure recognition law makes Arizona one of the easiest states for a military spouse to transfer an out-of-state professional license
Immediate in-state tuition residency for recent veterans using VA education benefits — no waiting period
Four state veterans homes and three state cemeteries, unusually good geographic coverage
100% disabled veterans get free hunting and fishing licenses plus free state park annual passes
Full income tax exemption on BOTH active duty pay and retired pay — one of a minority of states doing both
states.topHack: Ignore the property tax exemption — it is effectively dead letter for anyone who owns a normal house — and instead stack the income tax exemption with residency timing. Because Arizona exempts 100% of both active duty pay and military retired pay while charging only a 2.5% flat rate, a service member who changes state of legal residence to Arizona in the final years before retirement converts an entire pension to permanently state-tax-free without the phase-ins, age gates or dollar caps that Georgia, Colorado, Delaware and Idaho impose. Pair that with the immediate in-state tuition residency for VA education benefit users, which Arizona grants on day one rather than after 12 months.

states.name: Arkansas
states.headline: One of the few states that exempts active duty pay AND retired pay AND survivor annuities entirely, paired with a complete homestead and personal property tax exemption at 100% P&T that the surviving spouse keeps.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Arkansas exempts military retired pay from state income tax with no cap, and also exempts Survivor Benefit Plan, Reserve Component SBP and Retired Serviceman's Family Protection Plan annuities.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Military pay received by members serving in an active or reserve component of the U.S. Armed Forces is exempt from Arkansas income tax.
incomeTax.notes: Military disability retirement pay and VA disability compensation are excluded from taxable income. Arkansas also does not tax Social Security benefits. The combination of exempt active duty pay, exempt retired pay and exempt survivor annuities is genuinely unusual — most states do at most two of the three.

states.propertyTax: Arkansas grants a full exemption from homestead property tax AND from personal property tax for veterans with a 100% total and permanent service-connected disability rating, and for veterans receiving Special Monthly Compensation for loss or loss of use of a limb or for total blindness. There is no income test and no property value cap, which makes it materially stronger than the capped exemptions in Arizona, Idaho or Kansas. The unremarried surviving spouse and dependent children keep the exemption where the veteran was receiving it before death, where the service member died in the line of duty, was declared missing in action, or died from a service-connected cause. A spouse who remarried may regain the exemption if the later marriage terminates. Annual recertification is required, and missing it is the most common way veterans lose this benefit. There is no sliding scale — below 100% P&T or the specific SMC categories there is no veteran-specific property tax break.
states.education: The Arkansas Heroes Scholarship Program covers tuition, housing and mandatory fees remaining unpaid after federal Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance, for spouses and dependent children under 26 of service members who are POW/MIA, killed in action or on ordnance delivery, or rated 100% total and permanent. It is limited to eight semesters or degree completion and requires one year of Arkansas residency, a 2.0 GPA and 24 semester hours annually. The Arkansas National Guard Tuition Waiver (NGTW) waives tuition and mandatory fees (not books) for up to 120 credit hours or bachelor's completion at Arkansas public institutions for current Guard members who are Arkansas residents, have completed initial active duty training, hold no prior bachelor's degree and enroll full-time. In-state tuition is granted to nonresident honorably discharged veterans with 90+ days active duty enrolling within three years of separation, to their spouses and children, to active duty members and families, and to ROTC cadets. Local districts award high school diplomas to WWII, Korea and Vietnam veterans with 18+ months of wartime active duty, and students completing Basic Training before graduation receive two units of Career Focus credit.
states.employment: State hiring preference adds 5 points to a passing exam score for veterans, surviving spouses and National Guard/Reserve members, and 10 points for disabled veterans and spouses of disabled veterans unable to work; where no examination is used the hiring authority must document how preference was applied. State employees get 15 days of paid military leave annually for reserve training and 30 days of paid leave for emergency active duty call-ups, with no loss of seniority, ratings or promotion status. Arkansas expressly authorizes private and local government employers to adopt voluntary veteran hiring preference policies provided they are written and uniformly applied. The Division of Workforce Services runs transition assistance, skills assessment, apprenticeship placement and DVOP/LVER support with priority of service.
states.vehicleRec: The 'Veteran' designation on a driver license or ID is optional and available on presentation of a DD214, NGB 22, VA ID card, DD256/257 or DD2. Licenses for active and reserve members are extended until 60 days after separation. Nineteen military specialty plates are available: Medal of Honor (free first plate; surviving spouse pays $4), Purple Heart (free; survivors pay the registration fee), Disabled Veteran (free first plate, $4 for additional, $4 for survivors), and Gold Star Family (free, one per applicant, open to surviving spouse, sibling, child or parent with a DD1300). Hunting and fishing is exceptional: veterans rated 100% pay $1.50 for a resident lifetime fishing license, $1.50 for lifetime hunting, or $3.00 for a lifetime combination; veterans at 70%+ (or 50%+ with a Purple Heart) pay $52.50 for the combination. Military retirees aged 60+ pay $10.50 lifetime fishing, $25.00 lifetime hunting, $35.50 lifetime combination. Nonresident active duty assigned to Arkansas, and anyone who enlisted from Arkansas, pay resident prices. State park camping is half price year-round for residents rated 100% total and permanent.
states.cash: Arkansas has no wartime service bonus and no general state-funded emergency cash assistance fund for veterans — the weakest category in an otherwise strong state. The Arkansas National Guard provides State Sponsored Life Insurance with $1,000 of free coverage for all members, $10,000 free for the first year of new members, and optional coverage from $10,000 to $270,000 with 24-hour claims processing, no war or aviation exclusions, and full conversion on separation without proving insurability. Guard members injured on state active duty are covered under Arkansas workers' compensation. There is no state supplement to the VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Two state veterans homes: Fayetteville (1179 North College Avenue, 90-bed skilled nursing, 479-444-7001, ASVHF@arkansas.gov) and North Little Rock (2401 John Ashley Drive, 96-bed, 501-683-1406, ASVHNLR@arkansas.gov), both offering hospice, skilled nursing, physical/occupational/speech therapy, clinical social work, transportation and on-site barber/beautician services. Eligibility requires honorable discharge and demonstrable need for nursing care; spouses and Gold Star parents are also eligible. Two state veterans cemeteries: North Little Rock (1501 West Maryland Avenue, 501-683-2259) and Birdeye (3600 Hwy 163, 870-588-4608), providing free veteran burial, grave opening and closing, columbaria for cremains, federal headstones and perpetual care, with an $807 fee for dependents. The Arkansas Veterans Legal Services Clinic (501-916-3434) provides free legal assistance with VA appeals and discharge upgrades, supervised by a VA-accredited attorney with law student support.
other: Gross receipts (sales) tax exemption on specially adapted vehicles purchased or modified with VA funds for a service-connected injury
Arkansas Service Members Civil Relief Act allows a 180-day deferral of state income tax with no interest or penalties, and suspends the statute of limitations during service plus 270 days
National Guard State Sponsored Life Insurance with no war or aviation exclusion clauses — rare in the insurance market
Free Veterans Legal Services Clinic handling VA appeals and discharge upgrades
Service members do not lose home-of-record status or acquire Arkansas residency merely by being stationed there on orders
Full exemption covers personal property tax as well as real property — most states exempt only the home
states.topHack: Do not overlook that the 100% P&T exemption covers personal property tax, not just the homestead. Arkansas is one of a small number of states that levies annual ad valorem tax on vehicles, boats and trailers, and the disabled veteran exemption wipes that out too — for a household with two or three vehicles that is often worth more per year than the homestead portion. The trap: the exemption requires annual recertification with the county, and veterans who assume a P&T rating means permanent enrollment silently lose it. Set a calendar reminder. Also check Special Monthly Compensation: SMC for loss of use of a limb or total blindness qualifies for the full exemption even without a 100% schedular rating.

states.name: California
states.headline: The College Fee Waiver for dependents is among the best in the nation and the disabled veteran property tax exemption is large in dollar terms, but California only recently began exempting any military retirement income and still taxes most of it.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Partially exempt, and this is new. For tax years 2025 through 2029 California excludes up to $20,000 of military retired pay, phased against income: available to filers with income up to $125,000 (single or head of household) or $250,000 (married filing jointly). Before 2025 California taxed military retirement in full and was one of the last states to do so. The exclusion sunsets after 2029 unless the legislature extends it.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Partially taxed. Resident service members stationed outside California pay no California tax on military income; those stationed in California are taxed normally on it. Combat pay excluded federally is also excluded from California income.
incomeTax.notes: California's top marginal rate is 13.3%, so the $20,000 exclusion is worth more per dollar here than a full exclusion would be in a low-rate state — but it still leaves most of a typical O-5 or E-8 pension taxable. VA disability compensation is not taxed. Nonresident military spouses are covered by MSRRA.

states.propertyTax: The Disabled Veterans' Exemption comes in two tiers, both indexed annually for inflation by the Board of Equalization: a basic exemption of approximately $180,671 of assessed value with no income test, and a low-income exemption of approximately $271,009 for households with income at or below roughly $81,131. Eligibility requires a 100% disability rating or Individual Unemployability, wartime service, and a discharge other than dishonorable. The basic exemption is applied for once; the low-income exemption must be reclaimed annually. Because Proposition 13 caps assessed value growth at 2% per year, a long-tenured owner's assessed value may be far below market value, in which case the exemption can eliminate most or all of the tax; for a recent purchaser at California prices it covers only a fraction. The unremarried surviving spouse retains the exemption. These specific 2026 dollar figures were sourced from a DoD summary rather than directly from the Board of Equalization and should be confirmed against the BOE's current-year letter to assessors before being published.
states.education: The CalVet College Fee Waiver for Veteran Dependents is the marquee benefit and it waives mandatory systemwide tuition and fees at all California Community Colleges, CSU and UC campuses. Four plans: Plan A covers children and spouses of veterans rated 100% service-connected disabled or who died of service-connected causes (children aged 15–26, extended to 30 for a veteran's child who is themselves a veteran); Plan B covers children of veterans with any service-connected disability rating where the child's own income is below the filing requirement, with no age limit and no wartime service requirement — this is the plan most families miss; Plan C covers dependents of California National Guard members killed or disabled on state active duty; Plan D covers children of Medal of Honor recipients under 27. Note the waiver covers systemwide tuition and fees but not campus-based fees, books, housing or (at UC) the full professional degree supplemental tuition. Nonresident fee waivers apply to active duty members and dependents stationed in California. The California Military Department GI Bill pays up to 100% of tuition for California National Guard members who accept a two-year post-completion service obligation.
states.employment: California gives veterans top ranking on state civil service eligibility lists rather than a numeric point bonus — a strong form of preference for entry-level classifications, though it does not apply to promotional examinations. Federal 5- and 10-point preference applies separately. California honors the CDL military skills test waiver and accepts military training toward a range of occupational licenses; the state has also adopted expedited licensure and temporary licensure pathways for military spouses. USERRA reemployment and seniority protections apply. CalVet and the Employment Development Department (800-300-5616) run veteran employment services with DVOP specialists and priority of service.
states.vehicleRec: A 'Veteran' designation on the driver license is available at no additional fee. Registration fees are waived for veterans rated 100% disabled with a qualifying mobility impairment, and nonresident service members are exempt from the Vehicle License Fee. The first set of Medal of Honor, Purple Heart, Gold Star Family and Disabled Veteran plates is issued with no issuance or renewal fee; the Disabled Veteran plate confers accessible parking privileges. Hunting and fishing licenses are steeply reduced — roughly $10.54 for fishing and $9.79 for hunting — for veterans rated 50% or higher and for recovering service members. The Distinguished Veteran Pass gives free lifetime day use, camping and boat use at California State Parks to veterans rated 50%+, wartime veterans meeting income criteria, former POWs and Medal of Honor recipients; given California's park camping fees this is one of the more valuable recreation benefits in the country.
states.cash: California has no wartime service bonus. CalVet does not operate a large general-purpose emergency cash fund; county Veteran Service Offices administer limited emergency assistance and California's County Veterans Service Officer network is state-funded through a subvention program. The most financially significant non-tax program is CalVet Home Loans, a state-run VA-participating mortgage program funded by state bonds that can beat market rates and includes disaster and fire insurance coverage in the payment. There is no state supplement to the VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Eight Veterans Homes of California spanning independent living, assisted living, memory care and skilled nursing — the largest state veterans home system in the nation: Barstow (760-252-6200), Chula Vista (619-482-6010), Fresno (559-493-4400), Lancaster (661-974-8141), Redding (530-224-3300), Ventura (805-659-7502), West Los Angeles (424-832-8200) and Yountville (707-944-4601). Yountville is the oldest and largest veterans home in the United States. California also operates state veterans cemeteries including Northern California Veterans Cemetery (Igo), Yountville, and the Central Coast Veterans Cemetery (Seaside), alongside multiple VA national cemeteries.
