other: CalVet Home Loans — a state bond-funded mortgage program that can undercut market VA loan rates and bundles disaster/fire coverage
Distinguished Veteran Pass: free lifetime state park day use, camping and boat use at 50%+ rating
Largest state veterans home system in the country (eight homes)
College Fee Waiver Plan B has no age limit and no wartime service requirement — the most overlooked education benefit in the state
Property tax exemption interacts with Prop 13: long-tenured owners with low assessed values can be fully exempted
The $20,000 military retirement exclusion sunsets after tax year 2029 unless extended — plan around it
Business license fee exemptions for disabled veteran peddlers/vendors under Business and Professions Code provisions
states.topHack: College Fee Waiver Plan B. Almost everyone assumes the CalVet fee waiver requires a 100% rating or a deceased veteran — that is Plan A. Plan B waives systemwide tuition and fees at every CCC, CSU and UC campus for the child of a veteran with ANY service-connected disability rating, including 0% and 10%, with no age limit and no wartime service requirement. The only real test is the child's own income being below the federal filing threshold, which most full-time students meet. A veteran carrying a 10% tinnitus rating can put a child through a UC campus tuition-free and most never learn the plan exists. Apply through the County Veterans Service Officer, not the campus financial aid office.

states.name: Colorado
states.headline: Solid age-tiered retirement income deductions and excellent recreation benefits, but the property tax exemption caps out at 50% of the first $200,000 of value, which is thin relief in an expensive housing market.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Partially exempt, tiered by age: up to $15,000 for retirees under 55, up to $20,000 for ages 55–64, and up to $24,000 for age 65 and over. The under-55 military retirement subtraction is separate from the general pension/annuity subtraction that applies at 55+.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Generally taxed for residents, with an important exception: service members stationed outside Colorado for 305 days or more in the tax year may file as nonresidents and avoid Colorado tax on military income. Combat zone pay excluded federally is also excluded from Colorado income, with a 180-day filing extension.
incomeTax.notes: Colorado has a flat 4.4% individual rate (subject to TABOR-driven rate reductions in surplus years). SBP, RCSBP and RSFPP annuity recipients may subtract up to $20,000 under 65 and up to $24,000 at 65+. Nonresident military spouse wages earned in Colorado are not taxed where the spouse moved only to accompany the service member. A separate subtraction exists for former residents who reacquire Colorado residency and can demonstrate intent through voter registration, property purchase, vehicle titling or will modification.

states.propertyTax: The Disabled Veteran and Gold Star Spouse Homestead Exemption exempts 50% of the first $200,000 of a primary residence's actual value — a maximum of $100,000 of value removed from the base, not from the tax bill. On a typical Front Range home this is real but modest relief, and it does not scale with home price. Eligibility requires a 100% permanent service-connected disability rating or an Individual Unemployability rating (Colorado added the IU category by statute, which meaningfully expanded the pool), or status as the unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in the line of duty (Gold Star Spouse), or the unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran whose death resulted from a service-connected injury or disease and who receives Dependency and Indemnity Compensation. The applicant must own and occupy the property on January 1 and apply between January 1 and July 1 through the county assessor. There is no sliding scale by rating percentage — below 100%/IU there is no veteran exemption, though the separate senior homestead exemption may apply at 65+. Activated reserve component members called to federal active duty for 30+ days may defer property tax payment.
states.education: The Colorado National Guard Tuition Waiver covers 100% of tuition (not fees or textbooks) through a 50/50 cost share in which the institution waives half and the state reimburses half. Credit hour limits: 65 at two-year institutions, 130 at four-year, 145 combined, plus one certificate; postgraduate limits are 60 credits for a master's, 90 for a doctorate, 150 for a professional degree. Application windows are narrow and easy to miss — June 1–20 for fall, November 1–20 for spring, April 1–20 for summer. Colorado grants in-state tuition rates to nonresident service members, veterans and dependents stationed in Colorado on PCS orders, or where the veteran established Colorado permanent residence before the first day of class. Operation Recognition awards free high school diplomas to Colorado WWII, Korea and Vietnam veterans aged 60+ who left school to serve. Colorado does not offer a broad tuition waiver for veterans themselves or for dependents of disabled veterans, which is a notable gap.
states.employment: State employment preference gives 5 points for honorable discharge from active duty during a declared or undeclared war or when a campaign medal was authorized, and 10 points for a service-connected disability rated 50% or higher with compensation. Professional licensing is handled well: renewal fees are waived for those on active duty 120+ days during a declared war or emergency, military training and education count toward licensure qualifications, licenses can be reinstated after 30+ days of active duty or honorable discharge, and relocated military spouses receive licensure with no fees and six-year validity, renewable while on orders. Gold Star Spouses and dependents of stationed service members may practice regulated professions without fees. The Colorado Department of Labor and Employment provides free one-on-one veteran employment specialists.
states.vehicleRec: Service members stationed outside Colorado get a free three-year driver license extension, and effective January 1, 2027 spouses and dependents become eligible as well. Forty military and veteran plate options are available including Medal of Honor, Purple Heart, Disabled Veteran, Honorably Discharged Veteran and Fallen Soldier; selected plates are exempt from ownership taxes and registration fees. Nonresident service members claim specific ownership tax exemption on Form DR 2667, renewed annually. Recreation is where Colorado shines: veterans rated 50%+ and Purple Heart recipients get a free lifetime combination fishing and small-game hunting license, plus a free annual Independence Parks Pass giving unlimited state park access. The Wounded Warrior program sets aside 100 licenses each for deer, elk and pronghorn (male and female). Deployed service members receive preference points for missed draws and license refunds. Service members may test out of hunter education with a 90%+ score for $34.95. State parks are free to all on Veterans Day, and passport holders 64+ get a $3 camping discount Sunday through Thursday.
states.cash: No wartime service bonus and no broad state-funded emergency cash assistance program for veterans was identified in official sources — a genuine gap. The Colorado Veterans Assistance Grant Program makes grants to nonprofit and county organizations serving veterans rather than direct payments to individuals, so relief generally comes through a County Veterans Service Officer referral rather than a state check. There is no state supplement to the VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Five Veterans Community Living Centers offering skilled nursing, rehabilitation, memory care, respite and hospice: Fitzsimons (Aurora, 720-857-6400), Bruce McCandless (Florence, 719-784-6331), Homelake (Monte Vista, 719-852-5118), Rifle (970-625-0842) and Spanish Peaks (Walsenburg, 719-738-5000). Homelake also includes a domiciliary component. One state cemetery: the Veterans Memorial Cemetery of Western Colorado in Grand Junction, providing free burial for eligible veterans and family members including headstone, grave liner, opening and closing, and perpetual care. Fort Logan National Cemetery in Denver serves the Front Range as a VA facility.
other: Free lifetime combination fishing and small-game hunting license at a 50% rating — a low threshold by national standards
Free annual Independence Parks Pass for 50%+ disabled veterans and Purple Heart recipients
Wounded Warrior big-game license set-aside: 100 licenses each for deer, elk and pronghorn
Tax subtraction available to former Colorado residents who reacquire residency, proven by voter registration, property purchase, vehicle titling or will modification
Individual Unemployability qualifies for the property tax exemption, not just a 100% schedular rating
Military spouse licensure with zero fees and six-year validity
Deployed service members get hunting preference points restored for missed draws

agency.name: Colorado Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA), Division of Veterans Affairs

states.topHack: If you are rated less than 100% schedular but cannot work, pursue Individual Unemployability — Colorado explicitly extends the homestead exemption to IU recipients, and IU also unlocks the same treatment as 100% for most other state benefits. Second, the exemption is portable and is claimed at the county assessor between January 1 and July 1 only; veterans who buy a new home mid-year routinely lose a full year of benefit by not refiling. Third, and almost nobody does this: if you left Colorado and later return, claim the reacquired-residency subtraction by documenting intent (register to vote, title a vehicle, update your will) in the same tax year you move back.

states.name: Connecticut
states.headline: A high-tax state that is quietly excellent for veterans: military retirement is fully exempt, a new mandatory full property tax exemption for 100% P&T veterans hits 2026 tax bills, and there is a real cash bonus plus two emergency relief funds.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Connecticut exempts federally taxable military retired pay from state income tax entirely, with no dollar cap or age condition. Survivor Benefit Plan payments are also exempt.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxed for residents. A resident service member escapes Connecticut tax on military wages only by meeting all three tests: maintaining no permanent Connecticut abode, maintaining a permanent residence outside Connecticut, and spending 30 days or less in Connecticut during the year. Combat zone service brings a 180-day extension to file and pay plus federal-conforming exclusions for base pay, hostile fire pay and bonuses.
incomeTax.notes: Service members killed in combat or from combat injuries are exempt from Connecticut income tax for the year of death, with refunds of tax already paid. Nonresident military spouses sharing a non-Connecticut domicile with the service member are exempt from Connecticut tax on Connecticut-earned wages under MSRRA.

states.propertyTax: Connecticut's structure is municipal and layered, and it just changed materially. The baseline statutory exemptions are small — roughly $1,000 of assessed value for a veteran with 90+ days of wartime service, with larger amounts for disabled veterans and for severely disabled veterans, plus exemptions for the unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran receiving a government pension or compensation and for the surviving spouse or minor child of a service member who died on active duty. Veterans whose income falls below locally set thresholds, or who are rated 100%, may claim up to twice the standard amounts. The significant development: legislation effective for the October 1, 2024 grand list — appearing on tax bills payable in 2026 — requires municipalities to provide a complete property tax exemption for veterans with a total and permanent service-connected disability rating. A qualifying veteran who owns no real property instead receives a complete exemption on one motor vehicle. A veteran taking the new full exemption cannot simultaneously claim the other statutory exemptions. Because municipalities administer and in some cases supplement these amounts at local option, the precise dollar figures vary town to town and must be confirmed with the local assessor.
states.education: The Connecticut Veterans, National Guard Service Members and Dependent Tuition Waiver is the core program: at Connecticut State University campuses it waives 100% of tuition for fall and spring and 50% for summer or intersession; at Connecticut community colleges it waives full or part-time tuition (excluding summer, intersession and extension); at Charter Oak State College it waives 50% of course fees. It does NOT cover books, student activity fees, course fees, parking, or room and board — the waiver is tuition-only and students still face meaningful out-of-pocket costs. Eligibility requires Connecticut residency, honorable discharge or release under honorable conditions, and 90+ days of active duty during a recognized wartime period (waived if discharged earlier for a service-connected disability or if the conflict lasted under 90 days), or current Connecticut National Guard membership. Dependents qualify in narrow circumstances: children or the surviving spouse of a service member killed in action on or after September 11, 2001, and children of a service member declared MIA or POW after January 1, 1960. High school diplomas are awarded to WWII, Korea and Vietnam veterans who left school to serve.
states.employment: State hiring preference gives 10 points to disabled veterans eligible for or receiving VA compensation who served during a recognized wartime period, to spouses of disabled veterans unable to work, and to surviving spouses of veterans who would have qualified for 10-point preference; 5 points go to honorably discharged wartime veterans not receiving VA compensation or pension. State employees in reserve components receive 30 days per year of paid military leave, and a state employee honorably discharged who reapplies within 90 days must be reinstated to the former position. The standout item is procurement: a certified veteran-owned micro business (51%+ veteran-owned, under $3 million in revenue) receives a 15% price preference when the state determines the lowest bid — one of the most aggressive set-aside mechanisms in the country. Certification: 860-616-3685; state contract bidding: 860-713-5095.
states.vehicleRec: A veteran flag identifier appears on driver licenses and ID cards for those with 90+ days of service and an honorable discharge or a discharge for service-connected injury. Sixteen distinctive plates are available, including Purple Heart, Disabled American Veterans, Gold Star Family (free), and Military Veteran plates in a choice of ten wartime period designs (WWII, Korea, Vietnam, Lebanon, Grenada, Panama, Persian Gulf, Operation Earnest Will, Afghanistan, Iraq). Medal of Honor and former POW recipients and their unremarried surviving spouses receive two free plates and special registration certificates for life or until remarriage. Connecticut residents who entered military service have registration fees waived, including new and renewal registration, temporary plates, safety plates and clean air act fees; Guard and Reserve members on federal active duty also qualify. Nonresident service members pay a reduced 4.5% sales tax rate on motor vehicle purchases and leases. Connecticut honors the CDL skills test exemption for active duty, recently separated (within one year) and reserve component members licensed on military vehicles, and waives the motorcycle endorsement exam for members stationed out of state who complete an MSF course. Hunting and fishing: nonresident active duty stationed in Connecticut pay resident prices; persons who have lost a limb or the use of a limb get free inland fishing and small game hunting licenses with physician certification. Disabled resident veterans with service-connected disabilities receive a free Connecticut State Park Lifetime Disabled Veteran Pass.
states.cash: Connecticut is one of the few states in this group with real cash programs. The Connecticut Wartime Service Bonus pays $50 for every month of active duty, up to $500 for non-combat service and up to $1,200 for service in a combat zone, to current and former Connecticut National Guard members with 90+ consecutive days of active duty on or after September 11, 2001 in support of military operations, with honorable discharge or discharge for service-connected disability; applications must be filed within three years of the end of the military operation. The Connecticut Military Relief Fund makes grants up to $5,000 per case to service members and families in financial hardship arising from military service, serious injury, illness or death. The Connecticut Soldiers, Sailors and Marines Fund (SSMF), administered by the American Legion, is an unusually broad and long-standing state-chartered fund providing temporary assistance for weekly financial needs, rent or mortgage interest, utilities, medical and emergency dental expenses, eye exams and eyeglasses, hearing evaluations and hearing aids, funeral expenses and durable medical equipment, to Connecticut resident veterans with 90+ days of wartime active duty who demonstrate financial need.
states.homesHealth: Connecticut consolidates its facilities on the Rocky Hill campus. The Sgt. John L. Levitow Healthcare Center is a skilled nursing facility for veterans with acute and chronic conditions including cancer, cardiac disease, COPD, dementia, stroke, diabetes, Parkinson's and MS, with palliative and respite care (admissions 860-616-3708). The Connecticut Veteran Residential Facility at Rocky Hill provides rehabilitation and community living with individualized plans, employment and education resources, social work, case management and recovery support (860-616-3802). Patriots Landing offers temporary housing for homeless or at-risk veterans, spouses and children in five furnished single-family homes with supportive services. All require 90+ days active duty excluding training, honorable or general under honorable conditions discharge, and Connecticut residency at application or at entry into service. Cemeteries: the Connecticut Middletown State Veterans Cemetery provides burial plot, opening and closing, government headstone with placement, and perpetual care at no cost (860-616-3688); the Colonel Raymond F. Gates Memorial Cemetery at Rocky Hill is reserved for residents of the Connecticut veterans residential program.
other: 15% price preference for certified veteran-owned micro businesses on state contracts — among the strongest procurement preferences in the nation
Connecticut Wartime Service Bonus: up to $1,200 for combat zone service, $500 otherwise
Soldiers, Sailors and Marines Fund covers hearing aids, eyeglasses, dental and funeral expenses — categories almost no other state fund touches
Connecticut Wartime Service Medal awarded to residents with 90+ days of wartime active duty, including posthumously
Supervised Diversionary Program lets veterans with qualifying mental health conditions avoid prosecution for minor offenses, with charges dismissed on completion
Connecticut Military Support Program provides confidential behavioral health care through embedded clinicians, outside the VA system
Registration fee waiver covers new and renewal registration, temporary plates, safety plates and clean air fees
New mandatory municipal full exemption for 100% P&T veterans first appears on 2026 tax bills

agency.name: Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Advocacy and Assistance

states.topHack: Two moves. First, if you are rated 100% permanent and total, go to your town assessor now and claim the new mandatory complete property tax exemption that first applies to the October 1, 2024 grand list and therefore to your 2026 bill — it is new enough that many assessors are still processing it by exception, and you must affirmatively elect it instead of the older statutory exemptions you may already be receiving. If you rent rather than own, the same statute gives you a complete exemption on one motor vehicle instead, which nearly nobody claims. Second, the Soldiers, Sailors and Marines Fund is a genuinely unusual resource: it is not means-tested against VA benefits, it is administered by the American Legion rather than the state bureaucracy, and it pays for hearing aids, eyeglasses and dental work that VA priority groups often will not cover.

states.name: Delaware
states.headline: The 100% school property tax credit is worth more than it sounds because school levies dominate Delaware property tax bills, and there is no sales tax — but military retirement gets only a $12,500 exclusion.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Partially exempt. Delaware residents may exclude up to $12,500 of military retirement income annually. This is the same general pension exclusion Delaware applies at age 60+, applied to military retirees without the age gate.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxed. Delaware resident service members pay state income tax on military compensation.
incomeTax.notes: Military disability retirement pay resulting from active service injury or illness is excluded. Residents aged 60+ receiving SBP, RCSBP or RSFPP annuities may exclude up to $12,500; those under 60 are limited to a $2,000 exclusion. Delaware has no state or local sales tax, which materially offsets the modest income tax treatment for retirees who spend rather than save.

states.propertyTax: Delaware's Disabled Veterans School Tax Credit gives a credit equal to 100% of school district property tax on the primary residence. This is more valuable than its narrow name suggests: school district levies make up the large majority of a Delaware property tax bill, so the credit typically eliminates most of the total. Eligibility requires three or more years of Delaware residency, and a VA rating of 100% total and permanent disability or 100% via Individual Unemployability. The application deadline is April 30, and once approved no reapplication is needed — a genuinely low-friction program compared with states requiring annual recertification. Applications go to the county assessment offices: New Castle County 302-395-5520, Kent County 302-744-2401, Sussex County 302-855-7871. There is no sliding scale below 100%/IU, no separate Purple Heart or POW exemption identified, and the county and municipal portions of the bill are not covered. Delaware's overall effective property tax rate is among the lowest in the nation, so the absolute dollars at stake are smaller than in Illinois or Connecticut.
states.education: Delaware's dependent program covers children of veterans killed in service, who died of service-related causes, or declared POW/MIA: it pays tuition and fees for up to four years at state institutions (with exceptions permitted where the program is unavailable in-state), for children aged 16–24 with three or more years of Delaware residency. Delaware National Guard Tuition Assistance covers up to 100% of tuition at state colleges, or the average in-state private tuition rate, for one certificate, one associate degree and one bachelor's degree, with master's funding available if undergraduate funding is exhausted; it requires a six-year service commitment within a 15-year eligibility window (Education Office 302-326-7012). High school diplomas are awarded to veterans who left school for WWII, Korea or Vietnam service with honorable discharge. Delaware does not offer a broad tuition waiver for veterans themselves — a significant gap relative to Connecticut, Illinois or Florida.
states.employment: State hiring preference adds 5 points to civil service exam scores for veterans and 10 points for disabled veterans; unremarried spouses of deceased veterans and spouses of disabled, POW or MIA service members also qualify. Professional licensing offers provisional licenses valid up to six months for service members and spouses, keeps deployed members' licenses active during deployment, and credits military education, training and experience (METE) toward licensure requirements. State employees receive 112.5–120 hours of paid annual leave for training or active duty, and — unusually — the state supplements military base pay if it falls below the employee's state salary. State employees hired before July 1, 1976 may credit up to five years of military service toward retirement. The 'Heroes on the Highway' CDL skills test waiver covers service members with two or more years of military vehicle experience.
states.vehicleRec: The veteran indicator on a Delaware license or ID is free for honorably discharged veterans. Thirty-seven military and veteran plate designs are available: Purple Heart $10, Disabled American Veteran $10, Honorably Discharged Military Veteran $15, and Gold Star Family free. Disabled veterans with VA-funded specially adapted vehicles receive a registration fee exemption on one automobile. Active duty members and dependents stationed outside Delaware may renew licenses by mail with no late fees, and service members relocating to Delaware receive title fee waivers for out-of-state registration within 90 days. Hunting and fishing is broad: veterans rated 60% or higher receive a free exemption covering hunting, trapping and fishing; nonresident active duty pay resident prices; wartime veterans of Operations Iraqi Freedom and Enduring Freedom with 90+ days receive a one-year free exemption post-discharge; hospitalized service members and VA-hospitalized veterans receive free licenses. State parks give resident service members, veterans and retirees 50% off annual passes, and OIF/OEF veterans with 90+ days receive free passes for 12 months after discharge.
states.cash: Delaware has two genuine cash programs. The Paraplegic Veterans Pension pays $3,000 annually to paraplegic veterans rated totally disabled by the VA with an honorable discharge and a wartime service-connected disability — a rare example of a true state supplement to VA compensation. The Delaware Veterans Trust Fund provides emergency financial assistance for rent, utilities, medical bills, childcare and vehicle payments, with payments made directly to vendors rather than to the veteran. For the National Guard, a line of duty death on state active duty triggers a $200,000 benefit paid at $40,000 annually, plus four years of college tuition for surviving children and health insurance to age 26. There is no general wartime service bonus.
states.homesHealth: The Delaware Veterans Home in Milford is a 144-bed skilled nursing facility with 24-hour professional care, therapies, medical services and chaplaincy (302-424-8572, DOSDVH_admissions@delaware.gov). Eligibility requires an honorable discharge with 180+ days of active duty (181+ for Guard and Reserve), a need for skilled nursing care, and one or more years of Delaware residency; surviving spouses and parents of service-connected deaths are also eligible. Two Delaware Veterans Memorial Cemeteries accept casketed and cremated remains: New Castle County (302-834-8046) and Sussex County (302-934-5653), with eligibility mirroring VA national cemeteries plus a Delaware residency requirement (at death, three or more cumulative years, or at entry to service).
other: No state or local sales tax anywhere in Delaware — a permanent, uncapped benefit that dwarfs most veteran-specific tax breaks
Free notary services: Delaware notaries may not charge a fee for notarizing veterans' military benefit documentation
Honorably discharged veterans are exempt from auctioneer and book agent occupational licenses entirely
Paraplegic Veterans Pension: $3,000 per year, a true state supplement to VA compensation
One free certified death certificate to the veteran's next of kin for VA benefit claims
Free access to military records maintained by the Delaware Office of Veterans Services
Delaware Veterans Treatment Court diverts veterans from prosecution with charges dismissed on completion of a treatment plan
State supplements military base pay for state employees when military pay falls below their state salary
states.topHack: File for the Disabled Veterans School Tax Credit the moment you hit three years of Delaware residency and hold a 100% P&T or IU rating — and note that Individual Unemployability qualifies, which catches out veterans rated 70% schedular who assume they are ineligible. The deadline is a hard April 30, and unlike most states there is no annual recertification once approved, so a single filing produces a permanent credit against the school portion of your bill for as long as you own the home. The secondary move most people miss: if you were hospitalized at a VA facility, or served 90+ days in OIF/OEF, you qualify for free hunting, fishing and trapping licenses and a free state park pass — benefits keyed to service history rather than disability rating.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.headline: The District fully taxes both active duty pay and military retirement — the worst income tax treatment in this group — and offers no tuition waiver for veterans, though the $445,000 homestead deduction for 100% disabled veterans is large in a very expensive housing market.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully taxed. The District provides no reduction in taxes on military retired pay — it is one of very few jurisdictions in the country offering no military retirement exclusion whatsoever.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully taxed. DC residents pay District income tax on military compensation. Service members deployed to a combat zone receive a 180-day extension to file and pay after returning.
incomeTax.notes: Disability retirement pay for service-related injuries is not taxable, and VA disability compensation and DIC are tax-free. Survivor Benefit Plan annuities are excluded from DC gross income for survivors aged 62 and over. DC's top marginal rate approaches 10.75%, so the absence of a military retirement exclusion is expensive in absolute terms.

states.propertyTax: The Disabled Veterans Homestead Deduction reduces assessed value by up to $445,000 for qualifying veterans. Eligibility requires a VA rating of 100% service-connected disabled or Individual Unemployability paid at the 100% rate, DC residency, ownership of at least 50% of the property, a federal adjusted gross income below approximately $159,750, and use as the primary residence in a building with no more than five dwelling units. In a market where the median home price is high, $445,000 of exempt assessed value is genuinely substantial — often the difference between a four-figure and a near-zero bill — and it stacks on top of the standard DC homestead deduction. The income cap is indexed and should be confirmed for the 2026 tax year. Applications are handled through the Mayor's Office of Veterans Affairs (202-724-5454) and the Office of Tax and Revenue. There is no sliding scale for ratings below 100%/IU, and no separate Purple Heart or POW exemption was identified.
states.education: This is the District's weakest category. There is no tuition waiver or free-tuition program for veterans or their dependents at the University of the District of Columbia or elsewhere. The only substantial education benefit is the Major General David F. Wherley Jr. District of Columbia National Guard Retention and College Access Program (DCTA), which covers tuition not covered by Federal Tuition Assistance at up to $20,000 per fiscal year plus up to $500 for authorized fees, with no semester caps, paid directly to accredited institutions; it covers associate, bachelor's, master's or professional degrees, limited to one degree per level. This is a generous Guard program but it does nothing for veterans who are no longer serving. The DC Tuition Assistance Grant (DCTAG), which pays the difference between in-state and out-of-state tuition at public institutions nationwide, is available to DC residents generally and is not veteran-specific, but veterans establishing DC residency should be aware of it. DC participates in MIC3 for military children.
states.employment: DC government hiring preference adds 5 points for an honorable or general discharge with 180+ days of active duty during a time of war (limited to five years post-discharge), and 10 points for a service-connected disability rating of 30% or higher or receipt of VA disability compensation or pension. The Call for Hire Program is a non-competitive hiring pathway for eligible veterans and spouses into time-limited Career Service positions at grade 12 and below with potential conversion to permanent status, requiring DC residency and 180+ consecutive days of service. The CDL military skills test waiver is honored. The Department of Employment Services provides priority of service through American Job Centers. Federal 5- and 10-point preference is separately available and is disproportionately relevant here given the federal employer concentration.
states.vehicleRec: A 'Veteran' designation is available on DC driver licenses and ID cards with a DD214 or equivalent. The Veteran license plate is available to active duty, retired members, veterans with honorable or general discharge, spouses and surviving spouses. Disabled veterans with a total and permanent service-connected disability rating receive one set of tags with no annual registration fee; the Disabled American Veteran plate requires DAV membership. Recreation benefits are thin given the District's size — fishing licenses are not required for persons under 16 or 65 and over, but there is no veteran-specific fishing exemption, no state park system and no hunting. The most valuable recreation-adjacent benefit is transit: veterans rated 60% or higher receive 50% off Metrorail and Metrobus fares and regional bus passes through WMATA.
states.cash: No direct cash bonus, wartime service bonus, or state-funded emergency financial assistance program for veterans was identified in official District sources. There is no supplement to the VA pension. The closest analogue is VetsRide, an in-kind transportation benefit rather than a cash payment.
states.homesHealth: The District does not operate its own state veterans home or state veterans cemetery. The Armed Forces Retirement Home (AFRH) Washington is a federal facility located in the District offering independent living with assisted living and long-term nursing care options, plus a nine-hole golf course, fitness center, art studio, fishing ponds and shuttle service to military and VA facilities; eligibility requires honorable service with less than 50% officer service and either 20+ years active duty, a service-connected disability, war theater service, or VA retirement eligibility (800-422-9988, admissions@afrh.gov). One VA national cemetery operates in the District. Veterans needing state-home-style long-term care generally look to Virginia or Maryland facilities.
other: VetsRide: free transportation for DC veteran residents with income under $45,000 or recently unemployed, to medical appointments, education, employment, housing, food distribution and pharmacies, 6 a.m.–10 p.m. seven days a week (schedule at 202-398-0500)
50% off WMATA Metrorail and Metrobus fares for veterans rated 60% or higher
$445,000 homestead deduction is the largest single-property deduction figure of any jurisdiction in this group
DCTA National Guard program pays up to $20,000 per fiscal year with no semester cap — unusually generous for Guard tuition
DC Tuition Assistance Grant (not veteran-specific) can pay the in-state/out-of-state tuition gap at public universities nationwide for DC residents
No state veterans home and no state veterans cemetery — an atypical gap

agency.name: Mayor's Office of Veterans Affairs (MOVA), District of Columbia

states.topHack: If you hold a 100% or Individual Unemployability rating and your household AGI is under roughly $159,750, the $445,000 Disabled Veterans Homestead Deduction is by far the most money on the table anywhere in the District — and it stacks on the ordinary homestead deduction rather than replacing it. Because DC assesses at full market value with no Proposition-13-style cap, that deduction tracks your real home value and can reduce a five-figure annual bill to near zero. Apply through MOVA rather than trying to navigate the Office of Tax and Revenue alone. The honest counsel, though: if you are a military retiree with a choice of domicile, the District taxes your entire pension at rates approaching 10.75% while Virginia and Maryland both now offer substantial military retirement subtractions — the property tax deduction rarely offsets that.

states.name: Florida
states.headline: No income tax at all, a full homestead exemption at 100% P&T, an age-65 combat-disability discount that scales with your rating, and 20-point hiring preference — Florida is close to the national ceiling for veteran financial benefits.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Not taxed — Florida has no individual income tax. Military retired pay, Survivor Benefit Plan annuities and TSP distributions are all free of state tax.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Not taxed. No state income tax applies to active duty, Guard or Reserve pay.
incomeTax.notes: Florida's constitution prohibits a personal income tax, which makes this a stable rather than legislatively contingent benefit. There is no estate or inheritance tax either. VA disability compensation is untaxed for the same reason everything else is.

states.propertyTax: Florida runs the most complete layered system in this group. A veteran with a combat-related disability rating of 10% or more gets $5,000 removed from assessed value. A veteran with a service-connected total and permanent disability — or one confined to a wheelchair with VA-granted specially adapted housing — receives a full exemption from homestead property tax. The distinctive middle tier: a veteran aged 65 or older with a combat-related disability receives a discount on the homestead's assessed value equal to their disability rating percentage, so a 70%-rated 66-year-old gets 70% off the bill even without P&T status. This percentage discount is the benefit most veterans do not know exists. Unremarried surviving spouses of service members killed on active duty receive the full exemption; if the spouse remarries or sells, they retain only the amount previously received. Crucially, Florida allows portability — a surviving spouse who sells may carry the exemption to the next property up to the amount received on the prior one. Separately, service members deployed outside the United States during the prior calendar year receive an exemption percentage equal to the share of the year they were deployed. All of this sits on top of Florida's standard homestead exemption and Save Our Homes 3% assessment cap.
states.education: The Congressman C.W. Bill Young Veteran Tuition Waiver waives out-of-state fees for honorably discharged veterans at Florida state universities, Florida College System institutions and technical centers, provided the veteran physically resides in Florida while enrolled — effectively converting nonresident tuition to resident tuition from day one. The Scholarships for Children and Spouses of Deceased or Disabled Veterans (CSDDV) covers tuition and registration fees up to 110% of the required credit hours for an initial bachelor's degree or certificate, for dependents of deceased service members, veterans rated 100%, POWs and MIAs. A Purple Heart Tuition Waiver covers degree or certificate programs up to 110% of required hours for Purple Heart recipients and recipients of superior combat decorations. Surviving spouses and children of service members killed in the line of duty receive a waiver of tuition, matriculation and registration fees for a total of 120 credit hours. The Honorably Discharged Graduate Assistance Program (HDGAP) pays up to $50 per day for a maximum of 20 days per academic year toward living expenses during academic breaks. Educational Dollars for Duty (EDD) covers 100% of resident tuition for Florida National Guard members, capped at $218.71 per undergraduate credit and $265.35 per graduate credit, with book reimbursement available.
states.employment: Florida operates absolute-style veterans' preference with unusually high point values: 20 points for a veteran rated 30% or more disabled, 20 points for the surviving spouse of a veteran rated 100% disabled, 15 points for an unremarried surviving spouse of a deceased veteran, 15 points for a wartime veteran with honorable discharge, and 10 points for an active reserve component member. State employees required to serve receive reemployment to the same or an equal position within one year of discharge. Professional licensing offers fee waivers, reciprocity recognition, expedited processing and military training credit across healthcare, engineering, law enforcement and education. The Veterans to Teachers program waives application and exam fees, provides temporary certification allowing teaching while completing requirements, and pays a $4,000 sign-on bonus (plus $1,000 for high-demand subjects) to veterans employed after July 1, 2023 who commit to two years. Certified Veteran Business Enterprise status (51% veteran-owned, under $5 million net worth, 200 or fewer employees) confers preference in competitive state bidding. The CDL skills test waiver applies to those with two or more years of licensed military experience on similar vehicles.
states.vehicleRec: The veteran designation on a Florida driver license or ID is free for honorably discharged veterans, and veterans rated 100% disabled receive a free driver license or ID card outright. Homeless veterans and their families receive free Florida ID cards. Forty-five specialized plate designs are available, including Medal of Honor, Purple Heart, Disabled Veteran (with or without wheelchair symbol), Gold Star, standard Veteran and Florida National Guard. A free Disabled Toll Permit allows severely disabled veterans with specially adapted vehicles to pass tollgates at no charge — a meaningful benefit on Florida's heavily tolled expressway network. Service members stationed outside Florida may extend Class E licenses with a free military extension card valid 90 days after discharge. On hunting, fishing and state parks the DoD benefits summary did not enumerate specifics; Florida is widely reported to offer a discounted Military Gold Sportsman's License to resident active duty and to resident veterans rated 30% or higher, free licenses to residents rated 100%, and free or discounted state park entry for disabled veterans and Purple Heart recipients, but these figures were NOT verified against the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission or the Department of Environmental Protection and should be confirmed before publication.
states.cash: Florida has no general wartime service bonus and no broad emergency cash assistance fund for veterans. It does pay substantial death benefits: $75,000 to beneficiaries of service members killed in the line of duty, and $75,000 to families of Florida National Guard members killed or dying from injuries sustained on state active duty. HDGAP provides up to $50 per day for 20 days per academic year in living-expense assistance to student veterans. Florida National Guard State Sponsored Life Insurance provides $1,000 of no-cost coverage plus optional coverage from $10,000 to $250,000 with no military specialty, combat or war exclusions.
states.homesHealth: The Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs operates a network of state veterans homes comprising skilled nursing facilities plus at least one assisted living facility, distributed across the state from the Panhandle to South Florida; the exact current count and locations were NOT verified in this research because the DoD benefits page does not enumerate them, and FDVA has been actively opening new homes, so the number should be confirmed directly with FDVA before publication. Florida also does not operate a separate state veterans cemetery system comparable to Texas or California — the state relies primarily on the extensive VA national cemetery network within Florida, including Florida National Cemetery at Bushnell, Jacksonville, Bay Pines, Cape Canaveral, Sarasota and South Florida national cemeteries. Verify state cemetery status with FDVA.
other: Exemption from local business taxes and fees for veterans, spouses of veterans, and military spouses stationed in Florida
Free Disabled Toll Permit for severely disabled veterans with specially adapted vehicles
Age 65+ combat-disabled homestead discount scales with rating percentage — you do not need P&T status
Free driver license or ID card for veterans rated 100% disabled; free ID cards for homeless veterans
Homestead exemption portability for surviving spouses who sell and buy again
20-point hiring preference for 30%+ disabled veterans — the highest point value in this group of states
Veterans to Teachers $4,000 sign-on bonus plus $1,000 for high-demand subjects
Deployed service member exemption prorated to the share of the year spent deployed outside the U.S.
Purple Star Schools and Collegiate Purple Star Campuses, with a district designation at 75% of schools
states.topHack: Turn 65 with a combat-related disability and file for the age-65 percentage discount. Almost every Florida veteran knows about the $5,000 exemption and the full P&T exemption, but the middle tier — a homestead assessed-value discount equal to your disability rating percentage, available at 65+ for combat-related disabilities — is the one that goes unclaimed. A 60%- or 70%-rated veteran who will never reach P&T can still knock 60–70% off the homestead tax bill for life starting at 65. It must be applied for at the county property appraiser with proof the disability is combat-related, and it is not applied automatically when you age in. Second hack: the C.W. Bill Young waiver kills out-of-state tuition the moment you physically reside in Florida while enrolled — no 12-month residency wait.

states.name: Georgia
states.headline: A large and inflation-indexed disabled veteran homestead exemption plus generous retirement income exclusions after 62, but military retirees under 62 get relatively little and veteran education benefits are thin.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Partially exempt, tiered by age: under 62, up to $17,500, plus an additional $17,500 if the retiree has earned income of at least $17,500 (so up to $35,000 for a working retiree); ages 62–64, up to $35,000; age 65 and over, up to $65,000. These are the general retirement income exclusions applied to military pensions, with the under-62 tier added specifically for military retirees.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxed. Georgia residents pay state income tax on military pay. Combat zone pay excluded federally is excluded from Georgia income, and those serving outside the continental U.S. receive a six-month filing extension; combat zone deployment extends the deadline 180 days after the deployment ends.
incomeTax.notes: Georgia is transitioning to a flat individual rate in the low 5% range with scheduled reductions, which moderates the value of the exclusions. Service members killed in a combat zone receive complete income tax forgiveness including for all prior tax years back to the start of the deployment. Nonresident military spouses stationed in Georgia on orders are exempt.

states.propertyTax: Georgia's disabled veteran homestead exemption is set at $126,526 of assessed value for 2026 and is indexed annually — it rises each year with a federal index, which is why third-party sources quoting $109,986 or $100,896 are stale. Eligibility requires Georgia residency, an honorable discharge, and a VA rating of 100% service-connected disabled, Individual Unemployability paid at the 100% rate, or specific qualifying disabilities involving loss of limb or loss of sight. Unremarried surviving spouses and minor children are also eligible. A separate exemption for the unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in a war or armed conflict was set at $121,812 for 2025 and is similarly indexed. Because Georgia assesses property at 40% of fair market value, $126,526 of exempt assessed value corresponds to roughly $316,000 of fair market value — which fully exempts the great majority of Georgia homes. That makes this one of the strongest property tax benefits in the Southeast, though it is all-or-nothing at 100%/IU with no sliding scale below that. Eligible disabled veterans are also exempt from ad valorem tax on one vehicle regardless of plate type.
states.education: Georgia is comparatively weak here. The Georgia HERO Scholarship pays up to $2,000 per year to a maximum of $8,000 over four academic years, for Georgia National Guard and U.S. Reserve members deployed to a combat zone for 181 or more days, and for children and surviving spouses of deployed or deceased members (Georgia Student Finance Authority, 770-724-9249 or 800-505-4732). Combat veterans deployed after September 11, 2001 for 181 or more cumulative days, or with a full combat-related disability, receive a complete waiver of mandatory fees in the University System of Georgia — valuable but narrower than a tuition waiver. Nonresident active duty members, service members separated within 36 months, and their dependents receive in-state tuition rates. Full tuition and mandatory fee refunds are provided when a reserve or active duty member is reassigned mid-term. There is no broad tuition waiver for veterans generally or for dependents of disabled veterans, which is the main thing separating Georgia from Alabama, Florida and Illinois. High school diplomas are issued to WWII, Korea and Vietnam era veterans who left school to serve.
states.employment: State hiring preference adds 5 to 10 points depending on service and disability status, with 10 points for a rating of 10% or greater; spouses of disabled veterans are also eligible. Private employers may adopt written veteran hiring preference policies. The standout item is the Disabled Veteran Business Certificate: a veteran rated 10% or higher receives a ten-year exemption from local occupational taxes and business license fees — a long, genuinely valuable exemption for a small business owner, and far more generous in duration than comparable programs elsewhere. Georgia VECTR (Veterans Education Career Transition Resource Center, 833-448-3287) is a one-stop center providing career counseling, education financing guidance, employment services, credential testing and entrepreneurial training. USERRA protections apply with health coverage continuance up to 24 months.
states.vehicleRec: Georgia is unusually good on licensing fees. The veteran designation on a driver license is free; an honorary spouse driver license is free where the veteran cannot drive; and a Georgia National Guard driver license is free. Active duty members out of state get a six-month grace period on an expired license and may renew by mail. The first set of Disabled Veteran (100% rating), Purple Heart, Medal of Honor, general Army Veteran and Gold Star Family plates is free. Hunting and fishing: a one-time free annual veteran license valid one year for those with 90+ days of active duty after July 1, 2005; a Lifetime Sportsman's License at $603 for active service members and veterans; and disability licenses at roughly $6–18 per year for veterans rated 100%. State parks give disabled veterans a 25% discount on accommodations, fees, golf and historic site admission. A quirky but real benefit: a disabled veteran displaying disabled veteran plates may request full-service at a self-service fuel price.
states.cash: Georgia has no wartime service bonus and no broad state-funded emergency cash assistance fund for veterans identified in official sources — a real gap in an otherwise reasonable package. There is no state supplement to the VA pension. Assistance in a crisis generally routes through county service officers to federal programs and to private organizations rather than to a state fund.
states.homesHealth: Two Georgia War Veterans Nursing Homes: Augusta (130 beds, 706-721-2405) and Milledgeville (248 beds, 478-445-4295). Eligibility requires Georgia residency (two consecutive years, or five of the last fifteen), wartime service from WWII through the Persian Gulf, an other-than-dishonorable discharge, and VA approval for skilled nursing care. Two Georgia Veterans Memorial Cemeteries: Milledgeville (478-445-3363) and Glennville (912-654-5398), with no charge for gravesite or government marker, handling casketed burials, cremation and columbarium placement. Georgia also has a Women Veterans Office providing specialized support including military sexual trauma counseling and advocacy, and operates Veterans Treatment Courts combining drug court and mental health court approaches.
other: Ten-year exemption from local occupational taxes and business license fees for veterans rated 10% or higher — unusually long duration
Free vital records: marriage, divorce, birth and death certificates provided at no charge to veterans and families for benefits claims
Free honorary spouse driver license where the veteran is unable to drive
Disabled veterans may request full-service fuel at self-service prices when displaying disabled veteran plates
Homestead exemption is indexed annually — $126,526 for 2026, so third-party figures under $120,000 are out of date
Ad valorem tax exemption on one vehicle for eligible disabled veterans, regardless of plate type
Georgia VECTR Center — a dedicated statewide transition campus, not just a website
Dedicated Women Veterans Office with MST counseling and advocacy
states.topHack: If you own a small business and carry any rating of 10% or higher, get the Disabled Veteran Business Certificate from GDVS — it exempts you from local occupational taxes and business license fees for ten years, and the 10% threshold means an enormous number of Georgia veterans qualify while almost none apply. For homeowners, the key insight is that Georgia assesses at 40% of fair market value, so the $126,526 assessed-value exemption shelters roughly $316,000 of market value and fully zeroes out the county portion for most homes — but it is granted only on application to the county tax commissioner and is never applied automatically when your rating reaches 100% or IU. Finally, if you are approaching 62, note that Georgia's retirement exclusion jumps from $17,500 to $35,000 at 62 and to $65,000 at 65; timing a Roth conversion or a large distribution around those birthdays is worth real money.

states.name: Hawaii
states.headline: Military retirement is fully exempt and county property tax exemptions for totally disabled veterans can eliminate the bill entirely, but active duty pay is taxed, there is no veteran tuition waiver, and the cost of living erodes every benefit.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Hawaii does not tax military retired pay, and also exempts Survivor Benefit Plan payments and National Guard and Reserve drill pay.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxed. Active duty pay is included in federal adjusted gross income and is therefore taxable under Hawaii law for residents. Reserve component members may exclude a set amount of drill pay — $8,082 for the 2024 tax year, indexed annually; the 2026 figure was not verified.
incomeTax.notes: Hawaii's top marginal rate is among the highest in the nation, so the full retirement exemption is valuable in absolute terms. Hawaii does not tax Social Security benefits. TSP distributions ARE subject to Hawaii tax despite the absence of state withholding — a trap that catches retirees who assume TSP is treated like the pension. VA disability retirement pay and DIC are exempt. Nonresident military spouses stationed in Hawaii may claim exemption on earnings under MSRRA.

states.propertyTax: Hawaii has no statewide veteran property tax exemption — real property taxation is entirely a county function, and each of the four counties (Honolulu, Hawai'i, Maui, Kaua'i) sets its own eligibility rules, exemption amounts and application processes for totally disabled veterans and their unremarried surviving spouses. In practice the counties are generous to veterans with a total service-connected disability, several reducing the bill to a nominal statutory minimum rather than a percentage or dollar exemption, but the specific 2026 amounts, minimum-tax floors and income conditions vary by county and were NOT verified in this research. A veteran must contact the relevant county real property assessment division directly — Honolulu, Hawai'i County, Maui County or Kaua'i County — rather than relying on any statewide figure. There is no state-level sliding scale by rating percentage and no separate statewide Purple Heart or POW exemption.
states.education: Hawaii is thin here. There is no tuition waiver for veterans and no dependent tuition program comparable to mainland states. The Hawaii National Guard State Tuition Assistance Program (STAP) reimburses up to 100% of tuition at community colleges and 50% at public universities, requiring Hawaii residency, satisfactory Guard performance, rank of O-3 or below, and enrollment in a degree program. In-state tuition rates are granted to nonresident active duty members, Hawaii National Guard members, Reserve members based in Hawaii, and veterans using VA education benefits at University of Hawai'i System campuses — which matters given the size of the resident/nonresident tuition gap. Hawaii participates in MIC3 for military children. The absence of a veteran or dependent tuition waiver is the single biggest gap in the state's package.
states.employment: Hawaii relies largely on federal preference rather than a distinctive state scheme — federal 5- and 10-point preference applies based on service era and disability rating, including for Purple Heart recipients. State employees receive 15 days of paid military leave annually and up to 26 weeks of unpaid military caregiver leave. USERRA protections apply with the standard five-year cumulative absence limit, reemployment at equivalent position and seniority, and required reasonable accommodation for service-connected disabilities. Hawaii American Job Centers provide priority job referrals, skills assessment, resume assistance and employer recruitment events for veterans. Licensing accommodations for military spouses exist but are less developed than in Arizona, Colorado or Kansas.
states.vehicleRec: Veterans rated 100% disabled receive a motor vehicle registration fee exemption of $46 on one vehicle, and an exemption from the vehicle weight tax on one vehicle; nonresident active duty members and Hawaii resident service members also receive the weight tax exemption on one vehicle. Ten distinctive plate designs are available: Veteran, Combat Veteran, Purple Heart, Pearl Harbor Survivor, former POW, WWII, Korean, Vietnam and Persian Gulf Veteran, and Gold Star Family. The 'Veteran' notation is available on driver licenses and state ID cards for honorably discharged veterans. Nonresident active duty members and dependents may purchase hunting licenses at resident rates. Hawaii's recreation benefits are notably less developed than mainland states — there is no free state park pass program for disabled veterans comparable to California's Distinguished Veteran Pass or Idaho's lifetime pass, and freshwater fishing opportunities are limited.
states.cash: No statewide bonus program, no wartime service bonus and no dedicated state-funded emergency cash assistance fund for veterans was identified in official sources. Hawaii's benefits are structured almost entirely as exemptions, reduced fees and in-kind services rather than monetary grants. There is no state supplement to the VA pension.
states.homesHealth: The Yukio Okutsu State Veterans Home in Hilo is a 95-bed skilled nursing facility providing nursing care, rehabilitation, hospice, geriatric mental health, Alzheimer's and dementia care, adult day care and respite care. Eligibility requires age 55 or older, honorable discharge, Hawaii residency (before entering service or for one year prior to application), and ability to pay the resident cost share; admission is prioritized by disability severity, earning capacity, length of service, combat experience and family circumstances. Note this is the state's only veterans home and it is on the Big Island, which is a real access problem for the roughly two-thirds of Hawaii's veteran population living on O'ahu. Cemeteries: the Hawaii State Veterans Cemetery in Kaneohe plus seven county-operated veterans cemeteries provide gravesite, marker, liner, perpetual care and grave opening and closing; the National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific (Punchbowl) in Honolulu is a VA facility. Funeral honors are available through the Hawaii National Guard.
other: Full income tax exemption covers National Guard and Reserve drill pay, not just retired pay
TSP distributions ARE taxable in Hawaii despite no state withholding — the most expensive misunderstanding for Hawaii military retirees
County-level property tax exemptions for totally disabled veterans can reduce the bill to a nominal statutory minimum
Seven county veterans cemeteries in addition to the state cemetery — unusually dense for a small state
No state veterans tuition waiver and no dependent tuition program — the clearest gap in the package
Only one state veterans home, located in Hilo, far from the majority of the veteran population on O'ahu
Nonresident military spouse income tax exemption under MSRRA

agency.name: Hawaii Office of Veterans' Services (OVS), Department of Defense

states.topHack: Two things, one defensive and one offensive. Defensively: do not assume your TSP withdrawals are tax-free in Hawaii because your pension is. Hawaii exempts military retired pay but taxes TSP distributions, and because there is no state withholding on TSP the bill arrives as a surprise at filing — sequence withdrawals accordingly or convert before establishing Hawaii residency. Offensively: go directly to your county real property assessment division, not the state, and ask specifically about the totally-disabled-veteran exemption. Because there is no statewide program, there is no statewide publicity, and the county exemptions are among the most generous in the country for veterans who reach a total service-connected disability rating — several counties reduce the annual bill to a nominal minimum regardless of the home's value, which in Honolulu's market is worth many thousands of dollars a year.

states.name: Idaho
states.headline: Excellent hunting, fishing and state park benefits and a real emergency grant program, but the property tax benefit is capped at $1,500 and military retirement is only deductible at 65 (or 62 if disabled).

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Partially exempt with a hard age gate. The retirement benefits deduction requires the taxpayer to be 65 or older, or 62 or older and disabled, AND to hold a qualifying retirement benefit. For 2024 the maximum deduction was $68,796 married filing jointly and $45,864 single; the figures are indexed annually and the 2026 amounts were not verified. A military retiree under 65 (or under 62 if disabled) receives no deduction at all — which is most military retirees in their first decade or two after service.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Generally taxed for residents stationed in Idaho, but service members stationed outside Idaho for 120 continuous days or more are exempt from Idaho tax on military pay. Combat zone hostile fire and imminent danger pay may be excluded consistent with federal rules.
incomeTax.notes: Idaho has moved to a flat individual rate in the mid-5% range. TSP distributions remain subject to Idaho tax. Nonresident spouses of nonresident service members stationed in Idaho are exempt on Idaho earnings but must file an annual withholding exemption certificate — missing that filing is a common and avoidable cost.

states.propertyTax: Idaho's Veterans Property Tax Benefit reduces property tax on the home and up to one acre by up to $1,500 per year. Eligibility requires a 100% service-connected disability rating or compensation at the 100% rate due to Individual Unemployability, ownership and occupancy of the Idaho home as the primary residence, and a current Idaho Homeowner's Exemption. Notably, this benefit has NO income limit — it is available regardless of income, which distinguishes it from the state's general circuit breaker. Application is annual between January 1 and April 15 through the county assessor or online, and the annual filing requirement is the most common way veterans lose it. A surviving spouse may use the benefit but it is not transferable to a new property after the veteran's death. Separately, the general Property Tax Reduction (circuit breaker) program for those 65+, disabled, widows and widowers and certain veterans provides $250 to $1,500 of reduction subject to an income limit of approximately $39,130 for 2026. Because the veteran benefit caps at $1,500 in tax rather than in assessed value, it is far less valuable than a percentage or full exemption — this is Idaho's weakest financial category.
states.education: The Idaho National Guard State Education Assistance Program (SEAP) pays up to $8,000 per state fiscal year toward tuition at Idaho institutions for associate through doctoral degrees, with up to $20,000 for technical programs; the award is pay-grade based, with E9 and below receiving $8,000 and WO1–WO3 and O1–O3 receiving $4,000. The Idaho Operation Education Scholarship at the University of Idaho serves disabled veterans with a permanent disability rating from post-9/11 service, and their spouses, providing individualized support covering tuition, books, housing, childcare, adaptive equipment and job placement — an unusually holistic program, though limited to one campus. In-state tuition is granted to service members who entered as Idaho residents and maintain residency, nonresident active duty stationed in Idaho, National Guard members, and honorably discharged veterans who establish Idaho residence within one year of separation. Idaho has no broad veteran or dependent tuition waiver.
states.employment: Idaho's preference scheme is well designed. Five-point preference applies to those with 180+ days of active duty and honorable discharge, and to unremarried surviving spouses. Ten-point preference applies to veterans rated 10% or higher, Purple Heart recipients, and unremarried surviving spouses of eligible veterans. Most usefully, a veteran rated 30% or higher who lands among the top 25 qualified applicants receives a guaranteed interview — a mechanism more valuable in practice than points alone. Professional licensing is strong: service members are exempt from renewal fees while serving in an active or reserve component, licenses remain in good standing and cannot be cancelled, suspended or revoked during service, and remain valid until six months after discharge; boards may accept military training and experience toward licensure and expedite applications. State employees receive 120 hours of paid military leave.
states.vehicleRec: This is where Idaho excels. The veteran designation is free on a new or renewed license (a separate fee applies if added at another time), and service members and dependents may extend a license up to 25 months before expiration for extended out-of-state service, valid up to four years. Most military plates carry no fees: Medal of Honor, Purple Heart (surviving spouse eligible) and Disabled Veteran (100% rating, one set) are free with no renewal fees; Gold Star Family plates are free for surviving spouse and parents. Hunting and fishing is exceptional: veterans rated 40% or higher pay as little as $5 for a resident hunting license (nonresident $31.75), active duty on leave pay $17.50, and nonresident service members stationed in Idaho 30+ days pay resident rates, with refunds or rain checks for deploying members. The Disabled Veterans Special Big Game Tag Program provides five free annual tags for deer, elk, bear, turkey or mountain lion with a January 2–31 application window, two of them sponsored by the Division of Veterans Services, requiring a 40% rating. The State Parks Disabled Veteran Pass gives free lifetime day use AND camping to veterans rated 100% total and permanent, waiving both motor vehicle entrance and campsite fees, with a 14-night limit per 30 days.
states.cash: Idaho Veterans Financial Assistance provides grants of up to $1,500 for emergency food, fuel, shelter and daily necessities. Eligibility requires 90+ days of active duty (less if discharged for a service-connected disability), honorable discharge, and either five years of Idaho residency or entry into service from Idaho; the application must be filed within 90 days of the emergency, which is a tight and easily missed window. The Idaho National Guard Recruiting Assistant Sponsorship Program (GRASP) pays up to $1,000 per referral ($500 at enlistment, $500 at departure for basic training). There is no wartime service bonus and no state supplement to the VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Four state veterans homes, a strong network for a state of Idaho's population: Pocatello (1957 Alvin Ricken Drive, 66 beds, 208-235-7838), Boise (320 Collins Road, 80 beds, 208-780-1616), Lewiston (821 21st Avenue, 66 beds, 208-750-3683) and Post Falls (590 S Pleasant View Road 101, 64 beds, 208-415-3434). Eligibility requires 90+ days active duty, honorable discharge (wartime veterans receive priority), a need for skilled nursing care, Idaho residency at application, application for VA Aid and Attendance, and either Medicaid eligibility or ability to pay the current maximum monthly charge. Two state veterans cemeteries: Boise (10100 Horseshoe Bend Road, 208-780-1340) and Blackfoot (2651 Cromwell Lane, 208-701-7161), offering columbarium niches, in-ground burial and a scattering garden, with VA covering burial fees for veterans and a $1,002 fee for dependents.
other: Five free big-game tags per year (deer, elk, bear, turkey or mountain lion) for veterans rated 40% or higher — the most valuable hunting benefit in this group of states
Free lifetime state park day use AND camping for veterans rated 100% P&T
Guaranteed interview for veterans rated 30%+ who rank among the top 25 qualified applicants for a state job
Professional licenses cannot be cancelled, suspended or revoked during military service, and renewal fees are waived
Veterans property tax benefit has no income limit — unusual among capped-dollar programs
Incarcerated Veterans Transition Program provides classroom, occupational and apprenticeship training plus childcare, vehicle repair and rent assistance on release
Four state veterans homes covering north, southwest and southeast Idaho
states.topHack: If you are rated 40% or higher, apply between January 2 and 31 for the Disabled Veterans Special Big Game Tag Program — five free tags a year for deer, elk, bear, turkey or mountain lion, in a state where a single nonresident elk tag runs several hundred dollars and resident draw odds are competitive. It is the highest-dollar benefit Idaho offers to a mid-rated veteran and the application window is only 30 days. On the tax side, the trap to avoid is the annual April 15 refiling for the $1,500 Veterans Property Tax Benefit: it has no income limit, so unlike the circuit breaker you never age out or earn out of it, but it is not automatic and there is no grace period. And if you are a retiree under 65, understand that Idaho gives you nothing on your pension until you turn 65 — the state is considerably better as a place to retire into at 65 than to move to at 45.

states.name: Illinois
states.headline: The Illinois Veteran Grant pays full tuition and mandatory fees at every public college in the state for qualifying veterans, active duty and retired pay are both entirely untaxed, and a 70% rating zeroes out property tax — an elite package hidden inside a high-tax state.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Illinois does not tax military retired pay, with no cap, age condition or income limit. SBP, RCSBP and RSFPP annuities and VA DIC are also untaxed.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Military income included in federal AGI may be subtracted from Illinois base income, including basic training pay and ROTC compensation. Combat pay already excluded from federal AGI, and Voluntary Separation Incentive payments, are treated separately.
incomeTax.notes: Illinois taxes at a flat 4.95% and exempts all retirement income generally, not just military — so pensions, IRAs, 401(k)s and Social Security are all untaxed too. This makes Illinois one of the most favorable income tax states in the country for a retiree, which is not widely appreciated and partially offsets its property tax burden. Nonresident spouses of service members stationed in Illinois on orders are exempt on Illinois wages.

states.propertyTax: The Disabled Veterans' Standard Homestead Exemption (DVSHE) is a true sliding scale, available where the property's equalized assessed value is under $250,000: a 30–49% rating exempts $2,500 of EAV; a 50–69% rating exempts $5,000 of EAV; and a 70% or higher rating produces a FULL exemption from property tax. That 70% threshold for total exemption is among the lowest in the nation — most states require 100% P&T. As of 2024, WWII veterans receive a full exemption regardless of disability level. Unremarried surviving spouses of eligible veterans, and those receiving DIC, also qualify; surviving spouses of service members killed in the line of duty receive a full exemption on the primary residence. The Returning Veterans' Homestead Exemption (RVHE) separately gives a $5,000 EAV reduction for two consecutive tax years after returning from active duty in an armed conflict. The Specially Adapted Housing Exemption provides a $100,000 reduction in assessed value for totally and permanently disabled veterans who received federal, state or charitable assistance to purchase or adapt a home, including mobile homes, and lasts as long as the veteran, spouse or unremarried surviving spouse resides there. Given that Illinois has among the highest effective property tax rates in the country, a full exemption at 70% is worth an enormous amount annually.
states.education: The Illinois Veteran Grant (IVG) is the flagship and one of the best veteran education benefits in the United States: it pays tuition AND mandatory fees at all Illinois state-supported colleges, universities and community colleges, for an unlimited number of hours toward undergraduate and graduate study. Eligibility requires Illinois residency six months before entering the Armed Forces (or 15+ years of Illinois residency after discharge), at least one year of active duty OR a foreign assignment during hostilities, an honorable discharge, and return to Illinois within six months of discharge. The residency-before-service requirement is the binding constraint and the reason many veterans who move to Illinois later cannot use it. The Illinois National Guard Grant (ING) covers tuition and specified fees at Illinois public two- and four-year colleges for current Guard members with one full year of service, up to four academic years full-time (six years for members with 10+ years of service). The MIA/POW Veterans' Dependents Scholarship covers full tuition and mandatory fees for up to four years (maximum 120 points, 12 per semester) for children under 26 — natural, step, adopted or foster (2+ years guardianship) — of veterans who are POW/MIA, rated 100% permanent and total, compensated at 100% for unemployability, or who died of a service-connected cause. The Illinois Fallen Heroes Scholarship deposits $5,000 into a Bright Start 529 for children of service members killed in the line of duty. A separate $250 annual grant covers elementary through vocational school expenses for children aged 10–18 of deceased, disabled, MIA or POW veterans. Note that IVG and ING are subject to annual legislative appropriation and have historically been prorated in lean budget years — confirm the current funding level before relying on full coverage.
states.employment: State hiring preference adds 3 points for an honorable discharge with 6+ months of service or a hardship/disability discharge, 5 points for an honorable discharge after 6+ months during hostilities or the full hostilities period, and 10 points for a service-connected disability rating, Purple Heart receipt, or eligible family members including an unremarried spouse or parent of a deceased or disabled veteran. Promotion preference adds seven-tenths of a point per six months of active duty up to 30 months. Illinois waives education requirements for public safety roles: State Police and Conservation Police degree requirements are waived for veterans with campaign medals and honorable discharge; municipal police and firefighter associate degree requirements are waived with 24 months of honorable service or 180 days of combat, and bachelor's requirements with 36 months or 180 days of combat. IDPH reviews military EMT training for licensing when applied for within one year of discharge. The Illinois Service Member Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (ISERRA) supplements USERRA with a dedicated state advocate (800-382-3000). The Illinois Veterans Business Program targets 3% of state procurement to certified veteran-owned businesses (Illinois-based, under $150M in sales, 51%+ veteran-owned).
states.vehicleRec: The 'Veteran' designation is free at renewal ($5–$10 if added between renewals) and the 'Gold Star' designation is free for family of service members killed in service. Service members on active duty outside Illinois may drive on an expired license for 120 days after return with a free Military Deferral Certificate. Forty-four distinctive plate designs are available with a free first set for Medal of Honor, Purple Heart, Disabled Veteran, ISERVE (50%+ disabled), U.S. Army Veteran and Gold Star Family plates; surviving spouses may retain several of these. Recreation is outstanding: service members receive a free combined sportsman's license, free camping at state parks, and a free firearm deer permit for one year per year served, claimable within two years of return; veterans who served abroad or were mobilized get half-price fishing, hunting and sportsman combination licenses; veterans rated 10% or higher need NO fishing or hunting license at all and are exempt from the habitat stamp; and service members on leave may hunt and fish without a license. Disabled veterans and former POWs receive free camping and admission at Illinois State Parks for the veteran, spouse, minor children and grandchildren under 18, using a Veteran's Disability Card issued by IDVA.
states.cash: Illinois operates the Illinois Military Family Relief Fund (IMFRF), financed largely by an income tax check-off and by direct appropriation, which makes grants to Illinois National Guard and Reserve families and to veterans facing financial hardship arising from deployment or service; per-grant amounts, current funding status and the precise eligibility criteria were NOT verified in this research and should be confirmed with IDVA before publication. Illinois has historically paid Vietnam, Persian Gulf and Global War on Terrorism service bonuses of several hundred dollars under separate compensation acts, but whether any bonus program remains open for application in 2026 was NOT verified — treat any bonus claim with caution.
