Illinois Veterans Care provides subsidized health insurance at roughly $40–$70 monthly premiums for uninsured, low-income veterans aged 19–64 who are ineligible for VA care (877-483-8779), which functions as a significant recurring economic benefit.
states.homesHealth: The Illinois Department of Veterans' Affairs operates a network of state veterans homes historically comprising facilities at Quincy, Manteno, LaSalle, Anna and Chicago, providing skilled nursing and domiciliary care; the current count, bed capacity and operational status of each were NOT verified in this research and should be confirmed with IDVA, particularly given the Quincy facility's major reconstruction following the Legionnaires' disease outbreak and the more recent opening of the Chicago home. Illinois does not operate a large standalone state veterans cemetery system comparable to Texas or California; burial grounds are associated with certain veterans homes, and the state is served by several VA national cemeteries including Abraham Lincoln National Cemetery at Elwood, Camp Butler at Springfield, Danville, Mound City, Quincy and Rock Island. Confirm state cemetery status with IDVA.
other: Full property tax exemption at a 70% rating — one of the lowest thresholds in the nation, in one of the highest-property-tax states
Illinois exempts ALL retirement income from state income tax, not just military — pensions, IRAs, 401(k)s and Social Security included
Veterans rated 10%+ need no hunting or fishing license at all and are exempt from the habitat stamp
Free camping and park admission extends to the veteran's grandchildren under 18, not just children
Illinois Veterans Care: subsidized health insurance at $40–$70/month for uninsured low-income veterans ineligible for VA care
CTA Military Service Pass gives free Chicago Transit rides to veterans rated 10%+ and active duty
Police and firefighter degree requirements waived based on length of service or 180 days of combat
Returning Veterans' Homestead Exemption: an extra $5,000 EAV reduction for two years after deployment, stackable with the disability exemption
WWII veterans receive a full property tax exemption regardless of disability rating (2024 onward)
states.topHack: If you were an Illinois resident before you enlisted, the Illinois Veteran Grant is the single most valuable state benefit in this entire research set — full tuition and mandatory fees at every public university and community college in Illinois, including graduate programs, with no dollar cap and no hours cap. Veterans routinely burn their Post-9/11 GI Bill on an Illinois public school when they could have used IVG for that degree and saved all 36 months of Chapter 33 for a private school, a graduate program, or transfer to a child. The eligibility hinge is residency six months before entering service and return to Illinois within six months of discharge, so establish and document that return date immediately on separation. Second: the 70% rating threshold for a full property tax exemption is far lower than most veterans assume, and in a state with 2%+ effective rates, moving from 69% to 70% is worth more per year than almost any other single-point rating increase in the country.

states.name: Indiana
states.headline: Active duty pay and military retirement are both entirely exempt, dependents of disabled veterans get 124 credit hours free at public colleges, and the Military Family Relief Fund pays real emergency cash — the property tax deductions are the only modest piece.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Indiana exempts military retirement pay from state income tax entirely, following a phase-in that completed in recent years. Military disability retirement pay received as a pension or annuity for injury or sickness from active service is also exempt, as are SBP, RCSBP and RSFPP annuities.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Indiana residents serving in active or reserve components are exempt from Indiana income tax on military pay (effective from 2024). Those serving outside the U.S. and Puerto Rico get an automatic 60-day filing extension; combat zone service brings 180 days after redeployment.
incomeTax.notes: Indiana's flat state rate is around 3% with county income taxes added on top; the exemption applies to the state portion. Nonresident military spouses do not pay Indiana income tax on Indiana wages where the service member is stationed there on orders. Indiana resident service members on military orders are also exempt from jury duty.

states.propertyTax: Indiana uses three stacking deductions from assessed value rather than a single exemption, and all require an Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs Certificate of Eligibility. First, a $14,000 deduction for a veteran with 90+ days of honorable service who has either a total VA disability rating or is 62+ with a 10% or higher service-connected rating — but it is unavailable if the property's assessed value exceeds $200,000, which is an increasingly binding cap as Indiana home values rise. Second, a $24,960 deduction for a veteran with an honorable discharge during WWII, Korea, Vietnam or the Gulf War era who has at least a 10% service-connected rating; this one has no $200,000 property value cap. Surviving spouses are eligible for both. Third, a deduction equal to a percentage matching the disability rating (50%–100%) for property gifted by a charitable organization to a veteran with 90+ days of service, honorable discharge and a 50%+ rating. A distinctive extra: a disabled veteran with unused property tax deduction remaining may apply the overage against vehicle excise tax on up to two vehicles, receiving a $2 credit toward excise tax for every $100 of remaining deduction, capped at $70. These are deductions from assessed value, not full exemptions, so the dollar relief is modest compared with Illinois, Iowa or Arkansas.
states.education: Indiana's dependent education benefits are genuinely excellent. The Tuition and Fee Exemption for Children of Deceased or Disabled Veterans covers 100% of tuition and regularly assessed fees at Indiana public colleges, or up to $5,000 toward tuition at Indiana private non-profit institutions, limited to 124 credit hours at the undergraduate and professional degree level. An identical program covers Children of Purple Heart Recipients. Purple Heart recipients themselves receive 100% of tuition and regularly assessed fees for up to 124 credit hours at certificate, undergraduate, graduate or professional level. The National Guard Supplemental Grant (NGSG) pays 100% of tuition and regularly assessed fees at Indiana public institutions and up to $5,000 annually at Indiana private non-profits, requiring active drilling status with no AWOL in the prior 12 months and satisfactory academic progress, for first associate, bachelor's or master's degrees; an NGSG Scholarship Extension Program serves former members who could not complete degrees due to post-9/11 deployments. A supplemental grant covers children and spouses of Indiana National Guard members killed in action at 100% of tuition and fees up to 124 credit hours. All applications run through Indiana ScholarTrack (IDVA 317-232-3910 or 800-400-4520; Guard Education Services 317-964-7023). Note the eligibility for the disabled-veteran dependent program has been tightened over time with service-connection and residency conditions layered on — confirm current criteria before relying on it.
states.employment: State hiring preference adds 10% to a veteran's score in the hiring process for those with 181+ days of active duty and honorable discharge — a percentage-based rather than points-based approach. Private employers may adopt written veteran preference policies for hiring, promotion or retention. Indiana National Guard and Reserve members receive 15 days of military leave per calendar year for required training, granted with or without pay at employer discretion, and employers must grant 10 days of unpaid leave to a family member of a service member who received deployment orders, usable 30 days before, during, or within 30 days after deployment — a family leave right few states provide. Honorably discharged veterans receive free peddler, vendor and hawker licenses. The CDL military skills waiver is honored. Purple Star designated schools guarantee a job interview to service members and immediate family members who meet minimum qualifications.
states.vehicleRec: Indiana uses distinct driver license indicators: 'V' for veterans (DD214 required), 'AM' for active service members (Common Access Card), and 'VS' for surviving spouses (DD214, marriage and death certificates) — the surviving spouse indicator is unusual. There is no charge when added at new issuance or renewal. Licenses and IDs remain valid until 90 days after discharge or end of deployment for members and dependents serving outside Indiana. Nineteen distinctive plate types are available including Army Medal of Honor, Purple Heart, Disabled Hoosier Army Veteran, Hoosier Army Veteran and Gold Star Family, with initial applications at BMV branches and renewals online. Hunting and fishing: service members on leave hunt and fish free with leave papers and valid ID; nonresident active duty pay resident prices; disabled veterans pay $2.75 annually or $27.50 for a ten-year license, covering small game and fishing only. Disabled veterans and former POWs with qualifying plates may purchase the Hoosier Golden Passport at half price, giving unlimited admission to all Indiana state-owned parks, recreation areas, reservoirs and forests.
states.cash: The Indiana Military Family Relief Fund (MFRF) provides emergency monetary grants to Indiana veterans and dependents in financial hardship, covering housing, utilities, food, medical services and basic transportation. The lifetime limit is $2,500, with additional grants possible in exceptional circumstances. Eligibility requires Indiana residency, an honorable or general discharge, documented financial hardship, and household income not exceeding twice the federal poverty guidelines (IDVA 317-232-3914 or 317-234-8648, mfrf@dva.in.gov). Separately, a County Veterans Burial Allowance of $1,000 is paid to next of kin of honorably discharged veterans and spouses to offset burial expenses — a county-administered benefit many families never claim. Indiana National Guard State Sponsored Life Insurance offers $5,000 to $50,000 of coverage with $10,000 free for the first year for new recruits. There is no wartime service bonus and no state supplement to the VA pension.
states.homesHealth: The Indiana Veterans' Home (IVH) in West Lafayette is the single state home, offering long-term skilled nursing, short-term rehabilitation, independent living and memory care, with specialty services in pulmonology, endocrinology, nephrology, psychiatry, physical/speech/hearing therapy, podiatry, dentistry, social services and music therapy. Eligibility covers honorably discharged veterans, eligible spouses and surviving spouses, and Gold Star parents, requiring one year of Indiana residency (waivable) and a criminal background check (admissions&marketing@ivh.in.gov, 765-497-8072). The Indiana Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Madison provides burial plot, opening and closing, outer burial container, grave marker and chapel use at no cost, accommodating casketed burials, cremated remains, columbaria niches and a scatter garden, with eligibility matching VA national cemetery standards (812-273-9220, ivmc@dva.in.gov). A Governor's Memorial Certificate signed by the Governor is available to surviving family members of honorably discharged veterans.
other: Employers must grant 10 days of unpaid family leave to relatives of a service member who received deployment orders — a right few states provide
'VS' surviving spouse designation on driver licenses, distinct from the veteran indicator
County Veterans Burial Allowance of $1,000 paid to next of kin — widely unclaimed
Unused property tax deduction converts to vehicle excise tax credit on up to two vehicles ($2 per $100 of remaining deduction, capped at $70)
Free peddler, vendor and hawker licenses for honorably discharged veterans
Jury duty exemption for resident service members on military orders
Purple Star schools guarantee job interviews to service members and immediate family meeting minimum qualifications
Wartime-era $24,960 deduction has no $200,000 property value cap, unlike the $14,000 deduction
states.topHack: Stack the two property tax deductions rather than choosing one. A wartime-era veteran (WWII, Korea, Vietnam or Gulf War) with at least a 10% rating qualifies for the $24,960 deduction, which has NO $200,000 assessed value cap, and if they also meet the second test — total disability, or age 62+ with a 10%+ rating — they can claim the $14,000 deduction as well, subject to that one's cap. Most veterans and many county auditors treat these as alternatives. Then take whatever deduction you cannot absorb against your property tax and convert it into vehicle excise tax credit on up to two vehicles. Separately, the dependent tuition exemption — 124 credit hours of free tuition and fees at any Indiana public college for the child of a disabled veteran — is worth well over $50,000 per child and is claimed through ScholarTrack, not the campus, which is why so many families miss the deadline.

states.name: Iowa
states.headline: Active duty pay and military retirement are both fully exempt, a 100% rating produces a total property tax credit, and Iowa pays real cash — a $10,000 injured veterans grant and a $5,000 homebuyer grant — though veteran tuition benefits are thin.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Military retirement pay included in federal gross income is fully exempt from Iowa income tax, as are federal military survivor benefits.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Military pay received by service members on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces is not taxed in Iowa. Combat zone pay is exempt where excluded from federal AGI.
incomeTax.notes: Iowa has moved to a flat individual income tax rate (3.8% as of 2025) and exempts retirement income generally for taxpayers 55 and older, which compounds the military exemption for older retirees. TSP distributions remain subject to Iowa tax. Nonresident military spouses may exclude non-military income under MSRRA where the service member is in Iowa on orders.

states.propertyTax: Iowa runs two separate and stackable programs. The Military Service Property Tax Exemption reduces the taxable value of the homestead — the exemption was increased to $4,000 of taxable value in recent legislation, up from a long-frozen $1,852. Eligibility is unusually broad: honorably discharged veterans with 18+ months of service (or less if separated for a service-connected injury), reserve members with 20+ years, those with 90+ days of federal active duty, and qualifying family members including a spouse, surviving spouse, minor child or widowed parent. Surviving spouses may continue receiving it. Separately, the Disabled Veteran's Homestead Tax Credit provides a credit equal to 100% of the property tax on the homestead — a complete elimination of the bill, not a deduction from value — for veterans with a 100% service-connected disability rating or permanent and total disability based on Individual Unemployability. Unremarried surviving spouses of deceased disabled veterans also qualify. The credit is limited to a homestead of up to one-half acre within city limits or 40 acres outside. The combination of a broadly available small exemption and a full credit at the top is well designed; the gap is that there is no intermediate tier for veterans rated 30–90%.
states.education: This is Iowa's weakest area for veterans themselves. The Iowa National Guard Service Scholarship (INGSS) covers up to 120 credit hours (130 for STEM degrees) at up to 100% of resident tuition or the institution's rate, whichever is lower, for Iowa National Guard members at eligible state colleges and universities, and combines with federal aid. The Branstad-Reynolds Children of Fallen Iowa Service Members Scholarship covers tuition, books, fees, housing, required tools and equipment and tutoring for children of service members who died on active duty after September 11, 2001, where the deceased was an Iowa resident at enlistment and at death; the death need not be combat-related. Iowa also maintains War Orphans Educational Aid for children of veterans who died in service, though the award amount is small and was not verified for 2026. Iowa Operation Recognition awards honorary high school diplomas to honorably discharged wartime veterans from WWI through the Vietnam era who left school to enlist. There is no broad tuition waiver for veterans themselves and no dependent program for children of living disabled veterans comparable to Indiana, Illinois or Alabama.
states.employment: State hiring preference adds 5 percentage points on hiring exams, with an additional 5 points for a service-connected disability or receipt of VA compensation; it does not apply to police or fire chief promotions. Iowa law expressly authorizes private employers to adopt preferential hiring and promotion for veterans, and extends eligibility to spouses of disabled or deceased veterans. CDL knowledge and skills testing may be waived for military personnel with relevant occupational specialties, and separated service members within one year are eligible for the skills waiver. IowaWORKS Centers provide veteran employment services, resume building and job counseling with dedicated Veteran Career Planners and priority of service for federally funded programs. The Iowa SkillBridge Program places separating service members in internships up to six months before separation while they continue to receive military salary and benefits (skillbridge@iwd.iowa.gov).
states.vehicleRec: The veteran designation on a license or ID requires a DD214 and is certified through a County Veterans Service Office. Iowa exempts veterans from fees for chauffeur, commercial, operator and motorcycle licenses — a broader fee waiver than most states. Twenty-four distinctive plate options are available: the Veteran plate is free for the first set with additional sets $25 and a $5 annual validation fee; Purple Heart is free ($25 personalized) with a $5 annual fee; Medal of Honor carries no fees at all; the Disabled Veteran plate is fully exempt from fees on one vehicle; Gold Star Family is free or $25 personalized. Qualifying plates confer free parking in city lots and metered spaces — an underrated daily benefit in Des Moines, Iowa City and Cedar Rapids. Hunting and fishing: active duty on leave may hunt and fish without a license carrying leave papers and an LES; disabled veterans pay $7 for a lifetime license; honorably discharged veterans pay $7 for an annual combined license; veterans rated 100% pay $65 for a lifetime trout license.
states.cash: Iowa is one of the better states in this group for actual cash. The Iowa Injured Veterans Grant Program pays up to $10,000 to allow family presence during recovery, for service members and veterans injured after September 11, 2001 in a combat zone who required medical evacuation or 30+ consecutive days of hospitalization, with eligibility continuing through discharge while receiving treatment. The Iowa Veterans Trust Fund provides financial assistance for unemployment and underemployment, vision, hearing and dental care, durable medical equipment, prescriptions, counseling, vehicle and housing repairs and transitional housing, with all expenditures approved through the Iowa Veterans Commission and administered through County Veteran Service Offices. The Iowa Finance Authority Military Homeownership Assistance program provides a $5,000 grant toward down payment or closing costs for qualifying home purchases, for those with 90+ days of active duty between August 2, 1990 and April 6, 1991 or from September 11, 2001 to the present, veterans with a service-connected disability rating, and surviving spouses; it stacks with the FirstHome and Homes for Iowans programs.
states.homesHealth: The Iowa Veterans Home in Marshalltown is the state's single facility and one of the largest state veterans homes in the country, providing long-term health care to honorably discharged veterans, spouses, surviving spouses and Gold Star parents, with pharmacy, physical, speech, occupational and respiratory therapy, laboratory, X-ray, prosthetics, eyeglasses and hearing aids, plus recreation, chaplaincy, social work, Wi-Fi, barber and beauty services, laundry and massage. Eligibility requires Iowa residency; a spouse must have been married one year before application; Gold Star parents qualify where the service member died during wartime or from service (admissions 800-645-4591). The Iowa Veterans Cemetery at Van Meter, ten miles west of Des Moines, offers in-ground casket and cremation burial and above-ground columbarium placement with a free government granite headstone or niche marker; veterans are buried free and family members are charged $300. Three VA national cemeteries also operate in Iowa.
other: Iowa Finance Authority Military Homeownership Assistance: $5,000 grant toward down payment or closing costs, stackable with FirstHome and Homes for Iowans
Injured Veterans Grant of up to $10,000 specifically to fund family presence during recovery — nearly unique among states
Free parking in city lots and metered spaces with qualifying veteran plates
Fee exemption for chauffeur, commercial, operator and motorcycle driver licenses
$7 lifetime hunting/fishing license for disabled veterans; $7 annual combined license for any honorably discharged veteran
Iowa SkillBridge places separating members in internships up to six months pre-separation while still drawing military pay
Iowa exempts retirement income generally at 55+, which compounds with the military exemption
Military Service Property Tax Exemption is available to reserve members with 20+ years and to widowed parents, not just veterans
states.topHack: Claim both property tax programs, not one. The Military Service Property Tax Exemption and the Disabled Veteran's Homestead Tax Credit are separate statutes administered on separate forms, and the exemption's eligibility is far broader than most veterans realize — 18 months of honorable service is enough, and it also reaches reserve members with 20 years, surviving spouses, minor children and widowed parents. Many Iowa veterans file for one and never learn the other exists. Beyond property tax, the highest-dollar underused item is the Iowa Finance Authority's $5,000 Military Homeownership Assistance grant: it is a grant, not a loan, it stacks with Iowa's first-time buyer programs, and it is available to any veteran with a service-connected disability rating regardless of percentage — including 0% and 10% ratings that most people assume are worthless.

states.name: Kansas
states.headline: Military retirement is fully exempt and the education programs are surprisingly deep, but active duty pay is taxed and the property tax benefit is a $700 refund rather than an exemption — the weakest homeowner relief in this group.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Kansas exempts military retirement pay from state income tax where it is included in federal adjusted gross income, with no cap or age condition.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxed. Active duty military pay received by Kansas resident service members remains subject to Kansas income tax — one of the clearer weak points in the package.
incomeTax.notes: Veterans with a service-connected total and permanent disability rating receiving compensation at the 100% rate may claim an additional personal exemption — $2,250, rising to $2,320 for tax year 2025 and later. Nonresident spouses stationed in Kansas with a service member may be exempt from Kansas tax on earned income under MSRRA.

states.propertyTax: Kansas provides a Homestead Refund rather than an exemption, and it is modest: a property tax rebate of up to $700, available to disabled veterans with a service-connected rating of 50% or greater, subject to a home appraised value cap of $350,000 and a household income limit of approximately $56,450. Surviving spouses of eligible disabled veterans qualify, and surviving spouses of active duty members killed in service qualify until remarriage. Because the benefit is a capped refund rather than a percentage or full exemption, a veteran with a $300,000 home paying $4,000 a year in property tax still pays $3,300 — this is materially weaker than the full exemptions in Arkansas, Iowa and Illinois or the large deductions in Georgia and DC. On the positive side, the 50% rating threshold is lower than the 100% P&T requirement most states impose, so more veterans qualify for something. Service members deploying for six months or more may defer property tax on a principal residence for up to two years. The income and value caps are adjusted periodically and the 2026 figures should be confirmed with the Kansas Department of Revenue.
states.education: Kansas is genuinely strong here and it is the most underrated part of the state's package. The Kansas Hero's Scholarship waives tuition and fees for up to 10 semesters at Kansas public institutions for spouses and dependents of service members killed in the line of duty after 9/11, dependents of veterans rated 80% or higher, and former prisoners of war — note the 80% threshold rather than the near-universal 100% requirement. The Kansas Military Service Scholarship covers tuition and fees at Kansas public institutions for up to four years for veterans who served in a hostile fire pay area after 9/11 with an honorable or general discharge. All veterans eligible for federal education benefits and all current service members receive in-state tuition at Kansas public colleges regardless of residency, as do their spouses and dependents. Kansas National Guard Educational Assistance provides up to 100% of tuition and fees at accredited Kansas institutions, up to 15 credit hours per semester with a 180 undergraduate hour lifetime limit — and, importantly, unused hours became transferable to eligible dependents beginning fall 2025, a significant expansion. The Kansas EMERGE program provides advanced degree tuition assistance for Guard members at up to 15 credit hours per semester at state institution rates. Children of Vietnam veterans who died from service-connected disabilities receive a tuition and fee waiver for up to 12 semesters.
states.employment: Kansas uses guaranteed interviews and consideration rather than a points system for state employment, with preference applying to hiring, promotions and layoff retention. Professional licensing is among the best in this group: military education and training is accepted toward licensing requirements, licensure is expedited for service members and spouses holding a current valid license from another state, licenses remain valid during active duty with renewal extended six months post-discharge, probationary licenses are available for service members and military spouses, and military spouses are exempt from fees on both initial and renewal applications. State employees activated to Guard or Reserve duty for 30+ days receive differential pay covering the gap between state and military pay up to $1,000 per pay period, plus a one-time $1,500 activation payment. Public employees may purchase KPERS military service credit year-for-year for active duty and a quarter year per reserve year to increase retirement benefits. The CDL knowledge and skills waiver applies to those discharged within 12 months with qualifying MOSs (Army 88M, 92F, 14T; Air Force 2T1, 2F0, 3E2; Marine Corps 3531; Navy EO).
states.vehicleRec: The 'VETERAN' marking is available on Kansas driver licenses and ID cards for honorably discharged veterans. Service members in active or reserve components are exempt from motor vehicle tax on two vehicles. Plate options include Medal of Honor, Purple Heart (with optional combat decoration decals at $2 each), Disabled Veteran (no registration fee on the initial plate), U.S. Veteran (180+ days active duty, honorable discharge) and Gold Star Mother. Hunting and fishing licenses are free for Kansas National Guard members and for honorably discharged veterans with a 30% or higher disability rating — a low threshold — and active Guard members receive a free park vehicle permit. Nonresident active duty stationed in Kansas pay resident rates, Kansas residents stationed out of state may continue buying resident licenses, and permit holders who receive PCS orders before the season may obtain a refund. Military personnel at Fort Riley are eligible for dedicated military elk permits, which is a meaningful draw advantage.
states.cash: Kansas has no general wartime service bonus and no broad state-funded emergency cash assistance fund open to all veterans. The cash items are employment-linked: a one-time $1,500 activation payment for state employees called to Guard or Reserve duty for 30+ continuous days, and differential pay up to $1,000 per pay period during activation. Kansas National Guard and Reserve members and families may request emergency assistance through the Kansas National Guard Foundation Relief Fund when other options are exhausted — but this is a private foundation rather than a state program. There is no state supplement to the VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Two state facilities. The Kansas Veterans' Home in Winfield (1220 World War II Memorial Drive, 620-221-9479) offers domiciliary/assisted living, nursing and memory care. The Kansas Soldiers' Home at Fort Dodge (714 Sheridan Unit 128, 620-227-2121) offers three levels of care. Eligibility requires an honorable discharge and a need for 24-hour skilled nursing care; spouses and eligible family may be admitted when space allows, and notably Kansas residency is NOT required though residents receive preference — an unusual openness that makes these homes an option for out-of-state families. Four state cemeteries: Fort Dodge (620-682-7564), WaKeeney (785-743-5685), Winfield (620-705-6300) and Fort Riley/Manhattan (785-717-3050), with no burial fees for veterans or eligible family and casket burial, scattering garden or columbaria options; fees apply only for non-state grave liners or oversized caskets.
other: New sales tax exemption effective July 1, 2026: veterans rated 100% service-connected total and permanent or unemployable are exempt from Kansas sales tax on up to $24,000 of purchases annually (excluding tobacco, e-cigarettes, alcohol and motor vehicles), and purchases made on the veteran's behalf by a spouse or household member also qualify
Kansas National Guard tuition hours became transferable to dependents beginning fall 2025
Kansas Hero's Scholarship uses an 80% rating threshold rather than 100%
Free hunting and fishing licenses at a 30% rating — one of the lowest thresholds in the country
State veterans homes do not require Kansas residency for admission
$1,500 activation payment plus up to $1,000 per pay period differential pay for activated state employees
KPERS military service credit purchase increases public employee retirement benefits year-for-year
Military spouses pay no fees on initial or renewal professional license applications
Free vital records (birth, marriage, divorce, death certificates) for veterans for VA purposes
Vietnam War Medallion Program for Kansas residents who served February 28, 1961 – May 7, 1975
states.topHack: The sales tax exemption starting July 1, 2026 is the newest and least-known money in Kansas: a veteran rated 100% total and permanent or unemployable can make up to $24,000 of purchases per year free of Kansas state and local sales tax, and — critically — purchases made by a spouse or household member on the veteran's behalf also qualify. At combined Kansas rates approaching 9–10% in many jurisdictions, that is worth well over $2,000 a year to a household that actually uses it, which dwarfs the $700 homestead refund everyone focuses on. Register for it as soon as the Department of Revenue opens enrollment. Second: if you are a Guard member with unused Kansas National Guard tuition hours, they became transferable to dependents in fall 2025 — check your remaining balance against the 180-hour lifetime cap before it lapses.

states.name: Kentucky
states.headline: Active-duty pay is fully exempt and the flat rate keeps dropping, but military retirement only gets the same $31,110 exclusion every Kentucky retiree gets, and there is no veteran-specific property tax exemption.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Partially exempt. Retirement from service ending before 1/1/1998 is 100% exempt. For service after 12/31/1997, military pensions fall under the general $31,110 annual pension/retirement income exclusion (KRS 141.019), shared across ALL retirement income; amounts above $31,110 are taxed at the flat rate. Schedule P is used to compute the exempt portion, and service before 1998 can be pro-rated out first.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. All active-duty military pay is excluded from Kentucky income (KRS 141.019(1)(l)), subtracted on Schedule M. No Kentucky return is required if active-duty pay is the only income and nothing was withheld.
incomeTax.notes: Flat individual rate; 4.0% for 2025 and reduced to 3.5% effective 1/1/2026 under HB 1 (2025 session). VA disability compensation is not taxed. Combat-zone filing extensions mirror federal (12 months after service). Kentucky does nothing extra for VA disability beyond the federal exclusion.

states.propertyTax: Kentucky has NO veteran-specific property tax exemption. Veterans access relief only through the general constitutional homestead exemption (Ky. Const. Sec. 170), which is $49,100 of assessed value for the 2025-2026 assessment cycle and is available to homeowners age 65+ OR who are classified totally disabled. A 100% P&T VA rating generally supports the totally-disabled classification, but the veteran must apply to the county Property Valuation Administrator and the amount is capped at $49,100 regardless of rating — a 30% or 70% rated veteran gets nothing. The exemption is indexed and re-set by the Department of Revenue every two years. Surviving spouses do not inherit it as veterans; they must independently qualify (age 65+ or totally disabled). There is no separate Purple Heart, POW, or Medal of Honor property exemption.
states.education: Kentucky Dependent Tuition Waiver (KRS 164.507) is the marquee program: 100% tuition waiver at Kentucky state-supported two-year, four-year, and vocational/technical institutions for the spouse, unremarried widow(er), and children/stepchildren of a veteran who died on active duty, died from a service-connected disability, is rated 100% service-connected disabled, or is totally disabled (non-service-connected) with wartime service. Children must generally be under 26; spouses have no age cap. Administered by the Kentucky Department of Veterans Affairs, which issues the eligibility certificate — the school will not grant it without one. Separately, the Kentucky National Guard Tuition Award Program (KYNG TAP) pays tuition at Kentucky public institutions for drilling Guard members. Veterans and dependents using federal VA education benefits get in-state tuition rates immediately under KRS 164.020 / the federal Choice Act. There is no general tuition waiver for the veteran's own undergraduate study.
states.employment: Kentucky grants veterans preference in state and local government competitive classified hiring under KRS 18A.150 — veterans and eligible family members who meet minimum qualifications receive interview preference, and point preference is applied in the merit system (customarily 5 points for veterans, 10 for service-connected disabled; confirm current point values with Kentucky Personnel Cabinet). Kentucky accepts military training and experience toward occupational licensure and offers expedited/temporary licensure for military spouses under KRS 12.355. The Kentucky Career Center provides priority of service and the Kentucky Office of Employment and Training runs veteran employment representatives. Homegrown by Heroes certifies veteran-produced agricultural products under Kentucky Proud.
states.vehicleRec: Kentucky offers 41 military and veteran license plate designs, including Disabled Veteran (a no-fee version for qualifying 100% service-connected veterans and a standard fee version), Purple Heart, Medal of Honor, Army/Navy/Air Force/Marine Veteran, Ex-POW, and Gold Star Family plates for multiple relationships. Veteran designation is available on driver's licenses. Disabled veterans rated 50% or higher may buy the Disabled Sportsman's License at $12/year, which covers hunting and fishing including most permits. Kentucky State Parks offer discounts to active-duty and veterans on some packages but there is no statewide free-admission pass; day-use entry at most Kentucky state parks is free to everyone. There is no statewide free vehicle registration for disabled veterans.
states.cash: Kentucky has no active wartime service bonus program and no state supplement to VA pension. There is no large state-funded emergency financial assistance fund comparable to Michigan's Veterans Trust Fund or Louisiana's Military Family Assistance Fund; emergency help is routed through the Kentucky Department of Veterans Affairs field offices and nonprofit partners. No property-tax-credit-style refund for veterans.
states.homesHealth: Four state veterans nursing homes: Paul E. Patton Eastern Kentucky Veterans Center (Hazard), Thomson-Hood Veterans Center (Wilmore), Joseph 'Eddie' Ballard Western Kentucky Veterans Center (Hanson), and Carl M. Brashear Radcliff Veterans Center (Radcliff); a fifth, the Robert E. Spiller Bowling Green Veterans Center, has been under construction. Five state veterans cemeteries: Kentucky Veterans Cemetery West (Hopkinsville), Central (Radcliff), North (Williamstown), South East (Hyden), and North East (Grayson). No separate state-funded veterans health insurance program.
other: The $49,100 homestead exemption is a general age-65/disability benefit, not a veteran benefit — Kentucky is one of the weaker states in the region on property tax for veterans.
The $31,110 pension exclusion is shared across all retirement income, so a military retiree with a civilian 401(k) draw cannot double-dip.
Flat rate falls to 3.5% for tax year 2026, which quietly improves the value of the partial pension exclusion.
KDVA operates state-employed field service officers rather than a county VSO system, so benefit help is centralized.
states.topHack: If you are rated 100% service-connected, get the KDVA eligibility certificate for the Dependent Tuition Waiver — it puts your spouse AND every child through a Kentucky public university tuition-free, and it stacks on top of federal Chapter 35 DEA, which most families never claim together.

states.name: Louisiana
states.headline: Military retirement is fully exempt from a low 3% flat tax, 100%-rated veterans pay zero property tax, and the state runs an unusually generous $10,000/year emergency cash fund — but active-duty residents still pay state tax on their pay.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Louisiana R.S. 47:44.2 excludes federal retirement benefits received by federal retirees, both military and non-military, from Louisiana taxable income, and separately excludes federal Survivor Benefit Plan payments. No age or dollar cap.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxable for Louisiana-domiciled residents, with exceptions: combat and hazardous duty pay are exempt, and under the federal Military Spouses Residency Relief Act a non-domiciled spouse pays no Louisiana tax on Louisiana wages. Nonresident service members stationed in Louisiana are not taxed on military pay.
incomeTax.notes: Louisiana moved to a flat 3% individual rate effective tax year 2025 (2024 special session reform), with a large increased standard deduction. Social Security is also exempt. VA disability compensation and VA disability retirement payments are excluded. Louisiana does nothing extra for VA disability beyond the federal exclusion.

states.propertyTax: Layered on top of the standard $7,500 assessed-value homestead exemption (roughly $75,000 of fair market value, since Louisiana assesses residential property at 10%), disabled veterans get tiered additional exemptions that took effect 1/1/2023 under Constitutional Amendment 2 of November 2022: 50-69% rating adds $2,500 of assessed value (total $10,000 assessed exempt); 70-99% rating adds $4,500 (total $12,000 assessed exempt); and 100% service-connected disabled OR individually unemployable veterans are exempt from ad valorem tax on the ENTIRE remaining assessed value of the homestead — effectively zero property tax. Surviving spouses of eligible veterans keep the exemption as long as they continue to own and occupy that same home; it generally does not port to a newly purchased home after the veteran's death. Surviving spouses of service members who died on active duty also receive a full exemption. Applications go to the parish assessor with VA Form A25 documentation. Note: a Louisiana measure affecting homestead exemptions for surviving spouses of deceased veterans was certified for a 2026 statewide ballot; check whether it passed before relying on the surviving-spouse portability rules.
states.education: Louisiana Veterans Affairs Educational Assistance (the 'Dependents Educational Assistance' program, R.S. 29:288) waives tuition and registration fees at Louisiana public colleges, universities, and technical colleges for children age 16-25 and for surviving/unremarried spouses of veterans who are rated 90% or higher service-connected disabled, died in service, died of a service-connected disability, or are POW/MIA. The 90% threshold is lower than most states' 100% requirement — this is the state's standout education benefit. For the Guard: the Louisiana National Guard State Tuition Exemption Program for Drilling Guardsmen (STEP) waives tuition at state institutions, and the Louisiana National Guard Patriot Scholarship covers mandatory fees for up to four years. Nonresident active-duty members and their dependents are classified as residents for tuition purposes, and veterans using federal benefits get in-state rates.
states.employment: Louisiana Civil Service adds 5 preference points for wartime veterans and 10 points for service-connected disabled veterans to passing exam scores; surviving spouses and certain spouses of disabled veterans also qualify. Honorably discharged state employees have statutory reinstatement rights to the same or a similar position after military service. Louisiana Works / the Louisiana Workforce Commission provides priority of service in job training programs. The state offers a CDL skills-test waiver for qualifying military vehicle operators, and expedited/reciprocal occupational licensing for military spouses. Louisiana's Veteran Initiative gives certified veteran-owned and service-connected-disabled-veteran-owned small businesses a procurement preference.
states.vehicleRec: Free 'Veteran' designation on driver's licenses and ID cards for honorably discharged veterans; free driver's licenses for veterans rated 50% or more disabled, with a 'Disabled American Veteran' designation at 100%. About 50 distinctive military plate designs; Medal of Honor and Purple Heart plates are free with no renewal fee, and the Disabled Veteran plate is free and carries mobility-impaired parking privileges. Gold Star Family plates available. Recreation is a strong point: veterans rated 50%+ disabled get FREE LIFETIME hunting and fishing licenses covering all privileges; honorably discharged veterans and retirees can buy a $20 combination license; surviving spouses of KIA members get a $4 special-needs license; active-duty dependents pay resident prices. Disabled veterans get free state park admission and active-duty members plus one family member get 50% off. Disabled veterans and Guard members on official duty are exempt from tolls on state bridges.
states.cash: The Military Family Assistance Fund is Louisiana's standout cash program — up to $10,000 per year in grants to service members and their families for housing, utilities, medical expenses, and other need-based hardship, funded by a voluntary tax check-off and state appropriation. There is no active wartime service bonus. No state supplement to VA pension. The Boot Program provides all-expense-paid transition assistance and community visits for separating service members.
states.homesHealth: Five state veterans homes, each roughly 129-156 beds, in Bossier City (Northwest LA War Veterans Home), Jackson (LA War Veterans Home), Jennings (Southwest LA War Veterans Home), Monroe (Northeast LA War Veterans Home), and Reserve (Southeast LA War Veterans Home), offering skilled nursing, memory care, and 24/7 RN coverage with on-site VA benefits counselors. Five state veterans cemeteries: Leesville (Northwest), Rayville (Northeast), Keithville, Slidell (Southeast), and Jennings (Southwest), with no-cost interment, perpetual care, government headstones, and military honors.
other: The 90% disability threshold for free dependent college is one of the lowest in the country — most states require 100%.
Military Family Assistance Fund pays up to $10,000/year in real cash and is badly under-claimed.
Louisiana's move to a 3% flat tax in 2025 makes the already-full retirement exclusion worth less in absolute terms but lowers tax on spouse and second-career income.
Parish Veterans Service Offices are the delivery system statewide — Louisiana does use county/parish-level VSOs.
Free lifetime hunting and fishing at only a 50% rating is unusually low-threshold.
states.topHack: Get to a 90% combined rating, not 100% — at 90% Louisiana already gives your kids (16-25) and your spouse free tuition and fees at every public college in the state, and the Military Family Assistance Fund will write up to $10,000/year in hardship checks on top of it.

states.name: Maine
states.headline: Maine fully exempts military pensions and hands every honorably discharged veteran a free lifetime state park pass, but the headline property tax exemption is a nearly worthless $6,000 of value and the rest of the tax code is high-rate.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Maine does not tax military retired pay or Survivor Benefit Plan annuities; the full amount is subtracted on the Maine return (Maine also exempts military pension from the general pension deduction cap that applies to other retirement income).
incomeTax.activeDuty: Active-duty pay earned by Maine residents while stationed OUTSIDE Maine is exempt from Maine income tax. Active-duty pay earned while stationed in Maine by a Maine resident is taxable. Nonresident service members stationed in Maine are not taxed on military pay.
incomeTax.notes: Maine has a graduated income tax topping out at 7.15%, so the pension exemption is worth real money but other income (spousal wages, second career, investments) is taxed heavily. VA disability compensation is not taxed; Maine does nothing extra beyond the federal exclusion.

states.propertyTax: Maine's veteran property tax relief is small. The standard exemption (36 M.R.S. Sec. 653) removes $6,000 of JUST VALUE from the assessment for a veteran who served during a federally recognized war period AND is age 62 or older, OR who is receiving 100% disability compensation, OR who became 100% disabled while serving. At a typical Maine mill rate this is worth roughly $70-$120 per year. A much larger $50,000 of just value is exempt for a veteran who received a federal grant for a specially adapted housing unit (the paraplegic/SAH exemption) — that one is meaningful. Surviving spouses, minor children, and widowed parents of a qualifying deceased veteran may claim the $6,000 exemption. Applications go to the local town assessor and must be filed by April 1. There is no full exemption at 100% rating and no sliding scale by rating percentage. Maine partially compensates via the income-tax-side Property Tax Fairness Credit, which since 2022 has a veteran-specific component based on property tax paid — that credit, not the exemption, is where most Maine veterans get relief.
states.education: The Maine Veterans Dependents Educational Benefits Program (Sec. 100% waiver) is strong: a 100% waiver of TUITION AND ALL RELATED FEES at University of Maine System campuses, the Maine Community College System, and Maine Maritime Academy for the spouse and dependent children of a veteran who is 100% permanently and totally service-connected disabled, died of a service-connected disability, was killed in action, or is POW/MIA. Unlike many states, Maine waives fees as well as tuition, which is where the real cost sits. The Maine National Guard Education Assistance Program covers 100% of tuition at Maine public institutions for drilling Guard members. Maine grants immediate in-state tuition classification to veterans, active-duty members, and dependents using federal VA education benefits. There is no general tuition waiver for the veteran's own study outside of Guard service.
states.employment: Maine grants veterans hiring preference for state positions, including a guaranteed interview for qualified veterans who meet minimum qualifications. Maine CareerCenters provide priority of service and dedicated veteran employment representatives. Maine's professional and occupational licensing boards grant credit for military training and experience and provide expedited processing, with specific statutory accommodation for military spouses relocating on PCS orders. Maine also recognizes military CDL experience for skills-test waivers.
states.vehicleRec: Special plates include Medal of Honor, Purple Heart, Disabled Veteran, Ex-POW, and Gold Star Family. Veterans rated 100% disabled receive motor vehicle excise tax exemptions (reported as covering up to three vehicles in official summaries — verify the current vehicle count with Maine BMV, as most states cap at one). The standout: a FREE LIFETIME Maine State Park pass for any honorably discharged veteran who is a Maine resident, covering day-use admission at all Maine state parks and historic sites — one of the broadest park benefits in the Northeast. Disabled veterans rated 50%+ get free hunting and fishing licenses, and disabled veterans get free camping at Maine State Parks.
states.cash: Maine has no active wartime service bonus. Emergency financial assistance is administered through the Maine Bureau of Veterans' Services and the Maine Veterans' Homes network rather than a large dedicated state fund. The most significant cash-equivalent is the Property Tax Fairness Credit with its veteran component, claimed on the Maine individual income tax return. No state supplement to VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Six Maine Veterans' Homes providing skilled nursing and residential care — Augusta, Bangor, Caribou, Machias, Scarborough, and South Paris (note: the Machias and Caribou facilities have been subject to closure proposals in recent years; confirm current operating status). Four state veterans cemeteries, concentrated at the Maine Veterans' Memorial Cemetery complex in Augusta plus Springvale and Caribou. Maine does not run a separate state veterans health insurance program.
other: The $6,000 standard exemption has not been meaningfully increased in decades and is one of the smallest veteran property exemptions in the country.
The $50,000 specially-adapted-housing exemption is 8x larger and is the one worth chasing.
Free lifetime state park pass for ALL honorably discharged resident veterans, not just disabled ones.
Dependent tuition waiver covers fees as well as tuition, which most states do not.
Maine's high top marginal rate (7.15%) means the military pension exemption is worth more here than in a flat-tax state.
states.topHack: If the VA ever approves you for a Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant, the Maine property exemption jumps from $6,000 to $50,000 of just value — and most Maine assessors will not tell you the SAH tier exists, so bring the VA grant certificate to the town office yourself before April 1.

states.name: Maryland
states.headline: A full property tax exemption at 100% P&T is excellent, but Maryland is one of the last states still taxing most military retirement income, capping the subtraction at $20,000 and stacking a 2-3% local income tax on top.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Partially exempt, age-tiered. Maryland allows a subtraction of up to $12,500 of military retirement income if you are under age 55 on the last day of the tax year, and up to $20,000 if you are 55 or older (raised in 2023 from $5,000/$15,000). Everything above the cap is taxed at Maryland's graduated rate PLUS the county/Baltimore City local income tax. Claimed on Form 502, line 13. Qualifying service includes active duty, Reserve, National Guard, and Public Health Service/NOAA/Coast and Geodetic Survey commissioned service. NOTE: HB 761 in the 2026 session proposed eliminating the age split and raising the subtraction to $25,000 for TY2026 and $40,000 for TY2027+; I could not verify whether it was enacted — confirm before relying on a figure above $20,000.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxable for Maryland-domiciled residents. A separate subtraction of up to $15,000 is available for military pay earned while stationed OUTSIDE the United States, and only if total military pay is $30,000 or less. Nonresident service members stationed in Maryland are not taxed on military pay.
incomeTax.notes: Maryland's real sting is the county/Baltimore City local income tax of roughly 2.25%-3.20% layered on the state rate, which applies to the taxable portion of military retirement. Residents 65+ or totally disabled may also use Maryland's general pension exclusion for certain retirement systems (IRAs and Keogh plans do not qualify). VA disability compensation is not taxed; Maryland adds nothing beyond the federal exclusion.

states.propertyTax: Maryland gives a COMPLETE exemption from state and local real property tax on the dwelling house and surrounding yard for veterans the VA has determined to be 100% service-connected, permanent and total, or 100% permanently unemployable (IU) — Md. Tax-Property Sec. 7-208. There is no income test, no home-value cap, and no age requirement. Unremarried surviving spouses of qualifying veterans retain the exemption, as do surviving spouses of service members who died in the line of duty. Retroactive refunds of taxes paid are available back to the effective date of the VA rating in many cases, which can be a five-figure check. Below 100%, there is NO statewide exemption — relief at 50-99% is entirely a county option, and several counties (including Anne Arundel, Harford, Prince George's, and others) have adopted supplemental credits typically in the 25-50% range for ratings of 50-74% and higher tiers above that. Check your specific county; the statewide picture is all-or-nothing at 100%.
states.education: The Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program (now often styled the Conroy-Cryor Scholarship) is the flagship: it covers tuition and mandatory fees at Maryland public institutions, with an award value pegged to the annual University System of Maryland resident undergraduate rate (cited at roughly $13,689/year in recent guidance), with no financial-need requirement. Eligible: children and spouses of service members who died or are 100% disabled from military service, POW/MIA dependents, AND — importantly — veterans who themselves have a service-connected disability of 25% or more and have exhausted or are ineligible for federal VA education benefits. That 25% self-eligibility threshold is one of the lowest in the country and is widely unknown. The Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts (VAIC) Scholarship covers up to 50% of tuition, fees, and room and board for OEF/OIF-era veterans and their families attending Maryland institutions. The Maryland National Guard State Tuition Assistance program covers up to 50% of tuition at Maryland public institutions. Veterans and dependents using federal benefits get in-state tuition.
states.employment: Maryland state hiring adds 10 preference points for eligible veterans and 12 points for veterans with a service-connected disability, spouses of disabled veterans who cannot work, and surviving spouses of deceased veterans. Maryland accepts military training and experience toward occupational licensure and has adopted expedited/temporary licensure and interstate compacts for military spouses. The Maryland Department of Labor provides priority of service and dedicated Disabled Veteran Outreach Program specialists. Maryland certifies veteran-owned small businesses for a state procurement preference.
states.vehicleRec: Free or reduced-fee Disabled Veteran, Purple Heart, Ex-POW, Medal of Honor, and Gold Star plates; veteran designation available on driver's licenses. Vehicles purchased with a VA automobile grant are exempt from the vehicle excise tax, and Maryland also exempts certain vessels from the vessel excise tax for qualifying disabled veterans. Recreation: free lifetime hunting licenses (and free fishing licenses) for veterans rated 100% service-connected disabled, and free entry to Maryland state parks and day-use areas for qualifying veterans. Confirm current Maryland Department of Natural Resources rules, which have been revised recently.
states.cash: No wartime service bonus is currently active. The Maryland Veterans Trust Fund provides need-based grants and no-interest loans to veterans and their families facing financial emergencies (housing, utilities, transportation, medical) — this is the state's main emergency cash program and is modest in size. No state supplement to VA pension. The retroactive real property tax refund available to newly-rated 100% P&T veterans functions as the largest one-time cash event in the Maryland system.
states.homesHealth: Maryland operates only ONE state veterans home — Charlotte Hall Veterans Home in Charlotte Hall (St. Mary's County), roughly 450 beds, offering domiciliary and skilled nursing care. This is thin for a state Maryland's size and waitlists can be long. Five state veterans cemeteries: Cheltenham, Crownsville, Garrison Forest (Owings Mills), Eastern Shore (Hurlock), and Rocky Gap (Flintstone), with no-cost burial for eligible veterans. No separate state veterans health insurance program; Maryland relies on the VA Maryland Health Care System.
other: Maryland is one of a shrinking number of states that still taxes military retirement above a low cap — a major disadvantage versus neighboring Virginia, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia.
The local piggyback income tax (2.25-3.20%) applies to the taxable portion of the pension and is easy to overlook when comparing states.
The Conroy scholarship's 25%-disability self-eligibility tier lets a veteran with a modest rating get their OWN tuition covered — almost nobody claims this.
Retroactive property tax refunds after a 100% P&T rating decision can be very large; file with the county and SDAT promptly.
Only one state veterans home statewide.
The agency was renamed the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families (MDVMF) — older references say Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs.

agency.name: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families (MDVMF)

states.topHack: If you have any service-connected rating of 25% or more and are not using the GI Bill, apply for the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship for YOURSELF — it is written as a survivor/dependent scholarship and virtually every veteran assumes they are ineligible, but the 25% disabled-veteran tier pays your own tuition and mandatory fees at a Maryland public university with no need test.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.headline: Massachusetts pairs a full military pension exemption and the country's only true municipal cash-welfare system for veterans (Chapter 115) with absolute civil service preference — but its property tax exemptions are trivially small fixed credits.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Massachusetts excludes U.S. military pension income from Part B taxable income entirely — no age condition, no dollar cap. Survivor Benefit Plan annuities are likewise not taxed.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxable for Massachusetts-domiciled residents (combat zone pay is excluded because it is excluded federally and Massachusetts starts from federal gross income). Nonresident service members stationed in Massachusetts are not taxed on military pay. Massachusetts National Guard members receive an exclusion for certain in-state duty pay.
incomeTax.notes: Flat 5% on most income, plus the 4% 'millionaires surtax' on income above roughly $1M (indexed). VA disability compensation is not taxed. The state also lets state employees buy back up to four years of active-duty service toward their pension; the 2024 HERO Act extended the enrollment window to ten years after starting state employment.

states.propertyTax: Massachusetts uses fixed-dollar EXEMPTIONS off the tax bill (M.G.L. c.59, Sec.5), not percentage reductions, and the base amounts are small: Clause 22 = $400 (10%+ service-connected disability, Purple Heart recipients, Gold Star parents, and their spouses/unremarried surviving spouses); Clause 22A = $750 (loss or loss of use of one hand, foot, or eye; Medal of Honor, Distinguished Service Cross, Navy Cross, or Air Force Cross recipients; former POWs); Clause 22B = $1,250 (loss or loss of use of both hands, both feet, or both eyes); Clause 22C = $1,500 (total service-connected disability with VA specially adapted housing owned and occupied); Clause 22E = $1,000 (100% service-connected disabled). Two clauses give a FULL exemption: Clause 22D for unremarried surviving spouses of service members who died from active-duty injuries/illness or are MIA presumed dead, and Clause 22F for paraplegic veterans and veterans rated 100% for service-connected blindness. Clause 22H (local option) gives a full exemption to surviving parents. The 2024 HERO Act added two local options: Clause 22I lets a municipality index exemption amounts to CPI, and Clause 22J lets a municipality DOUBLE all amounts (so Clause 22E becomes $2,000). Neither is state-reimbursed, so adoption is uneven — call your assessor and ask specifically whether your town accepted 22I/22J. Spouses and unremarried surviving spouses generally retain the veteran's clause.
states.education: Two main tracks. (1) The Massachusetts Categorical Tuition Waiver for veterans waives TUITION on a space-available basis at state universities, UMass campuses, and community colleges for veterans who are Massachusetts residents. The catch that trips everyone up: Massachusetts public colleges charge low statutory 'tuition' and high mandatory 'fees,' and the waiver covers tuition only — so the out-of-pocket cost can still be most of the bill. (2) The Massachusetts National Guard Education Assistance Program waives 100% of tuition AND fees at state institutions for drilling Guard members, and benefits are transferable to spouses and dependents under program rules — this is dramatically more valuable than the veteran waiver. The Public Service Scholarship covers children of service members killed in the line of duty. Veterans and dependents using federal benefits receive in-state tuition rates.
states.employment: Massachusetts grants ABSOLUTE veterans preference in civil service — not points. Disabled veterans are placed at the top of the eligible list ahead of all other applicants, followed by other veterans, followed by non-veterans, regardless of exam score ranking. This is among the strongest hiring preferences in the United States and applies to municipal police, fire, and many other civil service positions. Massachusetts also honors military occupational credentials toward licensure, expedites licensure for military spouses, and runs veteran-specific workforce programs through MassHire. Every city and town is required to have a Veterans' Service Officer (VSO) — Massachusetts uses a municipal, not county, VSO structure.
states.vehicleRec: Motor vehicle excise tax is waived on one vehicle for veterans who qualify for disabled veteran status, and sales tax exemptions apply to vehicles for certain disabled veterans. Plates: veteran plate has a $60 initial fee, $40 special plate fee, and $100 biennial renewal; motorcycle veteran plates are $20 initial and $40 annual; decoration-specific plates (Medal of Honor, Bronze Star, Silver Star, Purple Heart, Ex-POW) carry NO fees. Disabled Veteran plates confer handicapped parking privileges and free metered parking in many municipalities. Recreation: free hunting, fishing, and sporting licenses for veterans rated 100% disabled and for certain paraplegic veterans; Massachusetts offers free or discounted MassParks access for disabled veterans. Confirm current MassWildlife fee schedules.
states.cash: This is Massachusetts's differentiator. (1) CHAPTER 115 BENEFITS: a means-tested, municipally administered program — unique in the country — paying ongoing monthly cash for food, shelter, clothing, fuel, and reimbursing medical, dental, and (since the 2024 HERO Act) outpatient behavioral health costs for low-income veterans and their dependents. The municipality pays and the Commonwealth reimburses 75%. The HERO Act cut the dependent residency requirement from three years to one day, fixed the COLA cliff so a federal benefit increase no longer wipes out state aid, aligned the state definition of 'veteran' with the federal VA definition, and authorized direct deposit. (2) ANNUITY: $2,500 per year (raised from $2,000 by the HERO Act — $1,250 paid February 2025, then a single $2,500 annual check starting August 2025) to veterans rated 100% service-connected disabled, blind veterans, Gold Star parents, and unremarried surviving spouses of eligible veterans. (3) WELCOME HOME BONUS: a one-time state bonus for veterans of designated campaigns; I could not verify the current dollar tiers from a primary source — confirm with the Executive Office of Veterans Services before quoting an amount.
states.homesHealth: Two state veterans homes — the Massachusetts Veterans Home in Chelsea and the Massachusetts Veterans Home in Holyoke (both formerly 'Soldiers' Homes'). Holyoke was the site of one of the deadliest COVID-19 outbreaks in a U.S. long-term care facility in 2020 and has been rebuilt with a new facility and restructured oversight under the 2022 reform law and the 2024 HERO Act. Two state veterans cemeteries: Agawam and Winchendon, with no-cost interment for eligible veterans and spouses. Chapter 115 reimburses medical and dental costs for eligible low-income veterans, functioning as a limited state health benefit.
other: Chapter 115 is the single most distinctive veteran benefit in the country — real recurring cash plus medical reimbursement, administered by your own town's VSO.
Absolute (not points-based) civil service preference is a career-defining advantage for municipal police and fire jobs.
The HERO Act (August 2024) was the largest Massachusetts veterans law in decades; it also elevated veterans services to a cabinet-level Executive Office.
Property tax clauses are fixed dollar amounts as small as $400 — ask whether your town adopted Clause 22J to double them.
The veteran tuition waiver covers tuition but NOT mandatory fees, which is where most of the cost actually is.
Massachusetts uses municipal (city/town) Veterans' Service Officers, not county VSOs — every municipality must have one.

agency.name: Massachusetts Executive Office of Veterans Services (EOVS)

states.topHack: Walk into your city or town hall and file for Chapter 115 with the municipal Veterans' Service Officer. It is means-tested but the income and asset ceilings are far more forgiving than people assume, it pays monthly cash plus medical and dental reimbursement, and the 2024 HERO Act removed the COLA cliff that used to kick veterans off when their VA check went up.

states.name: Michigan
states.headline: Michigan taxes neither active-duty pay nor military retirement, and a 100% P&T rating wipes out your entire property tax bill with no home-value cap and — since 2025 — no annual refiling.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Michigan excludes military retirement benefits from taxable income under MCL 206.30; there is no cap and no age condition. Survivor Benefit Plan payments are likewise excluded.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Michigan subtracts military compensation (active duty, National Guard, and Reserve pay) from taxable income for Michigan residents. Nonresident service members stationed in Michigan are not taxed on military pay.
incomeTax.notes: Flat 4.25% individual rate. Michigan cities may levy a separate local income tax (Detroit, Grand Rapids, etc.), and the state military subtraction does not automatically exempt you from every city tax — check the specific city ordinance. VA disability compensation is not taxed; Michigan adds nothing beyond the federal exclusion.

states.propertyTax: Michigan grants a COMPLETE exemption from all property taxes on the homestead under MCL 211.7b — no dollar cap, no income test, no home-value ceiling. Eligibility requires Michigan residency, ownership and occupancy of the property as a homestead, and one of: (a) VA determination of permanent and total disability from military service and entitlement to benefits at the 100% rate, (b) receipt of VA pecuniary assistance for specially adapted housing, or (c) a VA rating of individually unemployable (IU). The disability must be service-connected — do not rely on third-party summaries that claim any total disability qualifies. An unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran who was eligible at the time of death retains the exemption. Filed on Michigan Department of Treasury Form 5107 with the local assessing unit or Board of Review. Critically, beginning January 1, 2025, once the exemption is granted it REMAINS IN EFFECT WITHOUT ANNUAL REAPPLICATION — previously Michigan required veterans to refile every single year and thousands lost the benefit by missing a deadline. There is no partial exemption or sliding scale below 100%/IU, and no separate 65+, Purple Heart, POW, or Medal of Honor exemption. Note: the legislature has repeatedly debated converting this exemption into a state-funded credit to relieve local governments; as of September 2026 the exemption structure remains in force, but this is the Michigan provision most likely to change.
states.education: Children of Veterans Tuition Grant (CVTG): tuition assistance at Michigan public degree-granting colleges and universities for children age 16-26 of Michigan veterans who died of a service-connected cause, are rated 100% permanently and totally service-connected disabled, or are totally disabled from service and died from any cause; award is capped per academic year (commonly cited at up to $2,800/year for up to four years — verify the current maximum with the Michigan Student Aid office, as the cap has been adjusted). The Michigan National Guard State Tuition Assistance Program (MINGSTAP) is far richer, paying up to roughly $7,500 per year toward tuition for drilling Guard members at Michigan institutions (confirm the current annual cap). Michigan grants in-state tuition to veterans and dependents using federal VA education benefits, and several public universities layer on their own veteran waivers.
states.employment: Michigan Civil Service grants veterans preference in state government hiring (point preference generally 5 points for veterans and up to 10 for service-connected disabled veterans; confirm the current schedule with the Michigan Civil Service Commission). Michigan Works! centers provide priority of service and dedicated veteran employment representatives. Michigan accepts military training and occupational specialties toward licensure in a wide range of fields and offers expedited/temporary licensure for military spouses. The Michigan Veterans Affairs Agency runs employer outreach and a Veteran-Friendly Employer certification program.
states.vehicleRec: Disabled Veteran license plates are issued at no charge to qualifying veterans, and veterans rated 100% service-connected disabled are exempt from vehicle registration fees. Veteran designation is available on Michigan driver's licenses and state IDs. Recreation: FREE hunting and fishing licenses for veterans rated 100% service-connected disabled, and a free Recreation Passport (the state park entry sticker attached to vehicle registration) for 100% disabled veterans, giving free entry to all Michigan state parks and recreation areas. Reduced-fee licenses apply for certain lower-rated disabled veterans — check Michigan DNR's current fee schedule.
states.cash: The Michigan Veterans Trust Fund (MVTF) is the standout: emergency grants — not loans, never repaid — to wartime-era veterans and their families facing a temporary financial emergency, covering rent and mortgage arrears, utilities, medical and dental bills, vehicle repair, and similar urgent needs. Applications go through county-level MVTF committees and county Veterans Service Officers, and the program is funded by a dedicated state trust. There is no active wartime service bonus and no state supplement to VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Three Michigan Veteran Homes: Grand Rapids, Chesterfield Township, and Marquette (D.J. Jacobetti), providing skilled nursing and domiciliary care on income-based subsidized rates. Michigan has NO state-operated veterans cemetery — burial is handled through the federal Great Lakes National Cemetery in Holly and Fort Custer National Cemetery in Augusta. No separate state veterans health insurance program.
other: Full property tax exemption with no home-value cap is enormously valuable in high-assessment counties like Oakland and Washtenaw.
As of January 1, 2025 the exemption no longer requires annual reapplication — the single biggest administrative improvement in years.
Michigan exempts BOTH active-duty pay and retirement pay, which is rarer than exempting retirement alone.
Michigan Veterans Trust Fund grants are real, non-repayable cash and are badly under-used.
No state veterans cemetery — an unusual gap for a state this size.
Watch for legislation converting the property tax exemption into a credit; it has been introduced repeatedly.
Michigan uses county Veterans Service Officers (and MVTF county committees) as the delivery system.
states.topHack: If your rating was recently increased to 100% P&T or IU, file Form 5107 with your assessor immediately and ask the Board of Review for relief back to the effective date of the rating — Michigan Boards of Review can grant the exemption for the current and prior years, and since 2025 you never have to refile again.

states.name: Minnesota
states.headline: Minnesota fully subtracts military pensions and active-duty pay with no cap, excludes up to $300,000 of home market value at 100% P&T, and runs the deepest county VSO and state veterans home network in the region — but every other dollar is taxed hard.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt with no dollar cap. Minn. Stat. 290.0132 subd. 21 allows a subtraction for all qualifying military retirement pay included in federal taxable income — active component retired pay (10 U.S.C. 1401-1414), Reserve component retired pay (10 U.S.C. 12733), Survivor Benefit Plan payments including court-ordered payments to a former spouse, and the portion of a military pension received through a divorce settlement. Claimed on Schedule M1M. IMPORTANT EXCLUSION: pensions received exclusively from service as a dual-status technician do NOT qualify.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Minnesota allows a subtraction for federal active-duty military pay and for Minnesota National Guard and Reserve pay received for active service, training, and state active duty.
incomeTax.notes: Minnesota's graduated rates top out at 9.85%, so exempting military income is valuable, but spousal wages, second-career income, and investment income are taxed steeply. Separately, the Credit for Past Military Service is a nonrefundable credit of up to $750 for veterans with Minnesota AGI under $37,500 who separated before year-end and either served 20+ years, are rated 100% service-connected disabled, or were honorably discharged and receive a military pension. You may NOT claim both the credit and the military pension subtraction — the subtraction generally wins above about $37,500 of federal AGI. VA disability compensation is not taxed.

states.propertyTax: Minnesota uses a homestead MARKET VALUE EXCLUSION rather than an exemption: $150,000 of estimated market value is excluded for a veteran with a service-connected disability rating of 70% or more, and $300,000 is excluded for a veteran rated 100% permanent and total. Surviving spouses receive the $300,000 exclusion if the veteran was rated 100% P&T, was receiving Dependency and Indemnity Compensation, or died during active service. The exclusion continues until the spouse remarries, transfers, or disposes of the property, and a surviving spouse may make a ONE-TIME transfer of the exclusion to a replacement property if the new property's estimated market value does not exceed the original, they apply by December 31, and they have not received the exclusion on another property. The property must already be classified as homestead. Application deadline is December 31 for taxes payable the following year. Note this is an exclusion of value, not a full exemption — a 100% P&T veteran in a $500,000 home still pays tax on $200,000. Qualifying primary family caregivers of a disabled veteran can also hold the exclusion. There is no separate 65+, Purple Heart, POW, or Medal of Honor property benefit.
states.education: The Minnesota GI Bill provides state education benefits for higher education, on-the-job training, apprenticeships, and license/certification costs for eligible veterans and service members — official state summaries cite up to $15,000 in total benefits, though the program has historically been structured as roughly $3,000 per fiscal year with a $10,000 lifetime cap for higher education; verify the current per-year and lifetime maximums with MDVA, as they were raised in recent sessions. The Surviving Spouse and Dependent Education Benefit is the richest: FREE TUITION at any Minnesota public postsecondary institution through completion of a bachelor's degree, plus $750 per year toward fees, books, and room and board, for spouses and dependents of service members who died on active duty or are rated 100% permanently and totally disabled. Minnesota Veteran Education Assistance provides a one-time $750 grant when federal GI Bill benefits are exhausted. The Minnesota National Guard State Tuition Reimbursement program covers up to 100% of tuition for drilling Guard members.
states.employment: Minnesota state hiring adds veterans preference points — commonly 5 points for non-disabled veterans, 10 for service-connected disabled veterans, and official summaries cite up to 15 points for veterans rated 50% or higher; confirm the current point schedule with Minnesota Management and Budget. Minnesota's Veterans Preference Act (Minn. Stat. 197.46) also gives veterans in public employment strong statutory job protection — a covered veteran cannot be removed from a public position except for incompetency or misconduct after notice and a hearing, which is one of the strongest public-sector job protections in the country.
