Certified veteran-owned small businesses get a 6% procurement preference (official summaries cite up to 12% for service-disabled veteran-owned; verify current percentages). Private employers may voluntarily adopt a veterans preference without violating state anti-discrimination law.
states.vehicleRec: Free veteran designation on driver's licenses; 24 distinctive veteran plate designs; Medal of Honor plates issued free. Veterans rated 100% service-connected disabled are exempt from vehicle registration tax, title fees, and motor vehicle sales tax; active-duty service members get a registration tax exemption. Recreation: free small game and deer licenses plus fishing privileges for veterans rated 100% service-connected disabled; free annual state park permits for service members and disabled veterans. Minnesota also runs the Veterans Campground on Big Marine Lake — a veterans-only campground with cabins, RV sites, boating, and fishing, operated by a veterans nonprofit.
states.cash: The State Soldiers Assistance Program (SSAP), administered by MDVA through county VSOs, provides subsistence grants for veterans in temporary financial hardship plus dedicated dental, optical, and hearing assistance grants — recurring, needs-based state cash. Minnesota Support Our Troops grants provide direct financial assistance to deployed service members' families. There is no active wartime service bonus. The Credit for Past Military Service (up to $750, AGI under $37,500) functions as a small refundable-style benefit for low-income veteran retirees.
states.homesHealth: Minnesota operates one of the largest state veterans home systems in the country — eight Minnesota Veterans Homes at Minneapolis, Hastings, Luverne, Silver Bay, Fergus Falls, Preston, Bemidji, and Montevideo (the last three opened in recent years), providing skilled nursing, domiciliary, and memory care. State veterans cemeteries operate at Little Falls, Preston, Duluth, and Redwood Falls, with no-cost interment for eligible veterans and nominal fees for spouses. County Veterans Service Officers are statutorily required in all 87 counties.
other: Full, uncapped subtraction of BOTH military retirement and active-duty pay against rates reaching 9.85% is worth more in Minnesota than the same exemption in a flat-tax state.
Dual-status technician pensions are specifically carved OUT of the pension subtraction — a trap for retired Guard technicians.
The Veterans Preference Act gives near-tenure job protection in Minnesota public employment, not just hiring points.
You must choose between the pension subtraction and the $750 Credit for Past Military Service — run both.
Eight state veterans homes and four state cemeteries; county VSOs in all 87 counties.
The $300,000 exclusion is of market value, not a full exemption — high-value homes still owe tax.
states.topHack: Get the 70% rating, not just the 100% one — Minnesota is one of very few states where a 70% service-connected rating alone (no P&T, no unemployability) unlocks a $150,000 market value exclusion on your homestead, and the December 31 application deadline is the only thing standing between you and it.

states.name: Mississippi
states.headline: Mississippi fully exempts military retirement, zeroes out homestead property tax for 100% disabled veterans AND for any veteran age 90 or older, and is phasing its income tax toward elimination — but there is almost no state cash assistance or veteran tuition waiver.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Mississippi does not tax military retired pay at all, regardless of age, years of service, or amount. Survivor Benefit Plan payments are likewise exempt.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxable for Mississippi-domiciled residents, with important carve-outs: combat zone pay is exempt, and National Guard and Reserve members may exclude up to $15,000 annually of pay for inactive duty training, active duty training, and state active duty. A nonresident spouse of a service member stationed in Mississippi is exempt on Mississippi earnings under MSRRA.
incomeTax.notes: Mississippi has a flat individual rate on income above the exempt threshold, scheduled to step down toward roughly 4.0% for 2026 and lower thereafter under the 2025 tax elimination law (HB 1). Verify the exact 2026 rate with the Mississippi Department of Revenue before relying on it. VA disability compensation is not taxed. Mississippi also exempts Social Security and qualified retirement income generally.

states.propertyTax: Mississippi grants a TOTAL exemption from all ad valorem taxes on homestead property for honorably discharged veterans with a 100% service-connected total disability rating from the VA, and for their unremarried surviving spouses (Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 27-33-67, Sec. 27-33-75). There is no home-value cap and no income test. Mississippi also extends the total homestead exemption to veterans age 90 and older and to surviving spouses of service members killed on active duty — the age-90 provision is genuinely unusual and exists in almost no other state. Below 100%, veterans fall back on the general Mississippi homestead exemption, which exempts the first $7,500 of assessed value (or the full amount for qualifying homeowners age 65+ or totally disabled, up to a statutory cap). There is no sliding scale by rating percentage and no separate Purple Heart, POW, or Medal of Honor property exemption. Separately, veterans age 65+, blind, deaf, or with documented 50% disability and annual income of $900 or less are exempt from state privilege tax on specified businesses (Sec. 27-15-227) — an antiquated but still-on-the-books provision.
states.education: Mississippi has NO broad tuition waiver for veterans or their dependents, which is the state's weakest category. What exists: the Mississippi State Educational Assistance Program (SEAP) pays up to $10,000 per year toward tuition for Mississippi National Guard members attending state institutions; the Children of POW/MIA scholarship provides eight semesters of cost-free education at state institutions for dependents of prisoners of war and missing-in-action service members (Sec. 37-108-1); and Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 37-103-25 grants IN-STATE TUITION to veterans and anyone using Title 38 education benefits regardless of residency, which is a real saving at Ole Miss and Mississippi State. Military families are covered by the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children (MIC3). Honorary high school diplomas are available to WWII, Korean Conflict, and Vietnam-era veterans who left school for service (Sec. 37-16-13).
states.employment: Mississippi state hiring adds 4 preference points for veterans and 8 points for veterans with a 30% or greater service-connected disability — lower than most states. State employees receive 15 days of paid military leave annually. Reserve component members have statutory reemployment rights to their previous or a similar position with equivalent status, pay, and seniority (Sec. 33-1-19). Mississippi PERS grants military service credit toward state retirement. Since SB 2419 (2013), Mississippi provides expedited licensure for service members and military spouses relocating on active-duty transfer across teaching, accounting, engineering, medicine, nursing, and other licensed fields. Mississippi recognizes military training toward occupational credentials.
states.vehicleRec: Mississippi issues 71 specialty military and veteran license plates, including Purple Heart, Disabled Veteran, Medal of Honor, Ex-POW, and Gold Star Family; many carry property and privilege tax exemptions. Veterans with a 100% permanent service-connected disability may purchase annual motor vehicle plates for $1, and motorcycle plates on the same terms (Sec. 27-19-53). Driver's licenses carry a 'VETERAN' designation. Recreation: veterans with a total service-connected disability need NO hunting or fishing license at all — they simply carry proof of age, residency, and disability status (Sec. 49-7-5). Nonresident active-duty members may buy resident-priced licenses, and residents home on leave from an out-of-state assignment need no license. Mississippi state parks give a 15% discount off camping and lodging rates to veterans and active-duty members. Honorably retired or discharged veterans with firearms training are exempt from the concealed-carry permit requirement by affidavit, and service-connected disabled veterans and active-duty personnel are exempt from permit fees (Sec. 45-9-101, Sec. 97-37-7).
states.cash: Mississippi has no wartime service bonus, no state-funded emergency financial assistance fund of consequence, and no state supplement to VA pension. This is the state's biggest gap. What Mississippi does provide free: birth, death, marriage, and divorce records furnished at no cost when needed for dependency, disability, or survivor benefit claims, and free recording of discharge papers by county clerks with certified copies provided (Sec. 35-3-9, 35-3-11, 35-3-13, 41-57-25).
states.homesHealth: Five state veterans homes offering long-term skilled nursing care: Martha Jo Leslie Home in Kosciusko (662-289-7044), Oxford (662-236-7641), General Hilton R. Vance Home in Jackson (601-353-6142), Collins (601-765-0403), and the Tradition facility in Biloxi (228-295-7444). Two state veterans memorial cemeteries: Newton (601-683-2959) and Kilmichael (662-262-4232), providing burial with perpetual care and military honors. Mississippi Veterans Affairs employs veterans benefits specialists who provide free claims counseling; service is delivered through MVA field offices and county service officers.
other: Total homestead exemption at age 90+ regardless of disability rating is close to unique nationally.
A totally disabled veteran needs no hunting or fishing license at all — not a free license, no license required.
Concealed-carry permit exemption by affidavit for honorably discharged veterans with firearms training.
No general veteran or dependent tuition waiver — the biggest hole in Mississippi's package.
No state emergency cash assistance fund.
Only 4 hiring preference points (8 at 30%+ disability), well below the 5/10 national norm.
states.topHack: If you are a 100% service-connected disabled Mississippi resident, stop buying hunting and fishing licenses entirely — Sec. 49-7-5 exempts you from the license requirement itself, and pair that with the $1 annual license plate under Sec. 27-19-53, which almost no county tax collector volunteers.

states.name: Missouri
states.headline: Missouri exempts both military retirement and active-duty pay and charges combat veterans $50 a credit hour at public colleges, but it is one of the only states in this group with NO property tax exemption for disabled veterans at all.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Missouri allows a 100% deduction of military retirement benefits included in federal adjusted gross income (the phase-in completed in 2016). Survivor Benefit Plan payments are also deductible.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Missouri allows a 100% deduction for active-duty military pay, and separately for National Guard and Reserve inactive duty and annual training pay, for Missouri residents. Nonresident service members stationed in Missouri are not taxed on military pay.
incomeTax.notes: Missouri's top individual rate has been stepping down (4.7% for 2025, with further triggered reductions scheduled), and a 2025 law exempts long-term capital gains for individuals. Missouri does NOT tax Social Security for most filers. VA disability compensation is not taxed; Missouri adds nothing beyond the federal exclusion.

states.propertyTax: Missouri provides NO property tax exemption or assessed-value reduction for disabled veterans — this is the single biggest weakness in the state's package and it surprises veterans relocating from Texas, Oklahoma, or Michigan. The only relief is the Missouri Property Tax Credit (the 'circuit breaker'), a refundable income-tax credit of up to $1,100 for homeowners and up to $750 for renters, based on real estate taxes or rent paid and total household income (taxable and nontaxable). Veterans who are 100% disabled AS A RESULT OF MILITARY SERVICE qualify regardless of age — everyone else must be 65+ or disabled. Household income limits apply and are low enough that many retired veterans with a full VA award plus a pension are phased out; confirm the current-year income thresholds with the Missouri Department of Revenue, since they were adjusted in recent sessions. Renters in facilities that pay no property tax are ineligible. Separately, Missouri's 2023 senior real property tax credit (the 'assessment freeze' for homeowners 65+) is adopted county by county and is not veteran-specific. There is no sliding scale by rating, no surviving-spouse exemption, and no Purple Heart/POW/Medal of Honor property benefit.
states.education: The Missouri Returning Heroes Education Act is the standout: Missouri public colleges and universities may charge a combat veteran no more than $50 PER CREDIT HOUR for an undergraduate degree — roughly $1,500 for a full 30-credit year at a four-year public university, which undercuts even in-state tuition dramatically and can be used after the GI Bill runs out. Eligibility requires service in armed combat after September 11, 2001, an honorable discharge, Missouri residency, and maintenance of a 2.5 GPA. The Wartime Veteran's Survivors Grant provides up to $2,000 per semester toward room and board (plus tuition/fees coverage) for children and spouses of service members who died or became at least 80% disabled as a result of combat action or service-connected injury since September 11, 2001 — but it is capped at roughly 25 recipients statewide per year, so apply early. The Missouri National Guard State Tuition Assistance program covers tuition for drilling Guard members at Missouri institutions. Veterans and dependents using federal benefits receive in-state tuition.
states.employment: Missouri grants veterans preference in state hiring — customarily 5 points for eligible veterans and 10 points for service-connected disabled veterans, plus a guaranteed interview for qualified former Missouri National Guard members. Show-Me Heroes is the flagship employer program: it reimburses participating employers roughly 50% of wages during an on-the-job training period for hiring eligible veterans and Guard/Reserve members, and certifies Show-Me Heroes employers. Missouri Job Centers provide priority of service. Missouri accepts military training toward occupational licensure and provides expedited and temporary licensure for military spouses under its licensing reciprocity statutes.
states.vehicleRec: Missouri issues no-fee Disabled Veteran, Purple Heart, Medal of Honor, Ex-POW, and Gold Star plates, plus a wide range of branch and campaign specialty plates; veteran designation is available on driver's licenses. Disabled veterans rated 100% service-connected receive FREE hunting and fishing permits from the Missouri Department of Conservation. All service members and veterans receive a $2 per night discount on camping fees year-round at Missouri State Parks (day-use entry at Missouri state parks is free to everyone). There is no statewide free vehicle registration for disabled veterans and no general free-license benefit.
states.cash: Missouri has no active wartime service bonus and no state supplement to VA pension. The Missouri Property Tax Credit (up to $1,100) is the only broad cash-back mechanism, and it is income-limited. Missouri does maintain the Veterans Commission Capital Improvement Trust Fund, financed substantially by riverboat gaming admission fees, which funds the veterans homes and cemeteries system — a distinctive funding model, but it pays for facilities, not individual grants. Limited emergency assistance is available through Missouri Veterans Commission service officers and partner organizations.
states.homesHealth: Seven Missouri Veterans Homes providing skilled nursing care: Cameron, Cape Girardeau, Mexico, Mount Vernon, St. James, St. Louis, and Warrensburg. Five Missouri State Veterans Cemeteries: Higginsville, Springfield, Bloomfield, Jacksonville, and Fort Leonard Wood, offering no-cost interment for eligible veterans. The Missouri Veterans Commission provides free claims assistance through trained state veterans service officers statewide. No separate state veterans health insurance program.
other: No disabled veteran property tax exemption whatsoever — the biggest single gap among the 17 states reviewed.
$50-per-credit-hour tuition for post-9/11 combat veterans is one of the cheapest paths to a public bachelor's degree in the country.
Both active-duty pay and military retirement are fully deducted.
The Wartime Veteran's Survivors Grant is capped at about 25 students per year statewide — effectively first-come, first-served.
Veterans homes and cemeteries are funded largely by casino admission fees rather than general revenue.
Missouri uses state-employed Veterans Service Officers through the Missouri Veterans Commission rather than a county VSO system.

agency.name: Missouri Veterans Commission (MVC), Department of Public Safety

states.topHack: Finish your degree under the Returning Heroes Education Act AFTER your GI Bill is exhausted — at a capped $50 per credit hour a Missouri public university costs about $1,500 a year, so save the Post-9/11 GI Bill's housing allowance for a graduate program or transfer it to a dependent.

states.name: Montana
states.headline: Montana is the weakest state in this group: military retirement gets only a partial, five-year, wage-linked exemption, and the disabled veteran property benefit is strictly income-tested and shuts off entirely above roughly $64,000-$74,000 of income.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Only PARTIALLY exempt, and on unusual terms. Under Sec. 15-30-2120(3)(n), MCA, an eligible retired service member may exempt the LESSER of (a) their Montana source wage income or (b) 50% of their military pension or retirement income — for up to FIVE CONSECUTIVE YEARS only. The provision is designed to attract working-age military retirees who take Montana jobs: if you retire to Montana and do not work, your Montana source wage income is zero and the exemption is worth nothing. The 2025 Legislature removed the original December 31, 2033 termination date via Senate Bill 93, making the provision permanent. In tax year 2024 roughly 1,711 Montana residents claimed about $24.8 million of exempt income at a cost of $25.5 million to the state.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Montana exempts the active-duty salary of residents serving in the armed forces, and Montana National Guard members receive an exemption for certain state and federal duty pay. Nonresident service members stationed in Montana are not taxed on military pay. Verify the current active-duty provision with the Montana Department of Revenue, as Montana's individual income tax was restructured in 2024.
incomeTax.notes: Montana's restructured individual income tax tops out near 5.9%. There is no state sales tax, which partially offsets the weak retirement treatment. VA disability compensation is not taxed. Montana also offers a Veteran Apprenticeship tax credit to EMPLOYERS: $1,500 per registered veteran apprentice (double the $750 non-veteran credit), claimable for up to five years per apprentice, non-refundable and not carried forward (Sec. 15-30-2357, 15-31-173, 39-6-109, MCA).

states.propertyTax: The Montana Disabled Veteran Assistance Program (MDV), Sec. 15-6-311 MCA, reduces property tax on a primary residence by 50% to 100% depending on income — it is NOT a flat exemption. You must be rated 100% service-connected disabled and paid at that rate (or individually unemployable at the 100% rate), own or be under contract to purchase the residence, and occupy it at least seven months a year. Unmarried surviving spouses qualify if the veteran died on active duty, died from a service-connected disability, or was rated 100% at death. For tax year 2027 the income ceilings are: single filers up to $64,551, married/head of household up to $74,482, and unmarried surviving spouses up to $56,276 — above those figures you get NOTHING. Within each bracket the reduction slides: a single filer earning under $49,654 gets the full 100% reduction, while one earning $59,585-$64,551 gets only 50%. Income limits are inflation-adjusted annually; the 2026 figures are slightly lower than the 2027 figures shown. Application deadline is April 15. In 2025, 3,612 participants received about $6.9 million in total benefit ($1.2 million of state revenue loss plus $5.7 million shifted onto other local taxpayers). Separately, Sec. 15-6-203 MCA exempts veterans organization clubhouses and grounds used for educational or charitable purposes. There is no benefit below a 100% rating, no benefit for Purple Heart/POW/Medal of Honor recipients as such, and no separate 65+ veteran exemption.
states.education: Montana's principal veteran education benefit is the tuition waiver at Montana University System institutions (Sec. 20-25-421, MCA) for honorably discharged veterans who served during a qualifying wartime period, are Montana residents, and have exhausted or are ineligible for federal VA education benefits — it waives undergraduate TUITION but not fees, and the exhaustion requirement means most post-9/11 veterans cannot use it until the GI Bill is gone. A companion waiver covers children of Montana service members who were killed in action, died of service-connected causes, or are POW/MIA. The Montana National Guard State Tuition Assistance / STEP program covers tuition for drilling Guard members. Veterans and dependents using federal VA education benefits receive in-state tuition classification immediately. Montana has no broad dependent tuition waiver comparable to Nebraska's or Maine's.
states.employment: Montana grants veterans preference in public employment under Title 39, Chapter 29, MCA — generally 5 percentage points added for eligible veterans and 10 points for disabled veterans in state, county, and municipal hiring, with preference also applying to reduction-in-force retention. Montana accepts military education, training, and experience toward occupational licensure and provides expedited licensure and temporary practice permits for military spouses. The $1,500 employer tax credit for hiring registered veteran apprentices is unusual and effective. Job Service Montana provides priority of service and veteran employment representatives.
states.vehicleRec: Montana issues reduced-fee and no-fee plates: veterans rated 100% disabled, former POWs, Purple Heart recipients, and Medal of Honor recipients receive plates with fees waived or substantially reduced, and disabled veterans are exempt from certain registration and license fees. Veteran designation is available on Montana driver's licenses. Recreation: Montana residents effectively prepay state park access through a light vehicle registration fee, so park entry is free to resident vehicles; disabled veterans receive reduced-fee resident hunting and fishing licenses, and there are dedicated disabled-hunter permits and season accommodations. Confirm current Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks fee schedules for the disabled veteran license discount, which is set by rule rather than statute.
states.cash: Montana has no wartime service bonus, no state emergency financial assistance fund for veterans of any size, and no state supplement to VA pension. This is a genuine void. The only cash-equivalent state programs are the MDV property tax reduction and the employer apprenticeship credit. Emergency help is routed through county and tribal Veterans Service Officers to federal and nonprofit resources.
states.homesHealth: Three state veterans homes: the Montana Veterans Home in Columbia Falls, the Eastern Montana Veterans Home in Glendive, and the Southwest Montana Veterans Home in Butte. Three Montana State Veterans Cemeteries: Fort Harrison (near Helena), Miles City, and Missoula, offering no-cost interment for eligible veterans. Montana relies on the VA Montana Health Care System (Fort Harrison) plus a large network of community-based outpatient clinics for a very rural population; there is no state veterans health program.
other: The military retirement exemption is worthless to a retiree with no Montana wage income — it is explicitly an employment-attraction incentive, not a retiree benefit.
SB 93 (2025) made that exemption permanent by deleting its 2033 sunset.
The MDV property benefit is hard income-tested and produces a cliff: cross roughly $64,551 as a single filer and you lose 100% of it.
No state sales tax, which materially offsets the weak income and property treatment for day-to-day costs.
The veteran tuition waiver requires you to have EXHAUSTED federal education benefits first.
Montana uses county and tribal Veterans Service Officers under the Montana Veterans Affairs Division.
$1,500 employer credit per registered veteran apprentice is one of the better veteran-hiring incentives in the country.

agency.name: Montana Veterans Affairs Division (MVAD), Department of Military Affairs

states.topHack: Time your move. The Sec. 15-30-2120(3)(n) exemption only pays if you have Montana WAGE income, and it runs for exactly five consecutive years — so start the clock the year you take a Montana job, not the year you arrive, because a year spent not working burns one of the five for nothing.

states.name: Nebraska
states.headline: Nebraska is the strongest package in this group: 100% of military retirement is untaxed, a 100% P&T rating means a total homestead exemption with no income or home-value cap, dependents get a full tuition waiver, and a new vehicle tax exemption started January 1, 2026.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2022, Nebraska allows an exclusion of 100% of military retirement benefits from Nebraska taxable income. No application, no election, no age or dollar cap — the prior 40%/15% election regime was repealed.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxable for Nebraska-domiciled residents (combat zone pay is excluded because it is federally excluded). Nonresident service members stationed in Nebraska are not taxed on military pay, and a nonresident military spouse is protected under MSRRA.
incomeTax.notes: Nebraska is phasing its top individual rate down to 3.99% by 2027 under LB 754 (roughly 5.2% for 2025 and 4.55% for 2026 — verify the exact 2026 rate with the Nebraska Department of Revenue). Social Security benefits are now fully exempt. VA disability compensation is not taxed. NEW for 2026: effective January 1, 2026, disabled and/or blind veterans receive an exemption from the Motor Vehicle Tax and Motor Vehicle Fee on ONE vehicle used for personal transportation; sales tax and local wheel taxes still apply.

states.propertyTax: Nebraska's homestead exemption is delivered as a percentage of the home's taxable value and is administered through categories. Category 4V: veterans rated 100% permanently service-connected disabled or holding a 100% Individual Unemployability (IU) rating effective on or before January 1 of the application year receive a 100% EXEMPTION with NO income limit and NO home-value limit — this is unusual; most states with a full exemption still cap the value or means-test it. Category 4S: the unremarried surviving spouse, or a surviving spouse who remarried after attaining age 57, receives the same 100% exemption with no income or value limits. Category 5: paraplegic and multiple-amputee veterans whose homestead was substantially contributed to by the VA (specially adapted housing), and their surviving spouses, also receive a 100% exemption with no income or value limits. Veterans who are wartime-era but not 100% rated fall back on the income-tested general categories (age 65+ or disabled), where a sliding percentage applies and both household income and home value caps bite. You must own and occupy the homestead from January 1 through August 15, file Form 458 annually with the county assessor/treasurer, and file the VA certification with the first application and again in years ending in 0 or 5. The annual filing deadline is June 30 — miss it and you lose the year.
states.education: The Nebraska Waiver of Tuition is a genuine 100% TUITION WAIVER at the University of Nebraska campuses, the Nebraska state colleges, and Nebraska community colleges for the spouse and children of a veteran who died of a service-connected disability, is rated permanently and totally disabled from service-connected causes, died while on active duty, or is classified POW/MIA. Applications are filed with the Nebraska Department of Veterans' Affairs, which certifies eligibility to the institution. For drilling Guard members, the Nebraska National Guard Tuition Assistance program credits 75% of tuition at state educational institutions (50% for graduate degrees). Veterans and dependents using federal VA benefits receive resident tuition rates. Nebraska does not offer a general tuition waiver for the veteran's own undergraduate study outside of Guard service.
states.employment: Nebraska adds 5% preference to a veteran's passing examination score for state and political subdivision positions, with an ADDITIONAL 5% (total 10%) for veterans with a service-connected disability; spouses of disabled veterans and unremarried surviving spouses of deceased veterans also qualify. Preference applies in retention during reductions in force as well as in hiring. Nebraska enforces USERRA reemployment rights. The state accepts military training toward occupational licensure and provides expedited and provisional licensure for military spouses. Nebraska Department of Labor offices provide priority of service and veteran employment representatives.
states.vehicleRec: Nebraska issues specialty plates at no additional cost, including Purple Heart, Disabled American Veteran, Military Honor, Ex-POW, Gold Star Family, and branch-specific plates, plus a free 'Veteran' designation on driver's licenses. NEW as of January 1, 2026: disabled and/or blind veterans are exempt from the Motor Vehicle Tax and Motor Vehicle Fee on one personal vehicle. Recreation: veterans rated 50% or more service-connected disabled receive FREE LIFETIME hunting and fishing permits and free state park entry permits — the 50% threshold is low and the benefit is lifetime. Veterans over age 64 pay only $5 annually for hunting and fishing privileges. Nebraska Game and Parks administers both.
states.cash: The Nebraska Veterans Aid Fund (NVAF) is a real emergency cash program: grants — not loans — to veterans and their dependents for food, fuel, shelter, transportation, funeral expenses, and medical, dental, optical, and hearing costs during a temporary emergency. It is administered through county veterans service officers and the statewide veterans service organizations, funded by a dedicated state fund. Per-category limits apply. There is no active wartime service bonus and no state supplement to VA pension.
states.homesHealth: Four Nebraska Veterans' Homes offering domiciliary, intermediate, and skilled nursing care: the Eastern Nebraska Veterans' Home (Bellevue), the Central Nebraska Veterans' Home (Kearney), the Norfolk Veterans' Home (Norfolk), and the Western Nebraska Veterans' Home (Scottsbluff). One state cemetery, the Nebraska Veterans Cemetery at Alliance, with free burial for eligible veterans and family members. Nebraska also operates the Nebraska Veteran Registry and works through county VSOs for claims assistance; there is no separate state veterans health insurance program.
other: Category 4V's total exemption with NO income cap AND NO home-value cap is rarer than a 'full exemption' headline suggests — many states cap one or both.
A surviving spouse who remarries AFTER age 57 keeps the exemption — an unusually forgiving remarriage rule.
New motor vehicle tax and fee exemption for disabled/blind veterans effective January 1, 2026.
Free LIFETIME hunting, fishing, and park permits at only a 50% rating.
June 30 is the hard homestead filing deadline and it is annual — the single most common way Nebraska veterans lose the benefit.
Nebraska Veterans Aid Fund grants never have to be repaid.
Nebraska uses county Veterans Service Officers.
states.topHack: File Form 458 with the VA certification every single year by June 30 even though the exemption itself is permanent — Nebraska requires an ANNUAL homestead application, and veterans who assume a granted 100% exemption rolls over automatically are the ones who get a full tax bill in December.

states.name: Nevada
states.headline: No state income tax at all is the whole story in Nevada — the property tax exemption is modest, indexed annually, and its best feature is that you can spend it on vehicle registration instead of your house.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Not taxed — Nevada has no individual income tax of any kind.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Not taxed — Nevada has no individual income tax of any kind.
incomeTax.notes: Nevada levies no individual income tax, so military retirement, active-duty pay, Thrift Savings Plan distributions, SBP, IRA and 401(k) withdrawals, and Social Security are all free of state tax. This is worth more to a high-income retiree than any targeted veteran exemption in a taxing state. Nevada makes up revenue through high sales tax and gaming and payroll taxes. VA disability compensation is untaxed by default.

states.propertyTax: Nevada gives fixed assessed-value exemptions that are adjusted annually for inflation. FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027: the basic Veterans Exemption is $3,640 of assessed valuation (about $126/year of property tax savings, or up to about $145 applied to vehicle registration) for veterans with 90+ days of active duty during specified wartime periods. The Disabled Veterans Exemption is tiered by rating: 60-79% = $18,200 assessed value (about $649 property tax or $728 vehicle); 80-99% = $27,300 (about $974 property or $1,092 vehicle); 100% = $36,400 (about $1,299 property or $1,456 vehicle). The Surviving Spouse Exemption is $1,820 assessed value (about $64 property or $72 vehicle) and the Blind Exemption is $5,460. Because Nevada assesses at 35% of taxable value, the $36,400 figure corresponds to roughly $104,000 of market value — so this is a partial reduction, not a full exemption, and a 100% disabled veteran in a $600,000 Las Vegas home still pays most of the bill. THE KEY STRUCTURAL FEATURE: the exemption may be applied to the basic governmental services tax portion of MOTOR VEHICLE REGISTRATION instead of (or split with) real property tax, which makes it usable by renters. Secured property applications are due by June 15; vehicle and unsecured applications can be filed any time before the tax is due. Surviving spouses of disabled veterans may continue the exemption.
states.education: Nevada has no general veteran tuition waiver. What exists: the Nevada National Guard tuition waiver at Nevada System of Higher Education institutions for drilling Guard members; tuition and laboratory fee waivers for dependents of Nevada National Guard members killed in the line of duty; and fee waivers for Purple Heart and Medal of Honor recipients AND their children at NSHE institutions — the Purple Heart child provision is generous and under-publicized. Nonresident veterans who were discharged in Nevada, or who enroll within five years of discharge, qualify for in-state tuition, as do veterans and dependents using federal VA education benefits under the Choice Act. Nevada also has a state Grant-in-Aid program at NSHE schools.
states.employment: Nevada state hiring uses a tiered preference: veterans with a service-connected disability receive the highest preference, followed by other veterans, followed by surviving spouses of service members killed in the line of duty, followed by members of the Reserve and National Guard. Nevada honors military occupational credentials toward licensure, provides expedited and temporary licensure for military spouses (Nevada was an early adopter of spouse licensure portability), and grants CDL skills-test waivers for qualifying military drivers. Nevada certifies veteran-owned businesses for a state procurement preference, and Nevada JobConnect provides priority of service.
states.vehicleRec: Veteran designation on a Nevada driver's license costs $8.25. Multiple branch-specific and campaign plates are available; Disabled Veteran plates are exempt from state and local parking fees and carry handicapped parking authorization, and Gold Star Family plates are likewise exempt from parking fees. The property tax exemption can be redirected to the governmental services tax on registration, as described above. Recreation: disabled veterans rated 50%+ and active-duty members stationed outside Nevada receive $15 specialty combination hunting and fishing licenses. State parks: ALL veterans receive a free annual state park entrance permit, and disabled veterans can obtain a $30 annual permit that adds exemptions from camping and boat-launch fees — one of the better park deals in the West.
states.cash: Nevada has no wartime service bonus, no state-funded emergency financial assistance fund of significance, and no state supplement to VA pension. The absence of an income tax is the state's answer to cash benefits. The Nevada Department of Veterans Services runs the Nevada Veterans Coalition and partners with nonprofits for emergency aid rather than funding a state grant program. There is no property-tax-credit-style refund.
states.homesHealth: Two state veterans homes: the Southern Nevada State Veterans Home in Boulder City and the Northern Nevada State Veterans Home in Sparks, both offering skilled nursing and memory care. Two state veterans memorial cemeteries: the Southern Nevada Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Boulder City and the Northern Nevada Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Fernley, with free burial for eligible veterans. Nevada relies on the VA Southern Nevada Healthcare System and VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System; there is no state veterans health program.
other: No state income tax is the dominant financial fact — it outweighs every targeted veteran tax break in a taxing state for anyone with meaningful retirement income.
The exemption can be applied to vehicle registration instead of property tax, which is the only version of this benefit in the country that a renter can actually use.
Exemption amounts are inflation-adjusted every fiscal year — FY2026-27 figures are about 5.8% above FY2025-26 ($3,440 / $17,700 / $26,550 / $35,400).
Nevada's 35% assessment ratio means the headline assessed-value numbers correspond to roughly triple that in market value.
Purple Heart recipients AND their children get NSHE fee waivers.
Nevada uses state-employed Veterans Service Officers through NDVS, not county VSOs.
No state emergency cash fund and no bonus program.
states.topHack: If you rent, or if your property tax bill is small, take the disabled veteran exemption against your VEHICLE registration instead — a 100% rated veteran can knock roughly $1,456 off governmental services tax across their registered vehicles in FY2026-27, which is more than the same exemption is worth against a modest property tax bill, and county assessors almost never mention the option.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.headline: New Hampshire now has no personal income tax at all, but it funds itself with some of the highest property taxes in the country and hands veterans only small locally-optional CREDITS against that bill.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Not taxed. New Hampshire has never taxed earned income, and the 5% Interest and Dividends tax was fully repealed effective January 1, 2025 — so as of tax year 2025 New Hampshire has no personal income tax of any kind. Military retirement, SBP, TSP distributions, IRA and 401(k) withdrawals, Social Security, and investment income are all untaxed.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Not taxed. No state tax on W-2 wages or military pay.
incomeTax.notes: The Interest and Dividends tax repeal (completed 1/1/2025) matters specifically to military retirees living on investment income, who until recently did owe New Hampshire tax on dividends. VA disability compensation is untaxed by default. New Hampshire has no state sales tax either — the entire burden falls on property tax, which is why the credits below are the whole ballgame.

states.propertyTax: New Hampshire gives CREDITS against the tax bill (dollar-for-dollar reductions), not assessed-value exemptions, and every one of them is a LOCAL OPTION adopted town by town within a statutory range — so the same veteran gets wildly different treatment in two adjacent towns. Standard/optional veterans' tax credit (RSA 72:28): statutory minimum $50, up to $750 if the town adopts the optional amount, for residents with 90+ days of active duty in a qualifying war or conflict, plus spouses and unremarried surviving spouses. All Veterans' Tax Credit (RSA 72:28-b): same $50-$750 range, for any veteran with 90+ days of active service and an honorable discharge who is not already receiving a credit under 72:28 or 72:35 — this extended credits to peacetime veterans. Surviving spouse credit (RSA 72:29-a): $700 up to $4,000 for surviving spouses of service members killed or who died on active duty. Service-connected total disability credit (RSA 72:35): $700 minimum, with towns able to adopt substantially more (official state summaries cite adoption ceilings up to $4,000-$5,000; Portsmouth, for example, adopted $700) for honorably discharged veterans with a permanent service-connected total disability, double amputees, or paraplegics from service injury. Combat service credit (RSA 72:28-c): $50 up to $500. THE BIG ONE: RSA 72:36-a grants a COMPLETE EXEMPTION from all property tax on a specially adapted homestead acquired with VA assistance, for veterans with service-connected total disability who are double amputees, paraplegic, or blind — and the unremarried surviving spouse retains it. Applications are due April 15 annually at the local assessor's office with discharge papers and VA documentation. Call your town: the difference between a town that adopted $50 and one that adopted $750 is real money.
states.education: New Hampshire provides FREE TUITION at New Hampshire community colleges and University System of New Hampshire institutions for the children of: veterans rated 100% permanently and totally disabled (to age 27), service members killed in action or who died from a service-connected disability, and service members classified MIA or POW. There is no comparable waiver for the veteran's own study. The New Hampshire National Guard Tuition Assistance / Scholarship program provides free coursework at state institutions for drilling Guard members, with benefits extendable to spouses under program rules. Veterans and dependents using federal VA education benefits receive in-state tuition rates. New Hampshire's public tuition is among the highest in the nation, so the dependent waiver is worth a great deal to the families that qualify.
states.employment: New Hampshire grants veterans preference for certain state positions, notably at the Liquor Commission, the New Hampshire Veterans Home, and in general state government hiring; the state does not use a uniform statewide points formula as extensively as most states, so confirm with New Hampshire Division of Personnel for a specific posting. Federal preference (5-10 points) applies to federal jobs in the state. New Hampshire has adopted occupational licensing reciprocity and expedited licensure for military spouses and accepts military training toward credentials. New Hampshire Employment Security provides priority of service and veteran employment representatives.
states.vehicleRec: Free vehicle registration for veterans with total disability, former POWs, and qualifying amputees. Disabled Veteran license plates confer FREE PARKING STATEWIDE — an unusually broad privilege. Purple Heart and other decoration plates are available. Veteran indicator added to a driver's license at no cost at renewal. Recreation: free or reduced lifetime hunting and fishing licenses for disabled veterans (a $10 administrative fee typically applies), and free state park admission for disabled veterans and for lower-enlisted active-duty service members. New Hampshire State Parks also run free-admission days for veterans.
states.cash: New Hampshire has no wartime service bonus currently active, no large state emergency financial assistance fund, and no state supplement to VA pension. The New Hampshire Division of Veterans Services and the state's Veterans Council direct veterans to federal and nonprofit emergency resources. The property tax credits described above are the only recurring state financial benefit, and they are locally funded.
states.homesHealth: One state veterans home: the New Hampshire Veterans Home in Tilton, a roughly 250-bed intermediate and long-term care facility for honorably discharged veterans. One state veterans cemetery: the New Hampshire State Veterans Cemetery in Boscawen, offering columbarium, in-ground cremation, and casket burial. New Hampshire has historically had limited in-state VA inpatient capacity (the Manchester VA Medical Center), so many veterans travel to White River Junction, Vermont or Boston for specialty care — a real practical cost of living here.
other: No income tax AND no sales tax — but the property tax burden is among the highest per capita in the nation, so the small credits matter more here than the same credits would elsewhere.
The Interest and Dividends tax was fully repealed effective 1/1/2025, removing the last state tax on retiree investment income.
Every veteran property tax credit is a local option — two identical veterans in neighboring towns can receive $50 and $750 respectively.
RSA 72:36-a is a true total exemption, but only for SAH-grant homes occupied by double amputees, paraplegics, or blind veterans.
Disabled Veteran plates give free parking statewide.
Free tuition for children of 100% P&T veterans to age 27 at USNH and community colleges — valuable given New Hampshire's high public tuition.
New Hampshire does not use county VSOs; the state Division of Veterans Services employs service officers.

agency.name: New Hampshire Division of Veterans Services, Department of Military Affairs and Veterans Services

states.topHack: Go to your town's annual meeting or select board and get RSA 72:28-b and RSA 72:35 adopted at the statutory maximum. These credits are worth $50 by default and up to $750 and $4,000 respectively if the town votes for them — in New Hampshire, lobbying your own town is literally the highest-return veteran benefit action available.

states.name: New Jersey
states.headline: A 100% permanent and total rating means zero property tax in the state with the highest property taxes in America — roughly a $10,000-a-year benefit — and New Jersey grants absolute civil service preference, but it still taxes active-duty pay.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. New Jersey does not tax U.S. military pension or survivor's benefit payments from the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force, or Coast Guard — no age condition, no cap. IMPORTANT TRAP: a federal CIVIL SERVICE pension IS taxable in New Jersey even if it is based in part on military service credit, so a military retiree who converted to federal civilian service and bought back military time loses the exemption on that portion.
incomeTax.activeDuty: TAXABLE for New Jersey residents. This is the state's main tax weakness for serving members. Combat zone pay is excluded for tax years 2021 and after (not retroactive). Nonresident service members stationed in New Jersey are not taxed on military pay, and nonresident military spouses are protected under MSRRA.
incomeTax.notes: Separately, New Jersey gives every honorably discharged veteran a $6,000 ADDITIONAL PERSONAL EXEMPTION on the NJ-1040, every year, for life — and a spouse filing jointly who is also a qualifying veteran can claim a second $6,000. It does NOT transfer to a surviving spouse after the veteran's death, cannot be claimed for dependents or domestic partners, and requires a one-time submission of the DD-214. You must affirmatively check the box or it is disallowed. VA disability compensation is not taxed.

states.propertyTax: New Jersey has two separate benefits. (1) The $250 ANNUAL VETERANS PROPERTY TAX DEDUCTION off the property tax bill for honorably discharged veterans who own and occupy a New Jersey home — a 2020 constitutional amendment extended this to ALL honorably discharged veterans regardless of whether they served during a period of war, and extended it to residents of continuing care retirement communities. Unremarried surviving spouses of eligible veterans and of service members who died on active duty also qualify. (2) The 100% DISABLED VETERAN FULL PROPERTY TAX EXEMPTION: veterans certified by the VA as having a 100% permanent and total service-connected disability are FULLY EXEMPT from property taxes on their principal residence — and given New Jersey's average residential property tax bill of roughly $10,000 per year, this is arguably the single most valuable state veteran benefit in the United States on a dollar basis. The unremarried surviving spouse retains the full exemption, as does the surviving spouse of a service member who died on active duty. The 2020 amendment likewise removed the wartime-service requirement. Claims are filed with the municipal tax assessor; retroactive refunds back to the effective date of the VA rating are commonly available. There is no sliding scale between $250 and full exemption — New Jersey is all-or-nothing at 100% P&T.
states.education: New Jersey's education benefits are dependent- and Guard-focused. The POW/MIA Tuition Benefit Program provides FREE UNDERGRADUATE TUITION at New Jersey public AND independent (private) institutions for children of service members declared POW or MIA after January 1, 1960 — the inclusion of private colleges is unusual. The Survivor Tuition Benefits Program covers tuition at New Jersey public institutions for spouses and dependent children of emergency service personnel and service members killed in the line of duty. The War Orphans Tuition Assistance program pays $500 per year for four years of college or equivalent training for children of service members who died in service or from service-connected disabilities. The New Jersey National Guard Tuition Waiver covers up to 16 credits per semester tuition-free at New Jersey public institutions for drilling Guard members. Veterans and dependents using federal VA education benefits receive in-state tuition rates. There is no broad tuition waiver for the veteran's own study.
states.employment: New Jersey grants ABSOLUTE VETERANS PREFERENCE in civil service — not points. Disabled veterans who pass the examination are placed at the very top of the certification list, followed by all other veterans, followed by non-veterans, regardless of score. For state and local government jobs in New Jersey this is decisive and is one of the two strongest preferences in the country alongside Massachusetts. Veterans must obtain a Veterans Preference determination from the New Jersey Department of Military and Veterans Affairs before it can be applied. New Jersey also provides expedited and temporary occupational licensure for military spouses, accepts military training toward credentials, and runs veteran employment services through the New Jersey Department of Labor with priority of service.
states.vehicleRec: Free Disabled Veteran and Purple Heart license plates; free vehicle registration for disabled and blind veterans; veteran designation available on New Jersey driver's licenses. FREE PARKING AT MUNICIPAL METERS statewide for disabled veterans and Purple Heart recipients displaying qualifying plates — a real daily benefit in a dense state. Recreation: free hunting and fishing licenses for disabled veterans; free state park entry for disabled veterans and National Guard members; and access to the private beach at the National Guard Training Center at Sea Girt for service members and veterans.
states.cash: The Catastrophic Entitlement provides a monthly state payment (cited at $150 per month) to veterans with specified severe service-connected disabilities — blindness, amputation of limbs, paraplegia, hemiplegia, osteochondritis, or similar catastrophic conditions. This is a genuine state cash supplement on top of VA compensation and it is chronically under-claimed. New Jersey has no active wartime service bonus. Veterans Haven North (Glen Gardner) and Veterans Haven South (Winslow) provide transitional housing with therapeutic and vocational services rather than cash. The $6,000 income tax exemption and the $250 property tax deduction are the other recurring dollar benefits.
states.homesHealth: Three New Jersey Veterans Memorial Homes: Menlo Park, Paramus, and Vineland. Be aware that the Menlo Park and Paramus homes experienced among the worst COVID-19 mortality rates of any long-term care facilities in the United States in 2020 and were the subject of a U.S. Department of Justice investigation and settlement with findings of inadequate care; oversight and staffing have since been restructured, but families should research current survey results before placement. One state veterans cemetery: the Brigadier General William C. Doyle Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Wrightstown, one of the largest and busiest state veterans cemeteries in the country, with no-cost interment for eligible veterans and spouses. No state veterans health insurance program.
other: The full exemption at 100% P&T is worth more in New Jersey than anywhere else in the country because New Jersey has the nation's highest average property tax bill.
The $6,000 income tax exemption is permanent, annual, and available to EVERY honorably discharged veteran regardless of disability — but you must check the box and file the DD-214 once.
New Jersey still taxes active-duty pay of residents, unlike most states.
A federal civil service pension based on bought-back military time is TAXABLE — a costly surprise for military-to-federal-civilian retirees.
Absolute (not points) civil service preference, with disabled veterans at the top of every list.
Catastrophic Entitlement pays a monthly state cash supplement for specified severe disabilities and is badly under-claimed.
The 2020 constitutional amendment removed the wartime-service requirement from both the $250 deduction and the 100% exemption.
County Veteran Service Officers exist, but NJDMVA also runs its own statewide veterans service offices.

agency.name: New Jersey Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (NJDMVA)

states.topHack: If you are severely disabled, file for the Catastrophic Entitlement — it is a monthly New Jersey state check on top of your VA compensation for blindness, amputation, paraplegia, hemiplegia and similar conditions, it is not means-tested, and NJDMVA's own outreach data has long shown most eligible veterans never apply.

states.name: New Mexico
states.headline: New Mexico just rebuilt its property tax benefit into a proportional exemption — a 60% rating now cancels 60% of your property tax bill — and it stacks that on full active-duty exemption, a $30,000 retirement exemption, free college scholarships, and a free lifetime state parks pass.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Partially exempt. New Mexico exempts up to $30,000 of military retirement pay for tax year 2026. The exemption was phased in at $10,000 (2022), $20,000 (2023), and $30,000 (2024 onward). CAUTION: the statute was written with a sunset and has been extended legislatively; confirm with the New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department whether the $30,000 exemption remains in force beyond tax year 2026 before relying on it for planning.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Active-duty military pay is entirely exempt from New Mexico income tax for resident service members. Nonresident service members stationed in New Mexico are not taxed on military pay.
incomeTax.notes: New Mexico's graduated rates top out near 5.9%. Social Security is exempt below income thresholds. VA disability compensation is not taxed. New Mexico also offers an employer tax credit of up to $1,000 per recently returned veteran hired.

states.propertyTax: New Mexico rebuilt this benefit with two 2024 constitutional amendments, both effective for the 2026 tax year. AMENDMENT 2 raised the general Veteran Property Tax Exemption from $4,000 to $10,000 of TAXABLE VALUE, and indexed it to inflation annually going forward — available to any New Mexico resident veteran (and to surviving spouses). AMENDMENT 1 replaced the old all-or-nothing disabled veteran exemption with a PROPORTIONAL exemption: the percentage of property tax exempted now equals the VA disability rating. A veteran rated 60% has 60% of the property tax on their principal residence exempted; a 30% rating exempts 30%; a 100% rating exempts the entire bill. Before 2026, only 100%-rated veterans received anything under this heading, so this is a major expansion — official estimates put more than 7,000 New Mexico veterans in the newly eligible group. Surviving spouses retain the exemption. The process is two-step and trips people up: you take your DD-214, proof of New Mexico residency, and your VA award letter to a New Mexico Department of Veterans Services office, DVS issues you a certificate of eligibility, and you then file that certificate with your COUNTY ASSESSOR. Note New Mexico assesses at one-third of market value, so the $10,000 general exemption is off taxable (assessed) value.
states.education: New Mexico has the deepest scholarship lineup of any state in this group. The Vietnam Veteran Scholarship covers tuition, books, and fees at state-funded institutions for Vietnam-era veterans. The Wartime Veteran Scholarship Fund assists with undergraduate, master's, and doctoral costs for veterans who served in a conflict after 1990. The Children of Deceased Veterans Scholarship provides free tuition plus up to $300 per year for eligible children of veterans who died in service or of service-connected causes. The New Mexico National Guard Tuition Scholarship covers 100% of tuition at state institutions for drilling Guard members. Veterans using the GI Bill receive resident tuition rates immediately. New Mexico also awards high school diplomas to WWII, Korean, and Vietnam veterans who left school for service. Layered on top is New Mexico's Opportunity Scholarship, which makes public college tuition-free for most residents regardless of veteran status — so in practice a New Mexico veteran and their family have several overlapping free-tuition routes.
states.employment: New Mexico adds 5 points to civil service examination scores for honorably discharged veterans and 10 points for veterans with a service-connected disability. Employers receive a state business tax credit of up to $1,000 for each recently returned veteran hired. Certified veteran-owned businesses receive an additional 5% procurement preference on state contracts (higher for service-disabled veteran-owned businesses — confirm the current percentage with the General Services Department). New Mexico accepts military training toward occupational licensure and provides expedited licensure for military spouses. The New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions provides priority of service.
states.vehicleRec: Standard veteran plates (Armed Forces, Woman Veteran) carry a $17 one-time fee; Disabled Veteran (50%+), Purple Heart, Pearl Harbor Survivor, Ex-POW, and Medal of Honor plates are FREE, and Gold Star Family plates are free for life. Veterans who do not qualify for the full property tax exemption may register vehicles at two-thirds of the standard rate. Veterans who lost, or lost the use of, one or both legs at or above the ankle or one or both arms at or above the wrist are exempt from the motor vehicle excise tax. RECREATION IS EXCEPTIONAL: veterans rated 50% or more service-connected disabled receive a FREE LIFETIME STATE PARKS PASS covering unlimited day use AND CAMPING — most states cover day use only. Hunting and fishing licenses are reduced to $10, or free for life at 100% disability. Veterans rated 50%+ get free passes to New Mexico state museums and monuments, and all veterans get free state park and museum admission on Veterans Day.
states.cash: New Mexico has no wartime service bonus and no large state emergency financial assistance fund; the state's dollars go into the scholarship funds and the property tax exemptions instead. There is no state supplement to VA pension. New Mexico does provide statutory protections rather than cash: military discharge paper confidentiality, service member child custody protection during deployment, and school enrollment priority for military children.
states.homesHealth: One state veterans home: the New Mexico State Veterans Home at 992 South Broadway, Truth or Consequences (575-894-4200), serving honorably discharged veterans and eligible family members — thin coverage for a large, rural state, and a long drive from Albuquerque or Farmington. Three state veterans cemeteries in operation at Fort Stanton, Gallup, and Angel Fire, meeting VA National Cemetery eligibility standards, with additional state cemeteries developed or planned (Carlsbad, Yah-ta-hey, Fort Bayard) — confirm current operating status with NMDVS. Veterans also use the Raymond G. Murphy VA Medical Center in Albuquerque and a network of community-based outpatient clinics.
other: The proportional disabled veteran exemption is brand new for the 2026 tax year and is the biggest change in New Mexico veteran benefits in decades — a 30% or 50% rating is now worth real money for the first time.
The general veteran exemption tripled from $4,000 to $10,000 of taxable value AND is now inflation-indexed.
Two-step application: NMDVS issues the certificate, the COUNTY ASSESSOR applies it — veterans who go straight to the assessor get turned away.
Free lifetime state parks pass includes CAMPING, not just day use, at a 50% rating.
Active-duty pay is fully exempt, unlike New Jersey, Maryland, Massachusetts, or Nebraska.
Verify whether the $30,000 military retirement exemption has been extended past 2026 — it was enacted with sunset language.
Only one state veterans home for the whole state.
NMDVS employs state veterans service officers rather than relying on county VSOs.

agency.name: New Mexico Department of Veterans Services (NMDVS)

states.topHack: If you have ANY service-connected rating — even 10% or 30% — get the NMDVS certificate and file it with your county assessor for the 2026 tax year. Until this year only 100%-rated veterans got anything, so the entire 10-90% population has never applied and county assessors are not going to chase you; the exemption now cancels exactly your rating percentage of the bill.

states.name: New York
states.headline: Military pensions are fully exempt and combat veterans get free SUNY/CUNY tuition, but the property tax exemption is a capped percentage that school districts can refuse — though a new law makes a FULL exemption for 100% disabled veterans mandatory statewide starting with October 2026 taxable status dates.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. New York does not tax U.S. military retirement pay or Survivor Benefit Plan annuities, regardless of age or amount. This is a full subtraction, separate from and in addition to New York's general $20,000 pension and annuity exclusion available at age 59.5 — so a military retiree with a civilian pension can exempt the military pension entirely AND still use the $20,000 exclusion against the civilian pension.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxable for New York-domiciled residents (combat zone pay is excluded because it is federally excluded). New York residents who meet strict non-domicile or 'no permanent place of abode' tests while stationed elsewhere may avoid New York tax. Nonresident service members stationed in New York are not taxed on military pay, and nonresident military spouses are protected under MSRRA.
incomeTax.notes: New York's top state rate reaches 10.9%, and New York City residents pay an additional city income tax of roughly 3.08-3.88% (Yonkers levies a surcharge). Fully exempting the military pension against those rates is worth a great deal. VA disability compensation is not taxed. New York also offers employers a Veterans Hiring Tax Credit.

states.propertyTax: New York uses three mutually exclusive exemptions and a critical new mandate. (1) ALTERNATIVE VETERANS EXEMPTION (RPTL 458-a), the one most veterans use: 15% of assessed value for wartime service, an ADDITIONAL 10% for service in a combat zone or receipt of an expeditionary medal, PLUS an additional amount equal to one-half of the service-connected disability rating (a 40% rating adds 20% of assessed value). Every component is capped in dollars, and each municipality picks its cap tier. The BASIC maximums are $6,000 wartime / $4,000 combat / $20,000 disability; local options step up to $9,000/$6,000/$30,000, $12,000/$8,000/$40,000, $15,000/$10,000/$50,000, and $18,000/$12,000/$60,000; designated high-appreciation municipalities may go as high as $75,000/$50,000/$250,000. Each cap is then MULTIPLIED BY THE LATEST FINAL STATE EQUALIZATION RATE, so the effective dollar value changes every roll. Filed on Form RP-458-a. The exemption applies automatically to county, city, and town taxes, but SCHOOL DISTRICTS — which are the majority of a New York tax bill — must affirmatively opt in, and many have not. (2) ELIGIBLE FUNDS EXEMPTION (RPTL 458) for property purchased with pension, bonus, or insurance monies. (3) COLD WAR VETERANS EXEMPTION (RPTL 458-b), 10% or 15% of assessed value with caps around $8,000/$12,000, for service between September 2, 1945 and December 26, 1991. (4) NEW AND IMPORTANT: legislation signed to take effect for assessment rolls with taxable status dates on or after OCTOBER 1, 2026 MANDATES a full property tax exemption for veterans rated 100% service-connected disabled in ALL localities — removing the local opt-in and converting New York from a capped-percentage state into a full-exemption state at the top rating. The law provides that claiming it does not discontinue other benefits the veteran already receives. Implementation guidance from ORPTS was still emerging as of September 2026; confirm with your assessor.
states.education: The New York State Veterans Tuition Award (VTA) is the headline: it pays up to the full cost of SUNY undergraduate tuition (with a proportional award for part-time study and for private institutions) for New York resident veterans who served in Vietnam, the Persian Gulf, Afghanistan, or who received an expeditionary medal, and who are matriculated at an approved New York program. Because it pays TUITION, a veteran using the Post-9/11 GI Bill concurrently can often preserve GI Bill entitlement or direct it elsewhere — coordinate carefully with HESC, since awards cannot exceed actual costs. The MERIT Scholarship (Military Enhanced Recognition Incentive and Tribute) is the most generous: full SUNY/CUNY-rate tuition, fees, room, and board for children, spouses, and financial dependents of New York service members who died or became severely and permanently disabled as a result of service in a combat theater or during military training operations — it covers the entire cost of attendance. The Recruitment Incentive and Retention Program (RIRP) covers SUNY-rate tuition for New York Army and Air National Guard members. Veterans and dependents using federal benefits receive in-state tuition rates.
states.employment: New York civil service preference is points-based but has a critical catch. Non-disabled wartime veterans receive 5 additional points on open-competitive examinations and 2.5 points on promotional examinations. Disabled veterans (any service-connected rating) receive 10 points on open-competitive and 5 points on promotional exams. THE GOTCHA: New York's preference is a ONE-TIME LIFETIME USE — once the credits are actually used to obtain a permanent appointment, they are exhausted and can never be claimed again. Choose the exam you spend them on. New York also offers employers a Veterans Hiring Tax Credit (higher for disabled veterans), grants veteran-owned business certification (SDVOB program) with a state contracting goal, accepts military training toward occupational licensure, and provides expedited licensure for military spouses.
states.vehicleRec: Free veteran designation on a New York driver's license or non-driver ID. DMV offers reduced or waived registration fees for qualifying disabled veterans and free distinctive plates including Purple Heart, Ex-POW, Medal of Honor, Gold Star, and Disabled Veteran; Congressional Medal of Honor and Ex-POW plates carry registration fee exemptions. Recreation: the NEW YORK ACCESS PASS gives free entry to state parks and historic sites and free or discounted camping, boat launch, and golf to New York residents with a qualifying permanent disability, which includes veterans with a 40% or greater service-connected disability — this is the state's best recreation benefit. Veterans with a 40%+ service-connected disability may obtain lifetime hunting, fishing, and trapping licenses for a nominal fee ($5). Active-duty members home on leave may hunt and fish without a license under certain conditions.
states.cash: New York has no currently active wartime service bonus — the WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and Persian Gulf bonus programs have all closed. There is no broad state emergency financial assistance fund and no state supplement to VA pension. What New York does have that almost nowhere else does is the JOSEPH P. DWYER VETERAN PEER SUPPORT PROGRAM, a state-funded county-level veteran-to-veteran peer support network for PTSD and TBI that has been replicated nationally — services, not cash. The State of New York Mortgage Agency (SONYMA) offers a Homes for Veterans program with below-market interest rates and down payment assistance, which is the largest dollar-value New York program aimed at veterans outside the tax code.
states.homesHealth: Five New York State Veterans' Homes providing skilled nursing and long-term care: Batavia, Montrose, Oxford, St. Albans (Queens), and Stony Brook — operated under SUNY and the New York State Department of Health rather than the veterans agency. New York's veterans cemetery picture is unusual: most interment capacity is federal (Long Island National Cemetery, Calverton, Saratoga, Bath, Woodlawn), and New York was among the last large states to develop state-run veterans cemeteries; confirm the current status and locations of New York State-operated veterans cemeteries with NYS DVS, as several were authorized and developed recently. Every one of New York's 62 counties and New York City operates a County Veterans Service Agency.
other: The mandatory full exemption for 100% disabled veterans effective for October 1, 2026 and later taxable status dates is the most consequential change on this list — it converts New York from a capped-percentage state to a full-exemption state at the top rating.
School district taxes are the biggest line on most New York bills and school districts must OPT IN to the alternative veterans exemption — many have not.
Alternative exemption caps are multiplied by the state equalization rate, so the dollar value shifts every assessment roll.
Civil service preference credits are a ONE-TIME LIFETIME USE — spend them on the right exam.
The military pension exemption is separate from and additive to the general $20,000 pension exclusion at 59.5+.
MERIT Scholarship covers tuition, fees, room AND board — full cost of attendance — for survivors of combat deaths and severe disabilities.
The Dwyer Peer Support Program is a nationally copied New York innovation.
County Veterans Service Agencies operate in all 62 counties plus New York City.

agency.name: New York State Department of Veterans' Services (NYS DVS)

states.topHack: Ask your assessor two questions before October 1, 2026: whether your SCHOOL DISTRICT has opted into the alternative veterans exemption (that is where most of your tax bill sits), and how they intend to implement the new mandatory 100%-disabled full exemption — the mandate removes local discretion, and veterans who file early on the first affected roll capture a full year of relief that late filers lose.

states.name: North Carolina
states.headline: North Carolina fully exempts military retirement for 20-year and medically retired veterans and sends children of disabled veterans to UNC-system schools free, but the disabled veteran property exclusion is a stale $45,000 and retirees with under 20 years get nothing on the income tax side.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully deductible, BUT ONLY IF YOU QUALIFY. Under S.L. 2021-180, effective for tax year 2021 and after, North Carolina allows a 100% deduction of military retirement pay for a veteran who either (a) served at least 20 years, or (b) was medically retired under 10 U.S.C. Chapter 61. Survivor Benefit Plan payments to a beneficiary of a qualifying retiree are also deductible. THE GAP: a service member who separated with, say, 14 years and later receives retired pay through another route, or a Reserve retiree who does not meet the criteria, does NOT get the deduction. Separately, veterans covered by the Bailey v. State settlement (those with five or more years of creditable service vested as of August 12, 1989) remain fully exempt regardless of the 20-year test.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Taxable for North Carolina-domiciled residents (combat zone pay is excluded because it is federally excluded). Nonresident service members stationed in North Carolina are not taxed on military pay, and nonresident military spouses are protected under MSRRA.
incomeTax.notes: North Carolina has a flat individual rate that is stepping down — approximately 4.25% for 2025 and 3.99% for 2026, with further triggered reductions scheduled. The combination of a low flat rate and a full military retirement deduction is why North Carolina has one of the largest military retiree populations in the country. VA disability compensation is not taxed; North Carolina adds nothing beyond the federal exclusion.

states.propertyTax: The Disabled Veteran Homestead Exclusion (N.C.G.S. 105-277.1C) excludes the FIRST $45,000 OF APPRAISED VALUE of the permanent residence from taxation. Eligibility requires an honorable or under-honorable-conditions discharge plus either a VA certification of a service-connected, PERMANENT AND TOTAL disability, or receipt of VA benefits for specially adapted housing under 38 U.S.C. 2101. There is NO income limit, NO age limit, and no home-value ceiling on eligibility — but the benefit itself is capped at $45,000 of value, which at typical North Carolina rates of 0.7%-1.0% is worth only about $315-$450 per year. The figure has not been increased in many years and is now well below the value it represented when enacted. The unremarried surviving spouse of a qualifying disabled veteran, or of a veteran whose death was service-connected, may claim the exclusion. Applications are due by JUNE 1 to the county assessor with the VA award letter, photo ID, and deed. IMPORTANT RESTRICTION: a qualifying owner who receives this exclusion MAY NOT also receive North Carolina's elderly/disabled homestead exclusion or the circuit breaker deferment — you must pick the single most advantageous one. There is no sliding scale by rating, and no separate Purple Heart, POW, or Medal of Honor exemption. Certain vehicles specially adapted with VA assistance are exempt from the motor vehicle property tax.
states.education: The North Carolina Scholarships for Children of War Veterans is the state's signature program and it is genuinely valuable: up to EIGHT ACADEMIC SEMESTERS of free tuition and mandatory fees at North Carolina public colleges and universities (the UNC System and the community colleges), plus a substantial annual allowance (commonly cited around $4,500 per year) toward costs at approved North Carolina private institutions. It is awarded in classes (I-A, I-B, II, III, IV) keyed to whether the veteran parent died in service, died of a service-connected condition, is rated disabled at various thresholds, or was a POW/MIA — and the classes reach well below a 100% rating, which is why it is worth applying even with a partial rating. Strict conditions: the child must generally be under age 25 at the time of application, and THE VETERAN PARENT MUST HAVE BEEN A NORTH CAROLINA RESIDENT AT THE TIME OF ENTRY INTO SERVICE (or meet alternative residency rules) — this catches many families who moved to North Carolina after service. Administered by the NC Department of Military and Veterans Affairs, not the schools. The North Carolina National Guard Tuition Assistance Program covers tuition for drilling Guard members at North Carolina public institutions (annual caps apply — verify the current maximum). Veterans and dependents using federal VA benefits receive in-state tuition.
states.employment: North Carolina grants veterans preference in state government hiring — eligible veterans, and in some cases spouses and surviving spouses, receive preference in the state application process, and state agencies give priority consideration to qualified veteran applicants. North Carolina was an early and aggressive adopter of military credentialing reform: the state accepts military training and occupational specialties toward civilian licensure across many boards, provides expedited and temporary licensure for military spouses relocating on orders, and grants CDL skills-test waivers for qualifying military drivers. NCWorks Career Centers provide priority of service with dedicated Local Veterans Employment Representatives and Disabled Veteran Outreach Program specialists. The state's NC4VETS initiative coordinates employer outreach.
states.vehicleRec: Free Disabled Veteran plates for qualifying 100% permanently and totally disabled veterans, free Purple Heart, Medal of Honor, Ex-POW, and Gold Star plates, plus a wide range of branch and campaign specialty plates; veteran designation available on North Carolina driver's licenses. Handicapped placards are available at no cost to qualifying disabled veterans, and vehicles specially adapted with VA assistance are exempt from the motor vehicle property tax. Recreation: North Carolina offers a discounted Disabled Veteran Lifetime Sportsman license for veterans rated 50% or more service-connected disabled (a one-time reduced fee rather than a recurring license), and totally disabled veterans qualify for the lowest-cost or no-cost tier — verify the current fee schedule with the NC Wildlife Resources Commission. Day-use admission to North Carolina State Parks is free to everyone, so there is no separate veteran park pass.
states.cash: North Carolina has no wartime service bonus, no broad state-funded emergency financial assistance fund, and no state supplement to VA pension. The state's investment goes into the scholarship program, the veterans homes, and the cemeteries instead. County Veterans Service Officers connect veterans to federal and nonprofit emergency resources. There is no property-tax-credit-style refund for veterans.
states.homesHealth: Four North Carolina State Veterans Homes providing skilled nursing and rehabilitative care: Fayetteville, Salisbury, Kinston, and Black Mountain.
