Four North Carolina State Veterans Cemeteries: Spring Lake (Sandhills), Black Mountain (Western Carolina), Jacksonville (Coastal Carolina), and a fourth developed in the Goldsboro area — confirm current operating status with NCDMVA. Interment is at no cost for eligible veterans. North Carolina hosts three VA medical centers (Durham, Salisbury, Fayetteville) plus the large Fayetteville/Fort Bragg military health footprint. There is no state veterans health insurance program. All 100 counties have County Veterans Service Officers.
other: The $45,000 property exclusion has not been raised in years and is worth only about $315-$450 annually — North Carolina is far weaker on property tax than its reputation among military retirees suggests.
The military retirement deduction requires 20 years of service OR a Chapter 61 medical retirement — a real cliff that catches Reserve and early-separating retirees.
You cannot combine the disabled veteran exclusion with the elderly/disabled exclusion or the circuit breaker — run all three and take the best.
The Scholarships for Children of War Veterans reach well below a 100% rating, but the veteran parent generally must have been an NC resident AT TIME OF ENTRY into service.
Flat income tax falling to about 3.99% in 2026 makes North Carolina attractive to spouses and second-career earners as well as retirees.
State park day-use entry is free to everyone, so there is no veteran-specific park benefit.
County Veterans Service Officers operate in all 100 counties.

agency.name: North Carolina Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (NCDMVA)

states.topHack: Apply for the Scholarships for Children of War Veterans even if your rating is nowhere near 100% — the award classes extend to partial ratings and wartime service, it pays eight semesters of tuition and mandatory fees at any UNC-system school, and it is administered by NCDMVA rather than the university, so financial aid offices never tell families it exists.

states.name: North Dakota
states.headline: Quietly one of the best tax deals in the country: both military retirement and active-duty pay are fully exempt from an already-low income tax, and the disabled veteran property tax credit is worth far more than its small headline number because of North Dakota's unusual assessment math.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. North Dakota allows a deduction for the full federally taxable amount of military retirement benefits (and for surviving spouses receiving those benefits). Confirmed in the Tax Commissioner's 'Income Tax: Military Service Members' guideline, content revised 12-2025. NOTE: the ND Dept. of Veterans Affairs' own income-tax page is stale and still says retirement pay is taxed — the Tax Commissioner is the controlling source and says it is deductible.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. Under SB 2293 (effective for tax years beginning after 12/31/2022), federally taxable military pay received by resident active-component and reserve-component members is exempt from ND income tax. This covers drill pay, training, mobilization, bonuses, and State Active Duty pay. Nonresidents stationed in ND are protected by SCRA.
incomeTax.notes: North Dakota has an income tax but it is among the lowest in the nation: a zero-percent bracket covers roughly the first $48,475 single / $80,975 married filing jointly (indexed), with only two positive brackets above that topping out near 2.5%. Combined with the full military pay and retirement exemptions, most military households owe little or nothing. Combat pay and other federally tax-exempt military compensation cannot be deducted again.

states.propertyTax: The Disabled Veteran's Property Tax Credit requires a 50%+ VA service-connected rating (or an extra-schedular / individual unemployability rating paid at the 100% rate) plus honorable discharge, ownership, and residence on the property. The credit reduces TAXABLE value on a sliding scale: $9,000 at 100%, $8,100 at 90%, $7,200 at 80%, $6,300 at 70%, $5,400 at 60%, $4,500 at 50% — $900 per 10 points of rating. These figures look small but are not: North Dakota residential taxable value is only about 4.5% of true market value (50% assessed x 9%), so a $9,000 taxable-value credit wipes out roughly $200,000 of true market value. If two disabled veterans are married and living together the combined credit cannot exceed 100% / $9,000. A surviving spouse remains eligible after the veteran's death, and a spouse receiving VA Dependency and Indemnity Compensation gets the full 100% credit. Separately, veterans with a specially adapted housing award or paraplegia get a Paraplegic Veteran exemption on the first $120,000 of homestead value. Application goes to the local assessor — the Tax Commissioner's credit page states an April 1 deadline while the Army benefit library states March 31; confirm with your county.
states.education: Dependent Tuition Waiver: spouses and dependent children of veterans who were killed in action, died of service-connected causes, are rated 100% service-connected disabled, or are POW/MIA attend ND state institutions tuition-free, for up to 45 months or 10 semesters toward a bachelor's degree or certificate (NDDVA, 701-239-7165). ND National Guard Tuition Assistance covers a 25% tuition waiver at state schools plus a 75% grant, up to 144 semester / 208 quarter credit hours lifetime, and recent authorization permits use at out-of-state schools (701-333-3008). Resident tuition status extends to active duty members, stationed reservists, ND residents with 180+ days of active service, and eligible family members of deceased, totally disabled, POW or MIA veterans. The Veterans Educational Training (VET) program provides free tutoring and academic guidance. Honorary high school diplomas are available for WWII, Korea and Vietnam-era veterans.
states.employment: State hiring preference: for non-competitive hiring, disabled veterans get first preference, then non-disabled veterans; for competitive hiring, 5 points (5%) for veterans and 10 points (10%) for disabled veterans. Eligible spouses and unremarried surviving spouses also receive preference. State employees in the Guard/Reserve get 20 working days of paid military leave plus 10 additional unpaid days for extended active duty, with a protected right to return. Professional licensing is notably veteran- and spouse-friendly: expedited 30-day processing for service members and military spouses, temporary licenses issued at no fee and valid 2 years if full requirements are not yet met, and renewal exemptions for deployed members. Job Service North Dakota (jobsnd.com) provides priority of service and a dedicated Veterans' Employment Team.
states.vehicleRec: Driver license veteran indicator available (requires 180+ days continuous active duty or the full called-up period, other than dishonorable discharge; get form SFN 59980 from a county veteran service officer). Eleven license plate options: Purple Heart plates free for the first set; Disabled American Veteran plates for 100% disabled veterans are exempt from sales tax and registration fees with two sets available; Gold Star plates carry free personalization; others charge $25 for personalization. CDL knowledge and skills test waivers for qualifying MOSs. Recreation: fishing license for 50%+ disabled veterans is $10 plus a $2 certificate fee; combined hunting license for 100%-disabled or unemployable veterans is $10 plus $2. State parks give a FREE LIFETIME entrance pass to veterans with a 50%+ service-connected rating or former POWs, extended to surviving spouses of 50%+ disabled veterans; veterans under 50% pay $28 annually. Active duty members with expeditionary medals get one free white-tailed deer gun license, and resident service members can buy deer gun licenses without entering the lottery.
states.cash: Hardship Assistance Grant: up to $5,000 total (multiple grants possible) for dental work, optical and hearing expenses, medical transportation, housing deposits and other emergency needs. Income and asset limits apply and you must have been a ND resident 1+ years; apply through a local County or Tribal Veterans Service Officer. Veterans Aid Loan: up to $5,000 at 8% annual interest with 50% of interest refunded if repaid as agreed, terms of 6-48 months, for ND residents of 1+ years with demonstrated repayment ability. North Dakota has no general wartime service bonus program currently open. PTSD service dog grants cover acquisition costs for ND residents with a diagnosis, 1+ year of counseling, and a doctor's recommendation.
states.homesHealth: North Dakota State Veterans Home in Lisbon: 98 basic-care beds, 52 skilled-care beds, and a 13-bed memory care unit, with PT/OT/speech therapy, on-site pharmacy, mental health services, hospice, rehabilitation and chaplain services. Eligibility requires ND residency, service in the ND National Guard, or entry into service from ND, plus honorable discharge with 180+ days federal active duty (excluding training) or a service-connected disability; spouses and survivors of eligible veterans also qualify. North Dakota Veterans Cemetery in Mandan (701-667-1418) provides burial, plot, opening/closing and headstone at no cost for casketed or cremated remains, covering veterans, spouses and unmarried dependent children under 21 (23 if a full-time student). Fargo National Cemetery is a VA national cemetery in-state, and the VA-funded All Nations Veterans Cemetery is at Fort Yates (701-854-8527).
other: The disabled veteran property tax credit's headline dollar figures badly understate its value — because ND residential taxable value is only ~4.5% of true market value, the $9,000 credit at 100% effectively shelters about $200,000 of market value.

North Dakota is one of very few states that exempts BOTH military retirement pay AND all active-duty/drill pay, on top of a zero-bracket income tax that already exempts roughly the first $48K single / $81K joint.
Free LIFETIME state park pass at just a 50% rating — a much lower threshold than most states, which typically require 100%.
Veterans Aid Loan refunds half your interest if you repay on schedule, an unusual structure that makes the effective rate about 4%.
Veterans Treatment Courts operate in Grand Forks and Nelson County; a ND Veterans Justice Outreach Coordinator serves the state (701-461-7330 ext. 7364).
Military Outreach Program specialists in Minot (701-420-5848) and Bismarck (701-333-3828) handle benefits, records, PTSD, retirement, employment and homelessness.

agency.name: North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs (NDDVA)

states.topHack: Apply for the Disabled Veteran's Property Tax Credit at 50% — not 100%. Most ND veterans assume the credit is only worth chasing at a total rating, but the credit starts at a 50% rating ($4,500 of taxable value, roughly $100,000 of true market value sheltered) and steps up $900 per 10 rating points. Pair it with the free lifetime state park pass, which also triggers at 50%. And if your NDDVA paperwork or a third-party site tells you North Dakota taxes your military pension, ignore it — the Tax Commissioner's own military guideline allows a full deduction, and the DVA's web page is simply out of date.

states.name: Ohio
states.headline: Ohio fully exempts military retirement pay and runs one of the strongest dependent-scholarship systems in the Midwest, but its disabled veteran property tax break is a modest fixed deduction rather than a real exemption and active-duty pay is taxed if you're stationed in-state.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Ohio permits a deduction of military retired pay from state income tax under Ohio Revised Code 5747.01. SBP, Reserve Component SBP and Retired Serviceman's Family Protection Plan annuities are likewise exempt, as is military disability retirement pay received as a pension or annuity, and VA DIC.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Partially taxed. Ohio residents stationed IN Ohio pay Ohio income tax on active-duty pay. Service members stationed outside Ohio may deduct their military pay, and those on 30+ days of temporary duty outside Ohio may deduct that portion. Nonresident military spouses stationed in Ohio under orders are exempt from Ohio income and school district income taxes.
incomeTax.notes: Ohio's individual income tax has been flattening: for 2026 the state is moving to a flat 2.75% rate on income above the roughly $26,050 exemption threshold. Ohio does not tax Social Security. Watch out for municipal and school district income taxes, which are separate from the state tax and can still reach military households.

states.propertyTax: Ohio's enhanced homestead exemption for disabled veterans shields a fixed slice of MARKET value from taxation — it is a deduction, not a full exemption. Eligibility requires a 100% service-connected disability rating or compensation at the 100% rate for individual unemployability. The statutory base is $50,000 of market value, indexed annually for inflation; the Butler County Auditor documented $52,300 for tax year 2024 against $26,200 for the general/senior homestead exemption. The exact indexed figure for tax year 2026 could not be confirmed from a state-level .gov source and should be verified with your county auditor — expect roughly $54,000-$56,000. Critically, unlike the general senior homestead exemption (which for new 2024 applicants had an Ohio adjusted gross income limit around $38,600, also indexed), the disabled veteran enhanced exemption is NOT income-tested. Unremarried surviving spouses may continue the exemption if they occupied the homestead at the veteran's death and either acquired ownership or continue to occupy it. Applications go to the county auditor. At typical Ohio effective rates of roughly 1.5-2%, the DV exemption is worth only about $800-$1,100 per year.
states.education: Ohio War Orphan & Severely Disabled Veterans' Children Scholarship (WOS) is the flagship: for 2026-27 it pays 77% of tuition and general fees at Ohio public institutions, or a flat $6,397 per year at private Ohio institutions. Applicants apply between ages 16 and 24, must be Ohio residents enrolled full-time in an associate's or bachelor's program, and the veteran parent must have an overall combined rating or overall service connection of 60% or more, or have died in service, or be MIA/POW, with qualifying wartime service under ORC 5910 (service 05/08/1975-08/01/1990 requires the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal). Veterans whose DD214 shows non-Ohio entry need five years of Ohio residency. A 2.00 cumulative GPA must be reached by end of first year and maintained; maximum five academic years; deadline May 15 annually. Ohio National Guard Scholarship Program pays 100% of tuition at state-funded public colleges (or 100% of state average tuition at participating privates) for 48 semester hours on a 3-5 year enlistment or 96 hours on a 6-year enlistment. Ohio Safety Officers College Memorial Fund covers 100% of instructional and general fees at publics, $10,672/year at independents, four years max, and $8,000/year for certificate programs, for surviving spouses and children of those killed in the line of duty in OEF/OIF or designated combat zones. Ohio GI Promise grants in-state tuition to nonresident veterans at Ohio publics with no 12-month residency wait. Ohio Hidden Heroes Scholarship serves caregivers enrolled in the VA PCAFC program caring for a 100% service-connected disabled veteran.
states.employment: State civil service preference adds 20% to passing exam scores for honorably discharged veterans with 180+ days of active duty, and 15% for current reserve-component members who completed initial training. State employees get up to one month of paid military leave annually and continue accruing sick, vacation and personal leave while on it, plus pay supplements covering the difference between state salary and military pay for federal active duty over one month (capped at the state salary), health insurance continuation, and reinstatement rights. Educator licensing is a standout: fees eliminated for veterans, service members and spouses; a one-year out-of-state educator license option; military license extensions; temporary military licenses; alternative licensure pathways; and the Ohio Military Veteran Educators Program pays hiring awards of $3,000-$5,000 (614-466-4109). OhioMeansJobs centers give priority of service, a military skills translator and a licensed-occupations guide (ohiovetsfirst@jfs.ohio.gov). Ohio National Guard members on state active duty receive federal-equivalent pay with a $75/day minimum base.
states.vehicleRec: Free 'Armed Forces' designation on driver license or ID. Veterans with a 100% service-connected rating get NO-COST new, renewal and duplicate driver licenses (requires a VA Benefit Summary Letter). Free removable windshield placard for disabled veterans and active duty with a service-connected disability limiting ability to walk. 92 varieties of military and veteran plates with no additional fee for most; personalization $50; Medal of Honor recipients get one free set; veterans at 100% disability or with VA adaptive vehicle assistance get up to two free plates. CDL knowledge and skills waivers including an 'Even Exchange' program for qualifying MOSs, plus expedited dealer licensing for service members, veterans and spouses (844-644-6268). Recreation: a FIVE-YEAR FREE hunting and fishing license bundle (fishing license, hunting license, fur taker permit, deer permit, wild turkey permit and wetlands habitat stamp) for Ohio residents of 6+ months with honorable discharge who are 100% permanently and totally disabled, receiving VA pension or compensation, holding an Ohio Disabled Veteran plate, or a former POW. Free watercraft registration for 100% disabled veterans, MOH recipients and former POWs. State parks: 10% overnight discount for active duty and retirees with no residency restriction; FREE camping for resident former POWs and veterans rated 100% permanent and total (866-644-6727).
states.cash: Ohio has no currently open statewide wartime bonus program — the Ohio Veterans Bonus for Persian Gulf, Afghanistan and Iraq service closed to new applications. The live cash channel is short-term emergency financial assistance administered by County Veterans Service Offices, which provide emergency financial help to veterans and their families with amounts and categories varying by county; this is Ohio's distinguishing structural feature, since every county is statutorily required to fund a CVSO from a dedicated property tax levy (877-644-6838; locator at dvs.ohio.gov/what-we-do/find-a-cvso). Ohio Housing Finance Agency's Ohio Heroes program offers discounted mortgage rates plus optional down payment assistance forgiven after 7 years, with veterans exempt from the 3-year non-ownership requirement (888-362-6432). Ohio National Guard Association State Sponsored Life Insurance provides $1,000 of coverage at no cost, with $10,000 free for one year to members who joined within the last year.
states.homesHealth: Three state facilities: Georgetown (168 beds, 937-378-2900); Sandusky (427 beds, 419-625-2454); and the Sandusky Domiciliary (216 beds of independent living with medical care, same number). They offer independent living, intermediate nursing, skilled nursing and memory care. Eligibility requires one year of Ohio residency, honorable or general discharge, and active duty service during a period of war or armed conflict. Ohio does not operate a state veterans cemetery system of its own on the scale of neighboring states; burial is generally handled through VA national cemeteries in-state. Veterans' courts operate around the state with ODVS coordination, and the Ohio Attorney General provides free legal services to active duty and mobilized members including wills, powers of attorney, and SCRA/USERRA enforcement (800-282-0515).
other: Ohio's County Veterans Service Officer network is unusually well-funded — each county levies a dedicated property tax for veteran services, which is why emergency cash assistance is available county-by-county rather than from a single state fund.
The five-year free hunting/fishing bundle is one of the broadest in the nation and does NOT require a 100% rating — merely receiving VA pension or compensation, or holding a DV plate, qualifies you.
The disabled veteran homestead exemption is NOT income-tested, while the general senior homestead exemption is — a meaningful distinction for higher-income disabled veterans.
Ohio GI Promise eliminates the 12-month residency wait for in-state tuition, valuable for veterans moving to Ohio specifically for school.
Ohio's homestead exemption reduces MARKET value, not assessed value; because Ohio assesses at 35% of market value, a $52,300 market-value exemption removes only about $18,300 of assessed value.

Municipal and school district income taxes are separate from the state tax, and the military retirement exemption does not always flow through identically at the local level — check your municipality.
states.topHack: Go to your County Veterans Service Office before you go anywhere else. Ohio is one of the only states where every single county funds a CVSO from a dedicated statutory property tax levy, which means county-level emergency financial assistance — rent, utilities, car repair, medical — is real money that is routinely left unclaimed because veterans assume 'veteran assistance' means the VA. The second underused move: if you receive any VA compensation or pension at all (not just a 100% rating), you qualify for the five-year free hunting and fishing license bundle, which packages six separate permits most people buy individually.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.headline: Oklahoma is a top-tier state financially: military retirement and active-duty pay are both 100% exempt, 100% disabled veterans get a complete homestead property tax exemption, and the state runs a sales tax exemption worth up to $25,000 of purchases per year that exists almost nowhere else in the country.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. SB 401 (2022) made 100% of military retirement pay exempt from Oklahoma income tax beginning with the 2022 tax year, replacing the old 'greater of $10,000 or 75%' formula. WARNING: the Oklahoma Tax Commission's general Help Center 'Exemptions' page still describes the superseded 75%/$10,000 rule; the full exemption is confirmed by the Oklahoma Senate and the ODVA benefits page.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Fully exempt. 100% of income received as salary or compensation for service in the Armed Forces is deductible from Oklahoma taxable income, covering active and reserve component pay. Nonresident military spouses stationed in Oklahoma are exempt.
incomeTax.notes: Oklahoma has an income tax with a top rate of 4.75%, but it is effectively irrelevant to most military households given the full exemptions for both retirement and active-duty pay. VA disability compensation, DIC and SBP/RCSBP annuities are also tax-free.

states.propertyTax: Oklahoma grants a COMPLETE exemption of the full fair cash value of the homestead — not a capped deduction — to honorably discharged Oklahoma residents rated 100% permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected cause (disability sustained through military action or accident, or disease contracted during active service). This is among the cleanest 100% exemptions in the country: no dollar cap, no acreage-based dilution, no income test. Unremarried surviving spouses of qualifying veterans retain the exemption. Apply using Oklahoma Tax Commission Form 998 (2026 version published) with VA documentation, filed with the county assessor. Separately, 100% disabled veterans receive a motor vehicle excise tax exemption on one vehicle per three-year period (surviving spouses are NOT eligible for the vehicle excise exemption, a notable gap), and disabled veterans at 50%+ get reduced annual vehicle registration.
states.education: Oklahoma's veteran-specific education benefits are thinner than its tax benefits, and this is the state's weakest category. Oklahoma National Guard Educational Assistance covers tuition, mandatory fees and academic service fees at Oklahoma public colleges, up to 18 credit hours per semester with lifetime caps of 120 undergraduate and 40 graduate credit hours. Heroes Promise provides tuition assistance at Oklahoma publics (or partial coverage at privates) to children of service members killed in the line of duty after January 1, 2000, valid until age 21 or degree completion, five-year maximum. A Technology School Tuition Waiver gives veterans and children of MIA/POW service members a FULL tuition waiver at state-supported technology centers — an underappreciated benefit covering skilled-trades training. Wartime veterans who left school to serve (WWII, Korea, Vietnam eras) can receive high school diplomas. NOTE: Oklahoma does not have a broad Hazlewood-style tuition waiver for veterans generally or for children of 100% disabled living veterans at four-year institutions; the Oklahoma State Regents' student-veteran page confirms only the National Guard waiver among state programs.
states.employment: The Oklahoma Office of Veterans Assistance arranges interviews for eligible veterans matched to state executive branch positions. Private sector employers may establish written veteran preference policies, which requires registration in the Oklahoma Veterans Registry — registration in that registry is also a prerequisite for several other benefits including the driver license veteran identifier. State employees in reserve components receive 30 paid days of military leave annually, with the state covering the difference between state and military base pay. Professional licensing offers expedited processing and temporary licenses for military spouses, with military training recognized toward licensing requirements. DVOP specialists and Local Veteran Employment Representatives provide intensive placement services. Registry: registry.odva.ok.gov/registration.
states.vehicleRec: 100% disabled veterans get a FREE driver license (new, renewal or replacement). A 'Veteran' identifier can be added to a driver license or state ID for honorable or general discharges after registering in the Oklahoma Veterans Registry. Out-of-state stationed members and dependents keep license validity for 60 days after returning. Active duty members and spouses get reduced annual vehicle registration via Form 779. Eighty-five specialty plates: Medal of Honor free; Purple Heart at standard fee; Disabled Veteran (50%+) at reduced annual registration; Gold Star Spouse/Family/Parent/Survivor at standard fee. Recreation is genuinely generous: veterans with a 60%+ rating get FREE hunting and fishing permits plus exemption from the Wildlife Land Stamp; discounted lifetime combination licenses run $200 (under 60% disability) or just $25 (60%+); 100% disabled veterans additionally get free deer gun, deer archery, primitive firearms and bonus/special/second deer licenses. Nonresident service members stationed in Oklahoma buy at resident prices. The donor-funded Stars and Stripes License Project provides free licenses to veterans, Gold Star Pin recipients and military next of kin. State parks: FREE admission to all state-owned parks and museums for any honorably discharged Oklahoma resident veteran (bring an OK driver license and DD214) — no disability rating required.
states.cash: Oklahoma does not operate a general wartime service bonus or a large statewide emergency cash grant program; the state's financial benefit is delivered through tax exemption rather than cash transfer, and the $25,000 annual sales tax exemption functions as the de facto cash benefit (worth roughly $1,100-$2,300 per year in avoided sales tax at combined state-and-local rates of 4.5%-9%+). Veterans with a 70%+ disability rating receive FULL cost coverage at the seven state veterans homes, which is effectively a very large in-kind cash benefit for those needing long-term care. ODVA maintains a hotline at 833-993-0234.
states.homesHealth: Seven state veterans homes providing intermediate and skilled nursing, memory care and domiciliary care — one of the largest state systems per capita in the country: Ardmore (175 beds, 580-223-2266), Claremore (302, 918-342-5432), Clinton (148, 580-331-2200), Lawton (200, 580-351-6511), Norman (301, 405-360-5600), Sulphur (122, 580-331-6400) and Sallisaw (179, 539-230-2152). Admissions: 405-523-4092. Veterans rated 70%+ have their full cost covered. The Seaman First Class Billy Turner Oklahoma Veterans Cemetery (1555 Myall Street, Ardmore, 580-490-6489) provides gravesite, headstone, opening/closing, committal service and perpetual care free of charge for eligible veterans and family members. Tribal veterans cemeteries operate through the Seminole Nation (405-234-5242) and White Eagle Cemetery (580-762-8104).
other: THE SALES TAX EXEMPTION IS OKLAHOMA'S SIGNATURE BENEFIT AND IS NEARLY UNIQUE NATIONALLY: veterans certified by the VA at the 100% rate with a permanent service-connected disability may make up to $25,000 in exempt purchases per calendar year. The veteran's spouse or a member of the veteran's household may make purchases on the veteran's behalf, and additional exemption cards can be issued to authorized household members. Apply online through OkTAP with the VA certification letter from Muskogee.
The sales tax exemption does NOT cover cigarettes, tobacco, gasoline, or the 7% medical marijuana excise tax; it also runs alongside, not instead of, the separate vehicle excise tax break.
Unmarried surviving spouses get only a $1,000 annual sales tax exemption versus the veteran's $25,000 — a 96% cliff at the veteran's death that catches many families off guard.
Free state park and museum admission for ANY honorably discharged Oklahoma resident veteran, with no disability rating requirement — unusually broad.

The Oklahoma Veterans Registry is a gating mechanism: several benefits (private-sector hiring preference, driver license veteran identifier) require registration first, and veterans routinely miss benefits by skipping it.
Full cost coverage at state veterans homes at a 70% rating — a lower threshold than most states, which typically require 70-100% via federal per diem rules.
states.topHack: Get the $25,000 sales tax exemption card and add household members to it. Almost every 100%-rated Oklahoma veteran knows about the property tax exemption; far fewer actually execute the sales tax exemption, and fewer still realize their spouse and household members can be issued their own cards to make exempt purchases on the veteran's behalf. Used deliberately on a vehicle, appliances, furniture, building materials or a major home project, $25,000 of exempt purchases is worth roughly $1,100-$2,300 every single year, and it resets annually. The companion trap to avoid: the exemption collapses to $1,000/year for an unmarried surviving spouse, so front-load large planned purchases during the veteran's lifetime.

states.name: Oregon
states.headline: Oregon is the weakest state in this group for military retirees — it taxes military pensions for anyone who retired after October 1, 1991 at rates reaching 9.9%, and its disabled veteran property tax exemption is a small fixed deduction, though the dependent tuition waiver and emergency assistance fund are genuinely good.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Largely TAXED. Only service members who retired BEFORE October 1, 1991 may subtract all military retirement pay; those who retired after that date cannot. Members with service spanning the date calculate an eligible percentage based on months of pre-October-1991 service. In practice this means essentially every veteran retiring today pays full Oregon income tax on their military pension — one of the least favorable treatments in the nation.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Partially exempt. Military pay earned while stationed OUTSIDE Oregon is exempt. National Guard/Reserve pay for assignments away from home 21+ days is exempt. Oregon National Guard state active duty pay is exempt. An additional subtraction of up to $6,000 is available against remaining taxable military income. Nonresident military spouses under orders owe no Oregon tax on Oregon wages.
incomeTax.notes: Oregon's top marginal rate is 9.9%, among the highest in the country, and there is no standard-of-living offset from sales tax (Oregon has none). The combination of a fully taxable military pension and a 9.9% top rate makes Oregon the most expensive state in this jurisdiction set for a senior retiree. VA disability compensation, DIC, military disability retirement pay, Social Security, and SBP annuities attributable to pre-1991 service are tax-free.

states.propertyTax: Oregon's Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption is a fixed deduction from assessed value with two tiers, indexed upward 3% every year. Per the Oregon Department of Revenue's own form 310-676 for the current cycle: $32,512 for veterans with a VA- or Armed Forces-certified SERVICE-CONNECTED disability of 40% or more, and for unremarried surviving spouses of veterans who died from service-connected injury or illness; and $27,092 for veterans certified 40%+ disabled by a licensed physician (non-service-connected route), which carries an income cap of 185% of the prior year's Federal Poverty Level guidelines. Only the lower physician-certified tier is income-restricted. NOTE: the Army benefit library still lists last cycle's $31,565/$26,303 figures — the DOR form is the current authority. Claims are NOT automatic and must be filed with the county assessor by April 1 of the tax year claimed. At Oregon's typical effective rate near 1%, the exemption is worth only about $300/year — trivial relative to the income tax cost. Separately, reserve-component members called to federal active duty for 179+ days get an exemption that began at $60,000 of assessed value in 2005 and also rises 3% annually.
states.education: The Oregon Veterans Dependent Tuition Waiver (ORS 350.285) is the state's best education benefit: a FULL tuition waiver at Oregon public universities and Oregon Health & Science University for children age 23 or younger of Purple Heart recipients (2001 onward), and for children AND spouses of veterans with a 100% service-connected disability rating or who died on active duty or from service-connected causes. Maximum four years of undergraduate or two years of graduate study. Oregon National Guard State Tuition Assistance (ONGSTA) covers up to 90 credits at community colleges or 180 quarter / 120 semester credits at universities, requiring completion of basic training, good standing and a 2.0+ GPA. The Oregon Veterans Bridge Grant provides up to $5,000 to eligible Oregon resident veterans who cannot complete a VA-approved program because of missing required courses or student account debt — an unusual and practical gap-filler. Nonresident service members, spouses and dependents stationed in Oregon get resident tuition rates, and veterans using VA education benefits (GI Bill, DEA, Fry) get resident rates regardless of residency. High school diplomas are available to Oregon resident veterans who left school to serve in WWII, Korea, Vietnam or designated combat operations.
states.employment: State and public employment preference adds 5 points for veterans and 10 points for disabled veterans (10 points specifically for those rated 50%+). Critically, Oregon public employers MUST interview every qualified veteran applicant and must provide written reasons if the veteran is not selected — a stronger procedural protection than most states' point systems. State employees get 21 paid days annually for Guard/Reserve duty after six months of employment. The Oregon Military Family Leave Act requires employers with 25+ employees to grant 14 unpaid days to a military spouse or domestic partner when the service member is called to active duty. Oregon licensing boards accept military training and experience as substitutes for civilian education and experience requirements. WorkSource Oregon provides LVER and DVOP specialists with priority of service.
states.vehicleRec: Free veteran designation on driver licenses, instruction permits and ID cards (standard fees still apply); requires a DD214 showing honorable discharge. Plates available include Medal of Honor, Disabled Veteran (service-connected rating; note this plate does NOT confer special parking privileges in Oregon), Veteran Recognition with optional branch insignia, and Gold Star Family for parents, siblings, surviving spouses and dependents of those killed in action. Recreation is a bright spot: a FREE combination hunting/fishing/shellfish license for veterans at just a 25% disability rating, plus a discounted $25 elk tag, renewed annually. The Oregon Disabilities Hunting & Fishing Permit (65%+ rating) is valid five years and provides accommodations including fishing assistance, electric reels, hunting from a vehicle, and special facility access. Resident service members buy reduced $17 big game and game bird licenses; nonresidents stationed in Oregon pay resident prices. State Parks Special Access Pass for disabled veterans with a service-connected disability gives free camping (up to 10 nights at a single park or 30 days aggregate), free RV, tent and horse campsites and free day-use parking, valid ten years.
states.cash: The Oregon Veterans' Emergency Financial Assistance Program (OVEFAP) provides one-time emergency grants (amount varies by need) for housing, medical and dental expenses and transportation, paid directly to creditors. Eligible: honorably discharged Oregon resident veterans and their unremarried surviving spouses and children with immediate financial need. Apply through a county veteran service officer, by mail, or by email to ORVets.BENEFITS@odva.oregon.gov (503-373-2085). Oregon has no wartime service bonus program. ODVA also runs two unusual fiduciary services: Conservatorship Services, which authorizes conservators for veterans and family members to manage financial affairs, establish budgets and apply for benefits; and Representative Payee Services, providing limited-capacity bill payment for housing, utilities, care, food, medications and personal expenses with budget establishment and financial goal planning.
states.homesHealth: Two Oregon Veterans' Homes providing long-term, Alzheimer's/dementia and rehabilitative care: The Dalles Veterans' Home (151 beds, 541-296-7190 ext. 52330) and the Edward C. Allworth Veterans' Home in Lebanon (154 beds, 541-570-7477). Eligibility covers honorably discharged veterans, spouses, surviving spouses and Gold Star Parents; residents must demonstrate ability to pay the resident cost-share and need skilled nursing as determined by a physician or the VA. Oregon does not operate its own state veterans cemetery system — burial is handled through five VA national cemeteries located throughout the state, with no burial fees for eligible veterans and family members.
other: The October 1, 1991 military retirement cutoff is the single most consequential fact about Oregon for veterans: if you retired after that date, your entire pension is taxed at rates up to 9.9%, and no amount of property tax exemption offsets it.
Oregon has NO sales tax, which partially offsets the high income tax for veterans whose income is mostly non-taxable VA compensation rather than a pension.
The free hunting/fishing combination license kicks in at only a 25% disability rating — one of the lowest thresholds in the country.
Oregon public employers must not only give preference points but must INTERVIEW every qualified veteran applicant and justify non-selection in writing.
The Veterans Bridge Grant (up to $5,000) is nearly unknown and specifically designed for veterans stuck mid-degree because of an account hold or a missing prerequisite the GI Bill won't cover.
ODVA Conservatorship and Representative Payee services are a rare state-run fiduciary offering for veterans with diminished capacity — most states refer this to private conservators.
The DOR property tax exemption amounts rise 3% every single year automatically, so any figure you read more than 12 months old is wrong.
states.topHack: If you have a child and a 100% service-connected rating (or a Purple Heart), the Oregon Veterans Dependent Tuition Waiver is worth vastly more than every Oregon tax benefit combined — a full four-year tuition waiver at any Oregon public university or OHSU for each eligible child age 23 or under, and for your spouse. That is a six-figure benefit in a state whose property tax exemption is worth about $300 a year. The second move: file the property tax exemption claim with your COUNTY ASSESSOR by April 1 — it is not automatic, it does not carry over from a prior owner, and a large share of eligible Oregon veterans simply never file.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.headline: Pennsylvania never taxes retirement income of any kind, so military pensions are fully exempt, and its Disabled Veterans Real Estate Tax Exemption is a genuine 100% wipeout of property tax with a generous $114,637 income threshold — but it is strictly limited to 100% P&T, blind, paralyzed or multiple-limb-loss veterans.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Pennsylvania does not tax retirement income of any kind, so military retired pay is not taxable in Pennsylvania. SBP, RCSBP and RSFPP annuities are exempt, as are VA disability compensation, pension payments, DIC, and VA specially adapted housing and motor vehicle grants.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Partially taxed. Active-duty pay IS taxed for service members who reside in Pennsylvania and serve within the state; pay earned while on FEDERAL active duty outside Pennsylvania is tax-free. National Guard compensation for state active duty ordered due to an emergency is exempt. Reserve-component differential pay is taxable except in a combat zone. Nonresident military spouses under orders are exempt.
incomeTax.notes: Pennsylvania's flat personal income tax is 3.07%, and the state does not tax Social Security. Local earned income taxes (typically 1-3%) are levied separately by municipalities and school districts and generally do apply to earned income, though not to retirement income.

states.propertyTax: The Disabled Veterans Real Estate Tax Exemption is a FULL exemption from real estate tax on the principal residence — not a capped deduction. Eligibility is narrow but the benefit is total: honorable or under-honorable-conditions discharge; service during established war dates or receipt of an Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal; a 100% total and permanent service-connected disability rating from the VA, OR blindness, paralysis, or loss of two or more limbs due to military service; Pennsylvania residency; and the home must be the principal residence owned solely by the veteran or as an estate by the entirety. The program applies a financial-need test administered by the State Veterans Commission: gross annual household income of $114,637 or less AUTOMATICALLY qualifies (this threshold is adjusted periodically), and applicants above it must demonstrate that allowable monthly expenses exceed household income — so exceeding the threshold is a rebuttable presumption, not a hard cutoff. Unremarried surviving spouses may continue receiving the exemption. Apply through your County Director of Veterans Affairs (Ra-retx@pa.gov). Note that Pennsylvania offers NO partial exemption scaled by rating — below 100% P&T (or the blind/paralyzed/limb-loss categories) there is no state property tax benefit at all.
states.education: Pennsylvania Educational Gratuity pays $500 per term or semester for up to four scholastic years to children ages 16-23 of honorably discharged veterans who are 100% disabled or died during wartime, requiring five years of Pennsylvania residency before application (apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs; Ra-eg@pa.gov) — a modest amount that has not kept pace with tuition. The Postsecondary Educational Gratuity Program (PEGP) is far richer: it waives tuition, fees AND on-campus room and board for children age 25 or younger of National Guard members and other service members whose service-connected death occurred after 1976 (or 2001+), for full-time enrollment (PHEAA, 800-692-7392, pegp@pheaa.org). Educational Grant for POW/MIA Children pays up to $1,200 depending on state funding. The National Guard Education Assistance Program (EAP) is capped at $4,245 per semester with a lifetime limit of 10 full-time semesters or 120 part-time credits, requiring a six-year service commitment. The Military Family Education Program (MFEP) extends benefits to National Guard DEPENDENTS in exchange for a six-year commitment by the member, paying the lesser of tuition plus technology fees or the resident rate at a state-owned university, for up to five years (six years post-separation for spouses; age 26 limit for children). PHEAA also disregards a veteran's Student Aid Index and Pell eligibility to award the maximum state grant, and excludes VA benefit payments from income calculations. Honorably discharged resident veterans get early course registration at Pennsylvania public institutions.
states.employment: Veterans' preference adds 10 POINTS to passing state and municipal employment examination scores, and applies to appointments, promotions AND retention during layoffs — the retention protection is stronger than most states. Eligibility covers those who completed their initial obligation with a non-dishonorable discharge, served on active duty during war or conflict, currently serve in the reserves, are within 90 days of discharge, or are the surviving or disabled spouse of an eligible veteran (717-783-6655, ra-cs-vetpreference@pa.gov). State employees receive 15 days of paid military leave per year, and National Guard members get paid leave for ALL state active duty orders with no loss of seniority or efficiency rating. Employers must continue health benefits for at least 30 days during active military duty. PA CareerLink (pacareerlink.pa.gov) provides resume building, job alerts, a military skills translator, VR&E information and apprenticeships.
states.vehicleRec: Free veteran designation on driver's licenses and IDs, appearing automatically at renewal. 53 distinctive military plates. Veterans with a 100% service-connected disability get a FREE 'Severely Disabled Veteran' plate that confers two real privileges: parking in accessible areas, and the right to park for 60 MINUTES LONGER than the posted legal time limit — an unusual and genuinely useful perk. Veterans at 10%-99% can obtain a fee-based plate. Medal of Honor plates are requested in writing through the Bureau of Veterans Affairs at Fort Indiantown Gap. Driver's licenses remain valid while stationed outside PA and for 45 days after return or discharge, extending to the spouse and dependent children in the same household. CDL skills and knowledge waivers for qualifying MOSs (717-412-5300). Recreation: LIFETIME FREE fishing license (annual renewal required) for PA residents with a 100% service-connected rating; lifetime free hunting and furtaker licenses for residents with war/conflict-related disability including limb loss, a 100% rating, or 100% unemployability. Veterans at 60%-99% pay just $2.97 for hunting, furtaker or fishing licenses, and the $2.97 hunting license includes an antlered deer tag, both fall and spring turkey tags and small game privileges. Former POWs pay $2.97. Recently deployed reserve members (60+ consecutive days in the past 24 months) get a free fishing license per deployment and $2.97 hunting licenses.
states.cash: Veterans Temporary Assistance Program provides up to $1,600 in a twelve-month period for emergency financial aid, available to Pennsylvania resident veterans or surviving spouses with honorable discharge and qualifying active duty service or a service-connected disability. Blind Veterans Pension and the Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension each pay $150 PER MONTH ($1,800/year) for life. The Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension requires PA residency at the time of entering military service, honorable or under-honorable-conditions discharge, a service-connected injury or disease causing loss or loss of use of two or more extremities, and at least a 40% disability rating in each affected limb; apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs with DD214, proof of PA residency at entry, and the VA decision letter. IMPORTANT: the Persian Gulf Conflict Veterans' Benefit Program (the state bonus) is CLOSED — its application deadline passed in August 2018 and no new applications are accepted. National Guard members killed in the line of duty on state duty generate a monthly income benefit equal to the member's monthly salary, CPI-adjusted annually, with claims due within 3 years (717-787-2492).
states.homesHealth: Pennsylvania operates six state veterans homes through DMVA (Hollidaysburg, Erie, Pittsburgh, Scranton, Spring City/Southeastern, and Delaware Valley), providing skilled nursing, personal care and domiciliary care — one of the larger state systems in the country, though the Army benefit library's Pennsylvania page did not enumerate them and bed counts should be confirmed with DMVA directly. Indiantown Gap National Cemetery and Washington Crossing National Cemetery serve as the principal VA national cemeteries in-state. The PA National Guard Association's State Sponsored Life Insurance provides $1,000 of no-cost coverage to all active PA National Guard members, with additional coverage from $10,000 to $260,000, spouse and child coverage, and a $15,000 emergency death benefit paid within 24 hours, continuing until age 70 with no hazardous duty restrictions (pngas.org).
other: Pennsylvania never taxes ANY retirement income — military, civilian, IRA or 401(k) distributions after 59½ — making it one of the most retiree-friendly income tax regimes in the nation despite having an income tax.

The property tax exemption's $114,637 income figure is a threshold for AUTOMATIC qualification, not a hard cap: above it you can still qualify by showing allowable monthly expenses exceed household income. Many veterans wrongly self-disqualify.
There is no partial property tax exemption in Pennsylvania — it is 100% P&T (or blind/paralyzed/two-limb loss) or nothing, unlike neighboring states with sliding scales.
The Severely Disabled Veteran plate grants a 60-minute grace period beyond posted parking time limits, a privilege distinct from accessible parking.
The $2.97 hunting license for 60-99% disabled veterans bundles an antlered deer tag plus both turkey tags plus small game — a package worth well over $100 at retail.
The Blind Veterans Pension and Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension are $150/month lifetime payments that stack on top of federal VA compensation and are frequently unclaimed.
The Persian Gulf Conflict Veterans' Bonus is permanently closed (deadline August 2018) — third-party sites still list it as available.

agency.name: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
agency.phone: 717-861-8910 (DMVA); County Directors of Veterans Affairs handle most state benefit applications

states.topHack: Apply for the Disabled Veterans Real Estate Tax Exemption even if your household income exceeds $114,637. The income figure is widely misreported as a cap; it is actually the level at which need is AUTOMATICALLY presumed. Above it, the State Veterans Commission still grants the exemption if you document that allowable monthly expenses exceed household income — and for a 100% P&T veteran in a high-millage Pennsylvania school district, that is a complete elimination of a $5,000-$9,000 annual bill. Second, if you have loss or loss of use of two or more extremities at 40%+ each, claim the Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension: $150/month for life, paid by the state on top of everything the VA pays you, and almost nobody applies.

states.name: Puerto Rico
states.headline: Puerto Rico newly exempted all military retirement pay as of tax year 2025 and offers free University of Puerto Rico tuition plus a full property tax exemption for totally disabled veterans, but active-duty pay earned on-island is fully taxed and chronic fiscal strain limits program reliability.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt as of the 2025 tax year. Legislation signed August 29, 2024 exempts all military retired pay from Puerto Rico territorial income taxes. Previously the exemption was prorated based on years served in Puerto Rico versus elsewhere. Military disability retirement pay received as a pension, annuity or similar allowance is also excluded from taxable income.
incomeTax.activeDuty: TAXED. Resident service members stationed in Puerto Rico must pay Puerto Rico income taxes on all military pay earned there — a significant disadvantage relative to the many states that exempt active-duty pay entirely.
incomeTax.notes: Puerto Rico operates its own income tax system separate from the federal one (bona fide residents generally exclude PR-source income from US federal tax). Retirees under 60 receive an $11,000 standard deduction; those 60 and older receive $15,000. There is an additional veteran income tax exemption of $1,500, or $3,000 for married filing jointly where both spouses are veterans.

states.propertyTax: Puerto Rico offers a three-tier property tax exemption administered through CRIM (Centro de Recaudación de Ingresos Municipales). A standard veteran exemption covers up to $5,000 of appraised home value. Veterans with a service-connected disability of 50% or more receive an exemption on the first $50,000 of appraised value. Veterans who are 100% TOTALLY DISABLED receive a COMPLETE property tax exemption. All tiers apply to the primary residence and land up to 1,000 square meters urban or one cuerda rural. Note that Puerto Rico property tax valuations are notoriously outdated — many properties are still assessed on 1957-era values — so even the $5,000 standard exemption can cover a meaningful share of the assessed base, while the practical cash value of all tiers is lower than mainland equivalents. Verify current figures and application procedure directly with CRIM (portal.crim360.com), as PR fiscal legislation has changed frequently under the fiscal oversight board.
states.education: FREE TUITION at the University of Puerto Rico and its regional colleges for Puerto Rican veterans who do not have VA education benefits available — a full-ride benefit for the veteran personally, which is rarer than dependent-only programs. Dependents of veterans receive a 50% REDUCTION in tuition at the University of Puerto Rico. The 65th Infantry Regiment Scholarship funds bachelor's or master's degrees for children of veterans who are under 26 with a 2.5 GPA (Beca65@opv.pr.gov, 787-758-5760). The FIGNA Military Education Incentive pays up to $50 per credit for bachelor's degrees and $75 per credit for master's and doctoral degrees, maximum 18 credits annually, requiring a $5 monthly FIGNA membership contribution. Service members called to active duty receive priority registration and waived readmission fees on return. Wartime veterans who left school to serve can request high school diplomas.
states.employment: Government hiring preference adds 10 points or 10%, whichever is greater, to examination scores — among the strongest preference formulas in any US jurisdiction. Honorably discharged veterans have reinstatement rights to the same or a similar position within 180 days. New government employees may purchase up to 5 years of military service credit toward retirement. Federal hiring preference (5-point and 10-point) and USERRA protections apply as in the states.
states.vehicleRec: One FREE veteran license plate, with additional plates at $10, requiring verification of honorable discharge. Veterans rated 100% disabled receive a COMPLETE exemption from vehicle taxes and license plate fees. Notably, veterans aged 60 and older receive vehicle tax and fee exemptions REGARDLESS of disability status — an age-based benefit with no mainland parallel. VA-provided adaptive vehicles are exempt from taxes and fees. Recreation is limited: a 10% discount on fees at Puerto Rico parks, beaches, zoos and recreational facilities, extended to the veteran's spouse and minor or disabled children.
states.cash: Cash programs are thin. The principal one is the FIGNA National Guard Annuity, which pays $100 per month to retired Puerto Rico National Guard members aged 55-59 with 20+ years of service who are FIGNA members — a bridge payment before other retirement income begins (FIGNA: 787-253-4040, servicio@figna.pr.gov). There is no general territorial wartime bonus or broad emergency financial assistance fund comparable to mainland state programs. Puerto Rico's fiscal position under the PROMESA oversight board means cash benefit programs are vulnerable to suspension, and current-year funding status should be confirmed directly with the Office of the Veteran's Advocate.
states.homesHealth: Casa del Veterano in Juan Díaz is the territorial veterans home: a 240-bed facility providing domiciliary and nursing care (Carretera 532 Km 5.6, Juan Díaz, PR 00795; 787-837-6874 / 787-837-6550). Eligibility covers honorably discharged veterans, spouses, surviving spouses and Gold Star Parents. Burial: Puerto Rico National Cemetery in Bayamón (50 Avenida Cementerio Nacional, 787-798-8400) and Morovis National Cemetery (900 Carretera 137, same phone) are VA national cemeteries; the Atlantic Garden Veteran Cemetery in Aguadilla (Garden of Eden Boulevard, State Road 110, 787-221-6858, agvcaguadilla@gmail.com) is the territorial cemetery. Health care runs through the VA Caribbean Healthcare System, which serves one of the highest veteran-population-per-capita caseloads in the VA system and has historically faced access and staffing pressure.
other: The military retirement exemption is BRAND NEW (signed August 29, 2024, effective tax year 2025) — many advisors and nearly all third-party benefit summaries still describe the old prorated formula based on years served on-island.
Vehicle tax and fee exemption for ALL veterans aged 60+, with no disability requirement, has no mainland state equivalent.
Free University of Puerto Rico tuition for the VETERAN personally (not just dependents) is unusually generous — most states waive tuition only for survivors and dependents.
Active-duty pay earned in Puerto Rico is fully taxed, which makes PR materially worse than most states for currently-serving members even as it improved for retirees.
Puerto Rico residents generally exclude PR-source income from US federal income tax, so the territorial exemption on military retirement can mean a pension is untaxed at both levels.

Program funding is subject to the PROMESA fiscal oversight board; benefit availability and amounts have been less stable than in mainland states, so confirm current status before relying on any figure.
Property assessments are based on decades-old valuations, which distorts the practical value of the tiered exemptions relative to their headline dollar amounts.

agency.name: Puerto Rico Office of the Veteran's Advocate (Oficina del Procurador del Veterano)

states.topHack: If you are a bona fide Puerto Rico resident, your military pension can now be untaxed at BOTH levels simultaneously — exempt from PR territorial income tax under the August 2024 law effective for tax year 2025, and excluded from US federal income tax as Puerto Rico-source income under IRC 933 for bona fide residents. Very few retirees have caught up to this, because the prior prorated rule was in place for decades. The second underused item: veterans aged 60+ get vehicle tax and registration fee exemptions with no disability rating required at all — a benefit that exists nowhere on the mainland and that almost no one claims.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.headline: Rhode Island exempts military retirement pay and offers a rare tuition waiver at just a 10% disability rating, but it taxes active-duty pay, delegates property tax relief entirely to 39 municipalities with small and wildly inconsistent amounts, and pairs it all with a high cost of living.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Rhode Island exempts military retired pay from personal income tax under RIGL 44-30-12. SBP, RCSBP and RSFPP annuities are also exempt, as is VA disability retirement pay received as a pension or annuity.
incomeTax.activeDuty: TAXED. Active-duty military pay is subject to Rhode Island income tax for residents and follows federal rules. Military pay of NONRESIDENT service members stationed in Rhode Island is not subject to RI income tax, and Rhode Island follows federal combat zone exclusion rules.
incomeTax.notes: Rhode Island's income tax tops out at 5.99%. The state also has a separate modest pension/Social Security exclusion for retirees meeting age and income tests. The military retirement exemption is the main military-specific relief, and it is a full exemption rather than a capped subtraction.

states.propertyTax: Rhode Island does NOT provide a statewide property tax exemption — relief is delegated to each of the 39 cities and towns under RIGL 44-3-4 (veterans and widows/widowers of veterans), 44-3-5 (Gold Star parents) and 44-3-24. The statutory amounts set in the general laws are very low, but municipalities are authorized to increase them by local ordinance and the resulting amounts vary dramatically from town to town — some communities grant only a few hundred dollars of assessed value reduction, while others grant substantially more or offer full exemptions for totally disabled veterans. The RI Office of Veterans Services explicitly states 'exemptions vary by town' and directs applicants to their local tax assessor with a DD-214. Eligibility generally requires other-than-dishonorable discharge and wartime service during WWII, Korea, Vietnam, or a recognized conflict after Vietnam. Categories include general veteran, disabled veteran, former POW, Gold Star parent, and surviving spouse. BECAUSE THERE IS NO STATEWIDE FIGURE, NO SINGLE 2026 DOLLAR AMOUNT CAN BE STATED — you must check your specific municipality's ordinance, and the Division of Municipal Finance publishes a periodic report of municipal exemptions by town.
states.education: The Disabled Veterans Tuition Waiver is Rhode Island's standout and uses a remarkably low threshold: Rhode Island residents with a VA disability rating of just 10% OR MORE receive a tuition waiver at Rhode Island public institutions (CCRI, Rhode Island College, URI). The waiver covers TUITION ONLY — not fees, books or supplies. Free tuition for up to four years at state colleges and universities goes to surviving spouses and children ages 16-21 of National Guard members killed in the line of duty. The National Guard State Tuition Assistance Program (STAP) waives tuition for up to 5 classes per semester at CCRI, RIC or URI, and the State Tuition Exemption Program (STEP) adds one free course per summer semester, up to 4 classes per enlistment plus 4 more per extension year (RI National Guard Education Office, 401-275-4039). In-state tuition rates extend to active duty members serving 30+ days, their dependents, and eligible veterans using VA education benefits.
states.employment: Civil service preference gives standard veterans a 5-point credit on exam scores and disabled WARTIME veterans a 10-point credit. Eligibility requires 30+ days of active duty with honorable discharge, or fewer than 30 days with a service-connected discharge, or 20+ years of Guard/Reserve service. State employees called to federal active duty receive differential pay for one year covering the gap between state and federal pay. Rhode Island's Military Family Leave provisions are tiered by employer size: employers with 51+ employees must grant up to 30 unpaid days and those with 15-50 employees up to 15 unpaid days when a family member is activated for 30+ days. DLT career centers provide priority of service (Veterans Service Coordinator, 401-462-4131, dlt.vets@dlt.ri.gov).
states.vehicleRec: Free 'Veteran' or 'Disabled Veteran' (100% VA rating) designation on driver's licenses and IDs. Active duty members get a special operator's license valid until 30 days post-discharge. FREE vehicle registration AND free driver's license for wartime veterans with serious disabilities — specifically those who lost limbs, received a VA grant for an adapted vehicle, hold a 100% rating, or are rated unemployable. Disabled veteran parking placard for 100% service-connected veterans. Eight distinctive plates: Purple Heart plates are free with 2 sets authorized and TRANSFER TO THE SURVIVING SPOUSE; Disabled Veteran plates are free (1 set for 100% disabled); Veteran and Gold Star Family plates available. Recreation: complete exemption from hunting and fishing license fees for 100% disabled veterans; valid licenses remain valid for 6 months post-discharge; nonresident service members buy at resident prices (401-222-6647). State parks: FREE entry and parking at state recreational facilities and beaches for veterans with a 100% service-connected rating, with no renewal required for permanent ratings; 100% disabled veterans are also exempt from ALL GREENS FEES at Goddard Park Golf Course (401-667-6200).
states.cash: Military Family Relief Fund provides grants up to $5,000 for emergency expenses including rent, utilities, medical costs, prescriptions, insurance and vehicle payments, for active duty, National Guard and Reserve members with 1+ year of satisfactory service and documented financial need; additional casualty-based grants are available for Purple Heart recipients, non-combat injuries, KIA, or MIA/POW situations (401-275-1241/1242/1243/1240). The Service Members Assistance Fund (SMAF) provides annual grants to National Guard members and DEERS-enrolled dependents experiencing financial hardship (401-275-1242 or 1240). Rhode Island also pays burial expenses at public expense for honorably discharged wartime veterans whose families cannot afford services. Rhode Island has no general wartime service bonus.
states.homesHealth: The Rhode Island Veterans Home in Bristol (480 Metacom Avenue, 401-253-8000) provides assisted living and nursing care for wartime veterans, with on-site medical and nursing care, rehabilitation, X-ray, lab, dental, pharmacy, physical and occupational therapy and a VA counselor. Eligibility requires 90+ days of active duty during wartime plus two years of Rhode Island residency, or entry into service from Rhode Island. The Rhode Island Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Exeter (301 South County Trail, 401-268-3088) provides burial with military funeral honors; burials are free for veterans while eligible family members are charged a grave liner fee. Eligibility matches VA national cemetery standards plus a two-year Rhode Island residency requirement or entry into service from RI. The state provides a firing squad and a live bugler for 'Taps' for honorably discharged wartime veterans on request through the funeral director.
other: The 10% disability tuition waiver threshold is one of the lowest in the entire country — most states require 100%, and many require the veteran to be deceased. It covers tuition only, not fees or books.

Property tax relief is entirely municipal: there is no statewide exemption amount, and identical veterans in adjacent towns can receive wildly different benefits. Always check the specific town ordinance.
Purple Heart license plates transfer to the surviving spouse, which is unusual.
100% disabled veterans golf free at Goddard Park — all greens fees waived.
Half-fare RIPTA bus passes for veterans with a 70%+ disability rating cost $25 and are valid five years; no-fare passes are available below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (401-784-9500 ext. 604).
Public shelters waive pet adoption fees for veterans with the veteran designation on their driver's license, one pet per six months.
Wartime disabled veterans get FIRST placement preference in public elderly housing, with additional municipal preferences varying by community.
A Veterans Treatment Court operates in Kent County (401-458-5106, vetscourt@courts.ri.gov) alongside a statewide Veterans Justice Outreach program (401-639-0163).

agency.name: Rhode Island Office of Veterans Services

states.topHack: Get rated at 10%. In Rhode Island a mere 10% VA disability rating unlocks a tuition waiver at CCRI, Rhode Island College and the University of Rhode Island — the lowest qualifying threshold for a tuition benefit of any jurisdiction in this group, and a benefit most veterans assume requires a total rating. Combine it with in-state rates and the GI Bill and a degree becomes nearly free. Second: because Rhode Island has no statewide property tax exemption, call your town assessor directly rather than reading any state-level summary — several municipalities have adopted far more generous local ordinances than the statutory floor, and the only way to learn yours is to ask.

states.name: South Carolina
states.headline: South Carolina fully exempts military retirement pay at any age, gives 100% disabled veterans a complete property tax exemption covering the home plus five acres AND two vehicles, and recently made that exemption retroactive up to three years — a rare and valuable refund opportunity.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. South Carolina does not tax military retired pay, at any age, following the 2022 Workforce Enhancement and Military Recognition Act which removed the prior age-tiered caps. Military disability retirement pay is exempt, and spouses receiving SBP annuities are exempt from state income tax.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Partially taxed. Military pay received for service in a combat zone that is exempt from federal taxes is also exempt from South Carolina tax, but ordinary active-duty pay of South Carolina residents is otherwise taxable. National Guard and Reserve INACTIVE duty pay for weekend drills and annual training (up to 15 days) is exempt. Nonresident military spouses stationed in SC are exempt on wages earned in the state.
incomeTax.notes: South Carolina's top individual income tax rate has been declining under a multi-year reduction schedule and sits near 6% or below for 2026; confirm the exact current-year top rate with SCDOR. The full military retirement exemption applies regardless of age, which is more generous than the age-55 style restrictions common in other states.

states.propertyTax: Veterans with a VA service-connected rating of 100% total and permanent receive a COMPLETE property tax exemption on their owner-occupied home and land UP TO FIVE ACRES, plus exemption on TWO private passenger vehicles. Former POWs and Medal of Honor recipients receive the same treatment on a home and land up to one acre plus two vehicles. The 2024 expansions materially improved the program: the exemption now applies beginning with the YEAR IN WHICH THE DISABILITY OCCURS rather than the year of application; surviving spouses can claim the exemption IMMEDIATELY even if the deceased veteran never applied; vehicles titled to trusts qualify where the veteran or spouse is the beneficiary; and — most valuably — veterans applying in 2025 could claim RETROACTIVELY BACK TO 2023 where property taxes were paid on time, generating refunds. Apply via MyDORWAY at dor.sc.gov (form PT-401I), or mail to SCDOR, Government Services Division, PO Box 125, Columbia, SC 29214-0720 (803-898-5700, property.exemptions@dor.sc.gov). The five-acre allowance and the two-vehicle inclusion are both more generous than the typical one-acre, no-vehicle structure used elsewhere.
states.education: Free Tuition for Children of Certain War Veterans is the flagship: children age 26 or younger of qualifying veterans receive FULL TUITION WAIVERS at South Carolina public colleges, universities and technical institutions. The veteran parent must have been killed in action, died in service, have a service-connected disability, be POW/MIA, hold a 100% VA disability rating, or be a Medal of Honor or Purple Heart recipient, with wartime service and honorable discharge. Apply through SCDVA (803-647-2434 or the online application). In-state tuition rates extend to veterans with 90+ days of active duty service, active and reserve members, and their dependents, regardless of length of residency. The SC National Guard College Assistance Program (CAP) covers 100% of tuition and fees at state institutions up to $12,000 per year with a $25,000 lifetime cap for actively drilling SC National Guard members (803-299-2734).
states.employment: State hiring preference requires that at least one qualified veteran be interviewed for each full-time state position — an interview guarantee rather than a points system. State employees receive 15 workdays of paid military leave for training plus an additional 30 days for active duty in combat zones or declared emergencies. Public employees may purchase up to 6 years of retirement credit for military service at a minimum of 16% of career-highest annual pay per year. Operation Palmetto Employment (ope.sc.gov) is a statewide initiative connecting service members, veterans and spouses to civilian careers. SC Works centers provide career coaching, resume preparation and job training, and give veterans EXCLUSIVE ACCESS to new job listings for the first 24 hours — a concrete advantage rather than a procedural one (scworks.org).
states.vehicleRec: Free 'Veteran' designation on driver's licenses and permits. Driver's licenses remain valid 90 days after discharge for members stationed outside SC, and active duty members and dependents stationed out of state may renew online or by mail. Fifty-six military plate designs, several unusually generous: Medal of Honor recipients get THREE free sets plus free municipal parking; Purple Heart recipients get THREE free sets plus free municipal parking; Disabled Veteran plates (100% rating or combat disability) come as three free sets with motorcycle and disability options; Gold Star Family plates are free and include free parking. CDL knowledge and skills waivers for qualifying MOSs (CDLHelpDesk@scdmv.net). Recreation: FREE three-year disability combination licenses covering freshwater and saltwater fishing, hunting and waterfowl, or free disability fishing licenses, for disabled veterans providing VA disability certification dated within 12 months. Service members and dependents stationed in SC for 30+ days get resident hunting and fishing privileges with a military ID. Resident active duty stationed outside SC and home on leave may hunt and fish without licenses (big game and migratory bird permits still required). State parks: the SC All Park Passport is available at HALF PRICE ($49.50) for 100% disabled residents, the legally blind, seniors 65+, and SC National Guard members, providing unlimited park access for everyone in the vehicle plus free admission to historic sites (803-734-0156).
states.cash: The South Carolina Military Family Relief Fund (SCMFRF) provides tiered grants: status-based grants of $500, casualty-based grants of $1,000, and needs-based grants up to $2,000. Eligibility covers families of SC National Guard and US Armed Forces Reserve members called to active duty after September 11, 2001, with assistance covering food, housing, utilities and medical expenses; limited to one grant per fiscal year per person. Apply to SCDVA, ATTN: SCMFRF Coordinator, 1205 Pendleton Street, Ste. 369, Columbia, SC 29201 (803-734-0200). South Carolina has no general wartime service bonus program. The largest de facto cash benefit remains the retroactive property tax refund opportunity created by the 2024 expansion.
states.homesHealth: South Carolina operates SIX state veterans nursing homes — a large system relative to state population: E. Roy Stone Veterans Pavilion in Columbia (803-737-5301), Veterans' Victory House in Walterboro (843-538-3000), Richard Michael Campbell Veterans Nursing Home in Anderson (864-261-6734), Veteran Village in Florence (833-432-4600), Palmetto Patriots Home in Gaffney (864-649-2000) and Patriot's Village in Sumter (803-965-9002). Eligibility requires honorable discharge, one or more years of SC residency, and a skilled or intermediate care determination by the VA. Services include medical and nursing care, rehabilitation, pharmacy, recreation, social services, transportation and laundry (apply via SCDVA or county offices, 803-734-0200). The M.J. 'Dolly' Cooper State Veterans Cemetery in Anderson (864-332-8022) provides plots, grave liners, permanent markers and opening/closing at NO COST for veterans, with a $300 fee for an eligible spouse or child; it offers a columbarium, scattering garden and in-ground cremation options. Eligibility requires honorable discharge plus SC residency at entry, during service, or for five years.
other: THE RETROACTIVE REFUND IS THE BIG ONE: the 2024 expansion lets newly-approved 100% P&T veterans claim the property tax exemption back to the year the disability occurred — veterans applying in 2025 could reach back to 2023 — producing real refund checks for taxes already paid.
The exemption covers the home plus FIVE acres, versus the one-acre limit common in other states, which matters enormously for rural and semi-rural property.

Two private passenger vehicles are exempt from property tax as well — South Carolina taxes vehicles as property, so this is a recurring annual saving most states don't offer because they don't levy the tax at all.
Surviving spouses can now claim the exemption immediately even if the veteran never applied before dying — closing a gap that previously cost families years of relief.
Military retirement is exempt at ANY age, with no age-55 style gate.
Veterans get exclusive first-24-hour access to new job listings posted through SC Works.
Medal of Honor and Purple Heart recipients each get three free license plate sets plus free municipal parking statewide.
The $49.50 half-price All Park Passport covers everyone in the vehicle, not just the veteran.

agency.name: South Carolina Department of Veterans' Affairs (SCDVA)

states.topHack: If your 100% P&T rating was granted with an effective date earlier than the year you applied for the property tax exemption, file a retroactive claim through MyDORWAY. The 2024 statutory expansion tied the exemption to the year the disability OCCURRED rather than the year you filed paperwork, and it permits reaching back multiple years where taxes were paid on time — veterans applying in 2025 could claim back to 2023. Because VA rating decisions routinely carry effective dates one to three years before the decision letter arrives, a large share of newly-rated South Carolina veterans are sitting on an unclaimed refund of two or three full years of property tax on a house, five acres and two vehicles, and SCDOR will not volunteer it.

states.name: South Dakota
states.headline: No income tax at all, a $200,000 property tax exemption for permanently and totally disabled veterans with a full exemption for paraplegic veterans, and free state university tuition earned month-for-month by wartime service — though the legislature rejected expansion attempts in 2026.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Not taxed — South Dakota has no individual income tax whatsoever, so military retirement pay, active-duty pay, TSP distributions, SBP annuities and all other income are free of state income taxation.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Not taxed. No state individual income tax.
incomeTax.notes: South Dakota is one of the handful of states with no individual income tax and no corporate income tax.
