Revenue comes primarily from sales tax (state rate 4.2% plus municipal add-ons) and property tax, so the trade-off is a relatively high property tax burden — which is exactly why the disabled veteran property tax exemption matters so much here.

states.propertyTax: Two distinct programs. (1) The Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption exempts $200,000 of the full and true value of the dwelling — plus the garage and lot up to one acre — for veterans rated PERMANENTLY AND TOTALLY DISABLED as the result of a service-connected disability. Unmarried surviving spouses qualify if receiving Dependency and Indemnity Compensation as a result of the veteran's service-connected death and the property remains owner-occupied. Applications go to the county director of equalization ON OR BEFORE NOVEMBER 1 each year — an annual filing requirement that trips up many veterans. (2) Paraplegic veterans (and their unremarried surviving spouses) receive a FULL property tax exemption on the house, garage and lot up to one acre, where the property is specifically designed for wheelchair use; same November 1 deadline. 2026 LEGISLATIVE UPDATE: two expansion bills failed — a $225,000 exemption with income thresholds ($65,000 multi-income / $55,000 single-income households) died in committee, and a $300,000 exemption with no income restrictions was rejected by the Senate. One bill DID advance: the Senate Taxation Committee approved legislation allowing disabled veterans who missed application deadlines because of delayed VA rating decisions to receive refunds for up to FOUR YEARS of exemptions. Verify final enactment status of that refund bill with the SD Department of Revenue.
states.education: Free Tuition for Veterans is unusually structured and generous to the veteran personally: honorably discharged wartime veterans receive ONE MONTH OF FREE TUITION per month served during qualifying wartime periods, with a one-year minimum and a four-year maximum, for undergraduate degrees at state-supported universities and technical colleges. VA educational benefits must be exhausted first. Dependent programs: free tuition for children under 25 of service members who died during active duty; free tuition for spouses and children of POW/MIA service members for up to eight semesters; and free tuition for spouses and children of SD National Guard members disabled or killed in the line of duty. The SD National Guard receives a 100% REDUCTION in undergraduate tuition at state institutions, up to 128 undergraduate and 32 graduate credits, requiring service throughout each semester and 90% drill attendance. Honorary high school diplomas are available to wartime veterans who left school to serve.
states.employment: Hiring preference extends to state, county, city AND public education positions, with a strict priority order: disabled veterans first, then spouses of disabled veterans, then veterans, then unremarried surviving spouses. State employees in reserve components receive 15 days of military training leave annually, retain SD Retirement System service credit if they return within one year, and receive a quarterly wage adjustment covering the difference between state and military salary during state or federal active duty. The Department of Labor and Regulation provides specialized services including resume help, interview preparation, job referrals and priority of service at local DLR offices (reemployment assistance: 605-626-3179).
states.vehicleRec: 'Veteran' designation available on driver's licenses and ID cards for honorably discharged members. Licenses remain valid for members stationed outside the state plus 90 days after return. CDL military skills test waiver plus an Even Exchange Program waiving both knowledge and skills testing for specific MOSs. Specialty plates include Veteran (branch or operation choices), Disabled Veteran (requires 100% disability, SMC Level K, or extremity loss), Purple Heart, Medal of Honor (no fee), Gold Star Family, and Active Duty and Retired plates. Recreation: disabled veterans and former POWs pay just $10 FOR A FOUR-YEAR license, requiring a 40%+ VA disability rating, 40% SSA disability, or POW status — note the unusually low 40% threshold and the four-year term. Veterans at VA hospitals and service members stationed in state receive resident pricing. Active duty members stationed outside the state need no license to hunt or fish small game while on leave. State parks: a FREE LIFETIME state park license for 100% disabled veterans, SMC Level K recipients, former POWs and Purple Heart recipients, which includes free park entrance for the veteran and vehicle plus a 50% DISCOUNT ON CAMPING AND ELECTRICAL FEES.
states.cash: South Dakota still operates a WARTIME BONUS, which is increasingly rare. For non-hostile service it pays $100 for the first month and $20 for each additional month, capped at $240. For service in a hostile area it pays $150 for the first month and $50 for each additional month, capped at $500. Veterans with a 10%+ disability rating receive the maximum $500. Eligible service runs from August 2, 1990 onward, meaning Gulf War, OEF, OIF and later deployments all qualify. Burial-related cash: a $100 payment to beneficiaries of veterans without adequate burial funds (the veteran must have been an SD resident one year before military service or before death); up to $200 reimbursement toward government headstone installation; and $100 for professional military etching on a private headstone.
states.homesHealth: The Michael J. Fitzmaurice State Veterans Home in Hot Springs is a 100-bed facility providing nursing care, therapies and support services. Eligibility covers South Dakota resident veterans with honorable discharge, spouses married one or more years, and surviving spouses aged 60+. The South Dakota State Veterans Cemetery in Sioux Falls provides FREE burial for veterans including grave site, liner, headstone, niche cover and perpetual care; spouse and dependent burial costs $1,002. Three tribal veterans cemeteries also operate across the state. South Dakota does not operate a broader state-funded veterans health system beyond the single veterans home; VA facilities at Sioux Falls, Fort Meade and Hot Springs carry the clinical load.
other: One of the few states still paying a WARTIME BONUS for service from August 2, 1990 forward — up to $500 for hostile-area service, automatically maxed at $500 for anyone with a 10%+ disability rating.

The November 1 application deadline for the property tax exemption is ANNUAL and unforgiving; a 2026 bill advancing through the Senate Taxation Committee would allow up to four years of retroactive refunds for veterans whose VA rating decisions arrived late — confirm enactment.
2026 expansion attempts FAILED: a $225,000 income-tested exemption died in committee and a $300,000 uncapped exemption was rejected by the Senate, so $200,000 remains the figure.
Paraplegic veterans get a FULL exemption, not the $200,000 cap — a meaningful distinction for higher-value adapted homes.
The $10 four-year hunting/fishing license requires only a 40% rating, one of the lowest thresholds anywhere, and the four-year term makes the effective cost $2.50 a year.
Free tuition is earned month-for-month by the VETERAN personally, up to four years — a structure almost no other state uses.

With no income tax, South Dakota's veteran benefit value is concentrated almost entirely in the property tax exemption, which makes the annual November 1 filing the single highest-stakes administrative act in the state.

agency.name: South Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs

states.topHack: Put November 1 on a recurring calendar alarm. South Dakota's $200,000 disabled veteran property tax exemption must be re-filed with the county director of equalization by November 1 EVERY YEAR, and because the state has no income tax, this single filing is worth more than every other South Dakota veteran benefit combined. Veterans lose it constantly by assuming it renews automatically. If you already missed years because your VA rating decision arrived late, watch for the 2026 refund bill that cleared Senate Taxation — it would let you recover up to four years of exemptions retroactively. And if you served anywhere after August 2, 1990 and carry even a 10% rating, claim the $500 state wartime bonus; it is one of the last such programs still open in the country.

states.name: Tennessee
states.headline: No state income tax at all, five state veterans homes and five state cemeteries, but the disabled veteran property tax benefit is a reimbursement capped on only the first $175,000 of market value rather than a true exemption, and education benefits are thin.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Not taxed — Tennessee has no general state income tax and residents do not file an individual state income tax return. The former Hall income tax on interest and dividends was fully repealed effective 2021, so investment income is untaxed as well.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Not taxed. No state individual income tax.
incomeTax.notes: Tennessee has no individual income tax of any kind, including no tax on interest and dividends since the Hall tax repeal. TSP distributions are untaxed. The trade-off is one of the highest combined sales tax rates in the nation (state 7% plus local, often approaching 9.75%), which affects veterans with high consumption relative to income.

states.propertyTax: Tennessee runs a Property Tax RELIEF program (a reimbursement of taxes paid), not an exemption, and it is capped by market value. For 2026 the maximum market value on which relief is calculated for disabled veterans is $175,000 — tax on value above that is paid by the veteran. Eligibility requires owning and occupying the home as a primary residence, completing the 2026 F-16 consent form authorizing VA information release, and meeting ONE of three disability tests: (a) paraplegia, permanent paralysis, legal blindness, or loss of two or more limbs from service-connected causes; (b) 100% permanent total disability arising from prisoner-of-war status; or (c) service-connected permanent and total disability as determined by the VA. Crucially, there is NO INCOME LIMIT for the disabled veteran category — unlike the elderly and disabled homeowner categories, which for 2026 cap income at $38,470 and cap relief at only $33,600 of market value. Surviving spouses of disabled veterans get the same $175,000 cap using form F-16S, and must supply the veteran's death certificate and personal ID, remain unmarried, and show the veteran's death resulted from service-connected combat causes or deployment-related circumstances. Apply through your county trustee or city collecting official; some counties and cities offer supplemental local relief on top.
states.education: Tennessee's education offerings are the weakest part of its package. The Helping Heroes Grant pays up to $1,000 per semester for enrollment of 12+ hours, or $500 for 6-11 hours, to honorably discharged veterans of post-9/11 conflicts, for a maximum of 8 semesters or until a bachelor's degree is earned — a modest supplement rather than a tuition waiver. The Tennessee STRONG Act reimburses Tennessee National Guard members 100% of the maximum resident undergraduate or graduate in-state tuition, covering up to 130 undergraduate or 40 graduate semester hours, and is the state's most substantial education benefit. Public university veterans receive early registration ahead of the general student population. Honorary high school diplomas are available for wartime veterans who left school early. NOTE: Tennessee does not operate a broad Hazlewood-style tuition waiver for veterans or a comprehensive dependent tuition waiver comparable to Texas, South Carolina or Virginia — dependents rely primarily on federal transferred GI Bill benefits and the state's general HOPE/TELS lottery scholarships.
states.employment: State employees receive 20 days of paid military leave annually for reserve duty. Federal hiring preference (5 or 10 points) applies, and USERRA reemployment protections govern job restoration. Veterans employment assistance flows through the American Job Center network. Tennessee's state-level hiring preference structure is less formalized than the point systems in neighboring states, and the Army benefit library does not document a specific state civil service point award — confirm current state hiring preference terms with the Tennessee Department of Human Resources.
states.vehicleRec: License plates with free initial issuance and varying renewal fees: Medal of Honor (free, no annual fee), Purple Heart (free, no annual fee), Disabled Veteran (free, no annual fee), Gold Star Family (free, no annual fee), and Honorably Discharged ($29.80 initial, $26.50 annual). Veteran designation available on driver's licenses, with an extension code for active duty members. Motor vehicle tax benefits: active duty members stationed in Tennessee are exempt from sales tax on vehicles, and disabled veterans who received VA vehicle grants are exempt from registration fees and local privilege taxes. CDL skills test waiver for members with military commercial driving experience. Recreation: a LIFETIME hunting and fishing license for a ONE-TIME $10 FEE for veterans with 100% total disability OR a 30%+ WARTIME disability rating — the 30% wartime threshold is notably low and the lifetime term makes this exceptional value. State parks: veterans get free one-night camping on their service branch's birthday and on Veterans Day, a 25% discount on cabins and camping, and a 20% golf discount; 100% disabled veterans receive a 50% year-round camping and cabin discount.
states.cash: Tennessee does not operate a general wartime service bonus, a statewide veterans emergency financial assistance fund, or a property tax rebate beyond the Property Tax Relief program described above. This is a genuine gap relative to peer states — the Army benefit library's Tennessee entry lists no cash assistance programs in its state benefits section. Some counties and municipalities offer supplemental property tax relief or local emergency assistance through county veterans service officers; check locally. The absence of state cash programs is partly offset by the complete absence of state income tax.
states.homesHealth: Tennessee operates FIVE state veterans' homes providing long-term care, skilled nursing and rehabilitation, with free admission for eligible veterans: Murfreesboro (615-895-8850), Humboldt (731-784-8405), Knoxville (865-862-8100), Clarksville (931-245-4700) and Cleveland (423-813-3600). Tennessee also operates FIVE state veterans cemeteries providing free burial plots, grave opening and closing, government markers and perpetual care, with pre-registration available online. Five homes plus five cemeteries is a large state-run footprint relative to Tennessee's population and is the strongest non-tax element of the state's package.
other: No income tax of ANY kind, including no tax on interest and dividends since the Hall tax repeal in 2021 — relevant for retirees living on investment income.

The $175,000 market value cap makes Tennessee's property tax benefit a partial rebate rather than a true exemption; in higher-value Nashville, Franklin or Knoxville markets a substantial share of the bill remains.
There is NO income limit for the disabled veteran property tax relief category, unlike the elderly/disabled homeowner category which caps income at $38,470 and market value at just $33,600.
Property tax relief is a REIMBURSEMENT — you pay the bill and get money back — which creates a cash flow issue for veterans on fixed incomes.
The $10 LIFETIME hunting and fishing license requires only a 30% WARTIME disability rating, not 100% — one of the best recreation values in the country.
Five state veterans homes and five state cemeteries is an unusually large state-run infrastructure footprint.
Tennessee has essentially no state cash assistance or bonus programs for veterans, which is a real gap versus peer states.
Combined state and local sales tax approaching 9.75% is among the highest in the nation and partially offsets the no-income-tax advantage for lower-income veterans.
states.topHack: Buy the $10 lifetime hunting and fishing license the moment you hit a 30% wartime disability rating — not 100%. Nearly every Tennessee veteran assumes the lifetime license requires total disability, but a 30% wartime rating qualifies, and a one-time $10 payment covers hunting and fishing for the rest of your life in a state where an annual sportsman license runs well over $150. Second, on property tax: apply through your county trustee even though it is styled as 'relief' rather than an exemption, and note there is no income test for the disabled veteran category — veterans routinely skip applying because they assume the $38,470 income limit that governs the elderly category applies to them too. It does not.

states.name: Texas
states.headline: The most valuable overall package in the country: no income tax, a complete property tax exemption for 100% disabled veterans on a homestead of unlimited value, and the Hazlewood Act's 150 free credit hours that can be transferred to a child — a benefit routinely worth six figures per family.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Not taxed — Texas has no individual state income tax, so military retirement pay, active-duty pay, TSP distributions and SBP annuities are all free of state income taxation.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Not taxed. No state individual income tax.
incomeTax.notes: Texas has no individual income tax and the constitution requires a statewide referendum to impose one (a 2019 amendment made this even harder). Revenue relies on sales tax (6.25% state plus local up to 8.25% total) and notably high property taxes — which is precisely why the disabled veteran property tax exemption is the single most valuable state benefit in Texas.

states.propertyTax: Texas has the most valuable disabled veteran property tax structure in the nation, in large part because Texas property taxes are so high (effective rates commonly 1.5%-2.5%). (1) THE 100% EXEMPTION: veterans with a VA service-connected 100% total and permanent disability rating, OR rated at 100% due to individual unemployability, receive a TOTAL exemption from property tax on their residence homestead — no dollar cap, no acreage-based dilution, no income test. On a $500,000 Texas home this is worth $8,000-$12,000 every single year, making it the largest recurring state veteran benefit available anywhere in the US. (2) PARTIAL EXEMPTIONS BY RATING (Tax Code 11.22), which are flat dollar reductions of appraised value and much smaller: 10-29% rating = $5,000; 30-49% = $7,500; 50-69% = $10,000; 70-99% = $12,000. (3) DISABLED VETERANS 65+: $12,000 exemption if the service-connected disability is 10%+, or the veteran is blind or has lost use of a limb. (4) SURVIVING SPOUSES: unremarried surviving spouses of service members killed in action, missing in action, rated 100% disabled, or who died from VA-recognized presumptive conditions receive the 100% exemption. (5) DONATED HOMES: a separate exemption for residences donated by charitable organizations to disabled veterans, scaled by rating. All of this STACKS ON TOP OF the general residence homestead exemption for school district taxes, which is now $140,000 following the 2025 increase. Apply through your COUNTY APPRAISAL DISTRICT, not the state. The Comptroller administers a Local Government Relief program to reimburse jurisdictions heavily affected by the 100% exemption.
states.education: THE HAZLEWOOD ACT is the centerpiece: up to 150 CREDIT HOURS of tuition exemption including most fee charges at Texas public institutions of higher education. It does NOT cover living expenses, books or supply fees. Veteran eligibility requires: Texas as home of record at entry, entry into service in Texas, or Texas residency at entry; a minimum of 181 DAYS of active duty excluding training; honorable discharge or general discharge under honorable conditions; CURRENT Texas residency; no federal education benefits covering tuition and fees (or federal benefits that do not exceed Hazlewood's value); no default on state student loans; and satisfaction of the institution's GPA requirements. THE LEGACY ACT is what makes Hazlewood extraordinary: a veteran may TRANSFER unused hours to a child who is under 25 on the first day of the semester (extensions available for qualifying illness), classified as a Texas resident, and who is a biological, step- or adopted child or claimed dependent, meeting the same federal-benefit and academic standards. Only ONE child may use Legacy benefits at a time, but unused hours can be reassigned to another child. SPOUSES AND DEPENDENTS qualify in their own right only if the veteran is 100% total and permanent service-connected disabled, became totally disabled from a service-related injury, or is deceased, MIA or KIA — with GPA standards waived for families of deceased/MIA/KIA veterans. Contact: Texas Veterans Commission, 512-463-3168 / 877-898-3833, hazlewood@tvc.texas.gov. Also: Texas National Guard State Tuition Assistance covers up to 12 credit hours per semester for 10 semesters, need-based with a 2.0 GPA requirement.
states.employment: State employees in reserve components receive 15 paid workdays annually for authorized military training without loss of benefits, and reemployment rights within 5 years guarantee the same position or equivalent seniority, status and pay. Professional licensing through TDLR is unusually accommodating: military experience and training credited toward occupational licenses, NO late renewal fees if a license expires during active duty, a 2-year renewal extension, waived examination requirements, and expedited processing for out-of-state transfers (tdlr.texas.gov/military). The Texas Veterans Entrepreneur Program waives the $300 business registration fee for 100% veteran-owned businesses and provides a FIVE-YEAR FRANCHISE TAX WAIVER (requires a Veteran Verification Letter) — a substantial benefit for veteran business owners (830-658-3639, vep@tvc.texas.gov). Non-retired state employees may purchase up to 60 months of active duty service credit toward ERS retirement (877-275-4377). Texas Workforce Commission runs College Credit for Heroes, Operation Welcome Home and a leadership program.
states.vehicleRec: Free 'Veteran' or 'Disabled Veteran' designation on driver licenses and IDs. Disabled veterans rated 60%+ (or 40% with a lower extremity amputation) receive a NO-FEE driver license. Plates include Purple Heart, Disabled Veteran (50%+ disability or 40% amputation), Honorably Discharged Veteran, Medal of Honor (free) and Gold Star Family plates (free) for a parent, sibling, spouse or child of a service member killed in service. Recreation is excellent: disabled veterans rated 50%+ or with loss of use of a foot or leg receive a FREE SUPER COMBO LICENSE covering resident or nonresident hunting and all-water fishing, including archery, freshwater and saltwater endorsements and upland and migratory game bird endorsements (federal duck stamp separate). Active duty members who are Texas residents or stationed in Texas 6+ months also receive free Super Combo, All-Water Fishing or Hunting packages, and all active duty buy at resident rates. The FREE PARKLANDS PASSPORT gives free state park entry to service members, honorably discharged veterans, disabled veterans rated 60%+ or with lower extremity loss (whose COMPANION also enters free), and Gold Star family members.
states.cash: Texas does not pay a wartime service bonus, but the Veterans Land Board (VLB) operates the largest state veteran lending program in the country, which functions as a major financial benefit: LAND LOANS up to $200,000 with 5% minimum down, 30-year fixed rate, $325 appraisal/contract fee, minimum 1 acre with legal public road access; HOME LOANS up to $832,750 with 15, 20, 25 or 30-year fixed terms, little or no down payment, and a DISCOUNTED RATE for veterans rated 30%+ disabled; and HOME IMPROVEMENT LOANS up to $50,000 for 2-20 years — though these are TEMPORARILY ON MORATORIUM EFFECTIVE APRIL 30, 2026, so confirm status before relying on them. Eligibility covers active duty, Texas National Guard, reserve component members with 20+ qualifying years, veterans honorably discharged with 90+ days active duty (or sooner if medically discharged), and surviving spouses of MIA or service-connected deceased veterans (512-463-5060, 800-252-8387, VLBinfo@glo.texas.gov). County clerks record DD214s free of charge, and veterans filing VA disability claims get one free complete copy of their medical records.
states.homesHealth: TEN state veterans homes providing long-term nursing care — the largest state system in this jurisdiction group: Amarillo/Ussery-Roan (806-322-8387), Big Spring/Lamun-Lusk-Sanchez (432-268-8387), Bonham/Clyde W. Cosper (903-640-8387), El Paso/Ambrosio Guillen (915-751-0967), Floresville/Frank M. Tejeda (830-216-9456), Fort Worth/Tuskegee Airmen (817-502-6001), Houston/Richard A. Anderson (346-293-9600), McAllen/Alfredo Gonzalez (956-682-4224), Temple/William R. Courtney (254-791-8280) and Tyler/Watkins-Logan (903-617-6150). Eligibility requires Texas residency plus 90+ days active duty with honorable discharge, or 20 good years of reserve service; spouses and Gold Star parents are also eligible. Services include physical and occupational therapy, memory care, and equine, art and music therapy. Texas also operates four state veterans cemeteries through the VLB (Killeen, Mission, Abilene and Corpus Christi). Administered by the General Land Office Veterans Division (glo.texas.gov/veterans).
other: TEXAS COUNTY-LEVEL ADD-ONS ARE A HIDDEN LAYER: because Texas property tax is levied by counties, cities, school districts, hospital districts, community college districts and special districts independently, many jurisdictions adopt OPTIONAL additional exemptions beyond the state minimums. Optional percentage homestead exemptions of up to 20% of appraised value, additional over-65 and disabled exemptions, and tax ceilings/freezes on school district taxes at 65 vary enormously by district — always ask your appraisal district for the full list of optional local exemptions, not just the state ones.
The 100% disabled veteran homestead exemption has NO VALUE CAP, so its worth scales directly with home price — in high-value Austin, Dallas or Houston markets it can exceed $15,000 per year.
Hazlewood hours that a veteran does not use do not expire unused — the Legacy Act converts them into a child's college education, one child at a time, reassignable among children.

Hazlewood's federal-benefit offset rule means veterans with full Post-9/11 GI Bill entitlement often cannot stack both; the strategic play is frequently to use the GI Bill personally and Legacy-transfer Hazlewood hours to a child.
The Veterans Entrepreneur Program's five-year franchise tax waiver plus $300 registration fee waiver is a meaningful startup subsidy that almost no one outside TVC publicizes.
VLB Home Improvement Loans are ON MORATORIUM as of April 30, 2026 — a live change that stale third-party guides will miss.
The Parklands Passport admits a COMPANION free for veterans rated 60%+ or with lower extremity loss, not just the veteran.
The general school district homestead exemption rose to $140,000, which stacks beneath the veteran exemptions for partially disabled veterans.
states.topHack: Do not burn your Hazlewood hours on yourself if you still have Post-9/11 GI Bill entitlement. Hazlewood is reduced by federal education benefits that cover tuition and fees, so using both simultaneously wastes the state benefit — but the Legacy Act lets you transfer your unused 150 hours to a child under 25, and those hours are reassignable from one child to the next. Use the GI Bill for your own degree, bank Hazlewood, and hand a child 150 hours of free tuition at any Texas public university. That is commonly a $60,000-$100,000 transfer that costs nothing. Second, at the county level: after you file your 100% disabled veteran exemption with the appraisal district, ask specifically for the list of OPTIONAL local exemptions your county, city, school district, hospital district and community college district have adopted — Texas taxing units layer their own discretionary exemptions and freezes on top of the state minimums, and no one will volunteer them.

states.name: Utah
states.headline: Utah's military retirement tax credit effectively zeroes out state tax on a military pension, and its disabled veteran property tax exemption is one of the largest dollar caps in the nation at roughly half a million dollars of taxable value — but it scales down with your rating and active-duty pay is fully taxed.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Effectively fully exempt via a nonrefundable credit. Rather than a deduction, Utah grants a tax credit equal to federally taxable military retired pay multiplied by 0.0455 — which exactly matches Utah's 4.55% flat income tax rate, so the credit cancels the tax on the pension. A parallel credit applies to federally taxable survivor benefits (also multiplied by 0.0455). Because it is a nonrefundable credit rather than an exclusion, it offsets tax owed but does not generate a refund beyond liability.
incomeTax.activeDuty: TAXED. Utah taxes military pay the same as the IRS — all income included in federal adjusted gross income is included in Utah income. There is no general active-duty exclusion for Utah residents, though nonresidents stationed in Utah are protected by SCRA and nonresident military spouses by MSRRA.
incomeTax.notes: Utah uses a flat individual income tax rate of 4.55% (recently reduced from 4.65%). Because the military retirement credit is computed at exactly that rate, any future change in the flat rate should flow through to the credit formula — verify the current-year multiplier on the Utah State Tax Commission's TC-40 instructions, since the statute ties the credit to the rate.

states.propertyTax: Utah's 'veteran with a disability' property tax exemption has one of the highest dollar ceilings in the country. Per the Army benefit library, the maximum exemption is up to $521,620 of TAXABLE value on the residence and tangible personal property, requiring a service-connected disability rating of 10% OR GREATER — an unusually low entry threshold. The exemption SCALES WITH THE DISABILITY PERCENTAGE: a veteran rated 100% receives the full maximum, while lower ratings receive a proportional share (a 50% rating yields roughly half the maximum). The amount is adjusted annually for inflation, so the exact 2026 figure should be confirmed with your county (Utah county treasurers and the Utah State Tax Commission's Standards of Practice 3 publish the current-year number; the $521,620 figure reflects the most recent cycle documented on the .mil benefit library and could not be independently confirmed from a Utah .gov page during this research). Unmarried surviving spouses and minor orphans of a veteran with a disability, or of a veteran who died as a result of military service, also qualify. The property must be the primary residence and owned as of September 1, and APPLICATIONS ARE DUE SEPTEMBER 1 ANNUALLY. Separately, active duty members stationed outside Utah for 200+ days in a 365-day period receive a FULL exemption on their primary residence — a distinct and generous benefit for deployed and PCS'd service members.
states.education: The Purple Heart Tuition Waiver provides a FULL tuition waiver at Utah System of Higher Education schools for eligible degree programs — a strong benefit tied to a decoration rather than a rating. The Scott B. Lundell Military Survivors Tuition Waiver waives undergraduate tuition for surviving spouses and dependents of service members killed in service after September 11, 2001. The Veterans Tuition Gap Program funds a veteran's FINAL undergraduate year — a targeted, practical benefit for veterans who exhaust GI Bill entitlement short of graduation. Utah National Guard members receive a State Tuition Waiver for full-time attendance plus State Tuition Assistance of up to $7,000 per year. Utah's package is notable for covering the veteran personally (Purple Heart waiver, Tuition Gap) rather than being dependent-only.
states.employment: State government hiring preference adds 5 points or 5% for veterans and 10 points or 10% for disabled veterans and Purple Heart recipients. Federal 5-point and 10-point preferences apply to federal positions, and USERRA governs reemployment. Utah participates in interstate licensure compacts and provides military spouse licensing accommodations; confirm current spouse licensure terms with the Utah Division of Professional Licensing, as the Army benefit library's Utah entry does not enumerate them in detail.
states.vehicleRec: Sixteen distinctive plates available including Purple Heart, Disabled Veteran, Gold Star and Honors Veterans designs. A 'VETERAN' indicator is available on driver licenses for honorably discharged veterans aged 21 and older. CDL knowledge and skills test waivers for qualifying military commercial vehicle experience. Recreation: discounted hunting and fishing licenses for disabled veterans with a 20%+ rating — $12 for fishing, $25.50 for hunting and $28.50 for a combination license — again using a low rating threshold. State parks: a FREE ANNUAL HONOR PASS giving disabled veterans access to all Utah State Parks.
states.cash: Utah's principal cash program is the Veteran First-Time Homebuyer Grant, a $2,500 grant for veterans who separated within the past five years — a narrow window that rewards prompt application after separation. Utah does not operate a general wartime service bonus or a large statewide emergency financial assistance fund comparable to Pennsylvania's or Rhode Island's. The state's financial benefit is concentrated in the property tax exemption and the military retirement credit rather than in cash transfers.
states.homesHealth: FOUR state veterans homes, a strong system for Utah's population: William E. Christoffersen in Salt Lake City (801-584-1900), George E. Wahlen in Ogden (801-334-4300), Mervyn Sharpe Bennion in Payson (801-465-5400), and the Southern Utah Veterans Home in Ivins (435-634-5220). The Utah State Veterans Cemetery and Memorial Park in Bluffdale (801-254-9036) provides FREE burial for veterans, with a fee for spouse and dependent burials. Utah Department of Veterans and Military Affairs coordinates admissions and eligibility.
other: The property tax exemption threshold is only a 10% disability rating — one of the lowest entry points in the country — though the benefit scales proportionally, so a 10% rating yields roughly a tenth of the maximum.
The exemption cap (around $521,620 of taxable value in the most recent documented cycle) is among the highest dollar ceilings nationally and is inflation-adjusted annually.
September 1 is BOTH the ownership date and the application deadline for the property tax exemption — a tight and easily missed annual requirement.
Active duty members stationed outside Utah for 200+ days in a 365-day period get a FULL primary residence property tax exemption, which is distinct from the disability exemption and rarely claimed.
The military retirement benefit is structured as a CREDIT at exactly the flat tax rate (4.55%), not an exclusion — mathematically equivalent to full exemption but nonrefundable.
The Veterans Tuition Gap Program funding a veteran's final undergraduate year is an unusual and highly practical benefit for those who run out of GI Bill entitlement mid-degree.
Hunting and fishing discounts start at a 20% rating, not 100%.
The $2,500 first-time homebuyer grant is limited to veterans within five years of separation — use it or lose it.

agency.name: Utah Department of Veterans and Military Affairs (UDVMA)

states.topHack: File the property tax exemption at ANY rating, not just a high one. Utah sets the entry threshold at a 10% service-connected disability and then scales the benefit proportionally against a cap of roughly $521,620 of taxable value — so even a 30% or 40% rating shelters a six-figure chunk of your home's value, and the vast majority of eligible Utah veterans never apply because they assume the exemption is reserved for total disability. The deadline is September 1 and it is annual. The second overlooked move: if you are on active duty and stationed outside Utah for 200 or more days in a 365-day window, your Utah primary residence is FULLY exempt from property tax for that year — a benefit entirely separate from any disability rating.

states.name: Vermont
states.headline: Vermont is the weakest jurisdiction in this group: the military retirement exemption phases out entirely above $175,000 of AGI, the disabled veteran property tax exemption starts at a token $10,000 unless your town votes to raise it, and the state's high income and property tax rates swamp the modest benefits.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Income-capped exemption. Under Act 71 (signed May 2025), military retirement pay is fully exempt for filers with AGI of $125,000 or less, partially exempt for AGI between $125,000 and $175,000, and NOT exempt above $175,000. IMPORTANT: recipients must CHOOSE between the military retirement exclusion and the Social Security exclusion — you cannot take both, which meaningfully reduces the benefit for retirees drawing Social Security.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Partially exempt. Military pay earned while serving OUTSIDE Vermont is fully exempt. National Guard and Reserve members may exempt up to $2,000 if federal AGI is under $50,000. Otherwise active-duty pay of Vermont residents serving in-state is taxable.
incomeTax.notes: Vermont's top marginal income tax rate is 8.75%, among the highest in the country, and Vermont also has one of the highest effective property tax burdens in the nation. A new Veteran Tax Credit introduced in 2025 pays $250 for AGI of $25,000 or less, a reduced credit for AGI between $25,000 and $30,000, and nothing above $30,000 — a very narrowly targeted benefit.

states.propertyTax: Vermont's disabled veteran property tax exemption is the smallest in this jurisdiction group. State law mandates a MINIMUM exemption of only $10,000 of appraised value, which individual municipalities MAY vote to increase up to a maximum of $40,000. The exemption reduces assessed value before tax is calculated (a $200,000 home with a $20,000 exemption is taxed on $180,000). Eligibility requires a VA disability rating of 50% OR MORE, or receipt of a non-service-connected VA pension, or a permanent military medical retirement; surviving spouses of eligible veterans also qualify. The exemption applies only to owner-occupied primary residences, not rental property. APPLICATION IS ANNUAL: eligible veterans must submit proof of eligibility to the Vermont Office of Veterans Affairs by MAY 1 each year (VA verification: 800-827-1000), though veterans deemed permanently and totally disabled need only provide documentation once; the Office recommends applying by April 1. Because the exemption is town-by-town, two veterans in adjacent Vermont towns can receive a 4x difference in benefit. At Vermont's high effective property tax rates, even the $40,000 maximum is worth only roughly $700-$800 per year.
states.education: Vermont's veteran education offerings are thin and centered on the National Guard rather than veterans generally. Vermont National Guard members receive interest-free, FORGIVABLE LOANS covering tuition at Vermont state colleges, the University of Vermont, and private institutions; forgiveness requires two years of service per academic year funded, and certificate programs require a six-month commitment per certificate. Vermont does not operate a broad veterans tuition waiver or a comprehensive dependent/survivor tuition program comparable to those in Texas, South Carolina, Virginia or even neighboring Rhode Island. Veterans rely primarily on federal GI Bill benefits, in-state tuition provisions, and Vermont's general state grant program administered by VSAC.
states.employment: Vermont provides a state employment hiring preference by adding points to eligible applicants' scores, and federal 5-point and 10-point preference applies to federal positions. USERRA governs reemployment rights. Vermont's employment benefits for veterans are among the least developed in this group — the Army benefit library's Vermont entry documents no distinctive state licensing fee waivers, apprenticeship programs or credential-recognition initiatives specific to veterans and military spouses. Confirm current military spouse licensure accommodations with the Vermont Office of Professional Regulation.
states.vehicleRec: Free veteran designation on driver's licenses and IDs. CDL military test waiver available. Thirteen military license plates plus six combat theater plates. Driver's license extension of up to four years for service members. Recreation is where Vermont performs best: FREE hunting and fishing licenses for veterans with a 60%+ disability rating, and the GREEN MOUNTAIN PASSPORT — a $2 LIFETIME pass for any honorably discharged veteran, granting free day-use admission to Vermont state parks and historic sites. The Green Mountain Passport is a genuinely excellent value and requires no disability rating at all.
states.cash: The Vermont Veterans Assistance Fund provides a ONE-TIME emergency payment of up to $500 — the smallest emergency assistance program among the jurisdictions reviewed. The 2025 Veteran Tax Credit pays $250 for AGI of $25,000 or less, phasing out completely above $30,000. Vermont has no wartime service bonus program. Taken together, Vermont's cash assistance for veterans is minimal both in per-veteran amount and in program breadth.
states.homesHealth: The Vermont Veterans' Home in Bennington is the state's single long-term care facility for veterans, requiring a minimum of 90 days of active duty for eligibility; it serves veterans, spouses and Gold Star parents. The Vermont Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Randolph Center provides FREE burial with a government marker for eligible veterans. Vermont's state-run veteran health infrastructure is limited to this single home; clinical care runs through the White River Junction VA Medical Center and its community clinics.
other: The military retirement exemption forces an EITHER/OR choice against the Social Security exclusion — you cannot claim both, which quietly halves the benefit for most retirees over 62.
The retirement exemption phases out entirely above $175,000 AGI, so dual-income military households and second-career retirees frequently get nothing.
The property tax exemption's $10,000 statutory floor is the lowest in this group; whether you get $10,000 or $40,000 depends entirely on a town meeting vote in your municipality.
Annual May 1 filing with the Office of Veterans Affairs is required for the property tax exemption unless you are rated permanently and totally disabled, in which case documentation is one-time.
The $2 LIFETIME Green Mountain Passport for any honorably discharged veteran is Vermont's single best value and requires no disability rating.
Free hunting and fishing licenses begin at a 60% rating rather than 100%.

Vermont's 8.75% top income tax rate combined with among the highest effective property tax rates in the nation means the modest veteran benefits do not meaningfully change the state's overall cost position.
The 2025 Veteran Tax Credit of $250 is capped at $25,000 AGI and phases out by $30,000, reaching only the lowest-income veterans.
states.topHack: Go to your town meeting. Vermont's disabled veteran property tax exemption is set at a statutory floor of $10,000 but municipalities may vote it up to $40,000 — a 4x swing decided locally, town by town, and many Vermont towns have simply never had anyone ask. If your town is still at the $10,000 floor, the highest-leverage action available to a Vermont veteran is organizing the article for the next town meeting; it affects every eligible veteran in the municipality permanently. In the meantime, buy the $2 lifetime Green Mountain Passport — it requires nothing more than an honorable discharge and is the best dollar-for-dollar benefit in the state. And run the math carefully before electing the military retirement exclusion, because choosing it forfeits your Social Security exclusion.

states.name: Virginia
states.headline: Virginia pairs a full property tax exemption for 100% P&T veterans with VMSDEP — arguably the most generous dependent education program in the country, covering tuition, fees and stipends — and the military retirement subtraction reached $40,000 with the old age-55 restriction removed.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Substantially exempt via a $40,000 subtraction. For tax year 2025 and later, Virginia allows a subtraction of up to $40,000 of eligible military benefits — the top of the phase-in schedule that ran $10,000 (2022), $20,000 (2023), $30,000 (2024), $40,000 (2025+). Critically, the former AGE 55 AND OLDER restriction has been removed, so younger retirees now qualify. Eligible income includes military retirement income for service in the Armed Forces, SBP benefits paid to a veteran's surviving spouse, and military benefits paid to a surviving spouse. TSP distributions do NOT qualify. Medal of Honor recipients have their military retired pay fully exempt.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Narrowly exempt. Resident service members on active duty 90+ days with base pay under $30,000 may deduct up to $15,000 (the deduction phases down as pay rises toward $30,000 and disappears above it). National Guard members in grade O-6 and below may deduct up to 39 calendar days of pay or $5,500, whichever is less. Combat and hazardous duty pay is exempt. Nonresident military spouses are exempt.
incomeTax.notes: Virginia's top marginal income tax rate is 5.75%, reached at a very low income threshold ($17,000), so the $40,000 military subtraction is worth roughly $2,300 per year at the margin. Benefits must be included in federal income to be subtracted, so federally excluded 'qualified military benefits' like DIC cannot be subtracted again.

states.propertyTax: Virginia provides a COMPLETE exemption from real property tax on the principal residence plus up to ONE ACRE for veterans with a 100% total and permanent service-connected disability rating — no dollar cap and no income test. This is constitutionally grounded (Article X, Section 6-A) and administered by local commissioners of the revenue. Unremarried surviving spouses of eligible disabled veterans are eligible, and — unusually — a SURVIVING SPOUSE MAY RELOCATE WITHIN VIRGINIA AND RETAIN THE EXEMPTION, which most states do not permit. Surviving spouses of members killed in action or who died in the line of duty have a parallel exemption. Separately, veterans rated 100% permanently and totally disabled receive a SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION on ONE VEHICLE PURCHASE, and Virginia localities commonly reduce or eliminate the personal property (car) tax for disabled veterans — check your county or city, since personal property tax rates in Northern Virginia are substantial. Virginia does not offer a partial property tax exemption scaled by rating below 100% P&T.
states.education: The Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program (VMSDEP) is the crown jewel and one of the most generous programs of its kind nationally: it waives TUITION AND ALL MANDATORY FEES for up to EIGHT SEMESTERS at Virginia public colleges and universities, and additionally provides STIPENDS for room, board, books and supplies for families of service members killed in action or combat-disabled. Eligibility extends to the spouse, surviving spouse, or child aged 16-29 of a veteran with a 90% OR GREATER disability rating (a notably lower bar than the 100% used by most states) or of a service member killed in combat; the surviving spouse must be unremarried and the veteran must be a Virginia resident (804-225-2083, vmsdep@dvs.virginia.gov). ELIGIBILITY HISTORY IS IMPORTANT: the 2024 Appropriation Act imposed restrictions (including requirements to exhaust other financial aid and enrollment caps) that triggered significant backlash; Governor Youngkin signed HB 6003 on July 18, 2024, a clean full REPEAL of those eligibility changes, restoring the original framework. As of the 2026 General Assembly session those repealed rules still stand — two EXPANSION bills stalled (Sen. Roem's SB 92 to eliminate the five-year residency requirement for families relocated by military orders was deferred to 2027; Del. Feggans' HB 56 to extend waivers to dependents of members dying on active duty outside combat, including training accidents, service-connected illness and suicide, died in committee). Program cost is running near $150 million for 2025-26, so further legislative attention is likely.
states.employment: State hiring preference adds 5% for honorably discharged veterans, 10% for those with a service-connected disability rating, 5% for currently serving National Guard members, and 5% for surviving spouses and children of service members killed in action. Virginia Values Veterans (V3) is a well-regarded statewide program certifying employers and running a Transition Program providing peer support, resume review and job connections for separating service members and spouses (844-838-7838 / 804-786-0286). Virginia Works provides priority of service for employment assistance, training and placement. Troops to Trucks offers CDL Even Exchange for qualifying MOSs and a skills waiver for those with 2+ years of military commercial driving. Virginia Boots to Suits provides free career outfits to veterans within 60 days of separation.
states.vehicleRec: Sixty-three military and veteran plate designs: Purple Heart recipients get a free set; Disabled Veteran plates are free for those with 100% total and permanent disability or loss of limb or eyesight; Veteran and Gold Star Family plates are available. A free 'Veteran' indicator on driver's licenses requires honorable discharge or 180+ days of Guard/Reserve service with a DD214 or VA Benefit Summary Letter. Recreation uses a well-graduated disability scale for resident licenses: 100% P&T veterans get FREE hunting and fishing plus $15 trapping; 70%+ pay $50 hunting and $50 fishing; 50-69% pay $75 each; 30-49% pay $100 each. State parks: the Virginia State Parks Veteran Disability Passport gives veterans rated 100% free vehicle parking, free boat launch and free admission, plus a 50% camping discount and a 25% one-night yurt discount. Virginia National Guard members and their immediate families enter state parks free.
states.cash: Virginia does not operate a wartime service bonus or a large statewide veterans emergency cash grant program, which is a genuine gap relative to Pennsylvania, Rhode Island and South Carolina. The state's financial support is delivered through the property tax exemption, the $40,000 income tax subtraction and VMSDEP rather than direct cash transfers. Smaller in-kind programs fill part of the gap: Virginia Boots to Suits provides free professional clothing within 60 days of separation, and the Virginia Hilton Honors Military Program provides up to 100,000 hotel points for employment-related travel including interviews, required training and pre-employment testing (HiltonHonors@naswa.org). The Virginia Veteran and Family Support program (formerly VWWP) provides case management and peer support, including behavioral health navigation, at no cost.
states.homesHealth: Virginia operates FOUR Veterans Care Centers providing skilled nursing and memory care: Davis and McDaniel VCC in Roanoke (204 beds, 540-982-2860), Sitter and Barfoot VCC in Richmond (200 beds, 804-371-8000), Jones and Cabacoy VCC in Virginia Beach (128 beds, 757-630-3100) and Puller VCC in Warrenton (128 beds, 540-680-5200). Eligibility requires Virginia residency, 24 months of continuous active duty and honorable discharge. Virginia also operates THREE state veterans cemeteries — Amelia, Suffolk and Dublin — providing free burial including gravesite, headstone and perpetual care (855-482-8387). DVS provides free benefits counseling at regional offices statewide, and Virginia's benefit service structure is state-run rather than county-run, so veterans work with DVS Veteran Service Representatives rather than County Veterans Service Officers as in Ohio or Wisconsin.
other: VMSDEP triggers at a 90% DISABILITY RATING, not 100% — a materially lower bar than nearly every comparable state program, and a fact many Virginia families with a 90% rated veteran never discover.
VMSDEP covers spouses as well as children, with children eligible from age 16 all the way to 29 — an unusually wide age window.

The 2024 eligibility restrictions were fully repealed by HB 6003 and remain repealed as of the 2026 session; two expansion bills (SB 92 on residency, HB 56 on non-combat active duty deaths) stalled and were deferred or died.
The five-year Virginia residency requirement still blocks families relocated OUT of Virginia by military orders — SB 92 sought to fix this and was deferred to the 2027 session.
A surviving spouse may MOVE to a different home within Virginia and keep the 100% property tax exemption, which most states do not allow.
The age-55 restriction on the military retirement subtraction has been removed, making the $40,000 subtraction available to retirees in their 40s.
100% P&T veterans get a sales and use tax exemption on one vehicle purchase, separate from the property tax exemption.
Local personal property (car) tax relief for disabled veterans varies by locality and can be worth hundreds or thousands annually in Northern Virginia — check your commissioner of the revenue.
Virginia has no state veterans emergency cash assistance fund, unlike most of its peers.
states.topHack: If your VA rating is 90% — not 100% — apply to VMSDEP anyway. Virginia sets the VMSDEP threshold at 90% or greater, while nearly every comparable state program requires a total rating, and the result is that a large population of 90%-rated Virginia veterans never applies because they assume they are short of the bar. The benefit is a full tuition and mandatory fee waiver for eight semesters at any Virginia public college or university, available to your spouse AND each child aged 16 to 29, with room-and-board stipends for combat-disabled families. Per child that is commonly a $60,000-$120,000 benefit, and it is the single largest transfer available in the Commonwealth. Apply early: the program's cost is running near $150 million a year and the legislature has already tried once to tighten eligibility.

states.name: Washington
states.headline: No income tax, a free state parks pass at just a 30% rating, and a mandatory 200-credit tuition waiver for dependents of 100% disabled or deceased veterans — but the property tax relief is income-tested against county median income and the veterans' own tuition waiver is discretionary, so schools can decline it.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Not taxed — Washington has no individual state income tax, so military retirement pay, active-duty pay, TSP distributions and SBP annuities are all free of state income taxation.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Not taxed. No state individual income tax.
incomeTax.notes: Washington has no individual income tax on wages or retirement income. It does impose a 7% capital gains excise tax on certain long-term gains above an annually indexed threshold (roughly $270,000+), which can reach veterans selling appreciated assets. Revenue leans on sales tax (state 6.5% plus local, often 9-10.5% combined) and property tax.

states.propertyTax: Washington's program is a genuine EXEMPTION but it is INCOME-TESTED, which is the key limitation. Veterans qualify with a service-connected evaluation of at least 80%, OR by receiving VA compensation at the 100% rate for a service-connected disability. The applicant must also meet a qualifying income limit under 'Income Threshold 3,' which is set at 70% of the COUNTY MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME (or a statutory floor, whichever is greater) — so the dollar limit differs in every county and is re-set periodically as county median incomes are updated. In practice Income Threshold 3 ranges roughly from the mid-$40,000s in lower-income counties to the mid-$80,000s or higher in King County; the Department of Revenue's page confirms the county-specific structure but does not publish a single statewide figure, so YOU MUST CHECK YOUR COUNTY ASSESSOR for the current-year dollar threshold. Qualifying income is 'combined disposable income,' which excludes VA disability compensation — an important detail, since VA compensation often makes up most of a disabled veteran's cash flow and does not count against the limit. The exemption freezes the assessed value at the level in the year of first qualification and exempts the property from all excess and special levies, with the degree of regular-levy relief tiered by income band. A separate DEFERRAL program lets qualifying homeowners postpone taxes as a lien against the property. Surviving spouses of deceased service members aged 62+ (or disabled or retired) receive grants where combined disposable income is at or below Income Threshold 3.
states.education: Two very different programs, and the distinction matters enormously. (1) THE VETERANS' WAIVER IS DISCRETIONARY: RCW 28B.15.621 AUTHORIZES — but does not require — Washington community colleges, colleges and universities to waive all or a portion of tuition and fees for eligible veterans and National Guard members. Each institution designs and funds its own program, so coverage varies from generous to nonexistent depending on the school, and there is no statewide credit cap. You must ask the specific institution. (2) THE DEPENDENTS' WAIVER IS MANDATORY: institutions MUST waive ALL undergraduate tuition and fees for dependents of veterans who are 100% disabled or who died as a result of military service, up to 200 QUARTER CREDITS or the semester equivalent — graduate waivers are encouraged but not required. A $500 PER YEAR BOOK STIPEND for textbooks and course materials accompanies the waiver, subject to legislative funding. (3) The Washington National Guard Grant (NGG) pays $2,500-$6,500 depending on institution type, plus a $500 one-time allowance for books and supplies. Operation Recognition awards high school diplomas to WWII, Korea and Vietnam-era veterans who left school to serve. Administered through the Washington Student Achievement Council (wsac.wa.gov) and WDVA.
states.employment: State hiring preference adds 5-10% to scores. Veterans may credit up to 10 years of military service in the state retirement system — a substantial pension enhancement. WorkSource centers provide priority of service. Professional licensing offers expedited processing for military spouses, and Washington participates in interstate licensure compacts. USERRA governs reemployment rights. Washington also runs a well-established apprenticeship system with veteran-focused pathways through the Department of Labor and Industries; confirm current veteran apprenticeship initiatives with WDVA, as the Army benefit library's Washington entry is comparatively sparse on this point.
states.vehicleRec: Free veteran designation on driver's licenses. Multiple military and veteran plate options including Purple Heart, Disabled Veteran, Gold Star and Medal of Honor; DISABLED VETERAN PLATES ARE EXEMPT FROM LICENSING FEES. Recreation: disabled veterans receive reduced hunting and fishing fees at 50% OFF resident rates, and National Guard members receive a FREE annual hunting license package. Nonresident service members stationed in Washington buy at resident prices. State parks: a FREE LIFETIME WASHINGTON STATE PARKS PASS for veterans with a 30% OR GREATER disability rating — one of the lowest thresholds in the nation for a lifetime parks benefit, and a standout given Washington's exceptional state park system (the Disabled Veteran Lifetime Pass covers day use, camping and moorage fees).
states.cash: The Veterans Innovations Program (VIP) is WDVA's emergency financial assistance vehicle, providing help to veterans and their families facing financial hardship, typically for housing, utilities, transportation and other urgent needs. WDVA's Financial Assistance page confirms the program exists but does not publish current grant amounts or eligibility bands online — CURRENT AMOUNTS AND ELIGIBILITY SHOULD BE CONFIRMED DIRECTLY WITH WDVA (800-562-2308, benefits@dva.wa.gov). WDVA also operates the Veterans Estate Management Program, a fiduciary service managing finances for veterans unable to do so themselves. Washington additionally funds a network of COUNTY VETERANS ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS: counties are authorized to levy a dedicated veterans assistance fund and most do, providing county-level emergency cash for rent, utilities, food and burial — this county layer is often more accessible than state programs and is significantly underused. Washington has no wartime service bonus.
states.homesHealth: Washington operates FOUR state veterans homes: the Washington Soldiers Home in Orting, the Washington Veterans Home in Retsil (Port Orchard), the Spokane Veterans Home, and the Walla Walla Veterans Home. They provide skilled nursing, dementia and rehabilitative care. WDVA also runs a nationally recognized PTSD/behavioral health counseling program offering free, confidential counseling to combat veterans and their families through contracted counselors statewide — a state-funded clinical service that goes well beyond what most states provide and does not require VA enrollment. The Washington State Veterans Cemetery in Medical Lake (near Spokane) provides burial for eligible veterans and dependents. Admissions and eligibility through WDVA (800-562-2308).
other: The 30% rating threshold for a FREE LIFETIME state parks pass is among the lowest in the country and covers day use, camping and moorage — exceptional value in a state with one of the best park systems in the nation.
VA disability compensation is EXCLUDED from 'combined disposable income' for the property tax exemption, so many veterans who assume they earn too much actually qualify.

Income Threshold 3 is 70% of COUNTY median household income, so the dollar limit differs in every county and changes as county incomes are re-surveyed — always check your county assessor rather than a statewide summary.

The veterans' own tuition waiver is DISCRETIONARY (institutions may decline); the DEPENDENTS' waiver for families of 100% disabled or deceased veterans is MANDATORY at 200 quarter credits plus a $500/year book stipend. Do not confuse the two.
WDVA's free PTSD and behavioral health counseling for combat veterans and their families is state-funded, confidential, and does not require VA enrollment — a rare state-level clinical benefit.
County Veterans Assistance Programs, funded by a dedicated county levy, provide emergency cash in most Washington counties and are far less known than state programs.
Veterans may purchase up to 10 years of military service credit in the state retirement system, a significant benefit for those entering state or local government employment.
Washington's 7% capital gains excise tax can reach veterans selling appreciated assets despite the absence of an income tax.

agency.name: Washington State Department of Veterans Affairs (WDVA)

states.topHack: Apply for the property tax exemption even if you think you earn too much — VA disability compensation does not count toward the income test. Washington measures 'combined disposable income' against Income Threshold 3 (70% of your county's median household income), and VA service-connected compensation is excluded from that calculation. For an 80%-or-higher rated veteran whose income is mostly VA compensation plus a modest pension, this routinely puts them under the threshold even when their total cash flow looks high, and the exemption then FREEZES their assessed value at the year of qualification — which in Washington's appreciating markets is worth more every single year. Second: get the free lifetime state parks pass at 30%, and check whether your county runs a Veterans Assistance Program levy, because county-level emergency cash is the most accessible and least claimed money in the state.

states.name: West Virginia
states.headline: West Virginia fully exempts military retirement pay and — through an unusual refundable income tax credit — effectively refunds 100% of homestead property taxes paid by veterans rated 90% or higher, which combined with the nation's lowest housing costs makes it quietly excellent value.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. West Virginia does not tax military retired pay. VA disability compensation, pension payments and DIC are not included in taxable income, and SBP, RCSBP and RSFPP annuities are not taxed.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Partially exempt. Service members not spending 30+ days in West Virginia are not subject to state income tax on military pay. National Guard and Reserve members called to federal active duty for Operation Enduring Freedom or domestic security operations are exempt. Combat and hazardous duty pay excluded federally is also excluded from WV tax. Members separating after 30+ days of active duty may deduct military pay in the year of discharge. Nonresident spouses of nonresident service members stationed in WV are exempt.
incomeTax.notes: West Virginia has been cutting its income tax, with the top rate falling below 5% under a multi-year reduction schedule tied to revenue triggers; confirm the current-year rate with the WV Tax Division. West Virginia is also phasing out its tax on Social Security benefits. Combined with the military retirement exemption, tax exposure for military retirees is low.

states.propertyTax: West Virginia uses an unusual and generous mechanism: the DISABLED VETERAN REAL PROPERTY TAX CREDIT is a credit against personal income tax equal to the ACTUAL PROPERTY TAX PAID on the homestead — effectively a full refund of homestead property tax rather than a valuation exemption. Eligibility requires the veteran be 90-100% PERMANENTLY AND TOTALLY DISABLED per the VA, own a homestead used or occupied exclusively for residential purposes, and have occupied it at least 6 months. Property taxes must be paid TIMELY (first half by October 1, second half by April 1) — late payment forfeits the credit. Claim it by filing Form DV-1 with your West Virginia Personal Income Tax Return, entering total taxes paid on line 21(B) of the IT-140. Per the Tax Division's TSD-455, the credit amount equals the actual tax paid, with no maximum stated. An unremarried widow or widower may claim the credit if the homestead remains unsold and unreclassified. The credit TAKES PRECEDENCE over the Senior Citizen and Homestead Excess Property Tax Credits and must be claimed separately from those alternatives. Separately, West Virginia's general Homestead Exemption exempts $20,000 of assessed value for homeowners aged 65+ or permanently and totally disabled, which the veteran credit can supplement. Resident service members stationed outside WV get a property tax exemption on one vehicle. NOTE: the 90% (rather than 100%) threshold is notably more inclusive than most states.
states.education: West Virginia Educational Encouragement Program (WVEEP) covers National Guard members at 100% of tuition and fees up to $10,000 PER FISCAL YEAR at participating WV institutions — a high cap. The Medal of Honor / Purple Heart Tuition Waiver waives tuition and mandatory fees at all state-supported institutions for Medal of Honor recipients or Purple Heart recipients with permanent disabilities, for up to eight semesters, applied only after other benefits are exhausted. Veterans Re-Education Assistance pays up to $500 per semester to honorably discharged WV resident veterans who have exhausted their VA education benefits — a useful backstop. The War Orphans Education Program provides surviving spouses and children aged 16-25 of deceased wartime veterans up to $1,000 per semester and no more than $2,000 per year. Surviving spouses and children of service members killed in action receive a full tuition and fee WAIVER for undergraduate courses at state institutions for up to eight semesters or until a bachelor's degree is completed. Nonresidents using VA education benefits who enroll within three years of discharge (with 90+ days of service) qualify for in-state tuition. Operation Recognition awards high school diplomas to WWII, Korea and Vietnam-era veterans.
states.employment: State employment preference adds up to 10 points to passing exam scores: 5 points for honorable discharge or 90+ consecutive days of active duty training, plus an additional 5 points for Purple Heart recipients or those receiving VA service-connected disability compensation. State employees in reserve components receive 240 HOURS of paid military leave for training and drills, plus an ADDITIONAL 240 HOURS when mobilized to federal active duty — one of the most generous military leave allowances among the states. WorkForce West Virginia provides priority in state and federally funded employment programs, early job access, career counseling, resume assistance and job placement (800-252-5627). The Veterans and Heroes to Agriculture Program provides grants up to $24,000 to organizations supporting veterans in agriculture, plus scholarships up to $600 each fiscal year — a distinctive rural-economy program.
states.vehicleRec: Free 'Veteran' designation on driver's licenses and ID cards. Service member licenses are extended until six months after honorable separation. SPECIAL PLATES WITH NO REGISTRATION FEES for Disabled Veterans, Purple Heart recipients, Medal of Honor recipients, Distinguished Service Cross, Navy Cross, Air Force Cross and Pearl Harbor survivors. FREE METERED PARKING statewide for holders of Disabled Veteran and Purple Heart plates — a concrete recurring benefit. Gold Star Family plates and 40+ other military plates available. CDL skills test waiver (knowledge test still required) for those with 2+ years of military vehicle licensing. Recreation: FREE hunting and fishing for veterans with a 100% permanent service-connected disability, former POWs, and those exempt from vehicle registration fees. Active duty members on leave need no hunting, trapping or fishing license (carry leave papers). State parks: a 10% discount on lodge rooms, cabins and campsites using code 'Vets10,' and 15% off greens fees at Pipestem, Twin Falls and Cacapon Resort golf courses.
states.cash: West Virginia does not operate a wartime service bonus or a large statewide veterans emergency cash grant program. The John F. 'Jack' Bennett Fund pays for grave markers for deceased veterans whose families do not meet VA income limits. The Veterans and Heroes to Agriculture Program provides scholarships up to $600 per fiscal year to individuals and grants up to $24,000 to supporting organizations. National Guard members on state active duty receive full state coverage of medical care for line-of-duty injury or illness, continued pay until return to work is possible, and funeral, burial and survivor compensation in the event of death. The state's principal financial benefit remains the property tax credit, which functions as an annual cash refund.
states.homesHealth: West Virginia Veterans Home in Barboursville: a 125-bed facility for self-sufficient veterans providing domiciliary care — note it does NOT provide skilled nursing (304-736-1027). West Virginia Veterans Nursing Facility in Clarksburg: 120 beds including a 20-bed Alzheimer's unit providing skilled nursing care (304-626-1600). The Charles Calvin Rogers Veterans Nursing Facility in Beckley is a new 120-bed facility under development — confirm current opening and admissions status with WVDVA. The Donel C. Kinnard Memorial State Veterans Cemetery in Institute/Dunbar provides free burial and interment for eligible veterans including grave site, opening and closing, headstone and perpetual care, with a $780 fee for spouse or child burial (304-746-0026).
other: THE 90% THRESHOLD IS THE KEY: West Virginia's property tax credit reaches veterans rated 90-100%, not just 100% — one of the few states to extend a full property tax benefit below a total rating.
The benefit is a REFUNDABLE-style income tax credit equal to actual property tax paid, not a valuation exemption — you pay the bill, then recover it in full on your state return via Form DV-1.
TIMELY PAYMENT IS MANDATORY: first half by October 1 and second half by April 1, or the credit is forfeited for that year.
The credit takes precedence over, and must be claimed instead of, the Senior Citizen Tax Credit and Homestead Excess Property Tax Credit — veterans who claim the wrong one lose money.

West Virginia has among the lowest median home values and property tax rates in the nation, so while the credit's dollar value is modest in absolute terms, the overall cost-of-living position for a military retiree is excellent.
240 hours of paid military leave for state employees, PLUS another 240 hours when mobilized to federal active duty, is among the most generous state employee military leave in the country.
Free metered parking statewide for Disabled Veteran and Purple Heart plate holders.
The Veterans and Heroes to Agriculture Program is a distinctive rural program with grants up to $24,000 to supporting organizations.
WVEEP's $10,000 per fiscal year cap for National Guard tuition is among the highest state Guard tuition caps.

agency.name: West Virginia Department of Veterans Assistance (WVDVA)

states.topHack: File Form DV-1 with your West Virginia income tax return — and pay your property tax on time. West Virginia's disabled veteran benefit is not an exemption you claim at the courthouse; it is a credit you claim on your state income tax return equal to the ENTIRE property tax you paid on your homestead, available at a 90% rating rather than 100%. Two things sink veterans here: they never learn the credit runs through the income tax system, and they miss the strict October 1 / April 1 payment deadlines, which forfeits the credit entirely for that year. Also make sure you claim the DV-1 credit rather than the Senior Citizen or Homestead Excess credit — the DV-1 takes precedence and is almost always worth more, but you must choose it affirmatively.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.headline: Wisconsin pairs a fully uncapped refundable credit that returns 100% of property taxes paid with the Wisconsin GI Bill's full tuition remission for the veteran personally — a combination that makes it one of the two or three best states in the country for a 100% disabled veteran.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Fully exempt. Military retired pay is not taxed in Wisconsin.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Substantially exempt. Military pay from active duty service is subtractible from Wisconsin taxable income; however, reserve component INACTIVE duty pay (drill pay) does not qualify for the subtraction. Combat zone service carries a 180-day filing extension.
incomeTax.notes: Wisconsin's individual income tax top rate is 7.65%, though the vast majority of military retirees pay nothing on their pension given the full exemption. Wisconsin also exempts Social Security benefits entirely. The state's high top rate matters mainly for veterans with substantial second-career or investment income.

states.propertyTax: The Wisconsin Veterans and Surviving Spouses Property Tax Credit is among the most valuable in the nation because it is BOTH refundable AND uncapped: it refunds 100% OF PROPERTY TAXES PAID on the primary residence including land up to one acre, with no dollar ceiling stated. Eligibility requires honorable active duty service, a 100% service-connected disability rating from the VA or Individual Unemployability status, current Wisconsin residency, and a residency link — either Wisconsin residency at the time of entering service OR five consecutive years of Wisconsin residency after entry. Surviving spouses qualify in three ways: unremarried spouses of veterans who held 100% ratings and were Wisconsin residents at death; unremarried spouses of veterans who died on active duty while Wisconsin residents; and unremarried spouses receiving Dependency and Indemnity Compensation whose veteran met the service and residency requirements. RENTERS MAY ALSO QUALIFY for the portion of rent attributable to property taxes, with proof — a provision almost no other state offers. Married dual-veteran households may file jointly or separately, dividing the credit. Mechanically, WDVA certifies eligibility and the Department of Revenue administers the credit through the income tax return, so it arrives as a refund rather than a reduced tax bill. Apply starting with your County or Tribal Veterans Service Office.
states.education: The WISCONSIN G.I. BILL is the flagship and covers the VETERAN PERSONALLY, not just dependents: full tuition and segregated fee REMISSION at all University of Wisconsin System institutions and Wisconsin Technical College System schools, for up to 8 full-time semesters or 128 credits. Eligibility requires 90+ days of active duty during wartime, 2+ years of service, or discharge due to a service-connected disability, plus Wisconsin residency at entry or five consecutive years before application. The Wisconsin Veterans Grant for private nonprofit schools pays the lesser of $2,000 or 50% of tuition charged per semester, with institutions matching the grant. The VetEd Reimbursement Grant scales maximum credits by length of service — 30 credits for 90-180 days, 60 credits for 181-730 days, 120 credits for 731+ days — with a household income limit of $50,000 plus $1,000 per dependent over two, and must be used within 10 years of discharge for full credit. The Wisconsin National Guard Tuition Grant covers up to 100% of UW-Madison tuition for up to 8 full-time terms for actively drilling warrant officers and enlisted members. Veteran Upward Bound at UW-Milwaukee and the Zablocki VA Center provides free college readiness programming for low-income, first-generation or at-risk veterans. High school diplomas are available to wartime veterans aged 65+, or 55+ with a service-connected disability.
states.employment: State hiring preference is strong and tiered: 10 points added to passing examination scores for veterans, and 15-20 POINTS for disabled veterans rated 30% or higher, plus NON-COMPETITIVE APPOINTMENT authority for veterans rated 30%+ — meaning they can be hired outside the competitive process entirely. Permanent state employees in reserve components receive 30 DAYS of paid military leave annually, and differential pay covering the gap between state salary and military pay for up to 179 days of extended active duty, extendable by the Governor to 6 years total. Two direct cash employment programs: the RETRAINING GRANT pays up to $3,000 per year for 2 years to unemployed or underemployed veterans with financial need; and the VETERANS EMPLOYMENT GRANT pays EMPLOYERS up to $5,000 for a full-time hire or $2,500 part-time for each disabled veteran hired at a 50%+ rating — a hiring subsidy that veterans can point employers toward. Wisconsin Veteran Owned Business certification (51%+ veteran-owned, under $1,500,000 annual sales) may qualify for state contract preference, and a Veteran Farmer certification and directory supports veteran agriculture.
