states.vehicleRec: Veteran identifier on driver licenses and ID cards requires WDVA verification and either 2+ years of peacetime active duty or 90+ days of wartime service with honorable or general-under-honorable discharge. Disabled Veteran plates for service-connected disabilities affecting mobility authorize disabled parking privileges. Over 50 decal options covering service branch, wartime service and medals; personalization is $15 annually. Military plates TRANSFER TO THE SURVIVING SPOUSE. Gold Star Family plates carry no issue fee. Medal of Honor plates have no issue or renewal fee, are non-expiring, and transfer to the surviving spouse. Recreation: free small game hunting and fishing licenses for active duty service members on leave, bonus antlerless deer harvest authorizations, and enhanced harvest authorizations during deer season (Wisconsin DNR, 888-936-7463). Wisconsin's recreation benefits for DISABLED veterans specifically are less developed than its tax and education benefits — confirm current disabled veteran license and state park pass terms directly with the DNR.
states.cash: Beyond the property tax credit (which functions as an annual refund check), Wisconsin runs several direct assistance programs through WDVA: the Veterans Retraining Grant of up to $3,000 per year for two years for unemployed or underemployed veterans with financial need; and subsistence and emergency assistance grants administered through WDVA and County Veterans Service Offices. WDVA also operates the Veterans Housing and Recovery Program (VHRP) providing transitional housing and services at multiple sites. The Veterans Employment Grant pays employers up to $5,000 per disabled veteran hired. Wisconsin has no currently open wartime service bonus. Current subsistence aid amounts and eligibility bands are set administratively and should be confirmed with WDVA (800-947-8387), as the published figures change with biennial budget appropriations.
states.homesHealth: Wisconsin operates THREE state veterans homes: the Wisconsin Veterans Home at King (the largest, in Waupaca County, and one of the biggest state veterans homes in the country), the Wisconsin Veterans Home at Union Grove, and the Wisconsin Veterans Home at Chippewa Falls. They provide skilled nursing, rehabilitation and memory care for veterans, spouses and Gold Star parents. Wisconsin also operates THREE state veterans cemeteries — Central Wisconsin Veterans Memorial Cemetery (King), Northern Wisconsin Veterans Memorial Cemetery (Spooner) and Southern Wisconsin Veterans Memorial Cemetery (Union Grove) — providing burial for eligible veterans and dependents. WDVA additionally runs the Veterans Housing and Recovery Program for homeless and at-risk veterans. Wisconsin's county-based Veterans Service Officer network is statutorily established in all 72 counties plus tribal VSOs, and is the front door for nearly every state benefit including the property tax credit certification.
other: THE PROPERTY TAX CREDIT IS UNCAPPED AND REFUNDABLE — it returns 100% of property taxes paid on the home and one acre with no stated dollar ceiling, which in high-tax Wisconsin municipalities can exceed $6,000-$10,000 annually.
RENTERS CAN QUALIFY for the property tax credit on the share of rent attributable to property taxes — almost unique nationally, and it means a 100% disabled veteran who rents is not shut out.

The Wisconsin GI Bill covers the VETERAN PERSONALLY with full tuition remission at UW System and technical colleges for 128 credits — most states offer tuition benefits only to dependents and survivors.
The five-year-residency alternative means veterans who moved to Wisconsin after service can still qualify for both the GI Bill and the property tax credit after five consecutive years.
Veterans rated 30%+ can be hired into state government through NON-COMPETITIVE APPOINTMENT, bypassing the examination process entirely.
The Veterans Employment Grant pays the EMPLOYER up to $5,000 for hiring a 50%+ disabled veteran — a negotiating tool veterans can raise directly in interviews.
Military and Medal of Honor license plates transfer to the surviving spouse.
All 72 counties plus tribal governments maintain Veterans Service Officers, who certify eligibility for the property tax credit — the process runs county → WDVA → Department of Revenue.
Wisconsin's disabled-veteran recreation benefits are comparatively underdeveloped relative to its outstanding tax and education benefits.
states.topHack: If you are 100% service-connected or Individually Unemployable and you RENT rather than own, file for the Veterans and Surviving Spouses Property Tax Credit anyway. Wisconsin is one of the only states that lets renters claim the credit on the portion of rent attributable to property taxes, and essentially no renting veteran knows it — you simply need documentation from your landlord. For owners, the same credit is uncapped and refundable, returning every dollar of property tax on your home and one acre, which in a high-mill Wisconsin municipality routinely means a five-figure swing over a few years. Start at your County Veterans Service Office, which must certify eligibility to WDVA before the Department of Revenue will pay it — going straight to the Department of Revenue is the most common way veterans stall their claim for a year.

states.name: Wyoming
states.headline: No income tax and genuinely free tuition for overseas combat veterans and their families, but the property tax exemption is a token $6,000 of assessed value — worth only a couple hundred dollars a year — and the state has almost no cash assistance infrastructure.

incomeTax.militaryRetirement: Not taxed — Wyoming has no individual state income tax, so military retirement pay, active-duty pay, TSP distributions and SBP annuities are all free of state income taxation.
incomeTax.activeDuty: Not taxed. No state individual income tax.
incomeTax.notes: Wyoming has no individual or corporate income tax and among the lowest overall tax burdens in the country, funded largely by mineral severance taxes. Sales tax is low (4% state plus local, typically 5-6% combined) and property taxes are among the lowest in the nation — which is also why the veteran property tax exemption is worth so little in absolute terms.

states.propertyTax: Wyoming's veterans property tax exemption is a flat $6,000 REDUCTION IN ASSESSED VALUE on the primary residence. Because Wyoming assesses residential property at 9.5% of fair market value and mill levies typically run in the 60-70 range, $6,000 of assessed value translates to roughly $350-$450 of annual tax savings — modest in absolute terms, though it represents a meaningful share of a typically low Wyoming property tax bill. Eligibility is unusually BROAD rather than deep: it requires three or more years of Wyoming residency plus honorable discharge with qualifying wartime/campaign service, OR a service-connected disability — it is NOT restricted to highly-rated disabled veterans the way most states' exemptions are. A useful and little-known feature: IF THE EXEMPTION IS NOT USED AGAINST REAL PROPERTY, IT MAY BE APPLIED INSTEAD TO VEHICLE LICENSING FEES, which helps veterans who rent. Surviving spouses of qualifying veterans generally retain eligibility. Apply annually with your county assessor, typically by the fourth Monday in May. Wyoming does not offer an enhanced or full exemption scaled to disability rating.
states.education: The Wyoming Veterans Tuition Benefit is the state's strongest offering: FREE TUITION at Wyoming community colleges or the University of Wyoming for overseas combat veterans, their surviving spouses, and dependents, covering 8 semesters to be used within 8 years. Eligibility centers on qualifying overseas combat service (receipt of a campaign or expeditionary medal) with Wyoming residency requirements. The Wyoming National Guard Educational Assistance program covers 100% of the resident rate tuition and mandatory fees at state schools for TWO DEGREES, or up to $1,500 per semester at private institutions; after a six-year enlistment a service member may TRANSFER one degree's benefit to a college-aged dependent — an unusual transferability provision at the state level. Wyoming's small higher education system (one university and seven community colleges) means the benefit is concentrated but the free-tuition value is real: UW resident tuition plus fees runs several thousand dollars per year.
states.employment: State hiring preference gives a 5% advantage to veterans and 10% to disabled veterans. Federal 5-point and 10-point preferences apply to federal positions. State employees in reserve components receive 15 days of paid military leave annually. The Wyoming Department of Workforce Services provides workforce services and job placement assistance with priority of service. Wyoming's employment programs are among the least developed in this group, reflecting the state's very small population and limited agency infrastructure — the Army benefit library's Wyoming entry documents no distinctive licensing fee waivers, apprenticeship programs or credential recognition initiatives specific to veterans and military spouses. Confirm current military spouse licensure accommodations with the Wyoming Department of Workforce Services and relevant licensing boards.
states.vehicleRec: Free 'Veteran' designation on driver licenses and ID cards. Specialty plates: Purple Heart (free), Disabled Veteran (free, and REGISTRATION EXEMPT), Veteran ($50 fee) and Gold Star Family (free). Active duty members receive a driver license expiration date waiver. Recreation is where Wyoming genuinely excels, which matters a great deal in a state defined by its outdoors: 100% disabled veterans receive FREE LIFETIME HUNTING AND FISHING LICENSES; 50% disabled veterans receive a FREE LIFETIME FISHING LICENSE; Purple Heart recipients receive FREE LIFETIME hunting and fishing licenses; disabled veterans rated 50%+ receive a FREE LIFETIME STATE PARK PASS; and service members in combat zones receive complimentary licenses while on leave. Lifetime hunting and fishing privileges in Wyoming are a substantial recurring benefit given what nonresident and even resident licenses cost.
states.cash: The Wyoming Military Assistance Trust Fund provides emergency financial grants to service members and dependents experiencing hardship during active duty, and reimburses dependent care costs for up to 39 days annually. Beyond this, Wyoming has essentially no state cash assistance infrastructure for veterans — no wartime service bonus, no general veterans emergency financial assistance fund open to all veterans, and no property tax rebate program. This is the weakest category in Wyoming's package and reflects the state's minimal agency footprint. Veterans needing emergency assistance are generally directed to VA programs, county-level general assistance, and private veteran service organizations rather than state funds.
states.homesHealth: The Veterans' Home of Wyoming in Buffalo provides assisted living and skilled nursing care, with fees assessed based on ability to pay (307-684-5511). It is the state's single veterans long-term care facility. The Oregon Trail State Veterans Cemetery in Evansville (near Casper) provides FREE burial plots for eligible veterans (307-235-6673). Wyoming operates no state-funded veterans health programs beyond the single home; clinical care runs through the Cheyenne and Sheridan VA Medical Centers and community-based outpatient clinics, and Wyoming's vast geography means travel distances for VA care are among the longest in the nation — a practical consideration that offsets some of the state's tax advantages for veterans with significant health needs.
other: The $6,000 assessed-value exemption is worth only roughly $350-$450 per year — among the smallest property tax benefits in the country in absolute dollars.

BUT the exemption is unusually BROAD in eligibility: three years of Wyoming residency plus qualifying wartime service OR a service-connected disability, rather than requiring a high disability rating.
If you do not own real property, the exemption can be applied to VEHICLE LICENSING FEES instead — a provision almost no one uses and that helps renters capture the benefit.

Free LIFETIME hunting and fishing licenses at a 100% rating, and a free LIFETIME fishing license at just 50% — in a state where hunting and fishing are central to daily life, this is among the most practically valuable benefits available.
Free lifetime state park pass at a 50% disability rating.
Wyoming National Guard members can TRANSFER one degree's worth of tuition benefit to a dependent after a six-year enlistment — state-level transferability is rare.
The Veterans Tuition Benefit requires OVERSEAS COMBAT service (campaign or expeditionary medal), not merely wartime-era service — a narrower gate than it first appears.
Wyoming has essentially no state veterans emergency cash assistance program open to all veterans, unlike most peer states.
Travel distance to VA medical care is among the longest in the nation, a real cost that partially offsets the tax advantages.
states.topHack: If you rent, or if your property tax bill is already tiny, redirect the $6,000 veterans exemption to your VEHICLE LICENSING FEES instead of your real property — Wyoming explicitly permits this and virtually nobody does it, so renting veterans routinely let the benefit expire unused every year. The bigger prize, though, is recreational: a 100% rating buys free LIFETIME hunting and fishing licenses and a 50% rating buys a free lifetime fishing license plus a free lifetime state park pass. In Wyoming those lifetime licenses are worth far more over a retirement than the entire property tax exemption, and they require nothing but a one-time application with your rating letter to Wyoming Game and Fish.
